But words ending in the suffix `-tu` are for the most part of the same form in the three genders, as in the Therīpāḷi: '...an inquirer into the meaning and the Dhamma, a learner, a listener to the Dhamma, and an attendant.' Likewise, sometimes also words like `gacchanta`. 'Dispelling the mass of darkness, speaking such an ill-spoken word,' etc. There, `padālayaṃ` has the meaning of `padālayantī` (she who dispels), and `bhaṇaṃ` has the meaning of `bhaṇantī` (she who speaks).

Vīsā, tiṃsā, cattālīsā, paññāsā iccete saṅkhyārāsimhi āgamissanti.

Twenty, thirty, forty, fifty—these will come in the section on numerals.

Ākārantitthiliṅgarāsi niṭṭhito.

The section on feminine nouns ending in -ā is finished.

Ikārantitthiliṅgarāsi

The Section on Feminine Nouns Ending in ‘i’

‘Gasīna’nti silopo. Ratti tiṭṭhati, rattiyo tiṭṭhanti.

By the rule 'Gasīnaṃ', `si` is elided. The night stands; the nights stand.

‘Jantuhetvā’disuttena yolope –

By the sutta beginning with ‘Jantuhetvā’, when ‘yo’ is elided –

91. Yolopanīsu dīgho ka. 88; rū. 147; nī. 245.

91. In cases of `yo` elision or `nī` substitution, the vowel becomes long.

Tiliṅge yonaṃ lope ca niādese ca rassānaṃ dīgho hoti.

In the three genders, when `yo` is elided, and when `ni` is substituted, short vowels become long.

Rattī tiṭṭhanti.

The nights stand.

92. Ye passivaṇṇassa.

92. Elision of the `i`-vowel of a `pa`-class noun before `ya`.

Vibhattibhūte vibhattādesabhūte ca yakāre pare pasaññassa ivaṇṇassa lopo hoti. Gāthāsuyeva idaṃ vidhānaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

When the letter `ya` follows, being a case ending or a substitute for a case ending, the `i`-vowel of a `pa`-class noun is elided. This rule should be seen only in verses.

Ratyo tiṭṭhanti rū. 84 piṭṭhe -sandhivasena āditakāralopo.

The nights stand – due to sandhi, the initial ‘a’ sound is elided.

63. Ayunaṃ vā dīgho ka. 88; rū. 147; nī. 245.

63. For stems ending in `a` and `yu`, there is optional lengthening before the ending `naṃ`.

Ge pare tiliṅge aiunaṃ dīgho hoti vā.

When ‘ge’ follows, the vowels a, i, and u in the three genders are optionally lengthened.

He [M 0.0068] rattī, he ratti. Bahuvacane he rattī, he rattiyo, he ratyo.

He rattī, he ratti. In the plural: he rattī, he rattiyo, he ratyo.

Aṃvacane ‘paro kvacī’ti suttena parasare lutte niggahītaṃ pubbe ivaṇṇuvaṇṇesu tiṭṭhati.

In the ‘aṃ’ case ending, by the rule ‘paro kvacī’, when the subsequent vowel is elided, the niggahīta remains before the preceding i-vowels and u-vowels.

Rattiṃ, tathā itthiṃ, dhenuṃ, vadhuṃ, aggiṃ, daṇḍiṃ, bhikkhuṃ, sayambhuṃ iti. Rattiyaṃ, ‘bujjhassu jinabodhiya’nti pāḷi bu. vaṃ. 2.182, rattinaṃ vā, ‘yāvanto purisassatthaṃ, guyhaṃ jānanti mantina’ntipāḷi jā. 1.15.335.

Rattiṃ (night), likewise itthiṃ (woman), dhenuṃ (cow), vadhuṃ (bride), aggiṃ (fire), daṇḍiṃ (staff-bearer), bhikkhuṃ (monk), sayambhuṃ (Self-Existent One), and so on. Rattiyaṃ (in the night), as in the Pāli passage: ‘bujjhassu jinabodhiya’. Or rattinaṃ, as in the Pāli passage: ‘yāvanto purisassatthaṃ, guyhaṃ jānanti mantina’.

Rattī, rattiyo, ratyo-‘ghapatekasmiṃ nādīnaṃ yayā’ti nādīnaṃ yā hoti, rattiyā, yakāre pare ivaṇṇalopo, ratyā.

Rattī, rattiyo, ratyo – by the rule ‘ghapatekasmiṃ nādīnaṃ yayā’, for the `nādī` group, the ending is `yā`, giving rattiyā; when the letter ‘ya’ follows, the i-vowel is elided, resulting in ratyā.

94. Sunaṃhisu ka. 89; rū. 87; nī. 246.

94. Sunaṃhisu.

Su, naṃ, hisu rassānaṃ dīgho hoti.

The short vowels of `su`, `naṃ`, and `hisu` are lengthened.

Rattīhi, rattībhi, rattiyā, ratyā, rattīnaṃ, rattiyā, ratyā, rattīhi, rattībhi, rattiyā, ratyā, rattīnaṃ, rattiyā, ratyā, rattiyaṃ, ratyaṃ, rattīsu.

Rattīhi, rattībhi, rattiyā, ratyā, rattīnaṃ, rattiyā, ratyā, rattīhi, rattībhi, rattiyā, ratyā, rattīnaṃ, rattiyā, ratyā, rattiyaṃ, ratyaṃ, rattīsu.

Ettha garū su, naṃ, hisu dīghattaṃ aniccaṃ icchanti, taṃ gāthāsu yujjati.

Here, the teachers desire the lengthening of su, naṃ, and hisu to be optional; that is suitable in verses.

Patti yutti vutti kitti, mutti titti khanti kanti.

Patti (attainment), yutti (application), vutti (conduct), kitti (renown), mutti (release), titti (satisfaction), khanti (forbearance), kanti (loveliness).

Santi tanti siddhi suddhi, iddhi vuddhi buddhi bodhi.

Santi (peace), tanti (tradition), siddhi (success), suddhi (purity), iddhi (psychic power), vuddhi (growth), buddhi (intelligence), bodhi (enlightenment).

Bhūmi jāti pīti suti, nandi sandhi sāṇi koṭi.

Bhūmi (earth), jāti (birth), pīti (rapture), suti (hearing), nandi (joy), sandhi (connection), sāṇi (hempen cloth), koṭi (tip).

Diṭṭhi vuḍḍhi tuṭṭhi yaṭṭhi, pāḷi āḷi nāḷi keḷi.

Diṭṭhi (view), vuḍḍhi (growth), tuṭṭhi (satisfaction), yaṭṭhi (staff), pāḷi (Pāli), āḷi (row), nāḷi (tube), keḷi (play).

Sati mati gati muti, dhīti yuvati vikati.

Sati (mindfulness), mati (intellect), gati (going), muti (release), dhīti (resolve), yuvati (young woman), vikati (change).

Rati ruci rasmi asani vasani osadhi aṅguli dhūli dudrabhi

Rati (delight), ruci (pleasure), rasmi (ray), asani (thunderbolt), vasani (garment), osadhi (herb), aṅguli (finger), dhūli (dust), dudrabhi (drum).

Doṇi [M 0.0069] aṭavi chaviādayo rattādi.

Doṇi (boat), aṭavi (forest), chavi (skin), and others are of the `ratti` group.

Ettha visesavidhānamuccate.

Here, a special rule is stated.

95. Rattādīhi ṭo smiṃno ka. 69; rū. 186; nī. 218, 219; rattyādīhi ṭo smino (bahūsu) ratyādīhi (katthaci).

95. After `ratti` and so on, `ṭo` is substituted for `smiṃ` and `no`.

Rattisadda, ādisaddehi smiṃno ṭo hoti vā.

For the word `ratti` and the other words of its group, `ṭo` is optionally substituted for `smiṃ` and `no`.

Divā ca ratto ca khu. pā. 6.2; jā. 1.9.92, ādo, ādimhi, pādādo, pādādimhi, gāthādo, gāthādimhi-ādisaddo pana pulliṅgoyeva, rattiṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjati, ādiṃ tiṭṭhatīti ādhāratthe dutiyāva, ratyo amoghā gacchanti jā. 2.22.105, tiṇalatāni osadhyo jā. 2.22.2174, tato ratyā vivasāne jā. 2.22.1689, na jaccā vasalo hoti, na jaccā hoti brāhmaṇo su. ni. 142 -jaccāti jātiyā, na nikatyā sukhamedhati jā. 1.1.38, khantyā bhiyyo na vijjati saṃ. ni. 1.250.

Divā ca ratto ca (by day and by night); ādo, ādimhi (at the beginning, in the beginning); pādādo, pādādimhi (at the foot, in the foot); gāthādo, gāthādimhi (at the beginning of the verse, in the beginning of the verse) – the word ‘ādi’ is indeed only masculine. Rattiṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjati (he eats food at night); ādiṃ tiṭṭhatīti (he stands at the beginning) – here the accusative case is in the sense of location. Ratyo amoghā gacchanti (the nights pass not in vain). Tiṇalatāni osadhyo (grasses and creepers are herbs). Tato ratyā vivasāne (then at the end of the night). Na jaccā vasalo hoti, na jaccā hoti brāhmaṇo (not by birth is one an outcast, not by birth is one a brahmin) – ‘jaccā’ means by birth. Na nikatyā sukhamedhati (not by deception does one attain happiness). Khantyā bhiyyo na vijjati (there is nothing greater than patience).

Nāññatra bojjhā tapasā saṃ. ni. 1.98, yatheva khalatī bhūmyā, bhūmyāyeva patiṭṭhati jā. 2.22.1522, mahāvuttinā māti, pitisaddā nādīhi saddhiṃ matyā, petyāti sijjhanti, matyā ca petyā ca etaṃ jānāmimātito pititoti attho, matyā ca petyā ca kataṃ susādhu jā. 2.18.61 -katanti kataṃ nāmaṃ, susādhūti atisundaraṃ. ‘Anuññāto ahaṃ matyā, sañcatto pitarā aha’nti jā. 2.22.29 pāḷipadāni. ‘Mātīnaṃ dohaḷo nāma janinda vuccatī’ jā. 2.22.1347 ti ca pāḷi, vīsati, tiṃsati, saṭṭhi, sattati, asīti, navuti, koṭi, pakoṭi iccete saṅkhyārāsimhi āgamissanti.

Not otherwise than by enlightenment and asceticism. Just as one who stumbles on the ground is supported by the ground itself. By the great commentary, `māti` (mother) [is formed]. The words `mātu` and `pitu`, like the `nādī` group, are formed as `matyā` and `petyā`. By `matyā` and `petyā` I know this, meaning ‘from mother and from father’. What is done by `matyā` and `petyā` is well-done – ‘kataṃ’ means ‘done’, ‘susādhu’ means exceedingly beautiful. The Pāli verses are: ‘Anuññāto ahaṃ matyā, sañcatto pitarā ahaṃ’. And the Pāli passage: ‘Mātīnaṃ dohaḷo nāma janinda vuccatī’. Twenty, thirty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, koṭi, pakoṭi – these will come in the section on numerals.

Ikārantitthiliṅgarāsi niṭṭhito.

The Section on Feminine Nouns Ending in ‘I’ is completed.

Īkārantitthiliṅgarāsi

The Section on Feminine Nouns Ending in ‘Ī’

96. Simhi nānapuṃsakassa ka. 85; rū. 150; nī. 239 moga-du. 66; sismiṃ (bahūsu).

96. In the ‘si’ case, for that which is not neuter.

Simhi [M 0.0070] pare anapuṃsakassa pumitthīnaṃ dīghassa rasso na hoti.

When `si` follows, for a non-neuter word, that is, masculine or feminine, a long vowel is not shortened.

Itthī tiṭṭhati, itthī tiṭṭhanti.

Itthī tiṭṭhati, itthī tiṭṭhanti.

97. Ekavacanayosvaghonaṃ ka. 84; rū. 144; nī. 237, 238.

97. For singulars and ‘yo’ forms, of non-‘gha’ and non-‘o’.

Gho ca o ca gho, na gho agho. Ekavacanesu ca yosu ca paresu gha, ovajjitānaṃ sabbesaṃ dīghānaṃ rasso hoti.

‘Gha’ and ‘o’ are ‘gho’; not ‘gho’ is ‘agho’. When singulars and ‘yo’ forms follow, all long vowels, except those of ‘gha’ and ‘o’, become short.

Itthiyo tiṭṭhanti, ithyo tiṭṭhanti.

Itthiyo tiṭṭhanti, ithyo tiṭṭhanti.

98. Ge vā ka. 245, 246; rū. 152, 73; nī. 476-9.

98. Optionally, in the ‘ge’ case.

Ge pare gha, ovajjitānaṃ sabbesaṃ dīghānaṃ rasso hoti vā.

When ‘ge’ follows, all long vowels, except for those in ‘gha’ and ‘o’, optionally become short.

Bhoti itthi, bhoti itthī, bhotiyo itthī, bhotiyo itthiyo, bhotiyo ithyo, itthiṃ passati.

Bhoti itthi, bhoti itthī (O lady); bhotiyo itthī, bhotiyo itthiyo, bhotiyo ithyo (O ladies). Itthiṃ passati (he sees a woman).

99. Yaṃ pīto ka. 223; rū. 188; nī. 450.

99. The ‘yaṃ’ form is also found.

Yo pasañño īkāro, tato aṃvacanassa yaṃ hoti vā.

After an ‘ī’ vowel that is ‘pasañña’, the case ending ‘aṃ’ optionally becomes ‘yaṃ’.

Itthiyaṃ passati, ettha ca yanti suttavibhattena “bujjhassu jinabodhiya”nti bu. vaṃ. 2.182 sijjhati. Itthī passati, itthiyo passati, ithyo [M 0.0071] passati, itthiyā, ithyā, itthīhi, itthībhi, itthiyā, ithyā, itthīnaṃ, itthiyā, itthimhā, ithyā, itthīhi, itthībhi, itthiyā, ithyā, itthīnaṃ, itthiyā, ithyā, itthiyaṃ, ithyaṃ, itthimhi, itthīsu.

Itthiyaṃ passati (he sees a woman); and here, by the grammatical rule ‘yanti’, the form ‘bujjhassu jinabodhiya’ is accomplished. Itthī passati, itthiyo passati, ithyo passati, itthiyā, ithyā, itthīhi, itthībhi, itthiyā, ithyā, itthīnaṃ, itthiyā, itthimhā, ithyā, itthīhi, itthībhi, itthiyā, ithyā, itthīnaṃ, itthiyā, ithyā, itthiyaṃ, ithyaṃ, itthimhi, itthīsu.

Nadī sandati, nadī sandanti, nadiyo sandanti.

Nadī sandati (a river flows), nadī sandanti (rivers flow), nadiyo sandanti (rivers flow).

Ivaṇṇalope sandhisuttena yakāre pare tavaggassa cavaggo, yassa ca pubbarūpaṃ ka. 98; rū. 87 piṭṭhe; nī. 104; 262-3-4. Najjo sandanti ka. 98; rū. 87 piṭṭhe; nī. 104; 262-3-4, nādyekavacanesu najjā kataṃ, najjā deti, najjā apeti, najjā santakaṃ, najjā tiṭṭhati, najjaṃ tiṭṭhati, sesarūpāni itthisadisāni.

Upon the elision of the ‘i’-vowel, by a sandhi rule, when the letter ‘ya’ follows, the ‘ta’-group becomes the ‘ca’-group, and ‘ya’ is assimilated to the preceding consonant. Najjo sandanti (rivers flow). In the singular forms of ‘nadī’: najjā kataṃ (done by the river), najjā deti (gives to the river), najjā apeti (goes away from the river), najjā santakaṃ (belonging to the river), najjā tiṭṭhati (stands by the river), najjaṃ tiṭṭhati (stands in the river). The remaining forms are similar to those of ‘itthī’.

Evaṃ gacchatī gacchantī, satī santī, asatī asantī, mahatī mahantī, brahmatī brantī, bhotī bhontī, bhavissatī bhavissantī, gamissatī gamissantī, guṇavatī guṇavantī, sīlavatī sīlavantī, satimatī satimantī, sirimatī sirimantī, katavatī katavantī, bhuttāvatī bhuttāvantī, sabbāvatī sabbāvantī, yāvatī yāvantī, tāvatī tāvantī. Kamhi āgame rasso, yāvatikā, tāvatikā.

Thus: gacchatī, gacchantī; satī, santī; asatī, asantī; mahatī, mahantī; brahmatī, brantī; bhotī, bhontī; bhavissatī, bhavissantī; gamissatī, gamissantī; guṇavatī, guṇavantī; sīlavatī, sīlavantī; satimatī, satimantī; sirimatī, sirimantī; katavatī, katavantī; bhuttāvatī, bhuttāvantī; sabbāvatī, sabbāvantī; yāvatī, yāvantī; tāvatī, tāvantī. With which augment is there shortening? Yāvatikā, tāvatikā.

Gāvī, yakkhī, yakkhinī, ārāmikinī, daṇḍapāṇinī, daṇḍinī, bhikkhunī, paracittavidunī, muṭṭhassatinī, gharaṇī, pokkharaṇī, ācarinī, mātulānī, gahapatānī iccādayo. Nadādi.

Gāvī (cow), yakkhī (female yakkha), yakkhinī (female yakkha), ārāmikinī (female park-keeper), daṇḍapāṇinī (female staff-bearer), daṇḍinī (female staff-bearer), bhikkhunī (nun), paracittavidunī (knower of others’ minds), muṭṭhassatinī (forgetful one), gharaṇī (housewife), pokkharaṇī (lotus pond), ācarinī (female teacher), mātulānī (maternal aunt), gahapatānī (female householder), and so on. These belong to the Nadī-ādi group.

Visesavidhānamuccate.

A special provision is stated.

100. Najjā yosvāma nī. 262.

100. After ‘nadī’, before ‘yo’, ‘āma’.

Yosu paresu nadiyā ante āmaāgamo hoti vā.

When the ‘yo’ endings follow, the augment ‘āma’ optionally occurs after ‘nadī’.

Najjāyo [M 0.0072] sandanti saṃ. ni. 3.224, najjāyo supatitthāyo jā. 2.22.1414 ti pāḷi, nimijātake pana najjonupariyāyati, nānāpupphadumāyutāti ca najjo cānupariyātīti jā. 2.22.537 ca pāḷi, tattha mahāvuttinā sissa ottaṃ.

Najjāyo sandanti (rivers flow). The Pāli passage is: ‘Najjāyo supatitthāyo’ (rivers with good fords). But in the Nimijātaka, ‘najjonupariyāyati’ occurs, and also the Pāli passage: ‘nānāpupphadumāyutā’, and ‘najjo cānupariyātīti’. There, according to the Mahāvutti, the ending ‘si’ becomes ‘o’.

Uṭṭhehi revate supāpakamme vi. va. 863, dāsā ca dāsyo ca, anujīvino jā. 1.10.101, bārāṇasyaṃ mahārāja, kākarājā nivāsako jā. 1.3.124, bārāṇasyaṃ ahu rājā jā. 1.16.178, rañño mano ummādantyā niviṭṭho, ummādantyā ramitvāna, sivirājā tato siyaṃ jā. 2.18.70, dārakeva ahaṃ nessaṃ. Brāhmaṇyā paricārake jā. 2.22.2111. Tathā yosu pokkharañño. Nādīsu pathabyā, puthabyā, pokkharaññā. Smiṃmhi pathabyā, pathabyaṃ, puthabyā, puthabyaṃ, pokkharaññā, pokkharaññaṃ, vetraññā, vetraññaṃ ve traraññā, (nissaya) iccādīni dissanti.

Uṭṭhehi revate supāpakamme (Arise, Revata, you of evil deeds!). Dāsā ca dāsyo ca (slaves and slave women), anujīvino (dependents). Bārāṇasyaṃ mahārāja (in Benares, O great king), kākarājā nivāsako (the crow king, a resident). Bārāṇasyaṃ ahu rājā (in Benares there was a king). Rañño mano ummādantyā niviṭṭho (the king’s mind was fixed on Ummādantī). Ummādantyā ramitvāna (having delighted with Ummādantī), sivirājā tato siyaṃ (then I would be the king of Sivi). Dārakeva ahaṃ nessaṃ (I shall lead them like a child). Brāhmaṇyā paricārake (as a servant to the Brahmin woman). Likewise, before the ‘yo’ endings, pokkharañño. For nouns of the Nadī-group: pathabyā, puthabyā, pokkharaññā. Before ‘smiṃ’ and ‘mhi’: pathabyā, pathabyaṃ, puthabyā, puthabyaṃ, pokkharaññā, pokkharaññaṃ, vetraññā, vetraññaṃ, and so on, are seen.

Īkārantitthiliṅgarāsi niṭṭhito.

The Section on Feminine Nouns Ending in ‘ī’ is completed.

Ukārantitthiliṅgarāsi

The Section on Feminine Nouns Ending in ‘u’

Silopo, dhenu gacchati, dhenuyo gacchanti, yolope dīgho, dhenū gacchanti, bhoti dhenu, bhoti dhenū, bhotiyo dhenuyo, bhotiyo dhenū, dhenuṃ passati, dhenuyo passati, dhenū passati, dhenuyā, dhenūhi, dhenūbhi, dhenuyā, dhenūnaṃ, dhenuyā, dhenumhā, dhenūhi, dhenūbhi, dhenuyā, dhenūnaṃ, dhenuyā, dhenuyaṃ, dhenumhi, dhenūsu.

Elision of ‘si’: `dhenu gacchati` (the cow goes), `dhenuyo gacchanti` (the cows go). Upon elision of `yo`, there is lengthening: `dhenū gacchanti` (the cows go). Vocative: `bhoti dhenu`, `bhoti dhenū`, `bhotiyo dhenuyo`, `bhotiyo dhenū`. Accusative: `dhenuṃ passati`, `dhenuyo passati`, `dhenū passati`. Other forms: `dhenuyā, dhenūhi, dhenūbhi, dhenuyā, dhenūnaṃ, dhenuyā, dhenumhā, dhenūhi, dhenūbhi, dhenuyā, dhenūnaṃ, dhenuyā, dhenuyaṃ, dhenumhi, dhenūsu`.

Evaṃ yāgu, kāsu, daddu, kaṇḍu, kacchu, rajju, kareṇu, piyaṅgu, sassu iccādayo. Dhenvādi.

Similarly: yāgu (rice-gruel), kāsu (pit), daddu (ringworm), kaṇḍu (itch), kacchu (scabies), rajju (rope), kareṇu (female elephant), piyaṅgu (panic seed), sassu (mother-in-law), and so on. These belong to the Dhenu-ādi group.

Dhātusaddo [M 0.0073] pana pāḷinaye itthiliṅgo, saddasatthanaye pumitthiliṅgo.

The word 'dhātu', however, is feminine in the Pāli canon, but masculine and feminine in grammar.

Mātu, dhītu, duhitusaddā itthi liṅgā, tesaṃ rūpaṃ pitādigaṇe āgamissati.

The words 'mātu' (mother), 'dhītu' (daughter), and 'duhitu' (daughter) are of the feminine gender. Their forms will be given in the Pitā-ādi group.

Ukārantitthiliṅgarāsi niṭṭhito.

The Section on Feminine Nouns Ending in ‘u’ is completed.

Ūkārantitthiliṅgarāsi

The Section on Feminine Nouns Ending in ‘ū’

Vadhū gacchati, vadhū gacchanti, yosu rasso, vadhuyo gacchanti, bhoti vadhu, bhoti vadhū, bhotiyo vadhū, vadhuyo, vadhuṃ, vadhū, vadhuyo, vadhuyā, vadhūhi, vadhūbhi, vadhuyā, vadhūnaṃ, vadhuyā, vadhumhā, vadhūhi, vadhūbhi, vadhuyā, vadhūnaṃ, vadhuyā, vadhuyaṃ, vadhūsu. Evaṃ jambū, sarabhū, sutanū, nāganāsūrū, saṃhitorū, vāmorū, lakkhaṇūrū, brahmabandhū, bhū, camū iccādayo. Vadhādi.

`Vadhū gacchati` (the daughter-in-law goes), `vadhū gacchanti` (the daughters-in-law go). Before `yo`, there is shortening: `vadhuyo gacchanti` (the daughters-in-law go). Vocative: `bhoti vadhu`, `bhoti vadhū`, `bhotiyo vadhū`, `vadhuyo`. Accusative: `vadhuṃ`, `vadhū`, `vadhuyo`. Other forms: `vadhuyā, vadhūhi, vadhūbhi, vadhuyā, vadhūnaṃ, vadhuyā, vadhumhā, vadhūhi, vadhūbhi, vadhuyā, vadhūnaṃ, vadhuyā, vadhuyaṃ, vadhūsu`. Similarly: `jambū` (rose-apple), `sarabhū`, `sutanū` (fair-bodied), `nāganāsūrū` (with thighs like an elephant's trunk), `saṃhitorū` (with well-rounded thighs), `vāmorū` (with beautiful thighs), `lakkhaṇūrū` (with auspicious thighs), `brahmabandhū` (a kinswoman of Brahma), `bhū` (the earth), `camū` (an army), and so on. These belong to the Vadhū-ādi group.

Sāhaṃ gantvā manussattaṃ, vadaññū vītamaccharāti vi. va. 634 ca kodhanā akataññū cāti jā. 1.1.63 ca pāḷiyo, tasmā nīpaccayaṃ vināpi kvaci ūkārantakitakasaddā itthiliṅgā bhavanti.

And the Pāli texts say: 'Having attained the human state, I was generous and free from stinginess,' and 'angry and ungrateful.' Therefore, sometimes even without the 'nī' suffix, primary derivative nouns ending in 'ū' are feminine.

Ūkārantitthiliṅgarāsi niṭṭhito.

The Section on Feminine Nouns Ending in ‘ū’ is completed.

Okārantarāsi

The Section on Nouns Ending in ‘o’

Gosaddo dviliṅgo. Tassa rūpāni kānici dviyatthavasena itthiyampi vattanti pumepi vattanti missakepi vattanti, kānici itthiyaṃ kānici pume. Idha pana sabbāni yāni samodhānetvā dīpiyante.

The word 'go' is of two genders. Some of its forms, having a dual meaning, apply to the feminine, the masculine, and both genders combined; some apply only to the feminine, some only to the masculine. Here, however, all are brought together and explained.

Silopo, gogacchati-ettha ca goti abhinnasaddaliṅgattā goṇotipi yujjati, gāvītipi yujjati.

Elision of 'si'. In the phrase `go gacchati` (the bovine goes), because the word 'go' is not distinguished by form or gender, it can be understood as `goṇo` (bull) or as `gāvī` (cow).

101. Gossāgasihinaṃsu [M 0.0074] gāvagavā ka. 73-5; rū. 169, 170, 174; nī. 224.

101. Gossāgasihinaṃsu gāvagavā.

Ga, si, hi, naṃvajjitāsu vibhattīsu gosaddassa gāva, gavādesā honti.

In the case endings other than `ga`, `si`, `hi`, and `naṃ`, `gāva` and `gavā` are the substitutes for the word `go`.

102. Ubhagohi ṭo ka. 205; rū. 160; nī. 421.

102. Ubhagohi ṭo.

Ubha, gohi yonaṃ ṭo hoti.

After `ubha` and `go`, the ending `yo` becomes `o`.

Gāvo, gavo, he go, he gāvo, he gavo, gāvaṃ, gavaṃ.

Cows, cows; O cow; O cows, O cows; the cow, the cow.

103. Gāvumhi ka. 76; rū 171, 226.

103. Gāvumhi.

Aṃmhi gossa gāvu hoti vā.

When `aṃ` follows, `gāvu` is the optional substitute for `go`.

Gāvuṃ, gāvo, gavo, gāvena, gavena.

The cow; the cows, the cows; by a cow, by a cow.

104. Nāssā.

104. Nāssā.

Gossa gāva, gavādesato nāvacanassa ā hoti vā.

After `go`, for which `gāva` and `gavā` are substitutes, the ending `nā` is optionally replaced by `ā`.

Gāvā, gavā, gohi, gobhi, gāvassa, gavassa.

By a cow, by a cow; by cows, by cows; of a cow, of a cow.

105. Gavaṃ sena.

105. Gavaṃ sena.

Sena saha gossa gavaṃ hoti vā.

With the ending `sa`, `gavaṃ` is the optional substitute for `go`.

Gavaṃ, gonaṃ.

Of cows, of bulls.

106. Gunnañca naṃnā ka. 81; rū. 172; nī. 230.

106. Gunnañca naṃnā.

Naṃnā saha gossa gunnañca hoti gavañca.

With the ending `naṃ`, `gunnaṃ` and `gavaṃ` are substitutes for `go`.

Gunnaṃ, gavaṃ, gāvasmā, gavasmā, gāvamhā, gavamhā, gāvā, gavā, gohi, gobhi, gāvassa, gavassa, gavaṃ, gonaṃ, gunnaṃ, gavaṃ, gāvasmiṃ, gāvamhi, gāve, gavasmiṃ, gavamhi, gave, gosu, gāvesu, gavesu.

Of cows, of cows; from a cow, from a cow, from a cow, from a cow; by a cow, by a cow; by cows, by cows; of a cow, of a cow; of cows, of bulls, of cows, of cows; in a cow, in a cow, in a cow, in a cow, in a cow, in a cow; in cows, in cows, in cows.

Yosu [M 0.0075] gāva, gavādese kate ato yonaṃ ṭā, ṭe ca honti, usabhā rukkhā gāviyo gavā ca jā. 1.1.77. Balagavā dammagavā vā gaṅgāya pāraṃ agamiṃsu. Athāpare patāresi balagāve dammagāve ma. ni. 1.352 (thokaṃ visadisaṃ) ti pāḷipadāni.

When `gāva` and `gavā` have been substituted, `yo` following them becomes `ā` and `e`. For example: 'bulls, trees, cows and cattle.' 'The strong oxen and the tame oxen went across the Ganges.' And the Pāḷi phrases: 'Then he ferried across the others, the strong oxen, the tame oxen.'

Ettha ca gāvo no paramā mittā, yāsu jāyanti osadhā su. ni. 298 ti ca, gavā khīraṃ, khīramhā dadhi, dadhimhā navanītaṃ, navanītamhā sappi, sappimhā sappimaṇḍoti ca itthiyaṃ vattanti. Gāviyo gavāti ca balagavā dammagavā balagave dammagaveti ma. ni. 1.351 ca gāvuṃ vā te dammi gāviṃ vā te dammīti ca gavaṃva siṅgino siṅganti jā. 1.12.39 ca pume bhavanti. Atittheneva gāvo patāresi, atha kho tā gāvo majjhe gaṅgāya anayabyasanaṃ āpajjiṃsū ma. ni. 1.350 ti ca annadā baladā cetā, vaṇṇadā sukhadā ca tā, etamatthavasaṃ ñatvā, nāssu gāvo haniṃsu teti su. ni. 298 ca bhaddavasena itthiyaṃ atthavasena missake vattanti. Gunnaṃ ce taramānānaṃ, gavaṃ ce taramānānaṃ, ujuṃ gacchati puṅgavo, sabbā tā ujuṃ gacchantīti jā. 1.4.135; 2.18.104 ca missake eva. Balagava, dammagavasaddā jaraggava, puṅgava, sagava, paragava, dāragavasaddā viya akārantā samāsasaddātipi yujjati.

And here, the following are used in the feminine: 'Cows are our supreme friends, from whom medicines are produced'; and 'From the cow comes milk, from milk curd, from curd fresh butter, from fresh butter ghee, from ghee the cream of ghee.' The following are in the masculine: 'cows are `gāviyo` and `gavā`'; 'strong oxen and tame oxen,' 'strong oxen, tame oxen'; 'I will give you an ox (`gāvuṃ`) or I will give you a cow (`gāviṃ`)'; and 'the horned ones butt like oxen.' The following are used in the feminine by convention, but in the mixed gender according to the meaning: 'He ferried the cows across at a place that was not a ford, but then those cows met with disaster in the middle of the Ganges'; and 'They give food and they give strength, they give beauty and they give happiness; knowing this benefit, they did not kill the cows.' The following is in the mixed gender only: 'When they are crossing, when the cattle are crossing, if the lead bull goes straight, they all go straight.' It is also acceptable that the words `balagava` and `dammagava`, like the words `jaraggava`, `puṅgava`, `sagava`, `paragava`, and `dāragava`, are compound words ending in 'a'.

Missakaṭṭhānesu pana itthibahulattā tā gāvo etā gāvotiādinā itthiliṅgameva dissati.

However, in instances of mixed gender, due to the predominance of the feminine, only the feminine gender is seen, as in 'those cows,' 'these cows,' and so on.

Iti okārantarāsi.

Thus the section on nouns ending in 'o'.

Itthiliṅgarāsi niṭṭhito.

The collection of feminine nouns is completed.

Pulliṅgarāsi

The Masculine Gender

Akāranta pulliṅgapurisādirāsi

The Group of Masculine Nouns Ending in 'a', Beginning with 'purisa'

Atha pulliṅgāni dīpiyante.

Now, masculine nouns are explained.

Sattavidhaṃ pulliṅgaṃ – adantaṃ, ādantaṃ, idantaṃ, īdantaṃ, udantaṃ, ūdantaṃ, odantaṃ.

The masculine gender is of seven kinds: ending in 'a', ending in 'ā', ending in 'i', ending in 'ī', ending in 'u', ending in 'ū', and ending in 'o'.

107. Sisso ka. 104; rū. 66; nī. 272.

107. Sisso.

Ato sissa o hoti pume.

From a stem ending in 'a', the nominative singular ending 'si' becomes 'o' in the masculine.

Puriso tiṭṭhati.

A man stands.

108. Ato yonaṃ ṭāṭe ka. 107; rū. 69; nī. 275, 277.

108. From 'a', 'yo' becomes 'ā' and 'e'.

Ato paṭhamāyonaṃ dutiyāyonañca kamena ṭā, ṭe honti puṃ, napuṃsakesu. Ṭānubandho sabbādesattho.

From a stem ending in 'a', the nominative plural 'yo' and the accusative plural 'yo' become 'ā' and 'e' respectively in the masculine and neuter genders. The indicatory letter 'ṭ' signifies a substitute for the entire form.

Purisā tiṭṭhanti.

Men stand.

‘Gasīna’nti silopo, bho purisa, ‘ayunaṃ vā dīgho’ti dīgho, bho purisā, bhonto purisā, purisaṃ, purise.

By the rule 'gasīnaṃ si lopo,' the ending 'si' is elided, giving 'bho purisa.' By 'ayunaṃ vā dīgho,' the vowel is lengthened, giving 'bho purisā.' Other forms are: 'bhonto purisā,' 'purisaṃ,' 'purise.'

109. Atena ka. 103; rū. 79; nī. 271.

109. From 'a', 'ena'.

Ato nāvacanassa enādeso hoti puṃ, napuṃsakesu.

From a stem ending in 'a', the instrumental singular ending 'nā' is substituted by 'ena' in the masculine and neuter genders.

Purisena.

By a man.

110. Suhisvasse ka. 101; rū. 80; nī. 68.

110. Before 'su' and 'hi', 'a' becomes 'e'.

Su, hisu paresu assa e hoti puṃ, napuṃsakesu.

When the endings 'hi' and 'su' follow, the stem vowel 'a' becomes 'e' in the masculine and neuter genders.

Purisehi, purisebhi.

By men; with men.

111. Suu [M 0.0077] sassa ka. 61; rū. 86; nī. 208.

111. The augment 'sa' before 'sa'.

Sassa ādimhi sāgamo hoti. Ukāro uccāraṇattho, ñānubandho ādimhīti dīpanattho.

Before the ending 'sa', the augment 'sa' is inserted. The letter 'u' is for the sake of pronunciation; the indicatory letter 'ñ' is for the purpose of showing 'at the beginning'.

Purisassa, ‘sunaṃhisū’ti dīgho. Purisānaṃ, purisasmā, purisamhā.

Purisassa (of a man). By the rule 'sunaṃhisū,' the vowel is lengthened, giving: Purisānaṃ (of men). Other forms are: purisasmā, purisamhā (from a man).

112. Smāsmiṃnaṃ ka. 108; rū. 90; nī. 276.

112. Of 'smā' and 'smiṃ'.

Ato smā, smiṃnaṃ kamena ṭā, ṭe honti puṃ, napuṃsakesu.

From a stem ending in 'a', the endings 'smā' and 'smiṃ' respectively become 'ā' and 'e' in the masculine and neuter genders.

Purisā, purisehi, purisebhi, purisassa, purisānaṃ, purisasmiṃ, purisamhi, purise, purisesu.

purisā (men; from a man), purisehi (by/from men), purisebhi (by/from men), purisassa (of a man), purisānaṃ (of men), purisasmiṃ (in a man), purisamhi (in a man), purise (in a man), purisesu (in men).

Evaṃ buddho, dhammo, saṅgho, sakko, devo, satto, naro, goṇo, puṅgavo, jaraggavo, sagavo, paragavo, rājagavo, mātugāmo, orodho, dāroiccādi.

Similarly: buddho (Buddha), dhammo (Dhamma), saṅgho (Saṅgha), sakko (Sakka), devo (a god), satto (a being), naro (a man), goṇo (an ox), puṅgavo (a bull), jaraggavo (an old bull), sagavo (one's own bull), paragavo (another's bull), rājagavo (a king's bull), mātugāmo (womankind), orodho (the harem), dāro (wife), and so on.

Visesavidhānamuccate.

A special rule is stated.

113. Kvace vā nī. 277.

113. Somewhere 'e', optionally.

Ato sissa kvaci e hoti vā puṃ, napuṃsakesu.

From a stem ending in 'a', the nominative singular ending 'si' in some instances optionally becomes 'e' in the masculine and neuter genders.

Pume tāva –

First, in the masculine:

Vanappagumbe yatha phussitagge khu. pā. 6.13; su. ni. 236, “ke gandhabbe rakkhase ca nāge, ke kimpurise cāpi mānuse. Ke paṇḍite sabbakāmadade. Dīgharattaṃ bhattā me bhavissati” jā. 2.22.1352. Natthi attakāre natthi parakāre natthi purisakāre dī. ni. 1.168, eke ekatthe, same samabhāge, nahevaṃ vattabbe kathā. 1, ke chave siṅgāle, ke chave pāthikaputte dī. ni. 3.29-31 iccādi.

Examples: 'vanappagumbe yathā phussitagge' (as in a forest grove with blossoming tops); 'ke gandhabbe rakkhase ca nāge, ke kimpurise cāpi mānuse. Ke paṇḍite sabbakāmadade' (Who are the gandhabbas, rakkhasas, and nāgas? Who are the kimpurisas and humans? Who are the wise ones, givers of all desires?); 'dīgharattaṃ bhattā me bhavissati' (For a long time he will be my supporter); 'natthi attakāre natthi parakāre natthi purisakāre' (There is no self-agent, there is no other-agent, there is no human agent); 'eke ekatthe' (some with one meaning); 'same samabhāge' (in an equal share); 'nahevaṃ vattabbe' (it should not be said thus); 'ke chave siṅgāle, ke chave pāthikaputte' (in which corpse for the jackal? in which corpse for the son of Pāthika?), and so on.

Napuṃsake [M 0.0078] pana –

In the neuter, however:

Bhogavatī nāma mandire, nagare nimmite kañcanamaye jā. 2.22.1370 iccādi.

Examples: 'Bhogavatī nāma mandire' (in the mansion named Bhogavatī); 'nagare nimmite kañcanamaye' (in the created city made of gold), and so on.

Vāti kiṃ? Vanappagumbo.

Why 'optionally' (vā)? To allow for the form 'vanappagumbo' (a forest grove).

Kvacīti kiṃ? Puriso.

Why 'in some cases' (kvaci)? To exclude cases like 'puriso' (a man).

Mahāvuttinā paṭhamāyonañca kvaci ṭe hoti. Bāle ca paṇḍite ca sandhāvitvā saṃsaritvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti dī. ni. 1.168, kvaci yonaṃ pakati hoti, vane vāḷamigā ceva, acchakokataracchayo, bahūhi paripanthayo jā. 2.22.255, kyassa byapathayo assu iccādi.

According to the Mahāvutti, the nominative plural 'yo' also sometimes becomes 'e'. For example: 'Bāle ca paṇḍite ca sandhāvitvā saṃsaritvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti' (Both fools and wise ones, having run and wandered on, will make an end of suffering). Sometimes 'yo' remains in its natural form, for example: 'vane vāḷamigā ceva, acchakokataracchayo' (wild beasts in the forest, and bears, wolves, and hyenas); 'bahūhi paripanthayo' (many dangers); 'kyassa byapathayo assu' (what troubles might there be for him?), and so on.

114. Divādito ka. 206; rū. 165.

114. From 'diva', etc.

Divādīhi smiṃno ṭi hoti.

After words of the 'diva' group, the locative singular ending 'smiṃ' becomes 'i'.

Divi-devaloketyattho.

Divi: the meaning is 'in the deva world'.

Ādisaddena asa bhuvi, niccaṃ vāgamo. Ayyasaddamhā mahāvuttinā ālapane ga, yonaṃ ṭo hoti vā. Bho ayyo ayya vā, bhonto ayyo ayyā vā. Sesaṃ purisasamaṃ.

By the word 'ādi' (etc.), the words 'asa' and 'bhuvi' are included, and there is always the augment 'va'. From the word 'ayya', according to the Mahāvutti, in the vocative, the singular ending 'si' and the plural 'yo' optionally become 'o'. For example: 'bho ayyo' or 'ayya' (O noble one!); 'bhonto ayyo' or 'ayyā' (O noble ones!). The rest is like 'purisa'.

Purisādirāsi niṭṭhito.

The group beginning with 'purisa' is finished.

Manogaṇarāsi

The Manas Group

Mano, manā, bho mana, bho manā, bhonto manā.

Mano, manā; O mind, O minds, O venerable minds.

115. Manādīhi smiṃsaṃnāsmānaṃ sisoosāsā ka. 181-2, 184; rū. 95-97; nī. 373-4, 376-7.

115. After 'manas' and other such words, for 'smiṃ', 'sa', 'aṃ', 'nā', and 'smā', the substitutes are 'si', 'so', 'o', 'sā', and 'sā'.

Tehi smiṃ, sa, aṃ, nā, smānaṃ kamena si, so, o, sā, sā honti vā.

After those words, the endings 'smiṃ' (loc. sg.), 'sa' (gen. sg.), 'aṃ' (acc. sg.), 'nā' (instr. sg.), and 'smā' (abl. sg.) optionally become 'si', 'so', 'o', 'sā', and 'sā' respectively.

Manaṃ[M 0.0079], mano, mane, manena, manasā, manehi, manebhi, manassa, manaso, manānaṃ, manasmā, manamhā, manasā, manā, manehi, manebhi, manassa, manaso, manānaṃ, manasmiṃ, manamhi, manasi, mane, manesu.

The forms are: manaṃ, mano, mane, manena, manasā, manehi, manebhi, manassa, manaso, manānaṃ, manasmā, manamhā, manasā, manā, manehi, manebhi, manassa, manaso, manānaṃ, manasmiṃ, manamhi, manasi, mane, manesu.

Tamo, tapo, tejo, siro, uro, vaco, rajo, ojo, ayo, payo, vayo, saro, yaso, ceto, chando, radhatā, aho iccādi manogaṇo.

Tamo (darkness), tapo (austerity), tejo (energy), siro (head), uro (chest), vaco (speech), rajo (dust), ojo (vigor), ayo (iron), payo (milk), vayo (age), saro (lake), yaso (fame), ceto (mind), chando (intention), radhas (success), aho (day), etc., belong to the 'manas' group.

Idaṃ manogaṇalakkhaṇaṃ. Kriyākamme odanto, nādīnaṃ sāditā, samāsataddhitamajjhe odanto cāti.

This is the characteristic of the 'manas' group: ending in 'o' in the nominative and accusative cases; taking 'sā' and other such substitutes for 'nā' and other case endings; and ending in 'o' in the middle of compounds and derivatives.

Yo ve dassanti vatvāna, adāne kurute mano jā. 1.15.61, kassapassa vaco sutvā, tapo idha pakrubbati saṃ. ni. 1.204, ceto paricca jānāti dī. ni. 1.242, siro te bādhayissāmi iccādi.

Examples: 'Yo ve dassanti vatvāna, adāne kurute mano' (He who, having said 'I will give,' sets his mind on not giving); 'kassapassa vaco sutvā, tapo idha pakrubbati' (Having heard Kassapa's word, one undertakes austerity here); 'ceto paricca jānāti' (he knows their mind completely); 'siro te bādhayissāmi' (I will split your head), and so on.

Manasā ce pasannena dha. pa. 2, vippasannena cetasā jā. 2.22.551, vacasā manasā ceva, vandā me te tathāgate parittapāḷi āṭānāṭiyasutta. Ekūnatiṃso vayasā dī. ni. 2.214, tejasā yasasā jalaṃ vi. va. 857, tapasā uttamo satto, ghatena vā bhuñjassu payasā vā, vandāmi sirasā pāde jā. 2.20.68, ye etā upasevanti, chandasā vā dhanena vā jā. 2.21.350, urasā panudissāmi jā. 2.22.1833, ayasā paṭikujjhito a. ni. 3.36 iccādi.

Examples: 'Manasā ce pasannena' (with a confident mind); 'vippasannena cetasā' (with a very clear mind); 'vacasā manasā ceva, vandā me te tathāgate' (with speech and mind I worship those Tathāgatas); 'Ekūnatiṃso vayasā' (being twenty-nine in age); 'tejasā yasasā jalaṃ' (blazing with energy and fame); 'tapasā uttamo satto' (a being supreme through austerity); 'ghatena vā bhuñjassu payasā vā' (eat either with ghee or with milk); 'vandāmi sirasā pāde' (I bow with my head to the feet); 'ye etā upasevanti, chandasā vā dhanena vā' (those who attend on them, either with intention or with wealth); 'urasā panudissāmi' (I will push away with my chest); 'ayasā paṭikujjhito' (covered with iron), and so on.

Na mayhaṃ manaso piyo jā. 1.10.11, cetaso parivitakko udapādi pārā. 18, cetaso samannāhāro, sādhu khalu payaso pānaṃ, sāvittī chandaso mukhaṃ ma. ni. 2.400 iccādi.

Examples: 'Na mayhaṃ manaso piyo' (Not dear to my mind); 'cetaso parivitakko udapādi' (a reflection of the mind arose); 'cetaso samannāhāro' (an application of mind); 'sādhu khalu payaso pānaṃ' (good indeed is the drinking of milk); 'sāvittī chandaso mukhaṃ' (the Sāvittī is the chief of meters), and so on.

Sādhukaṃ [M 0.0080] manasi karotha dī. ni. 2.3, etamatthaṃ cetasi sannidhāya, sirasi añjaliṃ katvā apa. thera 1.41.82, urasilomo, pāpaṃ akāsi rahasi iccādi.

Examples: 'Sādhukaṃ manasi karotha' (Pay close attention); 'etamatthaṃ cetasi sannidhāya' (having placed this meaning in mind); 'sirasi añjaliṃ katvā' (having placed the joined palms on the head); 'urasilomo' (chest-hair); 'pāpaṃ akāsi rahasi' (he did evil in secret), and so on.

Manodhātu, manomayaṃ, tamokhandhaṃ padālayi, tapodhano, tejodhātu, siroruhā kesā, saroruhaṃ padumaṃ, rajoharaṇaṃ vatthaṃ, ojoharaṇā sākhā, ayopatto, vayoguṇā anupubbaṃ jahanti, yasodharā devī, cetoyuttā dhammā, chandovicitipakaraṇaṃ, rahogato cintesi, ahorattānamaccaye saṃ. ni. 1.112 iccādi.

Examples of compounds: manodhātu (mind-element), manomayaṃ (mind-made), tamokhandhaṃ padālayi (he dispelled the mass of darkness), tapodhano (rich in austerity), tejodhātu (fire-element), siroruhā kesā (head-growths, i.e., hair), saroruhaṃ padumaṃ (lake-grown, i.e., a lotus), rajoharaṇaṃ vatthaṃ (a dust-removing cloth), ojoharaṇā sākhā (a vigor-removing branch), ayopatto (an iron bowl), vayoguṇā anupubbaṃ jahanti (the qualities of age gradually depart), yasodharā devī (Queen Yasodharā), cetoyuttā dhammā (phenomena associated with mind), chandovicitipakaraṇaṃ (a treatise on the analysis of meters), rahogato cintesi (having gone to a solitary place, he thought), ahorattānamaccaye (at the passing of day and night), and so on.

Mahāvuttinā ahamhā smiṃno ni ca u ca hoti, tadahani, tadahu. Rahamhā smiṃno o hoti, mātugāmena saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisīdati pārā. 452, raho tiṭṭhati, raho manteti.

According to the Mahāvutti, after 'ahan' (day), the locative ending 'smiṃ' becomes 'ni' and 'u'; for example, 'tadahani' (on that day), 'tadahu' (on that day). After 'rahas' (solitude), the locative ending 'smiṃ' becomes 'o'; for example, 'mātugāmena saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisīdati' (a man sits in solitude alone with a woman), 'raho tiṭṭhati' (he stands in solitude), 'raho manteti' (he consults in solitude).

Manogaṇarāsi niṭṭhito.

The section on the 'manas' group is finished.

Manādigaṇarāsi

The Section on the Group of Words beginning with 'manas'

116. Kodhādīhi.

116. After 'kodha' and so forth.

Etehi nāvacanassa sā hoti vā.

After these, 'sā' is optionally the substitute for the instrumental ending 'nā'.

Kodhasā, kodhena, atthasā, atthena.

Kodhasā, kodhena (by wrath); atthasā, atthena (by benefit).

117. Nāssa sā ka. 181; rū. 95; nī. 373.

117. For 'nā', 'sā'.

Padādīhi nāvacanassa sā hoti vā.

After 'pada' and so forth, 'sā' is optionally the substitute for the instrumental ending 'nā'.

Padasā, padena, bilasā, bilena.

Padasā, padena (by foot); bilasā, bilena (by hole).

118. Padādīhi [M 0.0081] si.

118. After 'pada' and so forth, 'si'.

Padādīhi smiṃno si hoti vā.

After 'pada' and so forth, 'si' is optionally the substitute for 'smiṃ'.

Padasi, pade, bilasi, bile.

Padasi, pade (in the foot); bilasi, bile (in the hole).

Tattha kodhādiko pulliṅgo, padādiko napuṃsako. Tattha keci saddā samāsa, taddhitamajjhe odantā honti ka. 183; rū. 48; nī. 375, āpodhātu, āpomayaṃ, vāyodhātu, vāyomayaṃ, jīva tvaṃ saradosataṃ jā. 1.2.9, anuyanti disodisaṃ dī. ni. 3.281 iccādi.

Herein, the 'kodha' group is masculine, and the 'pada' group is neuter. Among these, some words end in 'o' in the middle of compounds and derivatives, such as: āpodhātu, āpomayaṃ, vāyodhātu, vāyomayaṃ, jīva tvaṃ saradosataṃ, anuyanti disodisaṃ, and so forth.

Keci nāssa sādesaṃ labhanti, kodhasā usunā vijjhi jā. 2.22.352, daḷhaṃ gaṇhāhi thāmasā jā. 1.7.30, padasāva agamāsi, mākāsi mukhasā pāpaṃ, saccena danto damasā upeto-damasāti indriyadamanena, suciṃ paṇītaṃ rasasā upetaṃ jā. 1.7.18, vegasā gantvāna, āyusā ekaputtamanurakkhe khu. pā. 9.7 iccādi.

Some obtain the 'sā' substitution for the instrumental ending 'nā', as in: kodhasā usunā vijjhi (pierced by the arrow of anger); daḷhaṃ gaṇhāhi thāmasā (grasp firmly with strength); padasāva agamāsi (he went just by foot); mākāsi mukhasā pāpaṃ (do not commit evil by speech); saccena danto damasā upeto (restrained by truth, endowed with self-control)—damasā means by restraint of the senses; suciṃ paṇītaṃ rasasā upetaṃ (pure and excellent, endowed with flavor); vegasā gantvāna (having gone swiftly); āyusā ekaputtamanurakkhe (may one protect one's only son with one's life), and so forth.

Keci smiṃno syādesaṃ labhanti, padasi, bilasi iccādi.

Some obtain the 'si' substitution for 'smiṃ', as in padasi, bilasi, and so forth.

Kehici mahāvuttinā nā, smānaṃ so hoti, atthaso, akkharaso, suttaso, byañjanaso, hetuso, yoniso, upāyaso, ṭhānaso, dīghaso, oraso, bahuso, puthuso, mattaso, bhāgaso iccādi.

According to some grammarians and the Mahāvutti, 'so' becomes the substitute for the instrumental ('nā') and ablative ('smā') endings, as in: atthaso (by meaning), akkharaso (by letter), suttaso (by discourse), byañjanaso (by expression), hetuso (by cause), yoniso (by origin), upāyaso (by means), ṭhānaso (by place), dīghaso (by length), oraso (by lineage), bahuso (by quantity), puthuso (by diversity), mattaso (by measure), bhāgaso (by portion), and so forth.

“Padaso dhammaṃ vāceyya pāci. 45, bilaso vibhajitvā nisinno assa” dī. ni. 2.378 iccādīsu pana vicchāyaṃ sopaccayo.

However, in phrases like 'padaso dhammaṃ vāceyya' (one should recite the Dhamma word by word) and 'bilaso vibhajitvā nisinno assa' (having divided into portions, one should sit), the suffix 'so' is used in the sense of distribution.

Yadā pana samāsante mahāvuttinā syādīsu vibhattīsu sāgamo hoti, tadā purisādigaṇopi hoti, byāsattamanaso, abyaggamanaso a. ni. 3.29, putto jāto acetaso jā. 2.22.4, sumedhaso a. ni. 4.62, bhūrimedhaso su. ni. 1137 iccādi.

However, when at the end of a compound, according to the Mahāvutti, the augment 'sa' occurs before 'si' and other case endings, then they are also treated as belonging to the 'purisa' group, as in: byāsattamanaso (of one with a distracted mind), abyaggamanaso (of one with an undistracted mind), putto jāto acetaso (a son was born to one without intelligence), sumedhaso (of one with good wisdom), bhūrimedhaso (of one with great wisdom), and so forth.

Iti manādigaṇarāsi.

Thus ends the section on the group of words beginning with 'manas'.

Guṇavādigaṇarāsi

The group of words beginning with guṇavā.

119. Ntussa ka. 124; rū. 98; nī. 299.

119. Of ntu.

Simhi [M 0.0082] ntussa ṭā hoti.

When si follows, ṭā is substituted for ntu.

Guṇavā tiṭṭhati.

Guṇavā stands.

120. Yvādo ntussa ka. 92; rū. 100; nī. 249.

120. Of ntu, when yo and so forth follow.

Yoādīsu ntussa attaṃ hoti.

When yo and so forth follow, atta is substituted for ntu.

Guṇavantā tiṭṭhanti.

Guṇavantā stand.

121. Ntantūnaṃ nto yomhi paṭhame ka. 92; rū. 100; nī. 249.

121. Of nta and ntu, nto for the nominative yo.

Paṭhame yomhi savibhattīnaṃ nta, ntūnaṃ nto hoti.

When the nominative yo follows, nto is substituted for the inflected stems ending in nta and ntu.

Guṇavanto tiṭṭhanti.

Guṇavanto stand.

122. Ṭaṭāaṃ ge ka. 126; rū. 101; nī. 301-2.

122. Ṭa, ṭā, and aṃ for the vocative singular.

Ge pare savibhattīnaṃ nta, ntūnaṃ ṭa, ṭā, aṃ honti.

When the vocative singular follows, ṭa, ṭā, and aṃ are substituted for the inflected stems ending in nta and ntu.

Bho guṇava, bho guṇavā, bho guṇavaṃ, bhonto guṇavantā, bhonto guṇavanto, guṇavantaṃ, guṇavante, guṇavantena.

Bho guṇava, bho guṇavā, bho guṇavaṃ, bhonto guṇavantā, bhonto guṇavanto, guṇavantaṃ, guṇavante, guṇavantena.

123. Totātitā sasmāsmiṃnāsu ka. 127, 187; rū. 102, 108; nī. 303, 386.

123. To, tā, ti, tā for sa, smā, smiṃ, and nā.

Sa, smā, smiṃ, nāsu savibhattīnaṃ nta, ntūnaṃ kamena to, tā,ti, tā honti vā.

When sa, smā, smiṃ, and nā follow, to, tā, ti, and tā are optionally substituted respectively for the inflected stems ending in nta and ntu.

Guṇavatā, guṇavantehi, guṇavantebhi, guṇavantassa, guṇavato.

Guṇavatā, guṇavantehi, guṇavantebhi, guṇavantassa, guṇavato.

124. Naṃmhi [M 0.0083] taṃ vā ka. 128; rū. 104; nī. 304.

124. When naṃ follows, taṃ optionally.

Naṃmhi savibhattīnaṃ nta, ntūnaṃ taṃ hoti vā.

When naṃ follows, taṃ is optionally substituted for the inflected stems ending in nta and ntu.

Guṇavantānaṃ, guṇavataṃ, guṇavantasmā, guṇavantamhā, guṇavantā, guṇavatā, guṇavantehi, guṇavantebhi, guṇavantassa, guṇavato, guṇavantānaṃ, guṇavataṃ, guṇavantasmiṃ, guṇavantamhi, guṇavati, guṇavante, guṇavantesu.

Guṇavantānaṃ, guṇavataṃ, guṇavantasmā, guṇavantamhā, guṇavantā, guṇavatā, guṇavantehi, guṇavantebhi, guṇavantassa, guṇavato, guṇavantānaṃ, guṇavataṃ, guṇavantasmiṃ, guṇavantamhi, guṇavati, guṇavante, guṇavantesu.

Evaṃ bhagavā, sīlavā, paññavā, balavā, dhanavā, vaṇṇavā, bhogavā, sutavā iccādi. Ettha ca ālapane bhagavāti niccaṃ dīgho.

Thus, bhagavā, sīlavā, paññavā, balavā, dhanavā, vaṇṇavā, bhogavā, sutavā, and so forth. And here, in the vocative, the form bhagavā is always long.

Sabbāvā, sabbāvanto, sabbāvantaṃ, sabbāvante, sabbāvantena, sabbāvatā, sabbāvantehi…pe… sabbāvantesu.

Sabbāvā, sabbāvanto, sabbāvantaṃ, sabbāvante, sabbāvantena, sabbāvatā, sabbāvantehi… and so on… sabbāvantesu.

Evaṃ yāvā, yāvanto, tāvā, tāvanto, ettāvā, ettāvanto, kiṃvā, kiṃvanto, kittāvā, kittāvanto iccādi. Tathā bhojanaṃ bhuttavā, bhuttavanto, dhammaṃ buddhavā, buddhavanto, kammaṃ katavā, katavanto iccādi ca.

Thus, yāvā, yāvanto, tāvā, tāvanto, ettāvā, ettāvanto, kiṃvā, kiṃvanto, kittāvā, kittāvanto, and so forth. Likewise, bhojanaṃ bhuttavā, bhuttavanto; dhammaṃ buddhavā, buddhavanto; kammaṃ katavā, katavanto, and so forth.

Satimā, satimantā, satimanto, bho satima, bho satimā, bho satimaṃ, bhonto satimantā, bhonto satimanto, satimantaṃ, satimante, satimantena, satimatā, satimantehi, satimantebhi, satimantassa, satimato, satimantānaṃ, satimataṃ, satimantasmā, satimantamhā, satimantā, satimatā, satimantehi, satimantebhi, satimantassa, satimato, satimantānaṃ, satimataṃ, satimantasmiṃ, satimantamhi, satimati, satimante, satimantesu.

Satimā, satimantā, satimanto, bho satima, bho satimā, bho satimaṃ, bhonto satimantā, bhonto satimanto, satimantaṃ, satimante, satimantena, satimatā, satimantehi, satimantebhi, satimantassa, satimato, satimantānaṃ, satimataṃ, satimantasmā, satimantamhā, satimantā, satimatā, satimantehi, satimantebhi, satimantassa, satimato, satimantānaṃ, satimataṃ, satimantasmiṃ, satimantamhi, satimati, satimante, satimantesu.

Evaṃ matimā, gatimā, pāpimā, jātimā, bhāṇumā, āyumā, āyasmā, sirimā, hirimā, dhitimā, kittimā, iddhimā, jutimā[M 0.0084], mutimā, thutimā, buddhimā, cakkhumā, bandhumā, gomā iccādi.

Thus, matimā, gatimā, pāpimā, jātimā, bhāṇumā, āyumā, āyasmā, sirimā, hirimā, dhitimā, kittimā, iddhimā, jutimā, mutimā, thutimā, buddhimā, cakkhumā, bandhumā, gomā, and so forth.

Visesavidhānamuccate.

A special rule is stated.

125. Himavato vā o ka. 94; rū. 105; nī. 252.

125. Of himavanta, o optionally.

Simhi himavantasaddassa o hoti vā. ‘Gasīna’nti lopo.

When si follows, o is optionally substituted for the word himavanta. Elision is by the rule 'Gasīnaṃ'.

Himavanto pabbato dha. pa. 304, himavā pabbato.

Himavanto pabbato, himavā pabbato.

126. Ntassa ca ṭa vaṃse ka. 93; rū. 106; nī. 251.

126. And ṭa for nta in the sense of lineage.

Aṃ, sesu ntassa ca ntussa ca sabbassa ṭa hoti vā.

When aṃ and the remaining case endings follow, ṭa is optionally substituted for the entirety of nta and ntu.

“Ajjhogāhetvā himava”nti apa. thera 2.47.59 pāḷi. Satimaṃ, bandhumaṃ, guṇavassa, satimassa, bandhumassa.

The Pāli text is: 'Ajjhogāhetvā himava'. Satimaṃ, bandhumaṃ, guṇavassa, satimassa, bandhumassa.

Mahāvuttinā kvaci simhi ge ca pare ntussa attaṃ hoti, “atulo nāma nāmena, paññavanto jutindharo”ti bu. vaṃ. 21.10 ca “gatimanto satimanto, dhitimanto ca yo isī”ti theragā. 1052 ca “cakkhumanto mahāyaso”ti ca “tuyhaṃ pitā mahāvīra, paññavanta jutindharā”ti apa. therī 2.2.389 ca pāḷī.

According to the Mahāvutti, sometimes when si or ge follow, attaṃ is the substitute for ntu, as in the Pāli texts: 'atulo nāma nāmena, paññavanto jutindharo'; 'gatimanto satimanto, dhitimanto ca yo isī'; 'cakkhumanto mahāyaso'; and 'tuyhaṃ pitā mahāvīra, paññavanta jutindharā'.

Paṭhamāyomhi kvaci ntussa ṭa hoti, vaggumudātīriyā pana bhikkhū vaṇṇavā honti pārā. 194, etha tumhe āvuso sīlavā hotha a. ni. 5.114, cakkhumā andhakā honti, ye itthīnaṃ vasaṃ gatā jā. aṭṭha. 2.3.36, saṃsuddhapaññā kusalā mutimā bhavanti su. ni. 887 (saṃsuddhapaññā kusalā mutīmā).

Sometimes in the nominative plural (yo), ā (ṭa) occurs for ntu, as in: 'vaggumudātīriyā pana bhikkhū vaṇṇavā honti' (But the monks on the banks of the Vaggumudā are eloquent); 'etha tumhe āvuso sīlavā hotha' (Come, friends, be virtuous); 'cakkhumā andhakā honti, ye itthīnaṃ vasaṃ gatā' (Those with eyes become blind, who fall under the sway of women); 'saṃsuddhapaññā kusalā mutimā bhavanti' (Those of purified wisdom, the skilled, become insightful).

Iti guṇavādigaṇarāsi.

Thus the group beginning with guṇavā.

Gacchantādigaṇarāsi

The group beginning with gacchant.

127. Ntassaṃ simhi ka. 186; rū. 107; nī. 382-4; ‘tassaṃ’ (bahūsu).

127. For nta, aṃ in the nominative singular.

Simhi [M 0.0085] ntassa aṃ hoti vā. Silopo.

In the nominative singular (si), nta optionally becomes aṃ. Elision of si.

Gacchaṃ, gacchanto, gacchantā, gacchanto, bho gaccha, bho gacchā, bho gacchaṃ, bhonto gacchantā, bhonto gacchanto, gacchantaṃ, gacchante, gacchantena, gacchatā, gacchantehi, gacchantebhi, gacchantassa, gacchato, gacchantānaṃ, gacchataṃ, gacchantasmā, gacchantamhā, gacchantā, gacchatā, gacchantehi, gacchantebhi, gacchantassa, gacchato, gacchantānaṃ, gacchataṃ, gacchantasmiṃ, gacchantamhi, gacchati, gacchante, gacchantesu.

Gacchaṃ, gacchanto, gacchantā, gacchanto, bho gaccha, bho gacchā, bho gacchaṃ, bhonto gacchantā, bhonto gacchanto, gacchantaṃ, gacchante, gacchantena, gacchatā, gacchantehi, gacchantebhi, gacchantassa, gacchato, gacchantānaṃ, gacchataṃ, gacchantasmā, gacchantamhā, gacchantā, gacchatā, gacchantehi, gacchantebhi, gacchantassa, gacchato, gacchantānaṃ, gacchataṃ, gacchantasmiṃ, gacchantamhi, gacchati, gacchante, gacchantesu.

Evaṃ karaṃ, kubbaṃ, caraṃ, cavaṃ, jayaṃ, jahaṃ, jānaṃ, jiraṃ, dadaṃ, dahaṃ, juhaṃ, suṇaṃ, pacaṃ, saraṃ, bhuñjaṃ, muñcaṃ, sayaṃ, saraṃ, haraṃ, tiṭṭhaṃ, bhavissaṃ, karissaṃ, gamissaṃ iccādi.

Thus: karaṃ (doing), kubbaṃ (making), caraṃ (walking), cavaṃ (departing), jayaṃ (conquering), jahaṃ (abandoning), jānaṃ (knowing), jiraṃ (decaying), dadaṃ (giving), dahaṃ (burning), juhaṃ (offering), suṇaṃ (hearing), pacaṃ (cooking), saraṃ (remembering), bhuñjaṃ (eating), muñcaṃ (releasing), sayaṃ (lying down), saraṃ (remembering), haraṃ (carrying), tiṭṭhaṃ (standing), bhavissaṃ (who will be), karissaṃ (who will do), gamissaṃ (who will go), and so on.

Visesavidhānamuccate.

A special provision is stated.

‘Ntassa ca ṭa vaṃse’ti aṃ, sesu ntassa ṭattaṃ, yaṃ yañhi rāja bhajati, santaṃ vā yadi vā asaṃ. Sīlavantaṃ visīlaṃ vā, vasaṃ tasseva gacchati jā. 1.15.181. Kiccānukrubbassa kareyya kiccaṃ jā. 1.2.145 – anukrubbassāti puna karontassa.

By the rule 'Ntassa ca ṭa vaṃse', the substitution is aṃ; in the remaining cases, nta becomes ā (ṭa). 'Whatever a king associates with, be they virtuous or unvirtuous. Whether virtuous or unvirtuous, one comes under his sway.' 'One should do what is to be done for one who does it repeatedly'—here, anukrubbassa means 'for one who is doing again'.

Mahāvuttinā paṭhamāyomhi ca savibhattissa ntassa aṃ hoti, api nu tumhe ekantasukhaṃ lokaṃ jānaṃ passaṃ viharatha dī. ni. 1.425, kasaṃ khettaṃ bījaṃ vapaṃ, dhanaṃ vindanti māṇavā therīgā. 112, bharanti mātāpitaro, pubbe katamanussaraṃ a. ni. 5.39.

According to the Mahāvutti, also in the nominative plural, nta together with its case ending becomes aṃ. 'But do you, knowing and seeing, dwell in a world of exclusive happiness?' 'Cultivating the field and sowing seed, young men find wealth.' 'They support their parents, remembering what was done before.'

128. Mahantārahantānaṃ ṭā vā nī. 387, 712.

128. For mahant and arahant, ā (ṭā) optionally.

Simhi etesaṃ ntassa ṭā hoti vā.

In the nominative singular (si), for these, nta optionally becomes ā (ṭā).

Mahā[M 0.0086], mahaṃ, mahanto, mahantā, mahanto, bho maha, bho mahā, bho mahaṃ, bhonto mahantā, bhonto mahanto, mahantaṃ.

Mahā, mahaṃ, mahanto, mahantā, mahanto, bho maha, bho mahā, bho mahaṃ, bhonto mahantā, bhonto mahanto, mahantaṃ.

‘Ntassa ca ṭa vaṃse’ti aṃmhi ntassa ṭattaṃ, “sumahaṃ puraṃ, parikkhipissa”nti jā. 2.22.792 pāḷi-suṭṭhu mahantaṃ bārāṇasipuranti attho. Sesaṃ gacchantasamaṃ.

By the rule 'Ntassa ca ṭa vaṃse', in the accusative singular (aṃ), nta becomes ā (ṭa). The Pāli text 'sumahaṃ puraṃ, parikkhipissaṃ' means 'a very great city, the city of Bārāṇasī'. The rest is like gacchant.

Arahā tiṭṭhati. ‘Ntassaṃ simhī’ti simhi ntassa aṃ, arahaṃ sugato loke saṃ. ni. 1.161, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho pārā. 1, arahantā, arahanto, arahantaṃ, arahante, arahantena, arahatā, arahantehi, arahantebhi, arahantassa, arahato, arahantānaṃ, arahataṃ iccādi.

The Arahant stands. By the rule 'Ntassaṃ simhi', in the nominative singular (si), nta becomes aṃ. Examples: 'arahaṃ sugato loke' (the Arahant, the Well-gone One in the world), 'arahaṃ sammāsambuddho' (the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One). The declensions are: arahantā, arahanto, arahantaṃ, arahante, arahantena, arahatā, arahantehi, arahantebhi, arahantassa, arahato, arahantānaṃ, arahataṃ, and so on.

Mahāvuttinā brahmantassa ca ntassa ṭā hoti simhi, brahā, brahanto, brahantā, brahanto, brahantaṃ, brahante iccādi.

According to the Mahāvutti, for the nta of brahmant, ā (ṭā) also occurs in the nominative singular (si). Examples: brahā, brahanto, brahantā, brahanto, brahantaṃ, brahante, and so on.

“Sā parisā mahā hoti, sā senā dissate mahā”ti jā. 2.22.771 ca “mahā bhante bhūmicālo”ti a. ni. 8.70 ca “mahā te upāsaka pariccāgo”ti jā. aṭṭha. 4.13.akittijātakavaṇṇanā ca “mahā me bhayamāgata”nti ca “bārāṇasirajjaṃ nāma mahā”ti jā. aṭṭha. 1.1.mahāsīlavajātakavaṇṇanā ca “mahāssa honti parivārā brāhmaṇagahapatikā, mahāssa honti parivārā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo”ti dī. ni. 3.204 ca “mahā vahanti dudiṭṭhiṃ, saṅkappā rāganissitā”ti ca pāḷī. Atra mahāsaddo nipātapaṭirūpakopi siyā.

The Pāli texts are: 'Sā parisā mahā hoti, sā senā dissate mahā' (That assembly is great, that army appears vast); 'mahā bhante bhūmicālo' (Great, venerable sir, is the earthquake); 'mahā te upāsaka pariccāgo' (Great, O lay follower, is your generosity); 'mahā me bhayamāgataṃ' (Great fear has come upon me); 'bārāṇasirajjaṃ nāma mahā' (The kingdom of Bārāṇasī is indeed great); 'mahāssa honti parivārā brāhmaṇagahapatikā, mahāssa honti parivārā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo' (Great are his retinues of brahmins and householders, great are his retinues of monks and nuns); and 'mahā vahanti dudiṭṭhiṃ, saṅkappā rāganissitā' (They carry great wrong views, thoughts rooted in lust). Here, the word mahā may also be in the form of a particle.

129. Bhūto.

129. From the root bhū.

Bhūdhātusiddhato ntassa aṃ hoti simhi. Suddhe niccaṃ, upapade aniccaṃ.

For a derivative from the root bhū, nta becomes aṃ in the nominative singular (si). When it is a simple word, this is obligatory; when it is in a compound, it is optional.

Bhavaṃ [M 0.0087] tiṭṭhati, sampattiṃ anubhavaṃ, anubhavanto, taṇhaṃ abhibhavaṃ, abhibhavanto, dukkhaṃ paribhavaṃ, paribhavanto tiṭṭhati, bhavantā, bhavanto, he bhavanta, he bhavantā, he bhavanto, he bhava, he bhavā, he bhavaṃ. “Kacci bhavaṃ abhiramasi araññe”ti jā. 2.18.18 pāḷi.

'Bhavaṃ tiṭṭhati' (The venerable one stands); 'sampattiṃ anubhavaṃ' (experiencing prosperity), or 'anubhavanto'; 'taṇhaṃ abhibhavaṃ' (overcoming craving), or 'abhibhavanto'; 'dukkhaṃ paribhavaṃ, paribhavanto tiṭṭhati' (he stands overcoming suffering). The forms are: bhavantā, bhavanto, he bhavanta, he bhavantā, he bhavanto, he bhava, he bhavā, he bhavaṃ. The Pāli text is: 'Kacci bhavaṃ abhiramasi araññe' (I trust, venerable sir, you delight in the forest?).

He bhavantā, he bhavanto, bhavantaṃ, bhavante, bhavantena, bhavatā, bhavantehi, bhavantebhi, bhavantassa, bhavato, bhavantānaṃ, bhavataṃ, bhavantasmā, bhavantamhā, bhavantā, bhavatā, bhavantehi, bhavantebhi, bhavantassa, bhavato, bhavantānaṃ, bhavataṃ, bhavantasmiṃ, bhavantamhi, bhavati, bhavante, bhavantesu.

He bhavantā, he bhavanto, bhavantaṃ, bhavante, bhavantena, bhavatā, bhavantehi, bhavantebhi, bhavantassa, bhavato, bhavantānaṃ, bhavataṃ, bhavantasmā, bhavantamhā, bhavantā, bhavatā, bhavantehi, bhavantebhi, bhavantassa, bhavato, bhavantānaṃ, bhavataṃ, bhavantasmiṃ, bhavantamhi, bhavati, bhavante, bhavantesu.

130. Bhavato vā bhonto gayonāse ka. 243; rū. 8, 110; nī. 484.

130. For bhavant, optionally bhonto before ga, yo, nā, se.

Ga, yo, nā, sesu bhavantassa bhonto hoti vā. Suttavibhattena aṃ, hi, naṃ, smādīsu ca.

Before the suffixes ga, yo, nā, and su, bhavant optionally becomes bhonto. And according to the Suttavibhatti, also before aṃ, hi, naṃ, smā, etc.

Bhontā, bhonto, he bhonta, he bhontā, he bhonto, bhontaṃ, bhonte, bhontena, bhotā, bhontehi, bhontebhi, bhontassa, bhoto, bhontānaṃ, bhotaṃ, bhontasmā, bhontamhā, bhontā, bhotā, bhontehi, bhontebhi, bhontassa, bhoto, bhontānaṃ, bhotaṃ, bhontasmiṃ, bhontamhi, bhoti, bhonte, bhontesu.

Bhontā, bhonto, he bhonta, he bhontā, he bhonto, bhontaṃ, bhonte, bhontena, bhotā, bhontehi, bhontebhi, bhontassa, bhoto, bhontānaṃ, bhotaṃ, bhontasmā, bhontamhā, bhontā, bhotā, bhontehi, bhontebhi, bhontassa, bhoto, bhontānaṃ, bhotaṃ, bhontasmiṃ, bhontamhi, bhoti, bhonte, bhontesu.

Bho, bhanteti dve vuddhiatthe siddhā āmantanatthe nipātā eva, tehi paraṃ ga, yonaṃ lopo, ito bho sugatiṃ gaccha itivu. 83, ummujjabho puthusile, kuto nu āgacchatha bho tayo janā jā. 1.9.87, passatha bho imaṃ kulaputtaṃ, ehi bhante khamāpehi, so te bhikkhū khamāpesi “khamatha bhante”ti. Tathā bhaddante, bhaddantāti dve “tuyhaṃ bhaddaṃ hotu[M 0.0088], tumhākaṃ bhaddaṃ hotū”ti atthe siddhā āmantananipātāva, “bhaddante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ saṃ. ni. 1.249, taṃ vo vadāmi bhaddante, yāvantettha samāgatā jā. 1.7.108. Bhaddanta, bhadantasaddā pana purisādigaṇikā eva.

The two words bho and bhante are particles established in the sense of prosperity and used in the vocative. After them, ga and yo are elided. Examples: 'ito bho sugatiṃ gaccha' (Go hence, sir, to a happy destiny); 'ummujjabho puthusile' (Rise up, sir of broad virtue); 'kuto nu āgacchatha bho tayo janā' (From where, sirs, have you three people come?); 'passatha bho imaṃ kulaputtaṃ' (Behold, sirs, this clansman); 'ehi bhante khamāpehi' (Come, venerable sir, ask for forgiveness); 'so te bhikkhū khamāpesi ‘‘khamatha bhante’’ti' (he had those monks ask for forgiveness, saying, 'Forgive us, venerable sirs'). Similarly, bhaddante and bhaddantā are two vocative particles established in the sense of 'May it be well with you'. Examples: '‘‘bhaddante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ' ('“Yes, venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One'); 'taṃ vo vadāmi bhaddante, yāvantettha samāgatā' (This I say to you, venerable sirs, all of you who are assembled here). The words bhaddanta and bhadanta, however, belong to the purisādi group.

Santasaddo pana sappurise vijjamāne samāne ca pavatto idha labbhati. Sameti asatā asaṃ jā. 1.2.16. Saṃ, santo, santā, santo, bhosanta, bhosantā, bhosa, bho sā, bho saṃ vā, bhonto santā, bhonto santo. Yaṃ yañhi rāja bhajati, santaṃ vā yadi vā asaṃ jā. 1.15.180. Sante, santena, satā.

The word santa, however, is found here used in the sense of a good person, one who is existing, and one who is tranquil. 'Sameti asatā asaṃ' (He associates with the bad, being bad himself). The forms are: Saṃ, santo, santā, santo, bhosanta, bhosantā, bhosa, bho sā, bho saṃ vā, bhonto santā, bhonto santo. 'Yaṃ yañhi rāja bhajati, santaṃ vā yadi vā asaṃ' (Whatever a king associates with, whether a good person or a bad one). Further forms: Sante, santena, satā.

131. Sato sabba bhe ka. 185; rū. 112; nī. 378.

131. For sant, sabba before bhi.

Bhe pare santassa sabaādeso hoti vā.

When bhi follows, sabba is optionally the substitute for sant.

Santehi, santebhi, sabbhi, santassa, sato, santānaṃ, sataṃ, santasmā, santamhā, santā, satā, santehi, santebhi, sabbhi, santassa, sato, santānaṃ, sataṃ, santasmiṃ, santamhi, sati, sante, santesu. Santo sappurisā loke, dūresanto pakāsenti dha. pa. 304, cattāro puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ a. ni. 4.85, pahusanto na bharati su. ni. 91.

Forms: Santehi, santebhi, sabbhi, santassa, sato, santānaṃ, sataṃ, santasmā, santamhā, santā, satā, santehi, santebhi, sabbhi, santassa, sato, santānaṃ, sataṃ, santasmiṃ, santamhi, sati, sante, santesu. Examples: 'Santo sappurisā loke, dūresanto pakāsenti' (Good people in the world shine from afar), 'cattāro puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ' (Four kinds of existing individuals are found in the world), 'pahusanto na bharati' (A capable person is not a burden).

Khede nirodhe ca pavatto santo purisādigaṇādiko, dīghaṃ santassa yojanaṃ dha. pa. 61, santā honti samitā niruddhā iccādi.

The word 'santa', occurring in the sense of 'kheda' (weariness) and 'nirodha' (cessation), belongs to the 'purisādi' group and so on. Examples: 'dīghaṃ santassa yojanaṃ' (Long is the journey for the weary), 'santā honti samitā niruddhā' (They are calmed, pacified, and ceased), and so on.

Iti gacchantādigaṇarāsi.

Thus ends the group beginning with 'gacchant'.

Rājādiyuvādigaṇarāsi

The class of words such as 'rājā' and 'yuva'.

132. Rājādiyuvādīhā ka. 189; rū. 113; nī. 390-1.

132. Rājādiyuvādīhā.

Rājādīhi [M 0.0089] yuvādīhi ca sissa ā hoti.

After words of the rājādi and yuvādi groups, the 'si' (nominative singular) ending becomes 'ā'.

Rājā gacchati.

The king goes.

133. Yonamāno ka. 190; rū. 114; nī. 392.

133. Yonamāno.

Rājādīhi yuvādīhi ca yonaṃ āno hoti vā.

After words of the rājādi and yuvādi groups, the endings 'yo' and 'naṃ' optionally become 'āno'.

Rājāno.

Kings.

Vāti kiṃ? Caturo ca mahārājā.

Why 'optionally'? [For the form:] 'Caturo ca mahārājā' (And the four Great Kings).

Bho rāja, bho rājā, bhonto rājāno.

O king, O king, O noble kings.

134. Vaṃmhānaṅ ka. 188; rū. 115; nī. 393.

134. Vaṃmhānaṅ.

Rājādīnaṃ yuvādīnañca ānaṅa hoti vā aṃmhi.

For words of the rājādi and yuvādi groups, the augment 'ānaṅ' optionally occurs before the endings 'aṃ' and 'mhi'.

Rājānaṃ, rājaṃ, rājāno, caturo ca mahārāje pe. va. 11.

The king, the king, the kings, and the four Great Kings.

135. Nāsmāsu raññā ka. 137, 270; rū. 116, 120; nī. 316, 542.

135. Nāsmāsu raññā.

Nā, smāsu rājassa raññā hoti vā.

For 'rājan', the form 'raññā' optionally occurs with the endings 'nā', 'smā', and 'su'.

Raññā, rājena.

By the king, by the king.

136. Rājassi nāmhi nī. 316.

136. Rājassi nāmhi.

Nāmhi rājassa i hoti.

For 'rājan', the augment 'i' occurs before the ending 'nā'.

Rājinā.

By the king.

137. Sunaṃhisvu ka. 169; rū. 117; nī. 357.

137. Sunaṃhisvu.

Su[M 0.0090], naṃ, hisu rājassa uhoti vā.

For 'rājan', the stem vowel optionally becomes 'u' before the endings 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hisu'.

Rājūhi, rājūbhi, rājehi, rājebhi.

By the kings, by the kings, by the kings, by the kings.

138. Raññoraññassarājino se ka. 139; rū. 118; nī. 314.

138. Raññoraññassarājino se.

Separe savibhattissa rājassa rañño, raññassa, rājino honti vā.

When the 'se' (genitive singular) ending follows, for 'rājan' together with its ending, the forms 'rañño', 'raññassa', and 'rājino' optionally occur.

Rañño, raññassa, rājino.

Of the king, of the king, of the king.

Vāti kiṃ? Rājassa.

Why 'optionally'? [For the form:] 'Rājassa'.

Rājūnaṃ, rājānaṃ.

Of kings, of kings.

139. Rājassa raññaṃ ka. 136; rū. 119; nī. 315.

139. Rājassa raññaṃ.

Naṃmhi rājassa raññaṃ hoti vā.

For the stem 'rāja', with the ending 'naṃ', the form is optionally 'raññaṃ'.

Raññaṃ, rājasmā, rājamhā, raññā, rājūhi, rājūbhi, rājehi, rājebhi, rañño, raññassa, rājino, rājassa vā, rājūnaṃ, rājānaṃ, raññaṃ.

Of the kings, from the king, from the king, by the king, by the kings, by the kings, by the kings, by the kings, of the king, of the king, of the king, or of the king, of the kings, of the kings, of the kings.

According to the Mahāvutti, for the stem 'rāja', the endings 'yo' (plural) and 'naṃ' become 'ino'. Pumunā, pumānehi, pumānebhi, pumehi, pumebhi, pumassa, pumuno, pumānaṃ, pumasmā, pumamhā, pumānā, pumunā, pumānehi, pumānebhi, pumehi, pumebhi, pumuno, pumassa, pumānaṃ, pumasmiṃ, pumamhi, pume.

Si[M 0.0097], yonaṃ purisādividhi ca hoti, “yathā balākayonimhi, na vijjati pumo sadā apa. thera 1.1.511, soḷasitthisahassānaṃ, na vijjati pumo tadā cariyā 3.49, itthī hutvā svajja pumomhi devo dī. ni. 2.354, thiyo tassa pajāyanti, na pumā jāyare kule”ti jā. 1.8.54 pāḷī.

For the case endings 'si' and 'yo', the procedure for 'purisa' and so on also applies. The Pāli text states: 'Just as in the womb of a crane, a male is not always found; among sixteen thousand women, a male was not found then; having been a woman, today I am a male god; daughters are born to him, males are not born in his family'.

Maghavasaddo yuvasaddasadisoti rūpasiddhiyaṃ rū. 66 vuttaṃ, guṇavādigaṇikoti saddanītiyaṃ nī. pada. 220 icchito. Aghanti dukkhaṃ pāpañca vuccati, na aghaṃ maghaṃ, sukhaṃ puññañca, magho iti purāṇaṃ nāmaṃ assa atthīti maghavāti saṃ. ni. 1.259 attho pāḷiyaṃ dissati.

The word 'maghavan' is similar to the word 'yuva', as stated in the Rūpasiddhi. In the Saddanīti, it is considered to belong to the 'guṇavādi' group. 'Agha' is said to mean suffering and evil. 'Magha' means not 'agha', but happiness and merit. The meaning 'maghavā' (one who has the ancient name 'Magha') is seen in the Pāḷi.

Thāmasaddo purisādigaṇo, thāmena, thāmunā, thāmassa, thāmuno, thāmasmā, thāmamhā, thāmā, thāmunā, thāmassa, thāmuno. Sesaṃ purisasamaṃ.

The word 'thāma' belongs to the 'purisa', etc., group. Examples are: thāmena, thāmunā, thāmassa, thāmuno, thāmasmā, thāmamhā, thāmā, thāmunā, thāmassa, thāmuno. The remaining forms are like those of 'purisa'.

Addhā vuccati kālo. Nādyekavacanesu-dīghena addhunā, addhanā, addhena, dīghassa addhuno, addhussa, addhassa, addhunā, addhumhā, addhusmā, addhā, addhamhā, addhasmā, addhuno, addhussa, addhassa, addhani, addhe, addhamhi, addhasminti cūḷamoggallāne āgataṃ. Sesaṃ yuvasadisaṃ.

'Addhan' is said to mean time. In the singular case endings beginning with 'nā', the forms found in the Cūḷamoggallāna are: dīghena addhunā, addhanā, addhena, dīghassa addhuno, addhussa, addhassa, addhunā, addhumhā, addhusmā, addhā, addhamhā, addhasmā, addhuno, addhussa, addhassa, addhani, addhe, addhamhi, addhasmiṃ. The remaining forms are similar to those of 'yuva'.

Upaddhavācako addhasaddo idha na labbhati, ekaṃsatthavācako ca nipāto eva. “Addhānamaggappaṭipanno”tiādīsu addhānasaddo pana visuṃ siddho napuṃsakaliṅgova.

The word 'addha' denoting misfortune is not taken here; the one expressing certainty is merely a particle. However, in phrases such as 'addhānamaggappaṭipanno', the word 'addhāna' is established separately and is of the neuter gender.

Muddhasadde “muddhā te phalatu sattadhā, muddhā me phalatu sattadhā” iccādīsu jā. 1.16.295; dha. pa. aṭṭha. 1.tissattheravatthu siro vuccati, “pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito” iccādīsu dī. ni. 2.70 matthakaṃ vuccati, tadubhayaṃ idha labbhati, smiṃvacane muddhanīti siddhaṃ, sesaṃ yuvasamaṃ. Bālavācako pana purisanayo. Hatthamuṭṭhivācako itthiliṅgo.

Regarding the word 'muddhan', in phrases like 'muddhā te phalatu sattadhā' and 'muddhā me phalatu sattadhā', it is said to mean 'head'. In phrases like 'pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito', it is said to mean 'summit'. Both meanings are taken here, and in the locative singular, 'muddhani' is established. The rest is similar to 'yuva'. However, the word denoting 'fool' follows the 'purisa' pattern. The word denoting 'fist' is of feminine gender.

Asmā vuccati pāsāṇo, usmā vuccati kāyaggi, bhismā vuccati bhayānako mahākāyo.

'Asman' is said to be stone, 'usman' is said to be bodily heat, and 'bhisman' is said to be that which is fearsome and of great body.

Tattha [M 0.0098] asmasadde “taṃ te paññāya bhindāmi, āmaṃ pakkaṃva asmanā su. ni. 445, mā tvaṃ cande khali asmanī”ti pāḷī. Sesaṃ yuvasamaṃ. Usmā, bhismāsaddāpi yuvasadisāti vadanti.

Regarding the word 'asman', the Pāḷi text is: 'taṃ te paññāya bhindāmi, āmaṃ pakkaṃva asmanā, mā tvaṃ cande khali asmanī'. The remaining forms are the same as for 'yuva'. It is said that the words 'usman' and 'bhisman' are also similar to 'yuva'.

Cūḷamoggallāne muddha, gāṇḍīvadhanva, aṇima, laghimādayo ca asmasadisāti vuttaṃ.

In the Cūḷamoggallāna, it is said that 'muddha', 'gāṇḍīvadhanva', 'aṇima', 'laghimā', and so forth are similar to 'asma'.

Yattha suttavidhānaṃ na dissati, tattha mahāvuttinā vā suttavibhattena vā rūpaṃ vidhiyati.

Where a rule of the sutta is not seen, the form is prescribed either by the Mahāvutti or by the Suttavibhatta.

Iti rājādiyuvādigaṇarāsi.

Thus ends the collection of groups beginning with 'rājā' and 'yuva'.

Akārantapulliṅgaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The masculine nouns ending in 'a' are concluded.

Ākārantapulliṅgarāsi

The collection of masculine nouns ending in 'ā'.

‘Gasīna’nti silopo, sā tiṭṭhati.

By the rule 'Gasīnaṃ', there is elision of 'si'; 'sā' remains.

‘Ekavacanayosvaghona’nti yosu ca ekavacanesu ca rasso, ‘ato yona’miccādinā vidhānaṃ, sā tiṭṭhanti.

By the rule 'Ekavacanayosvaghonaṃ', shortening occurs in the 'yo' endings and in the singular endings; by 'ato yonaṃ' and so forth, the rule applies, resulting in 'sā', as in 'sā tiṭṭhanti'.

163. Sāssaṃse cānaṅa.

163. For 'sā', in the 'aṃ' and 'se' endings, 'ānaṅa' is also substituted.

Aṃ, sesu ge ca sāsaddassa ānaṅa hoti.

For the word 'sā', the substitute 'ānaṅa' occurs in the 'aṃ' and 'se' endings, and also in the 'ge' ending.

Bho sāna, bhonto sā, saṃ, sānaṃ, se, sena, sāhi, sābhi, sassa, sānassa, sānaṃ, sasmā, samhā, sā, sāhi, sābhi, sassa, sānassa, sānaṃ, sasmiṃ, samhi, se, sāsu.

Bho sāna, bhonto sā, saṃ, sānaṃ, se, sena, sāhi, sābhi, sassa, sānassa, sānaṃ, sasmā, samhā, sā, sāhi, sābhi, sassa, sānassa, sānaṃ, sasmiṃ, samhi, se, sāsu.

Atha vā ‘sāssaṃse cānaṅa’iti sutte casaddo avuttasamuccayatthopi hotītikatvā sito sesāsu vibhattīsupi ānaṅa hoti vā, mahāvuttinā ca ānādesato yonaṃ o.

Alternatively, in the sutta 'sāssaṃse cānaṅa', because the word 'ca' also has the meaning of including what is unstated, the substitute 'ānaṅa' optionally occurs in the remaining inflections after 'si' as well. And by the Mahāvutti, from the 'āna' substitute, 'o' is substituted for 'yonaṃ'.

Sā [M 0.0099] gacchati, sāno gacchanti, sā vā, he sa, he sā, he sāna, he sā, he sāno, saṃ, sānaṃ, se, sāne iccādi.

Sā gacchati, sāno gacchanti, sā vā, he sa, he sā, he sāna, he sā, he sāno, saṃ, sānaṃ, se, sāne, and so forth.

Saddanītirūpaṃ vuccate –

The forms according to the Saddanīti are stated:

Sā tiṭṭhati, sā tiṭṭhanti, sāno tiṭṭhanti, bho sā, bhonto sā, sāno, sānaṃ, sāne, sānā, sānehi, sānebhi, sāssa, sānaṃ, sānā, sānehi, sānebhi, sāssa, sānaṃ, sāne, sānesūti nīti. pada. 211.

Sā tiṭṭhati, sā tiṭṭhanti, sāno tiṭṭhanti, bho sā, bhonto sā, sāno, sānaṃ, sāne, sānā, sānehi, sānebhi, sāssa, sānaṃ, sānā, sānehi, sānebhi, sāssa, sānaṃ, sāne, sānesūti.

Vattahā vuccati satto sakko (amarakosa, 1-145 gāthāyaṃ).

'Vattahā' is called a being.

164. Vattahā sanaṃnaṃ nonānaṃ.

164. For 'Vattahā', 'sa' and 'naṃ' become 'no' and 'nānaṃ'.

Vattahato sassa no hoti, naṃvacanassa nānaṃ hoti.

From 'vattahā', 'no' is substituted for 'sassa'; for the ending 'naṃ', 'nānaṃ' occurs.

Vattahāno deti, vattahānānaṃ deti. Sesaṃ yuvasaddasamaṃ.

Vattahāno deti, vattahānānaṃ deti. The rest is like the word 'yuva'.

Saddanītiyaṃ pana nā, sesu vattahinā, vattahinoti nīti. pada. 219; (tattha nāmhi vattahānāti dissati) vuttaṃ.

In the Saddanīti, however, it is said that for the 'nā' and 'se' endings, the forms are 'vattahinā' and 'vattahino'.

Daḷhadhammā, daḷhadhammā, daḷhadhammāno. “Sikkhitā daḷhadhammino”tipi saṃ. ni. 1.209 pāḷi. Bho daḷhadhammā, bhonto daḷhadhammā, daḷhadhammāno, daḷhadhammino, daḷhadhammānaṃ, daḷhadhammāne, daḷhadhamminā, daḷhadhammehi. Sesaṃ purisasamaṃ. Evaṃ paccakkhadhammāti. Vivaṭacchadasadde pana nāmhi ittaṃ natthi, sesaṃ daḷhadhammasamaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ pana “daḷhadhammoti vissuto”ti jā. 2.22.300 ca “loke vivaṭacchado”ti dī. ni. 1.258 ca diṭṭhattā ete saddā purisarūpā akārantāpi yujjanti.

Daḷhadhammā, daḷhadhammā, daḷhadhammāno. The Pāḷi also has 'Sikkhitā daḷhadhammino'. Bho daḷhadhammā, bhonto daḷhadhammā, daḷhadhammāno, daḷhadhammino, daḷhadhammānaṃ, daḷhadhammāne, daḷhadhamminā, daḷhadhammehi. The rest is like 'purisa'. Likewise for 'paccakkhadhammā'. For the word 'vivaṭacchada', however, the change to 'i' does not occur in the 'nā' ending; the rest is like 'daḷhadhamma'. In the Pāḷi, however, because 'daḷhadhammoti vissuto' and 'loke vivaṭacchado' are seen, these words are also suitable as masculine forms ending in 'a'.

Vuttasirā vuccati navavoropitakeso, vuttasirā brāhmaṇo, vuttasirā, vuttasirāno, vuttasirānaṃ, vuttasirāne, vuttasirānā, [M 0.0100] vuttasirānehi. Sesaṃ purisasamaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ pana “kāpaṭiko māṇavo vuttasiro”tipi ma. ni. 2.426 dissati.

'Vuttasirā' refers to one whose hair is newly shorn. Vuttasirā brāhmaṇo, vuttasirā, vuttasirāno, vuttasirānaṃ, vuttasirāne, vuttasirānā, vuttasirānehi. The rest is like 'purisa'. In the Pāḷi, however, 'kāpaṭiko māṇavo vuttasiro' is also seen.

Rahā vuccati pāpadhammo. Rahā, rahā, rahino, rahānaṃ, rahine, rahinā, rahinehi, rahinebhi, rahassa, rahino, rahānaṃ…pe… rahāne, rahānesūti nīti. pada. 217 sabbaṃ saddanītiyaṃ vuttaṃ, idha pana mahāvuttinā siddhaṃ.

'Rahā' is called an evil principle. Rahā, rahā, rahino, rahānaṃ, rahine, rahinā, rahinehi, rahinebhi, rahassa, rahino, rahānaṃ… and so forth… rahāne, rahānesūti—all this is stated in the Saddanīti, but here it is established by the Mahāvutti.

Iti ākārantapulliṅgarāsi.

Thus ends the collection of masculine nouns ending in 'ā'.

Ikārantapulliṅgarāsi

The collection of masculine nouns ending in 'i'.

‘Gasīna’nti lopo, muni gacchati.

By the rule 'Gasīnaṃ', there is elision; the sage goes.

165. Lopo ka. 118; rū. 146; nī. 293.

165. Elision.

Jha, lato yonaṃ lopo hoti. ‘Yolopanīsu dīgho’ti dīgho.

After 'jha' and 'la', elision of 'yo' occurs. By 'Yolopanīsu dīgho', lengthening occurs.

Munī gacchanti.

The sages go.

166. Yosu jhissa pume ka. 96; rū. 148; nī. 259.

166. In the 'yo' endings, of 'jhi', in the masculine.

Pulliṅge yosu jhasaññassa i-kārassa ṭa hoti vā.

In the masculine gender, in the 'yo' endings, 'ṭa' optionally replaces the i-vowel of that which has the designation 'jha'.

Munayo gacchanti.

The sages go.

Jhissāti kiṃ? Rattiyo, daṇḍino.

What are examples for 'jhi'? Nights, staff-bearers.

Pumeti kiṃ? Aṭṭhīni.

What is 'puma'? Bones.

Bho muni, ‘ayunaṃ vā dīgho’ti dīgho, bho munī, bhonto munī, bhonto munayo, muniṃ, munī, munayo, muninā, munīhi, munībhi, munissa, munino, munīnaṃ, munismā, munimhā.

O sage; by the rule 'ayunaṃ vā dīgho', there is lengthening; O sages, O sages, O sages; the sage, sages, sages; by the sage, by sages, by sages; of the sage, of the sage; of the sages; from the sage, from the sage.

167. Nā [M 0.0101] smāssa ka. 215; rū. 41; nī. 442.

167. 'Nā' is substituted for 'smā'.

Jha, lato smāssa nā hoti vā.

For a stem designated 'jha', 'nā' optionally occurs for 'smā'.

Muninā, munīhi, munībhi, munissa, munino, munīnaṃ, munismiṃ, munimhi, munīsu.

By the sage, by sages, by sages; of the sage, of the sage; of the sages; in the sage, in the sage; in the sages.

Isi gacchati, isī, isayo, bho isi, bho isī, bhonto isī, bhonto isayo iccādi.

The sage goes; sages, sages; O sage, O sages, O sages, O sages, and so on.

Aggi jalati, aggī, aggayo, bho aggi, bho aggī, bhonto aggī, bhonto aggayo iccādi.

The fire burns; fires, fires; O fire, O fires, O fires, O fires, and so on.

Evaṃ kucchi, muṭṭhi, gaṇṭhi, maṇi, pati, adhipati, gahapati, senāpati, narapati, yati, ñāti, sāti, vatthi, atithi, sārathi, bondi, ādi, upādi, nidhi, vidhi, odhi, byādhi, samādhi, udadhi, upadhi, nirupadhi, dhani, senāni, kapi, dīpi, kimi, timi, ari, hari, giri, kali, bali, sāli, añjali, kavi, ravi, asi, masi, kesi, pesi, rāsi, ahi, vīhiiccādayo.

Similarly: belly, fist, knot, jewel, lord, overlord, householder, general, king, ascetic, relative, attachment, bladder, guest, charioteer, body, beginning, clinging, treasure, method, limit, disease, concentration, ocean, substratum, without substratum, rich man, army leader, monkey, leopard, worm, fish, enemy, horse, mountain, strife, offering, rice, reverential salutation, poet, sun, sword, ink, hairy one, lump, heap, snake, rice, and so on.

Visesavidhānamuccate.

The special provision is stated.

Mahāvuttinā akatarassehipi kehici jhasaññehi yonaṃ no hoti, “cha munino agāramunino, anagāramunino, sekhamunino, asekhamunino, paccekamunino, munimunino”ti mahāni. 14 ca “ñāṇupapannā munino vadantī”ti ca “ekamekāya itthiyā, aṭṭhaṭṭha patino siyu”nti ca jā. 2.21.344 “patino kiramhākaṃ visiṭṭhanārīna” vi. va. 323 nti ca “haṃsādhipatino ime”ti jā. 2.21.38 ca suttapadāni dissanti.

According to the Mahāvutti, for some stems designated 'jha' which have not been shortened by certain grammarians, the plural ending 'yo' is not used; for example: 'the six sages: the householder sage, the homeless sage, the trainee sage, the adept sage, the solitary sage, the sage of sages,' and 'those endowed with knowledge speak of sages,' and 'for each woman, there may be eight husbands,' and 'indeed, our distinguished women have husbands,' and 'these are lords of swans'—such sutta passages are seen.

Gāthāsu ‘ghabrahmāditve’ti munito gassa ettañca hoti, porohicco tavaṃ mune apa. thera 1.1.540, dhammadasso tavaṃ mune apa. thera 1.1.540, ciraṃ [M 0.0102] jīva mahāvīra, kappaṃ tiṭṭha mahāmune apa. thera 1.2.168, paṭiggaṇha mahāmune apa. thera 1.41.83. Tuyhatthāya mahāmuneti apa. thera 1.3.345.

In verses, by the rule 'ghabrahmāditve', for 'muni', the vocative ending 'ga' also becomes 'e': 'You are a priest, O sage; you are a seer of Dhamma, O sage; live long, O great hero; endure for an aeon, O great sage; accept, O great sage; for your benefit, O great sage.'

Tehiyeva aṃvacanassa nañca hoti, tamāhu ekaṃ muninaṃ carantaṃ su. ni. 210, muninaṃ monapathesu sikkhamānaṃ jā. 1.8.44, pitaraṃ puttagiddhinaṃ jā. 2.22.2377, sabbakāmasamiddhinaṃ jā. 1.13.103.

By them alone, 'naṃ' also occurs for the accusative ending 'aṃ': 'They speak of that one wandering sage,' 'a sage training in the paths of silence,' 'a father greedy for sons,' 'one fulfilled in all desires.'

Isisadde pana –

Regarding the word 'isi'—

168. Ṭe sissisismā ṭe sissasmā (mūlapāṭhe).

168. 'Ṭe' occurs for 'si' and 'smiṃ' after 'isi'.

Isimhā sissa ṭe hoti vā.

From 'isi', 'ṭe' optionally occurs for the 'si' suffix.

Yo no’jja vinaye kaṅkhaṃ, atthadhammavidū ise jā. 2.22.1164. ‘Ghabrahmāditve’ti gassa ettañca hoti, nisīdāhi mahāise jā. 2.20.114, tvaṃ no’si saraṇaṃ ise jā. 2.22.1326, putto uppajjataṃ ise jā. 1.14.104.

'Who today might resolve our doubt in the Discipline, O seer, knower of meaning and Dhamma?' By the rule 'ghabrahmāditve', the vocative ending 'ga' also becomes 'e': 'Sit down, O great seer,' 'You are our refuge, O seer,' 'May a son be born, O seer.'

169. Dutiyassa yossa.

169. For the 'yo' of the second case.

Isimhā dutiyassa yossa ṭe hoti vā.

From 'isi', 'ṭe' optionally occurs for the 'yo' of the second case.

Samaṇe brāhmaṇe vande, sampannacaraṇe ise jā. 1.16.314.

I revere ascetics and Brahmins, seers who have attained perfect conduct.

Samāse pana mahesi gacchati, mahesī gacchanti, mahesayo, mahesino. Aṃvacane mahesinanti sijjhati. “Saṅgāyiṃsu mahesayo vi. va. ganthārambhakathā pe. va. ganthārambhakathā, vānamuttā mahesayo”ti abhidhammatthasaṅgahe 113 piṭṭhe ca “na taṃ sammaggatā yaññaṃ, upayanti mahesino, etaṃ sammaggatā yaññaṃ, upayanti mahesino saṃ. ni. 1.120, pahantā mahesino kāme, yena tiṇṇā mahesino”ti ca “mahesiṃ vijitāvina”nti ma. ni. 2.459 ca “saṅghañcāpi mahesinaṃ, kuñjaraṃva mahesinaṃ, upagantvā mahesinaṃ [M 0.0103] bu. vaṃ. 9.1, khippaṃ passa mahesinaṃ jā. 2.19.70, katakiccaṃ mahesina”nti jā. 2.19.102 ca suttapadāni dissanti.

In compounds, however: 'mahesi' goes; 'mahesī' go, 'mahesayo', 'mahesino'. In the accusative case, 'mahesinaṃ' is formed. 'The great seers chanted,' 'the great seers freed from craving,' and 'not to that sacrifice, rightly gone, do the great seers approach; to this sacrifice, rightly gone, do the great seers approach,' 'the great seers abandoning desires, by which the great seers have crossed over,' and 'the great seer, the conqueror,' and 'and also the Sangha of the great seers,' 'like an elephant, a great seer,' 'having approached a great seer,' 'quickly see a great seer,' 'a great seer who has done his duty'—such sutta passages are seen.

Aggisadde –

Regarding the word 'aggi'—

170. Sissaggito ni ka. 95; rū. 145; nī. 254; ‘sissāggito ni’ (bahūsu).

170. 'Ni' is substituted for 'si' after 'aggi'.

Aggito sissa ni hoti vā.

From 'aggi', 'ni' optionally occurs for the 'si' suffix.

Aggi jalati, aggini jalati, aggī jalanti, aggayo iccādi.
