The fire burns, the fire burns; the fires burn, fires, and so on.

Pāḷiyaṃ pana “aggi, gini, agginī”ti tayo aggipariyāyā dissanti – “rāgaggi, dosaggi, mohaggī”ti a. ni. 7.46 ca “channā kuṭi āhito gini, vivaṭā kuṭi nibbuto gini su. ni. 19, mahāgini sampajjalito theragā. 702 (thokaṃ visadisaṃ), yasmā so jāyate ginī”ti jā. 1.10.58 ca “agginiṃ sampajjalitaṃ pavisantī”ti su. ni. 675 ca. Tesaṃ visuṃ visuṃ rūpamālā labbhati.

In the Pāli canon, however, three synonyms for fire are found: 'aggi', 'gini', and 'agginī'—for example, 'the fire of lust, the fire of hatred, the fire of delusion,' and 'a thatched hut is ablaze with fire, an open hut has its fire extinguished, a great fire is blazing, from which that fire is born,' and 'entering the blazing fire.' For each of these, a distinct declension paradigm is found.

Seṭṭhi, pati, adhipati, senāpati, atithi, sārathisaddehi ca yonaṃ no hoti, aṃvacanassa naṃ hoti vā, seṭṭhino, seṭṭhinaṃ, patino, patinaṃ, adhipatino, adhipatinaṃ, senāpatino, senāpatinaṃ, atithino, atithinaṃ, sārathino, sārathinanti. Gahapatayo, jānipatayo iccādīni niccarūpāni dissanti.

From the words 'seṭṭhi', 'pati', 'adhipati', 'senāpati', 'atithi', and 'sārathi', the plural ending 'yo' is not used, and for the accusative plural, 'naṃ' optionally occurs: seṭṭhino, seṭṭhinaṃ; patino, patinaṃ; adhipatino, adhipatinaṃ; senāpatino, senāpatinaṃ; atithino, atithinaṃ; sārathino, sārathinaṃ. Forms like 'gahapatayo' (householders) and 'jānipatayo' (married couples) are seen as regular forms.

Ādisadde –

Regarding the word 'ādi'—

‘Ratthyādīhi ṭo smiṃno’ti smiṃno ṭo hoti, ādismiṃ, ādimhi, ādo, gāthādo, pādādo. “Ādiṃ, gāthādiṃ, pādādiṃ” iccādīsu pana ādhāratthe dutiyā eva “imaṃ rattiṃ, imaṃ divasaṃ, purimaṃ disaṃ, pacchimaṃ disaṃ, taṃ khaṇaṃ, taṃ layaṃ, taṃ muhuttaṃ” iccādīsu viya.

By the rule 'Ratthyādīhi ṭo smiṃno', 'ṭo' is substituted for the 'smiṃ' suffix: ādismiṃ, ādimhi, ādo, gāthādo, pādādo. But in cases like 'ādiṃ, gāthādiṃ, pādādiṃ,' the accusative is used in the sense of location, just as in 'imaṃ rattiṃ, imaṃ divasaṃ, purimaṃ disaṃ, pacchimaṃ disaṃ, taṃ khaṇaṃ, taṃ layaṃ, taṃ muhuttaṃ,' and so on.

Idāni samāse jhissa ṭādesābhāvo vuccati.

Now, the absence of the substitution ṭā for jhi in a compound is stated.

171. Itoññatthe [M 0.0104] pume.

171. From this [i-stem], in the masculine, in another sense.

Pume aññapadatthasamāse i-kāramhā paṭhamā, dutiyāyonaṃ kamena no, ne honti vā. Suttavibhattena uttarapadatthasamāsepi kvaci yonaṃ no, ne honti.

In a masculine compound where the meaning is that of another word, after an i-stem, for the 'yo' of the first and second cases, 'no' and 'ne' optionally occur, respectively. And by splitting the rule, sometimes also in a compound where the meaning of the latter word is prominent, 'no' and 'ne' occur for 'yo'.

Paṭhamāyomhi –

Regarding the 'yo' of the first case:

Micchādiṭṭhino, sammādiṭṭhino, muṭṭhassatino, upaṭṭhitassatino, asāre sāramatino dha. pa. 11, nimmānaratino devā, ye devā vasavattino saṃ. ni. 1.168, aṭṭhete cakkavattino, dhamme dhammānuvattino saṃ. ni. 5.34, saggaṃ sugatino yanti dha. pa. 126, tomara’ṅkusapāṇino jā. 2.22.223, daṇḍamuggarapāṇino, ariyavuttino, nipakā santavuttino iccādi.

Those of wrong view, those of right view, the unmindful, the mindful, those who perceive substance in the unsubstantial, the devas who delight in creation, the devas who wield power, these eight wheel-turning monarchs, those who follow the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, the well-gone ones go to heaven, those with spears and goads in hand, those with staffs and hammers in hand, those of noble conduct, the wise of peaceful conduct, etc.

Dutiyāyomhi –

Regarding the 'yo' of the second case:

Muṭṭhassatine, upaṭṭhitassatine, ariyavuttine, tomara’ṅkusapāṇine jā. 2.22.190 iccādi.

The unmindful, the mindful, those of noble conduct, those with spears and goads in hand, etc.

Vātveva? Micchādiṭṭhī janā gacchanti, micchādiṭṭhī jane passati.

Why 'optionally'? People of wrong view go; one sees people of wrong view.

Garū pana “tomara’ṅkusapāṇayo, atthe visāradamatayo”ti ka. 253 rūpāni idha icchanti.

The teachers, however, prefer forms here such as 'those with spears and goads in hand' and 'those whose minds are skilled in the meaning'.

Aññattheti kiṃ? Micchādiṭṭhiyo dhammā, micchādiṭṭhiyo dhamme.

Why 'in another sense'? [As in:] Wrong views are phenomena; (one sees) wrong views as phenomena.

Pumeti kiṃ? Micchādiṭṭhiniyo itthiyo, micchādiṭṭhīni kulāni.

Why 'in the masculine'? Women of wrong view; families of wrong view.

172. Ne smiṃno kvaci nī. 453.

172. For 'smiṃ', 'ne' sometimes.

Pume aññatthe ito smiṃno kvaci ne hoti.

In the masculine, in another sense, after an i-stem, for 'smiṃ', 'ne' sometimes occurs.

Kataññumhi ca posamhi, sīlavante ariyavuttine jā. 1.10.78. Sabbakāmasamiddhine kule, chattapāṇine, daṇḍapāṇine, tomara’ṅkusapāṇine jā. 2.22.190 iccādi.

And in the grateful man; in the virtuous one of noble conduct; in the family fulfilled with all desires; in one with an umbrella in hand; in one with a staff in hand; in one with a spear and goad in hand, etc.

Suttavibhattena [M 0.0105] ītopi smiṃno kvaci ne hoti, mātaṅgasmiṃ yasassine jā. 2.19.96, devavaṇṇine, brahmavaṇṇine, arahantamhi tādine theragā. 1182 iccādi.

By splitting the rule, 'ne' sometimes occurs for 'smiṃ' even after an ī-stem, as in: in Mātanga, the glorious one; in one of divine complexion; in one of Brahma-like complexion; in the Arahant, the such-like one, etc.

Ikārantapulliṅgarāsi niṭṭhito.

The section on masculine nouns ending in 'i' is completed.

Īkārantapulliṅgarāsi

The Section on Masculine Nouns Ending in 'ī'

Īkārante ‘simhi nā’napuṃsakassā’ti suttena simhi rassattaṃ natthi, ‘ge vā’ti ge pare vikappena rasso, yosu ca aṃ, nā, sa, smā, smiṃ su ca ‘ekavacanayosvaghona’nti niccaṃ rasso, daṇḍī gacchati. ‘Jantu hetu’ iccādisuttena vikappena yonaṃ lopo, daṇḍī gacchanti.

For an ī-ending noun, by the rule 'simhi nā’napuṃsakassa', there is no shortening before the 'si' suffix. By 'ge vā', when 'ge' follows, shortening is optional. And before 'yo', 'aṃ', 'nā', 'sa', 'smā', 'smiṃ', and 'su', by the rule 'ekavacanayosvaghona', there is always shortening; for example, 'daṇḍī gacchati' (the staff-bearer goes). By the rule 'jantu hetu', etc., there is optional elision of 'yo', as in 'daṇḍī gacchanti' (the staff-bearers go).

Pakkhe –

Alternatively:

173. Yonaṃ none pume ka. 225; rū. 151; nī. 452, 453.

173. For 'yo', 'no' and 'ne' in the masculine.

Pume jhasaññamhā ī-kārato paṭhamā, dutiyāyonaṃ kamena no, ne honti vā.

In the masculine, from a 'jha'-designated noun ending in 'ī', for the 'yo' of the first and second cases, 'no' and 'ne' optionally occur, respectively.

Daṇḍino gacchanti, bhodaṇḍi, bho daṇḍī, bhonto daṇḍino, daṇḍiṃ.

The staff-bearers go. O staff-bearer, O staff-bearer, O staff-bearers, the staff-bearer.

174. Naṃ jhīto ka. 224; rū. 153; nī. 451.

174. 'Naṃ' after a 'jha' ī-stem.

Pume jhasaññamhā ī-kārato aṃvacanassa naṃ hoti vā.

In the masculine, from a 'jha'-designated noun ending in 'ī', for the ending 'aṃ', 'naṃ' optionally occurs.

Daṇḍinaṃ.

daṇḍinaṃ

175. No vā ’no’ (bahūsu).

175. 'No' optionally.

Pume jhīto dutiyāyossa no hoti vā.

In the masculine, from a 'jha' ī-stem, for the 'yo' of the second case, 'no' optionally occurs.

Daṇḍī[M 0.0106], daṇḍino, daṇḍine, daṇḍinā, daṇḍīhi, daṇḍībhi, daṇḍissa, daṇḍino, daṇḍīnaṃ, daṇḍismā, daṇḍimhā, daṇḍinā, daṇḍīhi, daṇḍībhi, daṇḍissa, daṇḍino, daṇḍīnaṃ, daṇḍismiṃ, daṇḍimhi.

daṇḍī (nom. sg.), daṇḍino (nom. pl.; gen./dat. sg.), daṇḍine (acc. pl.), daṇḍinā (inst./abl. sg.), daṇḍīhi (inst./abl. pl.), daṇḍībhi (inst./abl. pl.), daṇḍissa (gen./dat. sg.), daṇḍino (gen./dat. sg.), daṇḍīnaṃ (gen./dat. pl.), daṇḍismā (abl. sg.), daṇḍimhā (abl. sg.), daṇḍinā (inst./abl. sg.), daṇḍīhi (inst./abl. pl.), daṇḍībhi (inst./abl. pl.), daṇḍissa (gen./dat. sg.), daṇḍino (gen./dat. sg.), daṇḍīnaṃ (gen./dat. pl.), daṇḍismiṃ (loc. sg.), daṇḍimhi (loc. sg.).

176. Smiṃno niṃ ka. 226; rū. 154; nī. 416.

176. For 'smiṃ', 'niṃ'.

Jhīto smiṃno ni hoti vā.

From a 'jha' ī-stem, for 'smiṃ', 'ni' optionally occurs.

Daṇḍini.

Daṇḍini.

‘Ne smiṃno kvacī’ti vibhattasuttena smiṃno ne ca hoti, daṇḍine, daṇḍīsu.

By the sutta on case-endings, ‘Ne smiṃno kvacī,’ the ending `smiṃ` also becomes `ne`. The forms are `daṇḍine`, `daṇḍīsu`.

Evaṃ cakkī, pakkhī, sukhī, sikhī, cāgī, bhāgī, bhogī, yogī, saṅghī, vācī, dhajī, bhajī, kuṭṭhī, raṭṭhī, dāṭhī, ñāṇī, pāṇī, gaṇī, guṇī, cammī, dhammī, sīghayāyī, pāpakārī, brahmacārī, māyāvī, medhāvī, bhuttāvī, bhayadassāvī, yasassī, tejassī, chattī, pattī, dantī, mantī, sattughātī, sīhanādī, sāmī, piyappasaṃsī. Atthadassī, dhammadassī iccādayo. Gāmaṇī, senānī, sudhī iccādīsu pana smiṃno nittaṃ natthi.

Likewise: Cakkī, Pakkhī, Sukhī, Sikhī, Cāgī, Bhāgī, Bhogī, Yogī, Saṅghī, Vācī, Dhajī, Bhajī, Kuṭṭhī, Raṭṭhī, Dāṭhī, Ñāṇī, Pāṇī, Gaṇī, Guṇī, Cammī, Dhammī, Sīghayāyī, Pāpakārī, Brahmacārī, Māyāvī, Medhāvī, Bhuttāvī, Bhayadassāvī, Yasassī, Tejassī, Chattī, Pattī, Dantī, Mantī, Sattughātī, Sīhanādī, Sāmī, Piyappasaṃsī, Atthadassī, Dhammadassī, and so on. In the cases of Gāmaṇī, Senānī, Sudhī, and so forth, however, there is no substitution of `ni` for `smiṃ`.

Visesavidhānamuccate.

A special provision is stated.

Mahāvuttinā yosu jhī-kārassapi kvaci ṭattaṃ hoti,

According to the Mahāvutti, before the `yo` endings, even the `ī`-vowel of a `jha`-class noun is sometimes substituted by `a`.

“Haṃsā koñcā mayūrā ca, hatthayo pasadā migā;

Sabbe sīhassa bhāyanti, natthi kāyasmiṃ tulyatā jā. 1.2.103.

“Swans, herons, and peacocks, elephants, spotted deer, and beasts; all fear the lion—there is no equality in physical form.”

Purisālū ca hatthayo, saññatā brahmacārayo a. ni. 6.37, apace brahmacārayo”ti dissanti. Tattha ‘hatthayo’ti hatthino, ‘purisālū’ti purisalolā balavāmukhayakkhiniyo, ‘brahmacārayo’ti brahmacārino, ‘apace’ti pūjeyya.

The forms `purisālū ca hatthayo`, `saññatā brahmacārayo`, and `apace brahmacārayo` are seen. Therein, `hatthayo` means `hatthino`; `purisālū` means 'powerful horse-faced yakkhiṇīs greedy for men'; `brahmacārayo` means `brahmacārino`; and `apace` means `pūjeyya` (one should honor).

Sussapi [M 0.0107] kvaci nesu hoti, susukhaṃ vata jīvāma, verinesu averino dha. pa. 197, verinesu manussesu, viharāma averino. Tattha ‘verinesū’ti verīcittavantesu.

Sometimes, for the ending `su`, the form `nesu` occurs. For example: ‘Happily indeed we live, free from hostility among the hostile. Among hostile people, we dwell free from hostility.’ Therein, `verinesu` means ‘among those with hostile minds’.

Samāsepi paṭhamāyossa nottaṃ, dutiyāyossa nottaṃ nettañca hoti. Tattha dve nottāni pākaṭāni. Nettaṃ pana vuccate, “assamaṇe samaṇamānine a. ni. 8.10, nare pāṇātipātine itivu. 93, mañjuke piyabhāṇine jā. 2.22.1721, māladhārine jā. 2.22.1727, kāsikuttamadhārine jā. 2.22.195, vaṇṇavante yasassine dī. ni. 2.282, cāpahatthe kalāpine, ubho bhassaravaṇṇine jā. 2.21.111, brāhmaṇe devavaṇḍine, samuddharati pāṇine apa. therī 2.3.137, evaṃ jarā ca maccu ca, adhivattanti pāṇine”ti saṃ. ni. 1.136 dissanti. Tattha ‘bhassaravaṇṇine’ti pabhassaravaṇṇavante. Smiṃno nette pana “mātaṅgasmiṃ yasassine” iccādīni jā. 2.19.96 pubbe vuttāneva.

Also in a compound, the nominative plural ending `yo` becomes `no`, and the accusative plural ending `yo` becomes `no` and also `ne`. Therein, the two substitutions to `no` are evident. The substitution to `ne`, however, is stated in the following: ‘non-ascetics who consider themselves ascetics,’ ‘men who destroy life,’ ‘charming ones who speak pleasantly,’ ‘wearers of garlands,’ ‘wearers of the finest Kāsi cloth,’ ‘the handsome and renowned,’ ‘those with bow in hand and quiver,’ ‘both of radiant complexion,’ ‘a brahmin who cheats the gods,’ ‘he rescues living beings,’ ‘thus do aging and death overcome living beings’—so are they seen. Therein, `bhassaravaṇṇine` means ‘one of radiant complexion.’ As for the substitution of `ne` for `smiṃ`, examples such as `mātaṅgasmiṃ yasassine` have already been stated before.

Īkārantapulliṅgarāsi niṭṭhito.

The section on masculine nouns ending in `ī` is concluded.

Ukārantapulliṅgarāsi

The Section on Masculine Nouns Ending in `u`

Bhikkhādigaṇarāsi

The Group Beginning with Bhikkhu

‘Gasīna’nti silopo, bhikkhu. Yonaṃ lope dīgho, bhikkhū.

By the sutta ‘Gasīnaṃ,’ there is elision of `si`, giving `bhikkhu`. Upon elision of `yo`, there is lengthening, giving `bhikkhū`.

Pakkhe –

Alternatively:

177. Lā yonaṃ vo pume ka. 119; rū. 155; nī. 294.

177. In the masculine, after a `la`-class noun, `yo` becomes `vo`.

Pume lasaññehi uvaṇṇehi yonaṃ vo hoti vāti yonaṃ vo.

In the masculine gender, after `la`-class nouns ending in the vowel `u`, the ending `yo` optionally becomes `vo`.

178. Vevosu [M 0.0108] lussa ka. 97; rū. 156; nī. 260.

178. Before `ve` and `vo`, the `u` of a `la`-class noun [becomes `a`].

Pume ve, vosu paresu lasaññassa u-kārassa ṭa hoti.

In the masculine gender, when `ve` or `vo` follow, the `u`-vowel of a `la`-class noun becomes `a`.

Bhikkhavo.

Bhikkhavo.

Lussāti kiṃ? Sayambhuvo.

Why specify `lussa`? [As a counter-example:] `Sayambhuvo`.

Bho bhikkhu, bho bhikkhū, bhonto bhikkhū.

O bhikkhu; O bhikkhus; O venerable bhikkhus.

179. Pumālapane vevo ka. 116; rū. 157; nī. 291.

179. In the masculine vocative, `ve` and `vo` [are used].

Pume ālapane lasaññamhā u-kārato yossa ve, vo honti vā.

In the masculine vocative, after a `la`-class noun ending in `u`, the ending `yo` optionally becomes `ve` or `vo`.

Bhonto bhikkhave, atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi “bhikkhavo”ti ma. ni. 1.1, devakāyā abhikkantā, te vijānātha bhikkhavo dī. ni. 2.334, bhikkhuṃ, bhikkhū, bhikkhavo, bhikkhunā. ‘Sunaṃhisū’ti dīgho, bhikkhūhi, bhikkhūbhi, bhikkhussa, bhikkhuno, bhikkhūnaṃ, bhikkhusmā, bhikkhumhā, bhikkhunā, bhikkhūhi, bhikkhūbhi, bhikkhussa, bhikkhuno, bhikkhūnaṃ, bhikkhusmiṃ, bhikkhumhi, bhikkhūsu.

‘Bhonto bhikkhave’ (O venerable bhikkhus). ‘Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus, saying, “Bhikkhavo.”’ ‘The hosts of devas have approached; recognize them, O bhikkhus.’ The forms are: `bhikkhuṃ`, `bhikkhū`, `bhikkhavo`, `bhikkhunā`. By the sutta ‘Sunaṃhisu,’ there is lengthening. The forms are: `bhikkhūhi`, `bhikkhūbhi`; `bhikkhussa`, `bhikkhuno`; `bhikkhūnaṃ`; `bhikkhusmā`, `bhikkhumhā`, `bhikkhunā`; `bhikkhūhi`, `bhikkhūbhi`; `bhikkhussa`, `bhikkhuno`; `bhikkhūnaṃ`; `bhikkhusmiṃ`, `bhikkhumhi`; `bhikkhūsu`.

Evaṃ maṅku, maccu, ucchu, paṭu, bhāṇu, setu, ketu, sattu, sindhu, bandhu, kāru, neru, meru, ruru, veḷu iccādayo.

Likewise: Maṅku, Maccu, Ucchu, Paṭu, Bhāṇu, Setu, Ketu, Sattu, Sindhu, Bandhu, Kāru, Neru, Meru, Ruru, Veḷu, and so on.

Visesavidhānamuccate.

A special provision is stated.

Hetu, jantu, kurusaddesu ‘jantuhetu’ iccādisuttena vikappena yonaṃ lopo, hetu dhammo, hetū dhammā, atīte hetavo pañca.

For the words `hetu`, `jantu`, and `kuru`, by the sutta beginning ‘jantuhetu,’ the elision of `yo` is optional. For example: `hetu dhammo` (the cause is a phenomenon), `hetū dhammā` (the causes are phenomena), `atīte hetavo pañca` (in the past there were five causes).

180. Yomhi vā kvaci ka. 97; rū. 156; nī. 260.

180. Before `yo`, optionally and sometimes [a change occurs].

Yosu lasaññino u-kārassa kvaci ṭa hoti vā.

Before the `yo` endings, the `u`-vowel of a `la`-class noun sometimes optionally becomes `a`.

Atīte hetayo pañca.

‘Atīte hetayo pañca’ (In the past, there were five causes).

Vāti [M 0.0109] kiṃ? Hetuyo.

What is the purpose of saying 'vā'? For example: Hetuyo.

Kvacīti kiṃ? Bhikkhavo.

What is the purpose of saying 'kvaci'? For example: Bhikkhavo.

Bho hetu, bho hetū, bhonto hetū, hetavo, hetayo, hetuyo vā, hetuṃ, hetū, hetavo, hetayo, hetuyo vā. Sesaṃ bhikkhusamaṃ.

O hetu, O hetū, O venerable hetū; hetavo, hetayo, or hetuyo (nominative plural); hetuṃ (accusative singular); hetū, hetavo, hetayo, or hetuyo (accusative plural). The rest is the same as for 'bhikkhu'.

Jantu gacchati, jantū, jantayo, jantuyo vā.

A creature goes. Jantū, jantayo, or jantuyo (nominative plural).

181. Jantādito no ca ka. 119; rū. 155; nī. 294; ‘jantvādito’ (bahūsu).

181. From 'jantu' and so on, 'no' also occurs.

Pume jantādito yonaṃ no ca hoti vo ca.

In the masculine gender, after 'jantu' and so on, the 'yo' endings also become 'no' and 'vo'.

Jantuno, jantavo, bhojantu, bhojantū, bhonto jantū, jantayo, jantuyo, jantuno, jantavo, jantuṃ, jantū, jantayo, jantuyo, jantuno, jantavo. Sesaṃ bhikkhusamaṃ.

Jantuno (nominative plural; genitive/dative singular), jantavo (nominative/accusative plural); O jantu, O jantū, O venerable jantū; jantayo, jantuyo (nominative/accusative plural); jantuṃ (accusative singular); jantū (accusative plural). The rest is the same as for 'bhikkhu'.

Kuru, kurū, kurayo, kuruyo, kuruno, kuravoti sabbaṃ jantusamaṃ.

Kuru (nominative singular); kurū, kurayo, kuruyo, kuruno, kuravo (nominative plural); thus all is the same as for 'jantu'.

“Ajjeva taṃ kurayo pāpayātu jā. 2.22.1632, nandanti taṃ kurayo dassanena jā. 2.22.1641, ajjeva taṃ kurayo pāpayāmī”ti jā. 2.22.1634 dissanti.

'May the Kurus attain it this very day; the Kurus rejoice at the sight of it; I shall make the Kurus attain it this very day'—thus it is seen.

Mahāvuttinā latopi aṃvacanassa kvaci naṃ hoti, “kimatthinaṃ bhikkhunaṃ āhu, bhikkhunamāhu maggadesiṃ, bhikkhunamāhu maggajīviṃ, buddhaṃ ādiccabandhuna”nti dissanti, tathā “roganiḍḍaṃ pabhaṅgunaṃ, bhogānañca pabhaṅgunaṃ dha. pa. 139, viññāṇañca virāguna”nti ca. Tattha ‘kimatthina’nti kiṃsabhāvaṃ, ‘maggadesi’nti maggaṃ desentaṃ, ‘maggajīvi’nti magge jīvantaṃ, ‘roganiḍḍa’nti rogānaṃ kulāvakabhūtaṃ, ‘pabhaṅguna’nti pabhijjanasīlaṃ, ‘virāguna’nti virajjanasīlaṃ. Katthaci paṭhamantampi dissati, tattha nāgamo.

According to the Mahāvutti, even for the singular, the 'aṃ' ending sometimes becomes 'naṃ', as is seen in: 'kimatthinaṃ bhikkhunaṃ āhu' (for what purpose do they call him a bhikkhu?), 'bhikkhunamāhu maggadesiṃ' (they call the bhikkhu a guide to the path), 'bhikkhunamāhu maggajīviṃ' (they call the bhikkhu one who lives by the path), 'buddhaṃ ādiccabandhunaṃ' (the Buddha, kinsman of the sun). Likewise: 'roganiḍḍaṃ pabhaṅgunaṃ' (a nest of disease, which is fragile), 'bhogānañca pabhaṅgunaṃ' (and wealth, which is fragile), 'viññāṇañca virāgunaṃ' (and consciousness, which is subject to fading). Therein, 'kimatthinaṃ' means 'of what nature'; 'maggadesiṃ' means 'one who teaches the path'; 'maggajīviṃ' means 'one who lives by the path'; 'roganiḍḍaṃ' means 'being a nest for diseases'; 'pabhaṅgunaṃ' means 'of a nature to break apart'; 'virāgunaṃ' means 'of a nature to fade away'. In some cases, a nominative ending is also seen; in that case, it is not an augment.

Iti bhikkhādigaṇarāsi.

Thus ends the section on the group of words beginning with 'bhikkhu'.

Satthādigaṇarāsi

The section on the group of words beginning with 'satthu'.

Satthādirāsi

The section on words beginning with 'satthu'.

182. Ltupitādīnamā simhi ka. 299; rū. 158; nī. 411.

182. For words ending in the 'tu' suffix and for the 'pitu' group, 'ā' occurs when the 'si' (nominative singular) ending follows.

Simhi [M 0.0110] pare ltupaccayantānaṃ satthu, kattuiccādīnaṃ pitādīnañca u-kāro ā hoti. ‘Gasīna’nti lopo.

When the 'si' (nominative singular) ending follows, for words ending in the 'tu' suffix, such as 'satthu', 'kattu', etc., and for the 'pitu' group, the vowel 'u' becomes 'ā'. The 'si' is elided by the rule 'Gānaṃ si lopo'.

Satthā.

The Teacher.

183. Ltupitādīnamase ka. 200; rū. 159; nī. 412.

183. For words ending in the 'tu' suffix and for the 'pitu' group, in cases other than 'si'.

Samhā aññasmiṃ vibhattigaṇe pare ltu, pitādīnaṃ u-kāro āraṅa hoti.

When a group of case endings other than 'sa' (nominative singular) follows, for words ending in the 'tu' suffix and for the 'pitu' group, the vowel 'u' becomes 'āra'.

184. Āraṅasmā ka. 205; rū. 160; nī. 421.

184. After 'āra'.

Āraṅato yonaṃ ṭo hoti.

After 'āra', the 'yo' endings become 'o'.

Satthāro.

The Teachers.

185. Ge a ca ka. 246; rū. 73; nī. 476, 478-9.

185. Before the 'ge' (vocative singular) ending, also 'a'.

Ge pare ltu, pitādīnaṃ u-kāro hoti a ca ā ca. Bhosattha, bho satthā, bhonto satthāro, satthāraṃ.

When 'ge' (vocative singular) follows, for words ending in the 'tu' suffix and for the 'pitu' group, the vowel 'u' becomes 'a' and also 'ā'. For example: O sattha, O satthā, O venerable satthāro, satthāraṃ.

186. Ṭoṭe vā ka. 205; rū. 260; nī. 421.

186. 'O' and 'e', optionally.

Āraṅato yonaṃ kamena ṭo, ṭe honti vā. Ettha ca vāsaddo sakhasadde vikappanattho tattha vidhyantarasabbhāvā. Puna ṭoggahaṇaṃ lahubhāvatthaṃ.

After 'āra', the 'yo' endings optionally become 'o' and 'e' respectively. And here, the word 'vā' indicates an option, because another rule exists. The repetition of 'o' is for the sake of brevity.

Satthāro, satthāre.

Satthāro, satthāre (nominative and accusative plural).

187. Ṭā [M 0.0111] nāsmānaṃ ka. 207, 270; rū. 161, 120; nī. 42, 542.

187. 'Ā' is the substitute for 'nā' and 'smā'.

Āraṅato nā, smānaṃ ṭā hoti.

After 'āra', 'nā' and 'smā' become 'ā'.

Satthārā, satthārehi, satthārebhi.

Satthārā (by/from the Teacher); satthārehi, satthārebhi (by/with the Teachers).

188. Lopo ka. 203; rū. 162; nī. 418.

188. Elision.

Ltu, pitādīhi salopo hoti vā.

From `ltu` and `pitādi` words, there is optionally elision of `sa`.

Satthu, satthussa, satthuno.

Of the teacher, of the teacher, of the teacher.

189. Naṃmhi vā ka. 201; rū. 163; nī. 416.

189. In the `naṃ` (genitive plural) ending, optionally.

Naṃmhi pare ltu, pitādīnaṃ u-kāro āraṅa hoti vā. Imesaṃ mahānāma tiṇṇaṃ satthārānaṃ ekā niṭṭhā udāhu puthu niṭṭhāti a. ni. 3.127. Satthūnaṃ.

When `naṃ` (genitive plural) follows, for `ltu` and `pitādi` words, the `u` optionally becomes `āraṅa`. 'Among these three teachers of great name, is their conclusion one or are they separate?' `Satthūnaṃ` (Of the teachers).

190. Ā ka. 202; rū. 164; nī. 417.

190. Ā.

Naṃmhi pare ltu, pitādīnaṃ u-kāro ā hoti vā.

When `naṃ` (genitive plural) follows, for `ltu` and `pitādi` words, the `u` optionally becomes `ā`.

Satthānaṃ, satthārā, satthārehi, satthārebhi, satthu, satthussa, satthuno, satthūnaṃ, satthārānaṃ, satthānaṃ.

`Satthānaṃ` (of the teachers), `satthārā` (by the teacher), `satthārehi` (by the teachers), `satthārebhi` (by the teachers), `satthu` (of the teacher), `satthussa` (of the teacher), `satthuno` (of the teacher), `satthūnaṃ` (of the teachers), `satthārānaṃ` (of the teachers), `satthānaṃ` (of the teachers).

191. Ṭi smiṃno ka. 206; rū. 165; nī. 422.

191. `Ṭi` for `smiṃ` and `no`.

Āraṅato smiṃno ṭi hoti.

After `āraṅa`, `smiṃ` and `no` become `ṭi`.

192. Rassāraṅa ka. 208; rū. 166; nī. 424.

192. Shortening of `āraṅa`.

Smiṃmhi pare āraṅkato rasso hoti.

When `smiṃ` (locative singular) follows, the `āraṅa` substitute is shortened.

Satthari, satthāresu.

In the teacher, in the teachers.

Bahulādhikārā [M 0.0112] nā, smāsu satthunāti ca sumhi satthūsūti ca siddhaṃ. “Dhammarājena satthunā, pūjaṃ labbhati bhattusū”ti jā. 2.22.1517 pāḷi. ‘Bhattusū’ti sāmīsu, ‘bhattāsū’tipi pāṭho.

By the governing rule of `bahula` (application in various ways), `satthunā` with `nā` and `smā` (instrumental and ablative singular), and `satthūsu` with `su` (locative plural) are established. The Pāli text states: 'By the Dhamma-king, the Teacher, homage is received among the lords.' `Bhattusū` means 'among lords'; `bhattāsū` is also a reading.

‘Ltupitādīnamase’ti aseggahaṇena tomhi āraṅa hoti nī. 414, “satthārato satthāraṃ gacchanti, satthārato satthāraṃ ghaṭentī”ti mahāni. 27 pāḷi.

By the inclusion of `ase` in the rule 'Ltupitādīnamase', `āraṅa` occurs with `to` (ablative singular). The Pāli text states: 'From teacher to teacher they go, from teacher to teacher they strive.'

Evaṃ kattā, bhattā, gantā, jetā, janetā, chettā, cheditā, viññātā, viññāpetā, uṭṭhātā, uṭṭhāpetā, taritā, tāretā, dātā, dāpetā, sandhātā, sandhāpetā, netā, nettā, posetā, bhettā, yātā, vattā, setā, hantā, sakamandhātā, mahāmandhātā iccādayo.

Thus, `kattā` (the doer), `bhattā` (the supporter), `gantā` (the goer), `jetā` (the conqueror), `janetā` (the generator), `chettā` (the cutter), `cheditā` (the one who causes to cut), `viññātā` (the knower), `viññāpetā` (the one who causes to know), `uṭṭhātā` (the riser), `uṭṭhāpetā` (the one who causes to rise), `taritā` (the one who crosses), `tāretā` (the one who causes to cross), `dātā` (the giver), `dāpetā` (the one who causes to give), `sandhātā` (the joiner), `sandhāpetā` (the one who causes to join), `netā` (the leader), `nettā` (the guider), `posetā` (the nourisher), `bhettā` (the breaker), `yātā` (the traveler), `vattā` (the speaker), `setā` (the one who binds), `hantā` (the killer), `Sakamandhātā`, `Mahāmandhātā`, and so on.

Visesavidhānamuccate.

A special rule is stated.

Mahāvuttinā yonaṃ ā hoti, avitakkitā gabbhamupavajanti jā. 1.13.138 (visadisaṃ), te bhikkhū brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

According to the Mahāvutti, `yo` becomes `ā`. 'The thoughtless enter the womb.' 'Those monks are the developers of empty dwellings.'

Amaccavācīhi kattu, khattusaddehi gassa ettaṃ, uṭṭhehi katte taramāno jā. 2.22.1690, natthi bho khatte paroloko dī. ni. 2.408.

From the words `kattu` and `khattu` when denoting ministers, `etta` occurs for `ga` (vocative singular). 'Rise up, O agent, hurrying!' 'There is no other world, O `khatte` (steward).'

Ge pare āraṅa ca hoti, pucchāma kattāra anomapañña, “kattāraṃ anomapañña”ntipi jā. 1.10.28 yujjati.

When `ge` (dative/genitive singular) follows, `āraṅa` also occurs. 'We ask the maker, O one of flawless wisdom.' `kattāraṃ anomapañña` is also suitable.

Aṃmhi pare pubbassaralopo ca hoti, anukampakaṃ pāṇasamampi bhattuṃ jahanti itthiyo. “So patīto pamuttena, bhattunā bhattugāravo”ti jā. 2.21.48 diṭṭhattā kattunā, gantunā iccādīnipi yujjanti.

When `aṃ` (accusative singular) follows, there is also elision of the preceding vowel. 'Women compassionately abandon a husband, even one as dear as life.' Since it is seen: 'He, pleased by the delighted husband, is respectful to the husband,' the forms `kattunā`, `gantunā`, etc., are also suitable.

Nettumhā [M 0.0113] smiṃno ettaṃ nī. 430, nette ujuṃ gate sati jā. 1.4.133, ete saddā tīsu liṅgesu samānarūpā honti, kattā itthī, kattā puriso, kattā kulaṃ iccādi.

After `nettu`, `smiṃ` and `no` become `ettaṃ`. 'When the leader has gone straight,' these words are of the same form in all three genders: `kattā` (a woman doer), `kattā` (a man doer), `kattā` (a family that does), and so on.

Iti satthādirāsi.

Thus ends the section on words beginning with `satthar`.

Pitādirāsi

The section on words beginning with `pitar`.

Pitā gacchati.

The father goes.

193. Pitādīnamanattādīnaṃ ka. 209; rū. 168; nī. 425; ‘pitādīnamanatvādīnaṃ’ (bahūsu).

193. For the `pitādi` group, excluding the `nattādi` group.

Nattādivajjitānaṃ pitādīnaṃ āraṅakato rasso hoti.

For words of the `pitādi` group, excluding the `nattādi` group, the `āraṅa` substitute is shortened.

Pitaro, bho pita, bho pitā, bhonto pitaro. Pitaraṃ, pituṃ vā. “Mātuṃ pituñca vanditvā”ti jā. 2.22.1859 dissati.

Fathers; O father, O father; O sirs, O fathers. The father, or `pituṃ`. 'Having venerated mother and father' is seen.

Pitaro, pitare, pitarā, pitunā, pitarehi, pitarebhi, pitūhi, pitūbhi, pitu, pitussa, pituno, pitūnaṃ, pitarānaṃ, pitarā, pitunā, pitarehi, pitarebhi, pitūhi, pitūbhi, pitu, pitussa, pituno, pitūnaṃ, pitarānaṃ, pitānaṃ, pitusmiṃ, pitumhi, pitari, pitaresu, pitūsu.

Fathers, fathers; by the father, by the father; by fathers, by fathers, by fathers, by fathers; of the father, of the father, of the father; of fathers, of fathers; by the father, by the father; by fathers, by fathers, by fathers, by fathers; of the father, of the father, of the father; of fathers, of fathers, of fathers; in the father, in the father, in the father; among fathers, among fathers.

Anaṇo ñātinaṃ hoti, devānaṃ pitunañca so jā. 2.22.126, mātāpitūnaṃ accayena, dhammaṃ cara mahārāja, mātāpitūsu khattiya jā. 2.17.39.

'He is free from debt to his relatives, and he is a father to the gods.' 'After the passing of mother and father, practice the Dhamma, O great king.' 'Toward mother and father, O warrior.'

Evaṃ bhātā, bhātaro, jāmātā, jāmātaroiccādi.

Thus, brother, brothers; son-in-law, sons-in-law, and so on.

Anattādīnanti kiṃ? Nattā, nattāro, nattāraṃ, nattāro, nattāre iccādi. Tathā panattusaddopi.

What is meant by 'not of the `nattādi` group'? The forms are `nattā`, `nattāro`, `nattāraṃ`, `nattāro`, `nattāre`, and so on. Likewise for the word `panattu`.

Mātu[M 0.0114], dhītu, duhitusaddā pana itthiliṅgā eva, mātā, mātaro, bhoti māta, bhoti mātā, bhoti māte vā, “acchariyaṃ nandamāte, abbhutaṃ nandamāte”ti a. ni. 7.53 dissati. ‘Ghabrahmāditve’ti gassa ettaṃ. Bhotiyo mātaro, mātaraṃ, mātuṃ, mātaro, mātare, mātuyā, mātarā, mātarehi, mātarebhi, mātūhi, mātūbhi, mātu, mātussa, mātuyā. “Mātussa sarati, pitussa saratī”ti rū. 169; nī. 160 piṭṭhe satthe dissati. “Buddhamātussa sakkāraṃ, karotu sugatoraso”ti apa. therī. 2.2.259 ca dissati. Mātūnaṃ, mātānaṃ, mātarānaṃ. Pañcamīrūpaṃ tatiyāsamaṃ. Chaṭṭhīrūpaṃ catutthīsamaṃ. Mātusmiṃ, mātumhi, mātari, mātuyā, mātuyaṃ, mātaresu, mātūsu. Evaṃ dhītu, duhitusaddā.

However, the words `mātu` (mother), `dhītu` (daughter), and `duhitu` (daughter) are indeed feminine. The forms are `mātā`, `mātaro`; or in the vocative, `bhoti māta`, `bhoti mātā`, or `bhoti māte`. As seen in: 'Wonderful, Nandamātā! Marvelous, Nandamātā!' By the rule `ghabrahmāditve`, the vocative singular ending `ga` becomes `e`. The forms are: `bhotiyo mātaro`, `mātaraṃ`, `mātuṃ`, `mātaro`, `mātare`, `mātuyā`, `mātarā`, `mātarehi`, `mātarebhi`, `mātūhi`, `mātūbhi`, `mātu`, `mātussa`, `mātuyā`. As seen in the scripture: 'He remembers his mother; he remembers his father.' And also seen: 'Let the Sugata's descendant honor the Buddha's mother.' The forms are `mātūnaṃ`, `mātānaṃ`, `mātarānaṃ`. The form of the fifth case is like the third. The form of the sixth case is like the fourth. The forms are `mātusmiṃ`, `mātumhi`, `mātari`, `mātuyā`, `mātuyaṃ`, `mātaresu`, `mātūsu`. The words `dhītu` and `duhitu` are declined in the same way.

Visesavidhimhi gāthāsu mahāvuttinā mātu, pitusaddehi nādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ ekavacanānaṃ yā hoti, smiṃno pana yañca hoti, antalopo ca. Matyā kataṃ, matyā deti, matyā apeti, matyā dhanaṃ, matyā ṭhitaṃ. Matyaṃ ṭhitaṃ. Evaṃ petyā kataṃiccādi, idha vuddhi.

In a special rule, in verses, according to the Mahāvutti, for the words `mātu` and `pitu`, `yā` occurs for the five singular case endings beginning with `nā`; `ya` also occurs for `smiṃ` and `no`; and there is elision of the final vowel. For example: `matyā kataṃ`, `matyā deti`, `matyā apeti`, `matyā dhanaṃ`, `matyā ṭhitaṃ`; and `matyaṃ ṭhitaṃ`. Likewise, `petyā kataṃ`, etc.—here, strengthening occurs.

Anuññāto ahaṃ matyā, sañcatto pitarā ahaṃ jā. 2.22.29. Matyā ca petyā ca kataṃ susādhu jā. 2.18.61, ahañhi jānāmi janinda etaṃ, matyā ca petyā ca jā. 2.18.59, sabbaṃ pubbepi vuttameva.

'I am permitted by my mother; I am restrained by my father.' 'What is done by mother and father is very well done.' 'Indeed, I know this, O lord of men, by mother and by father.' All this has been stated previously.

Satthu, pitādīnaṃ samāse vidhānaṃ samāsakaṇḍe āgamissati.

The rule regarding compounds of `satthar`, `pitar`, and so on, will come in the chapter on compounds.

Iti pitādirāsi.

Thus ends the group beginning with `pitar`.

Iti satthādigaṇarāsi.

Thus ends the group of `satthar`, etc.

Ukārantapulliṅgarāsi niṭṭhito.

The group of masculine nouns ending in `u` is concluded.

Ūkārantapulliṅgarāsi

The Group of Masculine Nouns Ending in `ū`

‘Gasīna’nti [M 0.0115] lopo, sayambhū gacchati. ‘Lopo’ti yonaṃ lopo, sayambhū gacchanti.

By `gasīnaṃ`, there is elision; `sayambhū gacchati` (the self-existent one goes). By `lopo`, there is elision of `yo`; `sayambhū gacchanti` (the self-existent ones go).

Pakkhe –

Alternatively:

‘Jantādito no cā’ti yonaṃ vo, no, sayambhuvo, sayambhuno.

By `jantādito no cā`, `yo` becomes `vo` or `no`: `sayambhuvo`, `sayambhuno`.

‘Ge vā’ti ge pare vikappena rasso, bho sayambhu, bho sayambhū, bhonto sayambhū, sayambhuvo, sayambhuno.

By `ge vā`, when `ge` follows, shortening is optional: `bho sayambhu`, `bho sayambhū`; `bhonto sayambhū`, `sayambhuvo`, `sayambhuno`.

‘Ekavacanayosvaghona’nti amādīsu ekavacanesu niccaṃ rasso, sayambhuṃ, gāthāyaṃ ‘sayambhuna’ntipi yujjati.

By `ekavacanayosvaghonaṃ`, in singular case endings beginning with `aṃ`, shortening always occurs: `sayambhuṃ`. In verses, `sayambhuna` is also acceptable.

Sayambhū, sayambhuvo, sayambhuno. Sayambhunā, sayambhūhi, sayambhūbhi, sayambhussa, sayambhuno, sayambhūnaṃ. Sayambhusmā, sayambhumhā, sayambhunā, sayambhūhi, sayambhūbhi, sayambhussa, sayambhuno, sayambhūnaṃ. Sayambhusmiṃ, sayambhumhi, sayambhūsu.

Sayambhū, sayambhuvo, sayambhuno. Sayambhunā, sayambhūhi, sayambhūbhi. Sayambhussa, sayambhuno, sayambhūnaṃ. Sayambhusmā, sayambhumhā, sayambhunā, sayambhūhi, sayambhūbhi. Sayambhussa, sayambhuno, sayambhūnaṃ. Sayambhusmiṃ, sayambhumhi, sayambhūsu.

Evaṃ abhibhū, parābhibhū, vessabhū, gotrabhū, vatrabhū iccādi. Sesesu pana yonaṃ no eva labbhati, cittasahabhuno dhammā dha. sa. dukamātikā 61.

Similarly: `abhibhū`, `parābhibhū`, `vessabhū`, `gotrabhū`, `vatrabhū`, and so forth. However, in the remaining cases, only `no` is obtained for `yo`, as in `cittasahabhuno dhammā`.

194. Kūto ka. 119; rū. 155; nī. 294.

194. From `kū`:

Pume kūpaccayantehi yonaṃ no hoti vā.

For masculine nouns ending in the suffix `kū`, `yo` optionally becomes `no`.

Sabbaññū, sabbaññuno. Sesaṃ suviññeyyaṃ.

Sabbaññū, sabbaññuno. The rest is easily understood.

Viññū[M 0.0116], vadaññū, atthaññū, dhammaññū, mattaññū, vidū. Idha kūsaddena rūpaccayantāpi gayhanti, vedagū, pāragū. Tathā bhīrū, pabhaṅgū, virāgūiccādi ca.

Viññū, vadaññū, atthaññū, dhammaññū, mattaññū, vidū. Here, by the word `kū`, those ending in the `rū` suffix are also included, such as `vedagū`, `pāragū`. Likewise, `bhīrū`, `pabhaṅgū`, `virāgū`, and so forth.

Ūkārantapulliṅgarāsi niṭṭhito.

The group of masculine nouns ending in `ū` is concluded.

Okāranto pana gosaddo eva, so pubbe vuttoyeva.

However, the only word ending in `o` is `go`; it has already been explained previously.

Pulliṅgarāsi niṭṭhito.

The group of masculine nouns is concluded.

Napuṃsakaliṅgarāsi

The Group of Neuter Nouns

Akārantanapuṃsaka cittādirāsi

The Group of Neuter Nouns Ending in `a`, beginning with `citta`

Atha napuṃsakaliṅgaṃ dīpiyate. Taṃ pana pañcavidhaṃ adantaṃ, idantaṃ īdantaṃ, udantaṃ, ūdantanti.

Now, the neuter gender is explained. It is fivefold: ending in `a`, ending in `i`, ending in `ī`, ending in `u`, and ending in `ū`.

195. Aṃ napuṃsake ka. 125; rū. 198; nī. 300.

195. `aṃ` in the neuter.

Napuṃsake ato sissa aṃ hoti.

In the neuter, after `a`, `si` becomes `aṃ`.

Cittaṃ.

Cittaṃ.

196. Yonaṃ ni ka. 218; rū. 196; nī. 445.

196. `yo` becomes `ni`.

Napuṃsake ato yonaṃ ni hoti. ‘Yolopanīsū’ti nimhi dīgho.

In the neuter, 'yo' becomes 'ni' after 'a'. According to the rule 'Yolopanīsū', when 'ni' is present, there is lengthening.

Cittāni.

Cittāni.

197. Nīnaṃ vā ka. 107; rū. 69; nī. 275; ‘nīna vā’ (bahūsu).

197. Of 'nī', optionally.

Ato nīnaṃ ṭā, ṭe honti vā.

After 'a', 'nī' optionally becomes 'ṭā' or 'ṭe'.

Cittā, he citta, he cittā, he cittāni, he cittā vā, cittaṃ, cittāni, citte, cittena. Sesaṃ purisasamaṃ.

Cittā, he citta, he cittā, he cittāni, he cittā vā, cittaṃ, cittāni, citte, cittena. The rest is the same as for 'purisa'.

Evaṃ [M 0.0117] dakaṃ, udakaṃ, sukhaṃ, dukkhaṃ, mukhaṃ, aṅgaṃ, liṅgaṃ, siṅgaṃ, aghaṃ, saccaṃ, naccaṃ, rajjaṃ, pajjaṃ, ambujaṃ, dhaññaṃ, thaññaṃ, araññaṃ, puññaṃ, kiliṭṭhaṃ, piṭṭhaṃ, bhaṇḍaṃ, tuṇḍaṃ, ñāṇaṃ, tāṇaṃ, leṇaṃ, karaṇaṃ, caraṇaṃ, chattaṃ, khettaṃ, nettaṃ, amataṃ, sotaṃ, pīṭhaṃ, vatthaṃ, padaṃ, gadaṃ, āvudhaṃ, kānanaṃ, ghānaṃ, jhānaṃ, dānaṃ, dhanaṃ, vanaṃ, pāpaṃ, dumaṃ, hadayaṃ, cīraṃ, cīvaraṃ, kulaṃ, mūlaṃ, balaṃ, maṅgalaṃ, bhisaṃ, sīsaṃ, lohaṃiccādayo.

Similarly: dakaṃ (water), udakaṃ (water), sukhaṃ (happiness), dukkhaṃ (suffering), mukhaṃ (face), aṅgaṃ (limb), liṅgaṃ (sign), siṅgaṃ (horn), aghaṃ (evil), saccaṃ (truth), naccaṃ (dance), rajjaṃ (kingdom), pajjaṃ (verse), ambujaṃ (lotus), dhaññaṃ (grain), thaññaṃ (milk), araññaṃ (forest), puññaṃ (merit), kiliṭṭhaṃ (defiled), piṭṭhaṃ (back), bhaṇḍaṃ (goods), tuṇḍaṃ (beak), ñāṇaṃ (knowledge), tāṇaṃ (protection), leṇaṃ (shelter), karaṇaṃ (action), caraṇaṃ (conduct), chattaṃ (umbrella), khettaṃ (field), nettaṃ (eye), amataṃ (deathlessness), sotaṃ (ear), pīṭhaṃ (seat), vatthaṃ (cloth), padaṃ (foot), gadaṃ (club), āvudhaṃ (weapon), kānanaṃ (forest), ghānaṃ (nose), jhānaṃ (meditation), dānaṃ (giving), dhanaṃ (wealth), vanaṃ (forest), pāpaṃ (evil), dumaṃ (tree), hadayaṃ (heart), cīraṃ (bark-cloth), cīvaraṃ (robe), kulaṃ (family), mūlaṃ (root), balaṃ (strength), maṅgalaṃ (blessing), bhisaṃ (lotus root), sīsaṃ (head), lohaṃ (metal), and so forth.

Iti cittādirāsi.

Thus concludes the section on nouns like 'citta'.

Kammādirāsi

The Section on Nouns like 'kamma'

Kammasadde –

Regarding the word 'kamma'–

198. Nāsseno ka. 103; rū. 79; nī. 271.

198. Of 'nā', 'eno'.

Kammādīhi nāssa eno hoti vā.

After words like 'kamma', 'nā' optionally becomes 'eno'.

Kammena, kammanā.

Kammena, kammanā.

‘Pumakammathāmaddhāna’nti suttena nā, smāsu uttaṃ, kammunā, kammassa, kammuno, kammasmā, kammamhā, kammanā, kammunā, kammassa, kammuno.

By the rule 'Pumakammathāmaddhāna', in the case of the suffixes 'nā' and 'smā', the following is stated: kammunā, kammassa, kammuno, kammasmā, kammamhā, kammanā, kammunā, kammassa, kammuno.

199. Kammādito ka. 197; rū. 125; nī. 404.

199. From 'kamma', etc.

Kammādīhi smiṃno ni hoti vā.

After words like 'kamma', 'smiṃ' optionally becomes 'ni'.

Kammasmiṃ, kammamhi, kammani, kamme. Sesaṃ cittasamaṃ.

Kammasmiṃ, kammamhi, kammani, kamme. The rest is the same as for 'citta'.

Kamma camma ghamma asma vesma addha muddha aha brahma attaātumā kammādi. Kammani, cammani. “Kiṃ chando kimadhippāyo, eko sammasi ghammanī”ti jā. 1.16.1 ca “kiṃ patthayaṃ mahābrahme, eko sammasi ghammanī”ti jā. 1.13.83 ca “mā tvaṃ cande khali asmanī”ti ca “tamaddasa mahābrahmā, nisinnaṃ samhi vesmanī”ti ca dissanti. Addhani[M 0.0118], muddhani, ahani, brahmani, attani, ātumani, sabbametaṃ pubbepi vuttameva ca. Tattha ‘sammasī’ti acchasi, ‘ghammanī’ti gimhakāle ātape vā, ‘asmanī’ti pāsāṇe, ‘vesmanī’ti ghare.

Kamma, camma, ghamma, asma, vesma, addha, muddha, aha, brahma, atta, ātumā—these are the group beginning with 'kamma'. Kammani, cammani. And it is seen: “What is your wish, what is your intention, that you sit alone in the heat?” and “What do you seek, O great Brahma, that you sit alone in the heat?” and “Do not, O moon, stumble on the stone,” and “The great Brahma saw him, seated in his own dwelling.” Addhani, muddhani, ahani, brahmani, attani, ātumani. And all this has indeed been stated previously. Therein, 'sammasī' means 'you sit'; 'ghammanī' means 'in the summer season' or 'in the sun'; 'asmanī' means 'on the stone'; 'vesmanī' means 'in the house'.

Iti kammādirāsi.

Thus concludes the section on nouns like 'kamma'.

200. Aṃ napuṃsake ka. 125; rū. 198; nī. 300; ‘aṃṅaṃ napuṃsake’ (bahūsu)?.

200. 'Aṃ' in the neuter.

Napuṃsake simhi ntussa aṃ hoti vā. Silopo.

In the neuter, when 'si' follows, the suffix 'ntu' optionally becomes 'aṃ'. There is elision of 'si'.

Guṇavaṃ kulaṃ.

Guṇavaṃ kulaṃ.

Pakkhe –

Alternatively–

Simhi mahāvuttinā ntussa anto a hoti, tato sissa aṃ hoti, guṇavantaṃ kulaṃ.

When 'si' is present, according to the Mahāvutti, the end of 'ntu' becomes 'a'; then 'si' becomes 'aṃ', resulting in guṇavantaṃ kulaṃ.

‘Yvādo ntussā’ti yvādīsu ntussantassa attaṃ, guṇavantāni, guṇavantā, he guṇava, he guṇavā, he guṇavantāni, he guṇavantā, guṇavaṃ, guṇavantaṃ, guṇavantāni, guṇavante, guṇavantena, guṇavatā kulena. Sabbaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ.

By the rule 'Yvādo ntussā', when suffixes beginning with 'y' etc. follow, the end of a stem in 'ntu' becomes 'at': guṇavantāni, guṇavantā, he guṇava, he guṇavā, he guṇavantāni, he guṇavantā, guṇavaṃ, guṇavantaṃ, guṇavantāni, guṇavante, guṇavantena, guṇavatā kulena. Everything is the same as in the masculine.

Satimaṃ kulaṃ, satimantaṃ kulaṃ iccādi.

Satimaṃ kulaṃ, satimantaṃ kulaṃ, and so forth.

Gacchaṃ kulaṃ, gacchantaṃ kulaṃ, gacchantāni kulāni iccādi.

Gacchaṃ kulaṃ, gacchantaṃ kulaṃ, gacchantāni kulāni, and so forth.

Iti akārantanapuṃsakarāsi.

Thus concludes the section on neuter nouns ending in 'a'.

Ikārantanapuṃsakarāsi

The Section on Neuter Nouns Ending in 'i'

Aṭṭhi tiṭṭhati, aṭṭhī tiṭṭhanti.

Aṭṭhi tiṭṭhati (a bone stands), aṭṭhī tiṭṭhanti (bones stand).

201. Jhalā vā ka. 217; rū. 199; nī. 444.

201. From 'jh' and 'l', optionally.

Napuṃsake jha, lato yonaṃ ni hoti vā. ‘Yolopanīsū’ti dīgho.

In the neuter gender, after stems designated by 'jha' and 'la', 'ni' is optionally substituted for 'yo'. By the rule 'Yolopanīsū', there is lengthening.

Aṭṭhīni[M 0.0119], he aṭṭhi, he aṭṭhī, he aṭṭhīni, he aṭṭhī vā, aṭṭhiṃ, aṭṭhinaṃ, aṭṭhīni, aṭṭhī, aṭṭhinā, aṭṭhīhi, aṭṭhībhi. Sesaṃ munisamaṃ.

Aṭṭhīni, he aṭṭhi, he aṭṭhī, he aṭṭhīni, he aṭṭhī vā, aṭṭhiṃ, aṭṭhinaṃ, aṭṭhīni, aṭṭhī, aṭṭhinā, aṭṭhīhi, aṭṭhībhi. The rest is similar to 'muni'.

Samāsepi sammādiṭṭhi kulaṃ, sammādiṭṭhīni kulāni iccādi, yonaṃ no, ne natthi.

In compounds, such as 'sammādiṭṭhi kulaṃ' (a family with right view), 'sammādiṭṭhīni kulāni' (families with right view), etc., 'yo' is not replaced by 'no', and 'ne' does not occur.

Smiṃmhi sammādiṭṭhismiṃ, sammādiṭṭhimhi, sammādiṭṭhini, sammādiṭṭhine kule, ariyavuttine kule iti vattabbaṃ.

In the locative singular, one should say 'sammādiṭṭhismiṃ', 'sammādiṭṭhimhi', 'sammādiṭṭhini', 'sammādiṭṭhine kule' (in a family with right view), and 'ariyavuttine kule' (in a family with noble conduct).

Evaṃ akkhi, acchi, satthi, dadhi, vāri iccādayo.

Similarly, akkhi (eye), acchi (eye), satthi (thigh), dadhi (curd), vāri (water), etc.

Iti ikārantanapuṃsakarāsi.

Thus ends the Class of Neuter Nouns Ending in 'i'.

Īkārantanapuṃsakarāsi

The Class of Neuter Nouns Ending in 'ī'.

Īkārante ‘ekavacanayosvaghona’nti suttena simhi rasso, daṇḍi kulaṃ, daṇḍīni kulāni, yonaṃ lope daṇḍī.

In nouns ending in 'ī', according to the rule 'ekavacanayosvaghona', the vowel is shortened in the nominative singular. 'Daṇḍi kulaṃ' (a family with a staff), 'daṇḍīni kulāni' (families with staffs), with the elision of 'yo', 'daṇḍī'.

‘Ge vā’ti rasso, he daṇḍi, he daṇḍī vā, he daṇḍīni, he daṇḍī, daṇḍiṃ, daṇḍinaṃ, daṇḍīni, daṇḍī, daṇḍinā, daṇḍīhi, daṇḍībhi. Pulliṅgasamaṃ.

By the rule 'Ge vā', there is optional shortening. He daṇḍi, he daṇḍī vā, he daṇḍīni, he daṇḍī, daṇḍiṃ, daṇḍinaṃ, daṇḍīni, daṇḍī, daṇḍinā, daṇḍīhi, daṇḍībhi. The rest is similar to the masculine.

Samāsepi sīghayāyi cittaṃ, sīghayāyīni, sīghayāyī, he sīghayāyi, he sīghayāyī vā, he sīghayāyīni, he sīghayāyī, sīghayāyiṃ, sīghayāyinaṃ, sīghayāyīni iccādi.

In compounds also, sīghayāyi cittaṃ, sīghayāyīni, sīghayāyī, he sīghayāyi, he sīghayāyī vā, he sīghayāyīni, he sīghayāyī, sīghayāyiṃ, sīghayāyinaṃ, sīghayāyīni, etc.

Evaṃ sukhakāri dānaṃ, cakkī, pakkhī, sukhī, sikhī iccādayo kulasambandhino ca veditabbā.

Similarly, sukhakāri dānaṃ, cakkī, pakkhī, sukhī, sikhī, etc., should be understood as related to a family.

Iti īkārantanapuṃsakarāsi.

Thus ends the Class of Neuter Nouns Ending in 'ī'.

Ukārantanapuṃsakarāsi

The Class of Neuter Nouns Ending in 'u'.

Āyu [M 0.0120] tiṭṭhati, ‘jhalā vā’ti yonaṃ nitte lope ca dīgho, āyūni, āyū, he āyu, he āyū, he āyūni, he āyū, āyuṃ, āyunaṃ, āyūni, āyū. Sesaṃ bhikkhusamaṃ.

Āyu tiṭṭhati. By the rule 'jhalā vā', when 'ni' is substituted for 'yo' and also upon the elision of 'yo', the vowel is lengthened: āyūni, āyū, he āyu, he āyū, he āyūni, he āyū, āyuṃ, āyunaṃ, āyūni, āyū. The rest is similar to 'bhikkhu'.

Āyusaddo pulliṅgepi vattati, “punarāyu ca me laddho dī. ni. 2.369, āyuñca vo kīvatako nu samma jā. 1.15.205, āyu nu khīṇo maraṇañca santike, na cāyu khīṇo maraṇañca dūre”ti pāḷipadāni.

The word 'āyu' also occurs in the masculine gender, as in the Pāli phrases: 'punarāyu ca me laddho', 'āyuñca vo kīvatako nu samma', 'āyu nu khīṇo maraṇañca santike', 'na cāyu khīṇo maraṇañca dūre'.

Evaṃ cakkhu, hiṅgu, siggu, jatu, vatthu, matthu, madhu, dhanu, tipu, dāru, vasu, assu iccādayo.

Similarly, cakkhu, hiṅgu, siggu, jatu, vatthu, matthu, madhu, dhanu, tipu, dāru, vasu, assu, etc.

202. Ambādīhi ka. 217; rū. 199; nī. 444; ‘ambādīhi’ (bahūsu).

202. From 'ambu' and so forth.

Ambu, paṃsuiccādīhi smiṃno ni hoti vā.

From 'ambu', 'paṃsu', etc., 'ni' is optionally substituted for 'smiṃ'.

Phalaṃ patati ambuni, pupphaṃ yathā paṃsuni ātape gataṃ. Sesaṃ āyusamaṃ. Citragu, vahagu, digu iccādayopi ukārantapakatikā evāti.

Phalaṃ patati ambuni, pupphaṃ yathā paṃsuni ātape gataṃ. The rest is similar to 'āyu'. Citragu, vahagu, digu, etc., are also stems ending in 'u'.

Iti ukārantanapuṃsakarāsi.

Thus ends the Class of Neuter Nouns Ending in 'u'.

Ūkārantanapuṃsakarāsi

The Class of Neuter Nouns Ending in 'ū'.

Simhi rasso, gotrabhu ñāṇaṃ, gotrabhūni, gotrabhū, he gotrabhu, he gotrabhū, he gotrabhūni, hegotrabhū, gotrabhuṃ, gotrabhunaṃ, gotrabhūni, gotrabhū. Sesaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ. Evaṃ sayambhu ñāṇaṃ, abhibhu jhānaṃ iccādi.

In the nominative singular, the vowel is shortened. Gotrabhu ñāṇaṃ, gotrabhūni, gotrabhū, he gotrabhu, he gotrabhū, he gotrabhūni, he gotrabhū, gotrabhuṃ, gotrabhunaṃ, gotrabhūni, gotrabhū. The rest is similar to the masculine. Similarly, sayambhu ñāṇaṃ, abhibhu jhānaṃ, etc.

Iti ūkārantanapuṃsakarāsi.

Thus ends the Class of Neuter Nouns Ending in 'ū'.

Napuṃsakaliṅgarāsi niṭṭhito.

The Class of the Neuter Gender is completed.

Sabbādirāsi

The Class of 'Sabba' and so forth.

Atha [M 0.0121] sabbanāmāni dīpiyante.

Now the pronouns are explained.

Sabba, katara, katama, ubhaya, itara, añña, aññatara, aññatama, pubba, para, apara, dakkhiṇa, uttara, adhara, ya, ta, tya, eta, ima, amu, kiṃ, eka, ubha, dvi,ti, catu, tumha, amha imāni aṭṭhavīsati sabbanāmāni nāma. Sabbesaṃ liṅgatthānaṃ sādhāraṇāni nāmāni sabbanāmāni.

Sabba, katara, katama, ubhaya, itara, añña, aññatara, aññatama, pubba, para, apara, dakkhiṇa, uttara, adhara, ya, ta, tya, eta, ima, amu, kiṃ, eka, ubha, dvi, ti, catu, tumha, amha—these twenty-eight are called pronouns. Pronouns are names common to the meanings of all genders.

Tattha sabbasaddo sakalattho.

Herein, the word 'sabba' means 'all'.

Katara, katamasaddā pucchanatthā.

The words 'katara' and 'katama' have an interrogative meaning.

Ubhayasaddo dvinnaṃ avayavānaṃ samudāyattho.

The word 'ubhaya' means the totality of two parts.

Itarasaddo ekato vuttassa paṭiyogīvacano.

The word 'itara' expresses the counterpart of something mentioned as one.

Aññasaddo yathādhigatamhā aparavacano.

The word 'añña' refers to something other than what has been obtained.

Aññatara, aññatamasaddā aniyamatthā.

The words 'aññatara' and 'aññatama' denote indeterminacy.

Pubbādayo saddā disā, kālādivavatthānavacanā.

The words 'pubba' and so forth denote directions, determinations of time, and so on.

Yasaddo aniyamatthavacano.

The word 'ya' expresses indefiniteness.

Ta, tyasaddā parammukhe dūravacanā.

The words 'ta' and 'tya' denote something distant and not present.

Etasaddo parammukhe samīpavacano, sammukhe dūravacano. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “eteti cakkhupathaṃ atikkamitvā dūragate sandhāyāhā”ti jā. aṭṭha 4.15.104 vuttaṃ, tasmā tasaddatthepi vattati.

The word 'eta' denotes something near but out of sight, or something distant but in sight. In the Commentary, however, it is stated: "'Eta' refers to something beyond the range of sight, far away." Therefore, it can also function in the sense of the word 'ta'.

Imasaddo sammukhe samīpavacano.

The word 'ima' indicates something near and present.

Amusaddo dūravacano. Samīpa, dūratā ca parikappabuddhivasenāpi hoti.

The word 'amu' indicates something distant. Nearness and distance also arise by way of conceptual understanding.

Kiṃsaddo pucchanattho.

The word 'kiṃ' has an interrogative meaning.

Ekasaddo saṅkhyattho aññattho ca.

The word 'eka' has the meaning of number and also another meaning.

Ubhasaddo [M 0.0122] dvisaddapariyāyo.

The word 'ubha' is a synonym for the word 'dvi'.

Tattha tyasaddopi bahulaṃ dissati. Khiḍḍā paṇihitā tyāsu, rati tyāsu patiṭṭhitā, bījāni tyāsu ruhanti jā. 2.21.120, kathaṃ nu vissase tyamhi jā. 1.16.288, atha vissasate tyamhiiccādi jā. 2.22.1474.

In this context, the word 'tya' is also frequently seen. Khiḍḍā paṇihitā tyāsu, rati tyāsu patiṭṭhitā, bījāni tyāsu ruhanti, kathaṃ nu vissase tyamhi, atha vissasate tyamhi, and so forth.

‘Itthiyamatvā’ti āpaccayo, ghasañño, silopo, sabbā itthī, sabbā, sabbāyo, he sabbe, he sabbā, he sabbāyo, sabbaṃ, sabbā, sabbāyo, sabbāya, sabbāhi, sabbābhi, sabbāya.

By the rule 'Itthiyamatvā', the suffix 'ā' is applied; it is designated 'gha'; and 'si' is elided. sabbā itthī, sabbā, sabbāyo, he sabbe, he sabbā, he sabbāyo, sabbaṃ, sabbā, sabbāyo, sabbāya, sabbāhi, sabbābhi, sabbāya.

203. Ghapāsassa ssā vā ka. 179, 62; rū. 204, 206; nī. 365, 209.

203. Ghapāsassa ssā vā.

Gha, pasaññehi sabbanāmehi sassa ssā hoti vā.

After pronouns designated 'gha' and 'pa', 'ssā' is optionally substituted for 'sa'.

204. Ghossaṃssāssāyaṃtiṃsu ka. 66; rū. 205; nī. 213.

204. Ghossaṃssāssāyaṃtiṃsu.

Ssamādīsu gho rasso hoti.

When 'ssa' and so forth follow, 'gha' is shortened.

Sabbassā.

Sabbassā.

205. Saṃsānaṃ ka. 168; rū. 203; nī. 353, 368.

205. Saṃsānaṃ.

Sabbādīhi naṃvacanassa saṃ, sānaṃ honti.

After 'sabba' and so forth, for the ending 'naṃ', 'saṃ' and 'sānaṃ' occur.

Sabbāsaṃ, sabbāsānaṃ, sabbāya, sabbāhi, sabbābhi, sabbāya, sabbassā, sabbāsaṃ, sabbāsānaṃ, sabbāya, sabbāyaṃ.

Sabbāsaṃ, sabbāsānaṃ, sabbāya, sabbāhi, sabbābhi, sabbāya, sabbassā, sabbāsaṃ, sabbāsānaṃ, sabbāya, sabbāyaṃ.

206. Smiṃno ssaṃ ka. 179, 62; rū. 204, 206; nī. 365, 209.

206. Smiṃno ssaṃ.

Sabbādīhi smiṃno ssaṃ hoti vā.

After 'sabba' and so forth, 'ssaṃ' is optionally substituted for 'smiṃ'.

Sabbassaṃ, sabbāsu.

Sabbassaṃ, sabbāsu.

Saddanītiyaṃ [M 0.0123] nā, smā, smiṃnampi ssādeso vutto nī. 366. “Tassā kumārikāya saddhiṃ pārā. 443, kassāhaṃ kena hāyāmī”ti pārā. 290 pāḷi. Idha pana suttavibhattena sādhiyati. Sabbassā kataṃ, sabbassā apeti, sabbassā ṭhitaṃ.

In the Saddanīti, the substitution of 'ssā' for 'nā', 'smā', and 'smiṃ' is also stated. 'Tassā kumārikāya saddhiṃ, kassāhaṃ kena hāyāmī' is a Pali passage. Here, however, it is derived by analysis of the rule. Sabbassā kataṃ, sabbassā apeti, sabbassā ṭhitaṃ.

Sabbo puriso.

Sabbo puriso.

207. Yonameṭa ka. 164; rū. 200; nī. 347.

207. Yonameṭa.

Akārantehi sabbādīhi yonaṃ eṭa hoti.

After 'sabba' and so forth ending in 'a', the ending 'yo' becomes 'eṭa'.

Sabbe purisā.

Sabbe purisā.

Atotveva? Sabbā itthiyo, amū purisā.

Atotveva? Sabbā itthiyo, amū purisā.

He sabba, he sabbā, he sabbe, sabbaṃ, sabbe, sabbena.

He sabba, he sabbā, he sabbe, sabbaṃ, sabbe, sabbena.

208. Sabbādīnaṃ naṃmhi ca ka. 102; rū. 202; nī. 270.

208. And for 'sabba' and so forth, before 'naṃ'.

Naṃmhi ca su, hisu ca sabbādīnaṃ assa e hoti.

Of 'sabba' and so forth, the final 'a' becomes 'e' before 'naṃ', 'su', and 'hisu'.

Sabbehi, sabbebhi, sabbassa, sabbesaṃ, sabbesānaṃ, sabbasmā, sabbamhā, sabbehi, sabbebhi, sabbassa, sabbesaṃ, sabbesānaṃ, sabbasmiṃ, sabbamhi, sabbesu.

Sabbehi, sabbebhi, sabbassa, sabbesaṃ, sabbesānaṃ, sabbasmā, sabbamhā, sabbehi, sabbebhi, sabbassa, sabbesaṃ, sabbesānaṃ, sabbasmiṃ, sabbamhi, sabbesu.

Cūḷaniruttiyaṃ pana smā, smiṃnaṃ ā, ettaṃ vuttaṃ, sabbā apeti, sabbe patiṭṭhitanti. “Sabbā ca savati, sabbathā savatī”ti ca “tyāhaṃ mante paratthaddho”ti jā. 2.22.835 ca pāḷī. Tattha ‘tyāha’nti te+ahaṃ, tasmiṃ manteti attho.

In the Cūḷanirutti, however, it is stated that 'ā' is substituted for 'smā' and 'smiṃ', as in 'sabbā apeti' and 'sabbe patiṭṭhitanti'. The Pāli passages 'Sabbā ca savati, sabbathā savatī' and 'Tyāhaṃ mante paratthaddho' are also found. There, 'tyāhaṃ' is 'te + ahaṃ', with the meaning 'in that mantra'.

Sabbanāmehi catutthiyā āyādesopi dissati, “yāya no anukampāya, amhe pabbājayī muni. So no attho [M 0.0124] anuppatto”ti theragā. 176 ca “yāyeva kho panatthāya āgaccheyyātha, tameva atthaṃ sādhukaṃ manasi kareyyāthā”ti ca dī. ni. 1.263 “neva mayhaṃ ayaṃ nāgo, alaṃ dukkhāya kāyacī”ti jā. 2.22.870 ca pāḷī.

With pronouns, the substitution of 'āya' for the dative ending is also seen, as in: 'Yāya no anukampāya, amhe pabbājayī muni. So no attho anuppatto'; and 'Yāyeva kho panatthāya āgaccheyyātha, tameva atthaṃ sādhukaṃ manasi kareyyāthā'; and 'Neva mayhaṃ ayaṃ nāgo, alaṃ dukkhāya kāyacī'.

Sabbaṃ cittaṃ.

Sabbaṃ cittaṃ.

209. Sabbādīhi.

209. From 'sabba' and so forth.

Sabbādīhi nissa ṭā na hoti.

After 'sabba' and so forth, the substitution of 'ṭā' for 'ni' does not occur.

Sabbāni, sabbaṃ, sabbāni. Sesaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ.

Sabbāni, sabbaṃ, sabbāni. The rest is similar to the masculine.

Bahulādhikārā kvaci nissa ṭā, ṭepi honti. Pāḷiyaṃ pana nissa ṭā, ṭepi dissanti- “yā pubbe bodhisattānaṃ, pallaṅkavaramābhuje. Nimittāni padissanti, tāni ajja padissare bu. vaṃ. 2.82. Kiṃ māṇavassa ratanāni atthi, ye taṃ jinanto hare akkhadhutto”ti jā. 2.22.1390. Evaṃ katara, katamasaddāpi ñeyyā.

Due to the governing rule of 'bahula', 'ṭā' and 'ṭe' sometimes occur as substitutes for 'ni'. In the Pāli canon, 'ṭā' and 'ṭe' for 'ni' are also seen: 'Yā pubbe bodhisattānaṃ, pallaṅkavaramābhuje. Nimittāni padissanti, tāni ajja padissare.' 'Kiṃ māṇavassa ratanāni atthi, ye taṃ jinanto hare akkhadhutto.' Similarly, the words 'katara' and 'katama' should also be understood.

Ubhayasadde itthi, pumesu ubhayā, ubhayoti paṭhamekavacanarūpaṃ appasiddhaṃ. Mahāvuttinā yonaṃ ṭo vā hoti, ubhayo itthiyo, ubhayaṃ itthiṃ, ubhayo itthiyo, ubhayāya, ubhayāhi, ubhayābhi. Sesaṃ sabbasamaṃ.

For the word 'ubhaya', in the feminine and masculine, the nominative singular forms 'ubhayā' and 'ubhayo' are established. According to the Mahāvutti, 'ṭo' is optionally substituted for 'yo': ubhayo itthiyo, ubhayaṃ itthiṃ, ubhayo itthiyo, ubhayāya, ubhayāhi, ubhayābhi. The rest is similar to 'sabba'.

Ubhayo purisā, ubhaye purisā, ubhayaṃ, ubhayo, ubhaye, ubhayena, ubhayehi, ubhayebhi, ubhayassa, ubhayesaṃ, ubhayesānaṃ. Sabbasamaṃ.

Ubhayo purisā, ubhaye purisā, ubhayaṃ, ubhayo, ubhaye, ubhayena, ubhayehi, ubhayebhi, ubhayassa, ubhayesaṃ, ubhayesānaṃ. The rest is similar to 'sabba'.

Ubhayaṃ kulaṃ tiṭṭhati, ubhayāni, ubhayaṃ, ubhayāni. Sabbasamaṃ. “Ekarattena ubhayo, tuvañca dhanusekha ca jā. 1.16.239, todeyya, kappā ubhayo, idhekarattiṃ ubhayo vasema, ubhaye devamanussā, ubhaye vasāmase”ti pāḷi.

Ubhayaṃ kulaṃ tiṭṭhati, ubhayāni, ubhayaṃ, ubhayāni. The rest is similar to 'sabba'. The Pāli passages are: 'Ekarattena ubhayo, tuvañca dhanusekha ca', 'todeyya, kappā ubhayo', 'idhekarattiṃ ubhayo vasema', 'ubhaye devamanussā', 'ubhaye vasāmase'.

210. Ssaṃssāssāyesitarekaññetimānami ka. 63; rū. 217; nī. 210; ‘ssaṃssāssāyesvitarekaññebhimānami’ (bahūsu).

210. Ssaṃssāssāyesitarekaññetimānami.

Ssamādīsu [M 0.0125] itarā, ekā, aññā, etā, imāsaddānaṃ i hoti.

Before case endings such as 'ssa', the final vowel of the stems itarā, ekā, aññā, etā, and imā becomes 'i'.

Itarissā kataṃ, itarissā deti, itarissā apeti, itarissā dhanaṃ, itarissā, itarissaṃ ṭhitaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbasamaṃ.

Itarissā kataṃ, itarissā deti, itarissā apeti, itarissā dhanaṃ, itarissā, itarissaṃ ṭhitaṃ. The rest is similar to 'sabba'.

Aññā, aññā, aññāyo, aññaṃ, aññā, aññāyo, aññāya, aññissā, aññāhi, aññābhi, aññāya, aññissā, aññāsaṃ, aññāsānaṃ, aññissā, aññāhi, aññābhi, aññāya, aññissā, aññāsaṃ, aññāsānaṃ, aññāya, aññissā, aññāyaṃ, aññissaṃ, aññāsu. Sesaliṅgesu sabbasamaṃ.

Aññā, aññā, aññāyo, aññaṃ, aññā, aññāyo, aññāya, aññissā, aññāhi, aññābhi, aññāya, aññissā, aññāsaṃ, aññāsānaṃ, aññissā, aññāhi, aññābhi, aññāya, aññissā, aññāsaṃ, aññāsānaṃ, aññāya, aññissā, aññāyaṃ, aññissaṃ, aññāsu. In the other genders, it is similar to 'sabba'.

“Aññatarissā itthiyā paṭibaddhacitto hotī”ti pārā. 73 pāḷi, idha suttavibhattena sijjhati. Sesaṃ aññatara, aññatamesu sabbasamaṃ.

The Pāli passage is: 'Aññatarissā itthiyā paṭibaddhacitto hotī'. Here, this form is accomplished by the inflection prescribed by the rule. For the rest, in the case of 'aññatara' and 'aññatama', the declension is similar to 'sabba'.

Iti sabbādiaṭṭhakarāsi.

Thus ends the section on the eight 'sabbādi' words.

Pubbā itthī, pubbā, pubbāyo, pubbaṃ, pubbā, pubbāyo, pubbāya, pubbassā, pubbāhi, pubbābhi, pubbāya, pubbassā, pubbāsaṃ, pubbāsānaṃ, sattamiyaṃ pubbāya, pubbassā, pubbāyaṃ, pubbassaṃ, pubbāsu.

Pubbā itthī, pubbā, pubbāyo, pubbaṃ, pubbā, pubbāyo, pubbāya, pubbassā, pubbāhi, pubbābhi, pubbāya, pubbassā, pubbāsaṃ, pubbāsānaṃ; in the locative: pubbāya, pubbassā, pubbāyaṃ, pubbassaṃ, pubbāsu.

211. Pubbādīhi chahi ka. 164; rū. 200; nī. 347; caṃ. 2.1.15; pā. 1.1.34.

211. By the six beginning with 'pubba'.

Tehi chahi yonaṃ eṭa hoti vā.

After these six, 'e' is the optional substitute for the 'yo' ending.

Pubbe, pubbā, pare, parā, apare, aparā, dakkhiṇe, dakkhiṇā, uttare, uttarā, adhare, adharā. Tattha ‘pubbe pubbā’ti puratthimadisābhāgā, tatraṭṭhakā vā atthā, purātanā vā sattā saṅkhārā ca. “Pubbabuddhā, pubbadevā, pubbācariyā”tiādīsu “pubbe buddhā [M 0.0126] pubbabuddhā, pubbā buddhā vā pubbabuddhā”tiādinā attho veditabbo. Evaṃ sesesu.

Pubbe, pubbā, pare, parā, apare, aparā, dakkhiṇe, dakkhiṇā, uttare, uttarā, adhare, adharā. Here, 'pubbe, pubbā' refers to the eastern direction or its parts, or to things situated there, or to ancient beings and formations. In phrases such as 'Pubbabuddhā', 'pubbadevā', 'pubbācariyā', the meaning should be understood as 'pubbe buddhā pubbabuddhā' or 'pubbā buddhā vā pubbabuddhā'. Similarly for the rest.

Pubbesaṃ, pubbesānaṃ, paresaṃ, paresānaṃ, aparesaṃ, aparesānaṃ, dakkhiṇesaṃ, dakkhiṇesānaṃ, uttaresaṃ, uttaresānaṃ, adharesaṃ, adharesānaṃ. Sesaṃ ñeyyaṃ.

Pubbesaṃ, pubbesānaṃ, paresaṃ, paresānaṃ, aparesaṃ, aparesānaṃ, dakkhiṇesaṃ, dakkhiṇesānaṃ, uttaresaṃ, uttaresānaṃ, adharesaṃ, adharesānaṃ. The rest is to be understood.

Pubbādīhīti kiṃ? Sabbe.

Why 'beginning with pubba'? Sabbe.

Chahīti kiṃ? Ye, te.

Why 'by the six'? Ye, te.

212. Nāññañca nāmappadhānā caṃ. 2.1.10; pā. 1.1.27-29.

212. And not for others, nor for nouns, nor for the non-primary.

Suddhanāmabhūtā ca samāse appadhānabhūtā ca sabbādito pubbe vuttaṃ sabbādikāriyaṃ aññañca upari vuccamānaṃ sabbādikāriyaṃ na hoti. Tattha suddhanāmabhūtaṃ sabbādināma na jānātīti atthena bālavācako aññasaddo, ājānātīti atthena majjhemaggaphalañāṇavācako aññasaddo, arahattaphalañāṇavācako aññasaddo, ‘pubbo lohita’ntiādīsu pubbasaddo, atirekaparamādivācako parasaddo, disākālādito aññesu atthesu pavattā dakkhiṇu’ttarasaddā ca saṅkhyatthavācito añño ekasaddo cāti sabbametaṃ suddhanāmaṃ nāma, tato sabbādikāriyaṃ natthi.

For words from the 'sabbādi' group that have become pure nouns, or have become non-primary in a compound, the 'sabbādi' operations mentioned before and those to be mentioned later do not apply. Herein, examples of pure nouns are: the word 'añña' meaning 'foolish' (in the sense of 'one who does not know'); the word 'añña' meaning 'one who knows', signifying the knowledge of the middle path and its fruit; the word 'añña' signifying the knowledge of the fruit of Arahantship; the word 'pubba' in phrases like 'pubbo lohita'; the word 'para' signifying 'excess', 'supreme', etc.; the words 'dakkhiṇa' and 'uttara' when used in meanings other than direction, time, etc.; and the word 'eka' when used in a sense other than 'number'. All these are what is called a pure noun, and therefore the 'sabbādi' operations do not apply to them.

Appadhāne diṭṭhapubba, gatapubba, piyapubba iccādi. Tattha pubbe diṭṭho diṭṭhapubbo buddho purisena. Pubbe diṭṭho yenāti vā diṭṭhapubbo puriso buddhaṃ. Evaṃ gatapubbo maggo purisena, gatapubbo vā puriso maggaṃ. Piyā vuccati bhariyā, piyā pubbā purāṇā etassāti piyapubbo, piyo vuccati pati, piyo pubbo yassāti piyapubbā. Etehi ca sabbādikāriyaṃ natthi.

In the case of non-predominant compounds, examples are `diṭṭhapubba`, `gatapubba`, `piyapubba`, and so forth. Therein, `diṭṭhapubbo` is a Buddha previously seen by a person, or `diṭṭhapubbo` is a person by whom the Buddha was previously seen. Similarly, `gatapubbo` is a path previously traveled by a person, or `gatapubbo` is a person who has traveled the path. `Piyā` is said to be a wife; `piyapubbo` is he whose former wife she was. `Piyo` is said to be a husband; `piyapubbā` is she whose former husband he was. And with these, there is no `sabbādi` function.

213. Tatiyatthayoge nī. 350; caṃ. 2.1.11; pā. 1.1.30.

213. In combination with the meaning of the third [case].

Tatiyatthena [M 0.0127] padena yoge sabbādikāriyaṃ natthi.

In combination with a word in the instrumental sense, there is no `sabbādi` function.

Māsena pubbānaṃ māsapubbānaṃ.

`Māsena pubbānaṃ` (earlier than them by a month) becomes `māsapubbānaṃ`.

214. Catthasamāse ka. 166; rū. 209; nī. 349; caṃ. 2.1.11; pā. 1.1.31.

214. In a compound with the meaning of 'ca'.

Catthasamāso vuccati dvandasamāso, tasmiṃ sabbādikāriyaṃ natthi.

A compound with the meaning of 'ca' is called a dvanda compound; in it, there is no `sabbādi` function.

Dakkhiṇā ca uttarā ca pubbā ca dakkhiṇuttarapubbā, dakkhiṇuttarapubbānaṃ.

Southern and northern and eastern becomes `dakkhiṇuttarapubbā`; [the genitive plural is] `dakkhiṇuttarapubbānaṃ`.

Cattheti kiṃ? Dakkhiṇassā ca pubbassā ca yā antaradisāti dakkhiṇapubbā, dakkhiṇā ca sā pubbā cāti dakkhiṇapubbā, dakkhiṇapubbassā, dakkhiṇapubbassaṃ.

Why [the specification] 'in the meaning of ca'? The intermediate direction of the south and the east is `dakkhiṇapubbā`; or, that which is southern and eastern is `dakkhiṇapubbā`. [The inflected forms are] `dakkhiṇapubbassā`, `dakkhiṇapubbassaṃ`.

215. Veṭa ka. 165; rū. 208; nī. 348; caṃ. 2.1.13; pā. 1.1.32.

215. Veṭa.

Catthasamāse yonaṃ eṭa hoti vā.

In a compound with the meaning of 'ca', `eṭa` is optionally substituted for the `yo` endings.

Katarakatame, katarakatamā, itaritare, itaritarā, aññamaññe, aññamaññā, pubbapare, pubbaparā, pubbāpare, pubbāparā iccādi.

`katarakatame`, `katarakatamā`, `itaritare`, `itaritarā`, `aññamaññe`, `aññamaññā`, `pubbapare`, `pubbaparā`, `pubbāpare`, `pubbāparā`, and so forth.

Imesu pubbādīsu smā, smiṃnaṃ ā, ettaṃ hoti, pubbā, pubbe, parā, pare, aparā, apare, dakkhiṇā, dakkhiṇe, uttarā, uttare, adharā, adhare.

For these words beginning with `pubba`, for the endings `smā` and `smiṃ`, `ā` and `e` occur, [resulting in forms such as]: `pubbā`, `pubbe`, `parā`, `pare`, `aparā`, `apare`, `dakkhiṇā`, `dakkhiṇe`, `uttarā`, `uttare`, `adharā`, `adhare`.

Iti pubbādichakkarāsi.

Thus the group of six beginning with `pubba`.

Yā itthī, yā, yāyo, yaṃ, yā, yāyo, yāya, yassā, yāhi, yābhi, yāya, yassā, yāsaṃ, yāsānaṃ, yāya[M 0.0128], yassā, yāhi, yābhi, yāya, yassā, yāsaṃ, yāsānaṃ, yāya, yassā, yāyaṃ, yassaṃ, yāsu.

The feminine `yā`: `yā itthī`, `yā`, `yāyo`, `yaṃ`, `yā`, `yāyo`, `yāya`, `yassā`, `yāhi`, `yābhi`, `yāya`, `yassā`, `yāsaṃ`, `yāsānaṃ`, `yāya`, `yassā`, `yāhi`, `yābhi`, `yāya`, `yassā`, `yāsaṃ`, `yāsānaṃ`, `yāya`, `yassā`, `yāyaṃ`, `yassaṃ`, `yāsu`.

Yo puriso, ye, yaṃ, ye, yena, yehi, yebhi, yassa, yesaṃ, yesānaṃ, yasmā, yamhā, yehi, yebhi, yassa, yesaṃ, yesānaṃ, yasmiṃ, yamhi, yesu.

The masculine `yo`: `yo puriso`, `ye`, `yaṃ`, `ye`, `yena`, `yehi`, `yebhi`, `yassa`, `yesaṃ`, `yesānaṃ`, `yasmā`, `yamhā`, `yehi`, `yebhi`, `yassa`, `yesaṃ`, `yesānaṃ`, `yasmiṃ`, `yamhi`, `yesu`.

Yaṃ cittaṃ, yāni cittāni, yaṃ, yāni. Sesaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ.

The neuter `yaṃ`: `yaṃ cittaṃ`, `yāni cittāni`, `yaṃ`, `yāni`. The rest is like the masculine.

216. Tyatetānaṃ tassa so ka. 174; rū. 211; nī. 360.

216. For the `t` of `tya`, `ta`, and `eta`, `so`.

Anapuṃsakānaṃtya, ta, etasaddānaṃ tabyañjanassa so hoti simhi. Silopo.

For the non-neuter words `tya`, `ta`, and `eta`, the consonant `t` becomes `so` when the `si` ending follows. There is elision of `si`.

Sā itthī, tā, tāyo, itthiyo, taṃ, tā, tāyo, tāya.

`Sā itthī`, `tā`, `tāyo`, `itthiyo`, `taṃ`, `tā`, `tāyo`, `tāya`.

217. Ssā vā tetimāmūhi ka. 179, 62; rū. 204, 206; nī. 365-6, 209.

217. And `ssā` optionally from `ta`, `eta`, `ima`, `amu`.

Gha, pasaññehi tā, etā, imā, amusaddehi nādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ ekavacanānaṃ ssā hoti vā. Rasso.

From the words `tā`, `etā`, `imā`, and `amu`, which have the `gha` and `pa` designations, `ssā` is optionally substituted for the five singular endings beginning with `nā`. Shortening occurs.

Tassā kataṃ, tāhi, tābhi, tāya, tassā.

`Tassā kataṃ` (done by her), `tāhi`, `tābhi`, `tāya`, `tassā`.

218. Tāssi vā ka. 64; rū. 216; nī. 211.

218. Tāssi vā.

Ssaṃ, ssā, ssāyesu ghasaññassa tāsaddassa i hoti vā.

When `ssaṃ`, `ssā`, and `ssāya` follow, for the word `tā`, which has the `gha` designation, its vowel optionally becomes `i`.

Tissā.

`Tissā`.

219. Tetimāto [M 0.0129] sassa ssāya ka. 65; rū. 215; nī. 212.

219. From `ta`, `eta`, and `ima`, `ssāya` for `sa`.

Tā, etā, imāhi sassa ssāyādeso hoti vā.

After `tā`, `etā`, and `imā`, the substitution `ssāya` optionally occurs for `sa`.

Tassāya, tissāya, tāsaṃ, tāsānaṃ, tāya, tassā, tassāya, tissāya, tāsaṃ, tāsānaṃ, tāya, tāyaṃ, tassā, tassaṃ, tissā, tissaṃ, tāsu.

`Tassāya`, `tissāya`, `tāsaṃ`, `tāsānaṃ`, `tāya`, `tassā`, `tassāya`, `tissāya`, `tāsaṃ`, `tāsānaṃ`, `tāya`, `tāyaṃ`, `tassā`, `tassaṃ`, `tissā`, `tissaṃ`, `tāsu`.

So puriso, te purisā, taṃ, te, tena, tehi, tebhi, tassa, tesaṃ, tesānaṃ, tasmiṃ, tamhi, tesu.

`So puriso`, `te purisā`, `taṃ`, `te`, `tena`, `tehi`, `tebhi`, `tassa`, `tesaṃ`, `tesānaṃ`, `tasmiṃ`, `tamhi`, `tesu`.

Taṃ cittaṃ, tāni cittāni, taṃ, tāni. Sesaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ.

`Taṃ cittaṃ`, `tāni cittāni`, `taṃ`, `tāni`. The rest is like the masculine.

220. Tassa no sabbāsu ka. 175; rū. 212; nī. 361.

220. For the pronoun `ta`, the substitution `no` does not occur in all cases.

Yvādīsu sabbāsu vibhattīsu tassa no hoti.

In all cases of `ya`, etc., `ta` becomes `no`.

Ne purisā, naṃ, ne, nehi, nebhi, nesaṃ, nesānaṃ, nehi, nebhi, nesaṃ, nesānaṃ, namhi, nesu.

Ne purisā, naṃ, ne, nehi, nebhi, nesaṃ, nesānaṃ, nehi, nebhi, nesaṃ, nesānaṃ, namhi, nesu.

Ettha ca ‘sabbāsū’ti vuttepi yā yā vibhatti labbhati, taṃ taṃ ñatvā yojetabbā.

Here, even though 'in all cases' is stated, whatever case ending is obtained should be known and applied accordingly.

Naṃ cittaṃ, nehi, nebhi. Pulliṅgasamaṃ.

Naṃ cittaṃ, nehi, nebhi. Like the masculine gender.

221. Ṭa sasmāsmiṃssāyassaṃssāsaṃmhāmhisvimassa ca ka. 176; rū. 213; nī. 362.

221. Rule: The substitution `ṭa` applies to `assa` in the cases `sasmā`, `smiṃ`, `ssa`, `āya`, `ssaṃ`, `ssā`, `saṃ`, `mhā`, `mhi`, and `sviṃ`.

Sādīsu tassa ca imassa ca ṭa hoti vā.

In `sa`, etc. (cases), `ṭa` optionally occurs for `tassa` and `imassa`.

Assā itthiyā kataṃ, assā, assāya deti. Saṃmhi dīgho nī. 368 – āsaṃ itthīnaṃ, nāsaṃ kujjhanti paṇḍitā jā. 1.1.65, assā apeti, assā, assāya dhanaṃ, āsaṃ dhanaṃ, “abhikkamo sānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo”ti saṃ. ni. 5.196 ettha ‘sāna’nti vedanānaṃ, mahāvuttinā tassa sattaṃ. Assā, assaṃ ṭhitaṃ.

Assā itthiyā kataṃ (done by that woman), assā, assāya deti (gives to her). In `saṃ`, elongation occurs: `āsaṃ` for women; `nāsaṃ` the wise do not get angry. Assā apeti (from her, it departs); assā, assāya dhanaṃ (wealth of her, to her); āsaṃ dhanaṃ (wealth of them). In "abhikkamo sānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo" (progress is evident for them, not retreat), here `sānaṃ` means 'of feelings'; according to the Mahāvutti, `sa` is substituted for `ta`. Assā, assaṃ ṭhitaṃ (it stands in her).

Assa [M 0.0130] purisassa, āsaṃ purisānaṃ. Nevāsaṃ kesā dissanti, hatthapādā ca jālino jā. 2.22.2221. Asmā, amhā, assa, āsaṃ, asmiṃ, amhi.

Assa purisassa (of that man), āsaṃ purisānaṃ (of those men). Nevāsaṃ kesā dissanti, hatthapādā ca jālino (nor are their hairs seen, and their hands and feet are webbed). Asmā, amhā, assa, āsaṃ, asmiṃ, amhi.

Assa cittassa. Pulliṅgasamaṃ.

Assa cittassa (of that mind). Like the masculine gender.

Esā itthī, etā, etāyo, etaṃ, etā, etāyo, etāya, etassā, etissā kataṃ.

Esā itthī (this woman), etā, etāyo, etaṃ, etā, etāyo, etāya, etassā, etissā kataṃ (done by her).

Eso puriso, ete, etaṃ, ete, etena.

Eso puriso (this man), ete, etaṃ, ete, etena.

Etaṃ cittaṃ, etāni, etaṃ, etāni, etena. Sabbaṃ tasaddasamaṃ ṭhapetvā nattaṃ, ṭattañca.

Etaṃ cittaṃ (this mind), etāni, etaṃ, etāni, etena. All is like the word `ta`, except for the `na` and `ṭa` substitutions.

222. Simhānapuṃsakassāyaṃ ka. 172; rū. 218; nī. 306-7; ‘simha…’ (bahūsu).

222. In the nominative singular (`si`) case, for non-neuter, `ayaṃ` occurs.

Simhi napuṃsakato aññassa imassa ayaṃ hoti. Silopo.

In the nominative singular (`si`) case, for the pronoun `ima` when it is non-neuter, `ayaṃ` occurs. The `si` is elided.

Ayaṃ itthī, imā, imāyo, imaṃ, imā, imāyo, imāya, imassā, imissā, imāhi, imābhi, imāya, imassā, imassāya, imissā, imissāya, imissaṃ, assā, assāya, imāsaṃ, imāsānaṃ, āsaṃ. Pañcamīrūpaṃ tatiyāsamaṃ, chaṭṭhīrūpaṃ catutthīsamaṃ. Imāya, imāyaṃ, imassā, imassāya, imassaṃ, imissā, imissāya, imissaṃ, assā, assaṃ, imāsu.

Ayaṃ itthī (this woman), imā, imāyo, imaṃ, imā, imāyo, imāya, imassā, imissā, imāhi, imābhi, imāya, imassā, imassāya, imissā, imissāya, imissaṃ, assā, assāya, imāsaṃ, imāsānaṃ, āsaṃ. The fifth case form is like the third, the sixth case form is like the fourth. Imāya, imāyaṃ, imassā, imassāya, imassaṃ, imissā, imissāya, imissaṃ, assā, assaṃ, imāsu.

Ayaṃ puriso, ime, imaṃ, ime.

Ayaṃ puriso (this man), ime, imaṃ, ime.

223. Nāmhinimi ka. 171; rū. 219; nī. 357; ‘nāmhanimhi’ (bahūsu).

223. Rule: Nāmhinimi.

Nāmhi anitthiliṅge imassa ana, imiādesā honti.

In the instrumental singular (`nā`) case, in non-feminine gender, `ana` and `imi` substitutions occur for `ima`.

Iminā, anena, imehi, imebhi.

Iminā, anena, imehi, imebhi.

224. Imassānitthiyaṃ ṭe ka. 170; rū. 220; nī. 356.

224. Rule: `Ṭe` for `ima` in non-feminine.

Anitthiliṅge [M 0.0131] imassa ṭe hoti vā su, naṃ, hisu.

In non-feminine gender, for `ima`, `ṭe` optionally occurs in the `su`, `naṃ`, and `hi` cases.

Ehi, ebhi, imassa, assa, imesaṃ, imesānaṃ, esaṃ, esānaṃ, imasmā, imamhā, asmā, amhā, imehi, imebhi, ehi, ebhi, imassa, assa, imesaṃ, imesānaṃ, esaṃ, esānaṃ, imasmiṃ, imamhi, asmiṃ, amhi, imesu, esu.

Ehi, ebhi, imassa, assa, imesaṃ, imesānaṃ, esaṃ, esānaṃ, imasmā, imamhā, asmā, amhā, imehi, imebhi, ehi, ebhi, imassa, assa, imesaṃ, imesānaṃ, esaṃ, esānaṃ, imasmiṃ, imamhi, asmiṃ, amhi, imesu, esu.

“Anamhi bhadde susoṇe, kinnu jagghasi sobhane”ti jā. 1.5.130 (anamhi kāle susoṇi) pāḷi- ‘anamhī’ti imasmiṃ ṭhāne, mahāvuttinā smiṃmhi anādeso.

The Pāḷi is: "Anamhi bhadde susoṇe, kinnu jagghasi sobhane." Here, `anamhi` is in place of `imasmiṃ`; according to the Mahāvutti, `ana` is the substitute for `ima` in the `smiṃ` case.

Imaṃ cittaṃ.

Imaṃ cittaṃ (this mind).

225. Imassidaṃ vā ka. 129; rū. 222; nī. 305.

225. Rule: `Idaṃ` for `ima` optionally.

Napuṃsake aṃ, sisu imassa tehi aṃ, sīhi saha idaṃ hoti vā.

In the neuter gender, for `ima` in the `aṃ` and `si` cases, `idaṃ` optionally occurs, together with those endings `aṃ` and `si`.

Idaṃ cittaṃ, imāni cittāni, imaṃ, idaṃ, imāni, iminā, anena. Sabbaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ.

Idaṃ cittaṃ (this mind), imāni cittāni (these minds), imaṃ, idaṃ, imāni, iminā, anena. All is like the masculine gender.

Idha missakarūpaṃ vuccati –

Here, what is called a mixed form is as follows:

Yā, sā itthī, yā, tā itthiyo, yaṃ, taṃ itthiṃ, yā, esā itthī, yā, etā itthiyo, yaṃ, etaṃ itthiṃ, yā, ayaṃ itthī, yā, imā itthiyo, yaṃ, imaṃ itthiṃ, yo, so puriso, ye, te purisāiccādayo.

The woman who, that woman; the women who, those women; the woman whom, that woman; the woman who, this woman; the women who, these women; the woman whom, this woman; the woman who, this woman; the women who, these women; the woman whom, this woman; the man who, that man; the men who, those men; and so on.

“Sa kho so kumāro vuddhimanvāyā”ti ettha so so kumāroti, ‘ese se eke ekatthe’ti ettha eso so eko ekatthoti vattabbaṃ. Tattha pubbaṃ pubbaṃ atthapadaṃ, paraṃ paraṃ byañjanamattaṃ. “Ayaṃ so sārathi etī”ti jā. 2.22.51 ettha pana dvepi visuṃ [M 0.0132] visuṃ atthapadāni evāti. Yaṃ, taṃ, idanti ime saddā nipātarūpāpi hutvā pāḷivākyesu sañcaranti sabbaliṅgavibhattīsu abhinnarūpāti.

In 'Sa kho so kumāro vuddhimanvāyā', the phrase is 'so so kumāro'; in 'ese se eke ekatthe', it should be stated as 'eso so eko ekattho'. In that case, the former is a word with meaning, the latter a mere consonant. However, in 'Ayaṃ so sārathi etī', both are indeed separate words with meaning. The words yaṃ, taṃ, and idaṃ, even having the form of particles, move through Pāli sentences in all genders and cases with unchanging form.

226. Imetānamenānvādese dutiyāyaṃ nī. 375-6 piṭṭhe; pā. 2.4.34.

226. For `ima` and `eta`, `ena` is the substitute in the accusative case when in anaphoric reference.

Anvādeso vuccati anukathanaṃ, punakathanaṃ, anvādesaṭhāne ima, etānaṃ enādeso hoti dutiyāvibhattīsu.

Anaphoric reference is called subsequent statement or repetition. In the context of anaphoric reference, for `ima` and `eta`, the substitution `ena` occurs in the accusative cases.

Imaṃ bhikkhuṃ vinayaṃ ajjhāpehi, atho enaṃ bhikkhuṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpehi, ime bhikkhū vinayaṃ ajjhāpehi, atho ene bhikkhū dhammaṃ ajjhāpehi, etaṃ bhikkhuṃ vinayaṃ ajjhāpehiiccādinā vattabbaṃ. Tamenaṃ bhikkhave nirayapālā a. ni. 3.36, yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ bhikkhuṃ iccādīsupi dī. ni. 1.213 anukathanameva.

Teach this monk the Vinaya, and then teach this monk the Dhamma; teach these monks the Vinaya, and then teach these monks the Dhamma; teach that monk the Vinaya—and so forth should it be stated. In 'Tamenaṃ bhikkhave nirayapālā,' 'yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ bhikkhuṃ,' and so forth, it is also merely a subsequent statement.

227. Massāmussa ka. 173; rū. 223; nī. 359.

227. `Massa` for `amussa`.

Simhi anapuṃsakassa amussa massa so hoti.

In the `si` (nominative singular) case, for the non-neuter `amu`, `massa` becomes `so`.

Asu itthī, amu vā, amū, amuyo, amuṃ, amū, amuyo, amuyā, amussā, amūhi, amūbhi, amuyā, amussā, amūsaṃ, amūsānaṃ, amuyā, amussā, amūhi, amūbhi, amuyā, amussā, amūsaṃ, amūsānaṃ, amuyā, amuyaṃ, amussā, amussaṃ, amūsu.

That woman, or that one; those, those; that one, those, those; by that one, by that one; by those, by those; to that one, to that one; to those, to those; from that one, from that one; from those, from those; of that one, of that one; of those, of those; in that one, in that one, in that one, in that one; in those.

Asu puriso, amu vā.

That man, or that one.

228. Lopomusmā ka. 118; rū. 146; nī. 293.

228. Elision after `amu`.

Amuto yonaṃ lopo hoti. Vo, nopavādoyaṃ ka. 119; rū. 155; nī. 294.

After `amu`, there is elision of the `yo` ending. This is not an exception.

Amū[M 0.0133], amuṃ, amū, amunā, amūhi, amūbhi.

Those, that one, those, by that one, by those, by those.

229. Na no sassa.

229. Not `no` for `sassa`.

Amuto sassa no na hoti.

After `amu`, `sassa` does not become `no`.

Amussa.

Of that one.

Mahāvuttinā samhi mussa duttaṃ, adussa. Pāḷiyaṃ “dussa me khettapālassa, rattiṃ bhattaṃ apābhata”nti jā. 1.4.62 ettha gāthāvasena a-kāralopo. Amūsaṃ, amūsānaṃ, amusmā, amumhā, amūhi, amūbhi, amussa, adussa, amūsaṃ, amūsānaṃ, amusmiṃ, amumhi, amūsu.

According to the Mahāvutti, in the genitive singular (`sa`), for `mussa` there is the change to `d`, giving the form `adussa`. In the Pāli text, 'dussa me khettapālassa, rattiṃ bhattaṃ apābhata,' here, due to the verse meter, the vowel 'a' is elided. [The forms are:] of those, of those; from that, from that; by those, by those; of that, of that; of those, of those; in that, in that; in those.

230. Amussāduṃ ka. 130; rū. 225; nī. 308.

230. `Aduṃ` for `amu`.

Napuṃsake aṃ, sisu amussa tehi saha aduṃ hoti vā.

In the neuter, `aduṃ` optionally occurs for `amu` with the `aṃ` (accusative singular) and `si` (nominative singular) endings.

Amuṃ cittaṃ, aduṃ cittaṃ, amūni, amuṃ, aduṃ, amūni. Sesaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ. ‘Sakatthe’ti suttena kapaccaye kate sabbādirūpaṃ natthi. Amukā kaññā, amukā, amukāyo. Amuko puriso, amukā purisā. Amukaṃ cittaṃ, amukāni cittāni iccādi.

That mind, that mind, those; that, that, those. The rest is like the masculine. According to the rule 'Sakatthe', when the `ka` suffix is applied, the pronominal declension does not occur. Such-and-such a maiden, such-and-such, such-and-such maidens. Such-and-such a man, such-and-such men. Such-and-such a mind, such-and-such minds, etc.

231. Ke vā.

231. Optionally when `ke` follows.

Ke pare amussa massa so hoti vā.

When `ke` follows, for `amu`, `massa` optionally becomes `so`.

Asukā itthī, asukā, asukāyo. Asuko puriso, asukā purisā. Asukaṃ kulaṃ, asukāni kulāni. Sabbaṃ kaññā, purisa, cittasamaṃ.

Such-and-such a woman, such-and-such, such-and-such women. Such-and-such a man, such-and-such men. Such-and-such a family, such-and-such families. All are declined like `kaññā`, `purisa`, and `citta` respectively.

‘Itthiyamatvā’ti ettha ‘itthiyaṃ ā’ti vibhattasuttena kiṃsaddato itthiyaṃ āpaccayo.

In 'Itthiyamatvā', by the case-ending rule 'itthiyaṃ ā', the suffix `ā` is added to the word `kiṃ` in the feminine.

232. Kiṃssa ko ka. 227-9; rū. 270, 226; nī. 456-7-8? ‘kissa ko sabbāsu’ (bahūsu).

232. `Ko` for `kiṃ`.

Sabbesu [M 0.0134] vibhattipaccayesu kiṃssa ko hoti.

In all case endings, `ko` is the substitute for `kiṃ`.

Kā itthī, kā, kāyo, kaṃ, kā, kāyo, kāya, kassā iccādi sabbasamaṃ. Ko puriso, ke purisā, kaṃ, ke, kena, kehi, kebhi, kassa.

Which woman, which, which women; whom, which, which women; by whom, to whom, etc., all are like `sabba`. Which man, which men; whom, which; by whom, by whom, by whom; to whom.

233. Ki sasmiṃsu vānitthiyaṃ.

233. `Ki` is the optional substitute in the non-feminine for the endings `sa` and `smiṃ`.

Anitthiliṅge sa, smiṃsu kiṃsaddassa ki hoti vā.

In the non-feminine gender, for the word `kiṃ`, `ki` is the optional substitute for the endings `sa` and `smiṃ`.

Kissa, kesaṃ, kesānaṃ, kasmā, kamhā, kehi, kebhi, kassa, kissa, kesaṃ, kesānaṃ, kasmiṃ, kamhi, kismiṃ, kimhi, kesu.

Of/to whom; of/to whom, of/to whom; from whom, from whom; by whom, by whom; of/to whom, of/to whom; of/to whom, of/to whom; in whom, in whom, in whom, in whom; in whom.

234. Kimaṃsisu napuṃsake ‘kimaṃsisu saha napuṃsake’ (bahūsu).

234. In the neuter, `kiṃ` is the form for the `aṃ` and `si` endings.

Napuṃsake aṃ, sisu kiṃsaddassa tehi aṃsīhi saha kiṃ hoti.

In the neuter, for the word `kiṃ` with the endings `aṃ` (accusative singular) and `si` (nominative singular), the form is `kiṃ`.

Kiṃ cittaṃ, kāni, kiṃ, kaṃ vā, kāni. Sesaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ. Idaṃ pucchanatthassa suddhakiṃsaddassa rūpaṃ.

What mind, what things; what, or what; what things. The rest is the same as the masculine. This is the form of the pure word 'kiṃ' in the sense of questioning.

‘Ci’itinipātena yutte pana ekaccatthaṃ vā appatthaṃ vā vadati. Kāci itthī, kāci itthiyo, kiñci itthiṃ, kāci, kāyaci, kāhici, kāyaci, kassāci, kāsañci, kutoci, kāhici. Sattamiyaṃ - kāyaci, katthaci, kāsuci.

However, when joined with the particle 'ci', it expresses either the sense of 'a certain one' or an indefinite sense. Some woman, some women; some woman, some; by some, by some; to some, of some, of some; from somewhere, from some. In the locative: in some, somewhere, in some.

Koci puriso, keci, kiñci, keci, kenaci, kehici, kassaci, kesañci, kismiñci, kimhici, katthaci, kesuci.

Some person, some; some person, some; by someone, by some; to/of someone, to/of some; in someone, in someone; somewhere, in some.

Kiñci kulaṃ, kānici kulāni, kiñci, kānici. Sesaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ.

Some family, some families; some family, some families. The rest is the same as the masculine.

Puna [M 0.0135] yasaddena yutte sakalatthaṃ vadati. Yā kāci itthī, yākāci itthiyo.
