Again, when joined with the word 'ya', it expresses a comprehensive sense. Whatever woman, whatever women.

Yo koci puriso, ye keci, yaṃ kiñci, ye keci yena kenaci, yehi kehici, yassa kassaci, yesaṃ kesañci yato kutoci, yehi kehici, yassa kassaci, yesaṃkesañci, yasmiṃ kismiñci, yamhi kimhici, yattha katthaci, yesu kesuci.

Whatever man, whoever; whatever, whoever; by whomever, by whomever; to/of whomever, to/of whomever; from wherever, by whomever, to/of whomever, to/of whomever; in whomever, in whomever; wherever, in whomever.

Yaṃ kiñcicittaṃ, yāni kānici, yaṃ kiñci, yāni kānici. Sesaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ.

Whatever mind, whatever minds; whatever, whatever minds. The rest is the same as the masculine.

Saṅkhyārāsi

Collection of Numerals

Ekasaddo saṅkhyatthe pavatto ekavacanantova, aññatthe pavatto ekabahuvacananto.

The word ‘eka’ (one), when used in the sense of a number, occurs only in the singular; but when used in other senses, it occurs in both the singular and plural.

Tattha saṅkhyatthe – ekā itthī, ekaṃ, ekāya, ekissā iccādi. Punnapuṃsakesu ekavacanesu purisa, cittarūpameva.

Therein, in the numerical sense: one woman, one, by one, to/of one, and so forth. In the masculine and neuter singular, the form is just like that of ‘purisa’ and ‘citta’ respectively.

Aññatthe – ekā itthī, ekā itthiyo, ekaṃ, ekā, ekāya, ekissā, ekāhi, ekābhi iccādi.

In other senses: a certain woman, some women; a certain woman, some women; by a certain one, to/of a certain one; by some, by some, and so forth.

Eko puriso, eke, ekaṃ, eke, ekena, ekehi, ekebhi, ekassa, ekesaṃ, ekesānaṃ. Pulliṅga sabbasamaṃ.

A certain man, some men; a certain man, some men; by a certain one, by some, by some; to/of a certain one, of some, of some. The masculine is the same as 'sabba'.

Ekaṃ kulaṃ, ekāni kulāni, ekaṃ kulaṃ, ekāni kulāni. Sesaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ.

A certain family, some families; a certain family, some families. The rest is the same as the masculine.

Kapaccaye pare sabbādirūpaṃ natthi.

When the suffix ‘ka’ follows, the pronominal forms of ‘sabba’ and so forth are not used.

“Ekikā sayane setu, yā te ambe avāhari jā. 1.4.175. Ekākinī gahaṭṭhāhaṃ, mātuyā paricoditā”ti apa. therī 2.3.188 pāḷi, ekako puriso, ekakaṃ, ekakena. Ekakaṃ kulaṃ iccādi ekavacanantameva, ekakānaṃ bahutte vattabbe dve ekakā, dve ekake[M 0.0136], dvīhi ekakehīti labbhati. “Pañcālo ca videho ca, ubho ekā bhavantu te”ti pāḷi. Iminā nayena bahuvacanampi labbhati. ‘Ekā’ti missakā.

The Pāḷi states: “Ekikā sayane setu, yā te ambe avāhari. Ekākinī gahaṭṭhāhaṃ, mātuyā paricoditā.” A single man is 'ekako puriso'; 'ekakaṃ', 'ekakena'. 'Ekakaṃ kulaṃ', and so forth, are only singular. When the plural of 'ekaka' is to be expressed, one obtains 'dve ekakā', 'dve ekake', 'dvīhi ekakehi'. The Pāḷi also states: “Pañcālo ca videho ca, ubho ekā bhavantu te.” By this principle, a plural is also obtained. 'Ekā' here means united.

Paṭisedhayutte pana anekā itthiyo, anekāsaṃ itthīnaṃ. Aneke purisā, anekesaṃ purisānaṃ. Anekāni kulāni, anekesaṃ kulānaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ pana “nekāni dhaññagaṇāni, nekāni khettagaṇāni, nekānaṃ dhaññagaṇānaṃ, nekānaṃ khettagaṇāna”ntipi atthi.

However, when joined with a negative: many women, of many women. Many men, of many men. Many families, of many families. Furthermore, in the Pāḷi, there are also found: “nekāni dhaññagaṇāni” (many heaps of grain), “nekāni khettagaṇāni” (many groups of fields), “nekānaṃ dhaññagaṇānaṃ” (of many heaps of grain), and “nekānaṃ khettagaṇānaṃ” (of many groups of fields).

Ekacca, ekacciya, kati, bahusaddāpi idha vattabbā. Ekaccā itthī, ekaccā, ekaccāyoti sabbaṃ kaññāsamaṃ.

The words ‘ekacca,’ ‘ekacciya,’ ‘kati,’ and ‘bahu’ should also be discussed here. ‘Ekaccā itthī’ (a certain woman), ‘ekaccā,’ ‘ekaccāyo’—all are the same as ‘kaññā’.

Ekacco puriso.

A certain man.

135. Ekaccādīhyato ‘ekaccādīhato’ (bahūsu).

135. After 'ekacca' and so forth.

Akārantehi ekaccādīhi yonaṃ ṭe hoti.

After words such as ‘ekacca’ that end in ‘a’, the plural ending ‘yo’ becomes ‘ṭe’.

Ekacce purisā, ekacce purise. Sesaṃ purisasamaṃ. Ādisaddena appekacca, ekatiya, ubhādayo saṅgayhanti. Appekacce purisā, ekatiye purisā, ubhe purisā.

Some men, some men. The rest is the same as ‘purisa’. By the word ‘ādi’ (etc.), ‘appekacca’, ‘ekatiya’, ‘ubha’, and so forth are included. For example: some men, certain men, both men.

Ekaccaṃ cittaṃ.

A certain mind.

236. Na nissa ṭā.

236. There is no ‘ṭā’ for ‘ni’.

Ekaccādīhi nissa ṭā na hoti.

After ‘ekacca’ and so forth, there is no ‘ṭā’ for ‘ni’.

Ekaccāni cittāni. Sesaṃ cittasamaṃ.

Some minds. The rest is the same as ‘citta’.

Ekacciya, ekacceyya, ekatiyasaddā kaññā, purisa, cittanayā. “Itthīpi hi ekacciyā, seyyā posa janādhipa saṃ. ni. 1.127. Saccaṃ kirevamāhaṃsu, narā ekacciyā idha. Kaṭṭhaṃ niplavitaṃ seyyo, na tvevekacciyo [M 0.0137] naro”ti jā. 1.1.73 ca “parivāritā muñcare ekacceyyā”ti ca “na vissase ekatiyesū”ti ca pāḷī – tattha ‘niplavita’nti udakato ubbhataṃ.

The words ‘ekacciya’, ‘ekacceyya’, and ‘ekatiya’ follow the patterns of ‘kaññā’, ‘purisa’, and ‘citta’. The Pāḷi states: “For even a certain woman is superior, O lord of men... Truly, they have said thus, some men here. A floating log is better, but not a certain man.” And: “some, being surrounded, are released.” And: “do not trust in some.” Therein, ‘niplavita’ means ‘raised from the water’.

Katisaddo bahuvacanantova.

The word ‘kati’ is only plural.

237. Ṭikatimhā rū. 120 piṭṭhe.

237. After 'kati', 'ṭi'.

Katimhā yonaṃ ṭi hoti.

After ‘kati’, the plural ending ‘yo’ becomes ‘ṭi’.

Kati itthiyo, kati purisā, kati purise, kati cittāni. Katihi itthīhi, katihi purisehi, katihi cittehi.

How many women, how many men, how many men, how many minds? By how many women, by how many men, by how many minds?

238. Bahukatīnaṃ ‘bahu katinnaṃ’ (bahūsu).

238. For ‘bahu’ and ‘kati’.

Naṃmhi bahu, katīnaṃ ante nuka hoti.

When ‘naṃ’ is present, ‘nuka’ occurs at the end of ‘bahu’ and ‘kati’.

Katinnaṃ itthīnaṃ, katinnaṃ purisānaṃ, katinnaṃ cittānaṃ, ayaṃ nāgamo bahulaṃ na hoti, ‘katinaṃ tithīnaṃ pūraṇī katimī’ti ca dissati. “Bahūnaṃ vassasatānaṃ, bahūnaṃ vassasahassāna”nti ca “bahūnaṃ kusaladhammānaṃ, bahūnaṃ akusaladhammāna”nti ca “bahūnaṃ vata atthāya, uppajjiṃsu tathāgatā”ti vi. va. 807 ca pāḷī.

Of how many women, of how many men, of how many minds. This ‘na’ augmentation does not usually occur. And ‘katinaṃ tithīnaṃ pūraṇī katimī’ is also seen. “Of many hundreds of years, of many thousands of years,” and “of many wholesome qualities, of many unwholesome qualities,” and “for the benefit of many, the Tathāgatas arose”—these are Pāli passages.

Katisu itthīsu, katisu purisesu, katisu cittesu.

In how many women, in how many men, in how many minds.

Bahusadde dvīsu naṃvacanesu bahunnaṃ, bahunnanti vattabbaṃ. Sesaṃ dhenu, bhikkhu, āyusadisaṃ.

With the word ‘bahu’, in the two ‘naṃ’ (genitive plural) forms, ‘bahunnaṃ’ and ‘bahunnaṃ’ should be stated. The rest is like ‘dhenu’, ‘bhikkhu’, and ‘āyu’.

Kapaccaye kaññā, purisa, cittasadisaṃ, bahū itthiyo, bahukā itthiyo. Bahū purisā, bahavo purisā, bahukā purisā. Bahūni cittāni, bahukāni cittāni iccādinā vattabbaṃ. Bahūnaṃ [M 0.0138] samudāyāpekkhane sati ekavacanampi labbhati, “bahujanassa atthāya bahujanassa hitāya, bahuno janassa atthāya hitāyā”ti a. ni. 1.141 pāḷi.

With the suffix ‘ka’, it is like ‘kaññā’, ‘purisa’, and ‘citta’. Many women, many women (with ‘ka’). Many men, many men, many men (with ‘ka’). Many minds, many minds (with ‘ka’), and so forth should be stated. When considering a collection of many, the singular form is also found, as in the Pāli passage: “for the benefit of many people, for the welfare of many people,” and “for the benefit and welfare of many people.”

Ubhasaddo bahuvacanantova, ‘ubhagohi ṭo’ti yonaṃ ṭo, ubho itthiyo, purisā, kulāni gacchanti, ubho itthiyo, purisā, kulāni passati.

The word ‘ubha’ is only plural-ending. By the rule ‘ubhagohi ṭo’, ‘ṭo’ replaces ‘yo’. Both women, men, and families go. Both women, men, and families he sees.

239. Suhisubhasso nī. 313 (rū. 109 piṭṭhe).

239. For ‘ubha’, ‘o’ in ‘su’ and ‘hi’.

Su, hisu ubhassa anto o hoti.

In the case of ‘su’ and ‘hi’, the final vowel of ‘ubha’ becomes ‘o’.

Ubhohi, ubhosu.

Ubhohi, ubhosu.

240. Ubhinnaṃ ka. 86; nīrū. 227; nī. 341.

240. Ubhinnaṃ.

Ubhamhā naṃvacanassa innaṃ hoti.

After ‘ubha’, the case ending ‘naṃ’ becomes ‘innaṃ’.

Ubhinnaṃ. Sabbattha itthi, purisa, kulehi yojetabbaṃ.

Of both. Everywhere, it should be combined with words like ‘itthi’, ‘purisa’, and ‘kula’.

241. Yomhi dvinnaṃ duvedve ka. 132; rū. 228; ni. 310.

241. In the case of ‘yo’, for ‘dvi’, ‘duve’ and ‘dve’.

Yosu savibhattissa dvissa duve, dve honti. ‘Dvinna’nti vacanaṃ dvissa bahuvacanantaniyamatthaṃ.

In the case of ‘yo’, for the inflected ‘dvi’, ‘duve’ and ‘dve’ occur. The mention of ‘dvinnaṃ’ is for the purpose of restricting ‘dvi’ to being plural-ending.

Dve itthiyo, dve purisā, dve purise, dve cittāni, duve itthiyo, duve purisā, duve purise, duve cittāni, dvīhi, dvībhi.

Two women, two men, two men (accusative), two minds; two women, two men, two men (accusative), two minds; by two, by two.

242. Naṃmhi nuka dvādīnaṃ sattarasannaṃ ka. 67; nī. 229; nī. 214.

242. In the case of ‘naṃ’, ‘nuka’ for ‘dvi’ and the numbers up to seventeen.

Naṃmhi [M 0.0139] pare dvādīnaṃ aṭṭhārasantānaṃ sattarasannaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ ante nuka hoti. U-kāro uccāraṇattho. Kānubandhaṃ disvā anteti ñāyati.

When ‘naṃ’ follows, ‘nuka’ occurs at the end of the numbers from ‘dvi’ up to eighteen, that is, seventeen. The vowel ‘u’ is for the sake of pronunciation. Seeing the ‘ka’ as an anubandha (marker), it is understood that it is at the end.

Dvinnaṃ.

Of two.

243. Duvinnaṃ naṃmhi ka. 132; rū. 228; nī. 244.

243. ‘Duvinnaṃ’ in the case of ‘naṃ’.

Naṃmhi savibhattissa dvissa duvinnaṃ hoti vā.

In the case of ‘naṃ’, for the inflected ‘dvi’, ‘duvinnaṃ’ occurs optionally.

Duvinnaṃ, dvīhi, dvībhi, dvinnaṃ, duvinnaṃ, dvīsu. Mahāvuttinā sumhi duve hoti, nāgassa duvesu dantesu nimmitā vi. va. 706, cakkāni pādesu duvesu vindati dī. ni. 3.205. Evañca sati duvehi, duvebhītipi siddhameva hoti, ayaṃ dvisaddo ubhasaddo viya aliṅgo.

Duvinnaṃ, by two, by two, dvinnaṃ, duvinnaṃ, in two. According to the Mahāvutti, in the case of ‘su’, ‘duve’ occurs, as in “fashioned on the two tusks of the elephant,” and “he finds wheels on two feet.” This being so, ‘duvehi’ and ‘duvebhi’ are also indeed established. This word ‘dvi’, like the word ‘ubha’, is without gender.

244. Tisso catasso yomhi savibhattīnaṃ ka. 133; rū. 230; nī. 311.

244. ‘Tisso’ and ‘catasso’ in the case of ‘yo’ for the inflected forms.

Itthiyaṃ yosu savibhattīnanti, catunnaṃ tisso, catasso honti.

In the feminine gender, in the case of ‘yo’, for the inflected ‘ti’ and ‘catu’, ‘tisso’ and ‘catasso’ occur.

Tisso itthiyo, catasso itthiyo.

Three women, four women.

Mahāvuttinā hisu ca tissa, catassā honti, “tissehi catassehi parisāhi, catassehi sahito lokanāyako”ti pāḷī. Tīhi, tībhi itthīhi, catūhi, catūbhi, catubbhi itthīhi.

According to the Mahāvutti, in the case of ‘hi’, ‘tissa’ and ‘catassā’ also occur, as in the Pāli passage: “with three or four assemblies,” and “the world leader accompanied by four.” By three women, by three women; by four women, by four women, by four women.

245. Naṃmhi ticatunnamitthiyaṃ tissacatassā dī. ni. 3.205.

245. In the case of ‘naṃ’, for ‘ti’ and ‘catu’ in the feminine, ‘tissa’ and ‘catassā’.

Itthiyaṃ naṃmhiti, catunnaṃ tissa, catassā honti.

In the feminine gender, in the case of ‘naṃ’, for ‘ti’ and ‘catu’, ‘tissa’ and ‘catassā’ occur.

Tissannaṃ [M 0.0140] itthīnaṃ, catassannaṃ itthīnaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ itthīnaṃ, catunnaṃ itthīnaṃ, samaṇo gotamo catunnaṃ parisānaṃ sakkato hoti, catunnaṃ parisānaṃ piyo hoti manāpoti dī. ni. 1.304, tissehi, catassehi, tīhi, tībhi, catūhi, catūbhi, catubbhi, tissannaṃ, catassannaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ, catunnaṃ, tīsu, catūsu.

Of three women, of four women, of three women, of four women. The ascetic Gotama is honored by the four assemblies, is beloved and pleasing to the four assemblies. By three, by four, by three, by three, by four, by four, by four; of three, of four, of three, of four; in three, in four.

Pāḷiyaṃ “catassehī”ti diṭṭhattā tissesu, catassesūtipi diṭṭhameva hoti.

In the Pāli, because “catassehi” is seen, “tissesu” and “catassesu” are also indeed seen.

246. Pume tayo cattāro ka. 133; rū. 230; nī. 311.

246. In the masculine, ‘tayo’ and ‘cattāro’.

Pulliṅge yosu savibhattīnanti, catunnaṃ tayo, cattāro honti.

In the masculine gender, for the inflected stems 'ti' (three) and 'catu' (four), the forms for the 'yo' endings (nominative/accusative plural) are 'tayo' and 'cattāro'.

Tayo purisā, tayo purise, cattāro purisā, cattāro purise.

Three men, three men (acc.), four men, four men (acc.).

247. Caturo catussa ka. 78, 205, 31; rū. 160; nī. 234; ‘caturo vā catussa’ (bahūsu).

247. ‘Caturo’ for ‘catu’.

Pume savibhattissa catusaddassa caturo hoti.

In the masculine, for the inflected word ‘catu’, ‘caturo’ occurs.

Caturo purisā, caturo purise. Kathaṃ caturo nimitte nādassiṃ, caturo phalamuttameti? “Liṅgavipallāsā”ti vuttiyaṃ vuttaṃ, tīhi, tībhi, catūhi, catūbhi, catubbhi.

Four men, four men (acc.). How is it in the examples: 'caturo nimitte nādassiṃ' (I did not see the four signs), and 'caturo phalamuttame' (the four supreme fruits)? It is said in the commentary that this is due to “gender inversion.” By three, by three; by four, by four, by four.

248. Iṇṇaṃiṇṇannaṃ tito jhā ka. 87; rū. 231; nī. 243; ‘ṇṇaṃṇṇannaṃtiko jhā’ (bahūsu).

248. ‘Iṇṇaṃ’ and ‘iṇṇannaṃ’ from ‘ti’ when ‘jha’ is present.

Jhasaññamhā timhā naṃvacanassa iṇṇaṃ, iṇṇannaṃ honti.

From ‘ti’ (three) when it has the ‘jha’ designation, the ‘naṃ’ (genitive plural) becomes ‘iṇṇaṃ’ and ‘iṇṇannaṃ’.

Tiṇṇaṃ, tiṇṇannaṃ, catunnaṃ, tīhi, tībhi, catūhi, catūbhi, catubbhi, tiṇṇaṃ, tiṇṇannaṃ, catunnaṃ, tīsu, catūsu.

Of three, of three, of four; by three, by three; by four, by four, by four; of three, of three, of four; in three, in four.

249. Tīṇicattāri napuṃsake ka. 133; rū. 230; nī. 311.

249. ‘Tīṇi’ and ‘cattāri’ in the neuter.

Napuṃsake [M 0.0141] yosu savibhattīnanti, catunnaṃ tīṇi, cattāri honti.

In the neuter gender, for the inflected stems 'ti' (three) and 'catu' (four), the forms for the 'yo' endings (nominative/accusative plural) are 'tīṇi' and 'cattāri'.

Tīṇi cittāni, cattāri cittāni. Sesaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ.

Three minds, four minds. The rest is like the masculine gender.

Vacanasiliṭṭhatte pana sati visadisaliṅgavacanānampi padānaṃ aññamaññasaṃyogo hoti, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā dī. ni. 3.145, cattāro sammappadhānā dī. ni. 3.145, tayomahābhūtā, tayo mahābhūte paṭṭhā. 1.1.58, sabbe mālā upenti maṃ dhu. 3.6, sabbe kaññā upenti maṃ dhu. 3.6, sabbe ratanā upenti maṃ dhu. 3.6, sabbe yānā upenti maṃ dhu. 3.6, avijjāya sati saṅkhārā honti, saṅkhāresu sati viññāṇaṃ hoti saṃ. ni. 2.50 iccādi.

However, when there is syntactic connection, even words of different genders and numbers can be mutually combined, such as: the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right exertions, the three great elements, the three great elements (acc.), all garlands approach me, all maidens approach me, all jewels approach me, all vehicles approach me; with ignorance as condition, volitional formations arise; with volitional formations as condition, consciousness arises, and so on.

Gāthāsu vipallāsāpi bahulaṃ dissanti, aññe dhammāni desenti, evaṃ dhammāni sutvāna, satañca dhammāni sukittitāni sutvā, atthāni cintayitvāna, uttamatthāni tayi labhimhā, kiṃ tvaṃ atthāni jānāsi, iccheyyāmi bhante sattaputtāni, siviputtāni avhaya jā. 2.22.2235, puttadārāni posenti, balībaddāni soḷasa iccādi.

In verses, inversions are also frequently seen: others teach the Dhamma; thus, having heard the Dhamma; having heard the well-praised Dhamma of the virtuous; having reflected on the meanings; we have attained the highest meanings in you; do you know the meanings?; I wish, venerable sir, for seven sons; call the sons of Sivi; they support wives and children; sixteen oxen; and so on.

Idha sesasaṅkhyānāmāni dīpiyante.

Here, the remaining numerical terms are explained.

250. Ṭa pañcādīhi cuddasahi ka. 134; rū. 251; nī. 247.

250. ‘Ṭa’ for the fourteen numerals from five onwards.

Pañcādīhi aṭṭhārasantehi saṅkhyāsaddehi yonaṃ ṭa hoti.

From the numerical words beginning with five and ending with eighteen, the ‘yo’ ending becomes ‘ṭa’.

Pañca itthiyo, pañca purisā, purise, pañca cittāni, cha itthiyo.

Five women, five men, five men (acc.), five minds, six women.

Ḷāgame [M 0.0142] pana “itthibhāvā na muccissaṃ, chaḷāni gatiyo imā”ti pāḷi.

However, with the augment ‘ḷa’, there is the Pāli text: ‘itthibhāvā na muccissaṃ, chaḷāni gatiyo imā’ (I will not be freed from womanhood; these are the six destinations).

Cha purisā, cha purise, cha cittāni. Evaṃ satta, aṭṭha, nava, dasa, ekādasa…pe… aṭṭhārasa.

Six men, six men (acc.), six minds. Thus seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven… up to… eighteen.

251. Pañcādīnaṃ cuddasannama ka. 90; rū. 252; nī. 247.

251. Of the fourteen numerals beginning with five, a.

Su, naṃ, hisu pañcādīnaṃ cuddasannaṃ assa attameva hoti, na ettaṃ vā dīghattaṃ vā hoti.

With the endings 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hi', for the fourteen numerals beginning with five, the stem vowel 'a' remains as 'a'; there is no shortening or lengthening.

Pañcahi, pañcannaṃ, pañcasu, chahi, channaṃ, chasu, sattahi, sattannaṃ, sattasu, aṭṭhahi, aṭṭhannaṃ, aṭṭhasu, navahi, navannaṃ, navasu, dasahi, dasannaṃ, dasasu, ekādasahi, ekādasannaṃ, ekādasasu…pe… aṭṭhārasahi, aṭṭhārasannaṃ, aṭṭhārasasu.

By five, of five, in five; by six, of six, in six; by seven, of seven, in seven; by eight, of eight, in eight; by nine, of nine, in nine; by ten, of ten, in ten; by eleven, of eleven, in eleven… up to… by eighteen, of eighteen, in eighteen.

Ete sabbe aliṅgā bahuvacanantā eva.

All these are without gender and are always in the plural.

‘Itthiyamatvā’ti vīsa, tiṃsa, cattālīsa, paññāsehi āpaccayo, mahāvuttinā simhi rasso silopo ca, ‘niggahīta’nti vikappena niggahītāgamo, vikappena aṃlopo, nādīnaṃ ekavacanānaṃ yādeso, vīsa itthiyo, vīsaṃ itthiyo, vīsa purisā, vīsaṃ purisā, vīsa purise, vīsaṃ purise, vīsa cittāni, vīsaṃ cittāni, vīsāya itthīhi kammaṃ kataṃ, vīsāya purisehi kammaṃ kataṃ, vīsāya kulehi kammaṃ kataṃ, vīsāya itthīnaṃ, purisānaṃ, kulānaṃ, sattamiyaṃ vīsāya itthīsu, purisesu, kulesu.

By the rule 'Itthiyamatvā', with twenty, thirty, forty, and fifty, there is the 'ā' suffix; according to the Mahāvutti, with the 'si' ending, there is shortening and elision of 'si'; optionally, there is the niggahīta augment and elision of 'aṃ'; for the singular endings of the 'nā' group, there is the substitution of 'yā'. Examples: twenty women (vīsa/vīsaṃ), twenty men (vīsa/vīsaṃ), twenty men (acc.) (vīsa/vīsaṃ), twenty minds (vīsa/vīsaṃ); a deed was done by twenty women, by twenty men, by twenty families; of twenty women, men, and families; in the locative case: among twenty women, men, and families.

Tipaccaye vīsati, tiṃsatisaddāpi saṭṭhi, sattati, asīti, navutisaddā viya niccaṃ itthi liṅgekavacanantā eva, si, aṃlopo, vīsati itthiyo, vīsati purisā, purise, vīsati kulāni, vīsatiyā itthīhi, itthīnaṃ, purisehi, purisānaṃ, kulehi, kulānaṃ[M 0.0143], vīsatiyā, vīsatiyaṃ itthi, purisa, kulesu, evaṃ yāvanavutiyā veditabbā. Vaggabhede pana sati bahuvacanampi vikappena dissati, dve vīsatiyo iccādi.

With the 'ti' suffix, the words 'vīsati' and 'tiṃsati', like the words 'saṭṭhi', 'sattati', 'asīti', and 'navuti', are always of feminine gender and singular number only, with the elision of 'si' and 'aṃ'. For example: 'vīsati itthiyo' (twenty women), 'vīsati purisā' (twenty men), 'vīsati purise' (twenty men, acc.), 'vīsati kulāni' (twenty families); 'vīsatiyā itthīhi' (by twenty women), 'vīsatiyā itthīnaṃ' (of twenty women), 'vīsatiyā purisehi' (by twenty men), 'vīsatiyā purisānaṃ' (of twenty men), 'vīsatiyā kulehi' (by twenty families), 'vīsatiyā kulānaṃ' (of twenty families); 'vīsatiyā' or 'vīsatiyaṃ' (in twenty) with 'itthīsu', 'purisesu', 'kulesu' (in women, men, families). Thus, it should be understood up to ninety. However, when there is a division into groups, the plural number is also seen optionally, such as 'two twenties' and so forth.

Sataṃ, sahassaṃ, dasasahassaṃ, satasahassaṃ, dasasatasahassanti ime napuṃsakaliṅgāyeva. Saṅkhyeyyapadhāne pana itthiliṅge vattabbe sahassī, dasasahassī, satasahassīti itthiliṅgaṃ bhavati. Vaggabhede pana dve satāni, tīṇi satāni, dve sahassāni, tīṇi sahassāni iccādīni bhavanti. Koṭi, pakoṭi, koṭipakoṭi, akkhobhiṇīsaddā itthiliṅgā eva. Sesaṃ sabbaṃ yāvaasaṅkhyeyyā napuṃsakameva.

A hundred, a thousand, ten thousand, a hundred thousand, and ten hundred thousand—these are all of neuter gender. However, when the enumerated is primary and is to be expressed in the feminine gender, then 'sahassī', 'dasasahassī', and 'satasahassī' become feminine. In the case of divisions into groups, then 'dve satāni' (two hundreds), 'tīṇi satāni' (three hundreds), 'dve sahassāni' (two thousands), 'tīṇi sahassāni' (three thousands), and so forth, occur. The words 'koṭi', 'pakoṭi', 'koṭipakoṭi', and 'akkhobhiṇī' are always of feminine gender. All the rest, up to 'asaṅkhyeyya', are neuter only.

Sahassaṃ kāsi nāma, dasasahassaṃ nahutaṃ nāma, satasahassaṃ lakkhaṃ nāma.

A thousand is called 'kāsi'; ten thousand is called 'nahuta'; a hundred thousand is called 'lakkha'.

Duvidhaṃ padhānaṃ saṅkhyāpadhānaṃ, saṅkhyeyyapadhānañca. Purisānaṃ vīsati hoti, purisānaṃ navuti hoti, purisānaṃ sataṃ hoti, sahassaṃ hoti iccādi saṅkhyāpadhānaṃ nāma, vīsati purisā, navuti purisā, sataṃ purisā, sahassaṃ purisā iccādi saṅkhyeyyapadhānaṃ nāma.

There are two kinds of principal usage: numerical principal usage ('saṅkhyāpadhāna') and enumerated principal usage ('saṅkhyeyyapadhāna'). For example: 'purisānaṃ vīsati hoti' (there are twenty of men), 'purisānaṃ navuti hoti' (there are ninety of men), 'purisānaṃ sataṃ hoti' (there are a hundred of men), 'sahassaṃ hoti' (there are a thousand) and so forth—this is called numerical principal usage. 'vīsati purisā' (twenty men), 'navuti purisā' (ninety men), 'sataṃ purisā' (a hundred men), 'sahassaṃ purisā' (a thousand men) and so forth—this is called enumerated principal usage.

Etthapi vīsatisaddo itthiliṅgekavacano eva. Sata, sahassasaddā napuṃsakekavacanā eva. Saṅkhyāsaddānaṃ pana padavidhānañca guṇavidhānañca samāsakaṇḍe āgamissati.

Here too, the word 'vīsati' is always of feminine gender and singular number. The words 'sata' and 'sahassa' are always of neuter gender and singular number. However, the formation of numerals and their qualifying properties will come in the section on compounds.

Saṅkhyārāsi niṭṭhito.

The section on numerals is concluded.

252. Simhāhaṃ ka. 149; rū. 232; nī. 319; ‘simhahaṃ’ (bahūsu).

252. In the `si` case ending, `ahaṃ`.

Simhi savibhattissa amhassa ahaṃ hoti.

In the `si` case ending, `ahaṃ` is the substitute for `amha` together with its case ending.

Ahaṃ gacchāmi.

I go.

253. Mayamasmāmhassa ka. 121; rū. 233; nī. 296.

253. `Mayaṃ` and `asmā` for `amha`.

Yosu [M 0.0144] savibhattissa amhassa kamena mayaṃ, asmā honti vā.

In the `yo` and `su` case endings, `mayaṃ` and `asmā` are optionally the respective substitutes for `amha` together with its case ending.

Mayaṃ gacchāma, asme passāmi.

We go; I see us.

Pakkhe –

Alternatively:

‘Yonameṭa’ iti vidhi, amhe gacchāma.

By the rule ‘Yonameṭa’, `amhe gacchāma`.

254. Tumhassa tuvaṃtvaṃmhi ca ka. 146; rū. 236; nī. 324; ‘tumhassa tuvaṃtvamamhica’ (bahūsu).

254. For `tumha`, `tuvaṃ` and `tvaṃ` in `si` and `aṃ`.

Simhi ca aṃmhi ca savibhattissa tumhassa tuvaṃ, tvaṃ honti.

In the `si` and `aṃ` case endings, `tuvaṃ` and `tvaṃ` are the substitutes for `tumha` together with its case ending.

Tuvaṃ buddho tuvaṃ satthā, tuvaṃ mārābhibhū muni theragā. 839, tvaṃ no satthā anuttaro, tumhe gacchatha, tuvaṃ passati, tvaṃ passati.

You are the Buddha, you are the Teacher, you are the Sage who has overcome Māra; you are our unsurpassed Teacher. You (plural) go. He sees you (singular); he sees you (singular).

255. Aṃmhi taṃ maṃ tavaṃ mamaṃ ka. 143-4; rū. 234-5; nī. 322.

255. In the `aṃ` case ending: `taṃ`, `maṃ`, `tavaṃ`, `mamaṃ`.

Aṃmhi savibhattīnaṃ tumhā’mhānaṃ taṃ, maṃ, tavaṃ, mamaṃ honti.

In the `aṃ` case ending, `taṃ`, `maṃ`, `tavaṃ`, and `mamaṃ` are the substitutes for `tumha` and `amha` together with their case endings.

Maṃ passati, mamaṃ passati, taṃ passati, tavaṃ passati, amhe passati, tumhe passati.

He sees me; he sees me. He sees you (singular); he sees you (singular). He sees us; he sees you (plural).

256. Dutiyāyomhi vā ka. 162; rū. 237; nī. 345; ‘dutiye yomhi vā’ (bahūsu).

256. In the `yo` of the second case, optionally.

Dutiyāyomhi savibhattīnaṃ tumhā’mhānaṃ ṅānubandhā aṃ, ākaṃādesā honti vā.

In the `yo` of the second case, for `tumha` and `amha` together with their case endings, the substitutes `aṃ` and `ākaṃ`, which have the indicator `ṅā`, optionally occur.

Amhaṃ, amhākaṃ passati, tumhaṃ, tumhākaṃ passati.

He sees us, he sees us; he sees you (plural), he sees you (plural).

257. Nāsmāsu tayāmayā ka. 145, 270; rū. 238, 120; nī. 323, 542.

257. In the `nā` and `smā` case endings, `tayā` and `mayā`.

Nā[M 0.0145], smāsu savibhattīnaṃ tumhā’mhānaṃ tayā, mayā honti.

In the `nā` and `smā` case endings, `tayā` and `mayā` are the substitutes for `tumha` and `amha` together with their case endings.

Mayā kataṃ, tayā kataṃ, mayā apeti, tayā apeti.

Done by me, done by you (singular); departs from me, departs from you (singular).

258. Tayātayīnaṃ tva vā tassa ka. 210; rū. 239; nī. 435.

258. For `tayā` and `tayī`, `tva` is the optional substitute for its `ta`.

Tayā, tayīnaṃ tassa tva hoti vā.

For `tayā` and `tayī`, `tva` is the optional substitute for their `ta` part.

Tvayā kataṃ, tvayā apeti, amhehi kataṃ, tumhehi kataṃ.

Done by you (singular), departs from you (singular); done by us, done by you (plural).

259. Tavamamatuyhaṃmayhaṃ se ka. 141-2; rū. 241-2; nī. 321.

259. In the `sa` case ending: `tava`, `mama`, `tuyhaṃ`, `mayhaṃ`.

Samhi savibhattīnaṃ tumhā’mhānaṃ tavādayo honti.

In the `sa` case ending, `tava` and the others are the substitutes for `tumha` and `amha` together with their case endings.

Mama dīyate, mayhaṃ dīyate, tava dīyate, tuyhaṃ dīyate.

It is given to me, it is given to me; it is given to you (singular), it is given to you (singular).

260. Naṃsesvasmākaṃmamaṃ nī. 438.

260. In `naṃ` and `su`, `asmākaṃ` and `mamaṃ`.

Naṃ, sesu savibhattissa amhassa kamena asmākaṃ, mamaṃ honti.

In the `naṃ` and `su` case endings, `asmākaṃ` and `mamaṃ` are the respective substitutes for `amha` together with its case ending.

Mamaṃ dīyate, asmākaṃ dīyate.

It is given to me; it is given to us.

261. Ṅaṃṅākaṃ naṃmhi ka. 161; rū. 244; nī. 344.

261. When naṃ follows, ṅaṃ and ṅākaṃ.

Naṃmhi savibhattīnaṃ tumhā’mhānaṃ ṅānubandhā aṃ, ākaṃādesā honti vā.

When the ending naṃ follows, for tumha and amha with their case endings, the substitutes aṃ and ākaṃ, which have ṅa as an anubandha, optionally occur.

Amhaṃ dīyate, amhākaṃ dīyate, tumhaṃ dīyate, tumhākaṃ dīyate. Pañcamiyaṃ mayā, tayā, tvayā, pubbe vuttāva.

It is given to us, it is given to us; it is given to you (pl.), it is given to you (pl.). In the fifth case, mayā, tayā, and tvayā have already been stated.

262. Smāmhi tvamhā.

262. When smā follows, tvamhā.

Smāmhi [M 0.0146] savibhattissa tumhassa tvamhā hoti.

When the smā ending follows, tvamhā occurs for tumha with its case ending.

Tvamhā apeti, amhehi, tumhehi, mama, mamaṃ, mayhaṃ, tava, tuyhaṃ, amhaṃ, amhākaṃ, asmākaṃ, tumhaṃ, tumhākaṃ.

He departs from you; by us, by you (pl.); of me, of me, to me; of you, to you; of us, of us, of us; of you (pl.), of you (pl.).

263. Smiṃmhi tumhamhānaṃ tayimayi ka. 139; rū. 245; nī. 318.

263. When smiṃ follows, tayi and mayi for tumha and amha.

Smiṃmhi savibhattīnaṃ tumhā’mhānaṃ tayi, mayi honti.

When the smiṃ ending follows, tayi and mayi occur for tumha and amha with their case endings.

Tayi, mayi, tvatte tvayi, amhesu, tumhesu.

In you (sg.), in me; tvatte or tvayi; in us, in you (pl.).

264. Sumhāmhassāsmā nī. 438.

264. When su follows, asmā for amha.

Sumhi amhassa asmā hoti.

When the su ending follows, asmā occurs for amha.

Asmāsu.

In us.

Mahāvuttinā yo, hisu amhassa asmādeso, yonaṃ ettañca, asmā gacchāma, asme passati, asmāhi kataṃ, asmākaṃ dīyate, asmāhi apeti, asmākaṃ dhanaṃ, asmāsu ṭhitaṃ. “Asmābhijappanti janā anekā”ti jā. 1.7.68 pāḷi-asme abhijappanti patthentīti attho. “Asmābhi pariciṇṇosi, mettacittā hi nāyakā”ti apa. therī 2.2.230 therīpāḷi – ‘pariciṇṇo’ti paricārito.

According to the Mahāvutti, when the endings yo, hi, and su follow, asmā is the substitute for amha, and e is substituted for yo. For example: asmā gacchāma (we go), asme passati (he sees us), asmāhi kataṃ (done by us), asmākaṃ dīyate (it is given to us), asmāhi apeti (he departs from us), asmākaṃ dhanaṃ (our wealth), asmāsu ṭhitaṃ (standing in us). The Pāli text states: 'asmābhijappanti janā anekā' (Many people long for us)—the meaning is 'they long for us, they desire'. The Therīpāli states: 'asmābhi pariciṇṇosi, mettacittā hi nāyakā' (You have been attended to by us, O leaders with minds of loving-kindness)—'pariciṇṇo' means 'served'.

Catutthiyaṃ asmākaṃ adhipannānaṃ, khamassu rājakuñjara jā. 2.21.181 – ‘adhipannāna’nti dukkhābhibhūtānaṃ.

In the fourth case: 'asmākaṃ adhipannānaṃ, khamassu rājakuñjara' (Forgive us, the afflicted, O royal elephant)—'adhipannānaṃ' means 'those overcome by suffering'.

Chaṭṭhiyaṃ esasmākaṃ kule dhammo jā. 1.4.147, esā asmākaṃ dhammatā.

In the sixth case: 'esasmākaṃ kule dhammo' (This is the Dhamma in our family), 'esā asmākaṃ dhammatā' (this is our nature).

Sattamiyaṃ yaṃ kiccaṃ parame mitte, katamasmāsu taṃ tayā. Pattā nissaṃsayaṃ tvamhā, bhattirasmāsu yā tava jā. 2.21.81 – tattha ‘yaṃ [M 0.0147] kicca’nti yaṃ kammaṃ kattabbaṃ, tava asmāsu yā bhatti, tāya mayaṃ tvamhā nissaṃsayataṃ pattāti attho.

In the seventh case: 'yaṃ kiccaṃ parame mitte, katamasmāsu taṃ tayā' (Whatever duty towards a supreme friend, that has been done by you for us). 'pattā nissaṃsayaṃ tvamhā, bhattirasmāsu yā tava' (We have attained certainty from you, through the devotion you have for us)—there, 'yaṃ kiccaṃ' means 'whatever action is to be done'; 'by the devotion you have for us, we have attained certainty from you' is the meaning.

265. Apādādo padatekavākye caṃ. 6.3.15; pā. 8.1.17, 18.

265. Not at the beginning of a pāda, after a word, in a single sentence.

Apādādimhi pavattānaṃ padato paresaṃ ekavākye ṭhitānaṃ tumhā’mhānaṃ vidhi hoti. Adhikārasuttamidaṃ.

The rule applies to the forms of tumha and amha that occur not at the beginning of a pāda, but after a word and within a single sentence. This is a governing rule.

266. Yonaṃhisvapañcamyā vono ka. 147, 151; rū. 246, 250; nī. 325, 329, 330.

266. When yo, naṃ, hi, and su follow, except in the fifth case, vo and no.

Pañcamīvajjitesu yo, naṃ, hisu paresu apādādopavattānaṃ padato paresaṃ ekavākye ṭhitānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tumhā’mhasaddānaṃ vo, no honti vā.

When the endings yo, naṃ, hi, and su follow, except for the fifth case, vo and no optionally occur for the words tumha and amha with their case endings, when they occur not at the beginning of a pāda, but after a word and standing in a single sentence.

Gacchatha vo, gacchatha tumhe, gacchāma no, gacchāma amhe, passeyya vo, passeyya tumhe, passeyya no, passeyya amhe, dīyate vo, dīyate tumhākaṃ, dīyate no, dīyate amhākaṃ, dhanaṃ vo, dhanaṃ tumhākaṃ, dhanaṃ no, dhanaṃ amhākaṃ, kataṃ vo puññaṃ, kataṃ tumhehi puññaṃ, kataṃ no puññaṃ, kataṃ amhehi puññaṃ.

You (pl.) go (gacchatha vo), you (pl.) go (gacchatha tumhe); we go (gacchāma no), we go (gacchāma amhe); may he see you (pl.) (passeyya vo), may he see you (pl.) (passeyya tumhe); may he see us (passeyya no), may he see us (passeyya amhe); it is given to you (pl.) (dīyate vo), it is given to you (pl.) (dīyate tumhākaṃ); it is given to us (dīyate no), it is given to us (dīyate amhākaṃ); your (pl.) wealth (dhanaṃ vo), your (pl.) wealth (dhanaṃ tumhākaṃ); our wealth (dhanaṃ no), our wealth (dhanaṃ amhākaṃ); merit has been made by you (pl.) (kataṃ vo puññaṃ), merit has been made by you (pl.) (kataṃ tumhehi puññaṃ); merit has been made by us (kataṃ no puññaṃ), merit has been made by us (kataṃ amhehi puññaṃ).

Apañcamyāti kiṃ? Nissaṭaṃ tumhehi, nissaṭaṃ amhehi.

Why 'except for the fifth case'? Departed from you (nissaṭaṃ tumhehi), departed from us (nissaṭaṃ amhehi).

Apādādotveva? Balañca bhikkhūnamanuppadinnaṃ, tumhehi puññaṃ pasutaṃ anappakaṃ khu. pā. 7.12.

Why 'not at the beginning of a pāda'? 'Balañca bhikkhūnamanuppadinnaṃ, tumhehi puññaṃ pasutaṃ anappakaṃ' (And strength not given to the bhikkhus, much merit has been produced by you).

Padatotveva? Tumhe gacchatha, amhe gacchāma.

Why 'after a word'? Tumhe gacchatha (you go), amhe gacchāma (we go).

Ekavākyetveva? Devadatto tiṭṭhati gāme, tumhe tiṭṭhatha nagare.

Why 'in a single sentence'? Devadatto tiṭṭhati gāme (Devadatta stays in the village), tumhe tiṭṭhatha nagare (you stay in the city).

Savibhattīnantveva? Arahati dhammo tumhādisānaṃ.

Why 'with case endings'? Arahati dhammo tumhādisānaṃ (the Dhamma is fitting for those like you).

267. Teme nāse ka. 148, 150; rū. 247, 249; nī. 326, 328; caṃ. 6.3.17; pā. 8.1.21.

267. When nā and se follow, te and me.

Nā[M 0.0148], sesu tādisānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tumha, amhasaddānaṃ te, me honti vā.

When the nā and se endings follow, te and me optionally occur for the words tumha and amha with their case endings, when they are of that kind.

Kataṃ te puññaṃ, kataṃ tayā puññaṃ, kataṃ me puññaṃ, kataṃ mayā puññaṃ, dinnaṃ te vatthaṃ, dinnaṃ tuyhaṃ vatthaṃ, dinnaṃ me vatthaṃ, dinnaṃ mayhaṃ vatthaṃ, idaṃ te raṭṭhaṃ, idaṃ tava raṭṭhaṃ, idaṃ me raṭṭhaṃ, idaṃ mama raṭṭhaṃ.

Merit has been made by you (sg.) (kataṃ te puññaṃ), merit has been made by you (sg.) (kataṃ tayā puññaṃ); merit has been made by me (kataṃ me puññaṃ), merit has been made by me (kataṃ mayā puññaṃ); a cloth has been given to you (sg.) (dinnaṃ te vatthaṃ), a cloth has been given to you (sg.) (dinnaṃ tuyhaṃ vatthaṃ); a cloth has been given to me (dinnaṃ me vatthaṃ), a cloth has been given to me (dinnaṃ mayhaṃ vatthaṃ); this is your (sg.) kingdom (idaṃ te raṭṭhaṃ), this is your (sg.) kingdom (idaṃ tava raṭṭhaṃ); this is my kingdom (idaṃ me raṭṭhaṃ), this is my kingdom (idaṃ mama raṭṭhaṃ).

268. Anvādese caṃ. 6.3.20; pā. 8.1.23.

268. In anaphoric reference.

Anvādesaṭṭhāne tumhā’mhasaddānaṃ vo, no, te, meādesā niccaṃ bhavanti punabbidhānā.

In the position of anaphoric reference, the substitutes `vo`, `no`, `te`, and `me` for the words `tumha` and `amha` always occur, by restatement.

Gāmo tumhākaṃ pariggaho, atho nagarampi vo pariggaho. Evaṃ sesesu.

The village is your possession; and the town, too, is your possession. Thus it is for the remaining cases.

269. Sapubbā paṭhamantā vā ‘saṃpubbā paṭhamanthā vā’ (mūlapāṭhe) caṃ. 6.1.21; pā. 8.1.26.

269. Or optionally, after a nominative that has a preceding word.

Saṃvijjati pubbapadaṃ assāti sapubbaṃ, sapubbā paṭhamantapadamhā paresaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tumhā’mhasaddānaṃ vo, no, te, meādesā vikappena honti anvādesaṭṭhānepi.

`Sapubbaṃ` is that which has a preceding word. After a nominative word that has a preceding word, for the inflected words `tumha` and `amha` that follow, the substitutes `vo`, `no`, `te`, and `me` occur optionally, even in the position of anaphoric reference.

Gāme paṭo tumhākaṃ, atho nagare kambalaṃ vo, atho nagare kambalaṃ tumhākaṃ vā. Evaṃ sesesu.

In the village, the cloak is yours; and in the city, the blanket is yours (`vo`), or in the city, the blanket is yours (`tumhākaṃ`). Thus it is for the remaining cases.

270. Na cavāhāhevayoge caṃ. 6.3.22; pā. 8.1.24.

270. Not in conjunction with `ca`, `vā`, `ha`, `aha`, and `eva`.

Ca, vā, ha, aha, evasaddehi yoge tumhā’mhānaṃ vo, no, te, meādesā na honti.

In conjunction with the words `ca`, `vā`, `ha`, `aha`, and `eva`, the substitutes `vo`, `no`, `te`, and `me` for `tumha` and `amha` do not occur.

Gāmo [M 0.0149] tava ca mama ca pariggaho, gāmo tava vā mama vā pariggaho iccādi.

The village is the possession of both you and me; the village is the possession of either you or me, and so on.

Cādiyogeti kiṃ? Gāmo ca te pariggaho, nagarañca me pariggaho.

Why the rule 'in conjunction with `ca`, etc.'? The village is your possession, and the city is my possession.

271. Dassanatthenālocane caṃ. 6.3.23; pā. 8.1.25.

271. [Not] in the case of consideration in the sense of seeing.

Ālocanaṃ olokanaṃ, ālocanato aññasmiṃ dassanatthe payujjamāne tumhā’mhānaṃ vo, no, te, meādesā na honti.

`Ālocana` is looking. When a word is used in a sense of seeing other than that of `ālocana`, the substitutes `vo`, `no`, `te`, and `me` for `tumha` and `amha` do not occur.

Gāmo tumhe uddissa āgato, gāmo amhe uddissa āgato – ‘gāmo’ti gāmavāsī mahājano.

The village has come on account of you; the village has come on account of us—'the village' here means the villagers, the great populace.

Anālocaneti kiṃ? Gāmo vo passati, gāmo no passati.

Why state 'other than `ālocana`'? The village sees you; the village sees us.

272. Āmantanapubbaṃ asantaṃva ‘āmantaṇaṃ pubbamasantaṃva’ (bahūsu) caṃ. 6.3.24; pā. 8.1.72.

272. A preceding vocative is as if non-existent.

Āmantanabhūtaṃ pubbapadaṃ asantaṃ viya hoti, padatoti saṅkhyaṃ na gacchati.

A preceding word that is a vocative is as if non-existent; it does not count as a word.

Devadatta! Tava pariggaho.

O Devadatta! Your possession.

273. Na sāmaññavacanamekatthe caṃ. 6.3.25; pā. 8.1.73.

273. Not a general term when there is a single referent.

Tulyādhikaraṇabhūte pade sati pubbaṃ sāmaññavacanabhūtaṃ āmantanapadaṃ asantaṃ viya na hoti, padatoti saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

When there is a word in apposition, a preceding vocative word that is a general term is not as if non-existent; it counts as a word.

Māṇavaka jaṭila! Te pariggaho.

O young man, ascetic! Your possession.

Sāmaññavacananti [M 0.0150] kiṃ? Māṇavaka devadatta! Tuyhaṃ pariggaho.

Why the specification 'general term'? O young man, Devadatta! Your possession.

Ekattheti kiṃ? Devadatta! Yaññadatta! Tumhākaṃ pariggaho.

Why the specification 'single referent'? O Devadatta! O Yaññadatta! Your possession.

274. Bahūsu vā caṃ. 6.3.26; pā. 8.1.74.

274. Or optionally, in the case of many.

Bahūsu janesu pavattamānaṃ sāmaññavacanabhūtampi āmantanapadaṃ ekatthe pade sati asantaṃ viya na hoti vā.

A vocative word that is a general term applying to many people is optionally not as if non-existent, when there is a word in apposition referring to the same entity.

Brāhmaṇā guṇavanto vo pariggaho, brāhmaṇā guṇavanto tumhākaṃ pariggaho.

O Brahmins, virtuous ones! It is your possession (`vo`), or it is your possession (`tumhākaṃ`).

Sabbādirāsi niṭṭhito.

The section on `sabba` and other pronouns is concluded.

Vibhattipaccayantarāsi

The Section on Suffixes for Case-Endings

Atha vibhattipaccayā dīpiyante.

Now, the suffixes used for case-endings are explained.

Vibhatyatthānaṃ jotakattā vibhattiṭṭhāne ṭhitā paccayā vibhattipaccayā.

Because they illuminate the meanings of the cases, suffixes that stand in the place of case-endings are called `vibhattipaccayā`.

275. To pañcamyā ka. 248; rū. 260; nī. 493; caṃ. 4.3.6; pā. 5.4.45.

275. The suffix `to` occurs in the sense of the fifth (ablative) case.

Pañcamiyā vibhattiyā atthe topaccayo hoti.

The suffix `to` occurs in the meaning of the fifth case-ending (ablative).

Tomhi dīghānaṃ rasso, kaññato, rattito, itthito, dhenuto. Mahāvuttinā tomhi mātāpitūnaṃ ittaṃ, mātito, pitito, vadhuto, purisato, munito, daṇḍito[M 0.0151], bhikkhuto, satthārato, kattuto, gotrabhuto, sabbato, yato, tato.

When the suffix `to` follows, long vowels are shortened: `kaññato`, `rattito`, `itthito`, `dhenuto`. According to the Mahāvutti, when `to` follows, `i` is substituted for the final vowel of `mātā` and `pitā`. Examples are: `mātito`, `pitito`, `vadhuto`, `purisato`, `munito`, `daṇḍito`, `bhikkhuto`, `satthārato`, `kattuto`, `gotrabhuto`, `sabbato`, `yato`, `tato`.

Ima, eta, kiṃsaddehi to.

From the words `ima`, `eta`, and `kiṃ`, the suffix `to` occurs.

276. Itotettokuto ‘ito tetto kato’ (bahūsu) caṃ. 4.3.8; pā. 7.2.104.

276. `Ito`, `ato`, `etto`, `kuto`.

Ito, ato, etto, kutoti ete saddā topaccayantā nipaccante.

The words `ito`, `ato`, `etto`, and `kuto` are formed as indeclinables ending in the suffix `to`.

Imamhā imehīti vā ito, etasmā etehīti vā ato, etto, kasmā kehīti vā kuto. Ettha ca imamhā, imehītiādikaṃ atthavākyaṃ disvā pakatiliṅgaṃ veditabbaṃ. Iminā suttena imassa ittaṃ, etassa attaṃ ettañca, ‘saramhā dve’ti esaramhā dvittaṃ, kiṃsaddassa kuttaṃ. Esa nayo sesesu nipātanesu.

From `imamhā` or `imehi` comes `ito`; from `etasmā` or `etehi` come `ato` and `etto`; from `kasmā` or `kehi` comes `kuto`. And here, by observing the explanatory phrases such as `imamhā`, `imehi`, etc., the original gender should be understood. By this rule, `i` is substituted for `ima`; `a` and `e` are substituted for `eta`, and by the rule `saramhā dve`, the consonant is doubled after the vowel; `ku` is substituted for the word `kiṃ`. This is the method for the remaining indeclinable formations.

277. Abhyādīhi pā. 5.3.9.

277. From `abhi` and so on.

Abhiādīhi to hoti, punabbidhānā’pañcamyatthepītipi siddhaṃ.

From `abhi` and so on, the suffix `to` occurs; and it is also established that it occurs even in a non-ablative sense due to the restatement of the rule.

Abhito gāmaṃ gāmassa abhimukheti attho.

`Abhito gāmaṃ` means 'facing the village'.

Parito gāmaṃ gāmassa samantatoti attho.

`Parito gāmaṃ` means 'all around the village'.

Ubhato gāmaṃ gāmassa ubhosu passesūti attho.

`Ubhato gāmaṃ` means 'on both sides of the village'.

Pacchato, heṭṭhato, uparito.

`Pacchato` (behind), `heṭṭhato` (below), `uparito` (above).

278. Ādyādīhi caṃ. 4.3.9; pā. 5.4.44.

278. From `ādi` and so on.

Ādipabhutīhi apañcamyatthepi to hoti.

From `ādi` and so on, the suffix `to` occurs even in a non-ablative sense.

Ādito[M 0.0152], majjhato, purato, passato, piṭṭhito, orato, parato, pacchato, puratthimato, dakkhiṇatoiccādīsu bahulaṃ sattamyatthe dissati.

`Ādito` (from the beginning), `majjhato` (from the middle), `purato` (from the front), `passato` (from the side), `piṭṭhito` (from behind), `orato` (from this side), `parato` (from the other side), `pacchato` (from behind), `puratthimato` (from the east), `dakkhiṇato` (from the south)—in these and similar cases, the locative sense is frequently seen.

Tathā tatiyatthepi rūpaṃ attato samanupassati saṃ. ni. 3.44, pañcakkhandhe aniccato vipassati iccādi.

Similarly, also in the sense of the instrumental case: `rūpaṃ attato samanupassati` (one regards form as self), `pañcakkhandhe aniccato vipassati` (one sees the five aggregates as impermanent), and so on.

Yatonidānaṃ su. ni. 275, yatvādhikaraṇaṃ, yatodakaṃ tadādittamiccādīsu jā. 1.9.58 paṭhamatthe icchanti.

In such cases as `yatonidānaṃ` (from which is the source), `yatādhikaraṇaṃ` (from which is the basis), `yatodakaṃ` (from which is the water), `tadādittaṃ` (from that, it is burning), and so on, they intend the nominative sense.

Ito ehi, ito balāke āgaccha, caṇḍo me vāyaso sakhā iccādīsu dutiyatthe.

`Ito ehi` (come here), `ito balāke āgaccha` (come here, O crane)—in these and similar cases, it is in the sense of the accusative case.

Paratoghoso, nādiṭṭhā parato dosaṃ iccādīsu chaṭṭhyatthe.

`Paratoghoso` (another's sound), `nādiṭṭhā parato dosaṃ` (not seeing another's fault)—in these and similar cases, it is in the sense of the genitive case.

279. Sabbādito sattamyā tratthā ka. 249; rū. 266; nī. 494; caṃ. 4.1.10; pā. 5.3.10.

279. From `sabba` and so on, the suffixes `tra` and `tthā` occur in the sense of the locative case.

Sabbādināmakehi sabbanāmehi sattamiyā atthe tra, tthā honti.

From the pronouns beginning with `sabba`, the suffixes `tra` and `tthā` occur in the sense of the locative case.

Sabbasmiṃ sabbesūti vā sabbatra, sabbattha, sabbassaṃ sabbāsu vātipi. Evaṃ kataratra, katarattha, aññatra, aññattha iccādi.

From `sabbasmiṃ` or `sabbesu` come `sabbatra` and `sabbattha`; similarly from `sabbassaṃ` or `sabbāsu`. Thus, `kataratra`, `katarattha`, `aññatra`, `aññattha`, and so on.

Yatra, yattha, tatra, tattha.

`Yatra` (where), `yattha` (where), `tatra` (there), `tattha` (there).

280. Katthetthakutrātrakvehidha ka. 251; rū. 269; nī. 499; caṃ. 4.1.11; pā. 5.3.11, 12.

280. `Kattha`, `ettha`, `kutra`, `atra`, `kva`, `iha`, `idha`.

Kattha, ettha, kutra, atra, tva, iha, idhāti ete saddāttha, tra,va ha, dhāpaccayantā sattamyatthe sijjhanti.

The words `kattha`, `ettha`, `kutra`, `atra`, `kva`, `iha`, and `idha` are formed ending in the suffixes `ttha`, `tra`, `va`, `ha`, and `dhā` respectively, in the sense of the locative case.

Kasmiṃ kesūti vā kattha, kutra, kva. ‘Kuva’ntipi sijjhati, “kuvaṃ sattassa kārako, kuvaṃ satto samuppanno saṃ. ni. 1.171, kuvaṃ asissaṃ, kuvaṃ khādissa”nti pāḷi.

From `kasmiṃ` or `kesu` come `kattha`, `kutra`, and `kva`. `Kuvaṃ` is also formed, as in the Pāli: "`Kuvaṃ sattassa kārako, kuvaṃ satto samuppanno, kuvaṃ asissaṃ, kuvaṃ khādissaṃ`" (Where is the maker of the being? Where is the being produced? Where shall I eat? Where shall I devour?).

Etasmiṃ [M 0.0153] etesūti vā ettha, atra, imasmiṃ imesūti vā iha, idha.

From `etasmiṃ` or `etesu` come `ettha` and `atra`; from `imasmiṃ` or `imesu` come `iha` and `idha`.

281. Dhi sabbā vā ka. 250; rū. 268; nī. 502.

281. The suffix `dhi` occurs optionally from `sabba`.

Sabbasaddamhā sattamyatthe dhi hoti vā.

From the word `sabba`, the suffix `dhi` occurs optionally in the sense of the locative case.

Namo te buddha vīra’tthu, vippamuttosi sabbadhi saṃ. ni. 1.90.

`Namo te buddha vīratthu, vippamuttosi sabbadhi` (Homage to you, O Buddha, hero! You are liberated in every way).

282. Yā hiṃ ka. 255; rū. 275; nī. 504.

282. From `ya`, the suffix `hiṃ` occurs.

Yamhā sattamyatthe hiṃ hoti.

From 'ya', the suffix 'hiṃ' occurs in the sense of the locative case.

Yahiṃ.

Yahiṃ (where).

283. Tā hañca ka. 253; rū. 273; nī. 501.

283. From 'ta', and 'haṃ' (occurs).

Tamhā sattamyatthe hiṃ hoti hañca.

From 'ta', in the sense of the locative case, the suffix 'hiṃ' occurs, and also 'haṃ'.

Tahiṃ, tahaṃ. Dutiyatthepi dissati “tahaṃ tahaṃ olokento gacchatī”ti.

Tahiṃ (there), tahaṃ (there). It is also seen in the sense of the accusative case, as in "going looking there and there."

284. Kiṃssa kukañca ka. 251, 227-8-9; rū. 226, 270-1-2; nī. 500, 456-7, 460.

284. For 'kiṃ', 'ku' and 'ka' (are substituted).

Kiṃmhā sattamyatthe hiṃ, taṃ hoti. Kiṃssa kuttaṃ kattañca hoti.

From 'kiṃ', in the sense of the locative case, the suffix 'hiṃ' occurs, and also 'haṃ'. For 'kiṃ', 'kuttaṃ' and 'kattaṃ' also occur.

Kuhiṃ gacchati, kuhaṃ gacchati. Kahaṃ ekaputtaka kahaṃ ekaputtaka saṃ. ni. 2.63. Kuhiñci, kuhiñcananti dve ci, cana-nipātantā sijjhanti.

Where does he go? Where does he go? Where, O only son? Where, O only son? Kuhiñci and kuhiñcana are formed ending in the particles 'ci' and 'cana' respectively.

Iti sāmaññasattamyantarāsi.

Thus ends the section on the general locative endings.

Kālasattamyantaṃ [M 0.0154] vuccate.

The locative endings in the sense of time are explained.

285. Sabbekaññayatehi kāledā ka. 257; rū. 276; nī. 505.

285. From 'sabba', 'eka', 'añña', 'ya', and 'ta', the suffix 'dā' occurs in the sense of time.

Sabba, eka, añña, ya, tasaddehi kāle dā hoti.

From the words 'sabba', 'eka', 'añña', 'ya', and 'ta', the suffix 'dā' occurs in the sense of time.

Sabbasmiṃ kāle sabbadā, ekasmiṃ kāle ekadā, aññasmiṃ kāle aññadā, yasmiṃ kāle yadā, tasmiṃ kāle tadā.

Sabbasmiṃ kāle (at all times) becomes sabbadā (always); ekasmiṃ kāle (at one time) becomes ekadā (once); aññasmiṃ kāle (at another time) becomes aññadā (at another time); yasmiṃ kāle (at which time) becomes yadā (when); tasmiṃ kāle (at that time) becomes tadā (then).

286. Kadākudāsadāadhunedāni ka. 257-8-9; rū. 276-8-9; nī. 505-6-7.

286. Kadā, kudā, sadā, adhunā, idāni.

Etepi sattamyatthe kāle dā, dhunā, dānipaccayantā sijjhanti.

These also are formed ending in the suffixes dā, dhunā, and dāni, in the sense of the locative of time.

Kiṃsmiṃ kāle kadā, kudā, sabbasmiṃ kāle sadā, imasmiṃ kāle adhunā, idāni.

Kiṃsmiṃ kāle (at what time) becomes kadā, kudā; sabbasmiṃ kāle (at all times) becomes sadā; imasmiṃ kāle (at this time) becomes adhunā, idāni.

287. Ajjasajjuparajjetarahikarahā ka. 259; rū. 279, 423; nī. 507.

287. Ajja, sajju, aparajju, etarahi, karahā.

Etepi kāle jja, jju, rahi, raha paccayantā sijjhanti.

These also are formed ending in the suffixes jja, jju, rahi, and raha, in the sense of time.

Imasmiṃ kāle ajja, imasmiṃ divasetyattho.

Imasmiṃ kāle (at this time) becomes ajja; the meaning is 'on this day'.

Samāne kāle sajju-‘samāne’ti vijjamāne. Na hi pāpaṃ kataṃ kammaṃ, sajju khīraṃva muccati dha. pa. 71, sajjukaṃ pāhesi – tattha ‘sajjū’ti tasmiṃ divase.

Samāne kāle (at the same time) becomes sajju—'samāne' meaning existing. As in: "For an evil deed done does not curdle at once, like milk"; "he sent immediately"—there, 'sajju' means 'on that day'.

Aparasmiṃ kāle aparajju, punadivaseti attho.

Aparasmiṃ kāle (at another time) becomes aparajju, meaning 'on the following day'.

Imasmiṃ kāle etarahi, kiṃsmiṃ kāle karaha. Kutoci, kvaci, katthaci, kuhiñci, kadāci, karahacisaddā pana ci-nipātantā honti, tathā yato kutoci, yattha katthaci, yadā kadācīti. Kiñcanaṃ, kuhiñcanaṃ, kudācananti cana-nipātantāti.

Imasmiṃ kāle (at this time) becomes etarahi; kiṃsmiṃ kāle (at what time) becomes karaha. But the words kutoci, kvaci, katthaci, kuhiñci, kadāci, and karahaci are formed ending in the particle 'ci'; similarly yato kutoci, yattha katthaci, and yadā kadāci. Kiñcanaṃ, kuhiñcanaṃ, and kudācanaṃ are formed ending in the particle 'cana'.

Vibhattipaccayantarāsi niṭṭhito.

The section on endings which are case suffixes is concluded.

Abyayapadāni

Indeclinable Words

Upasaggapadarāsi

The Section on Prefixes

Atha [M 0.0155] abyayapadāni dīpiyante.

Now the indeclinable words are explained.

Chabbidhāni abyayapadāni upasaggapadaṃ, nipātapadaṃ, vibhattipaccayantapadaṃ, abyayībhāvasamāsapadaṃ, abyayataddhitapadaṃ, tvādipaccayantapadanti. Byayo vuccati vikāro, nānāliṅgavibhattivacanehi natthi rūpabyayo etesanti abyayā, asaṅkhyāti ca vuccanti.

There are six kinds of indeclinable words: prefix words, particle words, words ending in case suffixes, indeclinable compound words, indeclinable derivative words, and words ending with the suffix -tvā and so forth. 'Byaya' is called change; since these have no change of form due to various genders, cases, or numbers, they are called indeclinables (abyayā), and are also called 'asaṅkhyā' (not subject to number).

Tattha vibhattipaccayantapadato puna vibhattuppatti nāma natthi. Abyayībhāvasamāsamhi vibhattīnaṃ vidhi samāsakaṇḍe vakkhati, tasmā tāni dve ṭhapetvā sesāni cattāri idha vuccante.

Therein, from a word ending in a case suffix, no further arising of a case ending occurs. The rule for case endings in an indeclinable compound will be explained in the chapter on compounds. Therefore, having set aside those two, the remaining four are discussed here.

288. Asaṅkhyehi sabbāsaṃ caṃ. 2.1.38; pā. 2.4.82.

288. After indeclinables, all case endings are elided.

Asaṅkhyehi padehi yathārahaṃ sabbāsaṃ vibhattīnaṃ lopo hoti, kehici padehi paṭhamāya lopo, kehici padehi dutiyāya lopo…pe… kehici sattamiyā, kehici dvinnaṃ, kehici tissannaṃ…pe… kehici sattannanti vuttaṃ hoti.

After indeclinable words, the elision of all case endings occurs appropriately. With some words, there is elision of the first case; with some words, elision of the second case… and so forth… with some, of the seventh; with some, of two; with some, of three… and so forth… with some, of seven—so it is said.

Tattha āvuso, bho, bhanteiccādīhi āmantananipātehi atthi, natthi, sakkā, labbhā, siyā, siyuṃ, sādhu, tuṇhīiccādīhi ca paṭhamāya lopo.

Here, with vocative particles such as 'āvuso,' 'bho,' 'bhante,' and so forth, and with words such as 'atthi,' 'natthi,' 'sakkā,' 'labbhā,' 'siyā,' 'siyuṃ,' 'sādhu,' 'tuṇhī,' and so forth, there is elision of the first case.

Ciraṃ, cirassaṃ, niccaṃ, satataṃ, abhiṇhaṃ, abhikkhaṇaṃ, muhuttaṃ iccādīhi accantasaṃyogalakkhaṇe dutiyāya.

With words like 'ciraṃ,' 'cirassaṃ,' 'niccaṃ,' 'satataṃ,' 'abhiṇhaṃ,' 'abhikkhaṇaṃ,' 'muhuttaṃ,' and so forth, denoting continuous connection, the second case is used.

Yathā, tathā, sabbathā, sabbaso, musā, micchāiccādīhi tatiyāya.

With words like 'yathā,' 'tathā,' 'sabbathā,' 'sabbaso,' 'musā,' 'micchā,' and so forth, the third case is used.

Kātuṃ, kātave iccādīhi catutthiyā.

With words like 'kātuṃ,' 'kātave,' and so forth, the fourth case is used.

Samantā[M 0.0156], samantato, dīghaso, orasoiccādīhi pañcamiyā.

With words like 'samantā,' 'samantato,' 'dīghaso,' 'oraso,' and so forth, the fifth case is used.

Pure, purā, pacchā, uddhaṃ, upari, adho, heṭṭhā, antarā, anto, raho, āvi, hiyyo, suveiccādīhi sattamiyā lopo.

With words like 'pure,' 'purā,' 'pacchā,' 'uddhaṃ,' 'upari,' 'adho,' 'heṭṭhā,' 'antarā,' 'anto,' 'raho,' 'āvi,' 'hiyyo,' 'suve,' and so forth, the seventh case ending is elided.

Namosaddamhā “namo te buddha vīra’tthū”ti ettha paṭhamāya. “Namo karohi nāgassā”ti ettha dutiyāya.

From the word 'namo,' as in 'namo te buddha vīratthu,' here the first case is used. As in 'namo karohi nāgassa,' here the second case is used.

Sayaṃsaddamhā “kusūlo sayameva bhijjate”ti ettha paṭhamāya. “Sayaṃ kataṃ sukhadukkha”nti dī. ni. 3.191, 193 ettha tatiyāya, iccādinā yathārahavibhāgo veditabbo.

From the word 'sayaṃ,' as in 'kusūlo sayaṃ eva bhijjate,' here the first case is used. As in 'sayaṃ kataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ,' here the third case is used. In this way, the appropriate case should be understood according to suitability.

Iti, evaṃsaddehi payogānurūpaṃ sattannaṃ vibhattīnaṃ lopaṃ icchanti.

With the words 'iti' and 'evaṃ,' according to usage, the elision of the seven cases is accepted.

Upasaggehipi atthānurūpaṃ taṃtaṃvibhattilopo.

Also with prefixes, the elision of the respective case endings occurs according to the meaning.

Rūpasiddhiyaṃ pana “tehi paṭhamekavacanameva bhavatī”ti rū. 131 (piṭṭhe) vuttaṃ.

In the Rūpasiddhi, however, it is said: 'With these, only the first case singular occurs.'

Tattha “abhikkamati, abhidhammo” iccādīsu dhātuliṅgāni upecca tesaṃ atthaṃ nānāppakāraṃ karontā sajjanti saṅkharontīti upasaggā. Te hi kvaci tadatthaṃ visiṭṭhaṃ karonti “jānāti, pajānāti, sañjānāti, avajānāti, abhijānāti, parijānāti, susīlo, dussīlo, suvaṇṇo, dubbaṇṇo, surājā, durājā” iccādīsu.

Here, in words like 'abhikkamati,' 'abhidhammo,' and so forth, prefixes are those which, having approached roots and nominal stems, fashion and construct their meanings in various ways. Indeed, they sometimes make that meaning distinct, as in 'jānāti,' 'pajānāti,' 'sañjānāti,' 'avajānāti,' 'abhijānāti,' 'parijānāti,' 'susīlo,' 'dussīlo,' 'suvaṇṇo,' 'dubbaṇṇo,' 'surājā,' 'durājā,' and so forth.

Kvaci tadatthaṃ nānāppakāraṃ katvā vibhajjanti “gacchati, āgacchati, uggacchati, ogacchati”iccādīsu.

Sometimes, having made that meaning various, they divide it, as in 'gacchati,' 'āgacchati,' 'uggacchati,' 'ogacchati,' and so forth.

Kvaci tadatthaṃ bādhetvā tappaṭiviruddhe vā tadaññasmiṃ vā atthe tāni yojenti.

Sometimes, having obstructed that meaning, they apply them to a contrary meaning or to another meaning.

Tattha [M 0.0157] tappaṭiviruddhe –

Therein, regarding a contrary meaning:

Jeti, parājeti, omuñcati, paṭimuñcati, gilati, uggilati, nimmujjati, ummujjati, dhammo, uddhammoiccādi.

'Jeti,' 'parājeti,' 'omuñcati,' 'paṭimuñcati,' 'gilati,' 'uggilati,' 'nimmujjati,' 'ummujjati,' 'dhammo,' 'uddhammo,' and so forth.

Tadaññasmiṃ –

Regarding another meaning:

Dadāti, ādadāti, dadhāti, vidheti, pidheti, nidheti, sandhiyati, saddahati, abhidhātiiccādi.

'Dadāti,' 'ādadāti,' 'dadhāti,' 'vidheti,' 'pidheti,' 'nidheti,' 'sandhiyati,' 'saddahati,' 'abhidhāti,' and so forth.

Kvaci pana padasobhaṇaṃ katvā tadatthaṃ anuvattanti, “vijjati, saṃvijjati, labhati, paṭilabhati” iccādi.

Sometimes, however, having embellished the word, they follow that meaning, as in 'vijjati,' 'saṃvijjati,' 'labhati,' 'paṭilabhati,' and so forth.

Te vīsati honti-pa, ā, u, o, du, ni, vi, su, saṃ, ati, adhi, anu, apa, api, abhi, ava, upa, pati, parā, pari.

They are twenty: pa, ā, u, o, du, ni, vi, su, saṃ, ati, adhi, anu, apa, api, abhi, ava, upa, pati, parā, pari.

Kaccāyane pana osaddo avakāriyamattanti taṃ aggahetvā nīsaddaṃ gaṇhāti, idha pana nīsaddo nissa dīghamattanti taṃ aggahetvā osaddaṃ gaṇhāti.

In Kaccāyana's grammar, however, the sound 'o' is considered merely a variant of 'ava'; therefore, not including it, he includes the sound 'nī'. Here, however, the sound 'nī' is considered merely a lengthened form of 'nis'; therefore, not including it, he includes the sound 'o'.

Tattha pa –

Therein, 'pa':

Pakāratthe-paññā. Ādikamme-vippakataṃ. Padhāne-paṇītaṃ. Issariye-pabhū. Antobhāve-pakkhittaṃ, passāso. Viyoge-pavāso. Tappare-pācariyo. Tadanubandhe-putto, paputto, nattā, panattā. Bhusatthe-pavaḍḍho. Sambhave-pabhavati. Tittiyaṃ-pahutaṃ annaṃ. Anāvile-pasanno. Patthanāyaṃ-paṇidhānaṃ.

In the sense of manifestation: 'paññā' (wisdom). In the sense of initial action: 'vippakataṃ' (unfinished). In the sense of excellence: 'paṇītaṃ' (excellent). In the sense of sovereignty: 'pabhū' (lord). In the sense of inner state: 'pakkhittaṃ' (cast in), 'passāso' (in-breath). In the sense of separation: 'pavāso' (living abroad). In the sense of being intent on that: 'pācariyo' (eminent teacher). In the sense of succession: 'putto' (son), 'paputto' (grandson), 'nattā' (grandchild), 'panattā' (great-grandchild). In the sense of abundance: 'pavaḍḍho' (greatly increased). In the sense of origin: 'pabhavati' (arises). In the sense of satisfaction: 'pahutaṃ annaṃ' (abundant food). In the sense of clarity: 'pasanno' (serene). In the sense of aspiration: 'paṇidhānaṃ' (aspiration).

Ā –

Ā –

Abhimukhe-āgacchati. Uddhaṃkamme-ārohati. Mariyādāyaṃ-āpabbatā khettaṃ. Abhividhimhi-ābrahmalokā kittisaddo. Pattiyaṃ-āpanno. Icchāyaṃ-ākaṅkhā. Parissajane-āliṅgati. Ādikamme-ārambho. Gahaṇe-ādīyati. Nivāse-āvasatho. Samīpe-āsannaṃ. Avhāne-āmantanaṃ.

In the sense of facing: 'āgacchati' (comes). In the sense of upward action: 'ārohati' (ascends). In the sense of boundary: 'āpabbatā khettaṃ' (the field up to the mountain). In the sense of pervasion: 'ābrahmalokā kittisaddo' (the sound of fame up to the Brahma world). In the sense of attainment: 'āpanno' (attained). In the sense of desire: 'ākaṅkhā' (longing). In the sense of embracing: 'āliṅgati' (embraces). In the sense of beginning: 'ārambho' (commencement). In the sense of taking: 'ādīyati' (takes). In the sense of dwelling: 'āvasatho' (abode). In the sense of proximity: 'āsannaṃ' (near). In the sense of calling: 'āmantanaṃ' (invitation).

U –

'U':

Uggate-uggacchati[M 0.0158]. Uddhaṃkamme-uṭṭhāti. Padhāne-uttaro. Viyoge-upavāso. Sambhave-ubbhūto. Atthalābhe-rūpassa uppādo. Sattiyaṃ-ussahati gantuṃ. Sarūpakhyāne-uddeso.

In the sense of rising: 'uggacchati' (goes upward). In the sense of upward action: 'uṭṭhāti' (rises up). In the sense of excellence: 'uttaro' (superior). In the sense of separation: 'upavāso' (fasting). In the sense of arising: 'ubbhūto' (originated). In the sense of gaining substance: 'rūpassa uppādo' (the arising of form). In the sense of ability: 'ussahati gantuṃ' (endeavors to go). In the sense of enumeration: 'uddeso' (outline).

O –

'O':

Antobhāve-ocarako, orodho. Adhokamme-okkhitto. Niggahe-ovādo. Antare, dese ca-okāso. Pātubhāve-opapātiko. Yesu atthesu avasaddo vattati, tesupi osaddo vattati.

In the sense of inner state: 'ocarako' (investigator), 'orodho' (confinement). In the sense of downward action: 'okkhitto' (thrown down). In the sense of restraint: 'ovādo' (admonition). In the sense of interval and place: 'okāso' (opportunity). In the sense of manifestation: 'opapātiko' (spontaneously born). In those meanings where the sound 'ava' occurs, the sound 'o' also occurs.

Du –

'Du':

Asobhaṇe-duggandho. Abhāve-dubbhikkhaṃ, dussīlo, duppañño. Kucchite-dukkaṭaṃ. Asamiddhiyaṃ-dusassaṃ. Kicche-dukkaraṃ. Virūpe-dubbaṇṇo, dummukho.

In the sense of unpleasantness: 'duggandho' (bad smell). In the sense of absence: 'dubbhikkhaṃ' (famine), 'dussīlo' (immoral), 'duppañño' (unwise). In the sense of blameworthiness: 'dukkaṭaṃ' (wrongdoing). In the sense of failure: 'dusassaṃ' (bad harvest). In the sense of difficulty: 'dukkaraṃ' (difficult to do). In the sense of ugliness: 'dubbaṇṇo' (ill-colored), 'dummukho' (ugly-faced).

Ni –

Ni –

Nissese-nirutti. Niggate-niyyānaṃ. Nīharaṇe-niddhāraṇaṃ. Antopavesane-nikhāto. Abhāve-nimmakkhikaṃ. Nisedhe-nivāreti. Nikkhante-nibbānaṃ. Pātubhāve-nimmitaṃ. Avadhāraṇe-vinicchayo. Vibhajjane-niddeso. Upamāyaṃ-nidassanaṃ. Upadhāraṇe-nisāmeti. Avasāne-niṭṭhitaṃ. Cheke-nipuṇo.

In the sense of thoroughness: 'nirutti' (etymology). In the sense of emergence: 'niyyānaṃ' (issuance). In the sense of singling out: 'niddhāraṇaṃ' (specification). In the sense of inner placement: 'nikhāto' (fixed). In the sense of absence: 'nimmakkhikaṃ' (flawless). In the sense of prevention: 'nivāreti' (wards off). In the sense of going forth: 'nibbānaṃ' (cessation). In the sense of manifestation: 'nimmitaṃ' (magically created). In the sense of ascertainment: 'vinicchayo' (judgment). In the sense of distinction: 'niddeso' (pointing out). In the sense of simile: 'nidassanaṃ' (example). In the sense of attention: 'nisāmeti' (observes). In the sense of termination: 'niṭṭhitaṃ' (finished). In the sense of cleverness: 'nipuṇo' (skilled).

Vi –

Vi –

Visese-vipassati. Vividhe-vicittaṃ. Viruddhe-vivādo. Vigate-vimalo. Viyoge-vippayutto. Virūpe-vippaṭisāro.

In the sense of distinction: 'vipassati' (discerns especially). In the sense of variety: 'vicittaṃ' (variegated). In the sense of opposition: 'vivādo' (dispute). In the sense of absence: 'vimalo' (stainless). In the sense of separation: 'vippayutto' (disconnected). In the sense of unseemliness: 'vippaṭisāro' (remorse).

Su –

Su –

Sobhaṇe-suggati[M 0.0159]. Sundare-sumano. Sammāsaddatthe-sugato. Samiddhiyaṃ-subhikkhaṃ. Sukhatthe-sukaro.

In the sense of beauty: 'suggati' (a good destination). In the sense of loveliness: 'sumano' (joyful). In the sense of 'rightly': 'sugato' (well-gone). In the sense of prosperity: 'subhikkhaṃ' (plenty). In the sense of happiness: 'sukaro' (easy).

Saṃ –

Saṃ –

Samodhāne-sandhi. Sammā, samatthesu-samādhi, sampayutto. Samantabhāve-saṃkiṇṇo. Saṅgate-samāgamo, saṅkhepe-samāso. Bhusatthe-sāratto. Sahatthe-saṃvāso, sambhogo. Appatthe-samaggho. Pabhave-sambhavo. Abhimukhe-sammukhaṃ. Saṅgahe-saṅgayhati. Pidahane-saṃvuto. Punappunakamme-sandhāvati, saṃsarati. Samiddhiyaṃ-sampanno.

In the sense of combination: 'sandhi' (connection). In the sense of correctness and ability: 'samādhi' (concentration), 'sampayutto' (connected). In the sense of completeness: 'saṃkiṇṇo' (mixed). In the sense of gathering: 'samāgamo' (assembly). In the sense of brevity: 'samāso' (summary). In the sense of intensity: 'sāratto' (strongly attached). In the sense of togetherness: 'saṃvāso' (living together), 'sambhogo' (enjoyment). In the sense of smallness: 'samaggho' (of little value). In the sense of origin: 'sambhavo' (becoming). In the sense of facing: 'sammukhaṃ' (face to face). In the sense of inclusion: 'saṅgayhati' (is included). In the sense of covering: 'saṃvuto' (covered). In the sense of repetition: 'sandhāvati' (runs on), 'saṃsarati' (transmigrates). In the sense of success: 'sampanno' (prosperous).

Ati –

Ati –

Atikkame-atirocati, accayo, atīto. Atikkante-accantaṃ. Atissaye-atikusalo. Bhusatthe-atikodho. Antokamme-mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā atiharitvā ṭhapeti.

In the sense of transgression: 'atirocati' (surpasses), 'accayo' (offense), 'atīto' (past). In the sense of surpassing: 'accantaṃ' (utterly). In the sense of excess: 'atikusalo' (very skillful). In the sense of intensity: 'atikodho' (excessive anger). In the sense of inner action: 'mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā atiharitvā ṭhapeti' (having carried a bed or chair inside, he places it).

Adhi –

Adhi –

Adhike-adhisīlaṃ. Issare-adhipati, adhibrahmadatte pañcālā. Uparibhāve-adhiseti. Paribhavane-adhibhūto. Ajjhāyane-ajjheti, byākaraṇamadhīte. Adhiṭṭhāne-navakammaṃ adhiṭṭhāti, cīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhāti, iddhivikubbanaṃ adhiṭṭhāti. Nicchaye-adhimuccati. Pāpuṇane-bhogakkhandhaṃ adhigacchati, amataṃ adhigacchati.

In the sense of superiority: 'adhisīlaṃ' (higher virtue). In the sense of sovereignty: 'adhipati' (lord), 'adhibrahmadatte pañcālā' (the Pañcālas under Brahmadatta). In the sense of being above: 'adhiseti' (dwells above). In the sense of overpowering: 'adhibhūto' (overpowered). In the sense of study: 'ajjheti' (studies), 'byākaraṇamadhīte' (studies grammar). In the sense of determination: 'navakammaṃ adhiṭṭhāti' (undertakes new construction), 'cīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhāti' (undertakes a formal determination regarding robes), 'iddhivikubbanaṃ adhiṭṭhāti' (undertakes psychic transformation). In the sense of conviction: 'adhimuccati' (is convinced). In the sense of attainment: 'bhogakkhandhaṃ adhigacchati' (obtains a mass of wealth), 'amataṃ adhigacchati' (attains the deathless).

Anu –

Anu –

Anugate-anveti. Anuppacchinne-anusayo. Pacchāsaddatthe-anurathaṃ. Punappunabhāve-anvaḍḍhamāsaṃ, anusaṃvaccharaṃ. Yogyabhāve-anurūpaṃ[M 0.0160].Kaniṭṭhabhāve-anubuddho, anuthero. Sesaṃ kārakakaṇḍe vakkhati.

In the sense of following: 'anveti' (follows). In the sense of unbroken continuity: 'anusayo' (underlying tendency). In the sense of 'after': 'anurathaṃ' (in pursuit). In the sense of repetition: 'anvaḍḍhamāsaṃ' (every half-month), 'anusaṃvaccharaṃ' (yearly). In the sense of suitability: 'anurūpaṃ' (suitable). In the sense of junior status: 'anubuddho' (subsequently awakened), 'anuthero' (junior elder). The rest will be explained in the section on cases.

Apa –

Apa –

Apagate-apeti, apāyo. Garahe-apagabbho, apasaddo. Vajjane-apasālāya āyanti. Pūjāyaṃ-vuḍḍha-mapacāyanti. Padussane-aparajjhati.

In the sense of going away: 'apeti' (goes away), 'apāyo' (loss). In the sense of blame: 'apagabbho' (unassuming), 'apasaddo' (bad sound). In the sense of avoidance: 'apasālāya āyanti' (they come avoiding the hall). In the sense of worship: 'vuḍḍhamapacāyanti' (they revere the elders). In the sense of offending: 'aparajjhati' (he offends).

Api –

Api –

Sambhāvane-apipabbataṃ bhindeyya, merumpi vinivijjheyya. Apekkhāyaṃ-ayampi dhammo aniyato. Samuccaye-itipi arahaṃ, chavimpi dahati, cammampi dahati, maṃsampi dahati. Garahāyaṃ-api amhākaṃ paṇḍitaka. Pucchāyaṃ-api bhante bhikkhaṃ labhittha, api nu tumhe sotukāmāttha.

In the sense of possibility: 'apipabbataṃ bhindeyya' (he could split a mountain), 'merumpi vinivijjheyya' (he could even pierce Mount Meru). In the sense of expectation: 'ayampi dhammo aniyato' (this law too is uncertain). In the sense of accumulation: 'itipi arahaṃ' (indeed, he is an arahant), 'chavimpi dahati' (he burns even the skin), 'cammampi dahati' (he burns even the hide), 'maṃsampi dahati' (he burns even the flesh). In the sense of reproach: 'api amhākaṃ paṇḍitaka' (is he even our wise one?). In the sense of questioning: 'api bhante bhikkhaṃ labhittha' (venerable sir, did you receive alms?), 'api nu tumhe sotukāmāttha' (do you wish to hear?).

Abhi –

Abhi –

Abhimukhe-abhikkanto. Visiṭṭhe-abhiññā. Adhike-abhidhammo. Uddhaṃkamme-abhirūhati. Kule-abhijāto. Sāruppe-abhirūpo. Vandane-abhivādeti. Sesaṃ kārakakaṇḍe vakkhati.

In the sense of facing: 'abhikkanto' (approaching). In the sense of distinction: 'abhiññā' (direct knowing). In the sense of superiority: 'abhidhammo' (higher Dhamma). In the sense of upward action: 'abhirūhati' (ascends). In the sense of lineage: 'abhijāto' (well-born). In the sense of suitability: 'abhirūpo' (handsome). In the sense of veneration: 'abhivādeti' (pays homage). The rest will be explained in the section on cases.

Ava –

Ava –

Adhobhāge-avakkhitto. Viyoge-avakokilaṃ vanaṃ. Paribhave-avajānāti. Jānane-avagacchati. Suddhiyaṃ-vodāyati, vodānaṃ. Nicchaye-avadhāraṇaṃ. Dese-avakāso. Theyye-avahāro.

In the sense of the lower part: 'avakkhitto' (thrown down). In the sense of separation: 'avakokilaṃ vanaṃ' (a forest without cuckoos). In the sense of contempt: 'avajānāti' (disdains). In the sense of knowing: 'avagacchati' (understands). In the sense of purity: 'vodāyati' (cleanses), 'vodānaṃ' (purity). In the sense of certainty: 'avadhāraṇaṃ' (ascertainment). In the sense of place: 'avakāso' (space). In the sense of theft: 'avahāro' (stealing).

Upa –

Upa –

Upagame-upanisīdati. Samīpe-upacāro, upanagaraṃ. Upapattiyaṃ-saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Sadise-upamāṇaṃ, upameyyaṃ. Adhike-upakhāriyaṃ doṇo. Uparibhāve – upasampanno[M 0.0161], upacayo. Anasane-upavāso. Dosakkhāne-paraṃ upavadati. Saññāyaṃ-upadhā, upasaggo. Pubbakamme-upakkamo, upahāro. Pūjāyaṃ-buddhaṃ upaṭṭhāti. Gayhākāre-paccupaṭṭhānaṃ. Bhusatthe-upādānaṃ, upāyāso, upanissayo.

In the sense of approach: 'upanisīdati' (sits nearby). In the sense of proximity: 'upacāro' (attendance), 'upanagaraṃ' (suburb). In the sense of rebirth: 'saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati' (is reborn into the heavenly world). In the sense of similarity: 'upamāṇaṃ' (comparison), 'upameyyaṃ' (object of comparison). In the sense of excess: 'upakhāriyaṃ doṇo' (a supplementary doṇa measure). In the sense of superiority: 'upasampanno' (fully ordained), 'upacayo' (accumulation). In the sense of not eating: 'upavāso' (fasting). In the sense of accusation: 'paraṃ upavadati' (reviles another). In the sense of designation: 'upadhā' (penultimate vowel), 'upasaggo' (prefix). In the sense of preliminary action: 'upakkamo' (commencement), 'upahāro' (offering). In the sense of worship: 'buddhaṃ upaṭṭhāti' (waits upon the Buddha). In the sense of apprehension: 'paccupaṭṭhānaṃ' (presence). In the sense of intensity: 'upādānaṃ' (grasping), 'upāyāso' (distress), 'upanissayo' (decisive support).

Pati –

Pati –

Patigate-paccakkhaṃ. Paṭilome-paṭisotaṃ. Paṭiyogimhi-paṭipuggalo. Nisedhe-paṭisedho. Nivatte-paṭikkamati. Sadise-paṭirūpakaṃ. Paṭikamme-rogassa paṭikāro. Ādāne-paṭiggaṇhāti. Paṭibodhe-paṭivedho. Paṭicce-paccayo. Sesaṃ kārakakaṇḍe vakkhati.

In the sense of going towards: 'paccakkhaṃ' (directly visible). In the sense of being against: 'paṭisotaṃ' (against the stream). In the sense of opposition: 'paṭipuggalo' (opponent). In the sense of prohibition: 'paṭisedho' (rejection). In the sense of turning back: 'paṭikkamati' (withdraws). In the sense of likeness: 'paṭirūpakaṃ' (resemblance). In the sense of remedy: 'rogassa paṭikāro' (remedy for a disease). In the sense of acceptance: 'paṭiggaṇhāti' (accepts). In the sense of realization: 'paṭivedho' (penetration). In the sense of dependence: 'paccayo' (condition). The rest will be explained in the section on cases.

Parā –

Parā –

Parihāniyaṃ-parābhavo. Parājaye-parājito. Gatiyaṃ-parāyanaṃ. Vikkame-parakkamo. Āmasane-parāmasanaṃ.

In the sense of decline: 'parābhavo' (downfall). In the sense of defeat: 'parājito' (vanquished). In the sense of destination: 'parāyanaṃ' (chief resort). In the sense of exertion: 'parakkamo' (effort). In the sense of touching: 'parāmasanaṃ' (grasping).

Pari –

Pari –

Samantabhāve-parivuto, parikkhitto, parikkhāro. Paricchede-pariññeyyaṃ, parijānāti. Vajjane-pariharati. Parihāro. Āliṅgane-parissajati. Nivāsane-vatthaṃ paridahati. Pūjāyaṃ-pāricariyā. Bhojane-parivisati. Abhibhave-paribhavati. Dosakkhāne-paribhāsati. Sesaṃ kārakakaṇḍe vakkhati.

In the sense of surrounding: 'parivuto' (enveloped), 'parikkhitto' (encircled), 'parikkhāro' (equipment). In the sense of delimitation: 'pariññeyyaṃ' (to be fully understood), 'parijānāti' (comprehends). In the sense of avoidance: 'pariharati' (avoids), 'parihāro' (protection). In the sense of embracing: 'parissajati' (embraces). In the sense of wearing: 'vatthaṃ paridahati' (puts on a garment). In the sense of worship: 'pāricariyā' (attendance). In the sense of feeding: 'parivisati' (serves). In the sense of overpowering: 'paribhavati' (overcomes). In the sense of accusation: 'paribhāsati' (reproaches). The rest will be explained in the section on cases.

Nīsaddo pana nīharaṇa, nīvaraṇādīsu vattati, nīharaṇaṃ, nīvaraṇaṃiccādi.

The prefix 'nī' occurs in words denoting removal, obstruction, etc., such as removal, obstruction, and so forth.

Iti upasaggapadarāsi.

Thus, the group of prefixes.

Nipātapadarāsi

The collection of indeclinables.

Niccaṃ [M 0.0162] ekarūpena vākyapathe patantīti nipātā. Padānaṃ ādi, majjhā’vasānesu nipatantīti nipātātipi vadanti.

Particles are so called because they always fall in a single form in the course of speech. Some also say that particles are what fall at the beginning, middle, or end of words.

Asatvavācakā cādisaddā nipātā nāma. Te pana vibhattiyuttā, ayuttā cāti duvidhā honti. Tattha vibhattiyuttā pubbe dassitā eva. Cādayo ayuttā nāma. Te pana anekasatappabhedā honti. Nighaṇṭusatthesu gahetabbāti.

Words such as 'ca', which do not denote a being, are called particles. They are of two kinds: those with case endings and those without. Among them, those with case endings have already been shown. Words such as 'ca' are those without case endings. They are of many hundreds of kinds and should be learned from glossaries.

Abyayataddhitapaccayapadarāsi

The collection of words formed with indeclinable taddhita suffixes.

Abyayataddhitapaccayantā nāma yathā, tathā, ekadhā, ekajjhaṃ, sabbaso, kathaṃ, itthaṃ iccādayo. Tehi tatiyālopo.

Words ending in indeclinable taddhita suffixes are, for example: yathā (as), tathā (so), ekadhā (in one way), ekajjhaṃ (together), sabbaso (entirely), kathaṃ (how), itthaṃ (thus), and so forth. By them, elision of the third case occurs.

Tvādipaccayantapadarāsi

The group of words ending in 'tvā' and other suffixes.

Tvādipaccayantā nāma katvā, katvāna, kātuna, kātuṃ, kātave, dakkhitāye, hetuye, ādāya, upādāya, viceyya, vineyya, sakkacca, āhacca, upasampajja, samecca, avecca, paṭicca, aticca, āgamma, ārabbhaiccādayo. Tesu tvā, tvānantehi paṭhamālopo. Tuṃ, tave, tāye, tuyepaccayantehi catutthīlopoti.

Words ending in 'tvā' and other suffixes are, for example: having done, having done, to do, to do, to do, for seeing, for the sake of, having taken, having taken up, having discerned, having removed, respectfully, having struck, having attained, having come together, having known, having depended on, having transcended, having come to, having undertaken, and so forth. Among these, for those ending in 'tvā' and 'tvāna', elision of the first case occurs. For those ending in the suffixes 'tuṃ', 'tave', 'tāye', and 'tuye', elision of the fourth case occurs.

Dhātavo paccayā ceva, upasagganipātakā.

Roots and suffixes, and also prefixes and particles.

Anekatthāva te paṭi-sambhidā ñāṇagocarā.

They have many meanings and are the domain of the analytical knowledges.

Iti niruttidīpaniyā nāma moggallānadīpaniyā

Thus in the Niruttidīpanī, the Exposition of Moggallāna.

Nāmakaṇḍo niṭṭhito.

The chapter on Nouns is completed.

3. Kārakakaṇḍa

3. The Section on Syntax

Paṭhamāvibhattirāsi

The Section on the First Case

Atha nāmavibhattīnaṃ atthabhedā vuccante.

Now the distinctions in meaning of the nominal case endings are explained.

Kasmiṃ atthe paṭhamā?

In what sense is the first case used?

289. Paṭhamatthamatte caṃ. 2.1.93; pā. 2.3.46.

289. Merely in the primary meaning.

Nāmassa abhidheyyamatte paṭhamāvibhatti hoti.

The first case occurs merely in the sense of the expressed meaning of the noun.

Rukkho, mālā, dhanaṃ.

A tree, a garland, wealth.

Ettha ca mattasaddena kattu, kammādike vibhatyatthe nivatteti. Tasmā atthamattanti liṅgatthoyeva vuccati.

Here, the word 'matta' (merely) excludes the meanings of the case endings related to agent, object, and so on. Therefore, 'atthamatta' (merely the meaning) refers only to the meaning of the nominal stem.

Tattha anuccārite sati suṇantassa avidito attho līnattho nāma. Taṃ līnamatthaṃ gameti bodhetīti liṅgaṃ, uccāritapadaṃ.

Herein, when a word is not uttered, the meaning unknown to the listener is called 'hidden meaning'. That which conveys and reveals that hidden meaning is the nominal stem, the uttered word.

Taṃ pana pakatiliṅgaṃ, nipphannaliṅganti duvidhaṃ. Tattha vibhattirahitaṃ pakatiliṅgaṃ idhādhippetaṃ liṅga, vibhattīnaṃ visuṃ visuṃ vibhāgaṭṭhānattā.

That, however, is of two kinds: the natural nominal stem and the derived nominal stem. Here, the natural nominal stem without case endings is the nominal stem intended, because the case endings are a basis for separate division.

Līnaṃ aṅganti liṅgaṃ. Tattha ‘līna’nti apākaṭaṃ. ‘Aṅga’nti avayavo. Liṅgaṃ, nāmaṃ, pāṭipadikanti atthato ekaṃ.

A 'hidden part' is a nominal stem (liṅga). Herein, 'līna' means unmanifest. 'Aṅga' means part. Nominal stem, noun, and crude form are one in meaning.

Liṅgassa attho paramattho, paññattiatthoti duvidho. Tathā visesanattho, visesyatthoti.

The meaning of the nominal stem is twofold: ultimate meaning and conventional meaning. Similarly, it is twofold: the meaning of the qualifier and the meaning of the qualified.

Tattha visesanattho nāma sakattho, tassa tassa saddassa paṭiniyato pāṭipuggalikatthoti vuttaṃ hoti. Soyeva tasmiṃ tasmiṃ atthe ādimhi sadduppattiyā cirakālañca saddapavattiyā nibaddhakāraṇattā nimittatthoti ca vuccati[M 0.0164]. So suti, jāti, guṇa, dabba, kriyā, nāma, sambandhavasena sattavidho hoti.

Here, the meaning of the qualifier is its own meaning; it is said to be the specific, individual meaning of each word. That very meaning, due to its being the constant cause for the initial arising of a word and its long-standing usage, is also called the meaning of the sign. It is sevenfold, by way of sound, species, quality, substance, action, name, and relation.

Visesyattho nāma sāmaññattho, bahunimittānaṃ sādhāraṇatthoti vuttaṃ hoti, soyeva taṃtaṃnimittayogā nemittakatthoti ca vuccati, so jāti, guṇa, dabba, kriyā, nāmavasena pañcavidho. Go, sukko, daṇḍī, pācako, tissoti.

The meaning of the qualified is the general meaning; it is said to be the common meaning of many signs. That very meaning, due to its connection with particular signs, is also called the meaning derived from a sign. It is fivefold by way of species, quality, substance, action, and name: cow, white, a man with a staff, a cook, Tissa.

Tattha gosaddo yadā jātimattaṃ vadati go jātīti, tadā suti visesanaṃ. Yadā dabbaṃ vadati go gacchatīti, tadā suti ca jāti ca visesanaṃ.

Here, when the word 'go' (cow) denotes merely the species, as in 'go jāti' (cow species), then sound is the qualifier. When it denotes a substance, as in 'go gacchati' (the cow walks), then both sound and species are the qualifier.

Sukkasaddo yadā guṇamattaṃ vadati sukko guṇoti, tadā suti visesanaṃ. Yadā guṇavisesaṃ vadati gossa sukkoti, tadā suti ca guṇajāti ca visesanaṃ. Yadā guṇavantaṃ dabbaṃ vadati sukko goti, tadā suti ca guṇajāti ca guṇaviseso ca sambandho ca visesanaṃ.

The word 'sukka' (white), when it merely denotes a quality, as in 'sukko guṇo' (the quality is white), then sound is the qualifier. When it denotes a specific quality, as in 'gossa sukko' (the whiteness of the cow), then both sound and the quality-species are the qualifier. When it denotes a substance possessing a quality, as in 'sukko go' (the white cow), then sound, the quality-species, the specific quality, and the relation are the qualifier.

Daṇḍīsaddo yadā jātimattaṃ vadati daṇḍī jātīti, tadā suti ca dabbañca visesanaṃ. Yadā dabbavantaṃ dabbaṃ vadati daṇḍī purisoti, tadā suti ca dabbañca jāti ca sambandho ca visesanaṃ.

The word 'daṇḍī' (staff-bearer), when it merely denotes a class, as in 'daṇḍī jāti' (the staff-bearer class), then both sound and substance are the qualifier.
