Saññāyaṃ uttarapade pare sahassa so hoti.

When it is a name, and a subsequent word follows, 'saha' becomes 'so'.

Saha [M 0.0269] āyattaṃ sāyattaṃ, saha palāsaṃ sapalāsaṃ, agarukārassetaṃ nāmaṃ.

With dependence is 'sāyattaṃ'. With foliage is 'sapalāsaṃ'. This is the name for a matter not to be taken seriously.

383. Apaccakkhe ka. 404; rū. 307; nī. 859; caṃ. 5.2.99; pā. 6.3.80.

383. When not directly perceptible.

Apaccakkhe gamyamāne uttarapade pare sahassa so hoti.

When what is meant is not directly perceptible, and a subsequent word follows, 'saha' becomes 'so'.

Oḍḍiyati etāyāti oḍḍi, pāso. Oḍḍiyā saha yo vattatīti soḍḍi, kapoto. Idha ‘oḍḍi’ apaccakkhā. “Sāggi kapoto”tipi pāṭho, picunā saha vattatīti sapicukā, vātamaṇḍalikā, sā ca apaccakkhā, uggantvā ākāse paribbhamantaṃ picusaṅghāṭaṃ disvā ñātabbā. “Sapisācā vātamaṇḍalikā”tipi pāṭho. Evaṃ sarajā, vātā, sarakkhasī, ratti.

One is bound by this, hence 'oḍḍi', a snare. He who exists with a snare is 'soḍḍi', a pigeon. Here, the 'oḍḍi' is not directly perceptible. There is also the reading 'sāggi kapoto' (a pigeon with fire). That which exists with cotton is 'sapicukā', a whirlwind. And that is not directly perceptible; it is to be known by seeing a mass of cotton rising and swirling in the sky. There is also the reading 'sapisācā vātamaṇḍalikā' (a whirlwind with demons). Similarly, 'sarajā vātā' (dusty winds), 'sarakkhasī ratti' (a night with a demoness).

384. Akāle sakatthassa ka. 404; rū. 370; nī. 859; caṃ. 5.2.110; pā. 6.3.81.

384. Of 'sakattha', when it is unseasonable.

Sakatthappadhānassa sahasaddassa so hoti akāle uttarapade pare.

For the word 'saha', when its primary meaning is 'sakattha' (one's own purpose), it becomes 'so' when a subsequent word not denoting time follows.

Sabrahmaṃ, sacakkaṃ.

Sabrahmaṃ (with Brahma), sacakkaṃ (with the discus).

Akāleti kiṃ? Saha pubbaṇhaṃ, saha paraṇhaṃ, sunakkhattena saha pavattaṃ pubbaṇhaṃ, paraṇhanti attho.

Why the stipulation 'not denoting time'? [Examples where the rule does not apply are:] 'Saha pubbaṇhaṃ' (with the forenoon), 'saha paraṇhaṃ' (with the afternoon). The meaning is: 'the forenoon and the afternoon occurring together with an auspicious constellation'.

385. Ganthantādhikye ka. 404; rū. 370; nī. 859; caṃ. 5.2.101; pā. 6.3.79.

385. Regarding the end of a treatise and excess.

Ganthassa anto ganthanto. Yathā taṃ kaccāyanaganthassa anto uṇādikappo, adhikabhāvo ādhikyaṃ, ganthante ca ādhikye ca vattamānassa sahasaddassa so hoti uttarapade pare.

The end of a treatise is 'ganthanta'. For example, the end of the Kaccāyana treatise is the Uṇādi chapter. The state of being in excess is 'ādhikya'. For the word 'saha', when it has the meaning of 'end of a treatise' and 'excess', it becomes 'so' when a subsequent word follows.

Saha [M 0.0270] uṇādinā’ yaṃ adhiyateti taṃ soṇādi, sakalaṃ kaccāyanaṃ adhītetyattho. Saha muhuttena sakalaṃ jotiṃ adhīte samuhuttaṃ, jotīti nakkhattasatthaṃ.

That which is studied together with the Uṇādi is 'soṇādi'; the meaning is that the entire Kaccāyana is studied. He studies the entire science of astrology in a moment, hence 'samuhuttaṃ'; 'joti' means the scripture of the constellations.

Ādhikye – sadoṇā, khārī, sakahāpaṇaṃ, nikkhaṃ, samāsakaṃ, kahāpaṇaṃ. Niccatthamidaṃ suttaṃ.

In the sense of excess: 'sadoṇā khārī' (a khārī with a doṇa in excess), 'sakahāpaṇaṃ nikkhaṃ' (a nikkha with a kahāpaṇa in excess), 'samāsakaṃ kahāpaṇaṃ' (a kahāpaṇa with a māsaka in excess). This rule is obligatory.

386. Samānassa pakkhādīsu vā ka. 404; rū. 370; nī. 859; caṃ. 5.2.103-4; pā. 6.3.84-86.

386. Of 'samāna', optionally, before 'pakkha' and so forth.

Pakkhādīsu uttarapadesu samānassa so hoti vā.

When subsequent words like 'pakkha' and so forth follow, 'samāna' optionally becomes 'so'.

Samāno pakkho sahāyo sapakkho, samāno pakkho yassāti vā sapakkho, samānapakkho vā. Evaṃ sajāti, samānajāti, sajanapado, saratti.

`Samāno pakkho` (an equal party), meaning a companion, becomes `sapakkho`; or, 'he whose party is equal' is `sapakkho`; or, `samānapakkho`. Similarly, `sajāti` or `samānajāti` (of the same birth); `sajanapado` (of the same country); `saratti` (of the same group).

Samāno pati yassā sā sapati. Evaṃ sanābhi, sabandhu, sabrahmacārī, sanāmo. Avhayaṃ vuccati nāmaṃ, candena samānaṃ avhayaṃ yassa so candasavhayo, sagotto, indena samānaṃ gottaṃ yassa so indasagotto, sarūpaṃ, saṭṭhānaṃ. Hari vuccati suvaṇṇaṃ, harinā samāno vaṇṇo yassa so harissavaṇṇo, sassa dvittaṃ. Evaṃ siṅgīnikkhasavaṇṇo, savayo, sadhano, sadhammo, sajātiyo.

She whose husband is common is `sapatī`. Similarly, `sanābhi` (of the same navel), `sabandhu` (of the same relatives), `sabrahmacārī` (a fellow practitioner of the holy life), `sanāmo` (of the same name). A name is called `avhaya`; he whose name is the same as the moon's is `candasavhayo`. `Sagotto` (of the same clan); he whose clan is the same as Indra's is `indasagotto`. `Sarūpaṃ` (of the same form), `saṭṭhānaṃ` (of the same place). Gold is called `hari`; he whose color is the same as gold is `harissavaṇṇo`, with the doubling of 's'. Similarly, `siṅgīnikkhasavaṇṇo` (of the color of Siṅgī gold), `savayo` (of the same age), `sadhano` (of the same wealth), `sadhammo` (of the same doctrine), `sajātiyo` (of the same birth).

Pakkhādīsūti kiṃ? Samānasīlo.

Why the stipulation 'before 'pakkha' and so forth'? [As a counter-example:] `Samānasīlo` (of similar virtue).

387. Udare iye ka. 404; rū. 370; nī. 859; caṃ. 5.2.105; pā. 6.3.88.

387. Before 'udara' when 'iya' follows.

Iyayutte udare pare samānassa so hoti vā.

When 'udara' joined with 'iya' follows, 'samāna' optionally becomes 'so'.

Samāne udare jāto sodariyo, samānodariyo.

Born of the same womb is 'sodariyo' or 'samānodariyo'.

Iyeti kiṃ? Samānodaratā.

Why the stipulation 'when 'iya' follows'? [As a counter-example:] `Samānodaratā` (the state of having the same womb).

Aññesupi [M 0.0271] samānassa so hoti, candena samānā sirī yassa taṃ candassasirīkaṃ, mukhaṃ. Evaṃ padumassasirīkaṃ, vadanaṃ.

In other cases too, 'samāna' becomes 'so'. That whose splendor is equal to the moon is 'candassasirīkaṃ', meaning a face. Similarly, 'padumassasirīkaṃ' (whose splendor is equal to a lotus), meaning a face.

Mahāvuttinā santādīnañca so hoti, saṃvijjati lomaṃ assāti salomako. Evaṃ sapakkhako, saṃvijjanti āsavā etesanti sāsavā, saṃvijjanti paccayā etesanti sappaccayā, saṃvijjanti attano uttaritarā dhammā etesanti sauttarā, santo puriso sappuriso. Tathā sajjano, saddhammo, santassa bhāvo sabbhāvo iccādi.

According to the Mahāvutti, the substitution 'sa' also occurs for 'santa' and so forth. 'Hair exists for him,' thus `salomako`. Similarly, `sapakkhako` (with wings). 'Taints exist in them,' thus `sāsavā`. 'Conditions exist for them,' thus `sappaccayā`. 'Qualities higher than their own exist for them,' thus `sauttarā`. A good person is `sappuriso`. Similarly, `sajjano` (a good person), `saddhammo` (the true Dhamma), 'the state of being good' is `sabbhāvo`, and so forth.

Iti sa-rāsi.

Thus the section on 'sa'.

388. Imassidaṃ ka. 129; rū. 222; nī. 305.

388. Of 'ima', 'idaṃ'.

Uttarapade pare imassa idaṃ hoti.

When a subsequent word follows, 'ima' becomes 'idaṃ'.

Ayaṃ attho etassāti idamatthī, samāsante ī, idamatthino bhāvo idamatthitā. Ayaṃ paccayo etesanti idappaccayā, idappaccayānaṃ bhāvo idappaccayatā. “Imesaṃ paccayā idappaccayā, idappaccayā eva idappaccayatā”tipi yojenti. ‘Ida’nti nipātapadampi atthi, “rūpañca hidaṃ bhikkhave attā abhavissā, vedanā ca hidaṃ. Saññā ca hidaṃ. Saṅkhārā ca hidaṃ bhikkhave attā abhavissaṃsu” iccādi mahāva. 20.

'This meaning is for this,' thus `idamatthī`; the suffix `ī` is at the end of the compound; the state of being `idamatthin` is `idamatthitā`. 'These conditions are for these,' thus `idappaccayā`; the state of being `idappaccayā` is `idappaccayatā`. They also construe it as: 'The conditions of these are `idappaccayā`; `idappaccayā` itself is `idappaccayatā`.' There is also the indeclinable particle 'ida', as in: 'And if, bhikkhus, this form were self... and this feeling... and this perception... and if, bhikkhus, these formations were self...' and so forth.

389. Puṃ pumassa vā ka. 82; rū. 149.

389. Of 'puma', optionally, 'puṃ'.

Uttarapade pare pumassa puṃ hoti vā.

When a subsequent word follows, 'puma' optionally becomes 'puṃ'.

Pumassa liṅgaṃ pulliṅgaṃ, pumassa bhāvo pumbhāvo, pumā ca so kokilo cāti puṅkokilo, pumā ca so go cāti puṅgavo, ‘go tvacatthe…’ti apaccayo, napuṃsako.

The gender of a male is `pulliṅgaṃ`; the state of being male is `pumbhāvo`. 'He is a male and a cuckoo,' thus `puṅkokilo`. 'He is a male and an ox,' thus `puṅgavo`. Regarding 'go' in the sense of 'skin'... it is the suffix 'a'; it is neuter.

Vāti kiṃ? Pumitthī.

Why the stipulation 'optionally'? [As a counter-example:] `Pumitthī` (a man and a woman).

390. Ṭa ntantūnaṃ ka. 126; rū. 101; nī. 301.

390. Of 'nta' and 'ntu', 'ṭa'.

Uttarapade [M 0.0272] pare nta, ntūnaṃ ṭa hoti vā kvaci.

When a subsequent word follows, 'nta' and 'ntu' optionally become 'ṭa' in some cases.

Bhavaṃ patiṭṭho yesaṃ te bhavaṃpatiṭṭhā, bindāgamo. Bhagavā mūlaṃ yesaṃ te bhagavaṃmūlakā, dhammā. Evaṃ bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā, dhammā.

'The venerable one is their foundation,' thus they are `bhavaṃpatiṭṭhā`; there is the insertion of a bindu. 'The Blessed One is their root,' thus they are `bhagavaṃmūlakā`, referring to the dhammas. Similarly, `bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā`, referring to the dhammas.

Bahulādhikārā tarādīsu ca paresu, mahantīnaṃ atisayena mahāti mahattarī, rattaññūnaṃ mahantassa bhāvo rattaññumahattaṃ. Evaṃ jātimahattaṃ, guṇamahattaṃ, puññamahattaṃ, arahantassa bhāvo arahattaṃ.

Due to the principle of extensive application, and also when 'tara' and so forth follow: 'Exceedingly great among the great' is `mahattarī`. The state of greatness of one long-experienced is `rattaññumahattaṃ`. Similarly, `jātimahattaṃ` (greatness of birth), `guṇamahattaṃ` (greatness of virtue), `puññamahattaṃ` (greatness of merit). The state of an arahant is `arahattaṃ`.

391. A ka. 642; rū. 589; nī. 1269; caṃ. 5.2.106; pā. 6.3.89.

391. The substitution of 'a'.

Uttarapade pare nta, ntūnaṃ a hoti.

When a subsequent word follows, 'nta' and 'ntū' become 'a'.

Bhavantapatiṭṭhā, mayaṃ, guṇavantapatiṭṭhā, mayaṃ.

We are established in the Blessed One; we are established in the virtuous.

392. Rīrikkhakesu ka. 642; rū. 589; nī. 1269; caṃ. 5.2.107; pā. 6.3.89-90.

392. Regarding 'rī', 'rikkha', and 'ka'.

Rī, rikkha, kapaccayantesu paresu samānassa so hoti.

When 'rī', 'rikkha', and words ending in the suffix 'ka' follow, 'samāna' becomes 'so'.

Niccasamāsattā aññapadena viggaho, saṃvijjatīti samāno, paccakkhe viya citte upalabbhatīti attho. Samāno viya so dissatīti sadī, sadikkho, sadiso, samānā viya te dissantīti sadisā.

Due to being a permanent compound, the analysis is with another word. 'Samāna' means 'existing'; the meaning is that it is perceived in the mind as if directly perceptible. Because he appears as if similar, hence 'sadī', 'sadikkho', 'sadiso'; because they appear as if similar, hence 'sadisā'.

393. Ntakimimānaṃ ṭākīṭī ka. 126; rū. 101; nī. 301.

393. Regarding 'nta', 'kiṃ', and 'ima' becoming 'ṭā', 'kī', and 'ṭī'.

Tesu paresu ntapaccayantassa ca kiṃ, imasaddānañca kamena ṭā, kī, ṭī honti.

When those follow, for words ending in the 'nta' suffix, and for the words 'kiṃ' and 'ima', the substitutions are respectively 'ṭā', 'kī', and 'ṭī'.

Bhavaṃ [M 0.0273] viya so dissatīti bhavādī, bhavādikkho, bhavādiso, ko viya so dissatīti kīdī, kīdikkho, kīdiso, ayaṃ viya so dissatīti īdī, īdikkho, īdiso.

Because he appears like the revered one, hence 'bhavādī', 'bhavādikkho', 'bhavādiso'; because he appears like whom, hence 'kīdī', 'kīdikkho', 'kīdiso'; because he appears like this one, hence 'īdī', 'īdikkho', 'īdiso'.

394. Sabbādīnamā ka. 642; rū. 589; nī. 1269; caṃ. 5.2.108; pā. 6.3.91.

394. For 'sabba' and so forth, 'ā'.

Tesu paresu sabbādināmakānaṃ ya, ta, eta, añña, amha, tumhasaddānaṃ anto ā hoti.

When those follow, the end of the pronouns 'sabba' and so forth, namely 'ya', 'ta', 'eta', 'añña', 'amha', and 'tumha', becomes 'ā'.

Yādī, yādikkho, yādiso, tādī, tādikkho, tādiso, etādī, etādikkho, etādiso.

Yādī, yādikkho, yādiso; tādī, tādikkho, tādiso; etādī, etādikkho, etādiso.

395. Vetasseṭa ka. 642; rū. 589; nī. 1269.

395. Optionally for 'etassa', 'eṭa'.

Tesu paresu etassa eṭa hoti vā.

When those follow, 'etassa' optionally becomes 'eṭa'.

Edī, edikkho, ediso, aññādī, aññādikkho, aññādiso, amhādī, amhādikkho, amhādiso, tumhādī, tumhādikkho, tumhādiso.

Edī, edikkho, ediso; aññādī, aññādikkho, aññādiso; amhādī, amhādikkho, amhādiso; tumhādī, tumhādikkho, tumhādiso.

396. Tumhamhānaṃ tāmekasmiṃ ka. 642; rū. 589; nī. 1269.

396. For 'tumha' and 'amha', 'tā' and 'mā' in the singular.

Tesu paresu ekavacane pavattānaṃ tumha’ mhasaddānaṃ tā, mā honti vā.

When those follow, for the words 'tumha' and 'amha' occurring in the singular, they optionally become 'tā' and 'mā'.

Ahaṃ viya so dissatīti mādī, mādikkho, mādiso, tvaṃ viya so dissatīti tādī, tādikkho, tādiso.

Because he appears like me, hence 'mādī', 'mādikkho', 'mādiso'; because he appears like you, hence 'tādī', 'tādikkho', 'tādiso'.

Ekasminti kiṃ? Amhe viya te dissantīti amhādino, amhādikkhā, amhādisā, tumhe viya te dissantīti tumhādino, tumhādikkhā, tumhādisā. Ettha ca upamānatthasseva ekattaṃ icchīyati, tasmā ahaṃ viya te dissantīti mādisā [M 0.0274] tvaṃ viya te dissantīti tādino, tādisātipi yujjanti. “Mādisā ve jinā honti, ye pattā āsavakkhaya”nti mahāva. 11 pāḷi, imāni padāni upari kitakaṇḍepi āgamissanti.

Why 'in the singular'? Because they appear like us, hence 'amhādino', 'amhādikkhā', 'amhādisā'; because they appear like you, hence 'tumhādino', 'tumhādikkhā', 'tumhādisā'. And here, only oneness of the standard of comparison is intended; therefore, 'because they appear like me', 'mādisā', and 'because they appear like you', 'tādino', 'tādisā', are also suitable. The Pāli text is: “Surely, victors are those like me, who have attained the destruction of the taints.” These words will also appear later in the Kitakaṇḍa.

397. Taṃmamaññatra ka. 143; rū. 235; nī. 322.

397. 'Taṃ' and 'maṃ' elsewhere.

Rī, rikkha, kapaccayehi aññasmiṃ uttarapade pare tumha’mhānaṃ taṃ, maṃādesā honti kvaci.

When a subsequent word other than those with the suffixes 'rī', 'rikkha', and 'ka' follows, 'taṃ' and 'maṃ' are sometimes substituted for 'tumha' and 'amha'.

Tvaṃ leṇaṃ yesaṃ te taṃleṇā, ahaṃ leṇaṃ yesaṃ te maṃleṇā saṃ. ni. 4.359. Evaṃ taṃdīpā, maṃdīpā saṃ. ni. 4.359, taṃpaṭisaraṇā, maṃpaṭisaraṇā.

Those for whom you are a shelter are 'taṃleṇā'; those for whom I am a shelter are 'maṃleṇā'. Similarly, 'taṃdīpā', 'maṃdīpā', 'taṃpaṭisaraṇā', 'maṃpaṭisaraṇā'.

398. Manādyāpādīnamo maye ca ka. 183; rū. 386; nī. 375.

398. For 'manādi' and 'āpādi', 'o' before 'maya', etc.

Uttarapade mayapaccaye ca pare manādīnaṃ āpādīnañca o hoti.

When a subsequent word and the suffix 'maya' follow, 'o' occurs for the 'manas' group and the 'āpas' group.

Manoseṭṭhā, manomayā, rajojallaṃ, rajomayaṃ, sabbo manogaṇo idha vattabbo, āpodhātu, āpomayaṃ. Anuyanti disodisaṃ dī. ni. 3.281, jīva tvaṃ saradosataṃ jā. 1.2.9.

Manoseṭṭhā, manomayā; rajojallaṃ, rajomayaṃ; the entire 'manas' group should be included here. Āpodhātu, āpomayaṃ. Anuyanti disodisaṃ; jīva tvaṃ saradosataṃ.

399. Parassa saṅkhyāsu ka. 36; rū. 47; nī. 130.

399. For 'para', before numbers.

Saṅkhyāsu parāsu parassa o hoti.

When numbers follow, 'o' occurs for 'para'.

Parosataṃ, parosahassaṃ, paropaṇṇāsa dhammā, idha parasaddo “indriyaparopariyatta”nti ettha viya adhikatthavācisaddantaraṃ, na sabbanāmaṃ.

Over a hundred, over a thousand, over fifty qualities. Here the word 'para', as in 'indriyaparopariyatta', is another word indicating an additional meaning, not a pronoun.

400. Jane puthassu ka. 49; rū. 44; nī. 129.

400. Before 'jana', for 'putha', 'u'.

Jane [M 0.0275] pare puthassa u hoti.

When 'jana' follows, 'u' occurs for 'putha'.

Ariyehi puthagevāyaṃ janoti puthujjano. Api ca pāḷinaye puthusaddoyeva bahulaṃ dissati, puthu kilese janentīti puthujjanā, puthu nānāsatthārānaṃ mukhaṃ ullokentīti puthujjanā, puthu nānāoghehi vuyhantīti puthujjanā mahāni. 51, 94, saññānānāttaputhuttapabhedaṃ paṭicca taṇhānānāttaputhuttapabhedo hoti dha. sa. aṭṭha. 1, iṅgha aññepi pucchassu, puthū samaṇabrāhmaṇe saṃ. ni. 1.246. Gāmā gāmaṃ vicarissaṃ, sāvake vinayaṃ puthū, āyatāni puthūni ca, puthunā vijjuvaṇṇinā jā. 2.22.968, puthukāyā puthubhūtā iccādi. Tasmā “puthageva, puthakkaraṇe” iccādīsu thussa ukārassa akāro akāroti? yujjati.

This person is called a 'puthujjana' because he is separate from the noble ones. Moreover, in the Pāli tradition, the word 'puthu' itself is frequently seen: 'puthujjanas' are those who generate diverse defilements; 'puthujjanas' are those who look to the mouths of diverse teachers; 'puthujjanas' are those who are carried away by diverse floods. Due to the diversity and manifoldness of perceptions, there arises the diversity and manifoldness of craving. “Go ahead, ask others, the many ascetics and brahmins.” “I shall wander from village to village, disciplining many disciples”; “and the sense-spheres are various”; “with a complexion like lightning”; “with various bodies, having become various,” and so on. Therefore, in cases like 'puthageva' (quite separate) and 'puthakkaraṇe' (making separate), the substitution of 'a' for the 'u' of 'thu' is appropriate.

401. So chassāhāyatanesu vā ka. 374; rū. 408; nī. 804.

401. For cha, so occurs optionally before aha and āyatana.

Ahe ca āyatane ca pare chassa so hoti vā.

When 'aha' and 'āyatana' follow, 'so' optionally occurs for 'cha'.

Cha ahāni sāhaṃ. Atthi sāhassa jīvitaṃ jā. 2.22.314, ‘sāhassā’ti sāhaṃ+assāti chedo. Saḷāyatanaṃ.

For cha ahāni (six days), sāhaṃ. Atthi sāhassa jīvitaṃ (There is life for six days). The division of ‘sāhassā’ is sāhaṃ+assa. Saḷāyatanaṃ (the six sense-bases).

Vāti kiṃ? Chāhappaṭicchannā āpatti cūḷava. 134, cha āyatanāni.

Why 'optionally'? An offense concealed for six days (chāhappaṭicchannā āpatti); the six sense-bases (cha āyatanāni).

402. Ltupitādīnamāraṅraṅa ka. 200; rū. 159; nī. 415; caṃ. 5.2.20; pā. 6.3.32.

402. For words ending in the suffix -ltu, and for pitu and so on, āraṅ and raṅa are the substitutes.

Samāsuttarapade pare ltupaccayantānaṃ pitādīnañca kamena āraṅa, raṅa honti vā.

When a subsequent member of a compound follows, āraṅa and raṅa optionally occur, respectively, for words ending with the -ltu suffix and for pitu and so on.

Satthuno [M 0.0276] dassanaṃ satthāradassanaṃ. Evaṃ kattāraniddeso. Mātā ca pitā ca mātarapitaro, mātāpitūsu saṃvaḍḍho mātāpitarasaṃvaḍḍho.

Seeing the Teacher (satthuno dassanaṃ) is satthāradassanaṃ. Similarly, kattāraniddeso. Mother and father (mātā ca pitā ca) are mātarapitaro. One brought up by mother and father (mātāpitūsu saṃvaḍḍho) is mātāpitarasaṃvaḍḍho.

Vāti kiṃ? Satthudassanaṃ, kattu niddeso, mātāpitaro.

Why 'optionally'? Satthudassanaṃ (seeing the Teacher), kattuniddeso (designation of the agent), mātāpitaro (mother and father).

403. Vijjāyonisambandhīnamā tatra catthe ka. 199; rū. 158; nī. 736; caṃ. 5.2.21; pā. 6.3.25.

403. For those related by knowledge or birth, ā is the substitute in that context, in a dvandva compound.

Catthasamāse vijjāsambandhīnaṃ yonisambandhīnañca ltupitādīnaṃ ā hoti tesveva paresu.

In a dvandva compound, for words such as those ending in -ltu and pitu, which are related by knowledge or birth, the final vowel becomes ā when another such word follows.

Mātāpitā, mātāpitaro iccādi.

Mātāpitā (mother and father), mātāpitaro (parents), and so on.

Tatrāti kiṃ? Mātuyā bhātā mātubhātā.

Why 'in that context'? The mother's brother (mātuyā bhātā) is mātubhātā.

Ettha ca vijjāsippāni sikkhāpentā ācariyā sissānaṃ vijjāsambandhī mātāpitaro nāma.

Herein, teachers who instruct students in knowledge and skills are called 'mother and father' in relation to knowledge for the students.

404. Putte ka. 199; rū. 158; nī. 736; caṃ. 5.2.22; pā. 6.3.25.

404. Before putta.

Catte putte pare vijjāyonisambandhīnaṃ ltupitādīnaṃ ā hoti.

When putta follows in a dvandva compound, the final vowel of words such as those ending in -ltu and pitu, which are related by knowledge or birth, becomes ā.

Mātāputtā gacchanti, pitāputtā gacchanti. Mahāvuttinā tesañca i hoti, mātipakkho, pitipakkho. Mātigho labhate dukhaṃ jā. 2.19.118, pitigho labhate dukhaṃ, māttikaṃ dhanaṃ, pettikaṃ dhanaṃ pārā. 34. Ettha ca mātuyā santakaṃ māttikaṃ, pituno santakaṃ pettikaṃ, dvittaṃ vuddhi ca. Mātito, pitito, bhātā eva bhātiko, bhātikarājā.

Mother and son go (mātāputtā gacchanti); father and son go (pitāputtā gacchanti). According to the Mahāvutti, for them i also occurs: mātipakkho (mother's side), pitipakkho (father's side). One who kills his mother obtains suffering (mātigho labhate dukhaṃ); one who kills his father obtains suffering (pitigho labhate dukhaṃ). Maternal wealth (māttikaṃ dhanaṃ); paternal wealth (pettikaṃ dhanaṃ). Herein, what belongs to the mother is māttikaṃ, and what belongs to the father is pettikaṃ; there is also doubling and vowel gradation. From the mother (mātito); from the father (pitito). A brother is also bhātiko; bhātikarājā (a brotherly king).

405. Jāyāya jāyaṃ patimhi ka. 339; rū. 358; nī. 731; ‘…jayaṃ patimhi’ (bahūsu).

405. For jāyā, jāyaṃ is the substitute before pati.

Patimhi [M 0.0277] pare jāyāsaddassa jāyaṃ hoti.

When pati follows, jāyaṃ occurs for the word jāyā.

Puttaṃ janetīti jāyā, jāyā ca pati ca jāyampatī jayampatī (bahūsu). Atha vā “jāyampatī”ti idaṃ sandhividhināva siddhaṃ, tasmā “jampatī”tipāṭho siyā yathā “devarājā sujampatī’ saṃ. ni. 1.264’ti, yathā ca sakkataganthesu “dāro ca pati ca dampatī”ti. Idha pana mahāvuttinā patimhi sujātāya sujaṃ hoti, dārassa ca daṃ hoti, tathā jāyā ca pati ca jampatīti niṭṭhaṃ gantabbaṃ.

She who bears a son is a jāyā; wife and husband (jāyā ca pati ca) are jāyampatī. Alternatively, this jāyampatī is established by the rules of sandhi alone; therefore, the reading may be jampatī, as in ‘devarājā sujampatī’, and as in Sanskrit texts, ‘dāro ca pati ca dampatī’. Here, however, according to the Mahāvutti, before pati, sujaṃ occurs for sujātā, and daṃ occurs for dāra; thus, it should be concluded that jāyā ca pati ca becomes jampatī.

Yañca vuttiyaṃ “jānipatīti pakatyantarena siddhaṃ, tathā dampatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha puttaṃ janetīti jānī. Jānī ca pati ca jānīpatīti yujjati. “Tudampatī”ti pāṭho. Kaccāyane ca ‘jāyāya tu daṃjāni patimhī’ti. Tattha tusaddo padapūraṇamatte yujjati.

And it is said in the commentary that jānipatī is established by another natural form, and likewise dampatī. There, 'she who begets a son' is jānī. Jānī and pati combine as jānīpatī, which is suitable. The reading is tudampatī. And in Kaccāyana, it is ‘jāyāya tu daṃjāni patimhī’. There, the particle tu is used merely for filling out the line.

406. Saññāyamudodakassa ka. 404; rū. 370; nī. 257; caṃ. 5.2.65; pā. 6.3.57.

406. For udaka, udo is the substitute in designations.

Saññāyaṃ gamyamānāyaṃ uttarapade pare udakassa udo hoti.

When a designation is implied and a subsequent word follows, udo occurs for udaka.

Udakaṃ dhāretīti udadhi, mahantaṃ udakaṃ dhāretīti mahodadhi, udakaṃ pivanti etthāti udapānaṃ, udakaṃ pivanti etāyāti udapāti.

'That which holds water' (udakaṃ dhāreti) is udadhi; 'that which holds much water' (mahantaṃ udakaṃ dhāreti) is mahodadhi; 'where water is drunk' (udakaṃ pivanti ettha) is udapānaṃ; 'by which water is drunk' (udakaṃ pivanti etāya) is udapāti.

407. Kumbhādīsu vā ka. 404; rū. 370; nī. 257; caṃ. 5.2.69; pā. 6.3.59.

407. Optionally before kumbha and so on.

Kumbhādīsu paresu udakassa udo hoti vā.

When kumbha and similar words follow, udo optionally occurs for udaka.

Udakassa [M 0.0278] kumbho udakumbho, udakakumbho. Evaṃ udapatto, udakapatto, udabindu, udakabindu. Mahāvuttinā syādīsupi, “nīlodā pokkharaṇī”ti pāḷi.

'A pot of water' (udakassa kumbho) is udakumbho or udakakumbho. Similarly, udapatto or udakapatto; udabindu or udakabindu. According to the Mahāvutti, this also applies before case endings, as in the Pāli passage ‘nīlodā pokkharaṇī’ (a blue-watered lotus pond).

408. Sotādīsu lopo ka. 404; rū. 370; nī. 256.

408. Before sota and so on, there is elision.

Sotādīsu paresu udakassa ussa lopo hoti.

When sota and similar words follow, the 'u' of udaka is elided.

Udakassa sotaṃ dakasotaṃ, udake rakkhaso dakarakkhaso, udakaṃ āsayo yesaṃ te dakāsayā, pāṇā. Mahāvuttinā syādīsupi, “dake dakāsayā sentī”ti saṃ. ni. 3.78 (thokaṃ visadisaṃ) pāḷi.

'A stream of water' (udakassa sotaṃ) is dakasotaṃ; 'a demon in the water' (udake rakkhaso) is dakarakkhaso; 'those whose abode is water' (udakaṃ āsayo yesaṃ) are dakāsayā, i.e., living beings. According to the Mahāvutti, this also applies before case endings, as in the Pāli passage, ‘dake dakāsayā sentī’ (water-dwellers sleep in the water).

409. Pubbāparajjasāyamajjhehāhassa ṇho ka. 404; rū. 370; nho (sī.).

409. For aha, ṇha is the substitute after Pubba, Apara, Ajja, Sāya, and Majjha.

Pubbādīhi parassa ahassa ṇho hoti.

After Pubba and so forth, ṇho is the substitute for a following aha.

Pubbaṇho, aparaṇho, ajjaṇho, sāyaṇho sāyanho, majjhaṇho.

Forenoon, afternoon, today, evening, midday.

Nānādesarāsi niṭṭhito.

The section on various substitutions is concluded.

Abyayarāsi

The Section on Indeclinables.

410. Kupādayo niccamasyādividhimhi ka. 324; rū. 339; caṃ. 2.2.24; pā. 2.2.18.

410. Ku, pa, and so forth are always compounded, except in the rule concerning case endings.

Syādividhito aññattha kuādayo pādayo ca saddā syādyantena saha niccaṃ ekatthā honti.

Apart from the rule concerning case endings, the words ku and so forth, and pa and so forth, always have a single meaning together with a word ending in a case suffix.

Kucchito brāhmaṇo kubrāhmaṇo, īsakaṃ uṇhaṃ kaduṇhaṃ, pākaṭo hutvā bhavatīti pātubhūto, āvī ‘āvi’pi dissati hutvā bhavatīti āvībhūto, tuṇhī bhavatīti tuṇhībhūto, pamukho nāyako panāyako, pakārena karitvā pakaritvā [M 0.0279] pakārena kataṃ pakataṃ, paṭhamaṃ vā kataṃ pakataṃ, virūpo puriso duppuriso. Evaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, sobhaṇo puriso supuriso. Evaṃ sukataṃ, abhidhammo, abhitthuto, bhusaṃ kaḷāro ākaḷāro, bhusaṃ bandho ābandho iccādi.

A despised brahmin is kubrāhmaṇa; slightly hot is kaduṇha; one who has become manifest is pātubhūta; one who has become evident is āvībhūta; one who has become silent is tuṇhībhūta; a prominent leader is panāyaka; having done in a special manner is pakaritvā; done in a special manner is pakata; or done first is pakata; an ugly man is duppurisa. Similarly, dukkaṭa (ill-done); a handsome man is supurisa. Similarly, sukata (well-done); abhidhamma; abhitthuto (greatly praised); bhusaṃ kaḷāro (very dark) is ākaḷāro; bhusaṃ bandho (very bound) is ābandho, and so forth.

Pādayo pakatādyatthe paṭhamāya ekatthā honti, pakato ācariyo pācariyo. Evaṃ payyako, paro antevāsī pantevāsī, paro putto paputto, paro nattā panattā.

Pa and so forth, in the sense of 'original' and so on, have a single meaning with a word in the nominative case: pakato ācariyo (an original teacher) is pācariyo. Similarly, payyako (an original elder); a distant pupil is pantevāsī; a distant son is paputto; a distant grandson is panattā.

Atyādayo atikkantādyatthe dutiyāya, mañcaṃ atikkanto atimañco. Evaṃ atibālo, ativelā.

Ati and so forth, in the sense of 'exceeding' and so on, are compounded with a word in the accusative case: one who has passed beyond the bed is atimañco. Similarly, atibālo (exceedingly foolish); ativelā (excessive time).

Avādayo kuṭṭhādyatthe tatiyāya, kokilāya avakuṭṭhaṃ vanaṃ avakokilaṃ, ‘avakuṭṭha’nti chaḍḍitanti vadanti. Evaṃ avamayūraṃ.

Ava and so forth, in the sense of 'despised' and so on, are compounded with a word in the instrumental case: a forest despised by cuckoos is avakokilaṃ. They say 'avakuṭṭha' means 'rejected'. Similarly, avamayūraṃ (despised by peacocks).

Pariyādayo gilānādyatthe catutthiyā, ajjhāyituṃ gilāno pariyajjheno.

Pari and so forth, in the sense of 'weary' and so on, are compounded with a word in the dative case: one who is weary of reciting is pariyajjheno.

Nyādayo nikkhantādyatthe pañcamiyā, kosambiyā nikkhanto nikkosambi, vānato nikkhantaṃ nibbānaṃ.

Ni and so forth, in the sense of 'departed' and so on, are compounded with a word in the ablative case: one who has departed from Kosambi is nikkosambi; that which has departed from craving (vana) is nibbānaṃ.

Asyādividhimhīti kiṃ? Rukkhaṃ pati vijjotate.

What is the purpose of [the phrase] 'except in the rule concerning case endings'? Rukkhaṃ pati vijjotate (It shines upon the tree).

411. Cī kriyatthehi caṃ. 2.2.25; pā. 1.4.60, 61.

411. Cī is compounded with words denoting action.

Cīpaccayanto saddo kriyatthehi saddehi saha ekattho hoti.

A word ending with the suffix cī has a single meaning together with words denoting action.

Balasā kiriya balīkiriya, pākaṭīkiriya, pākaṭībhuyya, pākaṭībhaviya.

Balasā kiriya (action by force) is balīkiriya; pākaṭīkiriya (making manifest); pākaṭībhuyya (having become manifest); pākaṭībhaviya (having become manifest).

412. Bhūsanādarānādarādīsvehi saha caṃ. 2.2.27; pā. 1.4.63, 64.

412. [Indeclinables are compounded] with these [words denoting action] in the sense of ornamentation, respect, disrespect, and so on.

Alamādayo [M 0.0280] saddā bhūsanādīsu atthesu etehi kriyatthehi saha ekatthā honti.

Words like alaṃ and so forth, in the sense of ornamentation and so on, have a single meaning together with these words denoting action.

Bhūsanaṃ akāsīti alaṃkiriya, samaṃ ādaraṃ akāsīti sakkacca, asamaṃ anādaraṃ akāsīti asakkacca, binduno pararūpattaṃ.

Bhūsanaṃ akāsi (he adorned) is alaṃkiriya; samaṃ ādaraṃ akāsi (he acted respectfully) is sakkacca; asamaṃ anādaraṃ akāsi (he acted disrespectfully) is asakkacca. The bindu is assimilated to the following sound.

Bhūsanādīsūti kiṃ? Alaṃ bhutvā gato, ‘ala’nti pariyattaṃ, sakkatvā gato, sobhaṇaṃ katvātyattho. “Kacca, kiriya” iccādinā saṃkhittarūpehi upapadena saha siddhehi eva ekatthasaññā, na “katvā” iccādinā asaṃkhittarūpehi visuṃ siddhehīti adhippāyo.

What is the purpose of [the phrase] 'in the sense of ornamentation and so on'? Alaṃ bhutvā gato (having eaten sufficiently, he went) – here alaṃ means 'sufficient'. Sakkatvā gato (having honored, he went) – the meaning is 'having done well'. The intention is that the unification of meaning applies only to concise forms like kacca, kiriya, and so forth, which are formed together with a prefix, and not to expanded forms like katvā, and so forth, which are formed separately.

413. Aññe ca ka. 324, 327; rū. 339, 351; nī. 682-688, caṃ. 2.2.30, 33, 34, 37, 44; pā 1.4.67, 71, 72, 75, 76; 3.4.63.

413. And others.

Aññe ca saddā kriyatthehi syādyantehi saha bahulaṃ ekatthā honti.

And other words often have a single meaning together with words that denote action and end in a case suffix.

Atirekaṃ abhavīti parobhuyya. Evaṃ tirobhuyya, parokiriya, tirokiriya, urasikiriya, manasikiriya, majjhekiriya, tuṇhībhuyya.

Atirekaṃ abhavi (it became excessive) is parobhuyya (surpassing). Similarly, tirobhuyya (disappearing); parokiriya (acting indirectly); tirokiriya (acting secretly); urasikiriya (taking to heart); manasikiriya (attending to); majjhekiriya (acting neutrally); tuṇhībhuyya (becoming silent).

Tyādisaddāpi saññābhāvaṃ pattā nipātarūpā honti, syādirūpā ca. Tasmā tepi imasmiṃ sutte saṅgayhanti.

Words ending in suffixes like tya and so forth, having attained the state of nouns, can be indeclinable forms or forms with case endings. Therefore, they too are included in this rule.

Atthikhīrā gāvī, nasantiputtā itthī, atthi hutvā paccayo atthipaccayo. Evaṃ natthipaccayo, ahosi eva kammaṃ ahosikammaṃ, ehi ca passa ca ehipassa, ehipassa iti vidhānaṃ arahatīti ehipassiko, ayaṃ taddhitantasamāso nāma. Evaṃ parattha.

A cow with milk is atthikhīrā gāvī; a woman without sons is nasantiputtā itthī; a condition that exists is atthipaccayo. Similarly, natthipaccayo (a condition that does not exist); an action that was is ahosikamma; ehi ca passa ca (come and see) is ehipassa; one who is worthy of the designation 'ehipassa' is ehipassiko – this is called a taddhitanta compound. Similarly elsewhere.

Ehi [M 0.0281] bhaddanteti vuttopi na etīti naehibhaddantiko dī. ni. 1.394, tiṭṭha bhaddanteti vuttopi na tiṭṭhatīti natiṭṭhabhaddantiko, ehi svāgataṃ tuyhanti vadanasīlo ehisvāgatiko, ehisvāgatavādī pārā. 432 vā, ehi bhikkhūti vacanena siddhā upasampadā ehibhikkhūpasampadā, evaṃ porāṇā āhaṃsu vā, evaṃ pure āsiṃsu vāti evaṃ pavattaṃ vidhānaṃ ettha atthīti itihāso dī. ni. 1.256, purāṇagantho, yaṃ pubbe anaññātaṃ, taṃ idāni ñassāmi iti pavattassa indriyaṃ anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ, asuko iti āha asuko iti āha, asukasmiṃvā ganthe iti āha asukasmiṃ ganthe iti āhāti evaṃ pavattavacanaṃ itihitihaṃ, aññāsi iti byākato koṇḍañño aññāsikoṇḍañño mahāva. 8 iccādi.

One who does not come even when told 'Ehi, bhaddante' (Come, Venerable Sir) is a naehibhaddantika; one who does not stay even when told 'Tiṭṭha, bhaddante' (Stay, Venerable Sir) is a natiṭṭhabhaddantika; one whose habit is to say 'Ehi, svāgataṃ tuyhaṃ' (Come, welcome to you) is an ehisvāgatika or ehisvāgatavādī; the higher ordination (upasampadā) conferred by the words 'Ehi, bhikkhu' (Come, monk) is ehibhikkhūpasampadā. Itihāsa (history, ancient text) is that wherein there is a tradition proceeding as: 'Thus the ancients said' or 'Thus it was in the past'. The faculty of one who proceeds with the thought, 'What was previously unknown, that I shall now know' is the anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ (the faculty of I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown). Itihitihaṃ (hearsay) is a way of speaking that proceeds thus: 'So-and-so said this, so-and-so said that,' or 'In such-and-such a text it says this, in such-and-such a text it says that.' Koṇḍañña, who was declared 'Aññāsi' (He understood), is Aññāsikoṇḍañño, and so forth.

Keci pana “sacchikaroti, manasikaroti, pākaṭīkaroti, āvīkaroti, pātukaroti, alaṅkaroti, sakkaroti, pabhavati, parābhavati” iccādīnampi ekatthībhāvaṃ vadanti. Tumantatvantādikāpi ettha saṅgayhanti, gantuṃ kāmetīti gantukāmo, kattukāmo, daṭṭhukāmo, gantuṃ mano etassāti gantumano, saṃvidhāya avahāro saṃvidhāvahāro, yalopo. Evaṃ upādāya uppannaṃ rūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ, anupādāya vimutto anupādāvimutto, paṭiccasamuppādo, āhaccabhāsito, upahaccaparinibbāyī pu. pa. 37, aveccappasādo, chakkhattuparamaṃ, sattakkhattuparamo pu. pa. 31 iccādi.

Some, however, say that words like sacchikaroti (to realize), manasikaroti (to attend), pākaṭīkaroti (to make manifest), āvīkaroti (to make evident), pātukaroti (to make manifest), alaṅkaroti (to adorn), sakkaroti (to honor), pabhavati (to originate), parābhavati (to decline), and so forth, also have a single meaning. Forms ending in tuṃ, tvā, and so forth are also included here: gantuṃ kāmeti (he desires to go) is gantukāmo (one who desires to go); kattukāmo (one who desires to do); daṭṭhukāmo (one who desires to see); gantuṃ mano etassa (his mind is set on going) is gantumano (one whose mind is set on going); saṃvidhāya avahāro (conduct by arrangement) is saṃvidhāvahāro, with elision of ya. Similarly, upādāya uppannaṃ rūpaṃ (material form arisen from clinging) is upādārūpaṃ; anupādāya vimutto (liberated without clinging) is anupādāvimutto; paṭiccasamuppādo (dependent origination); āhaccabhāsito (spoken impetuously); upahaccaparinibbāyī (one who attains final Nibbāna after encountering something); aveccappasādo (unshakable confidence); chakkhattuparamaṃ (at most six times); sattakkhattuparamo (at most seven times), and so forth.

Abyayarāsi niṭṭhito.

The Section on Indeclinables is concluded.

Saṅkhyārāsi

The Section on Numerals.

Idāni [M 0.0282] saṅkhyārāsi vuccate.

Now the numerical system is explained.

414. Vidhādīsu dvissa du ka. 386; rū. 410; nī. 811.

414. Before vidhā, etc., du is substituted for dvi.

Vidhādīsu paresu dvissa du hoti.

When words such as vidhā follow, du is substituted for dvi.

Dve vidhā pakārā yassāti duvidho, dve paṭṭāni yassāti dupaṭṭaṃ, cīvaraṃ, duvaṅgikaṃ, jhānaṃ iccādi.

That which has two kinds is duvidha (twofold); that which has two cloths is dupaṭṭaṃ (double-layered), a robe; duvaṅgikaṃ (two-factored) jhāna, and so on.

415. Di guṇādīsu ka. 386; rū. 410; nī. 811.

415. Before guṇa, etc., di is substituted [for dvi].

Guṇādīsu dvissa di hoti.

When words such as guṇa follow, di is substituted for dvi.

Dve guṇā paṭalā yassāti diguṇā, saṅghāṭi, dve gāvo digu, dve rattiyo dirattaṃ, dvirattaṃ vā.

That which has two folds or layers is diguṇā, the saṅghāṭi; two cows are digu; two nights are dirattaṃ or dvirattaṃ.

416. Tīsva ka. 383; rū. 253; nī. 815.

416. Before ti, a is substituted [for dvi].

Tīsu paresu dvissa a hoti.

When ti (three) follows, a is substituted for dvi (two).

Dve vā tayo vā vārā dvattikkhattuṃ, dve vā tayo vā pattā dvattipattā.

Two or three times is dvattikkhattuṃ; two or three bowls are dvattipattā.

417. Ā saṅkhyāyāsatādonaññatthe ka. 383; rū. 253; nī. 815; caṃ. 5.2.52; pā. 6.3.47.

417. When a numeral other than sata, etc., follows, and not in the sense of another word, ā is substituted [for dvi].

Aññapadatthavajjite samāse satādito aññasmiṃ saṅkhyāpade pare dvissa ā hoti.

In a compound excluding the sense of another word, when a numeral other than sata, etc., follows, ā is substituted for dvi.

Dve ca dasa ca dvādasa, dvīhi vā adhikā dasa dvādasa, dvāvīsati, dvattiṃsa, rassattaṃ.

Two and ten are dvādasa (twelve), or ten increased by two is dvādasa; dvāvīsati (twenty-two), dvattiṃsa (thirty-two). Shortening occurs.

Asatādoti kiṃ? Dvisataṃ, dvisahassaṃ.

Why 'not sata, etc.'? Dvisataṃ (two hundred), dvisahassaṃ (two thousand).

Anaññattheti kiṃ? Dve dasa yasminti dvidasa.

Why 'not in the sense of another word'? Dvidasa (that which has two tens).

418. Tisse ka. 404; rū. 370; caṃ. 5.2.53; pā. 6.3.48.

418. For ti, e is substituted.

Anaññatthe [M 0.0283] asatādo saṅkhyāpade pare tissa e hoti.

When not in the sense of another word, and when a numeral not beginning with sata, etc., follows, e is substituted for ti (three).

Tayo ca dasa ca terasa, tīhi vā adhikā dasa terasa. Evaṃ tevīsati, tettiṃsa.

Three and ten are terasa (thirteen), or ten increased by three is terasa. Similarly, tevīsati (twenty-three), tettiṃsa (thirty-three).

419. Cattālīsādo vā ka. 404; rū. 370; caṃ. 5.2.54; pā. 6.3.49.

419. Optionally, before cattālīsa, etc.

Cattālīsādīsu paresu tissa e hoti vā.

When cattālīsa, etc., follow, e is optionally substituted for ti (three).

Tecattālīsaṃ, ticattālīsaṃ, tepaññāsaṃ, tipaññāsaṃ, tesaṭṭhi, tisaṭṭhi, tesattati, tisattati, teasīti, tiasīti, tenavuti, tinavuti.

Tecattālīsaṃ, ticattālīsaṃ (forty-three); tepaññāsaṃ, tipaññāsaṃ (fifty-three); tesaṭṭhi, tisaṭṭhi (sixty-three); tesattati, tisattati (seventy-three); teasīti, tiasīti (eighty-three); tenavuti, tinavuti (ninety-three).

420. Dvissā ca ka. 404; rū. 370 caṃ. 5.2.54; pā. 6.3.69.

420. And for dvi, also ā.

Cattālīsādo dvissa e hoti vā ā ca.

Before cattālīsa, etc., e and ā are optionally substituted for dvi.

Dvecattālīsaṃ, dvācattālīsaṃ, dvicattālīsaṃ, dvepaññāsaṃ, dvipaññāsaṃ, dvāsaṭṭhi, dvesaṭṭhi, dvāsattati, dvesattati, dvāsīti, dvānavuti, dvenavuti. Vāsaddena paññāsamhi āttaṃ, asītimhi ettañca natthi.

Dvecattālīsaṃ, dvācattālīsaṃ, dvicattālīsaṃ (forty-two); dvepaññāsaṃ, dvipaññāsaṃ (fifty-two); dvāsaṭṭhi, dvesaṭṭhi (sixty-two); dvāsattati, dvesattati (seventy-two); dvāsīti (eighty-two); dvānavuti, dvenavuti (ninety-two). By the word vā (optionally), in the case of paññāsa, the substitution to ā does not occur, and in the case of asīti, the substitution to e also does not occur.

421. Bācattālīsādo vā ka. 380; rū. 255; nī. 810.

421. Optionally, bā is substituted before numerals not beginning with cattālīsa.

Acattālīsādo pare dvissa bā hoti vā.

When a numeral not beginning with cattālīsa follows, bā is optionally substituted for dvi.

Bārasa, dvādasa, bāvīsati, dvāvīsati, bāttiṃsa, dvattiṃsa.

Bārasa, dvādasa (twelve); bāvīsati, dvāvīsati (twenty-two); bāttiṃsa, dvattiṃsa (thirty-two).

Acattālīsādoti kiṃ? Dvācattālīsaṃ.

Why 'not beginning with cattālīsa'? Dvācattālīsaṃ (forty-two).

422. Catussa cuco dase ka. 390; rū. 256; nī. 826.

422. For catu, cu and co are substituted before dasa.

Dase [M 0.0284] pare catussa cu, co honti vā.

When dasa (ten) follows, cu and co are optionally substituted for catu (four).

Cuddasa, coddasa, catuddasa.

Cuddasa (fourteen), coddasa (fourteen), catuddasa (fourteen).

423. Vīsatidasesu pañcassa paṇṇapannā ka. 404; rū. 370; nī. 814.

423. When 'vīsati' (twenty) and 'dasa' (ten) follow, for 'pañca' (five), [the substitutes are] 'paṇṇa' and 'pannā'.

Esu pañcassa paṇṇa, pannā honti vā yathākkamaṃ.

In these [cases], for 'pañca' (five), 'paṇṇa' and 'pannā' are optionally substituted, respectively.

Paṇṇavīsati, pañcavīsati, pannarasa, pañcadasa.

Paṇṇavīsati (twenty-five), pañcavīsati (twenty-five); pannarasa (fifteen), pañcadasa (fifteen).

424. Chassa so ka. 374; rū. 408; nī. 806.

424. For 'cha' (six), 'so' [is substituted].

Dase pare chassa so hoti.

When 'dasa' (ten) follows, 'so' is substituted for 'cha' (six).

Soḷasa.

Soḷasa (sixteen).

425. Ekaṭṭhānamā ka. 383; rū. 253; nī. 815.

425. For 'eka' (one) and 'aṭṭha' (eight), 'ā' [is substituted].

Dase pare eka, aṭṭhānaṃ ā hoti.

When 'dasa' (ten) follows, 'ā' is substituted for 'eka' (one) and 'aṭṭha' (eight).

Ekādasa, aṭṭhārasa.

Ekādasa (eleven), aṭṭhārasa (eighteen).

426. Ra saṅkhyāto vā ka. 381; rū. 254; nī. 812.

426. After a numeral, 'ra' [is substituted for 'dasa'], optionally.

Ekādisaṅkhyamhā parassa dasassa ra hoti vā.

For 'dasa' (ten) following a numeral beginning with 'eka' (one), etc., 'ra' is optionally substituted.

Ekārasa, ekādasa, bārasa, dvādasa, pannarasa, pañcadasa, sattarasa, sattadasa, aṭṭhārasa, aṭṭhādasa, bādese pannādese ca niccaṃ. Idha na hoti, catuddasa.

Ekārasa (eleven), ekādasa (eleven); bārasa (twelve), dvādasa (twelve); pannarasa (fifteen), pañcadasa (fifteen); sattarasa (seventeen), sattadasa (seventeen); aṭṭhārasa (eighteen), aṭṭhādasa (eighteen). And it is always [substituted] in the case of the substitutions 'bā' and 'pannā'. Here it does not occur: 'catuddasa' (fourteen).

427. Chatīhi ḷo ca ka. 379; rū. 258; nī. 809.

427. After 'cha' (six) and 'ti' (three), also 'ḷo'.

Cha, tīhi parassa dassa ḷo hoti ro ca.

For 'dasa' (ten) following 'cha' (six) and 'ti' (three), 'ḷo' occurs, and also 'ro'.

Soḷasa, terasa, teḷasa.

Soḷasa (sixteen), terasa (thirteen), teḷasa (thirteen).

428. Catutthatatiyānamaḍḍhuḍḍhatiyā ka. 387; rū. 411; nī. 819.

428. For 'catuttha' (fourth) and 'tatiya' (third), [the forms are] 'aḍḍhuḍḍha' and 'aḍḍhatiya'.

‘Aḍḍhuḍḍhatiyā’ti [M 0.0285] aḍḍhā+uḍḍhatiyāti chedo, aḍḍhamhā paresaṃ catuttha, tatiyānaṃ uḍḍha, tiyā honti yathākkamaṃ.

'Aḍḍhuḍḍhatiyā' is analyzed as 'aḍḍhā + uḍḍhatiyā'. For 'catuttha' (fourth) and 'tatiya' (third) following 'aḍḍha' (half), 'uḍḍha' and 'tiyā' are substituted, respectively.

Aḍḍhena catuttho aḍḍhuḍḍho, aḍḍhena tatiyo aḍḍhatiyo.

The fourth with a half is 'aḍḍhuḍḍho'; the third with a half is 'aḍḍhatiyo'.

Sakatthe ṇyamhi aḍḍhateyyo.

In its own sense, when the suffix 'ṇya' is applied, [it becomes] 'aḍḍhateyyo'.

429. Dutiyassa saha diyaḍḍhadivaḍḍhā ka. 387; rū. 411; nī. 819.

429. For 'dutiya' (second), together [with 'aḍḍha'], [the forms are] 'diyaḍḍha' and 'divaḍḍha'.

Aḍḍhamhā parassa dutiyassa saha aḍḍhena diyaḍḍha, divaḍḍhā honti.

For 'dutiya' (second) following 'aḍḍha' (half), together with that 'aḍḍha', 'diyaḍḍha' and 'divaḍḍha' are formed.

Aḍḍhena dutiyo diyaḍḍho, divaḍḍho.

The second with a half is 'diyaḍḍho' or 'divaḍḍho'.

Yathā ca eka, dvi,ti, catu, pañca, cha, satta, aṭṭha, nava, dasasaddā paccekaṃ attano atthesu nipatanti, tathā vīsati, tiṃsati, cattālīsa, paññāsa, saṭṭhi, sattati, asīti, navutisaddā paccekaṃ attano atthesu nipatanti, dasasaddassa kāriyā na honti, evaṃ satasahassasaddāpīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Just as the words 'eka' (one), 'dvi' (two), 'ti' (three), 'catu' (four), 'pañca' (five), 'cha' (six), 'satta' (seven), 'aṭṭha' (eight), 'nava' (nine), and 'dasa' (ten) each apply to their own meanings individually, so too do the words 'vīsati' (twenty), 'tiṃsati' (thirty), 'cattālīsa' (forty), 'paññāsa' (fifty), 'saṭṭhi' (sixty), 'sattati' (seventy), 'asīti' (eighty), and 'navuti' (ninety) each apply to their own meanings individually; they do not undergo the operations of the word 'dasa' (ten). In the same way, the words 'sata' (hundred) and 'sahassa' (thousand) should also be understood.

Tato paraṃ pana dasa sahassāni dasasahassaṃ, idaṃ ‘nahuta’nti ca vuccati, sataṃ sahassāni satasahassaṃ, idaṃ ‘lakkha’nti ca vuccati, dasa satasahassāni dasasatasahassanti evaṃ digusamāsavasena etāni padāni sijjhanti.

Beyond that, however, ten thousands are 'dasasahassaṃ' (ten thousand), which is also called a 'nahuta'; a hundred thousands are 'satasahassaṃ' (a hundred thousand), which is also called a 'lakkha'; ten hundred-thousands are 'dasasatasahassaṃ' (a million). In this way, these terms are formed by way of Dvigu compounds.

Dve satāni dvisataṃ, tīṇi satāni tisataṃ, dve sahassāni dvisahassaṃ, tīṇi sahassāni tisahassaṃ iccādīni digumhi vuttāneva.

Two hundreds are 'dvisataṃ' (two hundred), three hundreds are 'tisataṃ' (three hundred); two thousands are 'dvisahassaṃ' (two thousand), three thousands are 'tisahassaṃ' (three thousand), and so on—these are just as stated in the Dvigu [section].

Gaṇanapathe pana ekaṭṭhānaṃ, dasaṭṭhānaṃ, sataṭṭhānaṃ, sahassaṭṭhānaṃ, dasasahassaṭṭhānaṃ, satasahassaṭṭhānaṃ, dasasatasahassaṭṭhānanti [M 0.0286] imāni satta ṭhānāni kamena dasaguṇitāni honti. Tattha ekaṭṭhānaṃ nāma ekaṃ, dve, tīṇi iccādi. Dasaṭṭhānaṃ nāma dasa, vīsaṃ, tiṃsaṃ iccādi. Sataṭṭhānaṃ nāma sataṃ, dvisataṃ, tisataṃ iccādi. Sahassaṭṭhānaṃ nāma sahassaṃ, dvisahassaṃ, tisahassaṃ iccādi. Evaṃ uparipi. Ekamekasmiñca ṭhāne nava padāni ca nava antaranavantāni ca honti. Ayaṃ mūlabhūmi nāma.

However, in the system of counting, there are these seven places: the 'ekaṭṭhāna' (ones place), 'dasaṭṭhāna' (tens place), 'sataṭṭhāna' (hundreds place), 'sahassaṭṭhāna' (thousands place), 'dasasahassaṭṭhāna' (ten-thousands place), 'satasahassaṭṭhāna' (hundred-thousands place), and 'dasasatasahassaṭṭhāna' (millions place). These seven places are successively multiplied by ten. Therein, the 'ekaṭṭhāna' refers to one, two, three, and so on. The 'dasaṭṭhāna' refers to ten, twenty, thirty, and so on. The 'sataṭṭhāna' refers to a hundred, two hundred, three hundred, and so on. The 'sahassaṭṭhāna' refers to a thousand, two thousand, three thousand, and so on. Thus also for the higher places. And in each single place, there are nine terms and nine intermediate numbers. This is called the 'mūlabhūmi' (root level).

Taduttari koṭibhūmi nāma. Tatthapi ekaṭṭhānaṃ, dasaṭṭhānaṃ, sataṭṭhānaṃiccādīni satta ṭhānāni honti. Tattha mūlabhūmiyā antimaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā dasaguṇite kate koṭibhūmiyaṃ ekaṭṭhānaṃ hoti, idhapi satta ṭhānāni kamena dasaguṇitāniyeva, idha dasakoṭisatasahassaṃ antimaṭṭhānaṃ bhavati.

Higher than that is what is called the 'koṭibhūmi' (koṭi level). There also, there are seven places: the ones place, the tens place, the hundreds place, and so on. When the last place of the 'mūlabhūmi' is taken and multiplied by ten, it becomes the ones place in the 'koṭibhūmi'. Here too, the seven places are successively multiplied by ten; here, 'dasakoṭisatasahassaṃ' becomes the last place.

Taduttari pakoṭibhūmi nāma. Etthapi satta ṭhānāni honti. Tattha koṭibhūmiyā antimaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā dasaguṇite kate pakoṭibhūmiyaṃ ekaṭṭhānaṃ hoti, idhapi satta ṭhānāni dasaguṇitāniyeva, dasapakoṭisatasahassaṃ antimaṭṭhānaṃ, iminā nayena sabbabhūmīsu uparūpari bhūmisaṅkanti ca ṭhānabhedo ca veditabbo.

Higher than that is what is called the 'pakoṭibhūmi' (pakoṭi level). Here too, there are seven places. When the last place of the 'koṭibhūmi' is taken and multiplied by ten, it becomes the ones place in the 'pakoṭibhūmi'. Here too, the seven places are multiplied by ten, with 'dasapakoṭisatasahassaṃ' being the last place. By this method, the progression from level to higher level and the distinction of places should be understood in all the levels.

Ayaṃ panettha bhūmikkamo-mūlabhūmi, koṭibhūmi, pakoṭibhūmi, koṭipakoṭibhūmi, nahutabhūmi, ninnahutabhūmi, akkhobhiṇībhūmi bhinī, bhanītipi dissanti, bindubhūmi, abbudabhūmi, nirabbudabhūmi, ahahabhūmi, abababhūmi, aṭaṭabhūmi, sogandhikabhūmi, uppalabhūmi, kumudabhūmi, puṇḍarīkabhūmi, padumabhūmi, kathānabhūmi, mahākathānabhūmi, asaṅkhyeyyabhūmīti ekavīsati bhūmiyo sattacattālīsasataṃ ṭhānāni ca honti.

Herein, the sequence of levels is as follows: 'mūlabhūmi' (root level), 'koṭibhūmi' (koṭi level), 'pakoṭibhūmi' (pakoṭi level), 'koṭipakoṭibhūmi' (koṭipakoṭi level), 'nahutabhūmi' (nahuta level), 'ninnahutabhūmi' (ninnahuta level), 'akkhobhiṇībhūmi' (akkhobhiṇī level), 'bindubhūmi' (bindu level), 'abbudabhūmi' (abbuda level), 'nirabbudabhūmi' (nirabbuda level), 'ahahabhūmi' (ahaha level), 'abababhūmi' (ababa level), 'aṭaṭabhūmi' (aṭaṭa level), 'sogandhikabhūmi' (sogandhika level), 'uppalabhūmi' (uppala level), 'kumudabhūmi' (kumuda level), 'puṇḍarīkabhūmi' (puṇḍarīka level), 'padumabhūmi' (paduma level), 'kathānabhūmi' (kathāna level), 'mahākathānabhūmi' (mahākathāna level), and 'asaṅkhyeyyabhūmi' (incalculable level)—these twenty-one levels are one hundred and forty-seven places.

Nirayabhūmīnaṃ kamena pana abbudabhūmi, nirabbudabhūmi, abababhūmi, aṭaṭabhūmi, ahahabhūmi, kumudabhūmi, sogandhikabhūmi, uppalabhūmi[M 0.0287], puṇḍarīkabhūmi, padumabhūmīti vattabbo. Ettha ca yasmā pāḷibhāsāyaṃ dasasatasahassaṃ nāma sattamaṭṭhānaṃ natthi, cha ṭhānāni eva atthi, tasmā garū aṭṭhakathāsu saṃ. ni. 1.181 āgatanayena sattamaṭṭhānaṃ ullaṅghetvā chaṭṭhaṭṭhānato upari bhūmisaṅkantiṃ kathentā sataguṇitaṃ katvā kathenti, satasahassānaṃ sataṃ koṭi, koṭisatasahassānaṃ sataṃ pakoṭi iccādi.

Then, in order of the hell realms, the list is as follows: the abbudabhūmi, nirabbudabhūmi, abababhūmi, aṭaṭabhūmi, ahahabhūmi, kumudabhūmi, sogandhikabhūmi, uppalabhūmi, puṇḍarīkabhūmi, and padumabhūmi. Here, because in the Pāli language there is no seventh place-value named 'dasasatasahassa' (ten hundred-thousands), and only six place-values exist, therefore the teachers, following the method that has come down in the commentaries, skipping the seventh place-value, speak of the progression of levels above the sixth place-value by making it a hundredfold. Thus, a hundred hundred-thousands is a koṭi; a hundred hundred-thousand koṭis is a pakoṭi, and so on.

Tattha satasahassānaṃ sataṃ nāma dasasatasahassānaṃ dasakameva hoti, tasmā tathā kathentāpi bhūmīnaṃ sabbaṭṭhānānañca dasaguṇasiddhimeva kathentīti veditabbaṃ. Yasmā ca gaṇanabhūmisaṅkhāto gaṇanapatho nāma nānādesavāsīnaṃ vasena nānāvidho hoti, tasmā dīpavaṃse akkhobhiṇī, bindu, kathāna, mahākathānāni vajjetvā pāḷinayena sattarasa bhūmiyova vuttā. Kaccāyane ka. 394, 395; rū. 416, 417 pubbe dassitā ekavīsati bhūmiyo, sakkataganthesu tato sādhikabhūmiyo, katthaci pana mahābalakkhandhapariyantā saṭṭhi bhūmiyoti āgatā.

Therein, a hundred hundred-thousands is just ten ten-hundred-thousands. Therefore, even when speaking in that way, it should be understood that they are speaking only of the tenfold progression of all positions of the levels. And because the path of calculation, known as the enumeration of levels, is of various kinds according to the inhabitants of different countries, in the Dīpavaṃsa, excluding akkhobhiṇī, bindu, kathāna, and mahākathāna, only seventeen levels are mentioned according to the Pāli method. Previously, in Kaccāyana, twenty-one levels were shown, while in Sanskrit texts, more levels than that are mentioned. In some places, however, as many as sixty levels are given, ending with mahābalakkhandha.

Tattha sakasakabhūmito atirekavatthūni gaṇanapathavītivattāni nāma honti, yesaṃ pana mūlabhūmimattaṃ atthi, tesaṃ koṭimattānipi vatthūni gaṇanapathātikkantāni eva.

Therein, objects that exceed their respective levels are called 'transcending the path of calculation'. However, for objects that are only of the measure of the root level, even if they are of the measure of a koṭi, they still transcend the path of calculation.

Api ca ‘gaṇanapathavītivatta’nti ca ‘gaṇanapathātikkanta’nti ca ‘asaṅkhyeyya’nti ca atthato ekaṃ. Tasmā idhapi vīsati bhūmiyo eva anukkamena dasaguṇitā gaṇanapathā nāma honti. Asaṅkhyeyyanti pana dasaguṇavinimuttā gaṇanapathātikkantabhūmi eva vuccati. Mahākathānabhūmātikkantato paṭṭhāya hi anantamahāpathaviyā sabbapaṃsucuṇṇānipi idha asaṅkhyeyyabhūmiyaṃ saṅgayhanti. Itarathā asaṅkhyeyyanti ca gaṇanapathabhūmīti ca viruddhametanti.

Moreover, the terms 'gaṇanapathavītivatta', 'gaṇanapathātikkanta', and 'asaṅkhyeyya' are, in meaning, one and the same. Therefore, here also, only twenty levels, each sequentially tenfold, are called the paths of counting. However, 'asaṅkhyeyya' refers specifically to the level that transcends the counting path, free from tenfold multiplication. For starting from the level beyond the mahākathānabhūmi, even all the dust particles of an infinite great earth are included in this asaṅkhyeyya level. Otherwise, 'asaṅkhyeyya' and 'counting path level' would be contradictory.

Dīpavaṃse [M 0.0288] ca “tato upari abhūmi, asaṅkhyeyyanti vuccatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha ‘abhūmī’ti vacanena gaṇanapathabhūmi eva paṭisiddhā, na tu gaṇanapathātikkantā visuṃ asaṅkhyeyyabhūmi nāma. Cariyāpiṭakasaṃvaṇṇanāyampi cariyā. aṭṭha. nidānakathā ayamattho vutto. Asaṅkhyeyyabhūmiyampi asaṅkhyeyyānaṃ cūḷa, mahādivasena anekappabhedo dakkhiṇavibhaṅgasuttena ma. ni. 3.370 dīpetabbo.

And in the Dīpavaṃsa, it is said: 'Beyond that, there is an abhūmi, which is called asaṅkhyeyya.' Here, by the word 'abhūmi', only the level of the path of calculation is negated, not a distinct asaṅkhyeyya-level that transcends the path of calculation. This meaning is also stated in the commentary on the Cariyāpiṭaka. Even within the asaṅkhyeyya-level, its many distinctions, such as minor and major, should be elucidated by the Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅga Sutta.

Saddanītiyaṃ nī. 833 pana pāḷinayaṃ gahetvā “vīsati abbudāni ekaṃ nirabbudaṃ nāma. Vīsati nirabbudāni ekaṃ ababaṃ nāma” iccādinā nirabbudādīnaṃ saṅkhyānampi vīsatimattaguṇaṃ nāma vuttaṃ. Taṃ na yujjati. Nirayesu hi vīsatimattaguṇena abbuda, nirabbudādīnaṃ dasannaṃ nirayānaṃ tāni nāmāni siddhāni bhavanti. Garū pana tāni nāmāni gahetvā dasaguṇasiddhesu gaṇanapathesu pakkhipiṃsu, tasmā nāmamattena sadisāni bhavanti, guṇavidhi pana visadisoeva.

In the Saddanīti, however, following the Pāli method, it is said: 'Twenty abbudas make one nirabbuda. Twenty nirabbudas make one ababa,' and so on; the numbers of nirabbuda and others are also said to be twentyfold. That is not correct. For in the hells, the names of the ten hells, abbuda, nirabbuda, and so on, are established by a twentyfold progression. But the teachers, taking those names, placed them in the counting systems which are established as tenfold. Therefore, they are similar only in name, but the method of multiplication is entirely different.

Evañcakatvā pāḷiyampi bakabrahmāsutte saṃ. ni. 1.175 “sataṃ sahassānaṃ nirabbudānaṃ, āyuṃ pajānāmi tavāhaṃ brahme”ti vuttaṃ. Ettha ca yadi gaṇanabhūmipathepi nirabbudānaṃ vīsatimattena abababhūmi bhaveyya, evaṃ sati nirabbudānaṃ satasahassaṃ nāma na vucceyya. Jātakaṭṭhakathāyañca jā. aṭṭha. 3.7.69 “nirabbudasatasahassānaṃ ekaṃ ahahaṃ nāma, ettakaṃ bakassa brahmuno tasmiṃbhave avasiṭṭhaṃ āyū”ti vuttaṃ. Tasmā imaṃ gaṇanabhūmipathaṃ patvā vīsatiguṇaṃ nāma natthīti siddhaṃ hoti. Akkhobhiṇī, bindu, kathāna, mahākathānānipi aññato gahetvā pakkhittāni siyuṃ. Evaṃ pakkhittānañca cuddasannaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ kaccāyane kamokkamatā pana pacchājātā siyāti.

Thus, in the Pāli text of the Bakabrahma Sutta, it is said: 'I know your lifespan, O Brahma, to be a hundred thousand nirabbudas.' Here, if in the path of numerical levels an ababa-level were formed by a twentyfold measure of nirabbudas, then 'a hundred thousand nirabbudas' could not be stated. And in the Jātaka commentary, it is stated: 'A hundred thousand nirabbudas is one ahaha; such was the remaining lifespan of Baka Brahmā in that existence.' Therefore, with regard to this path of numerical levels, it is established that there is no twentyfold multiplication. The terms Akkhobhiṇī, Bindu, Kathāna, and Mahākathāna may also have been taken from elsewhere and inserted. And the sequential order in Kaccāyana of the fourteen numbers thus inserted may have arisen later.

Iti niruttidīpaniyā nāma moggallānabyākaraṇadīpaniyā

Thus ends the Niruttidīpanī, which is also called the Moggallānavyākaraṇadīpanī.

Samāsakaṇḍo catuttho.

The fourth chapter: Compounds.

5. Taddhita

5. Derivatives

Atha [M 0.0289] taddhitavidhānaṃ dīpiyate.

Now, the exposition of taddhita formations is presented.

Taddhitavutti nāma vicitrā hoti, sātisayena vicitrañāṇahitaṃ vahati, tasmā tesaṃ tesaṃ kulaputtānaṃ hitanti taddhitaṃ, imasmiṃ kaṇḍe sabbavidhānassa nāmaṃ. Taṃ pana aṭṭhavidhaṃ hoti apaccaṃ, anekatthaṃ, assatthi, bhāvakammaṃ, parimāṇaṃ, saṅkhyā, khuddakaṃ, nānāttanti.

The exposition of taddhita is indeed varied; it carries the benefit of manifold knowledge in abundance. Therefore, it is called 'taddhita' as it is beneficial to those various noble sons. In this chapter, it is the name for all the rules. It is, however, of eight kinds: apacca, anekattha, assatthi, bhāvakamma, parimāṇa, saṅkhyā, khuddaka, and nānātta.

Apaccarāsi

Section on Descendants

430. Ṇo vāpacce ka. 344; rū. 361; nī. 752; caṃ. 2.4.16; pā. 4.1.92; ‘sarānamādissā…’ (bahūsu).

430. The suffix ṇa is added optionally in the sense of offspring.

Chaṭṭhyantā nāmamhā tassa apaccanti atthe vikappena ṇapaccayo hoti. Vāsaddo vākya, samāsānaṃ vikappanattho, ito paraṃ anuvattate, tena sabbattha vikappavidhi sijjhati. Ṇānubandho vuddhyattho, so payogaappayogī. Vasiṭṭhassa apaccanti atthe iminā suttena vasiṭṭhamhā ṇapaccayo, so sāmyatthañca apaccatthañca ubhayaṃ vadati, chaṭṭhī ca apaccapadañca tena vuttatthā nāma honti, vasiṭṭhapadaṃ paccayena saha ekatthaṃ hoti, ubhayaṃ ekato hutvā puttassa nāmaṃ hotīti attho. Tato ‘ekatthatāya’nti chaṭṭhiyā lopo, apaccapadaṃ pana vuttatthamattena luppati. Tañhi sutte padhānabhāvena niddiṭṭhaṃ hoti, na chaṭṭhīti, mahāvuttinā vā padānaṃ lopo. Evaṃ sabbattha.

From a noun ending in the sixth case, the suffix ṇa is optionally added in the sense of 'his offspring'. The word 'vā' (optionally) indicates choice in sentences and compounds, and it continues to apply from here onwards, thereby establishing optional application everywhere. The indicatory letter ṇa is for the purpose of lengthening (vuddhi), and it is not used in the actual formation. In the sense of 'descendant of Vasiṭṭha', by this rule, the suffix ṇa is added to Vasiṭṭha. It expresses both the sense of possession and the sense of offspring. The sixth case ending and the word 'apacca' are said to have their meaning already stated by it. The word Vasiṭṭha, together with the suffix, forms a single meaning, and both together become the son's name—this is the meaning. Therefore, the sixth case ending is elided due to the 'single meaning', but the word 'apacca' is elided simply because its meaning has been stated. For it is designated as the main element in the rule, not the sixth case ending. Alternatively, words are elided according to the Mahāvutti. Thus it is in all cases.

431. Padānamādissāyuvaṇṇassāeo ṇānubandhe ka. 405; rū. 365; nī. 860.

431. The initial a, i, and u vowels of words become ā, e, and o respectively, when a suffix with ṇa as an indicatory letter follows.

Padānaṃ ādibhūtassa akārassa ca ivaṇṇu’vaṇṇassa ca ā, e, o vuddhiyo honti ṇānubandhe paccaye pareti padādia-kārassa āvuddhi, syādyuppatti.

Of the initial a-sound of words, and of the vowels i and u, there are the vuddhi-strengthenings ā, e, and o, respectively, when a suffix with an indicatory ṇa follows. Thus, there is the ā-vuddhi of the initial a-sound of the word, and then the arising of the case endings.

Vāsiṭṭho, [M 0.0290] puriso, vāsiṭṭhī, itthī, vāsiṭṭhaṃ, kulaṃ, vasiṭṭhassa putto vāsiṭṭho, vasiṭṭhassa dhītā vāsiṭṭhī, vasiṭṭhassa kulaṃ vāsiṭṭhanti evampi yojetuṃ yujjati.

Vāsiṭṭho, a man; Vāsiṭṭhī, a woman; Vāsiṭṭhaṃ, a family. The son of Vasiṭṭha is Vāsiṭṭho, the daughter of Vasiṭṭha is Vāsiṭṭhī, the family of Vasiṭṭha is Vāsiṭṭhaṃ—thus also it is fitting to construe them.

Tattha ‘vasiṭṭhassā’ti etena gottasseva pitubhūtaṃ ādipurisaṃ vadati. Kasmā? Gottasaddattā. Evañhi sati tasmiṃ gotte paccājātā sabbepi janā tassa apaccā nāma honti.

Here, by 'Vasiṭṭhassa', the original ancestor of the clan, who is like a father, is indicated. Why? Because it is a clan term. For when that is the case, all people born subsequently in that clan are called his descendants.

432. Majjhe ka. 404; rū. 370; nī. 859.

432. In the middle.

Majjhe pavattānaṃ a, yuvaṇṇānaṃ ā, e, ovuddhiyo honti vā kvaci.

The vowels a, i, and u occurring in the middle of a word optionally become the vuddhi lengthenings ā, e, and o in some cases.

Vāseṭṭho, vāseṭṭhī, vāseṭṭhaṃ. Vāsaddena “vasiṭṭhassa putto dhītā kula”nti vākyaṃ vā “vasiṭṭhaputto vasiṭṭhadhītā vasiṭṭhakula”nti samāsaṃ vā vikappeti. Evaṃ sabbattha.

Vāseṭṭho, Vāseṭṭhī, Vāseṭṭhaṃ. By the word 'vā', it indicates the option of either the phrase 'son of Vasiṭṭha, daughter of Vasiṭṭha, family of Vasiṭṭha' or the compound 'Vasiṭṭha-son, Vasiṭṭha-daughter, Vasiṭṭha-family'. Thus everywhere.

Bharadvājassa apaccaṃ bhāradvājo, visāmittassa bhāradvājassa… vesāmittassa… (rū.) apaccaṃ vesāmitto, gotamassa apaccaṃ gotamo, kassapassa apaccaṃ kassapo, vasudevassa apaccaṃ vāsudevo. Evaṃ bāladevo.

The descendant of Bharadvāja is Bhāradvājo, the descendant of Visāmitta is Vesāmitto, the descendant of Gotama is Gotamo, the descendant of Kassapa is Kassapo, the descendant of Vasudeva is Vāsudevo. Similarly, Bāladevo.

Upagussa apaccanti ettha ‘uvaṇṇassāvaṅa…’ti ṇānubandhe paccaye pare uvaṇṇassa avaṅa hoti. Opagavo, opagavī, opagavaṃ, manuno apaccaṃ mānavo, bhagguno apaccaṃ bhaggavo, paṇḍuno apaccaṃ paṇḍavo, upavindussa apaccaṃ opavindavo iccādi.

Here, in the sense of 'offspring of Upagu', according to the rule 'uvaṇṇassāvaṅa…', when a suffix with ṇa as an indicatory letter follows, the u-vowel becomes 'ava'. Thus: Opagavo, Opagavī, Opagavaṃ. The offspring of Manu is Mānavo; the offspring of Bhaggu is Bhaggavo; the offspring of Paṇḍu is Paṇḍavo; the offspring of Upavindu is Opavindavo, and so on.

433. Vacchādito ṇānaṇāyanā ka. 345; rū. 366; nī. 754; pā. 4.1.93, 94, 162, 163.

433. From Vaccha and so on, the suffixes āna and āyana (with ṇ as an indicatory letter).

Chaṭṭhuntehi [M 0.0291] vacchādīhi gottasaddagaṇehi tassa apaccanti atthe ṇānubandhā āna, āyanapaccayā honti vā.

From the group of clan-terms like Vaccha and so on, ending in the sixth case, the suffixes āna and āyana, with ṇa as an indicatory letter, are optionally added in the sense of 'his offspring'.

Vacchassa apaccaṃ vacchāno, vacchāyano, vacchānī, vacchāyanī, vacchānaṃ, vacchāyanaṃ. Evaṃ kaccāno, kaccāyano, kātiyāno, kātiyāyano, sākaṭāno, sākaṭāyano, kaṇhāno, kaṇhāyano, moggallāno, moggallāyano, aggivessāno aggivessanotipi dissati dī. ni. 1.176; ma. ni. 1.353 ādayo, aggivessāyano, muñcāno, muñcāyano, kuñcāno, kuñcāyano iccādi.

The offspring of Vaccha is Vacchāno, Vacchāyano, Vacchānī, Vacchāyanī, Vacchānaṃ, Vacchāyanaṃ. Similarly, Kaccāno, Kaccāyano, Kātiyāno, Kātiyāyano, Sākaṭāno, Sākaṭāyano, Kaṇhāno, Kaṇhāyano, Moggallāno, Moggallāyano, Aggivessāno, Aggivessāyano, Muñcāno, Muñcāyano, Kuñcāno, Kuñcāyano, and so on.

434. Kattikāvidhavādīhi ṇeyyaṇerā ka. 346; rū. 367; nī. 755; pā. 4.1.120, 123, 126, 127, 128, 129, 131.

434. From Kattikā, Vidhavā, and so on, the suffixes ṇeyya and ṇera.

Chaṭṭhyantehi kattikādīhi vidhavādīhi ca tassa apaccanti atthe kamena ṇānubandhā eyya, erapaccayā honti vā.

From words such as Kattikā and so on, and Vidhavā and so on, ending in the sixth case, the suffixes eyya and era, which have ṇa as an indicatory letter, are optionally added respectively in the sense of 'his offspring'.

Ṇeyye – kattikāya nāma devadhītāya apaccaṃ kattikeyyo, vinatāya nāma deviyā apaccaṃ venateyyo, rohiṇiyā nāma deviyā apaccaṃ rohiṇeyyo, bhaginiyā apaccaṃ bhāgineyyo, nadiyā nāma itthiyā apaccaṃ nādeyyo. Evaṃ anteyyo, āheyyo, kāmeyyo, suciyā apaccaṃ soceyyo, bālāya apaccaṃ bāleyyo iccādi.

Regarding ṇeyya: the offspring of the goddess named Kattikā is Kattikeyyo; the offspring of the goddess named Vinatā is Venateyyo; the offspring of the goddess named Rohiṇī is Rohiṇeyyo; the offspring of a sister is Bhāgineyyo; the offspring of a woman named Nadī is Nādeyyo. Similarly, Anteyyo, Āheyyo, Kāmeyyo; the offspring of Suci is Soceyyo; the offspring of Bālā is Bāleyyo, and so on.

Ṇere – vidhavāya apaccaṃ vedhavero, vidhavā nāma matapatikā itthī. Bandhukiyā apaccaṃ bandhukero, nāḷikiyā nāma itthiyā putto nāḷikero, samaṇassa upajjhāyassa putto sāmaṇero, samaṇiyā pavattiniyā dhītā sāmaṇerī iccādi.

Regarding ṇera: the offspring of a widow is Vedhavero; a widow is a woman whose husband has died. The offspring of Bandhukī is Bandhukero; the son of a woman named Nāḷikī is Nāḷikero; the son of a monk preceptor is Sāmaṇero; the daughter of a nun preceptor is Sāmaṇerī, and so on.

435. Ṇya diccādīhi ka. 347; rū. 368; nī. 756; caṃ. 2.4.2; pā. 4.1.85.

435. From Diti and so on, the suffix ṇya.

Chaṭṭhuntehi [M 0.0292] ditiiccādīhi tassa apaccanti atthe ṇānubandho yapaccayo hoti vā.

From Diti and so on, ending in the sixth case, the suffix ya, with ṇa as an indicatory letter, is optionally added in the sense of 'his offspring'.

436. Lopovaṇṇivaṇṇānaṃ ka. 261; rū. 369; nī. 509.

436. Elision of the a-vowel and i-vowel.

Ye pare avaṇṇassa ivaṇṇassa ca lopo hotīti ṇyamhi pare avaṇṇi’vaṇṇānaṃ lopo.

When 'ya' follows, there is elision of the a-vowel and the i-vowel. Therefore, when the suffix ṇya follows, there is elision of the a-vowel and the i-vowel.

Ditiyā nāma devadhītāya apaccaṃ decco, aditiyā apaccaṃ ādicco.

The offspring of the goddess named Diti is Decco; the offspring of Aditi is Ādicco.

Tattha ivaṇṇalope ‘tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā’ti yamhi pare tavaggassa cavaggattaṃ, puna ‘vaggalasehi te’ti yassa pubbarūpattaṃ, kuṇḍaniyā apaccaṃ koṇḍañño.

Here, with the elision of the i-vowel, by the rule 'tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā', when 'ya' follows, the tavagga becomes cavagga. Again, by the rule 'vaggalasehi te', 'ya' takes the form of the preceding letter. The offspring of Kuṇḍanī is Koṇḍañño.

437. Uvaṇṇassāvaṅa sare ka. 348; rū. 371; nī. 757.

437. The u-vowel becomes 'ava' when a vowel follows.

Sare pare uvaṇṇassa avaṅa hotīti uvaṇṇassa avattaṃ. ‘Tavaggavaraṇāna…’nti suttena vassa battaṃ, puna ‘vaggalasehi te’ti suttena yassa pubbarūpattaṃ, bhātuno apaccaṃ bhātabyo.

When a vowel follows, the u-vowel becomes 'ava'; this is the transformation of the u-vowel into 'ava'. By the rule 'tavaggavaraṇāna…', 'va' becomes 'ba'. Again, by the rule 'vaggalasehi te', 'ya' takes the form of the preceding letter. The offspring of a brother is Bhātabyo.

438. Ā ṇi ka. 347; rū. 368; nī. 756; caṃ. 2.4.19; pā. 4.1.95.

438. The suffix ṇi.

Rassā’kārantato apaccatthe ṇānubandho rassi’paccayo hoti vā.

From a word ending in a short 'a', the suffix 'i', with ṇa as an indicatory letter, is optionally added in the sense of offspring.

Dakkhassa apaccaṃ dakkhi. Evaṃ doṇi, vāsavi, sakyaputti, nāṭaputti, dāsaputti, dāruno apaccaṃ dāravi vicāretabbamidaṃ, varuṇassa apaccaṃ vāruṇi[M 0.0293]. Evaṃ kaṇḍi, bāladevi, pāvaki, jinadattassa apaccaṃ jenadatti, suddhodani, anuruddhi iccādi.

The offspring of Dakkha is Dakkhi. Similarly, Doṇi, Vāsavi, Sakyaputti, Nāṭaputti, Dāsaputti; the offspring of Dāruṇa is Dāravi; the offspring of Varuṇa is Vāruṇi. Similarly, Kaṇḍi, Bāladevi, Pāvaki; the offspring of Jinadatta is Jenadatti; Suddhodani, Anuruddhi, and so on.

439. Rājato ño jātiyaṃ ka. 347; rū. 368; nī. 756; caṃ. 2.4.70; pā. 4.1.137.

439. From rāja, the suffix ña in the sense of lineage.

Jātiyaṃ gamyamānāyaṃ rājasaddamhā apaccatthe ñapaccayo hoti vā.

When lineage is implied, the suffix ña is optionally added to the word 'rāja' in the sense of offspring.

Rañño apaccaṃ rājañño, rājakulassa puttoti attho.

The offspring of a king is a rājañña; the meaning is 'a son of the royal family'.

Jātiyanti kiṃ? Rājaputto.

Why 'in the sense of lineage'? Rājaputto (king's son).

440. Khattā yiyā ka. 347; rū. 368; nī. 756; caṃ. 2.4.69; pā. 4.1.138.

440. From Khatta, the suffixes ya and iya.

Jātiyaṃ gamyamānāyaṃ khattasaddamhā apaccatthe ya, iyapaccayā honti.

When lineage is implied, from the word 'khatta', the suffixes 'ya' and 'iya' are added in the sense of offspring.

Khattakulassa apaccaṃ khatyo, khattiyo.

The offspring of the Khattiya clan is Khatyo, Khattiyo.

Jātiyantveva? Khatti.

Why 'only in the sense of lineage'? Khatti.

441. Manuto ssasaṇa ka. 348; rū. 371; nī. 753; caṃ. 2.4.94, 95; pā. 4.1.161.

441. From Manu, the suffixes ssa and saṇa.

Jātiyaṃ gamyamānāyaṃ manusaddamhā apaccatthe ssa, saṇapaccayā honti.

When lineage is implied, from the word 'manu', the suffixes 'ssa' and 'saṇa' are added in the sense of offspring.

Manuno apaccaṃ manusso, mānuso, manu nāma kappe ādikhattiyo mahāsammatarājā, itthiyaṃ manussī, mānusī,

The offspring of Manu is manusso, mānuso. Manu was the first Khattiya in the eon, the Great Elect King (Mahāsammatarājā). In the feminine, it is manussī, mānusī.

Jātiyantveva? Māṇavo.

In the sense of 'by birth'? A youth.

442. Janapadanāmasmā janakhattiyā raññe ca ṇo ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765; caṃ. 2.4.96; pā. 4.1.168; “janapadanāmasmā khattiyā…” (bahūsu).

442. From the name of a country, from words denoting people and khattiyas, and in the sense of 'king', the suffix 'ṇo' is added.

Janavācinā [M 0.0294] ca khattiyavācinā ca janapadanāmamhā raññe ca apacce ca ṇo hoti.

From words denoting people and khattiyas, from the name of a country, and in the sense of 'king' and 'descendant', the suffix 'ṇo' occurs.

Pañcālānaṃ janānaṃ rājā pañcālo, pañcālassa khattiyassa apaccaṃ pañcālo. Evaṃ kosalo, māgadho, okkāko dī. ni. 1.267.

The king of the Pañcāla people is Pañcālo; the offspring of a Pañcāla khattiya is Pañcālo. Similarly, Kosalo, Māgadho, and Okkāko.

Janapadanāmasmāti kiṃ? Dasaratharañño putto dāsarathi dāsaraṭṭhi.

What is meant by 'from the name of a country'? The son of King Dasaratha is Dāsarathi.

Janakhattiyāti kiṃ? Pañcālassa brāhmaṇassa apaccaṃ pañcāli.

What is meant by 'from words denoting people and khattiyas'? The offspring of a Pañcāla brahmin is Pañcāli.

443. Ṇya kurusivīhi ka. 346; rū. 367; nī. 755; caṃ. 2.4.101 …pe… 4.1.172.

443. The suffix 'ṇya' is added to 'Kuru' and 'Sivi'.

Kuru, sivisaddehi apacce raññe ca ṇyo hoti.

From the words 'Kuru' and 'Sivi', the suffix 'ṇya' occurs in the sense of 'descendant' or 'king'.

Kururañño apaccaṃ korabyo jā. 1.14.228, 232, 236, kururaṭṭhavāsīnaṃ rājā korabyo, korabbo, pubbarūpattaṃ, sivirañño apaccaṃ sebyo, siviraṭṭhavāsīnaṃ rājā sebyo.

The offspring of King Kuru is Korabyo; the king of the inhabitants of the Kuru country is Korabyo, or Korabbo, due to the preceding form. The offspring of King Sivi is Sebyo; the king of the inhabitants of the Sivi country is Sebyo.

Apaccarāsi niṭṭhito.

The section on descendants is concluded.

Anekattharāsi

The Section on Multiple Meanings

444. Ṇa rāgā tena rattaṃ ka. 347; rū. 368; nī. 756; caṃ. 3.1.1 …pe… 4.2.1.

444. The suffix 'ṇa' is added from a word denoting a dye, in the sense of 'dyed by that'.

Rajjanti vatthaṃ etenāti rāgo, rajanavatthu, rāgavācimhā tena rattanti atthe ṇo hoti.

'Rāgo' is that by which cloth is dyed, a dyeing substance. From a word denoting a dye, the suffix 'ṇo' occurs in the sense of 'dyed by that'.

Kasāvena rattaṃ vatthaṃ kāsāvaṃ dha. pa. 9, kāsāyaṃ vā. Evaṃ kosumbhaṃ, haliddiyā rattaṃ hāliddaṃ, pāṭaṅgena rattaṃ pāṭaṅgaṃ, mañjiṭṭhaṃ, kuṅkumaṃ iccādi.

Cloth dyed with kasāva is kāsāvaṃ, or kāsāyaṃ. Similarly, kosumbhaṃ; that dyed with turmeric is hāliddaṃ; that dyed with pāṭaṅga is pāṭaṅgaṃ; mañjiṭṭhaṃ, kuṅkumaṃ, and so forth.

“Nīlaṃ [M 0.0295] vatthaṃ, pītaṃ vattha”ntiādīsu pana nīla, pītādisaddā guṇasaddattā paccayena vinā guṇanissayaṃ dabbaṃ vadanti. Evaṃ sabbesu guṇasadda, jātisadda, nāmasaddesu.

However, in phrases such as 'blue cloth, yellow cloth', the words 'nīla' (blue), 'pīta' (yellow), and so on, being quality-words, denote the substance that possesses the quality without a suffix. Thus it is with all quality-words, class-words, and name-words.

445. Nakkhatteninduyuttena kāle ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765; caṃ. 3.1.5; pā. 4.2.3.

445. The suffix 'ṇa' is added from a word for a constellation conjoined with the moon, in the sense of time.

Induyuttena nakkhattena lakkhite kāle tannakkhattavācīhi ṇo hoti.

In a time marked by a constellation conjoined with the moon, the suffix 'ṇo' occurs after the words denoting that constellation.

Puṇṇacandayuttena phussanakkhattena lakkhitā phussā, ratti, phusso, aho. Evaṃ māgho iccādi.

The night marked by the Phussa constellation conjoined with the full moon is Phussā (the night); Phusso (the day). Similarly, Māgho, and so forth.

Nakkhattenāti kiṃ? Garugahena lakkhitā ratti.

What is meant by 'by a constellation'? The night marked by a heavy planet.

Induyuttenāti kiṃ? Phussena lakkhito muhutto.

What is meant by 'conjoined with the moon'? A moment marked by the Phussa constellation.

Kāleti kiṃ? Phussena lakkhitā atthasiddhi.

What is meant by 'in time'? The attainment of a purpose marked by the Phussa constellation.

446. Sāssa devatā puṇṇamāsī ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765; caṃ. 3.1.18, 19 …pe… 4.2.21-24.

446. The suffix 'ṇa' is added in the sense of 'that is its deity' or 'that is its full moon'.

Sā assa devatā, sā assa puṇṇamāsīti atthe paṭhamantā ṇo hoti.

In the sense of 'that is its deity' and 'that is its full moon', the suffix 'ṇo' occurs after a word in the first case.

Buddho assa devatāti buddho, yo buddhaṃ attano ārakkhadevataṃ viya garuṃ katvā vicarati, nirantaraṃ vā “buddho buddho”ti vācaṃ nicchāreti, tassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Sugato assa devatāti sogato, mahindadevo assa devatāti māhindo. Evaṃ yāmo, somo, vāruṇo.

'The Buddha is his deity'—thus, Buddho. This is the name for one who lives revering the Buddha as his protective deity, or who continuously utters the words, 'Buddho, Buddho'. 'The Sugata is his deity'—thus, Sogato. 'The great god Indra is his deity'—thus, Māhindo. Similarly, Yāmo, Somo, Vāruṇo.

Phussī assa puṇṇamāsīti phusso, māso. Evaṃ māgho, phagguno, citto, vesākho, jeṭṭhamūlo, āsaḷho, sāvaṇo, poṭṭhapādo, assayujo, kattiko, māgasiro.

'Phussī is its full moon'—thus, Phusso, the month. Similarly, Māgho, Phagguno, Citto, Vesākho, Jeṭṭhamūlo, Āsaḷho, Sāvaṇo, Poṭṭhapādo, Assayujo, Kattiko, Māgasiro.

Puṇṇamāsīti kiṃ? Phussī assa pañcamī tithī.

What is meant by 'full moon'? Phussī is its fifth lunar day.

447. Tamadhīte taṃ jānāti kaṇikā ca ka. 351; rū. 374; nī. 764; caṃ. 3.1.37 …pe… 4.2.59.

447. The suffixes 'ṇa', 'ka', and 'ṇika' are added in the sense of 'he studies that' or 'he knows that'.

Etesu [M 0.0296] atthesu dutiyantā ṇo ca ko ca ṇiko cāti ete paccayā honti.

In these meanings, the suffixes 'ṇo', 'ko', and 'ṇiko' occur after words in the second case.

Ṇamhi – byākaraṇaṃ adhīte jānāti vā veyyākaraṇo dī. ni. 1.256. Pakkhe “veyyākaraṇiko, byañjanaṃ adhīte jānāti vā veyyañjaniko”ti imāni ṇikena sijjhanti.

In the case of 'ṇa': one who studies or knows grammar is a veyyākaraṇo (grammarian). Alternatively, 'veyyākaraṇiko'; one who studies or knows expressions is 'veyyañjaniko'—these are formed with 'ṇika'.

Kamhi-chandaṃ adhīte jānāti vā chando. Evaṃ padako dī. ni. 1.256, nāmako.

In the case of 'ka': one who studies or knows meter is 'chando'. Similarly, 'padako' (one skilled in words), 'nāmako' (one skilled in names).

Ṇikamhi-vinayaṃ adhīte jānāti vā venayiko, suttantiko, ābhidhammiko.

Regarding 'ṇika': one who studies or knows the Vinaya is a 'venayiko'; similarly, a 'suttantiko' is one who studies or knows the Suttanta, and an 'ābhidhammiko' is one who studies or knows the Abhidhamma.

Ettha ca ‘veyyākaraṇo’ti pade viyyākaraṇaṃ adhīteti vākyaṃ, ‘veyañjaniko’ti pade viyañjanaṃ adhīteti. Upari ‘dovāriko, sovaggika’nti padesupi ‘duvāre niyutto, suvaggāya saṃvattatī’ti vākyaṃ, atthaṃ kathentena pana duvāra, suvaggasaddānaṃ taddhitabhāve eva siddhattā dvāreti ca saggāyāti ca kathetabbo.

Here, for the word 'veyyākaraṇo', the explanatory phrase is 'he studies grammar'; for the word 'veyañjaniko', it is 'he studies expressions'. Furthermore, for words like 'dovāriko' and 'sovaggika', the explanatory phrases are 'appointed at the gate' and 'it is conducive to heaven'. However, when explaining the meaning, since the words 'duvāra' and 'suvagga' are established only in their derived (taddhita) form, they should be explained as 'dvāre' and 'saggāya'.

448. Tassa visaye dese ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 365; caṃ. 3.1.61; pā. 4.2.52, 53.

448. In the sense of 'his sphere' or 'country'.

Tassa desarūpe visaye chaṭṭhuntā ṇo hoti.

In the sense of 'his sphere', when it is a country, the suffix 'ṇo' is applied to a word in the sixth case.

Thūyamigā vasātino nāma, vasātīnaṃ visayo deso vāsāto. Idha adesarūpattā ṇo na hoti, cakkhussa visayo rūpaṃ.

The Thūyamigā are called the Vasātino. The sphere, or country, of the Vasātino is Vāsāto. Here, in the case of 'the sphere of the eye is form', the suffix 'ṇo' is not applied because it is not in the form of a country.

449. Nivāse tannāme ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 365; caṃ. 3.1.64; pā. 4.2.69.

449. In the sense of 'a dwelling bearing that name'.

Tannāmabhūte [M 0.0297] nivāse chaṭṭhyantā ṇo hoti.

In the sense of a dwelling bearing that name, the suffix 'ṇo' is applied to a word in the sixth case.

Sivīnaṃ nivāso deso sebyo. Vasaṃ adenti bhakkhantīti vasādā, byagghā sīhā vā, vasādānaṃ nivāso deso vāsādo.

The country which is the dwelling of the Sivis is Sebyo. Those who eat fat (vasaṃ adenti) are Vasādā, that is, tigers or lions. The country which is the dwelling of the Vasādā is Vāsādo.

450. Anubhave ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765; caṃ. 3.1.65; pā. 4.2.70.

450. In the sense of 'vicinity'.

Samīpe bhavaṃ anubhavaṃ, “adūrabhave”tipi pāṭho, tannāme anubhave dese chaṭṭhyantā ṇo hoti.

That which is in the vicinity (samīpe bhavaṃ) is 'anubhavaṃ'. The reading 'adūrabhave' (in what is not distant) is also found. In the sense of a country which is a vicinity bearing that name, the suffix 'ṇo' is applied to a word in the sixth case.

Vidisāya anubhavaṃ vedisaṃ, nagaraṃ, udumbarassa anubhavaṃ odumbaraṃ, vimānaṃ.

The vicinity of Vidisā is Vedisaṃ, a city; the vicinity of Udumbara is Odumbaraṃ, a mansion.

451. Tena nibbatte ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765; caṃ. 3.1.66; pā. 4.2.68.

451. In the sense of 'produced by that'.

Tannāme tena nibbatte dese tatiyantā ṇo hoti.

In the sense of a country produced by that agent and bearing that derived name, the suffix 'ṇo' is applied to a word in the third case.

Kusambena nāma isinā nibbattā kosambī, itthiyaṃ ī, nagarī. Evaṃ kākandī, mākandī, sahassena dhanena nibbattā sāhassī, parikhā, ayañca tatiyā hetumhi kattari karaṇe ca yathāyogaṃ yujjati.

Kosambī, a city, was produced by the sage named Kusamba; the suffix 'ī' is used in the feminine. Similarly, Kākandī and Mākandī. Sāhassī, a moat, was produced with a thousand of wealth. And this third case is applied appropriately in the sense of cause, agent, or instrument.

452. Tamidhatthi ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765; caṃ. 3.1.67; pā. 4.2.67.

452. In the sense of 'that is here'.

Taṃ idha atthīti atthe tannāme dese paṭhamantā ṇo hoti.

In the sense of 'that is here', the suffix 'ṇo' is applied to a word in the first case, denoting a country bearing that name.

Udumbarā [M 0.0298] asmiṃ dese santīti odumbaro, badarā asmiṃ dese santīti bādaro. Evaṃ pabbajo.
