Because fig trees (udumbarā) are in this country, it is called 'Odumbaro'. Because jujube trees (badarā) are in this country, it is called 'Bādaro'. Similarly, 'Pabbajo'.

453. Tatra bhave ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765; caṃ. 3.2.48; pā. 4.2.133.

453. In the sense of 'being there'.

Tatra bhavatthe sattamyantā ṇo hoti.

In the sense of 'being there', the suffix 'ṇo' is applied to a word in the seventh case.

Udake bhavo odako, maccho, urasi bhavo oraso, putto, sāgamo. Nagare bhavo nāgaro. Evaṃ jānapado, māgadho, kapilavatthumhi bhavo kāpilavatthavo, ‘uvaṇṇassāvaṅa…’ti ussa avattaṃ. Kosambiyaṃ bhavo kosambo, mitte bhavā mettā, pure bhavā porī dī. ni. 1.9, vācā, manasmiṃ bhavo mānaso. Ettha pana –

That which is in water is 'odako', a fish. That which is from the breast is 'oraso', a son; there is an augment 'sa'. That which is in the city is 'nāgaro'. Similarly, 'jānapado' (one who is in the country) and 'māgadho' (one who is in Magadha). One who is in Kapilavatthu is 'kāpilavatthavo'; according to the rule 'uvaṇṇassāvaṅa…', 'ava' is substituted for 'u'. One who is in Kosambi is 'kosambo'. That which is in a friend is 'mettā' (friendship). That which was in the past is 'porī', as in ancient speech. That which is in the mind is 'mānaso'. Here, however—

454. Manādīnaṃ saka ka. 404; rū. 370; nī. 859.

454. The augment 'sa' for 'mana' and others.

Ṇānubandhe paccaye pare manādīnaṃ ante sāgamo hotīti sabbattha manogaṇādīnaṃ ante sāgamo.

When a suffix with 'ṇ' as an anubandha follows, the augment 'sa' occurs at the end of 'mana' and other such words. Thus, everywhere, the augment 'sa' occurs at the end of the terms in the mana-group and others.

Mānaso, rāgo, mānasā, taṇhā, mānasaṃ, sukhaṃ. Evaṃ cetaso, cetasā, cetasaṃ. Kvaci mano eva mānasaṃ, ceto eva cetasotipi yujjati.

'Mānaso', as in 'mānaso rāgo' (mental passion); 'mānasā', as in 'mānasā taṇhā' (mental craving); 'mānasaṃ', as in 'mānasaṃ sukhaṃ' (mental happiness). Similarly, 'cetaso', 'cetasā', 'cetasaṃ' (from 'ceto'). Sometimes 'mano' itself is used as 'mānasaṃ', and 'ceto' itself also as 'cetaso'.

455. Ajjādīhi tano ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765; caṃ. 3.15; pā. 4.2.105.

455. The suffix 'tano' after 'ajja' and others.

Tatra bhavoti atthe ajjādīhi tano hoti.

In the sense of 'being there', the suffix 'tano' is applied to 'ajja' and other such words.

Ajja bhavo ajjatano, attho, ajjattanī, vibhatti, dvittaṃ, ajjatanaṃ, hitaṃ, sve bhavo svātano, mahāvuttinā essa āttaṃ. Hiyyo bhavo hiyyattano, hiyyattano, hiyyattanaṃ, ossa attaṃ dvittañca.

That which is of today is 'ajjatano', as in 'attho'; 'ajjattanī', as in 'vibhatti'; there is doubling; 'ajjatanaṃ', as in 'hitaṃ'. That which is of tomorrow is 'svātano'; according to the Mahāvutti, 'ātta' is substituted for 'e'. That which is of yesterday is 'hiyyattano', 'hiyyattanī', 'hiyyattanaṃ'; 'atta' is substituted for 'o', and there is doubling.

456. Purāto ṇo ca ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765.

456. And from 'purā', the suffixes 'ṇo' and 'tano'.

Tatra [M 0.0299] bhavoti atthe purāsaddamhā ṇo ca tano ca honti.

In the sense of 'being there', the suffixes 'ṇo' and 'tano' are applied to the word 'purā'.

Pure bhavo purāṇo, idha ṇo anubandho na hoti, porāṇo vā, purātano.

That which was in the past is 'purāṇo' (here, the effect of the 'ṇ' anubandha does not take place), or 'porāṇo', or 'purātano'.

457. Amātvacco ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765; caṃ. 3.2.13; pā. 4.2.104.

457. But from 'amā', the suffix 'acco'.

Amāsaddamhā bhavatthe acco hoti. ‘Amā’ti sahatthavācī.

From the word 'amā', in the sense of 'being', the suffix 'acco' occurs. 'Amā' is a word with the meaning of 'with'.

Rājakiccesu raññā saha bhavatīti amacco dī. ni. ṭī. 1.339.

One who is with the king in royal duties is 'amacco' (a minister).

458. Majjhādīhimo ka. 353; rū. 378; nī. 767; caṃ. 3.2.82; pā. 4.3.8, 22; ‘majjhāditvimo’ (bahūsu).

458. The suffix 'imo' from 'majjha' and others.

Majjhādīhi bhavatthe imo hoti.

From 'majjha' and other terms, in the sense of 'being', the suffix 'imo' occurs.

Majjhe bhavo majjhimo. Evaṃ antimo, heṭṭhimo, uparimo, orimo, pacchimo, abbhantarimo, paccantimo, puratthimo.

That which is in the middle is 'majjhimo'. Similarly, 'antimo' (the last), 'heṭṭhimo' (the lowest), 'uparimo' (the uppermost), 'orimo' (the nearer), 'pacchimo' (the western), 'abbhantarimo' (the inner), 'paccantimo' (the outermost), 'puratthimo' (the eastern).

459. Kaṇa ṇeyya ṇeyyaka yiyā ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765; caṃ. 3.2.4, 5, 6 …pe… 4.2.94, 95, 97, 119-130.

459. The suffixes 'kaṇa', 'ṇeyya', 'ṇeyyaka', 'ya', and 'iya'.

Bhavatthe sattamyantā ete pañca paccayā honti.

In the sense of 'being', these five suffixes occur from words in the seventh case.

Kaṇa-kusinārāyaṃ bhavo kosinārako, magadhesu bhavo māgadhako, āraññako, vihāro.

Regarding 'kaṇa': that which is in Kusinārā is 'kosinārako'; that which is in Magadha is 'māgadhako'; 'āraññako' (belonging to the forest).

Ṇeyya-gaṅgāyaṃ bhavo gaṅgeyyo, pabbateyyo, vane bhavo vāneyyo.

Regarding 'ṇeyya': that which is in the Ganges is 'gaṅgeyyo'; 'pabbateyyo' (that which is on a mountain); that which is in the forest is 'vāneyyo'.

Ṇeyyaka-kosaleyyako[M 0.0300], bārāṇaseyyako, campeyyako, mithileyyako, idha na vuddhi.

Regarding 'ṇeyyaka': 'kosaleyyako', 'bārāṇaseyyako', 'campeyyako', 'mithileyyako'; here there is no vowel strengthening (vuddhi).

Ya-gāme bhavo gammo, dive bhavo dibbo,

Regarding 'ya': that which is in the village is 'gammo' (rustic); that which is in the divine realm is 'dibbo' (divine).

Iya-gāmiyo, gāmiko, yassa kattaṃ, udare bhavo odariyo, odariko, dive bhavo diviyo, pañcāliyo, bodhipakkhiyo, lokiyo.

Regarding 'iya': 'gāmiyo', 'gāmiko'; that which is in the belly is 'odariyo', 'odariko'; that which is in the divine realm is 'diviyo'; 'pañcāliyo', 'bodhipakkhiyo', 'lokiyo'.

460. Ṇiko ka. 351; rū. 374; nī. 764; caṃ. 3.2.40, 41, 42; pā. 4.2.126, 127, 128.

460. The suffix 'ṇiko'.

Bhavatthe sattamyantā ṇiko hoti.

In the sense of 'being', the suffix 'ṇiko' occurs from a word in the seventh case.

Sāradiko, divaso, sāradikā, ratti, sāradikaṃ, pupphaṃ. Bhavasaddena cettha aññepi atthe upalakkheti, pabbatato pakkhandā nadī pabbateyyā, kimīnaṃ kose jātaṃ koseyyaṃ, vatthaṃ. Evaṃ siveyyaṃ, bārāṇaseyyaṃ.

'Sāradiko' (autumnal), a day; 'sāradikā' (autumnal), a night; 'sāradikaṃ' (autumnal), a flower. And by the word 'bhava' here, other meanings are also indicated: a river descending from a mountain is 'pabbateyyā'; that which is born in the cocoon of worms is 'koseyyaṃ', cloth. Similarly, 'siveyyaṃ', 'bārāṇaseyyaṃ'.

461. Tamassa sippaṃ sīlaṃ paṇyaṃ paharaṇaṃ payojanaṃ ka. 351; rū. 374; nī. 764; caṃ. 3.4.49-66 …pe… 4.4.47-65.

461. That is his craft, virtue, merchandise, weapon, or purpose.

Tamassa sippaṃ, tamassa sīlaṃ, tamassa paṇyaṃ, tamassa paharaṇaṃ, tamassa payojananti atthesu paṭhamantā ṇiko hoti.

In the meanings 'that is his craft', 'that is his virtue', 'that is his merchandise', 'that is his weapon', and 'that is his purpose', the suffix 'ṇiko' occurs from a word in the first case.

Sippe – vīṇāvādanamassa sippaṃ veṇiko. Ettha ca vīṇāsaddena vīṇāvādanaṃ vuccati. Ekatthībhāvasāmatthiyañhetaṃ. Evaṃ sabbattha. Evaṃ modiṅgiko, pāṇaviko, vaṃsiko.

In the sense of craft: 'Playing the lute is his craft'—thus, 'veṇiko' (lute-player). Here, by the term 'vīṇā', 'lute-playing' is meant; this is due to the capacity for becoming one in meaning. Thus everywhere. Similarly, 'modiṅgiko' (drummer), 'pāṇaviko' (tabor-player), 'vaṃsiko' (bamboo-flute player).

Sīle-paṃsukūladhāraṇaṃ assa sīlaṃ paṃsukūliko, paṃsukūlaṃ dhāretuṃ sīlamassāti vā paṃsukūliko. Sīlasaddena cettha vata, dhamma, sādhukārāpi gayhanti, paṃsukūlaṃ dhāreti sīlenāti paṃsukūlikotipi yujjati. Evaṃ tecīvariko[M 0.0301], piṇḍaṃ piṇḍaṃ patatīti piṇḍapāto, piṇḍācārena laddhabhojanaṃ, piṇḍapātayāpanaṃ assa sīlanti piṇḍapātiko, piṇḍapātena yāpetuṃ sīlañca vatañca dhammo ca garukāro ca assāti piṇḍapātiko.

In the sense of virtue: 'wearing rag-robes is his virtue', thus 'paṃsukūliko' (a rag-robe wearer); or, 'he has the virtue of wearing rag-robes', thus 'paṃsukūliko'. Here, by the word 'sīla', 'vow', 'practice', and 'good conduct' are also understood. It is also fitting that 'paṃsukūliko' means 'one who wears rag-robes by virtue'. Similarly, 'tecīvariko' (one who wears the three robes). 'Piṇḍapāta' (almsfood) is so called because it falls lump by lump, it is food obtained by the alms-round. 'Living on almsfood is his virtue', thus 'piṇḍapātiko' (one who lives on almsfood); or, 'he has the virtue, vow, practice, and respect for living on almsfood', thus 'piṇḍapātiko'.

‘Paṇya’nti vikkeyyavatthu vuccati, gandho paṇyaṃ assāti gandhiko. Evaṃ teliko, goḷiko.

'Paṇya' (merchandise) means an article for sale. 'Perfume is his merchandise', thus 'gandhiko' (a perfumer). Similarly, 'teliko' (an oil-seller), 'goḷiko' (a molasses-seller).

Paharanti etenāti paharaṇaṃ, āvudhabhaṇḍaṃ, cāpo paharaṇamassāti cāpiko. Evaṃ tomariko, muggariko.

'Paharaṇa' (weapon) is so called because one strikes with it; it is an item of weaponry. 'A bow is his weapon', thus 'cāpiko' (a bowman). Similarly, 'tomariko' (a spear-bearer), 'muggariko' (a club-bearer).

Payojanaṃ vuccati phalaṃ, upadhi payojanamassāti opadhikaṃ a. ni. 8.59, puññaṃ, sataṃ payojanamassāti sātikaṃ. Evaṃ sāhassikaṃ jā. 2.21.415.

'Payojanaṃ' (purpose) is called the fruit. 'Attachment is his purpose', thus 'opadhikaṃ', which is merit. 'A hundred is his purpose', thus 'sātikaṃ'. Similarly, 'sāhassikaṃ'.

462. Taṃ hantārahati gacchatuñchati carati ka. 351; rū. 374; nī. 764; caṃ. 3.4.27-43; pā. 4.4.28-46.

462. He kills that, deserves that, goes to that, gleans that, or lives by that.

Taṃ hanti, taṃ arahati, taṃ gacchati, taṃ uñchati, taṃ caratīti atthesu dutiyantā ṇiko hoti.

In the meanings 'he kills it', 'he deserves it', 'he goes to it', 'he gleans it', and 'he lives by it', the suffix 'ṇiko' occurs from a word in the accusative case.

Pakkhīhi pakkhino hantīti pakkhiko. Evaṃ sākuṇiko a. ni. 2.263 (sākunikotipi dissati), māyūriko, macchehi macche hanatīti macchiko. Evaṃ dhenuko, magehi mage hanatīti māgaviko, majjhe vāgamo. Evaṃ hāriṇiko, ‘hariṇo’ti mago eva. Sūkariko, idha na vuddhi.

'He kills birds with birds', thus 'pakkhiko' (a fowler). Similarly, 'sākuṇiko' (a bird-catcher), 'māyūriko' (a peacock-hunter). 'He kills fish with fish', thus 'macchiko' (a fisherman). Similarly, 'dhenuko' (a cow-hunter). 'He kills deer with deer', thus 'māgaviko' (a deer-hunter); here there is an insertion of 'v' in the middle. Similarly, 'hāriṇiko' (an antelope-hunter); 'hariṇa' means deer. 'Sūkariko' (a boar-hunter); here there is no vowel strengthening (vuddhi).

Sataṃ arahatīti sātikaṃ. Evaṃ sāhassikaṃ.

'He deserves a hundred', thus 'sātikaṃ'. Similarly, 'sāhassikaṃ'.

Paradāraṃ gacchatīti pāradāriko, paradāriko vā. Evaṃ pathiko, maggiko.

'He goes to another's wife', thus 'pāradāriko' (an adulterer), or 'paradāriko'. Similarly, 'pathiko' (one who travels a path), 'maggiko' (one who travels a road).

Badare [M 0.0302] uñchati gavesatīti bādariko. Evaṃ āmalakiko.

'He gleans or seeks jujubes', thus 'bādariko' (a jujube-gleaner). Similarly, 'āmalakiko' (a myrobalan-gleaner).

Dhammaṃ caratīti dhammiko. Evaṃ adhammiko.

'He lives by the Dhamma', thus 'dhammiko' (righteous). Similarly, 'adhammiko' (unrighteous).

463. Tena kataṃ kītaṃ bandhaṃ abhisaṅkhataṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ hataṃ hanti jitaṃ jayati dibbati khaṇati tarati carati vahati jīvati ka. 350; rū. 373; nī. 364; caṃ. 3.4.1-26; pā. 4.4.1-27.

463. Done by him, bought by him, bound by him, fabricated by him, associated with by him, killed by him, he kills, conquered by him, he conquers, he plays, he digs, he crosses, he lives by, he carries, he lives.

Tena kataṃ, tena kītaṃ…pe… tena jīvati iccatthesu tatiyantā ṇiko hoti.

Done by him, bought by him… (and so on)… he lives by that—in these meanings, the suffix ṇika occurs after a word ending in the instrumental case.

Kāyena kataṃ kāyikaṃ. Evaṃ vācasikaṃ, mānasikaṃ, vātena kato vātiko, ābādho.

That which is done by the body is kāyikaṃ (physical). Similarly, vācasikaṃ (verbal), mānasikaṃ (mental). That which is caused by the wind is vātiko, a disease.

Satena mūlena kītaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ sātikaṃ. Evaṃ sāhassikaṃ.

Goods bought for a hundred are sātikaṃ. Similarly, sāhassikaṃ (worth a thousand).

Varattāya yottāya bandhito vārattiko, ayasā bandhito āyasiko, sāgamo. Evaṃ pāsiko.

Bound with a strap or a cord is vārattiko. Bound with iron is āyasiko, with the insertion of 's'. Similarly, pāsiko (bound with a noose).

Ghatena abhisaṅkhataṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ vā ghātikaṃ. Evaṃ goḷikaṃ, dādhikaṃ, māricikaṃ.

That which is prepared or mixed with ghee is ghātikaṃ. Similarly, goḷikaṃ (prepared with molasses), dādhikaṃ (prepared with curds), and māricikaṃ (prepared with pepper).

Jālena hato jāliko, maccho.

Caught by a net is jāliko, a fish.

Jālena hantīti jāliko, jālakevaṭṭo. Evaṃ bāḷisiko saṃ. ni. 2.158.

One who catches with a net is jāliko, a net-fisherman. Similarly, bāḷisiko (one who fishes with a hook).

Akkhehi jitaṃ dhanaṃ akkhikaṃ. Evaṃ sālākikaṃ.

Wealth won by dice is akkhikaṃ. Similarly, sālākikaṃ (won by lots).

Akkhehi jayati dibbatīti vā akkhiko.

One who wins or plays with dice is akkhiko (a gambler).

Khaṇittiyā khaṇatīti khāṇittiko. Evaṃ kuddāliko, idha na vuddhi.

One who digs with a spade is khāṇittiko. Similarly, kuddāliko (one who digs with a hoe); here there is no vowel strengthening.

Uḷumpena [M 0.0303] taratīti oḷumpiko, uḷumpiko vā. Evaṃ nāviko jā. 2.20.149, gopucchiko.

One who crosses with a raft is oḷumpiko, or uḷumpiko. Similarly, nāviko (a boatman), and gopucchiko (a cowherd).

Sakaṭena caratīti sākaṭiko. Evaṃ rathiko, yāniko, daṇḍiko,

One who travels by cart is sākaṭiko. Similarly, rathiko (a charioteer), yāniko (one who travels by vehicle), and daṇḍiko (one who travels with a staff).

Khandhena vahatīti khandhiko. Evaṃ aṃsiko, sīsiko, idha na vuddhi.

One who carries on the shoulder is khandhiko. Similarly, aṃsiko (a shoulder-bearer) and sīsiko (a head-bearer); here there is no vowel strengthening.

Vetanena jīvatīti vetaniko. Evaṃ bhatiko, kasiko, kayiko, vikkayiko, bhatikādīsu na vuddhi.

One who lives by wages is vetaniko. Similarly, bhatiko (a hired servant), kasiko (a farmer), kayiko (a buyer), and vikkayiko (a seller); in bhatika and the following words, there is no vowel strengthening.

464. Tassa saṃvattati ka. 351; rū. 374; nī. 765; caṃ. 3.4.67-69; pā. 4.4.66-68.

464. It conduces to that.

Tassa saṃvattatīti atthe catutthyantā ṇiko hoti.

In the sense 'it conduces to that,' the suffix ṇika occurs after a word ending in the dative case.

Puna bhavāya saṃvattatīti ponobbhaviko, punassa ottaṃ, bhassa dvittaṃ, ponobbhavikā mahāva. 14, taṇhā, lokāya saṃvattatīti lokiko, suṭṭhu aggoti saggo, saggāya saṃvattatīti sovaggikaṃ dī. ni. 1.163, puññaṃ. Evaṃ diṭṭhadhammikaṃ, samparāyikaṃ.

That which conduces to renewed existence is ponobbhaviko; for puna, there is o, and bha is doubled. Craving is ponobbhavikā. That which conduces to the world is lokiko. 'Supremely excellent' is saggo (heaven). That which conduces to heaven is sovaggikaṃ, which is merit. Similarly, diṭṭhadhammikaṃ (pertaining to the present life) and samparāyikaṃ (pertaining to the future life).

465. Tato sambhūtamāgataṃ ka. 351; rū. 374; nī. 765; caṃ. 3.3.49-51; …pe… 4.3.77-79.

465. Arisen from that, come from that.

Tato sambhūtaṃ, tato āgataṃ iccatthesu pañcamyantā ṇiko hoti.

In the senses 'arisen from that' and 'come from that,' the suffix ṇika occurs after a word ending in the ablative case.

Mātito sambhūtaṃ āgataṃ vā mattikaṃ pārā. 34, dvittaṃ rasso ca. Evaṃ pettikaṃ. Ṇya, ṇiyāpi dissanti, surabhito sambhūtaṃ sorabhyaṃ, thanato sambhūtaṃ thaññaṃ, pitito sambhūto pettiyo. Evaṃ mattiyo. Ṇyamhi-macco.

Arisen or come from the mother is mattikaṃ; there is doubling and shortening. Similarly, pettikaṃ (paternal). The suffixes ṇya and ṇiya are also seen: arisen from fragrance is sorabhyaṃ; arisen from the breast is thaññaṃ (breast milk); arisen from the father is pettiyo. Similarly, mattiyo. In the case of ṇya, there is macco.

466. Tattha vasati vidito bhatto niyutto ka. 351; rū. 374; nī. 765; caṃ. 3.4.70-75 …pe… 4.4.69-74.

466. Dwells there, is known there, is supported there, is appointed there.

Etesvatthesu [M 0.0304] sattamyantā ṇiko hoti.

In these meanings, the suffix ṇika occurs after a word ending in the locative case.

Rukkhamūle vasatīti rukkhamūliko. Evaṃ āraññiko, sosāniko.

One who dwells at the root of a tree is rukkhamūliko. Similarly, āraññiko (a forest-dweller) and sosāniko (a charnel-ground-dweller).

Ettha ca vasatīti sāmaññavacanepi tassīla, tabbata, taddhamma, tassādhukāritānaṃ vasena attho veditabbo taddhitapaccayānaṃ pasiddhatthadīpakattā. Na hi rukkhamūle muhuttamattaṃ vasanto rukkhamūlikoti voharīyati.

And here, in the general statement 'he dwells,' the meaning should be understood by way of his character, his vow, his practice, and his devotion to that practice, because taddhita suffixes illuminate established meanings. For one who dwells at the root of a tree for only a moment is not called a rukkhamūlika.

Loke vidito lokiko.

Known in the world is lokiko.

Catumahārājesu bhattā cātumahārājikā saṃ. ni. 5.1081.

Those supported by the Four Great Kings are the cātumahārājikā.

Dvāre niyutto dovāriko. Evaṃ bhaṇḍāgāriko, navakammiko, idha na vuddhi. “Jātikiyo, andhakiyo” iccādīsu mahāvuttinā kiyo.

Appointed at the gate is dovāriko (a gatekeeper). Similarly, bhaṇḍāgāriko (a storekeeper) and navakammiko (a supervisor of new works); here there is no vowel strengthening. In cases such as jātikiyo and andhakiyo, the suffix is kiyo, according to extensive usage.

467. Tassidaṃ ka. 351; rū. 374; nī. 764; caṃ. 3.3.85-102; pā. 4.3.120-133.

467. This is his.

Tassa idanti atthe chaṭṭhuntā ṇiko hoti.

In the sense 'this is his,' the suffix ṇika occurs after a word ending in the genitive case.

Saṅghassa ayaṃ saṅghiko, vihāro, saṅghikā, bhūmi, saṅghassa idaṃ saṅghikaṃ, bhaṇḍaṃ. Evaṃ puggalikaṃ, gaṇikaṃ, mahājanikaṃ, sakyaputtassa esoti sakyaputtiko. Evaṃ nāṭaputtiko, dāsaputtiko.

This monastery belongs to the Saṅgha, hence it is saṅghiko; this land is saṅghikā; this property belongs to the Saṅgha, hence it is saṅghikaṃ. Similarly, puggalikaṃ (personal), gaṇikaṃ (belonging to a group), and mahājanikaṃ (public). 'This belongs to a son of the Sakyans' becomes sakyaputtiko. Similarly, nāṭaputtiko (belonging to a son of the Nātas) and dāsaputtiko (belonging to a son of a slave).

468. Ṇikassiyo vā ka. 404; rū. 370; nī. 756.

468. Or, iyo for ṇika.

Ṇikapaccayassa iyo hoti vā.

The suffix ṇika optionally becomes iyo.

Sakyaputtiyo, sakyaputtiko iccādi.

Sakyaputtiyo, sakyaputtiko, and so forth.

469. Ṇo ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765; caṃ. 3.3.85; pā. 4.3.120.

469. The suffix ṇo.

Tassidanti [M 0.0305] atthe chaṭṭhuntā ṇo hoti.

In the sense of 'this is of that,' the suffix ṇo occurs after a word ending in the sixth case.

Kaccāyanassa idaṃ kaccāyanaṃ, byākaraṇaṃ. Evaṃ sogataṃ, sāsanaṃ, māhiṃsaṃ, maṃsādi.

This is of Kaccāyana, thus kaccāyanaṃ, i.e., the grammar. Similarly, sogataṃ, i.e., the Dispensation; māhiṃsaṃ, i.e., meat, etc.

470. Gavādīhi yo ka. 353; rū. 378; nī. 781.

470. After 'go' and so forth, yo.

Tassidanti atthe gavādīhi yo hoti.

In the sense of 'this is of that,' the suffix yo occurs after 'go' and so forth.

471. Yamhi gossa ca ka. 78; rū. 31; nī. 229.

471. And of 'go' before a suffix with 'ya'.

Yavante paccaye pare gossa ca uvaṇṇānañca avaṅa hotīti avādeso. ‘Tavaggavaraṇāna…’nti suttena vassa battaṃ, gunnaṃ idaṃ gabyaṃ, maṃsādi, du vuccati rukkho, tassa idaṃ dabyaṃ, dabbaṃ, mūlādi.

When a suffix beginning with 'ya' follows, for 'go' and for the u-vowels there is the substitution 'ava'; this is the 'ava' substitution. By the sutta 'Tavaggavaraṇāna…', 'va' becomes 'ba'. This belongs to cows, thus gabyaṃ, e.g., meat. 'Du' is said to be a tree; this belongs to it, thus dabyaṃ or dabbaṃ, e.g., roots.

Anekattharāsi niṭṭhito.

The Section on Various Meanings is concluded.

Assatthirāsi

The Section on the Sense 'He Has'

472. Tametthassatthīti mantu ka. 369; rū. 403; nī. 793; caṃ. 4.2.98; pā. 5.2.94.

472. In the sense of 'that is here' or 'he has that', mantu.

Taṃ ettha atthi, taṃ assa atthīti atthesu paṭhamantā mantupaccayo hoti, ivaṇṇu’vaṇṇo’kārehi mantu. Tattha ivaṇṇantehi niccaṃ, upaṭṭhitā sati etasmiṃ atthi, etassa vā atthīti satimā. Evaṃ gatimā, matimā, dhitimā saṃ. ni. 1.1952; jā. 2.22.1451, atthadassimā jā. 2.22.1451, sirīmā jā. aṭṭha. 1.avidūrenidānakathā iccādi.

In the senses 'that is here' or 'he has that,' the suffix mantu occurs after a word ending in the first case. After stems ending in the vowels 'i', 'u', or 'o', mantu. There, after stems ending in 'i', it is always applied. For example, 'established mindfulness is in this' or 'he has it,' thus satimā. Similarly, gatimā, matimā, dhitimā, atthadassimā, sirīmā, and so on.

Uvaṇṇantehi pana [M 0.0306] –

But from those ending in the vowel 'u'–

473. Āyussāyasa mantumhi ka. 371; rū. 404; nī. 797.

473. Of 'āyu', 'āyasa' when mantu follows.

Mantumhi pare āyussa āyasādeso hoti.

When the suffix mantu follows, 'āyu' is substituted by 'āyasa'.

Dīghaṃ āyu asmiṃ atthi, assa vā atthīti āyasmā mahāni. 49. Evaṃ cakkhumā, bandhumā, bhāṇumā iccādi.

Long life is in him, or he has it, thus āyasmā. Similarly, cakkhumā, bandhumā, bhāṇumā, and so on.

Bahū gāvo asmiṃ santi, assa vā santīti gomā. Candimā, pāpimāpadesu ca mahāvuttinā imantupaccayaṃ icchanti. Tattha candasaṅkhātaṃ vimānaṃ assa atthīti candimā dha. pa. 387, devaputto, upacārena pana vimānampi candimāti vuccati, devaputtopi candoti vuccati. Ati viya pāpo ajjhāsayo assa atthīti pāpimā saṃ. ni. 1.137, māro. Na hi appakena pāpena pāpimāti vuccati pahūtādivasena pasiddhe eva mantādīnaṃ pavattanato. Vuttañhi vuttiyaṃ –

Many cows are in this, or he has them, thus gomā. In the case of candimā and pāpimā, they desire the suffix imantu due to extensive usage. There, the celestial mansion called 'canda' belongs to him, thus candimā, the moon-god; by convention, however, the mansion is also called candimā, and the god is also called cando. An exceedingly evil disposition belongs to him, thus pāpimā, Māra. For one is not called pāpimā due to a small amount of evil, but rather because the suffixes mantu and so on are applied only in cases well-known for abundance and so forth. For it is said in the commentary–

“Pahūte ca pasaṃsāyaṃ, nindāyañcātisāyane.

In abundance, in praise, in censure, and in excess,

Niccayoge ca saṃsagge, hontime mantuādayo”ti moga. 78.

and in constant connection and in association, these suffixes mantu and so on occur.

Tattha pahūte-gomā saṃ. ni. 1.12, dhanavāti.

There, in the sense of abundance: gomā, dhanavā.

Pasaṃsāyaṃ-jātimā, guṇavāti.

In the sense of praise: jātimā, guṇavā.

Nindāyaṃ-valimāti.

In the sense of censure: valimā.

Atisāyane – buddhimā, vaṇṇavāti.

In the sense of excess: buddhimā, vaṇṇavā.

Niccayoge-satimā, sīlavā, daṇḍīti.

In the sense of constant connection: satimā, sīlavā, daṇḍī.

Saṃsagge – haliddimāti.

In the sense of association: haliddimā.

Tathā vijjamānehi eva satiādīhi satimā iccādayo vuccanti, na atītehi anāgatehi ca avijjamānehi, kasmā[M 0.0307]? Atthisaddena paccuppannena niddiṭṭhattā. Evaṃ pana sati kathaṃ pubbepi tvaṃ satimā āsi, anāgatepi satimā bhavissasīti idaṃ siddhanti? Tadapi tadā vijjamānāya eva satiyā siddhanti.

Thus, one is called satimā and so on only with existing qualities like mindfulness, not with past, future, or non-existing ones. Why? Because it is indicated by the word 'atthi', which is in the present tense. But this being so, how is this established: 'you were mindful in the past' and 'you will be mindful in the future'? That too is established by the mindfulness that was existing at that time.

Go, asso, manusso iccādīsu jātisaddesu tesaṃ dabbābhidhānasamatthattā mantādayo na honti, tathā nīlo paṭo, sukko paṭoiccādīsu guṇasaddesu tisso, phussoiccādīsu nāmasaddesu ca. Yesaṃ pana dabbābhidhānasāmatthiyaṃ natthi, tesveva honti, buddhimā, paññavā, rūpavā, vaṇṇavā iccādi.

In class-nouns like 'go' (cow), 'asso' (horse), 'manusso' (human), etc., the suffixes mantu and so on do not occur because of their ability to denote substance. The same is true for quality-nouns like 'nīlo paṭo' (blue cloth), 'sukko paṭo' (white cloth), etc., and for proper nouns like 'Tisso', 'Phusso', etc. But for those that do not have the ability to denote substance, they occur only in them, such as buddhimā, paññavā, rūpavā, vaṇṇavā, and so on.

374. Imiyā ka. 353; rū. 378; nī. 768.

374. The suffixes ima and iyā.

Paṭhamantā mantvatthe ima, iyā honti.

In the sense of possession, the suffixes ima and iyā occur after a word ending in the first case.

Bahavo puttā assa asmiṃ vā santīti puttimo, patthaṭā kitti assa asmiṃ vā atthīti kittimo. Evaṃ phalimo, khandhimo, rukkho, puttiyo, kappimo, kappiyo, jaṭimo, jaṭiyo, thiraṃ guṇajātaṃ assa asmiṃ vā atthīti theriyo, hānabhāgo assa atthi, asmiṃ vā vijjatīti hānabhāgiyo. Evaṃ ṭhitibhāgiyo, visesabhāgiyo, nibbedhabhāgiyo iccādi.

Many sons belong to him or are in him, thus 'puttimo' (having sons). Widespread fame belongs to him or is in him, thus 'kittimo' (famous). Similarly, 'phalimo' (fruitful), 'khandhimo' (having a trunk), 'rukkho' (tree), 'puttiyo' (having sons), 'kappimo' (suitable), 'kappiyo' (suitable), 'jaṭimo' (having matted hair), 'jaṭiyo' (having matted hair). A firm collection of qualities belongs to him or is in him, thus 'theriyo' (an elder). A share in loss belongs to him or is found in him, thus 'hānabhāgiyo' (partaking of loss). Likewise, 'ṭhitibhāgiyo' (partaking of stability), 'visesabhāgiyo' (partaking of distinction), 'nibbedhabhāgiyo' (partaking of penetration), and so on.

Ettha ca pāḷiyaṃ candimā, puttimāsaddānaṃ simhi rājādigaṇarūpaṃ dissati, rattimābhāti candimā dha. pa. 387, puttehi nandati puttimāti saṃ. ni. 1.12. Kittimāsaddassa pana kittimassa kittimatoti rūpanti.

Here, in the Pāḷi, for the words 'candimā' and 'puttimā', the form of the 'rājādi' group is seen in the 'si' case. For example, 'rattimābhāti candimā' (the moon shines at night) and 'puttehi nandati puttimā' (one with sons delights in his sons). For the word 'kittimā', however, the forms are 'kittimassa' and 'kittimato'.

475. Vantvāvaṇṇā ka. 368; rū. 402; nī. 792; caṃ. 6.3.35 …pe… 8.2.9.

475. The suffix `vantu` [is used] after an `a`-stem.

Avaṇṇabhūtā paṭhamantā mantvatthe vantu hoti.

After a word ending in the first case which is an `a`-stem, the suffix `vantu` occurs in the sense of possession.

Niccasīlavasena [M 0.0308] visuddhaṃ sīlaṃ assa atthi, asmiṃ vā vijjatīti sīlavā, pasattho guṇo assa atthi, asmiṃ vā vijjatīti guṇavā.

Pure virtue by way of constant morality belongs to him or is found in him, thus 'sīlavā' (virtuous). A praised quality belongs to him or is found in him, thus 'guṇavā' (virtuous).

Evaṃ sabbattha padatthānurūpaṃ mantvatthaviseso vattabbo, paṭisandhisahagatā paññā assa atthīti paññavā, paccaye pare dīghānaṃ kvaci rassattaṃ. Vidati etenāti vido, ñāṇaṃ, vido etassa atthi, etasmiṃ vā vijjatīti vidvā, byañjane pubbassaralopo.

Thus, in all cases, the specific meaning of possession should be stated according to the meaning of the base word. Wisdom accompanied by rebirth-linking belongs to him, thus 'paññavā' (wise). When a suffix follows, long vowels are sometimes shortened. One knows by this, thus 'vido', meaning knowledge; 'vido' belongs to him or is found in him, thus 'vidvā' (wise, knowing). Elision of the preceding vowel occurs before a consonant.

Avaṇṇāti kiṃ? Satimā, bandhumā.

Why the specification 'from an `a`-stem'? [For cases such as] `satimā`, `bandhumā`.

Bahulādhikārā rasmivā, lakkhivā, yasassivā, bhayadassivā, massuvā, gāṇḍīvadhanvātipi sijjhanti. Tattha gāṇḍīvadhanu assa atthi, asmiṃ vā vijjatīti gāṇḍīvadhanvā, byañjane pubbassaralopo.

By the governing rule of `bahulaṃ` (variously), forms like `rasmivā`, `lakkhivā`, `yasassivā`, `bhayadassivā`, `massuvā`, and `gāṇḍīvadhanvā` are also accomplished. Therein, the Gāṇḍīva bow belongs to him, or is in him, thus `gāṇḍīvadhanvā`; there is elision of the preceding vowel before a consonant.

476. Daṇḍādīhikaī vā ka. 366; rū. 400; nī. 790; caṃ. 4.2.118-121; pā. 5.2.115-6.

476. From `daṇḍa` and so on, `ika` and `ī` [are used] optionally.

Tehi mantvatthe ika, ī honti vā.

From these, in the sense of possession, `ika` and `ī` occur optionally.

Niccaṃ gahito daṇḍo assa atthi, asmiṃ vā vijjatīti daṇḍiko, daṇḍī, daṇḍavā. Evaṃ gandhiko, gandhī, gandhavā, rūpiko, rūpī, rūpavā. Iṇasāmike vattabbe dhanā iko, dhaniko, aññatra dhanī, dhanavā, atthiko, atthī, atthavā.

A constantly held staff belongs to him, or is in him, thus `daṇḍiko`, `daṇḍī`, `daṇḍavā`. Similarly, `gandhiko`, `gandhī`, `gandhavā`; `rūpiko`, `rūpī`, `rūpavā`. When a creditor is to be expressed, from `dhana` (wealth), `iko` is used, forming `dhaniko`; otherwise, `dhanī` and `dhanavā`. Similarly, `atthiko`, `atthī`, `atthavā` (one who has a purpose).

Ettha ca asannihitena atthena attho assa atthīti atthiko, mahagghena atthiko mahagghatthiko. Evaṃ dhanatthiko, puññatthiko, seyyatthiko, ayaṃ attho etassāti idamatthī, pāṭavena attho assāti pāṭavatthī. Evaṃ chekatthī, kusalatthīiccādīni sijjhanti.

Here, `atthiko` is one for whom a purpose exists, with a meaning that is not immediately present. One who has a purpose for something of great value is `mahagghatthiko`. Similarly, `dhanatthiko` (one with a purpose for wealth), `puññatthiko` (one with a purpose for merit), `seyyatthiko` (one with a purpose for what is better). `idamatthī` means 'this purpose is his'. One whose purpose is skill is `pāṭavatthī`. Likewise, `chekatthī`, `kusalatthī`, and so on are accomplished.

Vaṇṇasaddantā pana īyeva hoti, brahmuno vaṇṇo saṇṭhānaṃ assa atthīti brahmavaṇṇī. Atha vā brahmuno vaṇṇo brahmavaṇṇo[M 0.0309], brahmavaṇṇo viya vaṇṇo yassa so brahmavaṇṇī. Evaṃ brahmavacchasī, ‘vacchasa’nti sīsaṃ, taddhitantasamāsapadaṃ nāmetaṃ. Evaṃ devavaṇṇī.

From a word ending in `vaṇṇa`, however, only `ī` is used. The appearance, or form, of Brahmā belongs to him, thus `brahmavaṇṇī`. Alternatively, the appearance of Brahmā is `brahmavaṇṇo`; one whose appearance is like `brahmavaṇṇo` is `brahmavaṇṇī`. Similarly, `brahmavacchasī`—`vacchasa` means 'head'; this is a name which is a compound word ending in a taddhita suffix. Similarly, `devavaṇṇī`.

Hattha, dantādīhi jātiyaṃ ī, hatthī, dantī, gajo, dāṭhī, kesarī, sīho, aññatra hatthavā, dantavā. Brahmacārimhi vattabbe vaṇṇato īyeva, vaṇṇī, aññatra vaṇṇavā. Pokkharādīhi dese īyeva, pokkharaṃ vuccati kamalaṃ, pokkharaṇī, puna itthiyaṃ nī, pubbaī-kārassa attaṃ, uppalinī, kumudinī, bhisinī, muḷālinī, sālukinī, padumaṃ ettha dese atthīti padumī, tato itthiyaṃ nī, paduminī, pubbaī-kārassa rassattaṃ, sabbaṃ kamalākarassa vā kamalagacchassa vā nāmaṃ, aññatra pokkharavā hatthī, idha soṇḍā pokkharaṃ nāma.

From `hattha` (trunk), `danta` (tusk), and so on, in the sense of species, the suffix `ī` is used: `hatthī` (elephant), `dantī` (tusked one), `gajo` (elephant), `dāṭhī` (fanged one), `kesarī` (maned one), `sīho` (lion); otherwise, `hatthavā` or `dantavā`. When speaking of a celibate practitioner, from `vaṇṇa` (caste), only `ī` is used, forming `vaṇṇī`; otherwise, `vaṇṇavā`. From `pokkhara` and so on, in the sense of 'place', only `ī` is used. `Pokkhara` is called a lotus; `pokkharaṇī` (lotus pond). Then, in the feminine, `nī` is used, and the preceding `ī`-sound becomes `a`, as in `uppalinī`, `kumudinī`, `bhisinī`, `muḷālinī`, `sālukinī`. A lotus exists in this place, thus `padumī`; then in the feminine, `nī` is used, forming `paduminī`, with shortening of the preceding `ī`-sound. All are names for a lotus pond or a lotus cluster. Otherwise, `pokkharavā hatthī` (an elephant with a trunk); here, the trunk is called `pokkhara`.

Sikhī, sikhāvā, mālī, mālāvā, sīlī, sīlavā, balī, balavā. Samāsantepi ī, niddāsīlī, sabhāsīlī, bāhubalī, ūrubalī. Sukha, dukkhehi īyeva, sukhī, dukkhī iccādi.

`Sikhī`, `sikhāvā` (crested); `mālī`, `mālāvā` (garlanded); `sīlī`, `sīlavā` (virtuous); `balī`, `balavā` (strong). Even at the end of compounds, `ī` is used: `niddāsīlī` (one of sleepy habits), `sabhāsīlī` (one of sociable habits), `bāhubalī` (strong-armed), `ūrubalī` (strong-thighed). From `sukha` (happiness) and `dukkha` (suffering), only `ī` is used: `sukhī` (happy), `dukkhī` (suffering), and so on.

477. Tapādīhi sī ka. 365; rū. 399; nī. 789; caṃ. 4.2.106; pā. 5.2.102; ‘… ssī’ (bahūsu).

477. From `tapa` and so on, `sī` [is used].

Tapādīhi mantvatthe sī hoti vā.

From `tapa` and so on, in the sense of possession, the suffix `sī` occurs optionally.

Tapo assa asmiṃ vā vijjatīti tapassī, dvittaṃ. Evaṃ yasassī, tejassī, mano assa atthīti manassī.

Austerity is his or is in him, thus `tapassī` (ascetic); there is doubling. Similarly, `yasassī` (famous), `tejassī` (majestic). Mind is his, thus `manassī` (attentive).

Vātveva? Yasavā.

Why [the word] 'optionally'? [Because there is the form] `Yasavā`.

478. Ṇo tapā ka. 370; rū. 405; nī. 795; caṃ. 4.2.106; pā. 5.2.103.

478. From `tapa`, `ṇo` [is used].

Tapamhā mantvatthe ṇo hoti.

From `tapa`, in the sense of possession, the suffix `ṇo` occurs.

Tapo assa atthīti tāpaso, itthiyaṃ tāpasī.

Austerity is his, thus `tāpaso` (hermit); in the feminine, `tāpasī`.

479. Mukhādito ro ka. 367; rū. 401; nī. 791; caṃ. 4.2.110, 111; pā. 5.2.106, 107.

479. From `mukha` and so on, `ro` [is used].

Mukhādīhi [M 0.0310] mantvatthe ro hoti.

From `mukha` and so on, in the sense of possession, the suffix `ro` occurs.

Asaṃyataṃ mukhaṃ assa atthīti mukharo, susi assa atthīti susiro, rukkho, ūso khāro yasmiṃ atthīti ūsaro, khārabhūmippadeso, madhu raso assa atthīti madhuro, guḷo, nagā ettha santīti nagaro, bahupabbatappadeso, “nagara”ntipi pāṭho, kuñjo vuccati hanu, kuñjaro, hatthī, uṇṇatā dantā assa santīti danturo, hatthīyeva, mahāvuttinā assa uttaṃ.

An unrestrained mouth is his, thus `mukharo` (talkative). A hollow is its, thus `susiro` (hollow), a tree. Saline soil is in it, thus `ūsaro`, a region of saline land. The taste of honey is its, thus `madhuro` (sweet), jaggery. Mountains are here, thus `nagaro`, a region with many mountains; the reading is also `nagara`. `Kuñja` is called the jaw, thus `kuñjaro`, an elephant. Prominent teeth are his, thus `danturo`, also an elephant. This is stated in the Mahāvutti.

480. Tundyādīhi bho ka. 364; rū. 398; nī. 387; caṃ. 4.2.148; pā. 5.2.139.

480. From `tundi` and so on, `bho` [is used].

Tundiiccādīhi mantvatthe bho hoti vā.

From `tundi` and so on, in the sense of possession, the suffix `bho` occurs optionally.

Tundi vuccati vuddhā nābhi, tundibho, valiyo etasmiṃ atthīti valibho.

`Tundi` is called a prominent navel, thus `tundibho`. Folds are on it, thus `valibho`.

Vātveva? Tundimā.

Why [the word] 'optionally'? [Because there is the form] `Tundimā`.

481. Saddhāditva ka. 370; rū. 405; nī. 795; caṃ. 4.2.105; pā. 5.2.101 (saddādivha?).

481. From saddhā and so on, the suffix 'a'.

Saddhādīhi mantvatthe a hoti.

From saddhā and other words, in the sense of possession, the suffix 'a' occurs.

Saddhā assa atthi, asmiṃ vā vijjatīti saddho. Evaṃ pañño, sato.

He has faith, or it exists in him, thus he is 'saddho'. Likewise, 'pañño', 'sato'.

Vātveva? Paññavā, satimā.

And also with 'vā'? For example: 'paññavā', 'satimā'.

482. Ālvābhijjhādīhi ka. 359; rū. 384; nī. 779; caṃ. 4.2.157; pā. 3.2.158.

482. From abhijjhā and so on, 'ālu' optionally.

Abhijjhādīhi mantvatthe ālu hoti vā.

From abhijjhā and other words, in the sense of possession, the suffix 'ālu' occurs optionally.

Abhijjhā [M 0.0311] adhikā assa atthīti abhijjhālu, sītaladukkhaṃ adhikaṃ assa atthīti sītālu, dhajā bahulā asmiṃ rathe santīti dhajālu, dayā bahulā assāti dayālu, purisacittaṃ bahulaṃ assāti purisālu, purisalolā itthī.

He has excessive covetousness, thus he is 'abhijjhālu'. He has excessive suffering from cold, thus he is 'sītālu'. Many banners are on this chariot, thus it is 'dhajālu'. He has abundant compassion, thus he is 'dayālu'. Her mind is much on men, thus she is 'purisālu', a woman lustful for men.

Vātveva? Dayāvā.

And also with 'vā'? For example: 'dayāvā'.

483. Picchāditvilo ka. 364; rū. 398; nī. 787; caṃ. 4.2.102, 103; pā. 5.2.99, 100.

483. From piccha and so on, the suffix 'ilo'.

Picchādito mantvatthe ilo hoti vā.

From piccha and other words, in the sense of possession, the suffix 'ilo' occurs optionally.

Picchaṃ tūlaṃ assa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatīti picchilo, picchavā, tūlarukkho, picchilā sippali sippalī, sīmbalī, semmalītipi dissati, phenilo pheṇilotipi dissati, phenavā, addāriṭṭhako, jaṭilo, jaṭāvā, tāpaso, tuṇḍilo, tuṇḍavā, adhikā vācā assa atthīti vācālo, mahāvuttinā ilopo.

He has 'piccha' (cotton), or it exists in it, thus 'picchilo' or 'picchavā'; for example, a cotton tree. 'Picchilā sippali'. 'Phenilo' or 'phenavā'; for example, the addāriṭṭhaka tree. 'Jaṭilo' or 'jaṭāvā'; for example, an ascetic. 'Tuṇḍilo' or 'tuṇḍavā'. He has excessive speech, thus he is 'vācālo'. According to the Mahāvutti, there is elision of 'ilo'.

484. Sīlādito vo ka. 364; rū. 398; nī. 787; caṃ. 4.2.113; pā. 5.2.109.

484. From sīla and so on, the suffix 'vo'.

Sīlādīhi mantvatthe vo hoti.

From sīla and other words, in the sense of possession, the suffix 'vo' occurs.

Niccarakkhitasīlaṃ assa atthi, asmiṃ vā vijjatīti sīlavo, puriso, sīlavā, itthī, kesā atidīghā asmiṃ santīti kesavo, kesavā, aparimāṇā aṇṇā udakā asmiṃ santīti aṇṇavo, mahantaṃ balaṃ assa atthīti balavo, balavā, balavaṃ. Gāṇḍī vuccati sandhi, bahavo gāṇḍī asmiṃ atthīti gāṇḍīvaṃ, dhanu gaṇḍassa gaṇḍamigasiṅgassa ayaṃ gāṇḍī, so assa atthīti gāṇḍīti gāṇḍīvo. (pañcakāṭīkā). gāṇḍīmeṇḍasiṅgamassa atthīti gāṇḍīvaṃ, dhanu. (payogasiddhi). gāṇḍī ganthi, so atthi assa asmiṃ vā gāṇḍīvo ajjunadhanu, (mugdhabodhaṭīkā), bahukā rājī assa atthīti rājīvaṃ, paṅkajaṃ.

He has constantly protected virtue, or it exists in him, thus 'sīlavo' for a man, and 'sīlavā' for a woman. He has exceedingly long hair, thus he is 'kesavo' or 'kesavā'. Immeasurable waters exist in it, thus it is 'aṇṇavo'. He has great strength, thus he is 'balavo', 'balavā', or 'balavaṃ'. 'Gāṇḍī' is said to be a joint; as it has many joints, it is 'gāṇḍīvaṃ', a bow. As it has many stripes, it is 'rājīvaṃ', a lotus.

485. Māyāmedhāhi vī ka. 364; rū. 398; nī. 787; caṃ. 4.2.137; pā. 5.2.121.

485. From māyā and medhā, the suffix 'vī'.

Etehi [M 0.0312] mantvatthe vī hoti.

From these, in the sense of possession, the suffix 'vī' occurs.

Māyāvī, medhāvī.

'Māyāvī', 'medhāvī'.

486. Issare āmyuvāmī ka. 364; rū. 398; nī. 787; caṃ. 4.2.143; pā. 5.2.126; “sissare…” (bahūsu).

486. In the sense of 'issara', the suffixes 'āmī' and 'uvāmī'.

Issarabhūte mantvatthe āmī, uvāmī honti.

In the sense of possession signifying a lord, the suffixes 'āmī' and 'uvāmī' occur.

Issariyaṭṭhānabhūtaṃ saṃ assa atthīti sāmī, suvāmī su. ni. 671, itthiyaṃ sāminī, suvāminī, bindulopo, kāgame sāmiko.

He possesses 'saṃ', the state of lordship, thus he is 'sāmī' or 'suvāmī'. In the feminine, 'sāminī' and 'suvāminī'. With elision of the bindu and the augment 'ka', it becomes 'sāmiko'.

487. Lakkhyā ṇo a ca ka. 364; rū. 398; nī. 787; pā. 5.2.100.

487. From Lakkhī, the suffix 'ṇo', and 'ī' becomes 'a'.

Lakkhīmhā mantvatthe ṇo hoti, īkārassa attañca hoti.

From 'lakkhī', in the sense of possession, the suffix 'ṇo' occurs, and the vowel 'ī' becomes 'a'.

Lakkhī sirī etassa atthīti lakkhaṇo.

He possesses Lakkhī (fortune) and sirī (glory), thus he is 'lakkhaṇo'.

488. Aṅgā no kalyāṇe ka. 364; rū. 398; nī. 787; pā. 5.2.100.

488. From aṅga, 'no' in the sense of 'beautiful'.

Kalyāṇe vattabbe aṅgamhā mantvatthe no hoti.

When 'beautiful' is to be expressed, from 'aṅga', in the sense of possession, the suffix 'no' occurs.

Kalyāṇaṃ aṅgaṃ etissā itthiyā atthīti aṅganā.

This woman has beautiful limbs, thus she is 'aṅganā'.

489. So lomā ka. 364; rū. 398; nī. 787; caṃ. 4.2.104; pā. 5.2.100.

489. From loma, 'so'.

Lomamhā mantvatthe sapaccayo hoti.

From 'loma', in the sense of possession, the suffix 'sa' occurs.

Bahūni lomāni assa santīti lomaso. Ettha ‘so’ti suttavibhāgena “sumedhaso, bhūrimedhaso” iccādīnipi sijjhanti.

He has many hairs, thus he is 'lomaso'. Here, by analysis of the sutta 'so', forms such as 'sumedhaso' and 'bhūrimedhaso' are also accomplished.

Assatthirāsi niṭṭhito.

The Assatthirāsi section is concluded.

Bhāva, kammarāsi

The Section on State and Action.

490. Tassa [M 0.0313] bhāvakammesu tta tā ttana ṇya ṇeyyaṇiya ṇa iyā ka. 360; rū. 387; nī. 780; caṃ. 4.1.136-153; pā. 5.1.119-136.

490. In the sense of 'his state' or 'his action', the suffixes tta, tā, ttana, ṇya, ṇeyya, ṇiya, ṇa, and iyā occur.

Tassa bhāvo, tassa kammanti atthe chaṭṭhuntā ete aṭṭha paccayā bahulaṃ bhavanti.

These eight suffixes frequently occur after a word ending in the sixth case in the sense of 'his state' or 'his action'.

Tattha bhavanti buddhi, saddā etasmāti bhāvo, saddānaṃ attano atthesu ādimhi uppattikāraṇaṃ, cirakālaṃ pavattikāraṇañca. Tattha ādimhi pavattikāraṇaṃ byappattinimittaṃ nāma. Cirakālaṃ pavattikāraṇaṃ pavattinimittaṃ nāma. Tadubhayampi jāti, dabba, guṇa, kriyā, nāmavasena pañcavidhaṃ hoti.

Herein, 'bhāva' (state) is that from which intellect and sounds arise; it is the initial cause of the arising of sounds in their own meanings, and also the cause of their prolonged continuity. Among these, the initial cause of continuity is called 'byappattinimitta' (the ground for application), while the cause of prolonged continuity is called 'pavattinimitta' (the ground for continued use). Both are fivefold by way of genus (jāti), substance (dabba), quality (guṇa), action (kriyā), and name (nāma).

Tattha “gossa bhāvo gotta”nti ettha gojāti bhāvo nāma.

Herein, in "the state of a cow is 'gotta'", the state is called 'cow-genus'.

“Daṇḍino bhāvo daṇḍitta”nti ettha daṇḍadabbaṃ bhāvo nāma.

In "the state of one with a staff is 'daṇḍitta'", the state is called 'the substance of a staff'.

“Nīlassa paṭassa bhāvo nīlatta”nti ettha nīlaguṇo bhāvo nāma.

In "the state of a blue cloth is 'nīlatta'", the state is called 'the quality of blue'.

“Pācakassa bhāvo pācakatta”nti ettha pacanakriyā bhāvo nāma.

In "the state of a cook is 'pācakatta'", the state is called 'the action of cooking'.

“Tissanāmassa janassa bhāvo tissatta”nti ettha tissanāmaṃ bhāvo nāma.

In "the state of a person named Tissa is 'tissatta'", the state is called 'the name Tissa'.

Tattha gossa bhāvoti gosaddaṃ sutvā godabbe gobuddhiyā vā godabbaṃ disvā tasmiṃ dabbe govohārassa vā pavattikāraṇanti attho. Evaṃ sesesupi yathānurūpaṃ attho veditabbo.

Herein, 'the state of a cow' means the cause for the continuity of the convention 'cow' (govohāra) in that substance, which arises from hearing the word 'cow', from the concept of a cow in the cow-substance, or from seeing the cow-substance. Similarly, the meaning should be understood for the rest accordingly.

Ttamhi-gottaṃ, daṇḍittaṃ, pācakattaṃ, tissattaṃ iccādi.

With the suffix '-tta': 'gotta' (lineage), 'daṇḍitta' (the state of having a staff), 'pācakatta' (the state of being a cook), 'tissatta' (the state of being Tissa), etc.

Tāmhi-saṅgaṇikārāmatā[M 0.0314], niddārāmatā, bhassārāmatā iccādi.

With the suffix '-tā': 'saṅgaṇikārāmatā' (fondness for company), 'niddārāmatā' (fondness for sleep), 'bhassārāmatā' (fondness for talk), etc.

Ttanamhi-puthujjanattanaṃ, vedanattanaṃ, jārattanaṃ, jāyattanaṃ iccādi.

With the suffix '-ttana': 'puthujjanattanaṃ' (the state of an ordinary person), 'vedanattanaṃ' (the state of feeling), 'jārattanaṃ' (the state of being a paramour), 'jāyattanaṃ' (the state of being a wife), etc.

Ṇyamhi-alasassa bhāvo ālasyaṃ, samaṇassa bhāvo sāmaññaṃ, brāhmaṇassa bhāvo brāhmaññaṃ, sīlasamādhipaññāguṇo sāmaññañca brāhmaññañca nāma. Tāpasassa bhāvo tāpasyaṃ, nipuṇassa bhāvo nepuññaṃ, vipulassa bhāvo vepullaṃ, rañño bhāvo rajjaṃ, āpabbatassa khettassa bhāvo āpabbatyaṃ, dāyādassa bhāvo dāyajjaṃ, visamassa bhāvo vesammaṃ, sakhino bhāvo sakhyaṃ, vāṇijānaṃ bhāvo vāṇijjaṃ iccādi.

With the suffix '-ṇya': the state of a lazy person is 'ālasyaṃ' (laziness); the state of a recluse is 'sāmaññaṃ' (recluseship); the state of a brahmin is 'brāhmaññaṃ' (the state of a brahmin). The qualities of virtue, concentration, and wisdom are also called 'sāmaññaṃ' and 'brāhmaññaṃ'. The state of an ascetic is 'tāpasyaṃ' (asceticism); the state of a skillful person is 'nepuññaṃ' (skillfulness); the state of being abundant is 'vepullaṃ' (abundance); the state of a king is 'rajjaṃ' (kingship); the state of a field near a mountain is 'āpabbatyaṃ'; the state of an heir is 'dāyajjaṃ' (inheritance); the state of being uneven is 'vesammaṃ' (unevenness); the state of a friend is 'sakhyaṃ' (friendship); the state of merchants is 'vāṇijjaṃ' (commerce), etc.

Ṇeyyamhi – sucissa bhāvo soceyyaṃ. Evaṃ ādhipateyyaṃ iccādi.

With the suffix '-ṇeyya': the state of a pure person is 'soceyyaṃ' (purity). Similarly, 'ādhipateyyaṃ' (lordship), etc.

Ṇiyamhi-ālasiyaṃ, madabhāvo madiyaṃ. Evaṃ dakkhiyaṃ, purohitabhāvo porohitiyaṃ, byattassa bhāvo veyyattiyaṃ, byāvaṭassa bhāvo veyyāvaṭiyaṃ, imāni dve pubbe veyyākaraṇapadaṃ viya siddhāni.

With the suffix '-ṇiya': 'ālasiyaṃ' (laziness); the state of intoxication is 'madiyaṃ'. Similarly, 'dakkhiyaṃ' (skill); the state of a royal chaplain is 'porohitiyaṃ' (the office of a royal chaplain); the state of an expert is 'veyyattiyaṃ' (expertise); the state of being diligent is 'veyyāvaṭiyaṃ' (diligence). These last two are formed like a previous grammatical term.

Ṇamhi-garuno bhāvo gāravo, paṭubhāvo pāṭavaṃ iccādi.

With the suffix '-ṇa': the state of a respected one is 'gāravo' (respect); the state of being clever is 'pāṭavaṃ' (cleverness), etc.

Iyamhi-adhipatibhāvo adhipatiyaṃ, paṇḍitabhāvo paṇḍitiyaṃ, bahussutabhāvo bahussutiyaṃ, naggassa bhāvo naggiyaṃ, sūrabhāvo sūriyaṃ, vīrabhāvo vīriyaṃ iccādi.

With the suffix '-iya': the state of being a master is 'adhipatiyaṃ' (mastery); the state of being wise is 'paṇḍitiyaṃ' (wisdom); the state of being learned is 'bahussutiyaṃ' (great learning); the state of a naked person is 'naggiyaṃ' (nakedness); the state of being brave is 'sūriyaṃ' (bravery); the state of being heroic is 'vīriyaṃ' (heroism), etc.

Kammatthe kammaṃ nāma kriyā, alasassa kammaṃ alasattaṃ, alasatā, alasattanaṃ, ālasyaṃ, ālaseyyaṃ, ālasiyaṃ, ālasaṃ, alasiyaṃ iccādi.

In the sense of action, 'kamma' means 'action' (kriyā). The action of a lazy person is 'alasattaṃ', 'alasatā', 'alasattanaṃ', 'ālasyaṃ', 'ālaseyyaṃ', 'ālasiyaṃ', 'ālasaṃ', 'alasiyaṃ', etc.

491. Bya vaddhadāsā vā ka. 360; rū. 387; nī. 780.

491. From 'vaddha' and 'dāsa', the suffix 'bya' occurs optionally.

Bhāva[M 0.0315], kammesu vaddha, dāsehi byo hoti vā.

In the sense of state or action, from 'vaddha' and 'dāsa', the suffix 'bya' occurs optionally.

Vaddhassa bhāvo kammaṃ vā vaddhabyaṃ, vaddhatā, dāsabyaṃ, dāsatā, ‘vaddhava’nti idha ṇe pare vāgamo.

The state or action of an elder is 'vaddhabyaṃ' or 'vaddhatā'; the state or action of a slave is 'dāsabyaṃ' or 'dāsatā'. Here, in 'vaddhava', the insertion of 'va' occurs when 'ṇa' follows.

492. Naṇa yuvā bo ca vaye ka. 361; rū. 388; nī. 781; caṃ. 4.1.146; pā. 5.1.130; ‘…vassa’ (bahūsu).

492. From 'yuvan', in the sense of age, the suffix 'ṇa' and the insertion 'ba' occur.

Vaye gamyamāne bhāva, kammesu yuvato naṇa hoti vā bāgamo ca.

When age is expressed, in the sense of state or action, from 'yuvan' the suffix 'ṇa' occurs optionally, and there is an insertion of 'ba'.

Yuvassa bhāvo yobbanaṃ.

The state of a youth is 'yobbanaṃ'.

Vātveva? Yuvattaṃ, yuvatā.

Is it optional? Yes, hence also 'yuvattaṃ' and 'yuvatā'.

493. Aṇvādīhimo ka. 360; rū. 387; nī. 780; caṃ. 4.1.139; pā. 5.1.122; ‘aṇvāditvimo’ (bahūsu).

493. From 'aṇu' and so on, the suffix 'ima' occurs.

Tehi bhāve imo hoti vā.

From those words, in the sense of state, the suffix 'ima' occurs optionally.

Aṇuno bhāvo aṇimā, laghuno bhāvo laghimā.

The state of being minute is 'aṇimā'; the state of being light is 'laghimā'.

494. Kassamahatamime kasamahā ka. 404; rū. 370; ni. 859; ‘kassaka…’?.

494. Before the suffix 'ima', 'kisa' and 'mahat' are replaced by 'kasa' and 'maha'.

Imapaccaye pare kassa, mahantasaddānaṃ kamena kasa, mahā honti.

When this suffix follows, the words kassa and mahanta become kasa and mahā respectively.

Kassakassa kammaṃ kasimā (kisamahatamime kasamahā. imapaccaye pare kisa, mahanthasaddānaṃ kamena kasa, mahā honthi. kisassa bhāvo kasimā, moga. 4-133), mahantassa bhāvo mahimā. Sumanassa bhāvo somanassaṃ, ṇyamhi sāgamo, ‘vaggalasehi te’ti yassa pararūpattaṃ. Evaṃ domanassaṃ, sundaraṃ vaco [M 0.0316] etasminti suvaco, suvacassa bhāvo sovacassaṃ. Evaṃ dovacassaṃ.

The work of a farmer is kasimā; the state of greatness is mahimā. The state of a joyful mind is somanassaṃ; when the ṇya suffix follows, there is an augment of 's', and by 'vaggalasehi te', the 'y' is assimilated into the preceding consonant. Similarly, domanassaṃ. One whose speech is beautiful is suvaco; the state of being of good speech is sovacassaṃ. Similarly, dovacassaṃ.

“Ārāmarāmaṇeyyakaṃ, uyyānarāmaṇeyyakaṃ, bhūmirāmaṇeyyakaṃ” iccādīsu ramitabbanti ramaṇaṃ, ramaṇaṃ ettha atthīti rāmaṇo, ārāmo, ārāmarāmaṇassa bhāvo ārāmarāmaṇeyyakaṃ, ṇeyyo, sakatthe ca ko kathaṃ rāmaṇiyakatthi? sakatthe kanthā ṇena siddhaṃ, (moga. 4-59), ārāmasampatti, ārāmasirīti vuttaṃ hoti. Evaṃ sesesu.

In phrases like "ārāmarāmaṇeyyakaṃ, uyyānarāmaṇeyyakaṃ, bhūmirāmaṇeyyakaṃ," that which delights is ramaṇaṃ. Where delight exists is rāmaṇo, a park. The state of a delightful park is ārāmarāmaṇeyyakaṃ, formed with the suffix ṇeyya. The suffix ka is used in its own sense—it is said to mean ārāmasampatti, ārāmasirī. Similarly for the rest.

Bhāva, kammarāsi niṭṭhito.

The section on states and actions is concluded.

Parimāṇarāsi

The Section on Measure

495. Tamassa parimāṇaṃ ṇiko ca ka. 351; rū. 374; nī. 764; caṃ. 4.1.62; pā. 5.1.57, 58.

495. In the sense of 'that is its measure,' the suffix ṇika and also ka.

Taṃ assa parimāṇanti atthe paṭhamantā ṇiko hoti ko ca. Parimīyate anenāti parimāṇaṃ.

In the sense of 'that is its measure,' the suffix ṇika and also ka are added to a word in the nominative case. That by which something is measured is parimāṇa.

Doṇo parimāṇamassāti doṇiko. Evaṃ khāriko, kumbhiko, asītivassāni parimāṇamassāti āsītiko, vayo. Evaṃ nāvutiko, upaḍḍhakāyo parimāṇamassāti upaḍḍhakāyikaṃ, bimbohanaṃ, dve parimāṇamassāti dukaṃ. Evaṃ tikaṃ, catukkaṃ, pañcakaṃ, chakkaṃ, dvittaṃ. Dasakaṃ, satakaṃ.

A doṇa is its measure, thus doṇiko. Similarly, khāriko, kumbhiko. Eighty years is its measure, thus āsītiko, referring to age. Similarly, nāvutiko. Half the body is its measure, thus upaḍḍhakāyikaṃ, referring to a cushion. Two is its measure, thus dukaṃ. Similarly, tikaṃ, catukkaṃ, pañcakaṃ, chakkaṃ, dvittaṃ, dasakaṃ, satakaṃ.

496. Yatetehi ttako ka. 391; rū. 423; nī. 830; pā. 5.1.22, 23

496. After ya, ta, and eta, the suffix ttaka.

Tamassa parimāṇanti atthe ya, ta, etasaddehi sadisadvibhūto ttako hoti.

In the sense of 'that is its measure,' the suffix ttaka occurs after the words ya, ta, and eta, which are similar in form.

Yaṃ parimāṇamassāti yattakaṃ. Evaṃ tattakaṃ.

Whatever measure it has, that is yattakaṃ. Similarly, tattakaṃ.

497. Etasseṭa ttake ka. 404; rū. 370; nī. 859.

497. Eṭa is substituted for eta when ttaka follows.

Ttake [M 0.0317] pare etasaddassa eṭa hoti.

When ttaka follows, eṭa is substituted for eta.

Etaṃ parimāṇamassāti ettakaṃ, yāva parimāṇamassāti yāvattakaṃ. Evaṃ tāvattakaṃ, etāvattakaṃ. ‘Yatetehī’ti vacanena yāva, tāva, etāvāpi gayhanti.

This is its measure—ettakaṃ (so much); as far as its measure—yāvattakaṃ (so much). Likewise, tāvattakaṃ, etāvattakaṃ. By the expression ‘yatetehī’, yāva, tāva, and etāva are also included.

498. Sabbā ca ṭāvantu ka. 391; rū. 423; nī. 830; caṃ. 4.2.43; pā. 5.2.39; ‘sabbā cacavantu’ (bahūsu).

498. And after sabba, the suffix ṭāvantu.

Tamassa parimāṇanti atthe ya, te’tehi ca sabbato ca ṭāvantu hoti, etassa dvittaṃ.

In the sense of 'that is its measure,' the suffix ṭāvantu occurs after ya, ta, eta, and sabba; and for eta, there is doubling.

Sabbaṃ parimāṇaṃ assāti sabbāvantaṃ, sabbāvā, attho, sabbāvanto, sabbāvantā, atthā, sabbāvati, atthe, sabbāvantesu, atthesu, itthiyaṃ sabbāvatī, sabbāvantī, parisā. Evaṃ yāvā, yāvantā, yāvanto, tāvā, tāvantā, tāvanto, ettāvā, ettāvantā, ettāvanto iccādi.

All is its measure, thus sabbāvantaṃ. For example: sabbāvā attho (a whole thing); sabbāvanto, sabbāvantā atthā (a whole thing, whole things); sabbāvati atthe (in a whole thing); sabbāvantesu atthesu (in whole things). In the feminine, sabbāvatī, sabbāvantī, as in a `parisā` (assembly). Similarly yāvā, yāvantā, yāvanto, tāvā, tāvantā, tāvanto, ettāvā, ettāvantā, ettāvanto, etc.

Kvaci mahāvuttinā ekassa ta-kārassa lopo, yāvatako kāyo, tāvatako byāmo dī. ni. 3.200, yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi.

Sometimes, according to the Mahāvutti, one letter 'ta' is elided, as in: 'yāvatako kāyo, tāvatako byāmo,' and 'yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi.'

499. Kiṃmhā rati rīva rīvataka rittakā ka. 391; rū. 423; nī. 830; caṃ. 4.2.45; pā. 5.2.41.

499. After kiṃ, the suffixes rati, rīva, rīvataka, and rittakā.

Taṃ assa parimāṇanti atthe kiṃsaddato ete cattāro paccayā bhavanti.

In the sense of 'that is its measure,' these four suffixes occur after the word 'kiṃ'.

500. Rānubandhentasarādissa ka. 539; rū. 558; nī. 1124.

500. When `ra` is an anubandha, there is elision of the final vowel and consonant.

Rānubandhe [M 0.0318] paccaye pare padantasarādissa lopo hoti. Ādisaddena padantabyañjanaṃ gayhati, suttavibhattena rīvantu, rittāvantupaccayā ca honti.

When a suffix with `ra` as an anubandha follows, elision of the final vowel and consonant of the word occurs. By the term `ādi`, a final consonant of a word is included. By the force of the sutta, the suffixes rīvantu and rittāvantu also occur.

Kiṃ parimāṇamassāti kati. Pañcakkhandhā kati kusalā, kati akusalā vibha. 151, kativassosi tvaṃ bhikkhu, ekavasso ahaṃ bhagavā mahāva. 78, kiṃ parimāṇaṃ assāti kīvaṃ, kiṃva dūro ito gāmo. Evaṃ kīvatakaṃ, kittakaṃ.

What is its measure? Thus kati (how many). 'Of the five aggregates, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome?' 'How many years have you been a monk?' 'I have been one year, Blessed One.' What is its measure? Thus kīvaṃ (how much/far). 'How far is the village from here?' Similarly, kīvatakaṃ, kittakaṃ.

Rīvantumhi – kīvanto hontu yācakā jā. 2.20.103 ti.

With rīvantu: "How many should the beggars be?"

Rittāvantumhi – kittāvatā khandhānaṃ khandhapaññatti saṃ. ni. 3.82, kittāvatā nu kho bhante rūpanti vuccati, kittāvatā nu kho bhante māroti vuccati saṃ. ni. 3.161.

With rittāvantu: "To what extent is there designation of aggregates?" "To what extent, venerable sir, is it said to be 'form'?" "To what extent, venerable sir, is it said to be 'Māra'?"

Pubbasuttena ṭāvantumhi – ettāvatā khandhānaṃ khandhapaññatti, ettāvatā rūpanti vuccati, ettāvatā māroti vuccati.

By the previous sutta, with ṭāvantu: 'To this extent there is designation of aggregates; to this extent it is called form; to this extent it is called Māra.'

501. Māne matto ka. 328; rū. 352; nī. 708; caṃ. 4.2.38; pā. 5.2.37.

501. In the sense of measure, the suffix matta.

Mīyate etenāti mānaṃ, taṃ ummānaṃ, parimāṇanti duvidhaṃ, uddhaṃ mānaṃ ummānaṃ, tadaññaṃ mānaṃ parimāṇaṃ, imasmiṃ sutte pana sāmaññavacanattā duvidhampi labbhati, duvidhe māne pavattā hatthādisaddamhā tamassa parimāṇanti atthe mattapaccayo hoti.

That by which it is measured is māna. That is twofold: ummāna and parimāṇa. Upward measure is ummāna; the other measure is parimāṇa. In this sutta, however, due to the general expression, both are included. When referring to these two kinds of measure, the suffix matta occurs after words like hattha, etc., in the sense of 'that is its measure.'

Hattho parimāṇaṃ assāti hatthamattaṃ, dve hatthā parimāṇaṃ assāti dvihatthamattaṃ, dve aṅguliyo parimāṇaṃ assāti dvaṅgulamattaṃ. Evaṃ caturaṅgulamattaṃ, vidatthimattaṃ, yojanamattaṃ[M 0.0319], tīṇi yojanāni parimāṇaṃ assāti tiyojanamattaṃ, nāḷimattaṃ, patthamattaṃ, doṇamattaṃ, palaṃ vuccati ummānasaṅkhāto pātiviseso, palaṃ parimāṇaṃ assāti palamattaṃ, pañcamattaṃ, pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi saddhiṃ pārā. 1, tiṃsamattaṃ, saṭṭhimattaṃ, satamattaṃ, sahassamattaṃ, koṭimattaṃ, kumbhamattaṃ, cāṭimattaṃ, hatthimattaṃ, pabbatamattaṃ iccādi.

A hand is its measure, thus hatthamattaṃ; two hands are its measure, thus dvihatthamattaṃ; two fingers are its measure, thus dvaṅgulamattaṃ. Similarly, caturaṅgulamattaṃ, vidatthimattaṃ, yojanamattaṃ. Three leagues are its measure, thus tiyojanamattaṃ. Nāḷimattaṃ, patthamattaṃ, doṇamattaṃ. A pala is called a specific type of weight measure. A pala is its measure, thus palamattaṃ. Pañcamattaṃ, as in `pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi saddhiṃ` (together with five hundred bhikkhus). Tiṃsamattaṃ, saṭṭhimattaṃ, satamattaṃ, sahassamattaṃ, koṭimattaṃ, kumbhamattaṃ, cāṭimattaṃ, hatthimattaṃ, pabbatamattaṃ, etc.

‘Mattā’ti vā parimāṇavācisaddantaraṃ, hattho mattā etassāti hatthamattaṃ. Evaṃ dvihatthamattaṃ, iccādinā samāsopi yujjati. Abhedūpacārena pana hatthaparimāṇaṃ hatthoti katvā “dvihatthaṃ vatthaṃ, doṇo vīhi, doṇo māso”ti sijjhati.

Alternatively, 'mattā' is another word meaning measure. 'A hand is its measure' is hatthamattaṃ. Similarly, compounds like 'dvihatthamattaṃ', and so on, are formed. However, by way of a figurative expression of non-difference, treating 'the measure of a hand' as 'hand', expressions like "dvihatthaṃ vatthaṃ (a two-hand cloth)," "doṇo vīhi (a doṇa of rice)," and "doṇo māso (a doṇa of beans)" are valid.

502. Taggho cuddhaṃ ka. 328; rū. 352; nī. 708; caṃ. 4.2.39; pā. 5.2.37.

502. And the suffix taggha for upward measure.

Uddhaṃmāne pavattā saddā tamassa parimāṇanti atthe tagghapaccayo hoti matto ca.

From words occurring in the sense of upward measure, in the sense of 'that is its measure,' the suffix taggha occurs, and also matta.

Jaṇṇu parimāṇamassāti jaṇṇutagghaṃ, jaṇṇumattaṃ.

In the sense 'the knee is its measure,' the forms are jaṇṇutagghaṃ and jaṇṇumattaṃ.

503. Ṇo ca purisā ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765; caṃ. 4.2.40 …pe… 5.2.38.

503. And ṇa after the word purisa.

Uddhaṃmāne pavattā purisamhā ṇo ca hoti taggho ca matto ca.

In the sense of upward measure, after the word purisa, the suffix ṇa occurs, and also taggha, and also matta.

Catuhattho puriso parimāṇamassāti porisaṃ, tiporisaṃ, sataporisaṃ, gambhīraṃ. Evaṃ purisatagghaṃ, purisamattaṃ, uddhaṃ pasāritahatthena saddhiṃ pañcahatthaṃ purisapamāṇaṃ porisanti vadanti, “ekūnatīso vayasā”ti dī. ni. 2.214 (ekūnatiṃso) ettha ekūnatīsa vassāni āyuparimāṇaṃ assāti ekūnatīso. Evaṃ [M 0.0320] vīso, tīso, cattālīso, paññāso, sahasso brahmā, dvisahasso brahmā, dasasahasso brahmā. Ettha ca “sahassaparimāṇaṃ cakkavāḷaṃ assāti sahasso”-iccādinā ṇapaccayena sijjhati.

A man of four cubits is its measure, thus porisaṃ; three porisas deep, a hundred porisas deep. Similarly, purisatagghaṃ, purisamattaṃ. They say that a man's measure, a porisa, is five cubits including the hand stretched upwards. Here, in 'ekūnatīso vayasā' (twenty-nine years of age), the derivation is 'twenty-nine years is its measure of life,' thus ekūnatīso. Similarly, vīso, tīso, cattālīso, paññāso. The thousand-fold Brahmā, the two-thousand-fold Brahmā, the ten-thousand-fold Brahmā. And here, the formation is accomplished by the suffix ṇa in such cases as 'a thousand is the measure of his world-system, thus sahasso'.

Parimāṇarāsi niṭṭhito.

The section on measure is concluded.

Saṅkhyārāsi

The Section on Numerals

504. Ekā kākyasahāye ka. 391; rū. 423; nī. 835; caṃ. 4.2.67; pā. 5.3.52.

504. From eka, the suffixes ka and ākī are used in the sense of 'without a companion'.

Asahāyatthe ekamhā ka, ākī honti vā.

In the sense of 'without a companion', the suffixes ka and ākī are optionally affixed to eka.

Asahāyo eko, ekako, ekākī, eko vā.

One without a companion is expressed as: eko, ekako, ekākī, or eko.

Itthiyaṃ ekikā, ekākinī, ekā vā, ‘adhātussa ke’ti suttena itthiyaṃ kamhi pare assa ittaṃ.

In the feminine: ekikā, ekākinī, or ekā. By the rule 'adhātussa ke', when the suffix ka follows a non-root stem, its final 'a' becomes 'i' in the feminine.

505. Dviti catūhi tīyatthā ka. 385; rū. 409; nī. 817; tisatthā?.

505. From dvi, ti, and catu, the suffixes tīya and ttha are used.

Tehi tassa pūraṇanti atthe tīyo ca ttho ca honti.

From them, in the sense of 'its completion' (forming an ordinal number), the suffixes tīya and ttha occur.

506. Dvitīnaṃ dutā tīye ka. 386, 410; nī. 818; tiye?.

506. For dvi and ti, du and ta are substituted when the suffix tīya follows.

Tīye pare dvi, tisaddānaṃ du, tādesā honti.

When tīya follows, du and ta are the respective substitutes for the words dvi and ti.

Dvinnaṃ pūraṇo dutīyo chaṭṭhasaṃgīti pāṭhesu dutiyotyādinā dissanti, dvinnaṃ pūraṇī dutīyā, dvinnaṃ pūraṇaṃ dutīyaṃ. Evaṃ tatīyo, tatīyā, tatīyaṃ. Catunnaṃ pūraṇo catuttho, catutthī, catutthaṃ.

The ordinal of two is dutīyo (masculine), dutīyā (feminine), dutīyaṃ (neuter). Similarly, tatīyo, tatīyā, tatīyaṃ (third). The ordinal of four is catuttho, catutthī, catutthaṃ.

507. Ma pañcādikatihi ka. 373; rū. 406; nī. 802; caṃ. 4.2.55; pā. 5.2.49.

507. The suffix ma is used after five onwards and after kati.

Pañcādīhi [M 0.0321] ca katimhā ca tassa pūraṇanti atthe mo hoti.

After the numbers from five onwards and after kati, in the sense of 'its completion' (forming an ordinal number), the suffix ma occurs.

Pañcamo, pañcamī, pañcamaṃ. Evaṃ sattama, aṭṭhama, navama, dasama, ekādasamādi. Katinnaṃ pūraṇo katimo, katimī, tithī.

Pañcamo (m.), pañcamī (f.), pañcamaṃ (n.). Similarly, sattama, aṭṭhama, navama, dasama, ekādasama, and so on. The ordinal of 'how many' is katimo, katimī; also tithī (a lunar day).

508. Tassa pūraṇekādasādito vā ka. 374; rū. 412; nī. 805; caṃ. 4.2.51; pā. 5.2.48.

508. For forming its completion (ordinal), optionally from eleven onwards.

Pūrate anenāti pūraṇaṃ, ekādasādito tassa pūraṇanti atthe ṭānubandho apaccayo hoti vā.

Pūraṇaṃ is 'that by which it is completed'; from eleven onwards, in the sense of 'its completion', the suffix a, having ṭ as an indicatory letter, optionally occurs.

Ekādasannaṃ pūraṇo ekādaso, ekādasī, ekādasaṃ, ekādasamo vā. Evaṃ dvādaso, dvādasamo, teraso, terasamo, cuddaso, cuddasamo, pañcadaso, pañcadasamo, pannaraso, pannarasamo, soḷaso, soḷasamo, sattaraso, sattarasamo, aṭṭhāraso, aṭṭhārasamo.

The ordinal of eleven is ekādaso (masculine), ekādasī (feminine), ekādasaṃ (neuter), or ekādasamo. Similarly, dvādaso, dvādasamo (twelfth); teraso, terasamo (thirteenth); cuddaso, cuddasamo (fourteenth); pañcadaso, pañcadasamo (fifteenth); pannaraso, pannarasamo (fifteenth); soḷaso, soḷasamo (sixteenth); sattaraso, sattarasamo (seventeenth); aṭṭhāraso, aṭṭhārasamo (eighteenth).

509. Ṭe satissa tissa ka. 389; rū. 413; nī. 824.

509. When ṭa follows, for -sati and -ti.

Ṭe pare satissa ti-kārassa lopo hotīti vīsati, tīsatīnaṃ tissa lopo.

When ṭa follows, the syllable ti of a stem ending in -sati is elided; thus, for vīsati (twenty) and tīsati (thirty), the ti is elided.

Ekūnavīso, ekūnavīsatimo, vīso, vīsatimo, tīso, tīsatimo, cattālīso, cattālīsamo, paññāso, paññāsamo. Saṭṭhyādito purimasuttena mo, saṭṭhimo, sattatimo, asītimo, navutimo.

Ekūnavīso, ekūnavīsatimo (nineteenth); vīso, vīsatimo (twentieth); tīso, tīsatimo (thirtieth); cattālīso, cattālīsamo (fortieth); paññāso, paññāsamo (fiftieth). From sixty onwards, by the previous rule, the suffix ma occurs: saṭṭhimo (sixtieth), sattatimo (seventieth), asītimo (eightieth), navutimo (ninetieth).

510. Satādīnami ca ka. 373; rū. 406; nī. 802; caṃ. 4.2.53 …pe… 5.2.57.

510. And for sata and so on, the final vowel becomes i.

Satādito tassa pūraṇatthe mo hoti, satādīnaṃ antassa ittañca hoti.

From sata onwards, in the sense of its completion (ordinal), the suffix ma occurs, and the final vowel of sata and so on becomes i.

Satassa [M 0.0322] pūraṇo satimo, dvisatimo, tisatimo, sahassimo.

The ordinal of a hundred is satimo; dvisatimo (two-hundredth), tisatimo (three-hundredth), sahassimo (thousandth).

511. Chā ṭṭhaṭṭhamā ka. 384; rū. 407; nī. 803.

511. From cha (six), the suffixes ṭṭha and ṭṭhama occur.

Chamhā tassa pūraṇanti atthe ṭṭha, ṭṭhamā honti.

From 'cha', in the sense of its completion, the suffixes 'ṭṭha' and 'ṭṭhama' are employed.

Chaṭṭho, chaṭṭhī, chaṭṭhaṃ, chaṭṭhamo, chaṭṭhamī, chaṭṭhamaṃ.

Chaṭṭho (sixth, masculine), chaṭṭhī (sixth, feminine), chaṭṭhaṃ (sixth, neuter); chaṭṭhamo (sixth, masculine), chaṭṭhamī (sixth, feminine), chaṭṭhamaṃ (sixth, neuter).

512. Saṅkhyāya saccutīsāsadasantāyādhikāsmiṃ satasahasse ṭa ka. 328; rū. 352; nī. 701; caṃ. 4.2.50 …pe… 5.2.45, 46; ‘…ḍo’ (bahūsu).

512. From a numeral ending in 'sati', 'uti', 'īsa', 'āsa', or 'dasa', the suffix 'ṭa' is employed in the sense of being greater than a hundred or a thousand.

Sati, uti, īsa, āsa, dasantāhi saṅkhyāhi te adhikā asmiṃ satasahasseti atthe ṭānubandho apaccayo hoti.

From numerals ending in 'sati', 'uti', 'īsa', 'āsa', and 'dasa', in the sense that they are greater than a hundred or a thousand, the suffix 'a' with the indicatory letter 'ṭa' is employed.

Ettha ca ‘satasahasse’ti sate vā sahasse vāti attho.

And here, 'satasahasse' means either 'in a hundred' or 'in a thousand'.

Tattha sahassasaddena sahassaṃ dasasahassaṃ satasahassaṃ dasasatasahassañca gayhati.

Therein, by the word 'sahassa' is understood a thousand, ten thousand, a hundred thousand, and ten hundred thousand (a million).

Dasanta, satyanta, īsanta, āsanta, utyantāti evaṃ anukkamo veditabbo.

The sequence should be understood thus: ending in 'dasa', ending in 'sati', ending in 'īsa', ending in 'āsa', and ending in 'uti'.

Tattha dasa, ekādasato paṭṭhāya yāva aṭṭhārasā navasaṅkhyā dasantā nāma.

Therein, the nine numerals from ten up to eighteen are called 'dasantā' (ending in 'dasa').

Vīsati, ekavīsatito paṭṭhāya yāva aṭṭhavīsatiyā navasaṅkhyā ca tīsati, ekatīsatito paṭṭhāya yāva aṭṭhatīsatiyā navasaṅkhyā ca satyantā nāma.

The nine numerals from twenty up to twenty-eight, and the nine numerals from thirty up to thirty-eight, are called 'satyantā' (ending in 'sati').

Cattālīsa, ekacattālīsato paṭṭhāya yāva aṭṭhacattālīsāya navasaṅkhyā īsantā nāma.

The nine numerals from forty up to forty-eight are called 'īsantā' (ending in 'īsa').

Paññāsa[M 0.0323], ekapaññāsato paṭṭhāya yāva aṭṭhapaññāsāya navasaṅkhyā āsantā nāma.

The nine numerals from fifty up to fifty-eight are called 'āsantā' (ending in 'āsa').

Navuti, ekanavutito paṭṭhāya yāva aṭṭhanavutiyā nava saṅkhyā utyantā nāma.

The nine numerals from ninety up to ninety-eight are called 'utyantā' (ending in 'uti').

Sesā ṭṭhunta, tyantāpi idha saṅgayhanti. Ṭṭhuntā nāma saṭṭhi,-ekasaṭṭhyādikā navasaṅkhyā. Tyantā nāma sattati, ekasattatyādikā navasaṅkhyā ca asīti, ekāsītyādikā navasaṅkhyā ca.

The remaining numerals, those ending in 'ṭṭhu' and 'tya', are also included here. Those ending in 'ṭṭhu' are the nine numerals from sixty up to sixty-eight. Those ending in 'tya' are the nine numerals from seventy up to seventy-eight, and the nine numerals from eighty up to eighty-eight.

Dasantāsu tāva – dasa adhikā yasmiṃ sate tayidaṃ dasasataṃ. Evaṃ dasasahassaṃ, dasasatasahassaṃ, ekādasa adhikā yasmiṃ sate tayidaṃ ekādasasataṃ. Evaṃ ekādasasahassaṃ, ekādasasatasahassaṃ. Evaṃ dvādasasatamiccādīni.

First, among those ending in 'dasa': that hundred in which ten is additional is 'dasasataṃ' (one hundred and ten). Similarly, 'dasasahassaṃ' (one thousand and ten) and 'dasasatasahassaṃ' (one hundred thousand and ten). That hundred in which eleven is additional is 'ekādasasataṃ' (one hundred and eleven). Similarly, 'ekādasasahassaṃ' (one thousand and eleven) and 'ekādasasatasahassaṃ' (one hundred thousand and eleven). Likewise, 'dvādasasataṃ' (one hundred and twelve), and so on.

Satyantāsu – ṭamhi ti-kāralopo, vīsati adhikā yasmiṃ sate tayidaṃ vīsasataṃ. Evaṃ ekavīsasataṃ, dvāvīsasataṃ iccādi, tīsati adhikā yasmiṃ sate tayidaṃ tīsasataṃ. Evaṃ ekatīsasataṃ, dvattīsasataṃ iccādi. Esa nayo sahassepi.

Among those ending in 'sati': when the suffix 'ṭa' is added, the syllable 'ti' is elided. That hundred in which twenty is additional is 'vīsasataṃ' (one hundred and twenty). Similarly, 'ekavīsasataṃ' (one hundred and twenty-one), 'dvāvīsasataṃ' (one hundred and twenty-two), and so on. That hundred in which thirty is additional is 'tīsasataṃ' (one hundred and thirty). Similarly, 'ekatīsasataṃ' (one hundred and thirty-one), 'dvattīsasataṃ' (one hundred and thirty-two), and so on. This same method applies also to a thousand.

Īsantāsu – cattālīsaṃ adhikā yasmiṃ sate tayidaṃ cattālīsasataṃ. Evaṃ ekacattālīsasataṃ, dvecattālīsasataṃ iccādi. Esa nayo sahassepi.

Among those ending in 'īsa': that hundred in which forty is additional is 'cattālīsasataṃ' (one hundred and forty). Similarly, 'ekacattālīsasataṃ' (one hundred and forty-one), 'dvecattālīsasataṃ' (one hundred and forty-two), and so on. This same method applies also to a thousand.

Āsantāsu – paññāsaṃ adhikā yasmiṃ sate tayidaṃ paññāsasataṃ. Evaṃ ekapaññāsasataṃ, dvepaññāsasataṃ iccādi. Esa nayo sahassepi.

Among those ending in 'āsa': that hundred in which fifty is additional is 'paññāsasataṃ' (one hundred and fifty). Similarly, 'ekapaññāsasataṃ' (one hundred and fifty-one), 'dvepaññāsasataṃ' (one hundred and fifty-two), and so on. This same method applies also to a thousand.

Ṭṭhuntāsu – saṭṭhi adhikā yasmiṃ sate tayidaṃ saṭṭhisataṃ. Evaṃ ekasaṭṭhisataṃ, dvāsaṭṭhisataṃ iccādi. Esa nayo sahassepi.

Among those ending in 'ṭṭhu': that hundred in which sixty is additional is 'saṭṭhisataṃ' (one hundred and sixty). Similarly, 'ekasaṭṭhisataṃ' (one hundred and sixty-one), 'dvāsaṭṭhisataṃ' (one hundred and sixty-two), and so on. This same method applies also to a thousand.

Tyantāsu [M 0.0324] – sattati adhikā, ekasattati adhikā, asīti adhikā, ekāsīti adhikā iccādinā vattabbā.

Among those ending in 'tya': it should be stated in the manner of 'seventy is additional', 'seventy-one is additional', 'eighty is additional', 'eighty-one is additional', and so on.

Utyantāsu – navuti adhikā yasmiṃ sate tayidaṃ navutisataṃ. Evaṃ ekanavutisataṃ, dvenavutisataṃ iccādi. Esa nayo sahassepi.

Among those ending in 'uty': that hundred in which ninety is additional is 'navutisataṃ' (one hundred and ninety). Similarly, 'ekanavutisataṃ' (one hundred and ninety-one), 'dvenavutisataṃ' (one hundred and ninety-two), and so on. This same method applies also to a thousand.

Atha vā dasantā nāma ekato paṭṭhāya dasasaṅkhyā.

Alternatively, 'dasantā' are the ten numerals beginning from one.

Satyantā nāma ekādasato paṭṭhāya vīsasaṅkhyā.

'Satyantā' are the numerals from eleven up to twenty.

Īsantā nāma ekatīsato paṭṭhāya dasasaṅkhyā.

'Īsantā' are the ten numerals beginning from thirty-one.

Āsantā nāma ekacattālīsato paṭṭhāya dasasaṅkhyā.

'Āsantā' are the ten numerals beginning from forty-one.

Evaṃ ṭṭhunta, tyanta, utyantāpi veditabbā.

Thus, those numerals ending in 'ṭṭhu', 'tya', and 'uty' should also be understood.

Eko adhiko yasmiṃ sate tayidaṃ ekasataṃ, “athetthekasataṃ khatyā, anuyantā yasassino”ti jā. 2.22.594 pāḷi. “Dve adhikā yasmiṃ sate tayidaṃ dvisataṃ” iccādinā sabbaṃ vattabbaṃ, suvicittamidaṃ vidhānanti.

That hundred in which one is additional is 'ekasataṃ' (one hundred and one). The Pāli text states: 'Then here there were one hundred and one Khattiyas, glorious followers.' 'That hundred in which two are additional is dvisataṃ (one hundred and two),' and so forth, all should be stated. This arrangement is very diverse.

Yathā pana “eko ca dasa ca ekādasa, ekādhikā vā dasa ekādasā”ti sijjhati, tathā idhapi “dasa ca satañca dasasataṃ, dasādhikaṃ vā sataṃ dasasata”ntiādinā vutte sabbaṃ taṃ vidhānaṃ samāsavasena sijjhati.

Just as 'one and ten are eleven' (eko ca dasa ca ekādasa), or 'ten with one additional is eleven' (ekādhikā vā dasa ekādasā) is formed, so too here, when it is said 'ten and a hundred are one hundred and ten' (dasa ca satañca dasasataṃ), or 'a hundred with ten additional is one hundred and ten' (dasādhikaṃ vā sataṃ dasasataṃ), and so forth, all such arrangements are formed by way of compound.

Tattha pana “dve satāni dvisataṃ, tīṇi satāni tisata”miccādīni ca “dve sahassāni dvisahassaṃ, tīṇi sahassāni tisahassa”miccādīni ca “dve satasahassāni dvisatasahassaṃ, tīṇi satasahassāni tisatasahassa”miccādīni ca digusamāse sijjhanti.

Here, however, expressions such as 'two hundreds, dvisataṃ', 'three hundreds, tisataṃ', and so forth; and 'two thousands, dvisahassaṃ', 'three thousands, tisahassaṃ', and so forth; and 'two hundred thousands, dvisatasahassaṃ', 'three hundred thousands, tisatasahassaṃ', and so forth, are formed as digu compounds.

513. Vārasaṅkhyāyakkhattuṃ ka. 646; rū. 419; nī. 1282; caṃ. 4.4.5; pā. 5.4.17.

513. From a numeral of frequency, the suffix 'kkhattuṃ' is employed.

Vārasambandhibhūtā saṅkhyāsaddā kkhattuṃpaccayo hoti.

From a numeral word related to repetition, the suffix 'kkhattuṃ' is employed.

Dve [M 0.0325] vārā dvikkhattuṃ. Evaṃ tikkhattuṃ, catukkhattuṃ, pañcakkhattuṃ, dasakkhattuṃ, satakkhattuṃ, sahassakkhattuṃ.

Two times becomes dvikkhattuṃ. Thus, tikkhattuṃ (three times), catukkhattuṃ (four times), pañcakkhattuṃ (five times), dasakkhattuṃ (ten times), satakkhattuṃ (a hundred times), sahassakkhattuṃ (a thousand times).

514. Katimhā ka. 646; rū. 419; nī. 1282; caṃ. 4.4.6; pā. 5.4.20.

514. From the word kati.

Vārasambandhibhūtā katisaddā kkhattuṃ hoti. Kati vārā katikkhattuṃ.

From the word kati, when related to repetition, the suffix -kkhattuṃ occurs. Thus, kati vārā becomes katikkhattuṃ.

515. Bahumhā dhā ca paccāsattiyā ka. 646; rū. 419; nī. 1282; ‘paccāsattiyaṃ’ (bahūsu).

515. From the word bahu, and the suffix dhā, due to proximity.

Vārasambandhibhūtā bahusaddā paccāsattiyā sati dhā ca hoti kkhattuñca.

From the word bahu, when related to repetition and when there is proximity, the suffix dhā occurs, and also kkhattuṃ.

Bahuvārā bahukkhattuṃ, bahusaddena anekavāraṃ upalakkheti, anekavārā anekakkhattuṃ. Evaṃ bahuvārā bahudhā, anekavārā anekadhā. Paccāsatti nāma vārānaṃ accāsannatā vuccati, divasassa bahukkhattuṃ bhuñjati, bahudhā bhuñjati, vārānaṃ dūrabhāve sati te paccayā na honti, māsassa bahuvāre bhuñjati.

Many times becomes bahukkhattuṃ. By the word bahu, numerous instances are indicated, so numerous times becomes anekakkhattuṃ. Thus, many times becomes bahudhā, and numerous times becomes anekadhā. Proximity is called the extreme nearness of the instances. For example, 'He eats many times in a day' (divasassa bahukkhattuṃ bhuñjati), 'He eats many times' (bahudhā bhuñjati). When there is remoteness of the instances, those suffixes do not occur. For example, 'He eats many times in a month' (māsassa bahuvāre bhuñjati).

516. Sakiṃ vā ka. 646; rū. 419; nī. 1282; caṃ. 4.4.8; pā. 5.4.19.

516. Or sakiṃ.

Ekavāranti atthe sakinti nipaccate vā.

In the sense of 'one time,' the indeclinable sakiṃ is optionally formed.

Sakiṃ bhuñjati, ekavāraṃ bhuñjati.

He eats once (sakiṃ bhuñjati), he eats one time (ekavāraṃ bhuñjati).

Saṅkhyārāsi niṭṭhito.

The Section on Numbers is concluded.

Khuddakarāsi

The Minor Section

Pakārarāsi

The Section on Varieties

517. Dhā [M 0.0326] saṅkhyāhi ka. 397; rū. 420; nī. 836; caṃ. 4.3.20; pā. 5.3.42.

517. The suffix dhā from numbers.

Saṅkhyāvācīhi pakāre dhā hoti.

From number-denoting words, the suffix dhā occurs in the sense of variety.

Dvīhi pakārehi dvidhā. Evaṃ tidhā, catudhā, pañcadhā, dasadhā, satadhā, sahassadhā, bahudhā, ekadhā, anekadhā.

By two kinds becomes dvidhā. Thus, tidhā (threefold), catudhā (fourfold), pañcadhā (fivefold), dasadhā (tenfold), satadhā (a hundredfold), sahassadhā (a thousandfold), bahudhā (manifold), ekadhā (onefold), anekadhā (manifold).

518. Vekā jjhaṃ ka. 397; rū. 420; nī. 837; caṃ. 4.3.24; pā. 5.3.46.

518. Optionally, the suffix jjhaṃ from the word eka.

Ekamhā pakāre jjhaṃ hoti vā.

From the word eka, the suffix jjhaṃ optionally occurs in the sense of variety.

Ekena pakārena ekajjhaṃ, ekadhā vā.

By one manner becomes ekajjhaṃ, or ekadhā.

519. Dvitīhedhā ka. 404; rū. 420-370; nī. 859; caṃ. 4.3.24; pā. 5.3.46.

519. The suffix edhā from the words dvi and ti.

Dvitisaddehi pakāre edhā hoti vā.

From the words dvi and ti, the suffix edhā optionally occurs in the sense of variety.

Dvedhā, tedhā, dvidhā, tidhā vā.

Dvedhā, tedhā, or dvidhā, tidhā.

520. Sabbādīhi pakāre thā ka. 398; rū. 421; nī. 844; caṃ. 4.3.26; pā. 5.3.69.

520. The suffix thā from the words sabba and so forth.

Bahubhedo vā sāmaññassa bhedako viseso vā pakāro, sabbādīhi pakāre thā hoti.

Variety (pakāra) is a manifold division, or a specific distinction that differentiates a generality. From the words sabba and so forth, the suffix thā occurs in the sense of variety.

Sabbena pakārena sabbathā, sabbehi pakārehi sabbathā, yādisena pakārena yathā, yādisehi pakārehi yathā. Evaṃ tathā, aññathā, ubhayathā, itarathā.

By every manner becomes sabbathā; by all manners becomes sabbathā. By which manner becomes yathā; by which manners becomes yathā. Thus, tathā (so), aññathā (otherwise), ubhayathā (in both ways), itarathā (in another way).

521. Kathamitthaṃ ka. 399; rū. 422; nī. 845; pā. 5.3.24, 25.

521. Kathaṃ and itthaṃ.

Ete [M 0.0327] saddā pakāre nipaccanti.

These words are formed as indeclinables in the sense of variety.

Kena pakārena kathaṃ, iminā pakārena itthaṃ. Iminā suttena kiṃ, imasaddehi thaṃ, tthaṃpaccaye katvā kiṃssa kattaṃ, imassa ittañca kariyati.

By what manner becomes kathaṃ; by this manner becomes itthaṃ. By this rule, from the words kiṃ and ima, the suffixes thaṃ and tthaṃ are applied, and kiṃ is changed to ka and ima is changed to it.

522. Tabbati jātiyo ka. 398; rū. 421; nī. 844; caṃ. 4.3.26; pā. 5.3.69.

522. The Tabbati-jātiya Rule.

So pakāro assa atthīti tabbā, tasmiṃ tabbati, pakāravante dabbeti attho. Taṃsāmaññavācimhā tabbati jātiyapaccayo hoti.

The sense is 'it has that characteristic' (so pakāro assa atthīti). In that sense, meaning 'in a thing possessing that characteristic' (pakāravante dabbe ti attho), the suffix jātiya occurs after a word denoting that general quality.

Visesena paṭurūpo paṇḍito paṭujātiyo. Visesena mudurūpaṃ vatthu mudujātiyaṃ.

A wise person of an especially sharp nature is paṭujātiyo. A thing of an especially soft nature is mudujātiyaṃ.

523. So vīcchāppakāresu ka. 397; rū. 420; nī. 836; caṃ. 4.4.2 …pe… 5.4.43.

523. So vīcchāppakāresu .

Vīcchāyaṃ pakāre ca sopaccayo hoti.

Vīcchāyaṃ pakāre ca sopaccayo hoti.

Vīcchāyaṃ –

Vīcchāyaṃ –

Padaṃ padaṃ vāceti padaso vāceti. Khaṇḍaṃ khaṇḍaṃ karoti khaṇḍaso karoti, bilaṃ bilaṃ vibhajjati bilaso vibhajjati iccādi. Ettha ca ‘padaṃ padaṃ’ iccādīsu kriyāvisesane dutiyā.

Padaṃ padaṃ vāceti padaso vāceti. Khaṇḍaṃ khaṇḍaṃ karoti khaṇḍaso karoti, bilaṃ bilaṃ vibhajjati bilaso vibhajjati iccādi. Ettha ca ‘padaṃ padaṃ’ iccādīsu kriyāvisesane dutiyā.

Pakāre –

Pakāre –

Bahūhi pakārehi puthuso, sabbehi pakārehi sabbaso iccādi.

Bahūhi pakārehi puthuso, sabbehi pakārehi sabbaso iccādi.

“Yoniso [M 0.0328] upāyaso, ṭhānaso, hetuso, atthaso, dhammaso, suttaso, anubyañjanaso” iccādīsu pana mahāvuttinā tatiyekavacanassa sottaṃ. Tathā dīghaso, oraso iccādi.

‘‘Yoniso upāyaso, ṭhānaso, hetuso, atthaso, dhammaso, suttaso, anubyañjanaso’’ iccādīsu pana mahāvuttinā tatiyekavacanassa sottaṃ. Tathā dīghaso, oraso iccādi.

Iti pakārarāsi.

Iti pakārarāsi.

Kularāsi

Kularāsi

524. Pitito bhātari reyyaṇa ka. 352; rū. 376; nī. 765.

524. Pitito bhātari reyyaṇa .

Pitusaddamhā tassa bhātāti atthe reyyaṇa hoti.

Pitusaddamhā tassa bhātāti atthe reyyaṇa hoti.

Pitu bhātā petteyyo a. ni. 6.44. ‘Rānubandhentasarādissā’ti ussa lopo, tassa dvittaṃ.

Pitu bhātā petteyyo . ‘Rānubandhentasarādissā’ti ussa lopo, tassa dvittaṃ.
