In the kamma construction (passive voice): By that person, enjoyment is experienced; by him, enjoyments are experienced; by him, you (singular) are experienced; by him, you (plural) are experienced; by him, I am experienced; by him, we are experienced. Where there is doubling and shortening, the forms are: anubhuyyati, anubhuyyanti.

Tattha “anubhūyatī”ti ettha kyapaccayasahitassa tisaddassa attho duvidho vāccattho, abhidheyyatthoti.

Here, in the word 'anubhūyatī', the meaning of the suffix 'ti' accompanied by the 'kya' suffix is twofold: the expressed meaning (vāccattha) and the denoted meaning (abhidheyyattha).

Tattha kammasattisaṅkhāto sakattho vāccattho nāma.

Therein, its own meaning, designated as the 'power of the object' (kammasatti), is called the expressed meaning (vāccattha).

Sattinissayo liṅgattho abhidheyyattho nāma.

The meaning of the nominal stem (liṅgattha), which is dependent on that power (satti), is called the denoted meaning (abhidheyyattha).

Tisaddo pana kyapaccayasahito vāccatthameva ujuṃ vadati, na abhidheyyatthaṃ. “Anubhūyatī”ti suṇanto sādhyakriyāsahitaṃ kammasattiṃ eva ujuṃ jānāti, na kiñci dabbanti vuttaṃ hoti. Sesaṃ pubbe vuttanayameva.

But the suffix 'ti' accompanied by the 'kya' suffix directly states only the expressed meaning (vāccattha), not the denoted meaning (abhidheyyattha). Hearing 'anubhūyatī', one directly understands only the 'power of the object' (kammasatti) associated with the action to be accomplished, and it is said that this is not any substance. The rest is according to the method stated before.

Anubhūyate[M 0.0358], anubhuyyate, anubhūyante, anubhuyyante, anubhūyase, anubhūyavhe, anubhūye, anubhuyye, anubhūyamhe, anubhuyyamhe.

anubhūyate (it is experienced), anubhuyyate (it is experienced), anubhūyante (they are experienced), anubhuyyante (they are experienced), anubhūyase (you are experienced [sg.]), anubhūyavhe (you are experienced [pl.]), anubhūye (I am experienced), anubhuyye (I am experienced), anubhūyamhe (we are experienced), anubhuyyamhe (we are experienced).

570. Garupubbā rassā re ntentīnaṃ ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105; ‘guru…’ (bahūsu).

570. After a short vowel that is preceded by a heavy syllable, 're' is the substitute for 'nte' and 'ntī'.

Garupubbamhā rassato nte, ntīnaṃ reādeso hoti.

After a short vowel that is preceded by a heavy syllable, the substitution 're' occurs for 'nte' and 'ntī'.

Jāyare, jāyanti, jāyare, jāyante, gacchare, gacchanti, gacchare, gacchante, gamissare, gamissanti, gamissare, gamissante.

jāyare (they are born), jāyanti (they are born); jāyare (they are born), jāyante (they are born); gacchare (they go), gacchanti (they go); gacchare (they go), gacchante (they go); gamissare (they will go), gamissanti (they will go); gamissare (they will go), gamissante (they will go).

Garupubbāti kiṃ? Pacanti, pacante.

Why the condition 'preceded by a heavy syllable'? For example: pacanti (they cook), pacante (they cook).

Rassāti kiṃ? Pācenti, pācante.

What is an example of non-shortening? `Pācenti` (they cause to cook), `pācante` (they cause to cook).

Ettha ca suttavibhāgena “sabbaṃ hidaṃ bhañjare kālapariyāyaṃ jā. 1.15.370, muñcare bandhanasmā jā. 2.22.1648, jīvare’ vāpi sussatī”ti jā. 2.22.840 etāni pāḷipadāni sijjhanti.

Here, by way of the Sutta analysis, these Pāli words are established: ‘Indeed, all this breaks up in due course of time, they are released from bondage, or even a living being perishes.’

Tattha ‘bhañjare’ti bhijjati, ‘muñcare’ti muñcantu, ‘jīvare’ vāpī’ti jīvanto’vāpi. Anubhūyare, anubhūyanti, anubhūyare, anubhūyante.

Here, ‘bhañjare’ means ‘bhijjati’ (it breaks); ‘muñcare’ means ‘muñcantu’ (let them be released); ‘jīvare vāpi’ means ‘jīvanto vāpi’ (or even a living being). Examples: `Anubhūyare`, `anubhūyanti`, `anubhūyare`, `anubhūyante`.

Bhāvo nāma bhavana, gamanādiko kriyākāro, so dhātunā eva tulyādhikaraṇabhāvena visesīyati, na nāmapadena, tasmā tattha tumha’mha, sesanāmavasena tyādidukavisesayogo nāma natthi, paṭhamadukameva tattha bhavati, dabbasseva ca tassa abyattasarūpattā saṅkhyābhedopi natthi, ekavacanameva bhavati.

`Bhāva` is the name for the state of becoming, the mode of action such as going and so forth. It is specified by the root itself, by way of having the same locus, not by a nominal stem. Therefore, in that case, there is no connection with the specific pairs of endings, such as `ti`, etc., which are based on the pronouns `tumha`, `amha`, and other nouns. Only the first pair (i.e., third person) occurs there. And because its own form is unmanifest, like that of a substance, there is also no distinction in number; only the singular occurs.

Tena bhogaṃ anubhūyati, anubhuyyati, anubhūyate, anubhuyyate, anubhavanaṃ hotīti attho.

By that, enjoyment is experienced (`anubhūyati`, `anubhuyyati`, `anubhūyate`, `anubhuyyate`); the meaning is ‘experiencing occurs’ (`anubhavanaṃ hoti`).

Iti suddhabhāvakammarūpāni.

Thus end the Pure Bhāva-Kamma Forms.

Hetukatturūpa

Causative Agent Forms

571. Payojakabyāpāre [M 0.0359] ṇāpi ca ka. 438; rū. 540; nī. 914.

571. And `ṇāpi` in the activity of the instigator.

Yo suddhakattāraṃ payojeti, tassa payojakassa kattuno byāpāre kriyatthā ṇi ca ṇāpi ca honti. Ṇānubandhā vuddhutthā.

He who instigates an agent—in the activity of that instigating agent, the suffixes `ṇi` and `ṇāpi` occur in the sense of action. Those with `ṇ` as an indicatory letter cause `vuddhi`.

Tesu ca ākārantato ‘ato’ (moga.) ṇāpiyeva hoti, dāpeti, dāpayati.

And among these, from roots ending in `ā`, only `ṇāpi` occurs: `dāpeti`, `dāpayati`.

Uvaṇṇantato ṇiyeva, sāveti, sāvayati.

From roots ending in `u`, only `ṇi` occurs: `sāveti`, `sāvayati`.

Sesato dvepi, pāceti, pācayati, pācāpeti, pācāpayati.

From the remaining roots, both occur: `pāceti`, `pācayati`, `pācāpeti`, `pācāpayati`.

Payojakabyāpāropi kriyā evāti tadatthavācīhi ṇi,-ṇāpīhi paraṃ vibhatti, paccayā bhavanti, dhātvantassa ca ṇi, ṇāpīnañca vuddhi.

The activity of the instigator is also indeed an action. Therefore, after `ṇi` and `ṇāpi`, which express that meaning, verbal endings (`vibhatti`) and other suffixes (`paccaya`) are applied. And `vuddhi` of the final vowel of the root is caused by `ṇi` and `ṇāpi`.

So maggaṃ bhāveti, te maggaṃ bhāventi, tvaṃ maggaṃ bhāvesi, tumhe maggaṃ bhāvetha, ahaṃ maggaṃ bhāvemi, mayaṃ maggaṃ bhāvema.

He develops the path; they develop the path; you develop the path; you all develop the path; I develop the path; we develop the path.

572. Āyāvā ṇānubandhe ka. 515; rū. 541; nī. 1029.

572. Before a `ṇ`-indicatory suffix, `āya` and `āva`.

E, onaṃ kamena āya, āvā honti sarādo ṇānubandhe paccaye pare, suttavibhattiyā aṇānubandhepi āyā’vā honti.

`E` and `o` become `āya` and `āva` respectively when a vowel-initial suffix with `ṇ` as an indicatory letter follows. By a specific rule, `āya` and `āva` also occur even when a suffix without `ṇ` as an indicatory letter follows.

Ge-sadde, gāyati, gāyanti.

From the root `ge`, in the sense of sound: `gāyati` (he sings), `gāyanti` (they sing).

Apapubbo ce-pūjāyaṃ, apacāyati, apacāyanti.

From the root `ce` preceded by `apa`, in the sense of honoring: `apacāyati` (he honors), `apacāyanti` (they honor).

Jhe-cintāyaṃ, jhāyati, jhāyanti, ujjhāyati, nijjhāyati iccādi.

From the root `jhe`, in the sense of contemplation: `jhāyati`, `jhāyanti`, `ujjhāyati`, `nijjhāyati`, and so forth.

573. Ṇiṇāpyāpīhi ca “…vā” (bahūsu).

573. And with `ṇi`, `ṇāpi`, and `āpi`.

Ṇi[M 0.0360], ṇāpi, āpīhi ca kattari lo hoti vā.

After `ṇi`, `ṇāpi`, and `āpi`, there is optional elision of the case ending of the agent.

Kārayati, kārāpayati, saddāpayati.

`Kārayati`, `kārāpayati`, `saddāpayati`.

Iminā asare ṭhāne ayādesato paraṃ akāro hoti, so maggaṃ bhāvayati, bhāvayanti, bhāvayasi, bhāvayatha, bhāvayāmi, bhāvayāma.

By this rule, when a consonant follows, the vowel `a` is inserted after the `aya` substitute. For example: `So maggaṃ bhāvayati` (he cultivates the path), `bhāvayanti` (they cultivate), `bhāvayasi` (you cultivate), `bhāvayatha` (you all cultivate), `bhāvayāmi` (I cultivate), `bhāvayāma` (we cultivate).

Iti hetukatturūpāni.

Thus end the Causative Agent Forms.

Tyādi

The `ti`, etc. Endings

‘Kyo bhāvakammesū…’ti ṇi, ṇāpipaccayantato yo.

The sutra beginning ‘`Kyo bhāvakammesu...`’ refers to the `ya` suffix applied to a stem ending in the suffixes `ṇi` or `ṇāpi`.

574. Kyassa ka. 442; rū. 448; nī. 922.

574. Of `ya`

Kriyatthā parassa kyassa ādimhi īña hoti.

At the beginning of the `ya` suffix that follows, `ī` (with the indicatory letter `ñ`) is inserted.

Tena maggo bhāvīyati, tena maggā bhāvīyanti, tena tvaṃ bhāvīyasi, tena tumhe bhāvīyatha, tena ahaṃ bhāvīyāmi, tena mayaṃ bhāvīyāma.

By him, the path is caused to be developed; by him, the paths are caused to be developed; by him, you are caused to be developed; by him, you all are caused to be developed; by him, I am caused to be developed; by him, we are caused to be developed.

Rassatte-bhāviyati, bhāviyanti.

When shortened: `bhāviyati`, `bhāviyanti`.

Dvitte-bhāviyyati, bhāviyyanti. Tathā bhāvayīyati, bhāvayīyanti.

With a double consonant: bhāviyyati, bhāviyyanti. Likewise: bhāvayīyati, bhāvayīyanti.

Rassatte-bhāvayiyati, bhāvayiyanti.

With a short vowel: bhāvayiyati, bhāvayiyanti.

Dvitte-bhāvayiyyati, bhāvayiyyanti.

With a double consonant: bhāvayiyyati, bhāvayiyyanti.

Akammikāpi yā dhātu, kārite tve’kakammikā;

Ekakammā dvikammā ca, dvikammā ca tikammakā.

A root that is intransitive, when made causative, becomes transitive; one with a single object becomes one with a double object, and one with a double object becomes one with a triple object.

Iti [M 0.0361] suddhakatturūpaṃ, suddhakammarūpaṃ, hetukatturūpaṃ, hetukammarūpanti ekadhātumhi cattāri nipphannarūpāni labbhanti.

Thus, from a single root, four derived forms are obtained: the agentive form, the pure passive form, the agentive-passive form, and the causative-passive form.

Katturūpena cettha kammakatturūpampi saṅgayhati. Kusūlo bhijjati, bhijjanadhammo bhijjati.

Here, the object-as-agent form is also included in the agentive form. The granary breaks; that which is of a breakable nature, breaks.

Kammarūpena ca kattukammarūpampi saṅgayhati. Tattha yaṃ padaṃ kattuvācakaṃ samānaṃ saddarūpena kammarūpaṃ bhavati, taṃ kattukammarūpaṃ nāma, taṃ pāḷiyaṃ bahulaṃ dissati.

The passive form also includes the agentive-passive form. Therein, a word which, while denoting the agent, takes a passive form, is called the agentive-passive form; this is frequently seen in the Pāli texts.

Rūpaṃ vibhāviyyati mahāni. 108, atikkamiyyati, samatikkamiyyati, vītivattiyyati, nimittaṃ abhibhuyyatīti gotrabhu paṭi. ma. 1.59, pavattaṃ abhibhuyyati paṭi. ma. 1.59, cutiṃ abhibhuyyati, upapattiṃ abhibhuyyatīti paṭi. ma. 1.59 gotrabhu iccādi.

Form is discriminated, surpassed, completely surpassed, transcended; the sign is overcome—this is gotrabhū; the ongoing process is overcome; death is overcome; rebirth is overcome—this is gotrabhū, and so forth.

Tathā so pahīyethāpi nopi pahīyetha saṃ. ni. 1.249, so pahīyissati saṃ. ni. 1.249, nihiyyati yaso tassa dī. ni. 3.246, hiyyoti hiyyati poso, pareti parihāyati jā. 1.15.348, ājānīyā hasīyanti jā. 2.22.2369, vidhurassa hadayaṃ dhaniyati jā. 2.22.1350 iccādi.

Likewise: he might be abandoned, or he might not be abandoned; he will be abandoned; his fame dwindles; the man wastes away, he declines; the thoroughbreds neigh; the heart of the helpless is shattered, and so forth.

Yañca ‘yamhi dā dhā mā thā hā pā maha mathādīnamī’ti kaccāyane suttaṃ, taṃ kammani icchanti, kattari eva yujjati kammani ivaṇṇāgamassa sabbhāvā. Saddanītiyaṃ pana “so pahīyissatī”ti padānaṃ bhāvarūpattaṃ daḷhaṃ vadati, tāni pana kattukammarūpāni evāti.

And as for the rule in Kaccāyana, ‘yamhi dā dhā mā thā hā pā maha mathādīnamī’, they wish it for the passive, but it is suitable only for the active, because the augment of the vowel ‘i’ is present in the passive. The Saddanīti, however, firmly states that words such as ‘so pahīyissatī’ are impersonal forms, but they are in fact agentive-passive forms.

Ettha ca vattamānaṃ catubbidhaṃ niccapavattaṃ, pavattāvirataṃ, pavattuparataṃ, samīpavattamānanti.

Here, the present tense is fourfold: constantly occurring, occurring without ceasing, occurring and then ceasing, and the near present.

Tattha niccapavatte – idhāyaṃ pabbato tiṭṭhati, candimasūriyā pariyāyanti, disā bhanti virocamānā a. ni. 4.69.

Among these, in the constantly occurring: this mountain stands here; the moon and sun revolve; the directions gleam, shining brightly.

Pavattāvirate [M 0.0362] – api nu te gahapati kule dānaṃ dīyatīti, dīyati me bhante kule dānaṃ a. ni. 9.20.

In the occurring without ceasing: ‘Is charity given in your household, householder?’ ‘Yes, venerable sir, charity is given in my household.’

Ettha ca yāva dāne saussāho, tāva yathāpavattā dānakriyā vattamānā eva nāma hoti ussāhassa aviratattā.

Here, as long as there is enthusiasm for giving, the act of giving, as it occurs, is indeed called present, due to the unceasing effort.

Pavattuparate – na khādati ayaṃ maṃsaṃ, neva pāṇaṃ hanati a. ni. 3.67, na adinnaṃ ādiyati a. ni. 3.67. Ettha yāva tabbipakkhakriyaṃ na karoti, tāva viramaṇakriyā vattamānā eva nāma hoti.

In the occurring and then ceasing: he does not eat meat; he neither kills living beings, nor takes what is not given. Here, so long as one does not perform actions contrary to that, the act of abstaining is indeed called present.

Samīpe – atīte – kuto nu tvaṃ āgacchasi saṃ. ni. 1.130, rājagahato āgacchāmīti. Anāgate – dhammaṃ te desemi, sādhukaṃ suṇohi.

In the near present: For the past: ‘From where do you come?’ ‘I come from Rājagaha.’ For the future: ‘I will teach you the Dhamma, listen carefully.’

Suttavibhattena tadāyoge atītepi ayaṃ vibhatti hoti, vākacīrāni dhunanto, gacchāmi ambare tadā bu. vaṃ. 2.37.

According to the rule for this inflection, when used with 'tadā' (then), it also occurs in the past: 'shaking the bark garments, I go in the sky then.'

Yāva, pure, purāyoge anāgatepi-idheva tāva tiṭṭhāhi, yāvāhaṃ āgacchāmi, yaṃnūnāhaṃ dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyeyyaṃ pārā. aṭṭha. 1.paṭhamamahāsaṅgītikathā, pure adhammo dibbati, dhammo paṭibāhiyyati cūḷava. 437, dante ime chinda purā marāmi jā. 1.16.127.

Also in the future, when used with ‘yāva’, ‘pure’, ‘purā’: ‘Wait right here until I return.’ ‘Perhaps I should recite the Dhamma and the Discipline.’ ‘Before unrighteousness prevails, righteousness is rejected.’ ‘Cut these bonds before I die.’

Ekaṃsatthepi-nirayaṃ nūnagacchāmi, ettha me natthi saṃsayo jā. 2.22.331. Avassambhāviyatthepi-dhuvaṃ buddho bhavāmahaṃ bu. vaṃ. 2.109, dhuvaṃ buddho bhavissati bu. vaṃ. 2.81 vā.

Also in the sense of certainty: ‘Surely I shall go to hell, of this I have no doubt.’ Also in the sense of inevitability: ‘Surely I shall become a Buddha,’ or ‘Surely a Buddha will come to be.’

Aniyamatthepi-manasā ce pasannena, bhāsati vā karoti vā dha. pa. 2 cintetīti cittaṃ dha. sa. aṭṭha. 1, phusatīti phasso dha. sa. aṭṭha. 1, bujjhatīti buddho.

Also in the indefinite sense: 'If with a serene mind, one speaks or acts...'; 'It thinks, thus it is mind'; 'It touches, thus it is contact'; 'He understands, thus he is the Buddha.'

Kadā [M 0.0363] karahiyogepi-kadā gacchati, karahi gacchati, gamissati vā.

Also when used with ‘kadā’ and ‘karahi’: ‘When does he go?’ ‘When does he go?’ or ‘Will he go?’

Iti tyādi.

Thus, and so forth.

Tvādi

The 'tu' group

Atha tvādi vuccate.

Now the ‘tu’ group is explained.

575. Tu antu hi tha mi ma taṃ antaṃ su vho e āmase ka. 424; rū. 450; nī. 897; caṃ. 1.3.122; pā. 3.3.162.

575. Tu, antu, hi, tha, mi, ma, taṃ, antaṃ, su, vho, e, āmase.

Vattamāne kāle pañha, patthanā, vidhīsu kriyatthā tvādayo honti.

In the present time, the ‘tu’ group of suffixes are used with the meaning of an action in questions, aspirations, and injunctions.

Pañhe-dhammaṃ vā tvaṃ adhiyassu vinayaṃ vā pāci. 471 (atthato sadisaṃ).

In questions: ‘Should you study the Dhamma or the Vinaya?’

Patthanāsaddena āsīsādayopi saṅgayhanti.

By the term ‘aspiration,’ blessings and the like are also included.

Tattha patthanāyaṃ-bhavābhave saṃsaranto, saddho homi amaccharī.

Among these, in aspiration: ‘Wandering through existences, may I be faithful and un-miserly.’

Āsīsāyaṃ-etena saccavajjena, pajjunno abhivassatu cariyā. 3.89, sabbe bhadrāni passantu jā. 1.2.105, sabbe sattā averā hontu paṭi. ma. 2.22.

In blessings: ‘By this utterance of truth, may Pajjunna send down rain; may all behold auspicious things; may all beings be free from animosity.’

Yācane-ekaṃ me nayanaṃ dehi cariyā. 1.59.

In requesting: 'Give me one eye.'

Āyācane-desetu bhante bhagavā dhammaṃ dī. ni. 2.68, ovadatu maṃ bhagavā saṃ. ni. 3.1, anusāsatu maṃ sugata saṃ. ni. 3.1, ullumpatu maṃ bhante saṅgho mahāva. 71, asmākaṃ adhipannānaṃ, khamassu rājakuñjara jā. 2.21.181, etha byagghā nivattavho jā. 1.3.66.

In entreating: 'Venerable sir, may the Blessed One teach the Dhamma; may the Blessed One advise me; may the Sugata instruct me. Venerable sir, may the Saṅgha lift me up, who have fallen into distress. O royal elephant, forgive us. Come, tigers, turn back.'

Vidhisaddena niyojanādayopi saṅgayhanti.

By the word 'injunction,' enjoining and so forth are also included.

Tattha [M 0.0364] vidhimhi-akusalaṃ pajahatha, kusalaṃ upasampajja viharatha paṭi. ma. 3.30; pārā. 19, evaṃ vitakketha, mā evaṃ vitakketha paṭi. ma. 3.30.

Therein, in injunction: 'Abandon the unwholesome; undertaking the wholesome, you should dwell; think thus; do not think thus.'

Niyojane-etha bhikkhave sīlavā hotha a. ni. 5.114, appamādena sampādetha dī. ni. 2.185, etha gaṇhatha bandhatha dī. ni. 2.342, mā vo muñcittha kiñcanaṃ dī. ni. 2.342.

In enjoining: 'Come, monks, be virtuous; accomplish your goal with diligence. Come, seize them, bind them; do not release anything of yours.'

Ajjhesane-uddisatu bhante thero pātimokkhaṃ mahāva. 155.

In requesting: 'Venerable sir, may the elder recite the Pātimokkha.'

Āṇattiyaṃ-suṇātu me bhante saṅgho pārā. 368.

In command: 'Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me.'

Pesane-gacchatha tumhe sāriputtā pārā. 432.

In sending: 'Go, you Sāriputtas.'

Pavāraṇāyaṃ-vadatu maṃ bhante saṅgho mahāva. aṭṭha. 213, vadetha bhante yenattho pārā. 290.

In invitation: 'Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha speak to me; venerable sirs, speak for whatever reason.'

Anumatiyaṃ-paribhuñja vā vissajjehi vā yathāpaccayaṃ vā karohi pāci. 374.

In permission: 'Use it, or give it away, or do as is appropriate.'

Varadāne-phussatī varavaṇṇābhe, varassu dasadhā vare jā. 2.22.1655, icchitaṃ patthitaṃ tuyhaṃ, khippameva samijjhatu a. ni. aṭṭha. 1.1.192.

In granting a boon: 'O Phussati of excellent complexion and radiance, choose ten boons. May what is wished and longed for by you quickly be fulfilled.'

Anuññāyaṃ-puccha vāsava maṃ pañhaṃ, yaṃ kiñci manasicchasi dī. ni. 2.356.

In allowing: 'Ask me a question, Vāsava, whatever you wish in your mind.'

Katāvakāsā pucchavho su. ni. 1036.

Having been given the opportunity, you should ask.

Sampaṭicchane-evaṃ hotu dī. ni. 2.419.

In accepting: 'So be it.'

Akkose-muddhā te phalatu sattadhā jā. 1.16.295, corā taṃ khaṇḍākhaṇḍikaṃ chindantu ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.

In abuse: 'May your head split into seven pieces; may thieves cut you piece by piece.'

Sapathe-etena saccavajjena, putto uppajjataṃ ise jā. 1.14.104, musā me bhaṇamānāya, muddhā phalatu sattadhā jā. 1.14.104.

In an oath: 'By this declaration of truth, may a son be born to the sage; if I am speaking falsely, may my head split into seven pieces.'

Āmantane-etu [M 0.0365] vessantaro rājā jā. 2.22.2341, “ehi bhikkhu cara brahmacariyaṃ mahāva. 28, etha bhikkhave sīlavā hotha” iccādīsupi ehi, ethasaddā āmantane tiṭṭhanti.

In addressing: 'Let King Vessantara come.' 'Come, monk, live the holy life.' 'Come, monks, be virtuous.' In these and similar instances, the words 'ehi' and 'etha' stand in the sense of addressing.

Nimantane-adhivāsetu me bhante bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ pārā. 77.

In inviting: 'Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to my meal for tomorrow.'

Pavedane-vedayatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretu cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102, upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu dī. ni. 1.299, punārāyu ca me laddho, evaṃ jānāhi mārisa dī. ni. 2.369.

In announcing: 'May the Saṅgha remember me as one who makes this known. May the venerable Gotama remember me as a lay follower. And my life has been regained; know this, dear sir.'

Pattakāle-parinibbātu bhante bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālo bhante bhagavato dī. ni. 2.168, kālo kho te mahāvīra, uppajja mātukucchiyaṃ bu. vaṃ. 1.67, byākarohi aggivessana na dāni te tuṇhībhāvassa kālo ma. ni. 1.357.

At the proper time: 'Venerable sir, may the Blessed One attain final Nibbāna; may the Sugata attain final Nibbāna. Venerable sir, it is the time for the Blessed One's final Nibbāna. Indeed, O great hero, it is time for you; arise in a mother's womb. Explain, Aggivessana, now is not the time for your silence.'

Anubhotu, anubhontu, anubhohi, anubhotha, anubhomi, anubhoma, bhavatu, bhavantu, ‘himimesvassā’ti hi, mi, mesu assa dīgho, tvaṃ paṇḍito bhavāhi.

May he experience, may they experience, may you experience, may you all experience, may I experience, may we experience, may it be, may they be. Regarding 'himimesvassā': in the case of hi, mi, and me, the 'a' becomes long. 'You be wise.'

576. Hissato lopo ka. 479; rū. 452; nī. 960; caṃ. 5.3.99; pā. 6.4.105.

576. Elision of hi after 'a'.

Akārato parassa hissa lopo hoti.

There is elision of hi after the letter 'a'.

Atoti kiṃ? Brūhi, dehi, hohi.

Why 'after a'? 'Speak,' 'give,' 'be.'

Iminā ato hissa lopo, tvaṃ paṇḍito bhava.

By this, there is elision of hi after 'a'. 'You be wise.'

Tumhe paṇḍitā bhavatha, bhavāmi, bhavāma.

You all be wise; let me be; let us be.

Parachakke-so bhavataṃ, te bhavantaṃ, tvaṃ bhavassu, tumhe bhavavho, ahaṃ bhave, mayaṃ bhavāmase, imāni suddhakatturūpāni.

In the other set of six: 'He should be,' 'they should be,' 'you should be,' 'you all should be,' 'I should be,' 'we should be.' These are the forms of the optative.

Anubhūyatu[M 0.0366], anubhūyantu, anubhuyyatu, anubhuyyantu iccādi suddhakammarūpaṃ.

May it be experienced, may they be experienced, may it be experienced, may they be experienced, and so forth, is the pure passive form.

Bhāvetu, bhāventu, bhāvayatu, bhāvayantu iccādi hetukatturūpaṃ.

May he develop, may they develop, may he develop, may they develop, and so forth, is the causative active form.

Bhāvīyatu, bhāvīyantu. Rassatte-bhāviyatu, bhāviyantu. Dvitte-bhāviyyatu, bhāviyyantu. Tathā bhāvayīyatu, bhāvayīyantuiccādi hetukammarūpaṃ.

May it be caused to be developed, may they be caused to be developed. With shortening: may it be caused to be developed, may they be caused to be developed. With doubling: may it be caused to be developed, may they be caused to be developed. Similarly, may it be caused to be developed, may they be caused to be developed, and so forth, is the causative passive form.

‘Eyyāthasse’iccādisuttena thassa vho, tumhe bhavavho, bhavatha vā.

By the rule beginning 'Eyyāthasse,' 'tha' becomes 'vho.' Thus: 'tumhe bhavavho' (you all be), or 'bhavatha.'

Iti tvādi.

Thus ends the 'tvā' group.

Eyyādi

The 'eyya' group.

Atha eyyādi vuccate.

Now the 'eyya' group is explained.

577. Hetuphalesveyya eyyuṃ eyyāsi eyyātha eyyāmi eyyāma etha eraṃ etho eyyāvho eyyavho (moggallānādīsu) eyyaṃ eyyāmhe vā ka. 416; rū. 454; nī. 880; caṃ. 1.3.120; pā. 3.3.156.

577. In the sense of cause and effect, the endings are: eyyya, eyyuṃ, eyyāsi, eyyātha, eyyāmi, eyyāma; or, etha, eraṃ, etho, eyyāvho, eyyaṃ, eyyāmhe.

Aññamaññasambandhiniyā hetukriyāyañca phalakriyāyañca kriyatthā eyyādayo honti vā. Hetuphalesupi kadāci aññavibhattuppattidīpanattho vāsaddo, sace so yānaṃ labhissati, gamissati, sace na labhissati, na gamissati iccādi.

The 'eyya' group of endings optionally occurs in the sense of action for a causal action and a resultant action that are mutually related. The word 'vā' serves to indicate that sometimes, even in the context of cause and effect, other verbal endings may arise. For example: 'If he obtains a vehicle, he will go; if he does not obtain it, he will not go,' and so on.

Sace saṅkhāro nicco bhaveyya, sukho nāma bhaveyya, sace so paṇḍito bhaveyya, sukhito bhaveyya.

If formations were permanent, they would indeed be happiness; if he were wise, he would be happy.

578. Pañhapatthanāvidhīsu caṃ. 1.3.121; pā. 3.3.161.

578. In questions, aspirations, and injunctions.

Etesu [M 0.0367] eyyādayo honti.

In these contexts, the 'eyya' group of endings occurs.

Pañhe-kinnu kho tvaṃ vinayaṃ vā adhiyyeyyāsi dhammaṃ vā.

In a question: 'Indeed, would you study the Vinaya or the Dhamma?'

Patthanāyaṃ-bhaveyyaṃ jātijātiyaṃ.

In an aspiration: 'May I be reborn in existence after existence.'

Vidhimhi-pāṇaṃ na haneyya, adinnaṃ na ādiyeyya, dānaṃ dadeyya, sīlaṃ rakkheyya.

In an injunction: 'One should not kill living beings; one should not take what is not given; one should give alms; one should protect morality.'

579. Sattārahesveyyādī ka. 416; rū. 454; nī. 881-4; caṃ. 1.3.128; pā. 3.3.169-172; satyarahesveyyādī (bahūsu).

579. In ability and worthiness, the 'eyya' group.

Sattiyaṃ arahatthe ca eyyādayo honti.

In the sense of ability and in the sense of worthiness, the 'eyya' group of endings occurs.

Bhavaṃ rajjaṃ kareyya, bhavaṃ rajjaṃ kātuṃ sakko, kātuṃ arahoti attho.

‘The lord could rule the kingdom’ means: the lord is able to rule, is worthy to rule.

So imaṃ vijaṭaye jaṭaṃ saṃ. ni. 1.23.

He could unravel this tangle.

580. Sambhāvane vā ka. 416; rū. 854; nī. 881, 883-4; caṃ. 1.3.118-9; pā. 3.3.154-5.

580. Or in the sense of possibility.

Sambhāvanepi eyyādayo honti vā.

Even in the sense of possibility, the 'eyya' group of endings optionally occurs.

Pabbatamapi sirasā bhindeyya, bhaveyya, bhaveyyuṃ, bhaveyyāsi, bhaveyyātha, bhaveyyāmi, bhaveyyāma.

He might even split a mountain with his head. He might be, they might be, you might be, you all might be, I might be, we might be.

Parachakke-so bhavetha, te bhaveraṃ, tvaṃ bhavetho, tumhe bhaveyyāvho, ahaṃ bhaveyyaṃ, mayaṃ bhaveyyāmhe, iti suddhakatturūpāni.

Using the other set of six endings: he might be, they might be, you might be, you all might be, I might be, we might be—thus are the forms.

Anubhūyeyya, anubhūyeyyuṃ. Dvitte rassattaṃ, anubhuyyeyya, anubhuyyeyyuṃ iccādi suddhakammarūpaṃ.

It might be experienced, they might be experienced. With doubling and shortening: it might be experienced, they might be experienced, and so on—this is the pure passive form.

Bhāveyya[M 0.0368], bhāveyyuṃ, bhāvayeyya, bhāvayeyyuṃ iccādi hetukatturūpaṃ.

He might develop, they might develop; he might cause to develop, they might cause to develop, and so on—this is the causative active form.

Bhāvīyeyya, bhāvīyeyyuṃ. Rassatte-bhāvayiyeyya, bhāvayiyeyyuṃ. Dvitte-bhāviyyeyya, bhāviyyeyyuṃ. Tathā bhāvayīyeyya, bhāvayīyeyyuṃ iccādi hetukammarūpaṃ.

It might be caused to develop, they might be caused to develop. With shortening: it might be caused to develop, they might be caused to develop. With doubling: it might be caused to develop, they might be caused to develop. Likewise, it might be caused to develop, they might be caused to develop, and so on—this is the causative passive form.

581. Eyyeyyāseyyaṃnaṃ ṭe ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

581. Ṭe is substituted for eyya, eyyāsi, and eyyaṃ.

Eyya, eyyāsi, eyyamiccetesaṃ ṭe hoti vā.

For eyya, eyyāsi, and eyyaṃ, ṭe optionally occurs.

Atrimā pāḷī-caje mattā sukhaṃ dhīro, passe ce vipulaṃ sukhaṃ dha. pa. 290. Kiṃ tvaṃ sutasomā’nutappe jā. 2.21.399, dhīraṃ passe suṇe dhīraṃ, dhīrena saha saṃvase jā. 1.13.94 iccādi.

Here is the Pāli text: 'If a wise person, seeing a greater happiness, were to abandon a lesser happiness.' 'Why do you grieve, Sutasoma?' 'One should see the wise, hear the wise, and dwell with the wise,' and so on.

So bhave, bhaveyya, tvaṃ bhave, bhaveyyāsi, ahaṃ bhave, bhaveyyaṃ.

He might be (so bhave, bhaveyya); you might be (tvaṃ bhave, bhaveyyāsi); I might be (ahaṃ bhave, bhaveyyaṃ).

582. Eyyuṃssuṃ ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

582. For eyyuṃ, uṃ.

Eyyuṃssa uṃ hoti vā.

For eyyuṃ, uṃ optionally occurs.

Atrimā pāḷī-vajjuṃ vā te na vā vajjuṃ, natthi nāsāya rūhanā jā. 1.3.33, upayānāni me dajjuṃ, rājaputta tayī gateti jā. 2.22.26.

Here is the Pāli text: 'Whether they should speak or they should not speak, there is no healing for the nose. They should give me gifts. O prince, I have come to you.'

583. Eyyāmassemu ca ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

583. For `eyyāma`, `emu` is also substituted.

Eyyāmassa emu ca hoti, antassa u ca.

For `eyyāma`, `emu` also occurs; and for the final letter, `u` also occurs.

Atrimā pāḷī-kathaṃ jānemu taṃ mayaṃ dī. ni. 2.318, muñcemu naṃ uragaṃ bandhanasmā jā. 1.15.252, dakkhemu te nāga nivesanāni jā. 1.15.254, gantvāna taṃ paṭikaremu accayaṃ, appeva naṃ putta labhemu jīvitaṃ jā. 1.15.13, dajjemu kho [M 0.0369] pañcasatāni bhoto jā. 2.22.1302, pañhaṃ pucchemu mārisa dī. ni. 2.354, viharemu averino dī. ni. 2.357, tayājja guttā viharemu rattinti jā. 1.2.18. Bhaveyyāmu, bhaveyyāma.

The Pāli passage is as follows: How might we know that? We might release him, the serpent, from bondage. We might see your abodes, O nāga. Having gone, we might atone for the offense. Perhaps we might obtain the life of our son. Indeed, we might give five hundred to you, sir. We might ask a question, noble one. We might dwell free from enmity. Guarded by you today, we might dwell through the night. We might be; we might be.

Mahāvuttinā kvaci majjhe yyā-kārassa lopo, atthaṃ dhammañca pucchesi jā. 1.16.150, uregaṇḍāyo bujjhesi, tāyo bujjhesi māṇava jā. 2.17.132-133, yathā gatiṃ me abhisambhavetha jā. 2.17.87-89, yathā gatiṃ te abhisambhavema jā. 2.17.87-89, okāsaṃ sampajānātha, vane yattha vasemaseti jā. 2.22.1885 ‘vasāmase’.

In the Mahāvutti, sometimes the syllable 'yyā' in the middle is elided. You asked about meaning and Dhamma. You awakened from the chest-boils. You awakened from them, O youth. How you might attain my destination, how we might attain your destination. You should understand the opportunity. In the forest, where we might dwell—so it is said.

‘Eyyāthasse’iccādisuttena eyyāthassa o ca, tumhe bhaveyyātho, bhaveyyātha vā.

By the rule beginning with 'Eyyāthasse', 'o' is also substituted for `eyyātha`; thus, `tumhe bhaveyyātho`, or `bhaveyyātha`.

Ettha ca pubbe vuttā pañha, patthanā, vidhippabhedā idhapi yathāpayogaṃ veditabbā. Pañhasaddena paripañha, paripucchā, parivitakka, parivīmaṃsādayo saṅgayhanti.

Here also, the previously mentioned types of question, aspiration, and prescription should be understood as applicable according to usage. By the term 'question' are included detailed questioning, detailed inquiry, detailed reflection, detailed investigation, and so on.

Paripañhe-dhammaṃ vā paṭhamaṃ saṅgāyeyyāma vinayaṃ vā.

In detailed questioning: Should we first recite the Dhamma or the Vinaya?

Paripucchāyaṃ-vadetha bhante kimahaṃ kareyyaṃ, ko imassa attho, kathañcassa atthaṃ ahaṃ jāneyyaṃ.

In detailed inquiry: 'Venerable sirs, you should speak. What should I do? What is its meaning? And how should I know its meaning?'

Parivitakke-kassāhaṃ paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ dī. ni. 2.72, yaṃnūnāhaṃ dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyeyyaṃ pārā. aṭṭha. 1.paṭhamamahāsaṅgītikathā.

In detailed reflection: To whom should I first teach the Dhamma? What if I were to rehearse the Dhamma and the Vinaya?

Parivīmaṃsāyaṃ-gaccheyyaṃ vā ahaṃ uposathaṃ, na vāgaccheyyaṃ mahāva. 137.

In detailed investigation: Should I go to the Uposatha, or should I not go?

Patthanāyaṃ-evaṃrūpo siyaṃ ahaṃ anāgatamaddhānaṃ ma. ni. 3.274, ummādantyā ramitvāna, sivirājā tato siyaṃ jā. 2.18.70, passeyya taṃ vassasataṃ arogaṃ jā. 2.21.453.

In aspiration: 'May I be of such a form in the future.' 'Having delighted with Ummādantī, may I then be King Sivi.' 'May he see a hundred years, free from disease.'

Āyācane-labheyyāhaṃ [M 0.0370] bhante bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampadaṃ mahāva. 28; saṃ. ni. 2.17.

In entreaty: 'Venerable sir, may I receive the going-forth in the Blessed One's presence; may I receive the full ordination.'

Vidhimhi-careyya dhammaṃ jā. 1.14.63.

In prescription: One should practice the Dhamma.

Niyojane-careyyādittasīsova, natthi maccussa nā gamo saṃ. ni. 1.145.

In injunction: 'One should act as if one's head were on fire; there is no escape for a mortal.'

Ajjhesane-yassa siyā āpatti, so āvikareyya mahāva. 132, yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya mahāva. 70.

In invitation: 'Whoever has an offense should disclose it; whoever does not agree should speak.'

Pavāraṇāyaṃ-vadeyyātha bhante yenattho pārā. 290.

In invitation: 'Venerable sirs, you should speak if there is a need.'

Anumatiyaṃ-taṃ jano hareyya vā daheyya vā yathāpaccayaṃ vā kareyya ma. ni. 1.247.

In permission: 'People may take it away, or burn it, or do with it as they deem fit.'

Anuññāyaṃ-ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho kammaṃ kareyya cūḷava. 6.

In authorization: 'If the Saṅgha desires, it may perform the act.'

Āmantane-yadā te pahiṇeyyāmi, tadā eyyāsi khattiya jā. 2.22.635.

In addressing: 'When I send for you, then you should come, O khattiya.'

Nimantane-idha bhavaṃ nisīdeyya.

In invitation: 'May the venerable one be seated here.'

Pattakāle-saṅgho uposathaṃ kareyya, pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyya mahāva. 167.

At the proper time: 'The Saṅgha should hold the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha.'

‘Sambhāvane vā’ti vāsaddo avuttavikappanattho, tena parikappa, kriyātipannādayo saṅgayhanti.

Regarding 'or in the sense of possibility': The word 'vā' has the meaning of indicating an unstated alternative; thereby, supposition, unfulfilled conditions, etc., are included.

Tattha parikappo duvidho bhūtā’bhūtavasena.

Therein, supposition is twofold: according to what is actual and what is not actual.

Tattha bhūtaparikappe-yo bālaṃ seveyya, sopi bālo bhaveyya.

Therein, in the supposition of what is actual: 'Whoever associates with a fool, he too would be a fool.'

Abhūtaparikappe-yadā [M 0.0371] kacchapalomānaṃ, pāvāro tividho siyā jā. 1.8.78. Yadā sasavisāṇānaṃ, nisseṇī sukatā siyā jā. 1.8.79.

In the supposition of what is not actual: 'When a threefold robe might be made from the hairs of a tortoise, and when a well-made ladder might be made from the horns of a rabbit.'

Kriyātipanne-sace so agāraṃ ajjhāvaseyya, rājā assa cakkavattī dī. ni. 3.136.

In the case of an unfulfilled condition: 'If he were to live the household life, he would be a wheel-turning monarch.'

Iti eyyādi.

Thus `eyya`, and so on.

Hiyyattanī

The Aorist

Atha hiyyattanī vuccate.

Now, the aorist is explained.

584. Anajjattane ā ū o ttha a mhā ttha tthuṃ se vhaṃ iṃ mhase ka. 418; rū. 456; nī. 886; caṃ. 1.2.77; pā. 3.2.111.

584. For the aorist, the endings are ā, ū, o, ttha, a, mhā, ttha, tthuṃ, se, vhaṃ, iṃ, mhase.

Ajjato aññasmiṃ bhūte kāle kriyatthā paraṃ āiccādayo honti.

After the verbal stem, in a past time other than today, endings such as ā, etc., occur.

585. Ā ī ssādīsvaña vā ka. 519; rū. 457; nī. 1032.

585. The augment 'a' is optionally prefixed before the endings ā, ī, ssā, and so forth.

Āiccādīsu īiccādīsu ssādīsu ca tesaṃ ādimhi aña hoti vā.

Before endings such as ā, ī, and ssā, the augment 'a' may optionally be prefixed to the stem.

So abhavā, bhavā, te abhavū, bhavū, tvaṃ abhavo, bhavo, tumhe abhavattha, bhavattha, ahaṃ abhava, bhava, mayaṃ abhavamhā, bhavamhā.

He was (abhavā), he was (bhavā); they were (abhavū), they were (bhavū); you were (abhavo), you were (bhavo); you all were (abhavattha), you all were (bhavattha); I was (abhava), I was (bhava); we were (abhavamhā), we were (bhavamhā).

Parachakke-abhavattha, bhavattha, abhavatthuṃ, bhavatthuṃ, abhavase, bhavase, abhavavhaṃ, bhavavhaṃ, abhaviṃ, bhaviṃ, abhavamhase, bhavamhase.

In the other group of six: you all were (abhavattha), you all were (bhavattha); they were (abhavatthuṃ), they were (bhavatthuṃ); you were (abhavase), you were (bhavase); you all were (abhavavhaṃ), you all were (bhavavhaṃ); I was (abhaviṃ), I was (bhaviṃ); we were (abhavamhase), we were (bhavamhase).

586. Ā [M 0.0372] ī ū mhā ssā ssāmhānaṃ vā ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

586. Of the endings ā, ī, ū, mhā, ssā, and ssāmhā, optionally.

Etesaṃ rasso hoti vā.

Of these, shortening optionally occurs.

So abhava, te abhavu, mayaṃ abhavamha.

He was (abhava), they were (abhavu), we were (abhavamha).

‘Eyyāthasse’iccādinā āssa tthattaṃ, assa ca aṃ, so abhavattha, bhavattha, abhavā, bhavā vā, ahaṃ abhavaṃ, bhavaṃ, abhava, bhava vā, imāni suddhakatturūpāni.

By the rule 'Eyyāthasse,' etc., `ttha` is substituted for `ā`, and `aṃ` for `a`. Thus: he was (abhavattha, bhavattha), or optionally (abhavā, bhavā); I was (abhavaṃ, bhavaṃ), or optionally (abhava, bhava). These are the aorist forms.

Ettha ca mahāvuttinā ā-vibhattiyā thādeso bahulaṃ dissati, medanī sampakampatha jā. 2.22.1672, visaññī samapajjatha jā. 2.22.328, imā gāthā abhāsatha jā. 2.22.328, tuccho kāyo adissatha theragā. 172, nibbidā samatiṭṭhatha theragā. 273, eko rahasi jhāyatha jā. 1.15.286 iccādi. Tathā o-vibhattiyā ca, dubbheyyaṃ maṃ amaññatha iccādi.

And here, according to the great commentary, the substitution of 'tha' for the ā-ending is frequently seen, as in 'medanī sampakampatha' (the earth trembled), 'visaññī samapajjatha' (he became unconscious), 'imā gāthā abhāsatha' (he spoke these verses), 'tuccho kāyo adissatha' (the empty body appeared), 'nibbidā samatiṭṭhatha' (disenchantment arose), 'eko rahasi jhāyatha' (he meditated alone in solitude), etc. Similarly, for the o-ending, as in 'dubbheyyaṃ maṃ amaññatha' (he thought me difficult to harm), etc.

Iti hiyyattanī.

Thus ends the Aorist.

Ajjattanī

The Perfect Tense

Atha ajjattanī vuccate.

Now the Perfect Tense is explained.

587. Bhūte ī uṃ o ttha iṃ mhā ā ū se vhaṃ aṃ mhe ka. 419; rū. 469; nī. 887.

587. In the past tense, the endings are ī, uṃ, o, ttha, iṃ, mhā, ā, ū, se, vhaṃ, aṃ, mhe.

Abhavīti bhūto, atītoti attho, bhūte kāle kriyatthā paraṃ īiccādayo honti.

`Abhavī` means 'was'; the meaning is 'past'. In past time, after the verbal stem, endings such as ī, etc., occur.

588. A ī ssā ssatyādīnaṃ byañjanassiu ka. 516; rū. 466; nī. 1030; caṃ. 1.2.76; pā. 3.2.110 aīssaādīnaṃ byañjanassiu (bahūsu).

588. Before the consonant of endings such as A, Ī, SSĀ, SSATI, etc., `i` or `u` is inserted.

Aādissa īādissa ssāādissa ssatiādissa ca byañjanassa ādimhi iu hoti. ‘Byañjanassā’ti etena aādimhi [M 0.0373] pañca, īādimhi sattāti dvādasa suddhasaravibhattiyo paṭikkhipati.

At the beginning of the consonant of A-endings, Ī-endings, SSĀ-endings, and SSATI-endings, 'i' or 'u' occurs. By 'byañjanassa' (of the consonant), this rule excludes the twelve pure vowel endings: five in the A-group and seven in the Ī-group.

‘Āīssādīsvaña vā’iti suttena vikappena dhātvādimhi akāro.

By the rule 'Āīssādīsvaña vā', the letter 'a' is optionally prefixed to the root.

So abhavī, bhavī, te abhavuṃ, bhavuṃ, tvaṃ abhavo, bhavo, tumhe abhavittha, bhavittha, ahaṃ abhaviṃ, bhaviṃ, mayaṃ abhavimhā, bhavimhā, so abhavā, bhavā, te abhavū, bhavū, tvaṃ abhavise, bhavise, tumhe abhavivhaṃ, bhavivhaṃ, ahaṃ abhavaṃ, bhavaṃ, mayaṃ abhavimhe, bhavimhe.

He was (abhavī), he was (bhavī); they were (abhavuṃ), they were (bhavuṃ); you were (abhavo), you were (bhavo); you all were (abhavittha), you all were (bhavittha); I was (abhaviṃ), I was (bhaviṃ); we were (abhavimhā), we were (bhavimhā). He was (abhavā), he was (bhavā); they were (abhavū), they were (bhavū); you were (abhavise), you were (bhavise); you all were (abhavivhaṃ), you all were (bhavivhaṃ); I was (abhavaṃ), I was (bhavaṃ); we were (abhavimhe), we were (bhavimhe).

‘Āīū’iccādinā ī, mhā, ā, ūnaṃ rassatte-so abhavi, bhavi, mayaṃ abhavimha, bhavimha, so abhava, bhava, te abhavu, bhavu.

By the rule 'Āīū,' etc., with the shortening of ī, mhā, ā, and ū: he was (abhavi, bhavi); we were (abhavimha, bhavimha); he was (abhava, bhava); they were (abhavu, bhavu).

589. Eyyāthasseaāīthānaṃ o a aṃ ttha ttho vho vā ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105; ‘…vhoka’ (bahūsu).

589. For `eyyātha`, `ssa`, `a`, `ā`, `ī`, and `tha`, the substitutions `o`, `a`, `aṃ`, `ttha`, `ttho`, and `vho` optionally occur.

Eyyāthādīnaṃ yathākkamaṃ oādayo honti vā.

For `eyyātha`, etc., `o`, etc., optionally occur in respective order.

Tumhe gaccheyyātho, gaccheyyātha vā, tvaṃ agacchissa, agacchisse vā, ahaṃ agamaṃ, gamaṃ, agama, gama vā, so agamittha, gamittha, agamā, gamā vā, so agamittho, gamittho, agamī, gamī vā, tumhe gacchavho, gacchatha vāti.

You all should go (gaccheyyātho), or (gaccheyyātha); you went (agacchissa), or (agacchisse); I went (agamaṃ, gamaṃ), or optionally (agama, gama); he went (agamittha, gamittha), or optionally (agamā, gamā); he went (agamittho, gamittho), or optionally (agamī, gamī); you all went (gacchavho), or (gacchatha).

Iminā ī, ā, avacanānaṃ ttho, ttha, aṃādesā honti, so abhavittho, bhavittho, so abhavittha, bhavittha, ahaṃ abhavaṃ, bhavaṃ.

By this rule, the substitutions ttho, ttha, and aṃ occur for the ī, ā, and 'a' forms, respectively. Thus: he was (abhavittho, bhavittho); he was (abhavittha, bhavittha); I was (abhavaṃ, bhavaṃ).

Atrimā pāḷī – īmhi-paṅko ca mā visiyittho jā. 1.13.44, sañjagghittho mayā saha jā. 1.16.241. Āmhi-anumodittha vāsavo jā. 2.22.1667, nimantayittha [M 0.0374] vāsavo jā. 2.22.1667, khubbhittha nagaraṃ tadā jā. 2.22.1673, subhūtitthero gāthaṃ abhāsittha theragā. 1. Amhi-idhāhaṃ mallikaṃ deviṃ etadavocaṃ saṃ. ni. 1.119, ajānamevaṃ āvuso avacaṃ jānāmīti pārā. 195, ahaṃ kāmānaṃ vasamanvagaṃ jā. 2.19.45, ajjhagaṃ amataṃ santiṃ iccādi.

Here is the Pāḷi text: In the case of ī: 'and may the mud not dry up' (visiyittho), 'you laughed with me' (sañjagghittho). In the case of Ā: 'Vāsava rejoiced' (anumodittha), 'Vāsava invited' (nimantayittha), 'then the city was agitated' (khubbhittha), 'the Elder Subhūti spoke a verse' (abhāsittha). In the case of A: 'Here I said this to Queen Mallikā' (etadavocaṃ), 'not knowing, friend, I spoke as if I knew' (avacaṃ), 'I fell under the sway of desires' (vasamanvagaṃ), 'I attained the deathless peace' (ajjhagaṃ), and so on.

590. Uṃssiṃsvaṃsu ka. 504, 517; rū. 470-488; nī. 1016-1105.

590. For `uṃ`, `iṃsu` and `aṃsu` are substituted.

Umiccassa iṃsu, aṃsu honti.

For `uṃ`, `iṃsu` and `aṃsu` occur.

Agamiṃsu, agamaṃsu, agamuṃ. Iminā uṃssa iṃsu, abhaviṃsu, bhaviṃsu.

They went (agamiṃsu), they went (agamaṃsu), they went (agamuṃ). By this rule, `iṃsu` is substituted for `uṃ`: they were (abhaviṃsu, bhaviṃsu).

591. Ossa a i ttha ttho ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

591. For `o`, `a`, `i`, `ttha`, and `ttho` are substituted.

Ossa aiccādayo honti.

For `o`, `a`, etc., occur.

Tvaṃ abhava, tvaṃ abhavi, tvaṃ abhavittha, tvaṃ abhavittho.

You were (abhava), you were (abhavi), you were (abhavittha), you were (abhavittho).

Atrimā pāḷī-ossa atte-mā hevaṃ ānanda avaca dī. ni. 2.95, tvameva dāni’makara, yaṃ kāmo byagamā tayi jā. 1.2.167. Itte-mā tvaṃ bhāyi mahārāja, mā tvaṃ bhāyi rathesabha jā. 2.22.684, mā cintesi mā tvaṃ soci, yācāmi luddakaṃ ahaṃ gavesitabbaṃ. Tthattemāssu tiṇṇo amaññittha jā. 2.22.255, mā kilittha mayā vinā jā. 2.22.1713, māssu kujjhittha nāvika jā. 1.6.5. Tthotte-mā purāṇe amaññittho theragā. 280, mā dayhittho punappunaṃ saṃ. ni. 1.212, tiṇamatte asajjittho jā. 1.1.89, mā tvaṃ brahmuno vacanaṃ upātivattittho ma. ni. 1.502, mā tvaṃ maññittho na maṃ jānātī ma. ni. 1.502 ti.

Herein are the Pāli examples: For 'o' becoming 'a': 'Do not speak thus, Ānanda'; 'you alone now did'; 'what desire passed away in you'. For 'o' becoming 'i': 'Do not fear, O great king'; 'do not fear, O bull among charioteers'; 'do not worry, do not grieve'; 'I beg the hunter'. For 'o' becoming 'ttha': 'he thought he had crossed over'; 'do not be troubled without me'; 'do not be angry, O boatman'. For 'o' becoming 'ttho': 'Do not think of the old things'; 'do not burn again and again'; 'do not cling even to a blade of grass'; 'do not transgress the word of Brahmā'; 'do not think, "He does not know me."'.

Tattha [M 0.0375] ‘mā dayhittho’iccādīni parokkhāvacanenapi sijjhanti.

Therein, 'mā dayhittho' and so forth are also accomplished by the perfect tense ending.

Suttavibhattena tthassa ttho hoti, taṃ vo vadāmi bhaddante, yāvantettha samāgatā apa. thera 1.1.367, massu mittānaṃ dubbhittho. Mittadubbho hi pāpakoti jā. 1.16.222.

By the rule from the Sutta, 'ttho' occurs for 'ttha'. 'This I declare to you, venerable sirs, as many as have gathered here: do not indeed betray friends. For a betrayer of friends is indeed evil.'

Mahāvuttinā ossa kvaci lopo, puna dānaṃ adā tuvaṃ jā. 2.22.1786, mā no tvaṃ tāta adadā jā. 2.22.2126, mā bhoti kupitā ahu jā. 2.22.1931, māhu pacchānutāpinī saṃ. ni. 1.162; therīgā. 57.

According to the Mahāvutti, there is sometimes elision of 'o'. 'Again, you gave a gift.' 'Father, do not give to us.' 'May the lady not be angry.' 'May she not be regretful afterward.'

592. Si ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

592. The ending 'si'.

Ossa si hoti vā.

For 'o', there is optionally 'si'.

Tvaṃ abhavasi, bhavasi, tvaṃ anubhosi.

You were (abhavasi), you are (bhavasi), you experienced (anubhosi).

593. Mhātthānamuu ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

593. For 'mhā' and 'ttha', 'u'.

Mhā, tthānaṃ ādimhi uña hoti.

For 'mhā' and 'ttha', 'u' occurs at the beginning.

Assosumhā, ahesumhā, avocumhā, avocuttha iccādīni dissanti.

Forms such as 'assosumhā', 'ahesumhā', 'avocumhā', 'avocuttha' are seen.

Tumhe abhavuttha, bhavuttha, abhavittha, bhavittha vā, mayaṃ abhavumhā, bhavumhā, abhavimhā, bhavimhā vā.

You (plural) were (abhavuttha, bhavuttha), or you were (abhavittha, bhavittha); we were (abhavumhā, bhavumhā), or we were (abhavimhā, bhavimhā).

594. Iṃssa ca suu ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105; “…siu” (bahūsu).

594. And for 'iṃ', 'su'.

Imiccassa mhā, tthānañca ādimhi suu hoti, sāgamo hotīti attho. Casaddena īādīnampi ādimhi sāgamo hoti, sāgame ca sati byañjanaṃ hoti, tassa ādimhi iāgamo labbhati. Tena “imā gāthā abhāsisuṃ gavesitabbaṃ, te me [M 0.0376] asse ayācisuṃ, yathābhūtaṃ vipassisuṃ” jā. 2.22.1863 iccādīni dī. ni. 3.277 sijjhanti.

For the ending 'iṃ', and also for 'mhā' and 'ttha', 'su' occurs at the beginning; the meaning is that there is an 's'-augment. By the word 'ca', for 'ī' and other endings as well, there is an 's'-augment at the beginning. And when there is an 's'-augment, which is a consonant, an 'i'-augment is obtained at its beginning. By this, forms such as 'imā gāthā abhāsisuṃ' (they spoke these verses), 'te me asse ayācisuṃ' (they asked me for horses), and 'yathābhūtaṃ vipassisuṃ' (they saw things as they are) are established.

So bhogaṃ anubhosi, anubhavi vā, tumhe anubhosittha, anubhavittha vā, ahaṃ anubhosi, anubhaviṃ vā. Mayaṃ anubhosimhā anubhavimhā vā.

He experienced wealth (anubhosi), or (anubhavi); you (plural) experienced (anubhosittha), or (anubhavittha); I experienced (anubhosi), or (anubhaviṃ); we experienced (anubhosimhā), or (anubhavimhā).

595. Eontā suṃ ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105; ‘eottā suṃ” (bahūsu).

595. From stems ending in 'e' and 'o', 'suṃ'.

Edantato odantato ca parassa uṃvacanassa suṃ hoti vā.

After a stem ending in 'e' or 'o', the ending 'uṃ' optionally becomes 'suṃ'.

Ānesuṃ, sāyesuṃ, cintesuṃ, paccanubhosuṃ, paribhosuṃ, adhibhosuṃ, abhibhosuṃ.

They brought (ānesuṃ), they caused to lie down (sāyesuṃ), they thought (cintesuṃ), they repeatedly experienced (paccanubhosuṃ), they enjoyed (paribhosuṃ), they surpassed (adhibhosuṃ), they overcame (abhibhosuṃ).

Suttavibhattena ādantatopi ca, vihāsuṃ viharanti ca saṃ. ni. 1.173, te anubhosuṃ, imāni suddhakatturūpāni.

According to the Suttavibhanga, and also from stems ending in 'ā': 'vihāsuṃ' (they dwelt) and 'viharanti' (they dwell), and 'te anubhosuṃ' (they experienced)—these are the forms here.

Tena bhogo anvabhūyī, anubhūyī.

By him, wealth was experienced (anvabhūyī, anubhūyī).

Rassatte-anvabhūyi, anubhūyi.

With shortening: anvabhūyi, anubhūyi (it was experienced).

Dvitte-anvabhuyyi, anubhuyyi.

With doubling: anvabhuyyi, anubhuyyi (it was experienced).

Tena bhogā anvabhūyuṃ, anubhūyuṃ, anvabhūyiṃsu, anubhūyiṃsu iccādi suddhakammarūpaṃ.

By him, wealths were experienced (anvabhūyuṃ, anubhūyuṃ, anvabhūyiṃsu, anubhūyiṃsu), and so forth; this is the pure passive form.

So maggaṃ abhāvi, bhāvi, abhāvesi, bhāvesi, abhāvayi, bhāvayi, te maggaṃ abhāviṃsu, bhāviṃsu.

He cultivated the path (abhāvi, bhāvi, abhāvesi, bhāvesi, abhāvayi, bhāvayi); they cultivated the path (abhāviṃsu, bhāviṃsu).

‘Eontāsu’nti edantamhā suṃ. Te maggaṃ abhāvesuṃ, bhāvesuṃ, abhāvayiṃsu, bhāvayiṃsu, tvaṃ maggaṃ abhāvaya, bhāvaya, abhāvayi, bhāvayi, tvaṃ maggaṃ abhāvittha, bhāvittha, abhāvayittha, bhāvayittha, tvaṃ maggaṃ abhāvayittho, bhāvayittho, tvaṃ maggaṃ [M 0.0377] abhāvesi, bhāvesi, tumhe maggaṃ abhāvittha, bhāvittha, abhāvayittha, bhāvayittha, ahaṃ maggaṃ abhāviṃ, bhāviṃ, abhāvesiṃ, bhāvesiṃ, abhāvayiṃ, bhāvayiṃ, mayaṃ maggaṃ abhāvimhā, bhāvimhā, abhāvimha, bhāvimha, abhāvayimhā, bhāvayimhā, abhāvayimha, bhāvayimha.

The rule 'Eontā suṃ' means that 'suṃ' occurs after a stem ending in 'e'. They cultivated the path (abhāvesuṃ, bhāvesuṃ, abhāvayiṃsu, bhāvayiṃsu). You (singular) cultivated the path (abhāvaya, bhāvaya, abhāvayi, bhāvayi; abhāvittha, bhāvittha, abhāvayittha, bhāvayittha; abhāvayittho, bhāvayittho; abhāvesi, bhāvesi). You (plural) cultivated the path (abhāvittha, bhāvittha, abhāvayittha, bhāvayittha). I cultivated the path (abhāviṃ, bhāviṃ, abhāvesiṃ, bhāvesiṃ, abhāvayiṃ, bhāvayiṃ). We cultivated the path (abhāvimhā, bhāvimhā, abhāvimha, bhāvimha, abhāvayimhā, bhāvayimhā, abhāvayimha, bhāvayimha).

So maggaṃ abhāvā, bhāvā, abhāvittha, bhāvittha, abhāvayittha, bhāvayittha iccādi hetukatturūpaṃ.

He cultivated the path (abhāvā, bhāvā, abhāvittha, bhāvittha, abhāvayittha, bhāvayittha), and so forth; these are the forms here.

Tena maggo abhāviyi, bhāviyi, tena maggā abhāviyiṃsu, bhāviyiṃsu iccādi hetukammarūpaṃ.

By him the path was caused to be cultivated (abhāviyi, bhāviyi); by him the paths were caused to be cultivated (abhāviyiṃsu, bhāviyiṃsu), and so forth; this is the causative passive form.

Iti ajjattanī.

Thus the Aorist.

Parokkhā

The Perfect.

Atha parokkhā vuccate.

Now the Perfect is explained.

596. Parokkhe a u e tha aṃ mha ttha re ttho vho iṃ mhe ka. 417; rū. 460; nī. 887; caṃ. 1.2.81; pā. 3.2.115.

596. In the Perfect tense, the endings are: a, u, e, tha, aṃ, mha, ttha, re, ttho, vho, iṃ, mhe.

Akkhānaṃ indriyānaṃ paraṃ parokkhaṃ, apaccakkhanti attho. Bhūte kāle attano parokkhakriyāya vattabbāya kriyatthā aādayo honti.

Parokkha means beyond the sense faculties, that is, not directly perceived. In the past tense, for expressing an action unseen by oneself, the verbal endings beginning with 'a' occur.

Mahāvuttinā gassa dīgho vā, so kira jagāma, te kira jagāmu, tvaṃ kira jagāme, tumhe kira jagāmittha, ahaṃ kira jagāmaṃ, mayaṃ kira jagāmimha iccādi.

According to the Mahāvutti, the 'g' of the root 'gam' optionally becomes long. For example: 'so kira jagāma' (it seems he went), 'te kira jagāmu' (it seems they went), 'tvaṃ kira jagāme' (it seems you went), 'tumhe kira jagāmittha' (it seems you all went), 'ahaṃ kira jagāmaṃ' (it seems I went), 'mayaṃ kira jagāmimha' (it seems we went), and so on.

Ettha ca ‘so kira jagāma’ iccādīni anussavaparokkhāni nāma.

Here, forms such as 'so kira jagāma' are called the hearsay Perfect.

‘Ahaṃ [M 0.0378] kira jagāmaṃ, mayaṃ kira jagāmimhā’ti idaṃ attanā gantvāpi gamanaṃ pamuṭṭhassa vā asampaṭicchitukāmassa vā paṭivacanaparokkhaṃ nāma.

'Ahaṃ kira jagāmaṃ' (it seems I went), 'mayaṃ kira jagāmimha' (it seems we went)—this is called the Perfect of reply, used by one who, having gone, has forgotten the going, or is unwilling to admit it.

597. Parokkhāyañca ka. 458; rū. 461; nī. 939; caṃ. 5.1.3; pā. 6.1.2.

597. And in the Perfect tense.

Parokkhamhi pubbakkharaṃ ekassaraṃ dverūpaṃ hoti, casaddena aññasmimpi dvedverūpaṃ sijjhati.

In the Perfect tense, the preceding syllable containing a single vowel is reduplicated; and by the word 'ca', reduplication is also established elsewhere.

Caṅkamati, daddallati, dadāti, jahāti, juhoti, lolupo, momūho.

Caṅkamati (he walks back and forth), daddallati (it shines brightly), dadāti (he gives), jahāti (he abandons), juhoti (he sacrifices), lolupo (greedy), momūho (greatly deluded).

598. Dutiyacatutthānaṃ paṭhamatatiyā ka. 461; rū. 464; nī. 942.

598. The second and fourth consonants become the first and third.

Dvitte pubbesaṃ dutiya, catutthānaṃ kamena paṭhama, tatiyā honti.

In reduplication, the second and fourth consonants of the preceding syllable become the first and third respectively.

599. Pubbassa a ka. 450; rū. 463; nī. 946; caṃ. 6.2.126; pā. 7.4.73.

599. The vowel of the preceding syllable becomes 'a'.

Dvitte pubbassa bhūssa anto a hoti.

In reduplication, the vowel of the preceding syllable of the root 'bhū' becomes 'a'.

600. Bhūssa vuka ka. 475; rū. 465; nī. 956; caṃ. 5.3.92; pā. 6.4.88.

600. For 'bhū', the augment 'vuka'.

Dvitte bhūdhātussa ante vuka hoti, vāgamo hotīti attho.

In reduplication, 'vuka' occurs at the end of the root 'bhū', meaning there is an augment 'va'.

“Tatthappanādo tumulo babhūvā”ti jā. 2.22.1437 pāḷi.

Thus the Pāli text: “There a tumultuous din arose.”

So kira rājā babhūva, te kira rājāno babhūvu, tvaṃ babhūve.

It seems he became king; it seems they became kings; you became.

‘A ī ssā ssatyādīnaṃ byañjanassiu’ iti suttena byañjanādimhi iāgamo, tumhe babhūvittha, ahaṃ babhūvaṃ, mayaṃ babhūvimha[M 0.0379], so babhūvittha, te babhūvire, tvaṃ babhūvittho, tumhe babhūvivho, ahaṃ babhūviṃ, mayaṃ babhūvimhe, imāni suddhakatturūpāni.

By the rule ‘A ī ssā ssatyādīnaṃ byañjanassiu’, the augment ‘i’ is added before an ending beginning with a consonant: tumhe babhūvittha (you [plural] became), ahaṃ babhūvaṃ (I became), mayaṃ babhūvimha (we became); so babhūvittha (he became), te babhūvire (they became), tvaṃ babhūvittho (you [singular] became), tumhe babhūvivho (you [plural] became), ahaṃ babhūviṃ (I became), mayaṃ babhūvimhe (we became)—these are the middle voice forms.

‘Kyo bhāvakammesvaparokkhesū’ti paṭisiddhattā parokkhamhi bhāvakammesu yapaccayo na hoti, ‘tena kira bhogo anubabhūvittha, tena bhogo anubabhūvire’tiādinā yojetabbaṃ.

Since it is prohibited by the rule ‘Kyo bhāvakammesvaparokkhesū’, the affix ‘ya’ does not occur in the perfect tense in impersonal and passive constructions. It should be construed with examples such as ‘by him, it seems, wealth was enjoyed; by them, wealth was enjoyed,’ and so on.

Iti parokkhā.

Thus, the perfect tense.

Ssatyādi

The Future Tense Endings (Ssatyādi)

Atha ssatyādi vuccate.

Now, the future tense endings (ssatyādi) are explained.

601. Bhavissati ssati ssanti ssasi ssatha ssāmi ssāma ssate ssante ssase ssavhe ssaṃ ssāmhe ka. 421; rū. 473; nī. 892; caṃ. 1.3.2; pā. 3.3.13.

601. In the future tense: ssati, ssanti, ssasi, ssatha, ssāmi, ssāma, ssate, ssante, ssase, ssavhe, ssaṃ, ssāmhe.

Bhavissatīti bhavissanto, anāgatakālo, tasmiṃ bhavissati kāle kriyatthassa tyādayo honti.

The future tense (bhavissati) is that which is about to be (bhavissanta), the time yet to come. In that future time, the verbal endings beginning with 'ti' occur.

602. Nāme garahāvimhayesu ka. 421; rū. 473; nī. 893; caṃ. 1.3.109, 115; pā. 3.3.143, 150.

602. When the particle 'nāma' is used, and in blame and wonder.

Nipātanāmayoge garahāyañca vimhaye ca ssatyādayo honti, atītakālepi ssatyādīnaṃ uppattidīpanatthamidaṃ suttaṃ, anutthunana, paccānutāpa, paccānumodanādīnipi ettha saṅgayhanti.

When the particle 'nāma' is used, and in blame and wonder, the ssatyādi endings occur. This rule is to illustrate the occurrence of the ssatyādi endings even in the past tense. Lamentation, remorse, approval, and so on, are also included here.

Tattha garahāyaṃ-atthi nāma tāta sudinna ābhidosikaṃ kummāsaṃ paribhuñjissasi pārā. 32.

Therein, in blame: ‘Is it possible, dear Sudinna, that you would eat leftover sour gruel?’

Vimhaye-yatra [M 0.0380] hi nāma saññī samāno pañcamattānaṃ sakaṭasatānaṃ saddaṃ na sossati dī. ni. 2.192.

In wonder: ‘How is it possible that, being conscious, one would not hear the sound of five hundred carts?’

Anutthunanādīsu-na attanā paṭicodessaṃ, na gaṇassa ārocessaṃ pāci. 665, na pubbe dhanamesissaṃ jā. 1.12.50, iti pacchānutappati jā. 1.12.53, bhūtānaṃ nāpacāyissaṃ, pahu santo na posissaṃ, paradāraṃ asevissaṃ jā. 1.12.54, na pubbe payirupāsissaṃ jā. 1.12.58, iti pacchānutappati jā. 1.12.50, anekajātisaṃsāraṃ, sandhāvissaṃ anibbisaṃ dha. pa. 153.

In lamentation and so on: ‘Alas, I did not reprove myself, nor inform the community, nor seek wealth beforehand’—thus one regrets later. ‘Alas, I did not respect beings; though able, I did not support them; I consorted with another’s wife; I did not attend upon the wise beforehand’—thus one regrets later. ‘Through the endless cycle of many births I have wandered, not finding an end.’

Katthaci pana gāthāvasena ekasakāralopo, mitto mittassa pāniyaṃ, adinnaṃ paribhuñjisaṃ jā. 1.11.59, nirayamhi apaccisaṃ therīgā. 438, gacchanto naṃ udakkhisaṃ gavesitabbaṃ, yoniso paccavekkhisaṃ theragā. 347 iccādi.

However, in some places, by way of verse, there is elision of a single ‘sa’ sound, as in: ‘A friend’s water for a friend,’ ‘I consumed what was not given,’ ‘In hell, I was cooked,’ ‘Going, I saw him,’ ‘I reflected wisely,’ and so on.

‘A ī ssā ssatyādīnaṃ byañjanassiu’ iti iāgamo, bhavissati, bhavissanti, bhavissare, bhavissasi, bhavissatha, bhavissāmi, bhavissāma, bhavissate, bhavissante, bhavissare, bhavissase, bhavissavhe, bhavissaṃ, bhavissāmhe.

By the rule ‘A ī ssā ssatyādīnaṃ byañjanassiu’, the augment ‘i’ is added: bhavissati, bhavissanti, bhavissare, bhavissasi, bhavissatha, bhavissāmi, bhavissāma, bhavissate, bhavissante, bhavissare, bhavissase, bhavissavhe, bhavissaṃ, bhavissāmhe.

Anubhossati, anubhossanti, anubhossare iccādi suddhakatturūpaṃ.

Anubhossati, anubhossanti, anubhossare, and so on, are the active voice forms.

Anubhūyissati, anubhūyissanti, anubhūyissare.

Anubhūyissati, anubhūyissanti, anubhūyissare.

603. Kyassa sse ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

603. Kyassa sse.

Kyassa lopo hoti vā ssakāravati vibhattimhi.

The elision of ‘kya’ occurs optionally in a verbal ending containing ‘ssa’.

Tena maggo gamissati, gamīyissati vā, tena maggo agamissā, agamīyissā vāti vikappena kyassa lopo.

By him, the path will be gone, or it will be gone; by him, the path would have been gone, or it would have been gone—thus the elision of ‘kya’ occurs optionally.

Tena [M 0.0381] bhogo anubhavissati, anubhūyissati vā, tena bhogā anubhavissanti, anubhūyissanti vā iccādi suddhakammarūpaṃ.

By him, enjoyment will be experienced, or it will be experienced; by him, enjoyments will be experienced, or they will be experienced, and so on—this is the pure passive form.

Bhāvissati, ‘ūlasse’ti issa e, bhāvessati, bhāvayissatiiccādi hetukatturūpaṃ.

Bhāvissati; by the rule ‘ūlasse’, ‘issa’ becomes ‘e’, hence bhāvessati; bhāvayissati, and so on—such are the causative active forms.

Tena maggo bhāvīyissati, maggā bhāvīyissanti iccādi hetukammarūpaṃ.

By him, the path will be caused to be cultivated, paths will be caused to be cultivated, and so on—this is the causative passive form.

Iti ssatyādi.

Thus ends the section on the future tense endings beginning with ‘ssati’.

Ssādi

The Conditional Mood Endings

Atha ssādi vuccate.

Now, the conditional mood endings beginning with ‘ssa’ are explained.

604. Eyyādotipattiyaṃ ssā ssaṃsu sse ssatha ssaṃ ssāmhā ssatha ssiṃsu ssase ssavhe ssiṃ ssāmhase ka. 422; rū. 475; nī. 895; caṃ. 1.3.107; pā. 3.3.139; eyyādo vātipattiyaṃ (bahūsu).

604. In the conditional mood (kriyātipatti), which is in the domain of the optative (`eyyādi`): ssā, ssaṃsu, sse, ssatha, ssaṃ, ssāmhā, ssatha, ssiṃsu, ssase, ssavhe, ssiṃ, ssāmhase.

Eyyādivisaye kriyātipattiyaṃ ssādayo bhavanti. Eyyādivisayo nāma hetuphalakriyāsambhavo, tadubhayakriyāya abhāvo kriyātipatti.

In the domain of the optative (`eyyādi`), the endings beginning with `ssā` occur for the conditional (`kriyātipatti`). The domain of the optative is defined as the possibility of a cause-and-effect action; the non-occurrence of both those actions is the conditional (`kriyātipatti`).

Sā duvidhā atītā ca anāgatā ca.

It is of two kinds: past and future.

Tattha atītāyaṃ-sace so paṭhamavaye pabbajjaṃ alabhissā, arahā abhavissā ‘sace pana nikkhamitvā pabbajissa, arahattaṃ pāpuṇissa’ (dhammapada aṭṭha. 1) iccādi.

Therein, regarding the past: ‘If he had obtained the going forth in the first stage of life, he would have become an arahant,’ and so on.

Anāgatāyaṃ-sacāhaṃ na gamissaṃ, mahājāniyo so abhavissā iccādi.

Regarding the future: ‘If I were not to go, it would be a great loss for him,’ and so on.

‘Āīssādīsvaña [M 0.0382] vā’iti dhātvādimhi vikappena akārāgamo,‘a īssā ssatyādīnaṃ byañjanassiu’ iti ssādīsu iāgamo, abhavissā, bhavissā, abhavissaṃsu, bhavissaṃsu, abhavisse, bhavisse, abhavissatha, bhavissatha, abhavissaṃ, bhavissaṃ, abhavissāmhā, bhavissāmhā, abhavissatha, bhavissatha, abhavissiṃsu, bhavissiṃsu, abhavissase, bhavissase, abhavissavhe, bhavissavhe, abhavissiṃ, bhavissiṃ, abhavissāmhase, bhavissāmhase.

By the rule ‘Āīssādīsvaña vā’, the augment ‘a’ is optionally prefixed to the root; by the rule ‘a īssā ssatyādīnaṃ byañjanassiu’, the augment ‘i’ is inserted before the endings beginning with ‘ssa’: abhavissā, bhavissā, abhavissaṃsu, bhavissaṃsu, abhavisse, bhavisse, abhavissatha, bhavissatha, abhavissaṃ, bhavissaṃ, abhavissāmhā, bhavissāmhā, abhavissatha, bhavissatha, abhavissiṃsu, bhavissiṃsu, abhavissase, bhavissase, abhavissavhe, bhavissavhe, abhavissiṃ, bhavissiṃ, abhavissāmhase, bhavissāmhase.

‘Āīū’iccādinā ssā, ssāmhānaṃ rassatte-so abhavissa, bhavissa, mayaṃ abhavissāmha, bhavissāmha. ‘Eyyāthasse’iccādinā ssessa atte-tvaṃ abhavissa, bhavissa iccādīni rūpacatukkāni yathāsambhavaṃ yojetabbāni.

By the rule ‘Āīū’, etc., with the shortening of ‘ssā’ and ‘ssāmhā’: so abhavissa, bhavissa; mayaṃ abhavissāmha, bhavissāmha. By the rule ‘Eyyāthasse’, etc., with ‘sse’ becoming ‘a’: tvaṃ abhavissa, bhavissa. And so on, these fourfold forms should be applied as is possible.

Itissādi.

Thus ends the section on the conditional mood endings.

Bhūdhāturūpaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The forms of the root ‘bhū’ are concluded.

Aṭṭhavibhattuppattirāsi niṭṭhito.

The compilation on the origin of the eight verbal endings is concluded.

Bhūvādigaṇa

The Bhū Group of Roots

Sarantadhātu

Vowel-ending Roots

Ākārantadhāturūpa

Forms of Ā-ending Roots

Ito paṭṭhāya sarantadhātuyo sarānukkamena, byañjanantadhātuyo akkharānukkamena vuccante.

From here onward, vowel-ending roots are stated in the order of vowels, and consonant-ending roots are stated in alphabetical order.

Kaccāyanaganthe anekassaradhātuyo idha byañjanantadhātuyo nāma. Tasmā idha dhātvantasaralopakiccaṃ nāma natthi.

In the Kaccāyana grammar, many vowel-ending roots are here termed consonant-ending roots. Therefore, in this system, there is no operation for the elision of the final vowel of a root.

Khā, khyā-kathane, gā-sadde, ghā-gandhopādāne, ñā-paññāyane avabodhane ca, ṭhā-gatinivattiyaṃ, tā-pālane, thā-ṭhāne[M 0.0383], dā-dāne, dhā-dhāraṇe, pā-pāne, phā-vuddhiyaṃ, bhā-dittiyaṃ, mā-māne, yā-gatiyaṃ, lā-ādāne chedane ca, vā-gati, bandha, gandhanesu, sā-assādane tanukaraṇe antakammani ca, hā-cāge, nhā-soceyye.

‘Khā’, ‘khyā’—in the sense of speaking; ‘gā’—in the sense of sound; ‘ghā’—in the sense of smelling and taking; ‘ñā’—in the sense of knowing and understanding; ‘ṭhā’—in the sense of cessation of movement; ‘tā’—in the sense of protecting; ‘thā’—in the sense of standing; ‘dā’—in the sense of giving; ‘dhā’—in the sense of holding; ‘pā’—in the sense of drinking; ‘phā’—in the sense of increasing; ‘bhā’—in the sense of shining; ‘mā’—in the sense of measuring; ‘yā’—in the sense of going; ‘lā’—in the sense of taking and cutting; ‘vā’—in the sense of going, binding, and smelling; ‘sā’—in the sense of tasting, diminishing, and destroying; ‘hā’—in the sense of abandoning; ‘nhā’—in the sense of cleansing.

Tyādyuppatti, kattarilo, mahāvuttinā sare pare ādantamhā kvaci yāgamo, akkhāti. Parassaralopo, akkhāyati, kriyaṃ ākhyāti, ākhyāyati, jātiṃ akkhāhi pucchito su. ni. 423, saṅgāyati, saṅgāyiṃsu mahesayo vi. va. aṭṭha. ganthārambhakathā, gandhaṃ ghāyati, paññāyati, paññāyanti, paññāyatu, paññāyantu.

The origin of `ti`, etc. In the active voice. By the great rule, when a vowel follows, the augment `yā` sometimes comes after a root ending in `ā`; `akkhāti`. Elision of the following vowel; `akkhāyati`. `kriyaṃ ākhyāti`, `ākhyāyati`, `jātiṃ akkhāhi pucchito`, `saṅgāyati`, `saṅgāyiṃsu mahesayo`, `gandhaṃ ghāyati`, `paññāyati`, `paññāyanti`, `paññāyatu`, `paññāyantu`.

Kamme kyo, dhammo ñāyati, dhammā ñāyanti, viññāyati, viññāyanti.

In the passive, the suffix `kya` is used: dhammo ñāyati, dhammā ñāyanti, viññāyati, viññāyanti.

Payojakabyāpāre-ṇāpi, ñāpeti, ñāpenti, ñāpayati, ñāpayanti.

In the causative function, the suffix `ṇāpi` is used: ñāpeti, ñāpenti, ñāpayati, ñāpayanti.

Kamme-ñāpīyati, ñāpīyanti, ṭhāti, ṭhānti, opupphā padmā ṭhānti, mālāva ganthitā ṭhānti, dhajaggāneva dissare jā. 2.22.1989.

In the passive voice: ñāpīyati (it is made known), ñāpīyanti (they are made known). Examples for ṭhā-: ṭhāti (it stands), ṭhānti (they stand), opupphā padmā ṭhānti (fully blossomed lotuses stand), mālāva ganthitā ṭhānti (strung garlands stand), dhajaggāneva dissare (they appear like the tops of banners).

605. Ñcīlasse ka. 510; rū. 487; nī. 1023.

605. Of the suffixes `ī` (with indicatory `ñ`) and `la`.

Ñānubandhassa īāgamassa ca kattari vihitassa lapaccayassa ca kvaci ettaṃ hotīti lassa ettaṃ.

For the suffix `ī` with the indicatory letter `ñ`, and for the suffix `la` prescribed in the agentive, the letter `e` sometimes occurs; thus, `e` is the substitute for `la`.

Adhiṭṭheti, adhiṭṭhenti.

Adhiṭṭheti (he resolves), adhiṭṭhenti (they resolve).

606. Ṭhāpānaṃ tiṭṭhapivā ka. 468-9; rū. 492-4; nī. 949.

606. Of `ṭhā` and `pā`, `tiṭṭha` and `pivā` (are the respective substitutes).

Ṭhā, pānaṃ tiṭṭha, pivā honti nta, māna, tyādīsu.

`Ṭhā` and `pā` become `tiṭṭha` and `pivā` respectively, before suffixes such as `nta`, `māna`, and `ti`.

Tiṭṭhati, tiṭṭhanti.

Tiṭṭhati (he stands), tiṭṭhanti (they stand).

607. Pādito ṭhāssa vā ṭhaho kvaci ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

607. After a prefix, `ṭhaho` is sometimes optionally the substitute for `ṭhā`.

Pādayo [M 0.0384] upasaggā pādi nāma, pādito parassa ṭhāssa ṭhaho hoti vā kvaci.

Prefixes such as `pā` are called `pādi`. For the root `ṭhā` following a prefix, `ṭhaho` is sometimes optionally the substitute.

Saṇṭhahati, saṇṭhahanti, saṇṭhāti, saṇṭhānti, upaṭṭhahati, upaṭṭhahanti, upaṭṭhāti, upaṭṭhānti.

Saṇṭhahati (he stands firm), saṇṭhahanti (they stand firm), saṇṭhāti (he stands firm), saṇṭhānti (they stand firm); upaṭṭhahati (he attends), upaṭṭhahanti (they attend), upaṭṭhāti (he attends), upaṭṭhānti (they attend).

Kamme –

In the passive voice:

608. Aññādissi kye ka. 502; rū. 493; nī. 1015; ‘aññādissāsīkye’ (bahūsu).

608. Of the final `ā` of other roots, `i` (is the substitute) when `kya` follows.

Ñādito aññassa ākārantakriyatthassa i hoti kye paramhi.

When `kya` follows, `i` is the substitute for the final `ā` of a verbal root, other than `ñā` and so forth.

Adhiṭṭhīyati, adhiṭṭhīyanti, upaṭṭhīyati, upaṭṭhīyanti.

Adhiṭṭhīyati (it is resolved), adhiṭṭhīyanti (they are resolved); upaṭṭhīyati (it is attended to), upaṭṭhīyanti (they are attended to).

Aññādissāti kiṃ? Ñāyati, ñāyanti, ākkhāyati, ākkhāyanti, ākhyāyati, ākhyāyanti.

Why is `aññādissa` stated? To exclude forms such as: ñāyati (it is known), ñāyanti (they are known); ākkhāyati (it is spoken), ākkhāyanti (they are spoken); ākhyāyati (it is declared), ākhyāyanti (they are declared).

Ṇāpimhi-patiṭṭhāpeti, patiṭṭhāpenti, patiṭṭhāpayati, patiṭṭhāpayanti.

In the causative with `ṇāpi`: patiṭṭhāpeti (he establishes), patiṭṭhāpenti (they establish); patiṭṭhāpayati (he causes to establish), patiṭṭhāpayanti (they cause to establish).

Ajjhattanimhi vikappena sāgamo, aṭṭhāsi, patiṭṭhāsi, adhiṭṭhahi, adhiṭṭhāsi, adhiṭṭhesi, saṇṭhahi, saṇṭhāsi, upaṭṭhahi, upaṭṭhāsi.

In the Ajjhattanī (Aorist), there is optionally the augment `sa`: aṭṭhāsi (he stood), patiṭṭhāsi (he established), adhiṭṭhahi (he resolved), adhiṭṭhāsi (he resolved), adhiṭṭhesi (he resolved), saṇṭhahi (he stood firm), saṇṭhāsi (he stood firm), upaṭṭhahi (he attended), upaṭṭhāsi (he attended).

‘Uṃssiṃsvaṃsū’ti uṃssa iṃsu, aṃsu, adhiṭṭhahiṃsu, saṇṭhahiṃsu, upaṭṭhahiṃsu. Atthamentamhi sūriye, vāḷā panthe upaṭṭhahuṃ jā. 2.22.2186. Aṭṭhaṃsu, upaṭṭhahaṃsu.

By the rule `Uṃssiṃsvaṃsū`, for `uṃ` there is `iṃsu` or `aṃsu`. Examples: adhiṭṭhahiṃsu (they resolved), saṇṭhahiṃsu (they stood firm), upaṭṭhahiṃsu (they attended). Example from scripture: `Atthamentamhi sūriye, vāḷā panthe upaṭṭhahuṃ` (When the sun was setting, beasts of prey appeared on the path). Aṭṭhaṃsu (they stood), upaṭṭhahaṃsu (they attended).

Parachakke-aṭṭhā buddhassa santike su. ni. 431.

In the Parokkhā (Perfect tense): `aṭṭhā buddhassa santike` (he stood near the Buddha).

Kamme-adhiṭṭhiyi, adhiṭṭhiyiṃsu, upaṭṭhiyi, upaṭṭhiyiṃsu.

In the passive voice: adhiṭṭhiyi (it was resolved), adhiṭṭhiyiṃsu (they were resolved); upaṭṭhiyi (it was attended to), upaṭṭhiyiṃsu (they were attended to).

Ṇāpimhi-patiṭṭhāpesi[M 0.0385], patiṭṭhāpayi, saṇṭhāpesi, saṇṭhāpayi.

In the causative with `ṇāpi`: patiṭṭhāpesi (he established), patiṭṭhāpayi (he caused to establish); saṇṭhāpesi (he established firmly), saṇṭhāpayi (he caused to establish firmly).

‘Eontāsu’nti uṃssasuṃ, saralopo, aṭṭhāsuṃ, upaṭṭhāsuṃ, patiṭṭhāpesuṃ, saṇṭhāpesuṃ, patiṭṭhāpayuṃ, saṇṭhāpayuṃ, patiṭṭhāpayiṃsu, saṇṭhāpayiṃsu.

By the rule `Eontāsuṃ`, for `uṃ` there is `suṃ`, and elision of a vowel occurs. Examples: aṭṭhāsuṃ (they stood), upaṭṭhāsuṃ (they attended); patiṭṭhāpesuṃ (they established), saṇṭhāpesuṃ (they established firmly); patiṭṭhāpayuṃ (they caused to establish), saṇṭhāpayuṃ (they caused to establish firmly); patiṭṭhāpayiṃsu (they caused to establish), saṇṭhāpayiṃsu (they caused to establish firmly).

Ssatyādimhi-ṭhassati, ṭhassanti, rassattaṃ, upaṭṭhissati, upaṭṭhissanti, ahaṃ bhotiṃ upaṭṭhissaṃ jā. 2.22.1934, saṇṭhahissati, saṇṭhahissanti.

In the future tense (`ssati`, etc.): ṭhassati (he will stand), ṭhassanti (they will stand). With shortening: upaṭṭhissati (he will attend), upaṭṭhissanti (they will attend); `ahaṃ bhotiṃ upaṭṭhissaṃ` (I will attend to the lady); saṇṭhahissati (he will stand firm), saṇṭhahissanti (they will stand firm).

Ṇāpimhi-patiṭṭhāpessati, patiṭṭhāpessanti.

In the causative with `ṇāpi`: patiṭṭhāpessati (he will establish), patiṭṭhāpessanti (they will establish).

Tā-pālane, bhayaṃ tāyati.

The root `tā` in the sense of protecting: `bhayaṃ tāyati` (he protects from fear).

Thā-ṭhāne, avatthāti, avatthāyati, vitthāyati, vitthāyanti, mā kho vitthāsi mahāva. 126.

The root `thā` in the sense of standing: avatthāti (it stands), avatthāyati (it stands); vitthāyati (it spreads out), vitthāyanti (they spread out); `mā kho vitthāsi` (do not indeed spread out).

Dā-dāne, ‘ūlasse’ti lassa ettaṃ, deti, denti, desi, detha, demi, dema.

The root `dā` in the sense of giving: by the rule `ūlasse`, `e` is the substitute for the `la`-endings. Examples: deti (he gives), denti (they give), desi (you give), detha (you all give), demi (I give), dema (we give).

‘Parokkhāyañcā’ti sutte casaddena dāssa dvittaṃ. ‘Rasso pubbassā’ti pubbassa rassattaṃ, dadāti, dadanti, dadāsi, dadātha, dadāmi, dadāma.

In the sutta `Parokkhāyañcā`, by the word `ca`, there is doubling of `dā`. By the rule `Rasso pubbassā`, there is shortening of the preceding vowel. Examples: dadāti (he gives), dadanti (they give), dadāsi (you give), dadātha (you all give), dadāmi (I give), dadāma (we give).

609. Dāssa daṃ vā mimesvadvitte ka. 482; rū. 508; nī. 972.

609. For `dā` when not doubled, `daṃ` is optionally the substitute before `mi` and `me`.

Advitte dāssa daṃ hoti vā mi, mesu, niggahītassa vaggantattaṃ.

For `dā` when not doubled, `daṃ` is optionally the substitute before the suffixes `mi` and `me`. The niggahīta (`ṃ`) is assimilated to the nasal of the subsequent consonant's class.

Dammi, damma.

Dammi, I give; damma, we give.

Advitteti kiṃ? Dadāmi, dadāma.

What is meant by 'without doubling'? Dadāmi, I give; dadāma, we give.

610. Dāssiyaṅa ka. 502; rū. 493; nī. 1014.

610. The formation of dāssiya (slavery).

Pādito [M 0.0386] parassa dāssa iyaṅa hoti kvaci.

After pādi, the suffix iyaṅa is sometimes applied to a following dāssa.

‘Iyaṅa’ iti suttavibhattena aññadhātūnampi. Jā-hāniyaṃ, appena bahuṃ jiyyāma jā. 1.2.52, tassevā’nuvidhiyyati jā. 1.2.67, vidhurassa hadayaṃ dhaniyati jā. 2.22.1350, nihīyati tassa yaso jā. 1.10.60; a. ni. 4.17, eko rājā vihiyyasi jā. 2.22.1750, so pahīyissati saṃ. ni. 1.249 iccādi.

By the analysis of the sutta, the suffix ‘iyaṅa’ is also applied to other roots. For example: jā-hāniyaṃ (in decline); appena bahuṃ jiyyāma (by little, we lose much); tassevā’nuvidhiyyati (that very one is followed); vidhurassa hadayaṃ dhaniyati (the heart of the bereaved is shaken); nihīyati tassa yaso (his fame is lost); eko rājā vihiyyasi (one king was lost); so pahīyissati (he will be abandoned), and so on.

Ādiyati, ādiyanti, upādiyati, upādiyanti, samādiyati, samādiyanti, sikkhāpadaṃ samādiyāmi khu. pā. 2.1, vattaṃ samādiyāmi cūḷava. 85.

Ādiyati, he takes; ādiyanti, they take. Upādiyati, he clings; upādiyanti, they cling. Samādiyati, he undertakes; samādiyanti, they undertake. Sikkhāpadaṃ samādiyāmi, I undertake the training rule; vattaṃ samādiyāmi, I undertake the practice.

611. Gama vada dānaṃ ghamma vajja dajjā ka. 499-500-1; rū. 443-486-507; nī. 1013, 1005-1006.

611. For the roots gam, vad, and dā, the substitutes are ghamma, vajja, and dajjā.

Etesaṃ ghamma, vajja, dajjā honti vā nta, māna, tyādīsu.

For these roots, the forms ghamma, vajja, and dajjā optionally occur before suffixes such as nta, māna, ti, and so on.

Dajjati, dajjanti, dajjasi, dajjatha, dajjāmi, dajjāma.

Dajjati, he gives; dajjanti, they give; dajjasi, you give; dajjatha, you all give; dajjāmi, I give; dajjāma, we give.

‘Ūlasse’ti lassa ettaṃ, dajjeti, dajjenti.

By the rule ‘Ūlasse,’ la becomes e: dajjeti, dajjenti.

Kamme ‘aññādissi kye’ti kyamhi āssa ittaṃ, diyati, diyanti.

In the passive, by the rule ‘aññādissi kye,’ when the suffix kya follows, the ā of the root becomes i: diyati, diyanti.

Dīghatte-dīyati, dīyanti.

With lengthening: dīyati, dīyanti.

Dvitte-diyyati, diyyanti, dajjīyati, dajjīyanti.

With doubling: diyyati, diyyanti; dajjīyati, dajjīyanti.

Ṇāpimhi-dāpeti, dāpenti, dāpayati, dāpayanti.

In the causative: dāpeti, dāpenti; dāpayati, dāpayanti.

Pādipubbe rasso, samādapeti ma. ni. 2.387; 3.276, samādapenti, samādapayati, samādapayanti.

When a prefix is present, there is shortening: samādapeti, samādapenti; samādapayati, samādapayanti.

Kamme-dāpīyati[M 0.0387], dāpīyanti, samādapīyati, samādapīyanti.

In the passive: dāpīyati, dāpīyanti; samādapīyati, samādapīyanti.

Eyyādimhi mahāvuttinā dajjato eyyādīnaṃ antassa eyyassa lopo vā, dānaṃ dajjā, dadeyya, dajjuṃ, dadeyyuṃ, dajjāsi, dadeyyāsi, dajjātha, dadeyyātha, dajjāmi, dadeyyāmi, dajjāma, dadeyyāma, ahaṃ dajjaṃ, dadeyyaṃ, mayaṃ dajjāmhe, dadeyyāmhe.

In the optative, by the great rule, for the base dajjā and others, the final eyya of the ending is optionally elided: dānaṃ dajjā, dadeyya; dajjuṃ, dadeyyuṃ; dajjāsi, dadeyyāsi; dajjātha, dadeyyātha; dajjāmi, dadeyyāmi; dajjāma, dadeyyāma; ahaṃ dajjaṃ, dadeyyaṃ; mayaṃ dajjāmhe, dadeyyāmhe.

Atrimā pāḷī-dajjā sappuriso dānaṃ jā. 2.22.2261, upāyanāni me dajjuṃ jā. 2.22.24, mātaraṃ kena dosena, dajjāsi dakarakkhino jā 1.16.227. Tāni ammāya dajjesi jā. 2.22.2149, chaṭṭhāhaṃ dajjamattānaṃ, neva dajjaṃ mahosadhaṃ jā. 1.16.225.

Here are examples from the Pāli: A virtuous person should give a gift. They should give me offerings. For what fault of the mother would you give her to the water-demon? You gave those to my mother. I would give myself for six days, but I would not give Mahosadha.

Ajjhattanimhi-adadi, adāsi, adaduṃ, adaṃsu, adajji, adajjuṃ, tvaṃ adado. Varañce me ado sakka jā. 2.17.142.

In the aorist: adadi, adāsi; adaduṃ, adaṃsu; adajji, adajjuṃ; tvaṃ adado. If you would give me a boon, Sakka.

Parachakke-so dānaṃ adā, brāhmaṇassa adā dānaṃ, sivīnaṃ raṭṭhavaḍḍhano jā. 2.22.2117.

In the perfect tense: so dānaṃ adā, he gave a gift; brāhmaṇassa adā dānaṃ, he gave a gift to the brahmin; sivīnaṃ raṭṭhavaḍḍhano, the increaser of the Sivi kingdom.

Ssatyādimhi-dāssati, dāssanti, dadissati, dadissanti, dajjissati, dajjissanti.

In the future tense: dāssati, dāssanti; dadissati, dadissanti; dajjissati, dajjissanti.

Dāiccassa diccha, pavecchādesampi icchanti, vipulaṃ annaṃ pānañca, samaṇānaṃ pavecchasi therīgā. 272. Appasmeke pavecchanti, bahuneke na dicchare saṃ. ni. 1.33. Devo sammā dhāraṃ pavecchatu. Bhojanaṃ bhojanatthīnaṃ, sammadeva pavecchatha.

For the root dā, the substitute is diccha; they also accept the substitute paveccha. You provide abundant food and drink to ascetics. Some provide from a little; many do not wish to give. May the deva rightly provide a stream of rain. Rightly provide food to those in need of food.

Dhā-dhāraṇe, sandhāti, vidhāti, nidheti, nidhenti. Vidheti, vidhenti.

The root Dhā is in the sense of holding: sandhāti, vidhāti, nidheti, nidhenti; vidheti, vidhenti.

‘Parokkhāyañcā’ti casaddena dvittaṃ. ‘Dutiyacatutthāna…’nti dhassa dattaṃ. ‘Rasso pubbassā’ti pubbassa rasso.

By the word ca in the rule ‘Parokkhāyañcā,’ there is doubling. By the rule ‘Dutiyacatutthāna…,’ dh becomes d. By the rule ‘Rasso pubbassā,’ the preceding syllable is shortened.

612. Dhāssa ho ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

612. Of dhā, there is ho.

Dvitte [M 0.0388] parassa dhāssa ho hoti.

When doubled, the following dhā becomes ho.

Saddahāti, saddahati vā. Saddahāti tathāgatassa bodhiṃ. Vidahāti, nidahāti, saddahanti, vidahanti, nidahanti.

Saddahāti, or saddahati. One has faith in the Tathāgata’s awakening. Vidahāti, nidahāti; saddahanti, vidahanti, nidahanti.

‘Mayadā sare’ti sutte ‘mayadā’ti suttavibhattiyā byañjanepi niggahītassa dattaṃ, kammaṃ saddahāti, kammaphalaṃ saddahāti, saddahanti, vatthaṃ paridahāti, paridahanti.

In the rule ‘Mayadā sare,’ by the analysis of the rule as ma-ya-dā, the niggahīta becomes d even before a consonant. Examples: one has faith in action (kammaṃ saddahāti), one has faith in the result of action (kammaphalaṃ saddahāti), saddahanti; one puts on a garment (vatthaṃ paridahāti), paridahanti.

Kamme-sandhīyati, sandhīyanti, sandhiyyati, sandhiyyanti, vidhiyyati. Navena sukhadukkhena, porāṇaṃ apidhiyyati jā. 1.2.114.

In the passive: sandhīyati, sandhīyanti; sandhiyyati, sandhiyyanti; vidhiyyati. By new pleasure and pain, the old is covered over.

Ṇāpimhi-nidhāpeti, nidhāpenti, nidhāpayati, nidhāpayanti.

In the causative: nidhāpeti, nidhāpenti; nidhāpayati, nidhāpayanti.

Kamme-nidhāpīyati, nidhāpīyanti.

In the passive: nidhāpīyati, nidhāpīyanti.

Eyyādimhi-saddaheyyaṃ, saddaheyyuṃ.

In the optative: saddaheyyaṃ, saddaheyyuṃ.

Īādimhi-saddahi, saddahiṃsu. Tatra bhikkhavo samādahiṃsu dī. ni. 2.332, samādahaṃsu vā.

In the aorist: saddahi, saddahiṃsu. There, the bhikkhus concentrated, or samādahaṃsu.

Pā-pāne, pāti, pānti.

The root ‘Pā’ is in the sense of drinking: pāti, pānti.

‘Ṭhāpānaṃ tiṭṭhapivā’ti pāssa pivo, pivati, pivanti.

According to the rule ‘Ṭhāpānaṃ tiṭṭhapivā,’ ‘pā’ becomes ‘pivo’; pivati, pivanti.

Kamme-pīyati, pīyanti.

In the passive: pīyati, pīyanti.

Ṇimhi-‘āssā ṇāpimhi yuka’ iti suttena ṇānubandhe āssa ante yāgamo, puttaṃ thaññaṃ pāyeti, pāyenti, pāyayati, pāyayanti.
