In the causative (ṇimhi), according to the rule ‘āssā ṇāpimhi yuka,’ when ‘ṇā’ is the affix, the augment ‘yā’ is added at the end of ‘ā.’ One gives milk to a child to drink: pāyeti, pāyenti; pāyayati, pāyayanti.

Kamme-pāyīyati, pāyīyanti.

In the passive: pāyīyati, pāyīyanti.

In the future tense: passati, passanti; pissati, pissanti.

Atrimā [M 0.0389] pāḷī-ayañhi te mayā’ruḷho, saro pissati lohitaṃ jā. 2.22.1968,aggodakāni pissāmi, yūthassa purato vajaṃ jā. 1.8.14. Naḷena vāriṃ pissāma, na ca maṃ tvaṃ vadhissasi jā. 1.1.20.

The following are examples from the Pāli canon: 'For this arrow, placed by me, will drink your blood'; 'I will drink the first water, going before the herd'; 'We will drink water with a reed, and you will not kill me.'

Bhā-dittiyaṃ, bhāti, rattimābhāti candimā dha. pa. 387, disā bhanti virocamānā ma. ni. 1.503, daddallamānā ābhanti vi. va. 738; jā. 2.22.508, paṭibhāti, paṭibhanti, paṭibhātu, paṭibhantu taṃ cunda bojjhaṅgā saṃ. ni. 5.197, tisso maṃ upamāyo paṭibhaṃsu ma. ni. 1.374, ratti vibhāti, vibhāyati.

Mā-māne, dvittaṃ rasso ca, mamāyati, mamāyanti. Yemaṃ kāyaṃ mamāyanti, andhā bālā puthujjanā theragā. 575.

'Mā'—in the sense of measuring—doubled and shortened, becomes 'mamāyati,' 'mamāyanti.' Those blind, foolish, ordinary people cling to this body as 'mine.'

Yā-gatiyaṃ, yāti, yanti, yāyati, yāyanti, yāyanta’ manuyāyanti jā. 2.22.1753, uyyāti, uyyanti, niyyāti, niyyanti dhīrā lokamhā, hitvā māraṃ savāhanaṃ. Anuyāti, anuyanti, anupariyāyati, anupariyāyanti.

Yā—in the sense of going: one goes, they go, one goes, they go; they follow one who goes; one goes forth, they go forth; the wise go forth from the world, having abandoned Māra with his host. One follows, they follow, one goes around, they go around.

Lā-ādāne, lāti.

Lā—in seizing: he seizes.

Vā-gati, gandhanesu, vāti devesu uttamo dha. pa. 56, vāto vāyati, vāyanti, nibbāti, nibbanti, nibbāyati, nibbāyanti, parinibbāti, parinibbāyati.

Vā—in going, in smelling: 'the best among the gods blows'; the wind blows, they blow; it is extinguished, they are extinguished, it is extinguished, they are extinguished; it is fully extinguished, it is fully extinguished.

Ṇāpimhi-nibbāpeti, nibbāpayati.

In the causative: he causes to be extinguished, he causes to be extinguished.

Īādimhi-parinibbāyi, parinibbāyiṃsu.

In the aorist: he was fully extinguished, they were fully extinguished.

Ssatyādimhi-parinibbissati, parinibbissanti, parinibbāyissati, parinibbāyissanti.

In the future tense: one will be fully extinguished, they will be fully extinguished, one will be fully extinguished, they will be fully extinguished.

Sā-assādana, tanukaraṇa, antakriyāsu, sāti, sāyati, sāyanti, pariyosāyanti.

Sā—in tasting, in reducing, in making an end: he tastes, he tastes, they taste, they bring to completion.

Ṇāpimhi-osāpeti[M 0.0390], pariyosāpeti, osāpayati, pariyosāpayati.

In the causative: he causes to end, he causes to be completely finished, he causes to end, he causes to be completely finished.

In the passive: it is brought to an end, it is utterly brought to an end.

Hā-cāge, pahāti, pahāyati, pahāyanti.

Hā—in abandoning: one abandons, he abandons, they abandon.

Kattu, kammani kyo, īñaāgamo, hiyyoti hiyyati poso jā. 1.15.348, nihiyyati tassa yaso a. ni. 4.17; jā. 1.10.60, tvaṃ eko avahiyyasi, dvittaṃ rasso ca.

In the active and passive, kyo (suffix), īñaāgamo (augment): 'hiyyoti', a person declines; his fame diminishes; you alone are left behind. Doubling and shortening (of the vowel) occur.

613. Kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā ka. 462-4; rū. 467-504; nī. 943-5; caṃ. 6.2.116; pā. 7.4.62.

613. The k-group sounds become c-group sounds.

Dvitte pubbesaṃ kavagga, hānaṃ cavagga, jā honti.

In reduplication, the preceding consonants of the k-group become those of the c-group, and 'h' becomes 'j'.

Jahāti, pajahāti, jahanti, pajahanti.

He abandons, he completely abandons, they abandon, they completely abandon.

Kamme-pahīyati, pahīyanti.

In the passive: it is abandoned, they are abandoned.

Rassatte-pahiyati, pahiyanti.

With shortening of the vowel: it is abandoned, they are abandoned.

Dvitte-pahiyyati, pahiyyanti, pajahīyati, pajahīyanti.

In doubling: it is abandoned, they are abandoned, it is relinquished, they are relinquished.

Ṇāpimhi-hāpeti, hāpenti, hāpayati, hāpayanti, jahāpeti, jahāpenti, jahāpayati, jahāpayanti.

In the causative: he causes to abandon, they cause to abandon, he causes to abandon, they cause to abandon, he causes to abandon, they cause to abandon, he causes to abandon, they cause to abandon.

Kamme-hāpīyati, jahāpīyati.

In the passive: it is caused to be abandoned, it is caused to be abandoned.

Īādimhi-pahāsi, pahāsuṃ, pajahi, pajahiṃsu.

In the aorist: he abandoned, they abandoned, he abandoned, they abandoned.

614. Hāto ha ka. 480; rū. 490; nī. 961.

614. From the root 'hā', it becomes 'ha'.

Hāto parassa ssa-kārassa ha hoti vā.

After the root 'hā', the following 'ssa' optionally becomes 'ha'.

“Hāhisi [M 0.0391] tvaṃ jīvaloka”nti jā. 1.5.36 pāḷi, hāhiti, hāhinti, hāhati, hāhanti, jahissati, hissati, aññamaññaṃ vadhitvāna, khippaṃ hissāma jīvitaṃ jā. 2.22.673.

The Pāli text is: 'You will abandon the world of the living.' He will abandon, they will abandon, he will abandon, they will abandon; he will abandon, he will abandon. 'Having struck one another, we will quickly abandon life.'

Nhā-soceyye, nhāti, nhāyati, nhāyanti.

Nhā—in purification: he bathes, he bathes, they bathe.

Mahāvuttinā byañjanavaḍḍhane, nahāti, nahāyati, nahāyanti.

According to the Mahāvutti, with the augmentation of a consonant: he bathes, he bathes, they bathe.

Iti bhūvādigaṇe ākārantadhāturūpaṃ.

Thus in the Bhūvādi group are the forms of roots ending in 'ā'.

Ivaṇṇantadhāturūpa

The forms of roots ending in 'i'.

I-gatiyaṃ ajjhāyane ca, khi-khaye pakāsane ca, cicaye, ji-jaye, ḍī-vehāsagatiyaṃ, nī-naye, bhī-bhaye, lī-laye, sī-saye, mhi-hāse.

I—in going and in recitation; khi—in destruction and in revealing; ci—in accumulating; ji—in conquering; ḍī—in flying in the sky; nī—in leading; bhī—in fearing; lī—in dissolving; sī—in lying down; mhi—in smiling.

Tyādyuppatti, kattari lo, eti, enti, esi, etha, emi, ema, veti, venti, sameti, samenti, abbheti, abbhenti, abhisameti, abhisamenti, aveti, aventi, samaveti, samaventi, apeti, apenti, upeti, upenti, anveti, anventi, acceti, accenti, pacceti, paccenti, ajjheti, ajjhenti, udeti, udenti, samudeti, samudenti, pariyeti, pariyenti, upayati, upayanti, accayati, accayanti, udayati, samudayati.

The formation of 'ti' and other endings, in the active voice: eti, enti, esi, etha, emi, ema, veti, venti, sameti, samenti, abbheti, abbhenti, abhisameti, abhisamenti, aveti, aventi, samaveti, samaventi, apeti, apenti, upeti, upenti, anveti, anventi, acceti, accenti, pacceti, paccenti, ajjheti, ajjhenti, udeti, udenti, samudeti, samudenti, pariyeti, pariyenti, upayati, upayanti, accayati, accayanti, udayati, samudayati.

Etu, sametu, entu, samentu, ehi, samehi, etha, sametha, etha byagghā nivattavho, paccupetha mahāvanaṃ jā. 1.3.66.

According to the Mahāvutti, after this root, there is elision of the 'e' of 'eyya' and other endings. 'And not having reached the end of suffering, a wise person should not place trust. When I send for you, then you should go, O Khattiya.'

By the rule 'eontā su', 'uṃ' becomes 'suṃ': they understood, they understood, they understood.

Ssatyādimhi –

In the future tense and so on:

The root is indicated by 'eti'; the sound 'ti' is an indicator. After this root 'i', the following 'ssa' optionally becomes 'hi'.

Ehiti, essati. Bodhirukkhamupehiti bu. vaṃ. 2.63, nerañjaramupehiti bu. vaṃ. 2.63, upessati, tadā ehinti me vasaṃ jā. 1.1.33, tato nibbānamehisi cūḷava. 382 tassuddānaṃ, na punaṃ jātijaraṃ upehisi dha. pa. 238. Suttavibhattena aññadhātūhipi, kathaṃ jīvihisi tvaṃ apa. thera 1.3.13, jāyihitippasādo jā. 2.17.145, paññāyihinti etā daharā jā. 2.17.197.

After 'ni', the 'ca' sound of 'ci' becomes 'cho'.

In the passive, the suffix 'ya'—

617. Lengthening of the vowel.

Kamme-nayāpīyati, nayāpīyanti.

In the passive voice: nayāpīyati, nayāpīyanti.

In the 'ssati'-initial forms: nessati, nessanti, nayissati, nayissanti.

In the passive voice: atisīyati, atisīyanti.

In the causative (ṇi): sāyeti, sāyayati. With dejected minds, they laid down.

Thus in the Bhūvādi group are the forms of roots ending in the vowel 'i'.

Uvaṇṇantadhāturūpa

Forms of roots ending in the vowel 'u'.

Cu-cavane, ju-sīghagamane, thu-abhitthavane, du-gatiyaṃ upatāpe ca, bhū-sattāyaṃ, yu-missane gatiyañca, ru-sadde, brū-viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, su-sandane janane ca, sū-pasavane, hu-dāne bhakkhane pūjāyaṃ sattiyañca, hū-sattāyaṃ.

Ṇimhi-cāveti, cāvayati.

Du-upatāpe, upaddavati, upaddavanti.

Yu-gatiyaṃ[M 0.0396], yavati.

Yu—in the sense of going: he goes.

Ru-sadde, ravati, ravanti, viravati, viravanti.

Brū-viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ –

Brū—in the sense of clear speech, in utterance—

618. Na brūsso.

618. Do not speak.

Byañjane pare brūssa o na hoti.

When a consonant follows, the 'ū' of 'brū' is not changed to 'o'.

Brūti.

He speaks.

619. Brūto tissīu ka. 520; rū. 502; nī. 1033; caṃ. 6.2.34; pā. 7.3.93.

619. Brūto tissīu.

Brūto tissa ādimhi īña hoti. Īmhi pubbalopo.

In 'Brūto tissa,' at the beginning, 'īña' occurs. When 'ī' is present, there is elision of the preceding vowel.

Bravīti.

He speaks.

620. For the vowels i and u, the replacements iyaṅa and uvaṅa occur when a vowel follows.

For roots ending in the vowels i and u, sometimes the replacements iyaṅa and uvaṅa occur when a vowel follows.

Bruvanti, brunti vā. “Ajānantā no pabruntī”ti pāḷi. Brūsi, brūtha, brūmi, brūma.

They speak, or they say. "The ignorant revile us," so the Pāli reads. You speak, you all speak, I speak, we speak.

621. Tyantīnaṃ ṭaṭū ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105; caṃ. 1.4.13; pā. 3.4.84.

621. For 'ti' and 'anti', 'ṭa' and 'ṭū' are substituted.

Ti, antīsu brūssa āha hoti, tesañca ṭa, ṭū honti.

When 'ti' and 'anti' follow, 'brū' becomes 'āha', and they are replaced by 'ṭa' and 'ṭū' respectively.

So āha, te āhu.

He said, they said.

Atrimā pāḷī-nibbānaṃ bhagavā āha, sabbaganthapamocanaṃ, āha tesañca yo nirodho mahāva. 60, yaṃ pare sukhato āhu, tadariyā āhu dukkhato. Yaṃ pare dukkhato āhu, tadariyā sukhato vidū su. ni. 767. Tattha ‘āhā’ti katheti. ‘Āhū’ti kathenti.

The following Pāli passage: "The Blessed One spoke of Nibbāna, the release from all bonds; he spoke of their cessation. What others call happiness, that the noble ones call suffering. What others call suffering, that the noble ones know as happiness." Therein, 'āha' means 'he speaks'; 'āhu' means 'they speak'.

Brūtu[M 0.0397], brūvantu, brūhi maṅgalamuttamaṃ khu. pā. 5.2, brūtha, brūmi, brūma.

Let him speak, let them speak; speak the highest blessing; you all speak, I speak, we speak.

Eyyādimhi-brūssa uvaṅa hoti, bruveyya, bruveyyuṃ.

When 'eyya' and so on follow, the 'uvaṅa' substitution occurs for 'brū': bruveyya, bruveyyuṃ.

Īādimhi sare pare brūssa ottaṃ, ossa ca avādeso, abravi, abravuṃ, abraviṃsu.

When an aorist ending such as 'ī' or another vowel follows, the 'ū' of 'brū' is changed to 'o', and that 'o' is substituted by 'ava': abravi, abravuṃ, abraviṃsu.

Uvādese-abruvi, abruvuṃ, abruviṃsu.

With the 'uva' substitution: abruvi, abruvuṃ, abruviṃsu.

Parokkhamhi –

In the perfect tense—

622. Aādīsvāho brūssa ka. 475; rū. 465; nī. 956.

622. When 'a' and so on follow, 'āha' is the substitute for 'brū'.

Aādīsu brūssa āha bhavati.

When 'a' and so on follow, 'brū' becomes 'āha'.

So āha, te āhu.

He said, they said.

623. Ussaṃsvāhā vā nī. 1036.

623. Optionally, 'aṃsu' for 'u' after 'āha'.

Āhādesamhā parassa uvacanassa aṃsu hoti vā.

After the substitute 'āha', the plural ending 'u' is optionally replaced by 'aṃsu'.

Te āhaṃsu, saccaṃ kirevamāhaṃsu, narā ekacciyā idha jā. 1.13.123.

They said. "Truly, indeed, some men here said thus."

Su-sandane, nadī savati, savanti, ābhavaggā savanti.

Su—in the sense of flowing: the river flows, they flow; they flow up to the summit of existence.

Sū-pasavane, puññaṃ pasavati cūḷava. 354, pasavanti.

In the sense of generating: he generates merit, they generate.

Hu-pūjāyaṃ, ‘parokkhāyañcā’ti dvittaṃ, ‘kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā’ti hassa jo, juhoti, juhonti.

The root 'hu' in the sense of worship: by the rule 'parokkhāyañcā,' there is reduplication; by the rule 'kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā,' 'h' becomes 'j'; thus, 'juhoti' (he offers), 'juhonti' (they offer).

Kamme-tena aggi hūyate.

In the passive voice: by him, fire is offered.

Ṇimhi-juhāveti, juhāvayati.

With the causative suffix 'ṇi': he causes to offer (juhāveti), he causes to offer (juhāvayati).

Ṇāpimhi-juhāpeti, juhāpayati.

With the causative suffix 'ṇāpi': he causes to offer (juhāpeti), he causes to offer (juhāpayati).

Hu-sattiyaṃ, pahoti, sampahoti, pahonti, sampahonti.

The root 'hu' in the sense of power: he is able (pahoti), he is fully able (sampahoti); they are able (pahonti), they are fully able (sampahonti).

Hū-sattāyaṃ[M 0.0398], hoti, honti, hotu, hontu.

The root 'hū' in the sense of being: he is (hoti), they are (honti); let him be (hotu), let them be (hontu).

Eyyādimhi- ‘yuvaṇṇānamiyaṅauvaṅa sare’ti dhātvantassa uvādeso, huveyya, huveyyuṃ.

When 'eyya' and so on follow: according to the rule 'yuvaṇṇānamiyaṅauvaṅa sare,' there is the substitution of 'uva' for the final vowel of the root, forming 'huveyya' and 'huveyyuṃ'.

Āādimhi-so ahuvā. Vaṇṇagandhaphalūpeto, amboyaṃ ahuvā pure jā. 1.2.71. Ahuvā te pure sakhā saṃ. ni. 1.50, te ahuvū, tvaṃ ahuvo, tumhe ahuvattha ma. ni. 1.215, jhāyatha bhikkhave mā pamādāttha, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha, ahuva, ahuvaṃ vā, ahuvamhā. “Akaramhasa te kiccaṃ, yaṃ balaṃ ahuvamhase jā. 1.4.29. Ahuvamheva mayaṃ pubbe, na nāhuvamhā”ti ma. ni. 1.180 pāḷiyo.

In the aorist tense: he was (ahuvā). 'Endowed with color, fragrance, and fruit, this mango existed before.' 'They were your friends before (ahuvā)'; they were (ahuvū), you were (ahuvo), you all were (ahuvattha). 'Meditate, monks, do not be heedless, do not later become regretful (ahuvattha).' I was (ahuva), or I was (ahuvaṃ); we were (ahuvamhā). 'We have done your task, with what strength we had. We indeed existed before; it is not that we did not exist,' so say the Pāli passages.

Īādimhi sāgamo, ahosi, pāturahosi.

When 'ī' and so on follow, there is the insertion of 's': it was (ahosi), it appeared (pāturahosi).

Mahāvuttinā īlopo rasso ca. Ahudeva bhayaṃ ahu chambhitattaṃ. Ahudeva kukkuccaṃ, ahu vippaṭisāro pārā. 38. Ādīnavo pāturahu theragā. 269, dibbo ratho pāturahu.

According to the Mahāvutti, there is elision of 'ī' and shortening. 'Fear indeed arose (ahudeva), trembling arose (ahu).' 'Uneasiness indeed arose (ahudeva), remorse arose (ahu).' 'Danger appeared (pāturahu),' 'the divine chariot appeared (pāturahu).'

624. Hūto resuṃ ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

624. Hūto resuṃ.

Hūto ñuṃvacanassa resuṃ hoti. Suttavibhattena mhāssa resumhā ca. ‘Rānubandhentasarādissā’ti dhātvantalopo.

After 'hū', the plural ending 'uṃ' becomes 'esuṃ'. By extension of the rule, 'mhā' also becomes 'esumhā'. According to the rule 'Rānubandhentasarādissā', there is elision of the final vowel of the root.

Te pubbe ahesuṃ. Uvādese ahuvuṃ, pubbassaralope ahuṃ.

They existed before (ahesuṃ). With the substitution of 'uva', 'ahuvuṃ' is formed; with the elision of the preceding vowel, 'ahuṃ' is formed.

Atrimā pāḷī- sabbamhi taṃ araññamhi, yāvantettha dijā ahuṃ jā. 2.22.2425. Kūṭāgārasahassāni, sabbasoṇṇamayā ahuṃ apa. thera 1.1.407.

Here follows the Pāli text: 'In that entire forest, however many birds there were (ahuṃ), there were (ahuṃ) thousands of peaked mansions, all made of gold.'

Ossa [M 0.0399] si, ittha, ttho. Tvaṃ ahosi, ahuvi, ahuvittha, ahuvittho.

Ossa si, ittha, ttho. You (sg.) were (ahosi), you (sg.) were (ahuvi); you (pl.) were (ahuvittha), you (pl.) were (ahuvittho).

Mahāvuttinā olopo rasso, mā bhoti kupitā ahu jā. 2.22.1931, māhu pacchānutāpinī saṃ. ni. 1.162, ahosiṃ nu kho ahaṃ atītamaddhānaṃ, na nu kho ahosiṃ, kinnu kho ahosiṃ, kathaṃ nu kho ahosiṃ saṃ. ni. 2.20; ma. ni. 1.18, ahaṃ ahuviṃ, mayaṃ ahosimhā, ahosimha vā. Ahesumhā nu kho mayaṃ atītamaddhānaṃ, na nu kho ahesumhā, kinnu kho ahesumhā, kathaṃ nu kho ahesumhā ma. ni. 1.407. Mayaṃ pubbe ahuvimhā, ahumhā vā. “Mayaṃ pubbe dānapatino ahumhā”ti jā. 2.22.1617 pāḷi.

According to the Mahāvutti, there is elision of 'o' and shortening. 'Lady, do not be angry (ahu).' 'Do not be one who is later regretful (māhu).' 'Was I indeed in the past? Or was I not? What indeed was I? How indeed was I?' 'I was (ahuviṃ); we were (ahosimhā), or we were (ahosimha).' 'Were we indeed in the past? Or were we not? What indeed were we? How indeed were we?' 'We were before (ahuvimhā), or we were (ahumhā).' The Pāli text says: 'We were donors before (ahumhā).'

Rassatte-ahumha.

When shortened: 'ahumha'.

Mahāvuttinā mhāssa uñca. “Pañcasatā mayaṃ sabbā, tāvatiṃsupagā ahu”nti pāḷi.

According to the Mahāvutti, for 'mhā' there is also 'uṃ'. The Pāli text says: 'We, five hundred in all, were those who went to Tāvatiṃsa (ahu).'

Parachakke assa aṃ, ahaṃ pubbe ahuvaṃ, ahuva vā.

In another paradigm, 'a' becomes 'aṃ'. Thus: 'I was before (ahuvaṃ), or (ahuva).'

‘Paro kvacī’ti paralopo, ahuṃ.

According to the rule 'Paro kvacī', there is elision of the following vowel, resulting in 'ahuṃ'.

Atrimā pāḷī- “ahaṃ kevaṭṭagāmasmiṃ, ahuṃ kevaṭṭadārako apa. thera 1.39.86, cakkavattī ahuṃ rājā, jambumaṇḍassa issaro. Sattakkhattuṃ mahābrahmā, vasavattī tadā ahuṃ. Muddhābhisitto khattiyo, manussādhipatī ahu”nti. Mayaṃ ahuvimhe.

Here follows the Pāli text: 'In a fishermen's village, I was a fisherman's boy (ahuṃ). I was a wheel-turning king, the lord of Jambumaṇḍa (ahuṃ). Seven times a Mahābrahmā, a Vasavattī I was then (ahuṃ). An anointed Khattiya, a lord of men I was (ahu).' We were (ahuvimhe).

Ssatyādimhi –

Regarding the future tense (endings beginning with 'ssa'):

625. Hūssa hehehihohi ssaccādo ka. 480; rū. 490; nī. 961; ‘…ssatyādo’ (bahūsu).

625. For 'hū', 'he', 'hehi', and 'hohi' are substituted when 'ssa' and so on follow.

Ssatyādimhi hūdhātussa he ca hohi ca hohi ca honti.

When 'ssati' and so on follow, for the root 'hū', the substitutes 'he', 'hehi', and 'hohi' occur.

Hessati[M 0.0400], hessanti, hehissati, hehissanti, hohissati, hohissanti. Buddho hessaṃ sadevake bu. vaṃ. 2.55, anāgatamhi addhāne, hessāma sammukhā imaṃ bu. vaṃ. 2.74.

Hessati, hessanti, hehissati, hehissanti, hohissati, hohissanti. 'I will be a Buddha in the world with its gods.' 'In a future time, we will be face to face with this one.'

626. Dakkha sakkha hehi hohīhi lopo ka. 480; rū. 490; nī. 961; ‘dakkhā hehihohilopo’ (bahūsu).

626. After 'dakkha', 'sakkha', 'hehi', and 'hohi', there is elision.

Etehi ādesehi ssassa lopo hoti vā. Suttavibhattena aññehipi ssalopo.

After these substitutes, the 'ssa' of the future tense is optionally elided. By extension of the rule, the elision of 'ssa' also occurs in other cases.

Sakkhisi tvaṃ kuṇḍalini, maññisi khattabandhuni jā. 2.17.14. Na hi sakkhinti chettuṃ su. ni. 28, adhammo haññiti dhammamajja jā. 1.11.31, brahmadatto palāyiti iccādi.

'You will be able, O Kuṇḍalinī.' 'You will think, O Khattabandhunī.' 'Indeed, they will not be able to cut it.' 'Today, unrighteousness will destroy righteousness.' 'Brahmadatta will flee,' and so forth.

Hehiti, hehinti, hohiti, hohinti.

Hehiti, hehinti, hohiti, hohinti.

Atrimā pāḷī-piyo ca me hehiti mālabhārī, ahañca naṃ mālinī ajjhupessaṃ jā. 1.15.197, tilodano hehiti sādhupakko jā. 1.8.2. Doso pemañca hehiti theragā. 719. Mama tvaṃ hehisi bhariyā jā. 1.14.27. Tato sukhī hohisi vītarāgo. Khippaṃ hohisi anāsavo dī. ni. 2.207 iccādi.

The following Pāli text: 'And a garland-bearer will be dear to me, and I, as a garlanded woman, shall attend upon him. Sesame-rice will be well-cooked. There will be hatred and love. You will be my wife. Then you will be happy, free from passion. Quickly you will be without cankers,' and so forth.

Iti bhūvādigaṇe uvaṇṇantadhāturūpaṃ.

Thus in the Bhūvādi group are the forms of roots ending in the vowel 'u'.

Edantadhāturūpa

Forms of roots ending in 'e'

E-āgatiyaṃ gatiyañca, ke-sadde, khe-khādanu’paṭṭhānesu, ge-sadde, apapubba ce-pūjāyaṃ, jhe-cintāyaṃ dāha’jjhānesu ca, te-pālane, the-sadda, saṅghātesu, de-suddhi, niddāsu, pe-vuddhiyaṃ[M 0.0401], bhe-bhaye, le-chedane, ve-gatiyaṃ tantasantāne ca, se-antakriyāyaṃ, hare-lajjāyaṃ, gile-kilamane, pale-gatiyaṃ, mile-hāniyaṃ.

E, in coming and going; Ke, in sound; Khe, in eating and appearing; Ge, in sound; Ce, preceded by 'apa', in reverence; Jhe, in contemplation, burning, and meditation; Te, in protecting; The, in sound and in aggregations; De, in purity and in sleep; Pe, in growth; Bhe, in fear; Le, in cutting; Ve, in going and in the extension of a thread; Se, in making an end; Hare, in shame; Gile, in weariness; Pale, in going; Mile, in loss.

Ṇānubandhapaccayena vinā yesaṃ dhātūnaṃ āyādeso labbhati, te edantā nāma. Mahāvuttinā yalope sati ādantehi samānarūpaṃ, ādantānañca yāgame sati edantehi samānarūpaṃ, tasmā ādanta, edantā yebhuyyena samānarūpā bhavanti.

Those roots for which the 'āya' substitution is obtained without the suffix with the anubandha 'ṇa' are called Edanta. According to the Mahāvutti, when 'ya' is elided, they become similar in form to Ādanta roots, and when 'ya' is inserted into Ādanta roots, they become similar in form to Edanta roots. Therefore, Ādanta and Edanta roots are mostly of a similar form.

Mahāvuttinā edantānaṃ tyādīsu tabbādīsu ca āyādeso, kvaci yalopo, e-āgatiyaṃ. Ayaṃ so sārathī eti jā. 2.22.51, sace enti manussattaṃ saṃ. ni. 1.49, lakkhaṇaṃ passa āyantaṃ, migasaṅghapurakkhataṃ jā. 1.1.11, yoga’māyanti maccuno saṃ. ni. 1.20, āyāmāvuso pārā. 228, āyāmānanda dī. ni. 2.186; pārā. 22; ma. ni. 1.273.

According to the Mahāvutti, for Edanta roots, the 'āya' substitution occurs in suffixes beginning with 'ti' and 'tabba'; sometimes there is elision of 'ya'. From the root E, in the sense of coming: 'This is that charioteer who comes,' 'If they come to the human state,' 'See the mark of the one approaching, preceded by a herd of deer,' 'They approach the yoke of death,' 'Let us come, friend!' 'Let us come, Ānanda!'

Ettha edhātu āgaccha, gacchāmāti atthadvayaṃ vadati, yādhātuvasena āgaccha, yāmātipi atthaṃ vadanti.

Here, the root E expresses a twofold meaning, 'come' and 'go'; by means of the root Yā, they also state the meaning 'come' and 'go'.

E-vuddhiyaṃ vā, “kāyo, apāyo, upāyo, samudāyo”tiādīsu –

Or the root E in the sense of growth, as in 'kāyo', 'apāyo', 'upāyo', 'samudāyo', and so forth:

Kucchitā dhammā āyanti vaḍḍhanti etthāti kāyo, ‘āyo’ti vuccati vaḍḍhi, tato apeto apāyo, tena upeto upāyo, avayavadhammā samudenti etthāti samudāyo, paribyattaṃ āyanti etenāti pariyāyo.

Because contemptible things come and increase here, it is called 'kāyo'; 'āyo' is called increase; devoid of that is 'apāyo'; endowed with that is 'upāyo'; because component things come together here, it is called 'samudāyo'; because they come around by means of this, it is called 'pariyāyo'.

Ke-sadde, kāyati.

Ke, in sound: 'kāyati' (it sounds).

Kamme-kiyyati.

In the passive: 'kiyyati' (it is done).

Khe-khādane, tiṇaṃ khāyati, vikkhāyati, undurā khāyanti, vikkhāyanti.

Khe, in eating: 'tiṇaṃ khāyati' (it eats grass), 'vikkhāyati' (it chews up); 'undurā khāyanti' (rats eat), 'vikkhāyanti' (they chew up).

Khe-upaṭṭhāne[M 0.0402], khāyati, pakkhāyati, alakkhī viya khāyati.

Khe, in appearing: 'khāyati' (it appears), 'pakkhāyati' (it appears clearly), 'alakkhī viya khāyati' (it appears as if inauspicious).

Ge-sadde, gāyati, gāyanti.

Ge, in sound: 'gāyati' (he sings), 'gāyanti' (they sing).

Apapubba ce-pūjāyaṃ, apacāyati, ye vuddha’mapacāyanti jā. 1.1.37.

Ce, preceded by 'apa', in reverence: 'apacāyati' (one honors), 'ye vuddha’mapacāyanti' (those who honor an elder).

Jhe-cintāyaṃ, jhāyati, jhāyanti, pajjhāyati, pajjhāyanti, abhijjhāyati, abhijjhāyanti.

Jhe, in contemplation: 'jhāyati' (one contemplates), 'jhāyanti' (they contemplate); 'pajjhāyati' (one reflects), 'pajjhāyanti' (they reflect); 'abhijjhāyati' (one covets), 'abhijjhāyanti' (they covet).

Jhe-olokane, nijjhāyati, nijjhāyanti, upanijjhāyati, upanijjhāyanti, ujjhāyati, ujjhāyanti.

Jhe, in observing: 'nijjhāyati' (one gazes), 'nijjhāyanti' (they gaze); 'upanijjhāyati' (one scrutinizes), 'upanijjhāyanti' (they scrutinize); 'ujjhāyati' (one grumbles), 'ujjhāyanti' (they grumble).

Jhe-dayhane, padīpo jhāyati, parijjhāyati.

Jhe, in burning: 'padīpo jhāyati' (the lamp burns), 'parijjhāyati' (it burns down).

Kamme-jhāyīyati.

In the passive: 'jhāyīyati' (it is burned).

Ṇāpimhi yalopo, kaṭṭhaṃ jhāpeti, jhāpenti, jhāpayati, jhāpayanti.

With the causative suffix ṇāpi, 'ya' is elided: 'kaṭṭhaṃ jhāpeti' (he makes the wood burn), 'jhāpenti' (they make it burn), 'jhāpayati' (he makes it burn), 'jhāpayanti' (they make it burn).

Jhe-ajjhayane saṃpubbo, mahāvuttinā niggahītassa jādeso, sajjhāyati, sajjhāyanti, mantaṃ sajjhāyati.

Jhe, in recitation, when preceded by 'saṃ'; according to the Mahāvutti, 'jā' is substituted for the niggahīta: 'sajjhāyati' (he recites), 'sajjhāyanti' (they recite), 'mantaṃ sajjhāyati' (he recites the mantra).

Te-pālane, tāyati, tāyanti.

Te, in protection: 'tāyati' (it protects), 'tāyanti' (they protect).

The-sadda, saṅghātesu, thāyati.

The, in sound and in aggregations: 'thāyati' (it sounds).

De-suddhiyaṃ, vodāyati, vodāyanti.

De, in purity: 'vodāyati' (it purifies), 'vodāyanti' (they purify).

De-soppane, niddāyati, niddāyanti.

De, in sleep: 'niddāyati' (he sleeps), 'niddāyanti' (they sleep).

Pe-vuddhiyaṃ, appāyati, appāyanti.

Pe, in growth: 'appāyati' (it grows), 'appāyanti' (they grow).

Bhe-bhaye, bhāyati, bhāyanti, sabbe bhāyanti maccuno dha. pa. 129, bhāyasi, sace bhāyatha dukkhassa udā. 44, kinnu kho ahaṃ tassa sukhassa bhāyāmi ma. ni. 1.381, nataṃ bhāyāmi āvuso, bhāyāma apa. therī. 2.2.458.

Bhe, in fear: 'bhāyati' (he fears), 'bhāyanti' (they fear); 'sabbe bhāyanti maccuno' (all fear death); 'bhāyasi' (you fear); 'sace bhāyatha dukkhassa' (if you fear suffering); 'kinnu kho ahaṃ tassa sukhassa bhāyāmi' (why indeed should I fear that happiness?); 'nataṃ bhāyāmi āvuso' (I do not fear that, friend); 'bhāyāma' (we fear).

Ṇāpimhi-bhayāpeti, bhāyāpeti, bhāyāpayati.

With the causative suffix ṇāpi: 'bhayāpeti', 'bhāyāpeti', 'bhāyāpayati' (he causes to fear, he frightens).

Īādimhi-mā [M 0.0403] bhāyi, mā soci dī. ni. 2.207, mā cintayi.

In the aorist: 'mā bhāyi' (do not fear), 'mā soci' (do not grieve), 'mā cintayi' (do not worry).

Ssatyādimhi-bhāyissati, bhāyissanti.

In the future tense: 'bhāyissati' (he will fear), 'bhāyissanti' (they will fear).

Le-chedane, tiṇaṃ lāyati, sāliṃ lāyati, lāyanti.

In cutting, one reaps grass, one reaps rice, they reap.

Ve-gatiyaṃ, vāto vāyati, vātā vāyanti.

In movement, the wind blows, the winds blow.

Ve-tantasantāne, tantaṃ vāyati, vāyanti.

In weaving threads, he weaves a thread, they weave.

Kamme-vāyīyati, pubbalope vīyati, viyyati.

In the passive voice, it is woven; with elision of the preceding vowel, it is woven, it is woven.

Ṇāpimhi-cīvaraṃ vāyāpeti pārā. 638, vāyāpenti.

In the causative, he has the robe woven, they have it woven.

Se-antakriyāyaṃ, osāyati, pariyosāyati, ajjhosāyati.

The root 'Se' in the sense of final action: he terminates, he finishes, he clings.

Kamme-pariyosīyati.

In the passive voice, it is completed.

Ṇāpimhi-pariyosāpeti.

In the causative, he has it completed.

627. Ṇiṇāpīnaṃ tesu.

627. Regarding the elision of ṇi and ṇāpi in these.

Ṇi, ṇāpīnaṃ lopo hoti tesuṇi, ṇāpīsu paresu.

The elision of ṇi and ṇāpi occurs when these, ṇi and ṇāpi, follow.

Bhikkhu attanā vippakataṃ kuṭiṃ parehi pariyosāpeti pārā. 363. Ettha akammakattā dhātussa ‘kuṭi’nti ca ‘parehī’ti ca dve kammāni dvikkhattuṃ pavattehi kāritehi sijjhanti.

A monk, having himself improperly constructed a hut, has it completed by others. Here, because the root is ditransitive, the two objects, namely 'hut' and 'by others', are accomplished twice by the active causative verbs.

Anekassaraedantampi kiñci idha vuccati.

Something here is also called polysyllabic and ending in 'e'.

Hare-lajjāyaṃ, harāyati, harāyanti, aṭṭiyāmi harāyāmi saṃ. ni. 1.165, harāyāma, harāyatīti hirī, mahāvuttinā upantassa ittaṃ.

The root 'Hare' in the sense of shame: he is ashamed, they are ashamed; I am disgusted, I am ashamed; we are ashamed. 'Being ashamed' is 'hirī' (modesty); according to the Mahāvutti, the penultimate vowel is substituted with 'i'.

Gile-rujjane, gilāyati, piṭṭhi me āgilāyati cūḷava. 345; dī. ni. 3.300, gilāyanti.

The root 'Gile' in the sense of sickness: he is sick, my back aches, they are sick.

Pale-gatiyaṃ[M 0.0404], palāyati, palāyanti.

The root 'Pale' in the sense of going: he flees, they flee.

Mile-hāniyaṃ, milāyati, milāyanti.

The root 'Mile' in the sense of withering: it withers, they wither.

“Jhānaṃ, ujjhānaṃ, nijjhānaṃ, tāṇaṃ, parittāṇaṃ, vodānaṃ, niddānaṃ, gilāno, palāto, milātanti”ādīsu yalopo.

In 'jhāna, ujjhāna, nijjhāna, tāṇa, parittāṇa, vodāna, niddāna, gilāna, palāta, milāta,' and so on, there is elision of the letter 'ya'.

Iti bhūvādigaṇe edantadhāturūpaṃ.

Thus are the forms of 'e'-ending roots in the bhūvādi group.

Bhūvādigaṇe sarantadhātūnaṃ tyādyantarūpāni niṭṭhitāni.

In the bhūvādi group, the forms of vowel-ending roots with 'ti' and other endings are concluded.

Byañjanantadhātu

Consonant-Ending Roots

Avuddhikarūpa

Non-Augmented Forms

Tudādigaṇa

The Tudādi Group

Atha byañjanantadhāturūpāni vuccante. Tāni ca avuddhika, savuddhikavasena duvidhāni honti. Tattha avuddhikāni tāva vuccante.

Now, the forms of consonant-ending roots are stated. They are of two kinds: non-augmented and augmented. Among them, the non-augmented ones are stated first.

Khipa, guha, tuda, disa, pisa, phusa, likha, vadhādi.

Khipa, guha, tuda, disa, pisa, phusa, likha, vadha, and so on.

Idha dhātūnaṃ antassaro uccāraṇattho, so rūpavidhāne nappayujjate.

Here, the final vowel of the roots is for the purpose of pronunciation; it is not employed in the formation of forms.

628. Tudādīhi ko ka. 445; rū. 433; nī. 925; caṃ. 1.1.92; pā. 3.1.77.

628. From the tudādi group, 'ka'.

Tudādīhi kānubandho apaccayo hoti. Kānubandho avuddhidīpanattho.

From the tudādi group, the suffix 'a' has 'k' as an anubandha. The anubandha 'k' is for the purpose of indicating non-augmentation.

Khipa-khipane, khipati, pakkhipati, ukkhipati, okkhipati, nikkhipati, vikkhipati, paṭikkhipati, saṃkhipati.

The root 'Khipa' in the sense of throwing: he throws, he puts in, he raises up, he puts down, he lays down, he scatters, he rejects, he shortens.

Kamme-khipīyati.

In the passive voice, it is thrown.

Kārite-khipeti[M 0.0405], khipayati, khipāpeti, khipāpayati, khepeti, khepayati vā, udakaṃ khepeti, taṇhaṃ khepeti, khayāpetīti attho.

In the causative: 'khipeti,' 'khipayati,' 'khipāpeti,' 'khipāpayati'; or 'khepeti,' 'khepayati.' For example: 'udakaṃ khepeti' (he causes water to be exhausted), 'taṇhaṃ khepeti' (he causes craving to be exhausted), the meaning of which is 'to cause to be destroyed'.

Guha-saṃvaraṇe, guhati, nigguhati.

Guha—in concealing: guhati, nigguhati.

Kamme-guhiyati.

In the passive: guhiyati.

Kārite gussa dīgho, gūheti, gūhayati, gūhāpeti, gūhāpayati.

In the causative, the lengthening of ‘gu’: gūheti, gūhayati, gūhāpeti, gūhāpayati.

Kamme-gūhāpīyati.

In the passive: gūhāpīyati.

Ghaṭa-cetāyaṃ, ghaṭati.

Ghaṭa—in striving: ghaṭati.

Kamme-ghaṭīyati.

In the passive: ghaṭīyati.

Kārite-ghaṭeti, ghaṭayati, ghaṭāpeti, ghaṭāpayati.

In the causative: ghaṭeti, ghaṭayati, ghaṭāpeti, ghaṭāpayati.

Tuda-byadhane, byadhanaṃ vijjhanaṃ, tudati, vitudati.

Tuda—in piercing; byadhanaṃ, that is, vijjhanaṃ: tudati, vitudati.

Assa ette-tudeti, tudenti.

Its vowel becomes e: tudeti, tudenti.

Kamme-tudīyati.

In the passive: tudīyati.

‘Tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā’ti dassa jattaṃ. ‘Vaggalasehi te’ti yassa pubbarūpattaṃ, tujjati.

By the rule ‘Tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā,’ the ‘d’ becomes ‘j.’ By the rule ‘Vaggalasehi te,’ the ‘y’ is assimilated to the preceding consonant, resulting in: tujjati.

Kārite-tudeti, tudayati, tudāpeti, tudāpayati.

In the causative: tudeti, tudayati, tudāpeti, tudāpayati.

Disī-uddisane, uddisanaṃ sarūpato kathanaṃ. Uddisati, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti mahāva. 152, niddisati, niddisanti, apadisati, apadisanti.

Disī—in pointing out; uddisanaṃ, that is, speaking according to its nature: Uddisati, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti, niddisati, niddisanti, apadisati, apadisanti.

Kamme-uddisīyati, uddisīyanti.

In the passive: uddisīyati, uddisīyanti.

Kārite-ācariyo sissaṃ pāḷidhammaṃ uddisāpeti, uddisāpayati, vācetīti attho. Pāṭhesu pana sadvayampi dissati.

In the causative: ācariyo sissaṃ pāḷidhammaṃ uddisāpeti, uddisāpayati, meaning one causes another to recite. However, both forms are seen in the readings.

Nuda-khipane[M 0.0406], nudati, panudati, vinodeti, paṭivinodeti vā.

Nuda—in driving away: nudati, panudati, vinodeti, or paṭivinodeti.

Kamme-panudīyati, panujjati.

In the passive: panudīyati, panujjati.

Kārite-panudeti, panudayati, panudāpeti, panudāpayati.

In the causative: panudeti, panudayati, panudāpeti, panudāpayati.

Pisa-saṃcuṇṇe, pisati.

Pisa—in crushing: pisati.

Kamme-pisīyati.

In the passive: pisīyati.

Kārite-piseti, pisayati, pisāpeti, pisāpayati.

In the causative: piseti, pisayati, pisāpeti, pisāpayati.

Phusa-samphasse pattiyañca, phusati, phusanti dhīrā nibbānaṃ dha. pa. 23, vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyya pārā. 409; cūḷava. 344.

Phusa—in touching and attainment: phusati, phusanti dhīrā nibbānaṃ (the wise attain Nibbāna), vajjaṃ naṃ phuseyya (may harm not touch him).

Kamme-phusīyati.

In the passive: phusīyati.

Kārite-phuseti, phusayati, phusāpeti, phusāpayati.

In the causative: phuseti, phusayati, phusāpeti, phusāpayati.

Likha-lekhane, likhati, sallikhati, vilikhati.

Likha—in scratching or writing: likhati, sallikhati, vilikhati.

Kārite-likheti, sallikheti, vilikheti.

In the causative: likheti, sallikheti, vilikheti.

Vadha-hiṃsāyaṃ, vadhati, vadheti.

Vadha—in harming: vadhati, vadheti.

Kamme-vadhīyati.

In the passive: vadhīyati.

Yamhi dhassa jhattaṃ, yassa pubbarūpaṃ. ‘Catutthadutiyesvesaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā’ti jhassa tatiyajattaṃ, vajjhati, vajjhanti, vajjhare. Ime sattā haññantu vā vajjhantu vā ma. ni. 1.60.

When followed by ‘y,’ ‘dh’ becomes ‘jh,’ and the ‘y’ is assimilated. By the rule ‘Catutthadutiyesvesaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā,’ ‘jh’ becomes ‘j,’ resulting in: vajjhati, vajjhanti, vajjhare. For example: Ime sattā haññantu vā vajjhantu vā (Let these beings be struck or killed).

Kārite-vadheti, vadhayati, vadhāpeti, vadhāpayati, sāmiko purisaṃ maggaṃ gameti, gamayati, gamāpeti, gamāpayati iccādīnipi idha vattabbāni.

In the causative: vadheti, vadhayati, vadhāpeti, vadhāpayati. For example: sāmiko purisaṃ maggaṃ gameti, gamayati, gamāpeti, gamāpayati (the master makes the man go along the path). These and similar examples should also be stated here.

Iti tudādigaṇo.

Thus ends the Tudādi Group.

Savuddhikarūpa

Forms with Vuddhi

Atha [M 0.0407] savuddhikarūpāni vuccante.

Then, the forms with vuddhi are spoken of.

Asa-bhuvi, āsa-nivāse upavesane ca, isu-icchā, kantīsu, kamu-padagamane, kusa-akkose, gamu-gatimhi, jaravayohānimhi, jana-janane, mara-pāṇacāge, yamu-uparame, ruda-assuvimocane kandane ca, ruha-janane, labha-lābhe, vaca, vada-viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, vida-ñāṇe, vasa-nivāse, visapavesane, sada-gatyā’vasāne, hana-hiṃsāyaṃ, haraharaṇe.

Asa—in being; Āsa—in dwelling and sitting; Isu—in desiring and loving; Kamu—in going with the feet; Kusa—in reviling; Gamu—in going; Jara—in the decay of old age; Jana—in generating; Mara—in giving up life; Yamu—in restraining; Ruda—in shedding tears and weeping; Ruha—in growing; Labha—in gaining; Vaca, Vada—in the distinct utterance of speech; Vida—in knowing; Vasa—in dwelling; Visa—in entering; Sada—in motion and cessation; Hana—in harming; Hara—in taking.

Tyādyuppatti, kattari lo, asa-bhuvi, sattāyanti attho.

The derivation of 'ti', etc. In the agentive voice, the 'l'-affix. From 'as'—in being; the meaning is 'existence'.

629. Tassa tho ka. 494; rū. 495, 500; nī. 989, 991.

629. Its 't' becomes 'th'.

Atthito parassati, tūnaṃ tassa tho hoti.

After 'atthi', the 't' of the following verbal endings becomes 'th'.

‘Pararūpamayakāre byañjane’ti suttena byañjane pare dhātvantassa pararūpattaṃ, ‘catutthadutiyesvesaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā’ti suttena pararūpassa dutiyassa paṭhamattaṃ.

By the rule ‘Pararūpamayakāre byañjane’, when a consonant follows, the final of the root takes the form of the following consonant. By the rule ‘Catutthadutiyesvesaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā’, the second letter of the resultant form becomes the first.

Dhanaṃ me atthi.

I have wealth.

Ettha ca “atthi tvaṃ etarahi, na tvaṃ natthi, atthi ahaṃ etarahi, nāhaṃ natthi, puttā matthi dhanā matthi dha. pa. 62, atthi imasmiṃ kāye kesā”ti khu. pā. 3.dvitiṃsākāra ādīsu atthisaddo ākhyātapaṭirūpako kattuvācako nipāto.

And here, in phrases such as “You exist now, you do not not exist; I exist now, I do not not exist; I have sons, I have wealth; there are hairs in this body,” the word ‘atthi’ is a particle resembling a verb, expressing the agent.

“Atthīti kho kaccāyana ayameko anto, natthīti dutiyo anto”ti saṃ. ni. 2.15 ca “atthipaccayo, natthipaccayo”ti paṭṭhā. 1.1.paccayuddesa ca evamādīsu nāmapaṭirūpako. Tathā natthisaddo.

And in “‘Existence,’ Kaccāyana, is one extreme; ‘non-existence’ is the second extreme,” and in “condition of presence, condition of absence,” and so on, it resembles a noun. Similarly, the word ‘natthi’.

Tumhi-vipassissa [M 0.0408] ca namatthu dī. ni. 3.287, namo te buddha vīratthu saṃ. ni. 1.90, ettha ca “dhiratthumaṃ pūtikāya”nti ādīsu atthusaddo nipāto.

“Homage be to you, Vipassī,” and “Homage be to you, O heroic Buddha!” And here, in phrases such as “Shame be upon this foul body,” the word 'atthu' is a particle.

630. Ntamānantantiyiyuṃsvādilopo ka. 494-5; rū. 496; nī. 1019; ‘ntamānānti…’ (bahūsu).

630. Elision of the initial vowel before nta, māna, anti, antu, iyā, and iyuṃsu.

Nta, māna, anti, antu, iyā, iyuṃsu atthissa ādilopo hoti.

The initial vowel of 'atthi' is elided before the suffixes nta, māna, anti, antu, iyā, and iyuṃsu.

Santi, santu.

They are; let them be.

631. Sihīsvaṭa ka. 506; rū. 497; nī. 992.

631. Before si and hī, aṭa.

Atthissa aṭa hoti si, hīsu.

Of 'atthi', 'aṭa' occurs before 'si' and 'hī'.

Manussosi mahāva. 126, purisosi mahāva. 126. Himhi dīgho, tvaṃ paṇḍito āhi, bhavāhīti attho. Tavibhattīsu dhātvantassa pararūpaṃ, tumhe attha, kaccittha parisuddhā pārā. 233. Tvādimhi-mā pamādattha ma. ni. 1.88, 215, tumhe samaggā attha.

You are a human; you are a man. Before 'hi', there is lengthening. 'You are wise'; 'āhi' has the meaning 'be'. Before the 'tha' ending, the final of the root is assimilated to the following. 'You all are'; 'Are you all pure?' In the aorist, etc.: 'do not be negligent'; 'You all are united'.

632. Mimānaṃ vā mhimhā ca ka. 492; rū. 499; nī. 987; ‘sīhisvaṭa’ (bahūsu).

632. Mi and māna optionally become mhi and mhā.

Atthito paresaṃ mi, mānaṃ mhi, mhā honti vā, atthissa ca aṭa hoti.

After 'atthi', the endings 'mi' and 'māna' optionally become 'mhi' and 'mhā' respectively, and of 'atthi' there is the substitution 'aṭa'.

Ahaṃ pasannomhi, mayaṃ pasannāmha.

I am pleased; we are pleased.

Tvādimhi-ahaṃ iminā puññena anāgate paññavā amhi, mayaṃ paññavanto amha.

In the aorist, etc.: 'By this merit, I will be wise in the future'; 'We are wise'.

633. Esu sa ka. 492; rū. 499; nī. 987.

633. Before these, 's'.

Etesu [M 0.0409] mi, mesu atthissa sassa so hoti. Pararūpanisedhanatthamidaṃ suttaṃ.

Before these, 'mi' and 'me', the 's' of 'atthi' remains 's'. This rule is for the purpose of preventing assimilation.

Ahaṃ paṇḍito asmi, mayaṃ paṇḍitā asma.

I am wise; we are wise.

Tvādimhi-ahaṃ anāgate paññavā asmi, mayaṃ paññavanto asma.

In the aorist, etc.: 'I will be wise in the future'; 'We are wise'.

Eyyādimhi –

In the optative, etc. –

634. Atthiteyyādichannaṃ sa su sasi satha saṃsāma ka. 571, 517; rū. 624, 488; nī. 830, 1105; ‘atthiteyyādicchannaṃ sasusasatha saṃ sāma’ (bahūsu).

634. For the six optative endings of 'atthi', the substitutes are sa, su, sasi, satha, saṃ, and sāma.

‘Atthī’ti dhātuniddeso ti-kāro, atthito paresaṃ eyyādīnaṃ channaṃ sādayo honti.

The mention of the root as 'atthi' includes the 'ti' suffix. After 'atthi', for the following six optative endings, the replacements beginning with 'sa' occur.

Evamassa vacanīyo pārā. 411, evamassu vacanīyā pārā 418, tvaṃ assasi, tumhe assatha, ahaṃ assaṃ, mayaṃ assāma.

Thus he should be spoken to; thus they should be spoken to. You would be; you all would be; I would be; we would be.

Assunipātopi bahuṃ dissati, tayassu dhammā jahitā bhavanti khu. pā. 6.10, kenassu taratī oghaṃ, kenassu tarati aṇṇavaṃ saṃ. ni. 1.246. “Kiṃsu chetvā sukhaṃ seti, kiṃsu chetvā na socatī”ti saṃ. ni. 1.71 ettha niggahītamhā saṃyogādilopo.

The particle 'assu' is also seen frequently. 'Indeed, three qualities are abandoned'; 'By what indeed does one cross the flood? By what indeed does one cross the ocean?' In 'What having cut off does one sleep happily? What having cut off does one not grieve?', here there is elision of the initial consonant of the conjunct after the niggahīta.

635. Ādidvinnamiyāmiyuṃ ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 993; ‘…miyā iyuṃ’ (bahūsu).

635. For the first two, 'iyā' and 'iyuṃ'.

Atthito eyyādīsu ādimhi dvinnaṃ iyā, iyuṃ honti. ‘Ntamānantantiyiyuṃsū…’tiādilopo.

From 'atthi', for the first two of the 'eyyādi' group, 'iyā' and 'iyuṃ' occur. Elision of the initial part occurs, as in 'ntamānantantiyiyuṃsū...'

So [M 0.0410] siyā, te siyuṃ, ete dve nipātāpi honti. “Vedanākkhandho siyā kusalo, siyā akusalo, siyā abyākato”ti vibha. 152 ādīsu ekaccoti attho.

He might be; they might be. These two are also particles. In phrases such as 'The feeling aggregate might be wholesome, might be unwholesome, might be indeterminate,' the meaning is 'in some cases'.

“Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā”ti paṭṭhā. 1.1.35-38 ādīsu kinnūti attho.

In phrases such as 'It may be that, dependent on a wholesome phenomenon, a wholesome phenomenon might arise by way of root-condition,' the meaning is 'what then?'

“Dvādasākusalā siyu”nti abhidhammatthasaṅgaha 2 ādīsu bhavantīti attho.

In phrases such as 'The twelve unwholesome states might be,' the meaning is 'they are'.

Mahāvuttinā eyyuṃ, eyyamiccetesaṃ iyaṃsu, iyaṃ honti, ādilopo, siyaṃsu dve bhikkhū abhidhamme nānāvādā ma. ni. 3.35, evaṃrūpo siyaṃ ahaṃ anāgatamaddhānaṃ, evaṃvedano siyaṃ, evaṃsañño siyaṃ ma. ni. 3.274.

According to the Mahāvutti, for 'eyyuṃ', 'eyyaṃ', and so on, 'iyaṃsu' and 'iyaṃ' occur, with elision of the initial part. 'Two monks might hold different views on the Abhidhamma'; 'Such might I be in the future'; 'Such might be my feeling'; 'Such might be my perception'.

Ajjattanimhi –

In the Aorist tense –

636. Īādo dīgho ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1001.

636. Before 'ī', etc., there is lengthening.

Atthissa dīgho hoti īādīsu.

The vowel of 'atthi' becomes long before 'ī' and the like.

So āsi, te āsuṃ, āsiṃsu, tvaṃ āsi, tumhe āsittha, ahaṃ āsiṃ. Tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃvaṇṇo dī. ni. 1.245; ma. ni. 1.68. Mayaṃ āsimha, āsimhā.

He was; they were; they were; you were; you all were; I was. There, 'āsiṃ' is of such a form. We were; we were.

637. Aāssādīsu ka. 507; rū. 501; nī. 1020; caṃ. 5.4.79; pā. 2.4.52.

637. Before 'a', 'ā', 'ssa', and the like –

Aādiparokkhāyañca āādihiyyattaniyañca ssādīsu bhavissanti, kālātipattīsu ca atthissa bhū hoti. Idañca suttaṃ atthissa etāsaṃ vibhattīnampi sādhāraṇakaraṇatthaṃ. Rūpampi bhūrūpameva.

In the perfect tense (beginning with 'a' and 'ā'), the imperfect tense (beginning with 'ā'), the future tense (with 'ssa' and the like), and in the conditional tenses, 'atthi' becomes 'bhū'. And this rule is for making 'atthi' common to these inflections as well. The form is also just the form of 'bhū'.

So [M 0.0411] babhūva, te babhūvu, so abhavā, te abhavū, so bhavissati, te bhavissanti, so abhavissā, te abhavissaṃsu iccādi.

He became; they became; he was; they were; he will be; they will be; he would have been; they would have been; and so on.

638. Atyādintesvatthissa bhū ka. 517; rū. 500; nī. 1020; caṃ. 5.4.79; pā. 2.4.52.

638. In suffixes other than `tyādi` and `nta`, `bhū` is substituted for `atthi`.

Tyādivajjitesu ntavajjitesu ca paccayesu atthissa bhū hoti. Etena tyādi, tvādi, eyyādi, īādisaṅkhātāsu catūsu vibhattīsu ntapaccaye ca atthissa bhūādeso natthi, sesāsu catūsu vibhattīsu ca ntavajjitesu tabbādīsu ca atthissa bhūādeso labbhatīti veditabbo.

In suffixes other than `tyādi` and `nta`, `atthi` becomes `bhū`. By this, it is to be understood that in the four inflections designated as `tyādi`, `tvādi`, `eyyādi`, and `īādi`, and in the `nta` suffix, there is no substitution of `bhū` for `atthi`; but in the remaining four inflections, and in `tabbādi` and so on, excluding `nta`, the substitution of `bhū` for `atthi` is obtained.

Āsa-upavesane. Guruṃ upāsati, payirupāsati, upāsanti, payirupāsanti.

The root `āsa` in the sense of attending upon. He attends upon a teacher; he reverentially attends upon; they attend upon; they reverentially attend upon.

Kamme-upāsīyati, payirupāsīyati.

In the passive voice: he is attended upon; he is reverentially attended upon.

Kārite-mātā puttaṃ guruṃ upāseti, payirupāseti, upāsayati, payirupāsayati.

In the causative voice: a mother causes her son to attend upon a teacher; she causes him to reverentially attend upon; she causes him to attend upon; she causes him to reverentially attend upon.

Īādimhi-upāsi, payirupāsi, upāsiṃsu, payirupāsiṃsu, upāsuṃ, payirupāsuṃ.

In the aorist tense: he attended upon; he reverentially attended upon; they attended upon; they reverentially attended upon; they attended upon; they reverentially attended upon.

Āsa-nivāse.

The root `āsa` in the sense of dwelling.

639. Gamayamisāsadisānaṃ vā cchaṅa ka. 476, 522; rū. 442, 476; nī. 957, 1035.

639. For the roots `gam`, `yam`, `is`, `ās`, and `dis`, `ccha` with the anubandha `ṅ` is an optional substitute.

Gamu, yamu, isu, āsa, disānaṃ anto byañjano ṅānubandho ccho hoti vā nta, māna, tyādīsu.

For the roots `gam`, `yam`, `is`, `ās`, and `dis`, the final consonant optionally becomes `ccha` with the anubandha `ṅ` when followed by `nta`, `māna`, `tyādi`, and so on.

Gacchanto, niyacchanto, icchanto, acchanto, dicchantoti iminā tyādīsu āsassa ccho, acchati, acchanti, so acchi, te acchiṃsu.

Examples are: `gacchanto`, `niyacchanto`, `icchanto`, `acchanto`, `dicchanto`. By this rule, for the root `ās`, `ccha` is substituted before `ti` and other endings. For example: `acchati`, `acchanti`; `so acchi`, `te acchiṃsu`.

Isu-esanāyaṃ[M 0.0412].

The root `isu` in the sense of seeking.

640. Lahussupantassa ka. 485; rū. 434; nī. 975; caṃ. 6.1.105-106 …pe… 7.3.77-78.

640. Of a light and penultimate vowel.

Antassa samīpe pavattatīti upanto, byañjanantadhātūnaṃ pubbassaro ‘upanto’ti vuccati, lahubhūtassa upantabhūtassa ca ivaṇṇu’vaṇṇassa e, ovuddhī honti.

That which occurs near the end is `upanta`. The vowel preceding the final consonant of a root is called `upanta`. For an `i` or `u` vowel that is both light and penultimate, the `vuddhi` substitutions `e` and `o` occur.

Ira-kampane, erati, modati.

The root `ira` in the sense of trembling. For example: `erati`, `modati`.

Lahussāti kiṃ? Jīvati, dhūpati, ikkhati, sukkhati.

Why the specification 'of a light vowel'? For example: `jīvati`, `dhūpati`, `ikkhati`, `sukkhati`.

Upantassāti kiṃ? Siñcati, bhuñjati, niggahītāgamena byavahitattā upanto na hoti.

Why the specification 'of a penultimate vowel'? For example: `siñcati`, `bhuñjati`. Because of the separation by the `niggahīta` augment, it is not penultimate.

Ivaṇṇuvaṇṇassātvevaṃ? Pacati, vadati.

And what of ivaṇṇa and uvaṇṇa? Thus: `pacati`, `vadati`.

Iminā issa evuddhi hoti, esati, anvesati, pariyesati.

By this rule, `i` becomes `e` through vuddhi. Examples: `esati`, `anvesati`, `pariyesati`.

Adhipubbo isu-āyācane, ajjhesati.

The root `isu` with the prefix `adhi` is used in the sense of 'requesting'. Example: `ajjhesati`.

Kamme-esīyati, pariyesīyati, anvesīyati, ajjhesīyati.

In the passive voice: `esīyati`, `pariyesīyati`, `anvesīyati`, `ajjhesīyati`.

Kārite-eseti, esayati, esāpeti, esāpayati.

In the causative: `eseti`, `esayati`, `esāpeti`, `esāpayati`.

Isu-icchāyaṃ, cchādeso, icchati, icchanti, sampaṭicchati, sampaṭicchanti.

The root `isu` is used in the sense of 'wishing'. `ccha` is the substitute for `is`. Examples: `icchati`, `icchanti`, `sampaṭicchati`, `sampaṭicchanti`.

Kamme-icchīyati.

In the passive voice: `icchīyati`.

Kārite-icchāpeti, icchāpayati, sampaṭicchāpeti, sampaṭicchāpayati.

In the causative: `icchāpeti`, `icchāpayati`, `sampaṭicchāpeti`, `sampaṭicchāpayati`.

Kamme-icchāpīyati, icchāpayīyati, so icchi, te icchiṃsu, icchissati, icchissanti.

In the passive causative voice: `icchāpīyati`, `icchāpayīyati`. Aorist: `so icchi`, `te icchiṃsu`. Future: `icchissati`, `icchissanti`.

Kamu-vijjhane, gambhīresu ṭhānesu ñāṇaṃ kamati, na satthaṃ kamati, na visaṃ kamati, na aggi kamati a. ni. 8.1, na vijjhatīti attho.

The root `kamu` is used in the sense of 'piercing'. Knowledge penetrates deep places; a weapon does not penetrate, poison does not penetrate, fire does not penetrate—the meaning is, it does not pierce.

Kamu-padagamane[M 0.0413], pakkamati, apakkamati, upakkamati, vikkamati, abhikkamati, paṭikkamati, atikkamati, saṅkamati, okkamati.

The root `kamu` is used in the sense of 'going'. Examples: `pakkamati`, `apakkamati`, `upakkamati`, `vikkamati`, `abhikkamati`, `paṭikkamati`, `atikkamati`, `saṅkamati`, `okkamati`.

641. Nito kamassa ka. 20; rū. 27; nī. 50.

641. Of `kam` after `ni`.

Nimhā parassa kamassa kassa kho hoti. ‘Ādissā’ti saṅketattā kassāti ñāyati.

Of the `ka` of the root `kam` following `ni`, `kha` is the substitute. By the convention 'of the initial', it is understood as applying to the `ka`.

Nikkhamati, nikkhamanti.

`Nikkhamati`, `nikkhamanti`.

Kārite –

In the causative:

642. Assā ṇānubandhe ka. 483; rū. 527; nī. 973.

642. `A` becomes `ā` when `ṇa` is an anubandha.

Byañjanantassa dhātussa ādimhi a-kārassa āvuddhi hoti ṇānubandhe paccaye. ‘Bahula’nti adhikatattā ṇāpimhi āvuddhi natthi.

For a root ending in a consonant, the initial `a` vowel undergoes `āvuddhi` when a suffix with `ṇa` as an anubandha follows. Because `bahula` is the governing rule, there is no `āvuddhi` with `ṇāpi`.

Pakkāmeti, pakkāmayati, nikkhāmeti, nikkhāmayati, nikkhamāpeti, nikkhamāpayati.

`Pakkāmeti`, `pakkāmayati`, `nikkhāmeti`, `nikkhāmayati`, `nikkhamāpeti`, `nikkhamāpayati`.

Īādimhi mahāvuttinā ādidīgho vā hoti, so pakkami, pakkāmi, idaṃ vatvāna pakkāmi, maddī sabbaṅgasobhaṇā jā. 2.22.1857, pakkamuṃ, pakkāmuṃ, sammodamānā pakkāmuṃ, aññamaññaṃ piyaṃ vadā jā. 2.22.1868, pakkamiṃsu, pakkāmiṃsu, pakkamaṃsu, pakkāmaṃsu, pakkamissati, pakkamissanti, pakkamissare.

In the aorist, according to the Mahāvutti, the initial vowel is optionally lengthened. Examples: `so pakkami`, `pakkāmi`; `idaṃ vatvāna pakkāmi, maddī sabbaṅgasobhaṇā`; `pakkamuṃ`, `pakkāmuṃ`; `sammodamānā pakkāmuṃ, aññamaññaṃ piyaṃ vadā`; `pakkamiṃsu`, `pakkāmiṃsu`; `pakkamaṃsu`, `pakkāmaṃsu`. Future examples: `pakkamissati`, `pakkamissanti`, `pakkamissare`.

Āpubbo kusa-akkose, lahupantattā vuddhi, akkosati, akkosanti. Papubbo āmantane, pakkosati, pakkosanti. Vipubbo uccasadde, vikkosati, vikkosanti. Paṭipubbo nīvāraṇe, paṭikkosati, paṭikkosanti.

The root `kusa` with the prefix `ā` is used in the sense of 'abusing'; due to the light penultimate vowel, vuddhi occurs. Examples: `akkosati`, `akkosanti`. With the prefix `pa`, in the sense of 'summoning'. Examples: `pakkosati`, `pakkosanti`. With the prefix `vi`, in the sense of 'a loud sound'. Examples: `vikkosati`, `vikkosanti`. With the prefix `paṭi`, in the sense of 'preventing'. Examples: `paṭikkosati`, `paṭikkosanti`.

Īādimhi [M 0.0414] –

In the aorist:

643. Kusaruhīssacchi ka. 498; rū. 480; nī. 1114; ‘kusaruhehīssa chi’ (bahūsu).

643. After `kusa` and `ruha`, `ī` becomes `cchi`.

Kusato ruhato ca parassa īssa cchi hoti.

After `kusa` and `ruha`, `ī` becomes `cchi`.

Akkocchi maṃ avadhi maṃ dha. pa. 3-4, idañca rūpaṃ kudha, kupadhātūhipi sādhenti, evaṃ sati “akkocchi me”ti pāṭho siyā. Akkosi, akkosiṃsu.

`Akkocchi maṃ avadhi maṃ` (He abused me, he struck me). This form is also derived from the roots `kudha` and `kupa`. This being so, the reading `akkocchi me` would be possible. Examples: `akkosi`, `akkosiṃsu`.

Gamu gatimhi, kattari lo, ‘ūlasse’ti lassa ettaṃ, gameti, gamenti. Avapubbo ñāṇe, avagameti, avagamenti, adhipubbo ñāṇe lābhe ca, adhigameti, adhigamenti. Vipubbo vigame, vigameti, vigamenti.

The root `gamu` is used in the sense of 'going'. In the active voice, `lo` is the suffix; by the rule `ūlasse`, `la` becomes `etta`. Examples: `gameti`, `gamenti`. With the prefix `ava`, in the sense of 'knowledge'. Examples: `avagameti`, `avagamenti`. With the prefix `adhi`, in the sense of 'knowledge and gain'. Examples: `adhigameti`, `adhigamenti`. With the prefix `vi`, in the sense of 'departure'. Examples: `vigameti`, `vigamenti`.

Kamme-gamīyati, gamiyati, gamiyyati.

In the passive voice: `gamīyati`, `gamiyati`, `gamiyyati`.

Pubbarūpatte-gammati, gammanti, adhigammati, adhigammanti, adhigammare, adhigammate, adhigammante, adhigammare.

With assimilation: `gammati`, `gammanti`, `adhigammati`, `adhigammanti`, `adhigammare`, `adhigammate`, `adhigammante`, `adhigammare`.

Kārite vuddhi natthi, gameti, gamayati, gamāpeti, gamāpayati.

In the causative, there is no vuddhi. Examples: `gameti`, `gamayati`, `gamāpeti`, `gamāpayati`.

Kamme-gamayīyati, gamayīyanti, gamāpīyati, gamāpīyanti.

In the passive causative voice: `gamayīyati`, `gamayīyanti`, `gamāpīyati`, `gamāpīyanti`.

Hiyyattanimhi-so agamā, gamā, te agamū, gamū, tvaṃ agamo, agama, agami, tumhe agamuttha, ahaṃ agamiṃ, gamiṃ, mayaṃ agamamhā, gamamhā, agamumhā, gamumhā, so agamattha, te agamatthuṃ, tvaṃ agamase, tumhe agamavhaṃ, ahaṃ agamaṃ, mayaṃ agamamhase.

In the Hiyyattanī past tense: `so agamā`, `gamā`; `te agamū`, `gamū`; `tvaṃ agamo`, `agama`, `agami`; `tumhe agamuttha`; `ahaṃ agamiṃ`, `gamiṃ`; `mayaṃ agamamhā`, `gamamhā`, `agamumhā`, `gamumhā`; `so agamattha`; `te agamatthuṃ`; `tvaṃ agamase`; `tumhe agamavhaṃ`; `ahaṃ agamaṃ`; `mayaṃ agamamhase`.

Ajjhattanimhi īādīsu ikārāgamo, so agamī, gamī.

In the ajjattanī (aorist), for endings beginning with `ī` and so on, the augment `i` is prefixed. Examples: `so agamī`, `gamī`.

Rassatte-agami, gami.

Upon shortening: `agami`, `gami`.

Mahāvuttinā [M 0.0415] ākārena saha sāgamo, so agamāsi, gāmaṃ agamāsi, nagaraṃ agamāsi.

According to Mahāvutti, with the augment `a` and the form containing `ā`: `so agamāsi`, `gāmaṃ agamāsi`, `nagaraṃ agamāsi`.

‘Eyyāthasse’iccādinā īssa ttho, so gāmaṃ agamittho, gamittho, te agamuṃ, gamuṃ.

By the rule beginning `Eyyāthasse`, etc., `ī` becomes `ttho`. Thus: `so gāmaṃ agamittho`, `gamittho`; `te agamuṃ`, `gamuṃ`.

‘Uṃssiṃsvaṃsū’ti iṃsu, aṃsu, te agamiṃsu, gamiṃsu, agamaṃsu, gamaṃsu, tvaṃ agamo, gamo.

By the rule `Uṃssiṃsvaṃsū`, the endings are `iṃsu` and `aṃsu`. Thus: `te agamiṃsu`, `gamiṃsu`, `agamaṃsu`, `gamaṃsu`; `tvaṃ agamo`, `gamo`.

‘Ossa a i ttha ttho’ ‘sī’ti suttāni, tvaṃ agama, gama, agami, gami, agamittha, gamittha, agamittho, gamittho, agamāsi, gamāsi, tumhe agamittha.

By the suttas `Ossa a i ttha ttho` and `sī`: `tvaṃ agama`, `gama`, `agami`, `gami`, `agamittha`, `gamittha`, `agamittho`, `gamittho`, `agamāsi`, `gamāsi`; `tumhe agamittha`.

‘Mhātthānamuu’iti uttaṃ, tumhe agamuttha, gamuttha, ahaṃ agamiṃ, gamiṃ, agamāsiṃ, gamāsiṃ, mayaṃ agamimhā, gamimhā.

By the rule `Mhātthānamuu`, it is said: `tumhe agamuttha`, `gamuttha`; `ahaṃ agamiṃ`, `gamiṃ`, `agamāsiṃ`, `gamāsiṃ`; `mayaṃ agamimhā`, `gamimhā`.

Rassatte-agamimha, gamimha, agamumhā, gamumhā, agamumha, gamumha, agamāsimhā, gamāsimhā, agamāsimha, gamāsimha.

Upon shortening: `agamimha`, `gamimha`, `agamumhā`, `gamumhā`, `agamumha`, `gamumha`, `agamāsimhā`, `gamāsimhā`, `agamāsimha`, `gamāsimha`.

Parachakke-so agamā, gamā.

In the other paradigm: `so agamā`, `gamā`.

Rassatte-agama, gama.

Upon shortening: `agama`, `gama`.

‘Eyyāthasse’iccādinā tthatte-so agamittha, gamittha, te agamū, gamū.

By the rule beginning `Eyyāthasse`, etc., with the ending `ttha`: `so agamittha`, `gamittha`; `te agamū`, `gamū`.

Rassatte-agamu, gamu, tvaṃ agamise, gamise, tumhe agamivhaṃ, gamivhaṃ, ahaṃ agama, gama, agamaṃ, gamaṃ vā, agamimhe, gamimhe.

Upon shortening: `agamu`, `gamu`. Also: `tvaṃ agamise`, `gamise`; `tumhe agamivhaṃ`, `gamivhaṃ`; `ahaṃ agama`, `gama`, or `agamaṃ`, `gamaṃ`; `mayaṃ agamimhe`, `gamimhe`.

Kamme-agamīyi, agammi, agamīyittho, agammittho, agamīyuṃ, gamīyuṃ, agamīyiṃsu, gamīyiṃsu, agammuṃ, gammuṃ, agammiṃsu, gammiṃsu.

In the passive voice: `agamīyi`, `agammi`, `agamīyittho`, `agammittho`, `agamīyuṃ`, `gamīyuṃ`, `agamīyiṃsu`, `gamīyiṃsu`, `agammuṃ`, `gammuṃ`, `agammiṃsu`, `gammiṃsu`.

Parachakke-agamīyittha, gamīyittha, agammittha, gammittha.

In the other paradigm: `agamīyittha`, `gamīyittha`, `agammittha`, `gammittha`.

Kārite-agamāpayi, gamāpayi, agamāpesi, gamāpesi, agamāpayuṃ, gamāpayuṃ, agamāpayiṃsu, gamāpayiṃsu.

In the causative: `agamāpayi`, `gamāpayi`, `agamāpesi`, `gamāpesi`, `agamāpayuṃ`, `gamāpayuṃ`, `agamāpayiṃsu`, `gamāpayiṃsu`.

644. Gamissa ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

644. `Gamissa`.

Āādimhi [M 0.0416] īādimhi ca gamissa massa ā hoti. Saralopo.

Before endings beginning with `ā` and `ī`, for `gamissa`, the `m` becomes `ā`. There is elision of `s`.

So agā, te agū, tvaṃ ago, tumhe aguttha, ahaṃ agaṃ, mayaṃ agumhā.

`So agā`, `te agū`, `tvaṃ ago`, `tumhe aguttha`, `ahaṃ agaṃ`, `mayaṃ agumhā`.

Īādimhi īsaralopo, agā devāna santike jā. 1.14.205, vāyaso anupariyagā su. ni. 449.

Before an ending beginning with `ī`, there is elision of the vowel `ī`. Examples: `agā devāna santike` (he went near the gods); `vāyaso anupariyagā` (the crow went around).

Āpubbo āgamane, anavhito tato āgā jā. 1.5.21, sopā’gā samitiṃ vanaṃ dī. ni. 2.335.

With the prefix `ā`, it means 'to come'. Examples: `anavhito tato āgā` (uninvited, he then came); `sopā’gā samitiṃ vanaṃ` (he came to the assembly in the forest).

Adhipubbo paṭilābhe, ajjhagā amataṃ santiṃ vi. va. 846, taṇhānaṃ khayamajjhagā dha. pa. 154.

With the prefix `adhi`, it means 'to attain'. Examples: `ajjhagā amataṃ santiṃ` (he attained the deathless peace); `taṇhānaṃ khayamajjhagā` (he attained the destruction of craving).

Atipubbo upādhipubbo ca titikkame, nakkhattaṃ paṭimānentaṃ, attho bālaṃ upajjhagā jā. 1.1.49. Khaṇo ve mā upajjhagā.

With the prefixes `ati` and `upa-adhi`, it means 'to pass by' or 'to overcome'. Examples: `nakkhattaṃ paṭimānentaṃ, attho bālaṃ upajjhagā` (while he waited for the constellation, the opportunity passed the fool by); `Khaṇo ve mā upajjhagā` (do not let the moment pass you by).

Etāni o, avacanānaṃ lope sati tumha’mhayogepi labhanti, aguṃ, agiṃsu, agaṃsu. Samantā vijjutā āguṃ jā. 2.22.2264, tepā’guṃsamitiṃ vanaṃ (gavesitabbaṃ), visesaṃ ajjhagaṃsute dī. ni. 2.354, asesaṃ parinibbanti, asesaṃ dukkhamajjhaguṃ itivu. 93, sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ upajjhaguṃ paṭi. ma. 1.236; ma. ni. 3.271. Ajjhago, ajjhaga, ajjhagi, ajjhaguttha, ajjhagiṃ, ajjhagimhā, ajjhagumhā, agā, āgā, anvagā, ajjhagā, upajjhagā, agū, āgū. Āgū devā yasassino dī. ni. 2.340, cittassa ekadhammassa, sabbeva vasamanvagū saṃ. ni. 1.61. Cetā haniṃsu vedabbaṃ, sabbe te byasanamajjhagū jā. 1.1.48.

O, when there is elision of the pronouns, these forms are also found in connection with `tumha` and `amha`: `aguṃ`, `agiṃsu`, `agaṃsu`. Examples: `Samantā vijjutā āguṃ` (lightning flashed all around); `tepā’guṃsamitiṃ vanaṃ` (they came to the assembly in the forest); `visesaṃ ajjhagaṃsute` (they attained distinction); `asesaṃ parinibbanti, asesaṃ dukkhamajjhaguṃ` (they are completely extinguished, they have completely overcome suffering); `sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ upajjhaguṃ` (they have overcome all suffering). Further forms: `Ajjhago`, `ajjhaga`, `ajjhagi`, `ajjhaguttha`, `ajjhagiṃ`, `ajjhagimhā`, `ajjhagumhā`, `agā`, `āgā`, `anvagā`, `ajjhagā`, `upajjhagā`, `agū`, `āgū`. Examples: `Āgū devā yasassino` (the glorious gods came); `cittassa ekadhammassa, sabbeva vasamanvagū` (all came under the power of the one thing, the mind); `Cetā haniṃsu vedabbaṃ, sabbe te byasanamajjhagū` (the Cetīs killed Vedabba, they all met with disaster).

Parokkhāyaṃ [M 0.0417] ādissa dvittaṃ, ‘kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā’ti pubbassa cavaggo. So jagama, mahāvuttinā upantassa dīgho, kvaci assa ittaṃ, “rājā dudīpo jagāmi magga”nti jā. 2.22.911; ‘rājā dudīpopi jagāma saggaṃ’ pāḷi. So jagāma, te jagāmu, tvaṃ jagame.

In the Parokkhā (perfect tense), there is reduplication of the beginning of the root. By the rule `kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā`, the preceding guttural becomes a palatal. Thus: `so jagama`. By Mahāvutti, the penultimate vowel is lengthened. Sometimes `a` becomes `i`; the Pāli text is: `rājā dudīpo jagāmi maggaṃ` (King Dudīpa, I went the path). Further forms: `So jagāma`, `te jagāmu`, `tvaṃ jagame`.

Byañjanādimhi ikārāgamo, tumhe jagamittha, ahaṃ jagamaṃ, mayaṃ jagamimha, so jagamittha, te jagamire, tvaṃ jagamittho, tumhe jagamivho, ahaṃ jagamiṃ, mayaṃ jagamimhe.

Before an ending beginning with a consonant, there is the augment `i`. Examples: `tumhe jagamittha`, `ahaṃ jagamaṃ`, `mayaṃ jagamimha`, `so jagamittha`, `te jagamire`, `tvaṃ jagamittho`, `tumhe jagamivho`, `ahaṃ jagamiṃ`, `mayaṃ jagamimhe`.

Ssatyādimhi-gamissati, gamissanti, gamissare.

Before endings beginning with `ssati`: `gamissati`, `gamissanti`, `gamissare`.

Parachakke-so gamissate, te gamissante, gamissare, tvaṃ gamissase, tumhe gamissavhe, ahaṃ gamissaṃ, mayaṃ gamissāmhe.

In the other paradigm: `so gamissate`, `te gamissante`, `gamissare`, `tvaṃ gamissase`, `tumhe gamissavhe`, `ahaṃ gamissaṃ`, `mayaṃ gamissāmhe`.

Ssādimhi-so agamissā, gamissā.

Before endings beginning with `ssā`: `so agamissā`, `gamissā`.

‘Āīūmhāssāssāmhānaṃ vā’ti ssā, ssāmhānaṃ rasso, agamissa, gamissa, te agamissaṃsu, gamissaṃsu, tvaṃ agamisse, gamisse.

By the rule `Āīūmhāssāssāmhānaṃ vā`, `ssā` and `ssāmha` are optionally shortened. Examples: `agamissa`, `gamissa`; `te agamissaṃsu`, `gamissaṃsu`; `tvaṃ agamisse`, `gamisse`.

‘Eyyāthasse’ iccādinā ssessa attaṃ, tvaṃ agamissa, gamissa, tumhe agamissatha, gamissatha, ahaṃ agamissaṃ, gamissaṃ, mayaṃ agamissāmhā, gamissāmhā, agamissāmha, gamissāmha.

By the rule beginning `Eyyāthasse`, etc., `sse` becomes `a`. Thus: `tvaṃ agamissa`, `gamissa`. Further forms: `tumhe agamissatha`, `gamissatha`; `ahaṃ agamissaṃ`, `gamissaṃ`; `mayaṃ agamissāmhā`, `gamissāmhā`, `agamissāmha`, `gamissāmha`.

‘Gama vada dānaṃ ghammavajjadajjā’ti sabbavibhattīsu gamissa ghammo, ghammati, ghammanti.

By the rule ‘Gama vada dānaṃ ghammavajjadajjā,’ in all inflections, ‘ghamma’ is substituted for ‘gam.’ Examples: ghammati (he goes), ghammanti (they go).

Kamme-ghammīyati, ghammīyanti.

In the passive voice: ghammīyati (it is gone), ghammīyanti (they are gone).

Mahāvuttinā gagghādeso vā, tvaṃ yena yeneva gagghasi, phāsuṃyeva gagghasi a. ni. 8.63.

Or, according to the Mahāvutti, there is the substitution of ‘gaggha.’ Example: tvaṃ yena yeneva gagghasi, phāsuṃyeva gagghasi (wherever you go, you go comfortably).

‘Gamayamisāsadisānaṃ [M 0.0418] vācchaṅa’ iti suttena sabbavibhattīsu gamissa massa ccho, gacchati, gacchanti, gacchare.

By the sutta ‘Gamayamisāsadisānaṃ vācchaṅa,’ in all inflections, ‘ccha’ is substituted for the ‘m’ of ‘gam.’ Examples: gacchati (he goes), gacchanti (they go), gacchare (they go).

Kamme-gacchīyati, gacchīyanti, gacchiyyati, gacchiyyanti, gacchiyyare.

In the passive voice: gacchīyati (it is gone), gacchīyanti (they are gone), gacchiyyati (it is gone), gacchiyyanti (they are gone), gacchiyyare (they are gone).

Kārite-gacchāpeti, gacchāpayati. Gacchatu, gacchantu, gaccheyya, gaccheyyuṃ.

In the causative voice: gacchāpeti (he causes to go), gacchāpayati (he causes to go). Imperative: gacchatu (let him go), gacchantu (let them go). Optative: gaccheyya (he should go), gaccheyyuṃ (they should go).

‘Eyyuṃssuṃ’iti uṃttaṃ, gacchuṃ.

By the rule ‘Eyyuṃssuṃ,’ ‘uṃ’ is stated. Example: gacchuṃ (they went).

‘Eyyeyyāseyyaṃnaṃ ṭe’iti suttena eyya, eyyāsi, eyyaṃvibhattīnaṃ ettaṃ, so gacche, tvaṃ gacche, ahaṃ gacche.

By the sutta ‘Eyyeyyāseyyaṃnaṃ ṭe,’ the inflections ‘eyya,’ ‘eyyāsi,’ and ‘eyyaṃ’ become ‘e.’ Examples: so gacche (he should go), tvaṃ gacche (you should go), ahaṃ gacche (I should go).

‘Eyyāthasse’ iccādinā eyyāthassa ottaṃ, tumhe gaccheyyātho.

By the rule beginning with ‘Eyyāthasse,’ ‘eyyātha’ becomes ‘o.’ Example: tumhe gaccheyyātho (you all should go).

Āādimhi-agacchā, gacchā, agaccha, gaccha vā.

In the aorist: agacchā (he went), gacchā (he went), agaccha (he went), or gaccha (he went).

Īādimhi-agacchi, gacchi, agacchuṃ, gacchuṃ, agacchiṃsu, gacchiṃsu.

In the aorist: agacchi (he went), gacchi (he went); agacchuṃ (they went), gacchuṃ (they went); agacchiṃsu (they went), gacchiṃsu (they went).

645. Ḍaṃsassa ca ñchaṅa ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105; ‘chaṅa’ (bahūsu).

645. And for ‘ḍaṃs,’ there is the substitution of ‘ñcha.’

Āādīsu īādīsu ca ḍaṃsassa ca anto byañjano ñchaṅa hoti.

In the aorist tenses, the final consonant of ‘ḍaṃs’ becomes ‘ñcha.’

So agañchā, gañchā. Tathā agañchū, gacchū.

So agañchā (he bit), gañchā (he bit). Similarly, agañchū (they bit), gañchū (they bit).

Īādimhi-so agañchi, gañchi.

In the aorist: so agañchi (he bit), gañchi (he bit).

Tasmiṃ paṭipaviṭṭhamhi, añño āgañchi brāhmaṇo su. ni. 985. Khippameva upāgañchi, yattha sammati temiyo jā. 2.22.73. Te agañchuṃ, gañchuṃ.

“When he had entered, another brahmin came. Quickly he approached where Temiya dwells.” Te agañchuṃ (they came), gañchuṃ (they came).

Ssatyādimhi-gacchissati, gacchissanti, gacchissare.

In the future tense: gacchissati (he will go), gacchissanti (they will go), gacchissare (they will go).

646. Labha vasa chida gama bhida rudānaṃ cchaṅa ka. 481; rū. 524; nī. 966, 968.

646. For ‘labh,’ ‘vas,’ ‘chid,’ ‘gam,’ ‘bhid,’ and ‘rud,’ there is the substitution of ‘ccha.’

Ssena [M 0.0419] saha etesaṃ cchaṅa hoti vā ssayuttāsu vibhattīsu, suttavibhattena susassa ca, “nadīva avasucchatī”ti jā. 2.22.2140 pāḷi.

For these roots, together with ‘ssa,’ the substitution ‘ccha’ optionally occurs in the inflections connected with ‘ssa’ (future and conditional); and by splitting the sutta, also for the desiderative suffix ‘sa.’ The Pāli passage is: “nadīva avasucchatī.”

Lacchati, labhissati, alacchā, alabhissā, vacchati, vasissati, avacchā, avasissā, checchati, chindissati, acchecchā, acchindissā, bhecchati, bhindissati, abhecchā, abhindissā, rucchati, rodissati, arucchā, arodissāti.

lacchati (he will obtain), labhissati (he will obtain), alacchā (he obtained), alabhissā (he would obtain); vacchati (he will dwell), vasissati (he will dwell), avacchā (he dwelt), avasissā (he would dwell); checchati (he will cut), chindissati (he will cut), acchecchā (he cut), acchindissā (he would cut); bhecchati (he will break), bhindissati (he will break), abhecchā (he broke), abhindissā (he would break); rucchati (he will weep), rodissati (he will weep), arucchā (he wept), arodissā (he would weep).

Iminā ssayuttāsu dvīsu vibhattīsu ssena saha gamissa massa ccho, gacchati, gacchissati, gacchanti, gacchissanti, ahaṃ gacchaṃ, gacchissaṃ.

By this rule, in the two inflections connected with ‘ssa,’ for the ‘m’ of ‘gam’ together with ‘ssa,’ there is the substitution ‘ccha.’ Examples: gacchati (he will go), gacchissati (he will go), gacchanti (they will go), gacchissanti (they will go), ahaṃ gacchaṃ (I go), gacchissaṃ (I will go).

Atrimā pāḷī-gacchaṃ pāraṃ samuddassa, kassaṃ purisakāriyaṃ jā. 2.22.131, tassāhaṃ santikaṃ gacchaṃ, so me satthā bhavissati, sabbāni abhisambhossaṃ, gacchaññeva rathesabha jā. 2.22.1832, vedhabyaṃ kaṭukaṃ loke, gacchaññeva rathesabha jā. 2.22.1835.

The following is the Pāli text: “gacchaṃ pāraṃ samuddassa, kassaṃ purisakāriyaṃ, tassāhaṃ santikaṃ gacchaṃ, so me satthā bhavissati, sabbāni abhisambhossaṃ, gacchaññeva rathesabha, vedhabyaṃ kaṭukaṃ loke, gacchaññeva rathesabha.” (I go to the other shore of the ocean; I will perform a man’s deed. I go to his presence; he will be my teacher. I shall fully comprehend all things. I shall indeed go, O bull among charioteers! Widowhood is bitter in the world; I shall indeed go, O bull among charioteers!)

Ssādimhi-agacchā, agacchissā, agacchaṃsu, agacchissaṃsu.

In the conditional tense: agacchā (he went), agacchissā (he would go), agacchaṃsu (they went), agacchissaṃsu (they would go).

Jara-vayohānimhi –

He became; they became; he was; they were; he will be; they will be; he would have been; they would have been; and so on.

647. Jarasadānamīma vā ka. 505, 609; rū. 482, 484; nī. 1018, 1213.

638. The substitution of 'bhū' for 'atthi' does not occur with the 'tyādi' and 'nta' suffixes.

Jara, sadānaṃ saramhā īmaāgamo hoti vāti īmaāgamo.

In suffixes other than 'tyādi' and other than 'nta', 'atthi' becomes 'bhū'. By this, it is to be understood that in the four inflections designated as 'tyādi', 'tvādi', 'eyyādi', and 'īādi', and in the 'nta' suffix, there is no substitution of 'bhū' for 'atthi'; but in the remaining four inflections, and in 'tabbādi' etc. other than 'nta', the substitution of 'bhū' for 'atthi' is obtained.

Jīrati, jīranti.

'Āsa' (root) – in attending. He attends upon a teacher; he attends upon; they attend upon; they attend upon.

Kārite-jīrāpeti, jīrāpayati.

In the passive voice – he is attended upon; he is attended upon.

648. Jaramarānamiyaṅa ka. 505; rū. 482; nī. 1018; ‘…mīyaṅa’ (bahūsu).

In the causative voice – a mother causes her son to attend upon a teacher; she causes him to attend upon; she causes him to attend upon; she causes him to attend upon.

Etesaṃ [M 0.0420] iyaṅa hoti vā nta, māna, tyādīsu.

In the 'īādi' group – he attended; he attended upon; they attended; they attended upon; they attended; they attended upon.

Jiyati, jiyanti.

'Āsa' (root) – in dwelling.

Dīghatte-jīyati, jīyanti.

639. For the roots 'gam', 'yam', 'is', 'ās', and 'dis', 'ccha' with an indicatory 'ṅ' is an optional substitute.

Dvitte-jiyyati, jiyyanti.

For 'gam', 'yam', 'is', 'ās', and 'dis', the final consonant optionally becomes 'ccha' with an indicatory 'ṅ', when followed by 'nta', 'māna', 'tya', etc.

Kārite-jiyāpeti, jiyāpayati.

'Gacchanto', 'niyacchanto', 'icchanto', 'acchanto', 'dicchanto'—by this rule, 'ccha' is substituted for 'ās' in the 'tyādi' forms. Examples: 'acchati', 'acchanti', 'so acchi', 'te acchiṃsu'.

Janī-pātubhāve, mahāvuttinā sabbavibhattīsu nassa yādeso ādidīgho ca, jāyati, upajāyati, vijāyati, jāyanti, jāyare, pajāyanti, pajāyare, upajāyanti, upajāyare.

The root 'isu' – in seeking.

Kārite vuddhi natthi, janeti, janenti, janayati, janayanti.

640. Of a light and penultimate vowel.

Kamme-janīyati, janīyanti, jāyatu, jāyantu, jāyeyya, jāyeyyuṃ.

What occurs near the end is called 'upanta' (penultimate). The vowel preceding the final consonant of a root is called 'upanta'. For a light and penultimate 'i' or 'u' vowel, the 'vuddhi' forms 'e' and 'o' occur.

Kārite-janeyya, janeyyuṃ, janayeyya, janayeyyuṃ.

The root 'ira' – in trembling. Examples: 'erati', 'modati'.

Īādimhi-ajāyi, ajāyiṃsu, vijāyi, vijāyiṃsu, ajani, jani vā.

Why 'of a light vowel'? Examples: 'jīvati', 'dhūpati', 'ikkhati', 'sukkhati'.

Kārite-ajanesi, janesi, ajanayi, janayi, ajanesuṃ, janesuṃ, ajanayuṃ, janayuṃ, ajanayiṃsu, janayiṃsu.

Why 'of a penultimate vowel'? Examples: 'siñcati', 'bhuñjati'. Because of the intervention of the 'niggahīta' augment, it is not penultimate.

Ssatyādimhi-jāyissati, vijāyissati.

In the future tense: jāyissati (it will be born), vijāyissati (it will be born forth).

Ssādimhi-ajāyissā, jāyissā.

In the conditional: ajāyissā (it would be born), jāyissā (it would be born).

Ḍaṃsa-ḍaṃsane, ḍaṃsati, ḍaṃsanti.

The root Ḍaṃsa, in the sense of biting: ḍaṃsati (he/it bites), ḍaṃsanti (they bite).

Kārite-ḍaṃseti, ḍaṃsayati, ḍaṃsāpeti, ḍaṃsāpayati.

In the causative: ḍaṃseti (he causes to bite), ḍaṃsayati (he causes to bite), ḍaṃsāpeti (he causes to bite), ḍaṃsāpayati (he causes to bite).

Ā[M 0.0421], īādīsu ‘ḍaṃsassa ca ñchaṅa’ iti suttaṃ, niggahītalopo, aḍañchā, ḍañchā, aḍañchi, ḍañchi.

In the aorist (forms beginning with ā, ī, etc.), by the rule 'ḍaṃsassa ca ñchaṅa', with the elision of the niggahīta: aḍañchā, ḍañchā, aḍañchi, ḍañchi.

Daha-dāhe, dahati, dahanti.

The root Daha, in the sense of burning: dahati (it burns), dahanti (they burn).

Kamme yamhi ‘hassa vipallāso’ti pubbāparavipallāso, agginā gāmo dayhati, dayhanti.

In the passive with the 'ya' suffix, there is a transposition of 'h' (metathesis): agginā gāmo dayhati (the village is burned by fire), dayhanti (they are burned).

Kārite-dāheti, dāhayati, dahāpeti, dahāpayati.

In the causative: dāheti (he causes to burn), dāhayati (he causes to burn), dahāpeti (he causes to burn), dahāpayati (he causes to burn).

649. Dahassa dassa ḍo ka. 20; rū. 27; nī. 50; ‘…dasadadakkhā’ (bahūsu).

649. Of 'daha', the 'd' becomes 'ḍ'.

Dahadhātussa dassa ḍo hoti vā.

Of the root 'daha', the 'd' optionally becomes 'ḍ'.

Ḍahati, ḍahanti.

Ḍahati (it burns), ḍahanti (they burn).

Disa-pekkhane, tyādyuppatti, kattari lo.

The root Disa, in the sense of seeing; the verbal endings beginning with 'ti' are produced in the agentive sense; lo.

650. Disassa passadassadasadadakkhā ka. 471; rū. 483; nī. 951.

650. For 'disa', the substitutions are 'passa', 'dassa', 'dasa', 'da', and 'dakkha'.

Disadhātussa passa ca dassa ca dasa ca da ca dakkha cāti ete ādesā honti vā.

For the root 'dis', 'passa', 'dassa', 'dasa', 'da', and 'dakkha' are the optional substitutions.

Vipassanā, vipassī bhagavā, sudassī, piyadassī, atthadassī, dhammadassī, sudassaṃ vajjamaññesaṃ dha. pa. 252, sudassananagaraṃ, mahāsudassano nāma rājā dī. ni. 2.242.

Vipassanā (insight); the Blessed One, the penetrative seer (vipassī bhagavā); sudassī (seeing well); piyadassī (pleasant to see); atthadassī (seeing the meaning); dhammadassī (seeing the Dhamma); 'the fault of others is easy to see' (sudassaṃ vajjamaññesaṃ); the city of Sudassana; the king named Mahāsudassana.

Dasādese-catusaccaddaso nātho vibha. aṭṭha. suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā, duddaso dhammo mahāva. 7; dī. ni. 2.64, attano pana duddasaṃ dha. pa. 252, so ve bhikkhu dhammadasoti vuccati gavesitabbaṃ. Passa dhammaṃ durājānaṃ, sammuḷhettha aviddasū. Daṭṭhabbaṃ, daṭṭhā, daṭṭhunti.

With the 'dasa' substitution: 'the Lord who has seen the four truths' (catusaccaddaso nātho); 'the Dhamma is difficult to see' (duddaso dhammo); 'but one's own (fault) is difficult to see' (attano pana duddasaṃ); 'that monk is indeed called a Dhamma-seer' (so ve bhikkhu dhammadasoti vuccati). 'See the Dhamma, hard to understand; here the ignorant are bewildered' (Passa dhammaṃ durājānaṃ, sammuḷhettha aviddasū). Daṭṭhabbaṃ (to be seen), daṭṭhā (having seen), daṭṭhunti.

Iminā suttena disassa sabbavibhattīsu yathārahaṃ passa, dassa, dakkhādesā honti, ā, īādīsu dasa, dādesā honti, “dissati, dissantī”ti rūpāni pana yassa pubbarūpattena idha [M 0.0422] kamme sijjhanti, divādigaṇe kattari sijjhanti. Mahāvuttinā addassa, dissādesāpi honti. Atrimā pāḷī-yaṃ vāsavaṃ addassāmaṃ jā. 1.6.112; ‘addasāma’, ye mayaṃ bhagavantaṃ addassāma gavesitabbaṃ, api me mātaraṃ adassatha ma. ni. 2.356, dissanti bālā abyattā mahāva. 82, mayi ime dhammā sandissanti, ahañca imesu dhammesu sandissāmi ma. ni. 3.253, nimittāni padissanti, tāni ajja padissareti bu. vaṃ. 2.82, tasmā tyādīsupi “adassati, adassanti, adassasi, adassatha, adassāmi, addassāmā”ti yujjanti.

By this rule, for 'disa' in all inflections, 'passa', 'dassa', and 'dakkha' are the appropriate substitutions; in the aorist (forms beginning with 'ā', 'ī', etc.), 'dasa' and 'da' are the substitutions. However, the forms 'dissati' and 'dissanti' are formed here in the passive, and in the divādi class, they are formed in the active. According to the Mahāvutti, 'addassa' and 'dissa' are also substitutions. In the following Pali examples: 'we saw Vāsava' (yaṃ vāsavaṃ addassāmaṃ); 'we who saw the Blessed One' (ye mayaṃ bhagavantaṃ addassāma); 'did you see my mother?' (api me mātaraṃ adassatha); 'fools and the unwise appear' (dissanti bālā abyattā); 'these dhammas will be seen in me, and I will be seen in these dhammas' (mayi ime dhammā sandissanti, ahañca imesu dhammesu sandissāmi); 'signs will appear; those are apparent today' (nimittāni padissanti, tāni ajja padissareti). Therefore, even with the present tense endings (beginning with 'ti'), the forms 'adassati', 'adassanti', 'adassasi', 'adassatha', 'adassāmi', and 'addassāmā' are correct.

Kārite ṇimhi dassādeso, dasseti, dassayati, nidasseti, nidassayati, sandasseti, sandassayati.

In the causative, with the 'ṇi' suffix, 'dassa' is the substitution: dasseti (he shows), dassayati (he shows), nidasseti (he points out), nidassayati (he points out), sandasseti (he explains), sandassayati (he explains).

Kamme-dassīyati, dassīyanti, nidassīyati, nidassīyanti, sandassīyati, sandassīyanti, dakkhati, dakkhanti.

In the passive: dassīyati (is shown), dassīyanti (are shown), nidassīyati (is indicated), nidassīyanti (are indicated), sandassīyati (is revealed), sandassīyanti (are revealed). Also: dakkhati (he will see), dakkhanti (they will see).

Kamme-dakkhīyati, dakkhīyanti.

In the passive: dakkhīyati (it will be seen), dakkhīyanti (they will be seen).

‘Gamayamisāsadisānaṃ cchaṅa’ iti cchādese- dicchati, dicchanti iccādi.

By the rule 'Gamayamisāsadisānaṃ cchaṅa', when `ccha` is substituted: `dicchati`, `dicchanti`, etc.

Passati, passanti, dakkhati, dakkhanti, passīyati, passīyanti, dakkhīyati, dakkhīyanti.

Passati (he sees), passanti (they see); dakkhati (he will see), dakkhanti (they will see); passīyati (it is seen), passīyanti (they are seen); dakkhīyati (it will be seen), dakkhīyanti (they will be seen).

Yassa pubbarūpatte-dissati, dissanti, dissate, dissante, uddissate, uddissante, niddissate, niddissante, apadissate, apadissante.

When `ya` takes the form of the preceding consonant: `dissati` (is seen), `dissanti` (are seen); `dissate` (is seen), `dissante` (are seen); `uddissate` (is pointed out), `uddissante` (are pointed out); `niddissate` (is designated), `niddissante` (are designated); `apadissate` (is referred to), `apadissante` (are referred to).

Kārite-passāpeti, passāpayati, dakkhāpeti, dakkhāpayati.

In the causative: `passāpeti` (he causes to see), `passāpayati` (he causes to see); `dakkhāpeti` (he causes to see), `dakkhāpayati` (he causes to see).

Kamme-passāpīyati, dassīyati, nidassīyati, sandassīyati, dakkhāpīyati.

In the passive: `passāpīyati` (is caused to be seen), `dassīyati` (is shown), `nidassīyati` (is indicated), `sandassīyati` (is revealed), `dakkhāpīyati` (is caused to be seen).

Passatu[M 0.0423], passantu, dakkhatu, dakkhantu, passeyya, passeyyuṃ, dakkheyya, dakkheyyuṃ.

Passatu (let him see), passantu (let them see); dakkhatu (let him see), dakkhantu (let them see); passeyya (he should see), passeyyuṃ (they should see); dakkheyya (he should see), dakkheyyuṃ (they should see).

Eyyāmassa emu ca antassa u ca honti. “Kattha passemu khattiyaṃ jā. 2.2.1947, dakkhemu te nivesana”nti jā. 1.15.254 (…nivesanāni) pāḷi. Passeyyāma, passeyyāmu, dakkheyyāma, dakkheyyāmu.

For `eyyāma`, `emu` is the substitute, and for `anta`, `u` is the substitute. The Pāli states: 'Where shall we see the khattiya?' (`Kattha passemu khattiyaṃ`), 'we shall behold your dwelling' (`dakkhemu te nivesana`). Also: `passeyyāma`, `passeyyāmu`, `dakkheyyāma`, `dakkheyyāmu`.

Āādimhi-apassā, adakkhā.
