In the aorist: `apassā` (he saw), `adakkhā` (he saw).

Dasa, dādesesu dakārassa dvittaṃ, addasā kho bhagavā mahāva. 9; dī. ni. 2.69; saṃ. ni. 1.159, addasā kho āyasmā ānando ma. ni. 1.364.

When `dasa` and `dā` are substituted, the letter `d` is doubled. Examples: 'The Blessed One indeed saw' (`addasā kho bhagavā`), 'The Venerable Ānanda indeed saw' (`addasā kho āyasmā ānando`).

Rassatte-tamaddasa mahābrahmā, nisinnaṃ samhi vesmani jā. 1.16.148. Te addasū. Rassatte-addasu, āmantayassu vo putte, mā te mātaramaddasu jātake “āmantayassu te putte, mā te mātara maddasuṃ”.

When shortened: 'Mahābrahmā saw him, seated in his own abode' (`tamaddasa mahābrahmā, nisinnaṃ samhi vesmani`). 'They saw' (`Te addasū`). When shortened: `addasu`. 'Summon your sons, lest they see their mother' (`āmantayassu vo putte, mā te mātaramaddasu`).

Dādese-so addā.

When `dā` is substituted: `so addā` (he saw).

Rassatte-adda. Yāyamāno mahārājā, addā sīdantare nage jā. 2.22.2105. Yo dukkhaṃ sukhato adda, dukkhamaddakkhi sallato dī. ni. 2.368.

When shortened: `adda`. 'The great king, while journeying, saw in a mountain cleft' (`Yāyamāno mahārājā, addā sīdantare nage`). 'He who saw suffering as happiness, saw suffering as a dart' (`Yo dukkhaṃ sukhato adda, dukkhamaddakkhi sallato`).

Īādimhi-apassi, passi, apassī, passī, apassiṃsu, passiṃsu, apassi, passi, apassittha, passittha, apassiṃ, passiṃ, apassimhā, passimhā.

In the aorist with `ī`: `apassi` (he saw), `passi` (he saw); `apassī` (he saw), `passī` (he saw); `apassiṃsu` (they saw), `passiṃsu` (they saw); `apassi` (you saw), `passi` (you saw); `apassittha` (you saw), `passittha` (you saw); `apassiṃ` (I saw), `passiṃ` (I saw); `apassimhā` (we saw), `passimhā` (we saw).

Dassādese-addassi, addassuṃ, addassiṃsu, addassaṃsu, addassi, addassittha, addassiṃ, addassimhā.

When `dassa` is substituted: `addassi` (he saw), `addassuṃ` (they saw), `addassiṃsu` (they saw), `addassaṃsu` (they saw); `addassi` (you saw), `addassittha` (you saw); `addassiṃ` (I saw), `addassimhā` (we saw).

Dakkhādese-adakkhi, dakkhi iccādi.

When `dakkha` is substituted: `adakkhi` (he saw), `dakkhi` (he saw), etc.

Dasādese gāthāsu-addasi, addasuṃ, addasiṃsu, addasaṃsu.

When `dasa` is substituted, in verses: `addasi` (he saw), `addasuṃ` (they saw), `addasiṃsu` (they saw), `addasaṃsu` (they saw).

Parachakke-addasā[M 0.0424], addasū, ahaṃ addasaṃ, mayaṃ addassimhe. Addasaṃ kāma te mūlaṃ, saṅkappā kāma jāyasi jā. 1.8.39.

In the perfect tense: `addasā` (he saw), `addasū` (they saw), `ahaṃ addasaṃ` (I saw), `mayaṃ addassimhe` (we saw). 'I have seen, O craving, your root; from intention, O craving, you are born' (`Addasaṃ kāma te mūlaṃ, saṅkappā kāma jāyasi`).

Kvaci sāgame ākārāgamo, so addasāsi, te addasāsuṃ, ahaṃ addasāsiṃ, mayaṃ adasāsimha. Yaṃ addasāsiṃ sambuddhaṃ, desentaṃ dhammamuttamaṃ theragā. 287. Athaddasāsiṃ sambuddhaṃ, satthāramakutobhayaṃ theragā. 912.

Sometimes, with the `sa`-augment, there is an `ā`-augment: `so addasāsi` (he saw), `te addasāsuṃ` (they saw), `ahaṃ addasāsiṃ` (I saw), `mayaṃ adasāsimha` (we saw). 'The Sambuddha whom I saw, teaching the supreme Dhamma' (`Yaṃ addasāsiṃ sambuddhaṃ, desentaṃ dhammamuttamaṃ`). 'Then I saw the Sambuddha, the Teacher free from fear from any quarter' (`Athaddasāsiṃ sambuddhaṃ, satthāramakutobhayaṃ`).

Mahāvuttinā iṃssa imhi hoti, pathe addasāsimhi bhojaputte jā. 2.17.146.

According to the Mahāvutti, `iṃ` becomes `imhi`. Example: 'On the path, I saw the sons of Bhoja' (`pathe addasāsimhi bhojaputte`).

Ssatyādimhi-passissati, passissanti.

In the future tense: `passissati` (he will see), `passissanti` (they will see).

Dakkhādese‘dakkha sakkha hehi’iccādinā ssassalopo, dakkhati, dakkhanti, dakkhiti, dakkhinti, dakkhissati, dakkhissanti.

When `dakkha` is substituted, by rules such as 'dakkha sakkha hehi', there is elision of `ssa`: `dakkhati`, `dakkhanti`, `dakkhiti`, `dakkhinti`, `dakkhissati`, `dakkhissanti`.

Ssādimhi-apassissā, adakkhissā iccādi.

In the conditional: `apassissā` (he would have seen), `adakkhissā` (he would have seen), etc.

Mara-pāṇacāge, marati, maranti.

The root `mara` in the sense of 'giving up life': `marati` (he dies), `maranti` (they die).

‘Jaramarānamiyaṅa’iti iyādeso, miyati, miyanti, amhaṃ daharā na miyyare jā. 1.10.97.

By the rule 'Jaramarānamiyaṅa', `iya` is substituted: `miyati` (he dies), `miyanti` (they die). Example: 'Our young ones do not die' (`amhaṃ daharā na miyyare`).

Kārite ‘assā ṇānubandhe’ti āvuddhi, māreti, mārenti, mārayati, mārayanti, mārāpeti, mārāpenti, mārāpayati, mārāpayanti.

In the causative, by the rule 'assā ṇānubandhe', there is strengthening to `ā`: `māreti` (he kills), `mārenti` (they kill); `mārayati` (he kills), `mārayanti` (they kill); `mārāpeti` (he causes to kill), `mārāpenti` (they cause to kill); `mārāpayati` (he causes to kill), `mārāpayanti` (they cause to kill).

Yamu-uparame, yamati, yamanti. Pare ca na vijānanti, mayamettha yamāmase. Ettha ca ‘yamāmase’ti viramāmase, maraṇaṃ gacchāmaseti attho.

The root `yamu` in the sense of 'ceasing': `yamati` (he ceases), `yamanti` (they cease). 'And others do not know that here we are ceasing' (`Pare ca na vijānanti, mayamettha yamāmase`). Here, `yamāmase` means 'we desist', that is, 'we go to death'.

Saṃpubbo saṃyame, saṃyamati, saṃyamanti.

Preceded by `saṃ`, in the sense of 'restraint': `saṃyamati` (he restrains), `saṃyamanti` (they restrain).

Niggahītassa ñādese-saññamati, saññamanti.

When `ñ` is substituted for the niggahīta: `saññamati` (he restrains), `saññamanti` (they restrain).

Nipubbo [M 0.0425] niyame, niyamati, niyamanti.

Preceded by `ni`, in the sense of 'regulation': `niyamati` (he regulates), `niyamanti` (they regulate).

‘Gamayamisāsadisānaṃ vā cchaṅa’iti massa cchādeso, niyacchati, niyacchanti.

By the rule 'Gamayamisāsadisānaṃ vā cchaṅa', `ccha` is substituted for `ma`: `niyacchati` (he restrains), `niyacchanti` (they restrain).

Kamme-niyamīyati, niyamīyanti.

In the passive voice: it is restrained, they are restrained.

Pubbarūpe-niyammati, niyammanti.

In the prior form: it is restrained, they are restrained.

Kārite-niyāmeti, niyāmayati.

In the causative: he causes to regulate, he causes to regulate.

Ṇāpimhi na vuddhi, niyamāpeti, niyamāpayati, vavatthapetīti attho.

When `ṇāpi` follows, there is no vowel strengthening: he causes to regulate, he causes to regulate; the meaning is 'he determines'.

Ruda-assuvimocane, rodati, rodanti.

The root `rud` in the sense of shedding tears: he weeps, they weep.

Ssatyādimhi-‘labhavasachidagamabhidānaṃ cchaṅa’iti ssena saha dassa cchādeso, sā nūna kapaṇā ammā, cirarattāya rucchati jā. 2.22.2136. Koñjī samuddatīreva, kapaṇā nūna rucchati jā. 2.21.113. Sā nūna kapaṇā ammā, ciraṃ rucchati assame jā. 2.22.2138, kaṃ nva’jja chātā tasitā, uparucchanti dārakā jā. 2.22.2153. Rodissati, rodissanti, rucchati, rucchanti.

In the section beginning with the future tense suffix `ssa`: by the rule 'labhavasachidagamabhidārudānaṃ cchaṅa', for the roots `labha`, `vasa`, `chida`, `gama`, `bhida`, and `ruda`, the final consonant of the root together with `ssa` is substituted by `ccha`. 'Surely, that wretched mother weeps for a long time. Like a curlew on the seashore, surely the wretched one weeps. Surely, that wretched mother weeps for a long time in the hermitage. For whom now, hungry and thirsty, do the children lament?' He will weep, they will weep; he will weep, they will weep.

Ssādīsu-arucchā, arucchaṃsu, arodissā, arodissaṃsu.

In the section beginning with `ssa`: he would have wept, they would have wept; he would have wept, they would have wept.

Ruha-pāpuṇane, ruhati, ruhanti, āruhati, āruhanti, ārohati, ārohanti, abhiruhati, abhiruhanti, oruhati, oruhanti, orohati, orohanti.

The root `ruh` in the sense of reaching: he ascends, they ascend; he ascends, they ascend; he ascends, they ascend; he climbs up, they climb up; he descends, they descend; he descends, they descend.

Kamme-ārohīyati.

In the passive voice: it is climbed.

‘Hassa vipallāso’ti ha, yānaṃ vipariyāyo, āruyhati, oruyhati.

By the rule 'inversion of `h`', there is an inversion of `h` and `y`: one ascends, one descends.

Īādimhi-ruhi, āruhi, oruhi.

In the section beginning with `ī`: he ascended, he ascended, he descended.

‘Kusaruhissa cchī’ti suttaṃ, abhirucchi, abhiruhi vā.

By the sutta 'cchī for `kusa` and `ruh`': he ascended, or he ascended.

Labha-lābhe[M 0.0426], labhati, labhanti.

The root `labh` in the sense of obtaining: he obtains, they obtain.

Yassa pubbarūpatte ‘catutthadutiyesvesaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā’ti saṃyogādissa catutthassa tatiyattaṃ, labbhati, labbhanti, labbhare.

For which, in the prior form, by the rule 'the fourth and second consonants become the third and first respectively', the fourth consonant at the beginning of a conjunct becomes the third: it is obtained, they are obtained, they are obtained.

Īādimhi-alabhi, alabhiṃsu.

In the section beginning with `ī`: he obtained, they obtained.

651. Labhā iṃīnaṃ thaṃthā vā ka. 497; rū. 477; nī. 1013.

651. For `labh`, the endings `iṃ` and `ī` are optionally replaced by `thaṃ` and `thā`.

Labhamhā paresaṃ iṃ, īnaṃ kamena thaṃ, thā honti vā, dhātvantassa pararūpattaṃ, saṃyogādissa dutiyassa paṭhamattaṃ.

After `labh`, the following endings `iṃ` and `ī` optionally become `thaṃ` and `thā` respectively. The final consonant of the root is assimilated to the following consonant, and the second consonant of a conjunct becomes the first.

Ahaṃ alatthaṃ, alabhiṃ vā, so alattha, alabhi vā.

I obtained, or I obtained; he obtained, or he obtained.

Mahāvuttinā uṃssa thuṃ, thaṃsu honti, mhāssa ca thamhā, thuṃmhā honti, te bhagavato santike pabbajjañca upasampadañca alatthuṃ dī. ni. 2.77, satiṃ paccalatthuṃ, viparītasaññaṃ paccalatthuṃ, te satiṃ paccalatthaṃsu, agamamhā kho tava gehaṃ, tattha neva dānaṃ alatthamhā ma. ni. 2.300 (thokaṃ visadisaṃ), akkosameva alatthamhā, mayañca alatthamhā savanāya, alatthumhā vā. Dhātvantassa ccho ca. Tadāhaṃ pāpikaṃ diṭṭhiṃ, paṭilacchiṃ ayoniso jā. 1.16.204.

According to the Mahāvutti, `uṃ` becomes `thuṃ` or `thaṃsu`, and `mhā` becomes `thamhā` or `thuṃmhā`. 'They obtained the going forth and the higher ordination in the presence of the Blessed One. They regained mindfulness; they regained distorted perception. They regained mindfulness. We went to your house, but there we did not obtain a gift; we only obtained abuse. And we obtained the opportunity to hear, or we obtained.' And the final consonant of the root becomes `ccha`. 'Then I improperly acquired a wrong view.'

Ssatyādimhi-‘labhavasa chida gama bhida rudānaṃ cchaṅa’iti suttena ssena saha dhātvantassa cchādeso, lacchati, labhissati, lacchanti, labhissanti, lacchasi, labhissasi, lacchatha, labhissatha, lacchāmi, labhissāmi, lacchāma, labhissāma. Lacchāma putte jīvantā, arogā ca bhavāmase jā. 2.22.2260.

In the section beginning with the future tense suffix `ssa`: by the sutta 'labhavasachidagamabhidarudānaṃ cchaṅa', the final consonant of the root together with `ssa` is substituted by `ccha`. He will obtain, he will obtain; they will obtain, they will obtain; you will obtain, you will obtain; you (plural) will obtain, you (plural) will obtain; I will obtain, I will obtain; we will obtain, we will obtain. 'May we obtain living sons and be free from illness.'

Ssādimhi-alacchā, alabhissā, alacchaṃsu, alabhissaṃsu.

In the section beginning with `ssa`: he would have obtained, he would have obtained; they would have obtained, they would have obtained.

Vaca-viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, vacati, vacanti.

The root `vac` in the sense of clear speech: he speaks, they speak.

Kamme-vacīyati, vacīyanti.

In the passive voice: it is spoken, they are spoken.

Yassa [M 0.0427] pubbarūpatte ‘assū’ti suttena ādimhi akārassa uttaṃ, vuccati, vuccanti, vuccare, vuccate, vuccante, vuccare.

For which, in the prior form, by the sutta 'assū', the `a` of the root becomes `u`: it is said, they are said, they are said; it is said, they are said, they are said.

Kārite-vāceti, vācenti, vācayati, vācayanti, vācāpeti, vācāpenti, vācāpayati, vācāpayanti.

In the causative: he causes to speak, they cause to speak; he causes to speak, they cause to speak; he causes to speak, they cause to speak; he causes to speak, they cause to speak.

Īādimhi-avaci, vaci.

In the section beginning with `ī`: he spoke, he spoke.

Mahāvuttinā ākārena saha sāgamo, avacāsi, vacāsi, avacuṃ, vacuṃ, avaciṃsu, vaciṃsu, tvaṃ avaco, avaca, avaci, avacāsi, avacittha, avacittho, tumhe avacittha.

According to the Mahāvutti, there is the augment `sā` along with `ā`: he spoke, he spoke; they spoke, they spoke, they spoke; you spoke, you spoke, you spoke, you spoke; you (plural) spoke, you (plural) spoke; you (plural) spoke.

‘Mhāthānamuña’iti suttaṃ, tumhe avacuttha, vacuttha, ahaṃ avaciṃ, vaciṃ, avacāsiṃ, vacāsiṃ, mayaṃ avacimhā, vacimhā, avacimha, vacimha vā, mayaṃ avacumhā, vacumhā, so avacā, vacā.

By the sutta 'Mhāthānamuña': you (plural) spoke, you (plural) spoke; I spoke, I spoke, I spoke, I spoke; we spoke, we spoke, or we spoke, we spoke; we spoke, we spoke; he spoke, he spoke.

Rassatte-avaca, avacittha, vacittha vā, ahaṃ avacaṃ, avaca, vaca vā, mayaṃ avacimhe, vacimhe.

When shortened: he spoke; you (plural) spoke, or you (plural) spoke; I spoke, I spoke, or I spoke; we spoke, we spoke.

652. Īādo vacassoma ka. 477; rū. 479; nī. 958; caṃ. 6.2.69; pā. 7.4.20.

652. In the section beginning with `ī`, for `vac` there is the ending `oma`.

Īādīsu vacassa mānubandho o hoti.

Before the aorist endings beginning with ī, the augment o is prefixed to vac.

So avoci, te avocuṃ, avociṃsu, tvaṃ avoci, tumhe avocuttha, ahaṃ avociṃ, mayaṃ avocumhā, so avoca, rasso, bhagavā etadavoca udā. 20.

He said, they said, they said, you said, you (pl.) said, I said, we said, he said (with shortening); the Blessed One said this.

Ssatyādimhi –

Before the future endings beginning with ssa:

653. Vacabhujamucavisānaṃ kkhaṅa ka. 481; rū. 524; nī. 963; ‘bhuja muca vaca visānaṃ kkhaṅa (bahūsu).

653. For the roots vac, bhuj, muc, and vis, there is the substitution kkhaṅa.

Ssena saha vacādīnaṃ anto byañjano kkhaṅa hoti vā ssayuttāsu vibhattīsu.

The final consonant of the roots beginning with vac, together with ssa, optionally becomes kkhaṅa before the endings connected with ssa.

Vakkhati[M 0.0428], vacissati, vakkhanti, vakkhare, vacissanti, vacissare, vakkhasi, vakkhatha, vakkhāmi, vakkhāma, vakkhate, vakkhante, vakkhase, vakkhavhe, ahaṃ vakkhaṃ, vacissaṃ, mayaṃ vakkhāmhe, vacissāmhe.

He will speak, he will speak; they will speak, they will speak (middle), they will speak, they will speak (middle); you (sg.) will speak; you (pl.) will speak; I will speak; we will speak. (Middle voice:) he will speak; they will speak; you (sg.) will speak; you (pl.) will speak; I will speak, I will speak; we will speak, we will speak.

‘Ssenā’ti adhikārena vinā dhātvantassa kkhādesopi labbhati, vakkhissati, vakkhissanti.

Without the governing rule 'Ssenā', the substitution of kkhā for the final letter of the root is also found: he will speak, they will speak.

Ssādimhi-avakkhā, avacissā, avakkhaṃsu, avacissaṃsu.

Before the conditional endings beginning with ssā: he would have spoken, he would have spoken; they would have spoken, they would have spoken.

Vada-viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, vadati, vadanti, ovadati, ovadanti, vadasi, vadatha, vadāmi, vadāma.

The root vad, in the sense of clear speech: he speaks, they speak; he advises, they advise; you speak, you (pl.) speak; I speak, we speak.

Lassa ette-vadeti, vadenti, vadesi, vadetha, vademi, vadema.

When `la` becomes `e`: he should speak, they should speak; you should speak, you (pl.) should speak; I should speak, we should speak.

Kamme-vadīyati, vadiyyati, ovadīyati, ovadiyyati.

In the passive voice: it is spoken, it is spoken; it is advised, it is advised.

Dassa cavaggatte yassa pubbarūpattaṃ, vajjati, vajjanti, ovajjati, ovajjanti.

When `d` becomes a palatal and `y` is assimilated to the preceding consonant: it is said, they are said; it is advised, they are advised.

Kārite-bheriṃ vādeti, vādenti, vādayati, vādayanti, guruṃ abhivādeti, abhivādenti, abhivādesi, abhivādetha, abhivādemi, abhivādema.

In the causative: he causes the drum to sound, they cause it to sound, he causes it to sound, they cause it to sound; he pays homage to the teacher, they pay homage, you (sg.) pay homage, you (pl.) pay homage, I pay homage, we pay homage.

Mahāvuttinā assa ittaṃ, abhivādiyāmi, abhivādiyāma, abhivādayāmi, abhivādayāma vā, abhivandāmi, abhivandāmāti attho. Vandanto hi “sukhī hotū”ti abhimaṅgalavacanaṃ vadāpeti nāma, tathāvacanañca vandanīyassa vattaṃ.

According to the Mahāvutti, `a` becomes `i`, hence `abhivādiyāmi`, `abhivādiyāma`; or `abhivādayāmi`, `abhivādayāma`. The meaning is 'I venerate', 'we venerate'. For one who venerates indeed causes auspicious words like “May you be happy” to be spoken, and such speech is the duty of the one worthy of veneration.

Ṇāpimhi na vuddhi, vadāpeti, vadāpayati.

Before the `ṇāpi` suffix, there is no vuddhi-strengthening: he causes to say, he causes to say.

‘Gamavadadānaṃ ghammavajjadajjā vā’ti vajjādeso, ‘ūlasse’ti lassa ettaṃ, vajjeti, vajjenti.

According to the rule ‘Gamavadadānaṃ ghammavajjadajjā vā’, there is the substitution `vajja` for `vada`; according to ‘ūlasse’, `la` becomes `e`. Thus: he blames, they blame.

Kamme-vajjīyati, vajjīyanti.

In the passive: one is blamed, they are blamed.

Kārite-vajjāpeti, vajjāpayati.

In the causative: one causes to accuse, one causes to accuse.

Eyyādimhi-‘eyyeyyāseyyaṃnaṃṭe’iti [M 0.0429] eyyādīnaṃ ekavacanānaṃ ettaṃ, vade, vadeyya, vajje, vajjeyya, vadeyyuṃ, vajjeyyuṃ.

Before the optative endings beginning with `eyya`, according to the rule 'eyyeyyāseyyaṃnaṃ ṭe', the singular endings beginning with `eyya` become `e`: he should speak, he should speak; he should blame, he should blame; they should speak, they should blame.

Vajjādese mahāvuttinā eyyassa āttaṃ, eyyumādīnaṃ eyyasaddassa lopo, so vajjā, te vajjuṃ.

In the case of the substitution `vajja`, according to the Mahāvutti, `eyya` becomes `ā`, and for endings like `eyyum`, the `eyya` is elided. Thus: he would accuse, they would accuse.

Eyyādīnaṃ yyāsaddassa lopo vā, tvaṃ vajjāsi, vajjesi, tumhe vajjātha, vajjetha, ahaṃ vajjāmi, vajjemi, mayaṃ vajjāma, vajjema, ahaṃ vajjaṃ, mayaṃ vajjāmhe, vajjeyyāmhe.

For the optative endings, `yyāsa` is optionally elided: you would accuse, you would accuse; you (pl.) would accuse, you (pl.) would accuse; I would accuse, I would accuse; we would accuse, we would accuse; I should accuse; we should accuse, we would accuse.

Atrimā pāḷī-vajjuṃ vā te na vā vajjuṃ, natthi nāsāya rūhanā jā. 1.3.33, ammaṃ ārogyaṃ vajjāsi, tvañca tāta sukhī bhava jā. 2.22.2148, ammaṃ ārogyaṃ vajjātha, ayaṃ no neti brāhmaṇo jā. 2.22.2174 iccādi.

Here is the Pāli text: 'Whether they would speak or not speak'; 'There is no regrowth for a nose'; 'May you speak of health to mother, and you, dear one, be happy'; 'May you (pl.) speak of health to mother'; 'This brahmin leads us', etc.

Hiyyattaniyaṃ-so avadā, vadā, avajjā, vajjā, te avadū, vadū, avajjū, vajjū.

In the aorist: he said, he said; he blamed, he blamed; they said, they said; they blamed, they blamed.

Ajjattaniyaṃ-so avadi, vadi, avajji, vajji, te avaduṃ, vaduṃ, avajjuṃ, vajjuṃ, avadiṃsu, vadiṃsu, avajjiṃsu, vajjiṃsu.

In the aorist: he said, he said; he blamed, he blamed; they said, they said; they blamed, they blamed; they said, they said; they blamed, they blamed.

Ssatyādimhi-vadissati, vajjissati.

Before the future endings: he will speak, he will blame/avoid.

Ssādimhi-avadissā, avajjissā iccādi.

In the conditional: he would have spoken, he would have blamed, etc.

Vida-ñāṇe, vidati.

The root `vid` in the sense of knowledge: he knows.

‘Yuvaṇṇānamiyaṅauvaṅa sare’ti saramhi iyādeso, te vidiyanti.

According to the rule 'Yuvaṇṇānamiyaṅauvaṅa sare', before a vowel, there is the substitution `iya`; thus: they are known.

Kārite-nivedeti, paṭivedeti, nivedayati, paṭivedayati, paṭivedayāmi vo bhikkhave ma. ni. 1.416, jānāpemīti attho. Vedayāmahaṃ bhante, vedayatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretūti cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102 jānāpemi, pākaṭaṃ karomīti vā attho.

In the causative: he informs, he reports, he makes known, he communicates. 'I declare to you, monks' means 'I make known'. 'I announce, venerable sir, let the Saṅgha remember me as one who announces' means 'I make known' or 'I make manifest'.

“Vediyāmahaṃ [M 0.0430] bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”tipi cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102 pāṭho, tattha apaccaye pare iyādeso yujjati.

‘Vediyāmahaṃ bhante, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū’ is also a reading. In that case, the substitution `iya` is suitable when a non-causative suffix follows.

Eyyādimhi-videyya, vidiyeyya, videyyuṃ, vidiyeyyuṃ.

In the optative: `videyya` (he should know), `vidiyeyya` (he might know), `videyyuṃ` (they should know), `vidiyeyyuṃ` (they might know).

Īādimhi-paccayānaṃ khayaṃ avedi, te viduṃ, vidiṃsu.

In the aorist: `paccayānaṃ khayaṃ avedi` (he knew the destruction of conditions), `te viduṃ` (they knew), `vidiṃsu` (they knew).

Kārite-nivedesi, nivedayi, paṭivedesi, paṭivedayi, nivedayuṃ, nivedayiṃsu, paṭivedayuṃ, paṭivedayiṃsu.

In the causative: `nivedesi`, `nivedayi` (he made known); `paṭivedesi`, `paṭivedayi` (he reported); `nivedayuṃ`, `nivedayiṃsu` (they made known); `paṭivedayuṃ`, `paṭivedayiṃsu` (they reported).

Ssatyādimhi-vidissati, vedissati, parisuddhāti vedissāmi mahāva. 134 iccādi.

In the future tense: `vidissati` (he will know), `vedissati` (he will experience), `parisuddhāti vedissāmi` (I will know it as pure), and so forth.

Vasa-nivāse, vasati, vasanti, nivasati, nivasanti.

The root `vas` in the sense of dwelling: `vasati` (he dwells), `vasanti` (they dwell), `nivasati` (he resides), `nivasanti` (they reside).

Kamme-adhi, āpubbo, tena gāmo adhivasīyati, āvasīyati, ajjhāvasīyati.

In the passive, preceded by `adhi` and `ā`: `tena gāmo adhivasīyati` (the village is inhabited by him), `āvasīyati` (it is dwelt in), `ajjhāvasīyati` (it is occupied).

‘Assū’ti suttena akārassa uttaṃ, vussati, vussanti, vussare, “bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti ma. ni. 1.257 pāḷi.

By the rule `Assū`, the letter `a` becomes `u`, thus: `vussati`, `vussanti`, `vussare`. The Pāli passage is: `bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī` (the holy life is lived in the Blessed One).

Kārite-vāseti, adhivāseti, vāsayati, adhivāsayati.

In the causative: `vāseti`, `vāsayati` (he causes to dwell); `adhivāseti`, `adhivāsayati` (he causes to dwell; he accepts/endures).

Ṇāpimhi vuddhi natthi, vasāpeti, vasāpayati.

With the `ṇāpi` suffix, there is no vowel strengthening: `vasāpeti` (he causes to dwell), `vasāpayati` (he causes to dwell).

Īādimhi-avasi, vasi, avasuṃ, vasuṃ, avasiṃsu, vasiṃsu.

In the aorist: `avasi`, `vasi` (he dwelt); `avasuṃ`, `vasuṃ` (they dwelt); `avasiṃsu`, `vasiṃsu` (they dwelt).

Ssatyādīsu-‘labha vasa chida gama bhida rudānaṃ cchaṅa’iti ssena saha dhātvantassa cchādeso, vacchati, vasissati, vacchanti, vasissanti, āyasmato nissāya vacchāmi mahāva. 77, na te vacchāmi santike jā. 2.22.1933, avacchā, avasissā, avacchaṃsu, avasissaṃsu.

In the future tense and so forth, by the rule `labha vasa chida gama bhida rudānaṃ cchaṅa`, the final consonant of the root together with `ssa` is replaced by `ccha`: `vacchati`, `vasissati` (he will dwell); `vacchanti`, `vasissanti` (they will dwell). Examples: `āyasmato nissāya vacchāmi` (I shall dwell relying on the venerable one); `na te vacchāmi santike` (I shall not dwell near you). Also: `avacchā`, `avasissā` (he would dwell); `avacchaṃsu`, `avasissaṃsu` (they would dwell).

Visa-pavisane, pavisati, pavisanti.

The root `vis` in the sense of entering: `pavisati` (he enters), `pavisanti` (they enter).

Kamme-pavisīyati[M 0.0431], pavisīyanti, pavisīyate, pavisīyante.

In the passive: `pavisīyati`, `pavisīyate` (it is entered); `pavisīyanti`, `pavisīyante` (they are entered).

Yassa pubbarūpatte-pavissati, pavissanti, pavissare, pavissate, pavissante, pavissare.

In the future tense: `pavissati` (he will enter), `pavissanti` (they will enter). In the middle voice: `pavissate` (he will enter), `pavissante`, `pavissare` (they will enter).

Kārite-paveseti, pavesayati.

In the causative: `paveseti`, `pavesayati` (he causes to enter).

Kamme-pavesīyati, pavesīyanti.

In the passive of the causative: `pavesīyati` (it is caused to enter), `pavesīyanti` (they are caused to enter).

Īādimhi upasaggassa dīgho vā, pāvisi.

In the aorist, the vowel of the prefix is optionally lengthened, for example: `pāvisi` (he entered).

Mahāvuttinā dhātvantassa kkho hoti, pāvekkhi pathaviṃ cecco jā. 1.19.98, so pāvekkhi kāsirājā jā. 1.15.266, so tassa gehaṃ pāvekkhi jā. 1.15.303, pāvisuṃ, pāvisiṃsu, pāvekkhiṃsu.

According to the Mahāvutti, the end of the root becomes `kkha`: `pāvekkhi pathaviṃ cecco` (the rogue entered the earth), `so pāvekkhi kāsirājā` (that king of Kāsī entered), `so tassa gehaṃ pāvekkhi` (he entered his house). Plural forms: `pāvisuṃ`, `pāvisiṃsu`, `pāvekkhiṃsu` (they entered).

Ssatyādīsu ‘vaca bhuja muca visānaṃ kkhaṅa’iti ssena saha dhātvantassa kkho, pavekkhati, pavisissati, pavekkhanti, pavisissanti, esa bhiyyo pavekkhāmi, vammikaṃ sataporisaṃ jā. 1.4.100, pāvekkhā, pavisissā, pāvekkhaṃsu, pavisissaṃsu.

In the future tense and so forth, by the rule `vaca bhuja muca visānaṃ kkhaṅa`, the final consonant of the root together with `ssa` becomes `kkha`: `pavekkhati`, `pavisissati` (he will enter); `pavekkhanti`, `pavisissanti` (they will enter). Example: `esa bhiyyo pavekkhāmi, vammikaṃ sataporisaṃ` (I shall enter further into the anthill a hundred persons deep). Also: `pāvekkhā`, `pavisissā` (he would enter); `pāvekkhaṃsu`, `pavisissaṃsu` (they would enter).

Sada-saṃsīdane, ‘jarasadānamīma vā’tiādisaramhā īmaāgamo hoti vā, sīdati, sīdanti, lābūni sīdanti, silā plavanti jā. 1.1.77, saṃsīdati, visīdati, osīdati, avasīdati.

The root `sad` in the sense of sinking. By a rule such as `jarasadānamīma vā`, the form becomes `sīd-`: `sīdati` (it sinks), `sīdanti` (they sink). Example: `lābūni sīdanti, silā plavanti` (gourds sink, stones float). Also: `saṃsīdati` (it sinks down), `visīdati` (it despairs), `osīdati` (it sinks down), `avasīdati` (it sinks down).

Nipubbo nisajjāyaṃ, nisīdati, nisīdanti.

Preceded by `ni`, in the sense of sitting: `nisīdati` (he sits down), `nisīdanti` (they sit down).

Papubbo pasāde, pasīdati, pasīdanti.

Preceded by `pa`, in the sense of faith or clarity: `pasīdati` (he has faith), `pasīdanti` (they have faith).

Kāritepi na vuddhi ādesantarattā, sīdeti, sīdayati, saṃsīdeti, saṃsīdayati, osīdeti, osīdayati, osīdāpeti, osīdāpayati, nisīdāpeti, nisīdāpayati.

Even in the causative, there is no vowel strengthening because a substitution has already occurred: `sīdeti`, `sīdayati` (he causes to sink); `saṃsīdeti`, `saṃsīdayati` (he causes to sink down); `osīdeti`, `osīdayati` (he causes to sink down); `osīdāpeti`, `osīdāpayati` (he causes to sink down); `nisīdāpeti`, `nisīdāpayati` (he causes to sit down).

Papubbamhi īma na hoti, pitā puttaṃ buddhe pasādeti, pasādayati, pasādenti, pasādayanti.

When preceded by `pa`, the `īma` augment does not occur. For example: `pitā puttaṃ buddhe pasādeti`, `pasādayati` (a father inspires faith in the Buddha in his son); `pasādenti`, `pasādayanti` (they inspire faith).

Kamme-pasādīyati[M 0.0432], pasādīyanti.

In the passive: `pasādīyati` (faith is inspired), `pasādīyanti` (faith is inspired).

Hana-hiṃsā, gatīsu, hanati, hananti.

The root `han` in the senses of harming and going: `hanati` (he strikes), `hananti` (they strike).

‘Kvaci vikaraṇāna’nti suttena lavikaraṇassa lope hanti, phalaṃ ve kadaliṃ hanti, sakkāro kāpurisaṃ hanti cūḷava. 335, hanti kuddho puthujjano a. ni. 7.64.

By the rule `Kvaci vikaraṇānaṃ...`, through the elision of the conjugational sign, `hanti` is formed. Examples: `phalaṃ ve kadaliṃ hanti` (its fruit indeed kills the plantain tree); `sakkāro kāpurisaṃ hanti` (honor kills a wicked person); `hanti kuddho puthujjano` (an angry worldling strikes).

Mahāvuttinā kvaci dhātvantalopo, vikkosamānā tibbāhi, hanti nesaṃ varaṃ varaṃ jā. 2.22.2370, luddakā migaṃ hanti, kevaṭṭā macchaṃ hanti.

According to the Mahāvutti, there is sometimes elision of the end of the root. Examples: `vikkosamānā tibbāhi, hanti nesaṃ varaṃ varaṃ` (shrieking with sharp cries, he strikes their best and finest); `luddakā migaṃ hanti` (the hunters kill the deer); `kevaṭṭā macchaṃ hanti` (the fishermen kill the fish).

Kamme-hanīyati, hanīyanti.

In the passive: `hanīyati` (he is struck), `hanīyanti` (they are struck).

Dhātvantassa cavaggatte yassa pubbarūpattaṃ, haññati, haññanti.

When the `ya` suffix is assimilated, the final consonant of the root becomes a palatal: `haññati` (he is struck), `haññanti` (they are struck).

Kārite –

In the causative:

654. Hanassa ghāto ṇānubandhe ka. 591; rū. 544; nī. 1195.

654. For 'han', 'ghāta' is substituted when 'ṇa' is an anubandha.

Hanassa ghāto hoti ṇānubandhe paccaye.

For 'han', 'ghāta' is substituted when the suffix has 'ṇa' as an anubandha.

Ghāteti, ghātayati, ghātāpeti, ghātāpayati.

Ghāteti, ghātayati, ghātāpeti, ghātāpayati.

Kamme-ghātīyati, ghātāpīyati.

In the passive: ghātīyati, ghātāpīyati.

Īādimhi-ahani, hani, ahaniṃsu, haniṃsu.

In forms beginning with 'ī': ahani, hani, ahaniṃsu, haniṃsu.

Kamme-ahaññi, haññi, ahaññiṃsu, haññiṃsu.

In the passive: ahaññi, haññi, ahaññiṃsu, haññiṃsu.

Ssatyādimhi –

In forms beginning with 'ssati':

655. Hanā jekhā ka. 481; rū. 524; nī. 967, 969? ‘…chakhā’ (bahūsu) ‘chekhā’ (katthaci).

655. From 'han', 'je' and 'khā'.

Hanamhā parassa ssakārassa je, khādesā honti vā, mahāvuttinā dhātvantassa pararūpattaṃ.

After 'han', for the following 'ssa', the substitutions 'je' and 'khā' optionally occur; by the Mahāvutti, the final of the root takes the form of the following.

Hajjeti[M 0.0433], hanissati, hajjenti, hajjesi, hajjetha, hajjemi, hanissāmi, hajjema, hanissāma.

Hajjeti, hanissati, hajjenti, hajjesi, hajjetha, hajjemi, hanissāmi, hajjema, hanissāma.

Khādese mahāvuttinā dhātvantassa vaggantattaṃ, paṭihaṅkhati, paṭihanissati, paṭihaṅkhanti, paṭihaṅkhasi, paṭihaṅkhāmi, paṭihaṅkhāma, paṭihanissāma.

In the case of the 'khā' substitution, by the Mahāvutti, the final of the root becomes the nasal of the class: paṭihaṅkhati, paṭihanissati, paṭihaṅkhanti, paṭihaṅkhasi, paṭihaṅkhāmi, paṭihaṅkhāma, paṭihanissāma.

Hara-haraṇe, harati, haranti.

The root 'hara' in the sense of carrying: harati, haranti.

Kamme-harīyati, harīyanti.

In the passive: harīyati, harīyanti.

Kārite-hāreti, hārayati.

In the causative: hāreti, hārayati.

Ṇāpimhi na vuddhi, harāpeti, harāpayati.

When 'ṇāpi' follows, there is no vuddhi: harāpeti, harāpayati.

Kamme-hārīyati, harāpīyati.

In the passive: hārīyati, harāpīyati.

Ā, īādīsu –

In forms beginning with 'ā', 'ī', etc.:

656. Āīādīsu harassā.

656. In forms beginning with 'ā' and 'ī', 'ā' is substituted for 'hara'.

Āādīsu īādīsu ca harassa rakārassa ā hoti vā, so ahā, aharā.

In forms beginning with 'ā' and 'ī', 'ā' is optionally substituted for the 'ra' of 'hara': so ahā, aharā.

Īādimhi-so ahāsi, ajini maṃ ahāsi me dha. pa. 3-4, attānaṃ upasaṃhāsi, āsanaṃ abhihāsi, sāsane vihāsi, vihāsi purisuttamo gavesitabbaṃ, dhammaṃ payirudāhāsi, ahari, hari, vihāsuṃ, āhiṃsu, vihiṃsu vā, “mā me tato mūlaphalaṃ āhaṃsū”ti jā. 2.18.22 pāḷi, ahāsuṃ, aharuṃ, haruṃ, ahariṃsu, hariṃsu, tvaṃ ahāsi, ahari, tumhe ahāsittha, aharittha, ahaṃ ahāsiṃ, ahariṃ, vihāsiṃ sāsane rato apa. thera 1.2.84, mayaṃ ahāsimhā, aharimhā.

In forms beginning with 'ī': so ahāsi, 'ajini maṃ ahāsi me', 'attānaṃ upasaṃhāsi', 'āsanaṃ abhihāsi', 'sāsane vihāsi', 'vihāsi purisuttamo', 'dhammaṃ payirudāhāsi', ahari, hari, vihāsuṃ, āhiṃsu, vihiṃsu optionally. The Pāli text is: “mā me tato mūlaphalaṃ āhaṃsū”. Also: ahāsuṃ, aharuṃ, haruṃ, ahariṃsu, hariṃsu, tvaṃ ahāsi, ahari, tumhe ahāsittha, aharittha, ahaṃ ahāsiṃ, ahariṃ, 'vihāsiṃ sāsane rato', mayaṃ ahāsimhā, aharimhā.

Parachakke assa tthattaṃ, so ahāsittha, aharittha.

In the second person plural, 'assa' becomes 'ttha': so ahāsittha, aharittha.

Ssatyādīsu [M 0.0434] –

In forms beginning with 'ssati':

657. Harassa cāhaṅa sse ‘hāssa cāhaṅa ssena’ (bahūsu).

657. And for 'hara', 'āhaṅa' is substituted before 'ssa'.

Ssakāravatīsu vibhattīsu ssena saha harassa ca karassa ca rakārassa āhaṅa hoti vā.

In endings containing 'ssa', 'āhaṅa' is optionally substituted for the 'ra' of 'hara' and 'kara', together with 'ssa'.

Iu āgame-hāhiti, khārikājañca hāhiti jā. 2.22.1759. Hāhati vā, harissati, hāhinti, hāhanti, harissanti, hāhasi, sukhaṃ bhikkhu vihāhisi dha. pa. 379. Hāhatha, hāhāmi, hāhāma, harissāma.

When 'i' or 'u' is the augment: hāhiti, 'khārikājañca hāhiti'. Or hāhati, harissati, hāhinti, hāhanti, harissanti, hāhasi, 'sukhaṃ bhikkhu vihāhisi'. Hāhatha, hāhāmi, hāhāma, harissāma.

Mahāvuttinā harassa dhātvantassa lopo ca, “yo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye appamatto vihassati saṃ. ni. 1.185, purakkhatvā vihassāma therīgā. 121, ahaṃ udakamāhissa”nti jā. 2.22.1931 pāḷī.

And by the Mahāvutti, there is elision of the final of the root 'hara'. The Pāli texts are: “yo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye appamatto vihassati”, “purakkhatvā vihassāma”, “ahaṃ udakamāhissa”.

Ssādimhi-ahāhā, aharissā, ahāhaṃsu, aharissaṃsu.

In forms beginning with 'ssā': ahāhā, aharissā, ahāhaṃsu, aharissaṃsu.

Āpubba sīsa-patthanāyaṃ, āsīsati, āsīsanti, paccāsīsati, paccāsīsanti.

The root 'sīsa' preceded by 'ā', in the sense of aspiring: āsīsati, āsīsanti, paccāsīsati, paccāsīsanti.

658. Ādismā sarā caṃ. 5.1.3; pā. 6.1.2.

658. The vowels begin with 'a'.

Ādibhūtā saramhā paraṃ paṭhamasaddarūpaṃ ekassaraṃ dverūpaṃ hoti, iminā sarapubbānaṃ dhātupadānaṃ padadvitte āsīsa, sīsa iti rūpadvayaṃ bhavati.

Following the initial vowel, the subsequent form of the first sound is single-vowel or double-form. By this, for root-words preceded by a vowel, in word-doubling, the two forms 'āsīsa' and 'sīsa' are produced.

659. Loponādibyañjanassa caṃ. 6.2.112; pā. 7.4.60.

659. Elision of a non-initial consonant.

Dvitte anādibhūtassa ekassa byañjanassa lopo hotīti purime sīsarūpe sakāralopo.

In doubling, there is elision of a single, non-initial consonant; thus, in the prior form 'sīsa', there is elision of the letter 's'.

Āsīsīsati[M 0.0435], āsīsīsanti iccādi.

Āsīsīsati, āsīsīsanti, etc.

Tathā ‘parokkhāyañcā’ti sutte casaddena kamādīnaṃ dhātupadānaṃ padadvitte kate ‘loponādibyañjanassā’ti purime padarūpe anādibyañjanalopo, ‘kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā’ti sesassa kavaggassa cavaggattaṃ, ‘niggahītañcā’ti niggahītāgamo, caṅkamati, caṅkamanti, caṅkamatu, caṅkamantu, caṅkameyya, caṅkameyyuṃ iccādi.

Similarly, in the rule 'parokkhāyañca', by the word 'ca', when the root-words such as 'kama' are doubled, by 'loponādibyañjanassa', there is elision of the non-initial consonant in the prior word-form. By 'kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā', the remaining k-group becomes the c-group. By 'niggahītañca', there is the insertion of a niggahīta. For example: caṅkamati, caṅkamanti, caṅkamatu, caṅkamantu, caṅkameyya, caṅkameyyuṃ, and so on.

Kuca-saṅkocane, caṅkocati, caṅkocanti.

Kuca, in the sense of contracting: caṅkocati, caṅkocanti.

Cala-calane, cañcalati, cañcalanti.

Cala, in the sense of shaking: cañcalati, cañcalanti.

Mahāvuttinā niggahītassa pararūpatte jara-bhijjane, jajjarati jajjaranti.

According to the Mahāvutti, when the niggahīta takes the form of the following consonant: jara, in the sense of decaying or breaking: jajjarati, jajjaranti.

Daḷa-dittiyaṃ, daddallati, daddallanti.

Daḷa, in the sense of shining: daddallati, daddallanti.

Muha-vecitte, momuhati, momuhanti, mahāvuttinā ussa ottaṃ.

Muha, in the sense of being bewildered: momuhati, momuhanti. According to the Mahāvutti, 'u' becomes 'o'.

Tathā ru-sadde, roruvati, roruvanti.

Similarly, ru, in the sense of making a sound: roruvati, roruvanti.

Lupa-giddhe, loluppati, loluppanti iccādi.

Lupa, in the sense of being greedy: loluppati, loluppanti, and so on.

Padadvittaṃ nāma padatthānaṃ atisayatādīpanatthaṃ, vicchāyaṃ pana ponopuñña, sambhamādīsu ca dvitte anādibyañjanalopo natthi, gāmo gāmo ramaṇīyo. Tathā kvaci atisayadīpanepi, rūparūpaṃ, dukkhadukkhaṃ, ajjhattajjhattaṃ, devadevo, munimuni, rājarājā, brahmabrahmā, varavaro, aggaaggo, jeṭṭhajeṭṭho, seṭṭhaseṭṭho, pasatthapasattho, uggatauggato, ukkaṭṭhukkaṭṭho, omakomako, dubbaladubbalo, abalaabalo, mahantamahanto iccādi.

Word-doubling serves to indicate an intensification of the meaning of words. However, in the senses of distribution (vicchā), frequency (ponopuñña), haste (sambhama), and so on, there is no elision of a non-initial consonant in doubling; for example, 'gāmo gāmo ramaṇīyo' (every single village is delightful). Similarly, in some cases also for indicating intensification: rūparūpaṃ (every single form), dukkhadukkhaṃ (extreme suffering), ajjhattajjhattaṃ (the purely internal), devadevo (god of gods), munimuni (sage of sages), rājarājā (king of kings), brahmabrahmā (brahmā of brahmās), varavaro (the most excellent), aggaaggo (the very highest), jeṭṭhajeṭṭho (the very eldest), seṭṭhaseṭṭho (the very best), pasatthapasattho (the most praised), uggatauggato (the most exalted), ukkaṭṭhukkaṭṭho (the most pre-eminent), omakomako (the very lowest), dubbaladubbalo (the very weakest), abalaabalo (the most powerless), mahantamahanto (the very greatest), and so on.

Bhūvādigaṇo niṭṭhito.

The Bhūvādi group is concluded.

Rudhādigaṇa

The Rudhādi Group

Atha [M 0.0436] rudhādigaṇo vuccate.

Now the Rudhādi group is explained.

‘Kattarī’ti padaṃ vattate, tañca bahulādhikārā vikaraṇānaṃ kattari nibandhaṃ bhāva, kammesu anibandhaṃ vikappena pavattiṃ dīpeti, tasmā bhāva, kammesu ca kāritarūpesu ca vikaraṇānaṃ pavatti veditabbā hotīti.

The term 'kattari' (agentive) is current. And by the governing principle of general application (bahulādhikāra), it indicates that the vikaraṇas are obligatory in the agentive sense, but in the impersonal (bhāva) and passive (kamma) senses, their application is optional. Therefore, the application of vikaraṇas is to be understood in the impersonal, passive, and also causative forms.

Chida, bhida, bhuja, muca, yuja, rica, rudha, lipa, vida, sica, subha.

Chida (to cut), bhida (to split), bhuja (to enjoy), muca (to release), yuja (to join), rica (to empty), rudha (to obstruct), lipa (to smear), vida (to find), sica (to sprinkle), subha (to shine/be beautiful).

660. Mañca rudhādīnaṃ ka. 446; rū. 509; nī. 926; caṃ. 1.1.93; pā. 3.1.78.

660. Mañca rudhādīnaṃ.

Rudhādīhi kriyatthehi kattari lo hoti, tesañca rudhādīnaṃ pubbantasaramhā paraṃ niggahītaṃ āgacchati, mānubandho pubbantadīpanattho, akāro uccāraṇattho, casaddena rudha, subhādīhi i, ī, e, opaccaye saṅgaṇhāti, niggahītassa vaggantattaṃ.

After the Rudhādi roots, which have the sense of action, the vikaraṇa 'a' occurs in the agentive. And for these Rudhādi roots, a niggahīta is inserted after the vowel of the initial part of the root. The indicatory letter 'm' is for the purpose of indicating this initial part. The letter 'a' is for pronunciation. By the word 'ca', it also includes the affixes i, ī, e, and o for roots such as rudha, subha, etc. The niggahīta becomes the nasal of the following consonant's class.

Rundhati.

Rundhati.

Chida-dvidhākaraṇe, chindati, chindanti.

Chida, in the sense of dividing into two: chindati, chindanti.

Kamme kyo, ‘tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā’ti yamhi dhātvantassa cavaggattaṃ, ‘vaggalasehi te’ti yassa pubbarūpattaṃ. Chijjati, chijjanti.

In the passive, the vikaraṇa 'ya' occurs. By the rule 'tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā', when 'ya' follows, the final consonant of the root becomes a palatal. By the rule 'vaggalasehi te', the 'ya' takes the form of the preceding consonant. Chijjati, chijjanti.

‘Garupubbā rassā re ntentīna’nti catunnaṃ nte, ntīnaṃ rettaṃ, chindate, chijjate, chijjante, chijjare.

By the rule 'Garupubbā rassā re ntentīnaṃ', the endings 'nte' and 'nti' may become 're'. Examples: chindate, chijjate, chijjante, chijjare.

Iminā niggahītāgamo, chindīyati, chindīyanti, chindīyate, chindīyante.

By this rule, there is the insertion of a niggahīta. Examples: chindīyati, chindīyanti, chindīyate, chindīyante.

Kārite-chedeti, chedayati, chedāpeti, chedāpayati, chindeti, chindayati, chindāpeti, chindāpayati.

In the causative: chedeti, chedayati, chedāpeti, chedāpayati, chindeti, chindayati, chindāpeti, chindāpayati.

Īādimhi-acchindi[M 0.0437], chindi, acchinduṃ, chinduṃ, acchindiṃsu, chindiṃsu.

In the aorist: acchindi, chindi, acchinduṃ, chinduṃ, acchindiṃsu, chindiṃsu.

Mahāvuttinā dhātvantassa ccho pubbassa dvittañca, acchecchi taṇhaṃ, vivattayi saṃyojanaṃ itivu. 53, “acchejjī”tipi divādipāṭho dissati, acchecchuṃ vata bho rukkhaṃ jā. 2.22.1788.

According to the Mahāvutti, the final consonant of the root becomes 'ccha', and the preceding consonant is doubled. Example: 'acchecchi taṇhaṃ, vivattayi saṃyojanaṃ' (he cut off craving, he rolled back the fetter). The reading 'acchejjī' is also seen as a Divādi group reading. 'acchecchuṃ vata bho rukkhaṃ' (Indeed, sirs, they cut down the tree).

Kamme-acchijji, chijji, acchindiyi, chindiyi.

In the passive: acchijji, chijji, acchindiyi, chindiyi.

Kārite-chedesi, kaṇṇanāsañca chedayi jā. 1.4.49, chindesi, chindayi.

In the causative: chedesi; 'kaṇṇanāsañca chedayi' (and he had the ears and nose cut off); chindesi, chindayi.

Ssatyādimhi-‘labhavasachidagamabhidarudānaṃ cchaṅa’iti ssena saha dhātvantassa ccho, checchati, chindissati, checchanti, chindissanti, checchasi, checchata, checchāmi, checchāma, chindissāma.

In the future tense: by the rule 'labhavasachidagamabhidarudānaṃ cchaṅa', the final consonant of the root together with the following `ssa` becomes `ccha`. For example: `checchati`, `chindissati`, `checchanti`, `chindissanti`, `checchasi`, `checchata`, `checchāmi`, `checchāma`, `chindissāma`.

Ssādimhi-acchecchā, acchindissā, acchecchaṃsu, acchindissaṃsu.

In the conditional tense: `acchecchā`, `acchindissā`, `acchecchaṃsu`, `acchindissaṃsu`.

Bhida-vidāraṇe, bhindati, bhindanti.

The root `bhida` in the sense of splitting: `bhindati`, `bhindanti`.

Kamme-bhijjati, bhijjanti, bhijjare, bhindiyati, bhindiyanti.

In the passive voice: `bhijjati`, `bhijjanti`, `bhijjare`; `bhindiyati`, `bhindiyanti`.

Kārite-bhikkhū bhikkhūhi bhedeti mahāva. 107, bhedayati, bhedāpeti, bhedāpayati, bhindeti, bhindayati, bhindāpeti, bhindāpayati.

In the causative voice: `bhikkhū bhikkhūhi bhedeti`, `bhedayati`, `bhedāpeti`, `bhedāpayati`, `bhindeti`, `bhindayati`, `bhindāpeti`, `bhindāpayati`.

Kamme-bhedīyati, bhedāpīyati.

In the passive voice: `bhedīyati`, `bhedāpīyati`.

Īādimhi-abhindi, bhindi, abhinduṃ, bhinduṃ, abhindiṃsu, bhindiṃsu.

In the aorist tense: `abhindi`, `bhindi`, `abhinduṃ`, `bhinduṃ`, `abhindiṃsu`, `bhindiṃsu`.

Kamme-abhijji, bhijji, abhindiyi, bhindiyi.

In the passive voice: `abhijji`, `bhijji`; `abhindiyi`, `bhindiyi`.

Kārite-abhedesi, bhedesi, abhedayi, bhedayi, bhedāpesi, bhedāpayi.

In the causative voice: `abhedesi`, `bhedesi`, `abhedayi`, `bhedayi`, `bhedāpesi`, `bhedāpayi`.

Ssatyādimhi-‘labhavasa…’iccādinā [M 0.0438] ssena saha dassa ccho, bhecchati, bhindissati, bhecchanti, bhindissanti, bhecchasi, bhecchatha, bhecchāmi, bhecchāma, bhindissāma, “taṃ te paññāya bhecchāmī”ti su. ni. 445 pāḷi.

In the future tense: by the rule 'labhavasa...' and so on, the `da` of the root together with the following `ssa` becomes `ccha`. For example: `bhecchati`, `bhindissati`, `bhecchanti`, `bhindissanti`, `bhecchasi`, `bhecchatha`, `bhecchāmi`, `bhecchāma`, `bhindissāma`. The Pāli passage is: 'taṃ te paññāya bhecchāmī'.

Ssādimhi-acchecchā, acchindissāiccādi.

In the conditional tense: `acchecchā`, `acchindissā`, and so on.

Bhuja-pālana, byavaharaṇesu, bhuñjati, bhuñjanti.

The root `bhuja` in the senses of protecting and of using: `bhuñjati`, `bhuñjanti`.

Kamme-bhujjati, bhujjanti.

In the passive voice: `bhujjati`, `bhujjanti`.

Kārite-bhojeti, bhojayati, bhojāpeti, bhojāpayati.

In the causative: bhojeti, bhojayati, bhojāpeti, bhojāpayati (he causes to eat/feed).

Kamme-bhojīyati, bhojāpīyati.

In the passive: bhojīyati (it is eaten/fed), bhojāpīyati (it is caused to be eaten/fed).

Ssatyādimhi-‘vacabhujamucavisānaṃ kkhaṅa’iti ssena saha dhātvantassa kkho, ādivuddhi, bhokkhati, bhuñjissati, bhokkhanti, bhokkhasi, bhokkhatha, bhokkhāmi, bhokkhāma, bhuñjissāma.

In the future tense, etc.: according to the rule 'vacabhujamucavisānaṃ kkhaṅa,' with 'ssa,' the final consonant of the root becomes 'kkha,' and the initial vowel is strengthened. Examples: bhokkhati (he will eat/consume), bhuñjissati (he will eat/consume), bhokkhanti (they will eat/consume), bhokkhasi (you [sg.] will eat/consume), bhokkhatha (you [pl.] will eat/consume), bhokkhāmi (I will eat/consume), bhokkhāma (we will eat/consume), bhuñjissāma (we will eat/consume).

Ssādimhi-abhokkhā, abhuñjissā, abhokkhaṃsu, abhuñjissaṃsu iccādi.

In the conditional: abokkhā (he would have eaten/consumed), abhuñjissā (he would have eaten/consumed), abhokkhaṃsu (they would have eaten/consumed), abhuñjissaṃsu (they would have eaten/consumed), etc.

Muca-mocane, muñcati, muñcanti, muñcare.

The root muc in the sense of releasing: muñcati (he releases), muñcanti (they release), muñcare (they are released).

Kamme-muccati, muccanti, muñcīyati, muñcīyanti.

In the passive: muccati (he/it is released), muccanti (they are released), muñcīyati (he/it is being released), muñcīyanti (they are being released).

Kārite-mocāpeti, mocāpayati.

In the causative: mocāpeti (he causes to release), mocāpayati (he causes to release).

Īādimhi-amuñci, muñci, amuñciṃsu, muñciṃsu.

In the aorist: amuñci (he released), muñci (he released), amuñciṃsu (they released), muñciṃsu (they released).

Kārite-amocesi, mocesi, amocayi, mocayi, amocesuṃ, mocesuṃ, amocayuṃ, mocayuṃ, amociṃsu, mociṃsu, amocayiṃsu, mocayiṃsu.

In the causative aorist: amocesi, mocesi, amocayi, mocayi (he caused to release); amocesuṃ, mocesuṃ, amocayuṃ, mocayuṃ, amociṃsu, mociṃsu, amocayiṃsu, mocayiṃsu (they caused to release).

Ssatyādimhi-ssena saha cassa kkho, mokkhati, muñcissati, mokkhanti mārabandhanā dha. pa. 37. Na me samaṇa mokkhasi saṃ. ni. 1.140. Mokkhatha, mokkhāmi, mokkhāma, muñcissāma.

In the future tense, etc.: with 'ssa,' 'ca' becomes 'kkha.' Examples: mokkhati (he will be freed/released), muñcissati (he will be freed/released). Mokkhanti, as in 'they will be freed from Māra's bonds.' Na me samaṇa mokkhasi, as in 'O ascetic, you will not escape me.' Mokkhatha (you [pl.] will be freed/released), mokkhāmi (I will be freed/released), mokkhāma (we will be freed/released), muñcissāma (we will be freed/released).

Ssādimhi-amokkhā[M 0.0439], mokkhā, amuñcissā, muñcissā, amokkhaṃsu, mokkhaṃsu, amuñcissaṃsu, muñcissaṃsu.

In the conditional: amokkhā (he would have been freed/released), mokkhā (he would have been freed/released), amuñcissā (he would have been freed/released), muñcissā (he would have been freed/released), amokkhaṃsu (they would have been freed/released), mokkhaṃsu (they would have been freed/released), amuñcissaṃsu (they would have been freed/released), muñcissaṃsu (they would have been freed/released).

Yuja-yoge, yuñjati buddhasāsane, ārabhatīti attho, yuñjanti, pamādamanuyuñjanti, bālā dummedhino janā dha. pa. 26. Yuñjasi, yuñjatha buddhasāsane saṃ. ni. 1.185. Yuñjāmi, yuñjāma.

The root yuj in the sense of joining/engaging: yuñjati, as in 'he engages in the Buddha's teaching,' the meaning is 'he undertakes.' Yuñjanti, as in 'foolish, unwise people indulge in heedlessness.' Yuñjasi (you [sg.] engage). Yuñjatha, as in 'you [pl.] engage in the Buddha's teaching.' Yuñjāmi (I engage), yuñjāma (we engage).

Kamme-yuñjīyati, yuñjīyanti.

In the passive: yuñjīyati (he/it is engaged), yuñjīyanti (they are engaged).

Kārite-yojeti, payojeti, niyojeti, uyyojeti, yojayati, payojayati, niyojayati, uyyojayati.

In the causative: yojeti, yojayati (he causes to join/apply); payojeti, payojayati (he causes to employ/apply); niyojeti, niyojayati (he causes to appoint/direct); uyyojeti, uyyojayati (he causes to send forth/dispatch).

Kamme-yojīyati, payojīyati, niyojīyati, uyyojīyati.

In the passive: yojīyati (it is caused to be joined/applied), payojīyati (it is caused to be employed/applied), niyojīyati (it is caused to be appointed/directed), uyyojīyati (it is caused to be sent forth/dispatched).

Rudha-āvaraṇe, rundhati, rundhiti, rundhīti, rundheti, rundhoti, rundhanti, orundhati, avarundhati, rundhāpeti, rundhāpayati, avarodheti, avarodhayati, uparodheti, uparodhayati, rodhāpeti, rodhāpayati.

The root rudh in the sense of obstructing/enclosing: rundhati, rundhiti, rundhīti, rundheti, rundhoti (he obstructs); rundhanti (they obstruct); orundhati, avarundhati (he obstructs/blocks); rundhāpeti, rundhāpayati (he causes to obstruct); avarodheti, avarodhayati (he obstructs/blocks); uparodheti, uparodhayati (he obstructs/harasses); rodhāpeti, rodhāpayati (he causes to obstruct).

Kamme-avarodhīyati iccādi.

In the passive: avarodhīyati (it is obstructed), etc.

Lipa-limpane, limpati, limpanti.

The root 'lipa' in the sense of smearing: limpati (he smears), limpanti (they smear).

Kamme-limpīyati.

In the passive voice: limpīyati (it is smeared).

Kārite-limpeti, limpayati, limpāpeti, limpāpayati, lepeti, lepayati, lepāpeti, lepāpayati iccādi.

In the causative voice: limpeti, limpayati, limpāpeti, limpāpayati (he causes to smear); lepeti, lepayati, lepāpeti, lepāpayati (he causes to smear or plaster), etc.

Vida-paṭilābhe, vindati, vindanti.

The root 'vida' in the sense of acquisition or obtaining: vindati (he obtains), vindanti (they obtain).

Kamme-vindīyati, vindīyanti.

In the passive voice: vindīyati (it is obtained or found), vindīyanti (they are obtained or found).

Kārite-vindeti, vindayati, vindāpeti, vindāpayahi.

In the causative voice: vindeti, vindayati, vindāpeti, vindāpayati (he causes to obtain).

Īādimhi-avindi[M 0.0440], vindi, udaṅgaṇe tattha papaṃ avinduṃ jā. 1.1.2, avindiṃsu, vindiṃsu iccādi.

In the aorist: avindi (he obtained), vindi (he obtained); as in, 'in the courtyard there they obtained demerit'; avindiṃsu (they obtained), vindiṃsu (they obtained), etc.

Sica-secane, siñcati, siñcanti.

The root 'sica' in the sense of sprinkling: siñcati (he sprinkles), siñcanti (they sprinkle).

Kamme-siñcīyati, siñcīyanti.

In the passive voice: siñcīyati (it is sprinkled or watered), siñcīyanti (they are sprinkled or watered).

Kārite-siñceti, siñcayati, siñcāpeti, siñcāpayati, siñceyya vā siñcāpeyya vā pāci. 140 iccādi.

In the causative voice: siñceti, siñcayati, siñcāpeti, siñcāpayati (he causes to sprinkle); as in, 'he might sprinkle or he might cause to sprinkle,' etc.

Subha-sampahāre, yo no gāvova sumbhati jā. 2.22.2132. Sumbhanti, sumbhasi, sumbhatha, bhūmiṃ sumbhāmi vegasā jā. 1.5.51, sumbhāma, sumbhiti, sumbhīti, sumbheti, sumbhoti iccādi.

The root 'subha' in the sense of striking or butting; as in, 'who butts us like a cow.' Sumbhanti (they butt), sumbhasi (you singular butt), sumbhatha (you plural butt); as in, 'I butt the ground forcefully.' Sumbhāma (we butt), sumbhiti, sumbhīti, sumbheti, sumbhoti (he butts), etc.

Gahadhātupi idha saṅgahitā. Gaha-upādāne. ‘Mañca rudhādīna’nti niggahītena saha lapaccayo.

The root 'gaha' is also included here. The root 'gaha' is in the sense of grasping or taking. According to the rule 'Mañca rudhādīnaṃ,' the suffix 'la' is used along with the niggahīta.

661. Ṇo niggahītassa ka. 490; rū. 518; nī. 982.

661. 'Ṇo' is substituted for the niggahīta.

Gahadhātumhi āgatassa niggahītassa ṇo hoti. Mahāvuttinā vikappena lassa dīgho.

For the niggahīta that occurs in the root 'gaha', 'ṇo' is substituted. According to the Mahāvutti, the 'la' is optionally lengthened.

Gaṇhāti, gaṇhati vā, gaṇhanti, gaṇhasi, gaṇhatha, gaṇhāmi, gaṇhāma.

Gaṇhāti (he seizes), or gaṇhati (he seizes), gaṇhanti (they seize), gaṇhasi (you singular seize), gaṇhatha (you plural seize), gaṇhāmi (I seize), gaṇhāma (we seize).

Kamme-gaṇhīyati, gaṇhīyanti.

In the passive voice: gaṇhīyati (he or it is seized), gaṇhīyanti (they are seized).

‘Hassa vipallāso’ti ha, yānaṃ vipariyāyo, gayhati, gayhanti, gayhare.

According to the rule 'hassa vipallāso' (inversion of 'h'), whereby 'h' is changed to 'y': gayhati (he or it is seized), gayhanti (they are seized), gayhare (they are seized).

Kārite-gāheti, gāhayati, gāhāpeti, gāhāpayati iccādi.

In the causative voice: gāheti, gāhayati, gāhāpeti, gāhāpayati (he causes to seize), etc.

662. Gahassa gheppo ka. 489; rū. 519; nī. 901.

662. For the root 'gaha', 'gheppa' is substituted.

Nta, māna, tyādīsu gahassa gheppādeso hoti vā.

With suffixes such as 'nta', 'māna', and 'ti', the substitute 'gheppa' optionally occurs for 'gaha'.

Gheppati[M 0.0441], gheppanti.

Gheppati (he is seized or grasped), gheppanti (they are seized or grasped).

Kamme-gheppīyati, gheppīyanti.

In the passive voice: gheppīyati, gheppīyanti.

Īādimhi-agaṇhi, gaṇhi.

In the aorist: agaṇhi (he seized), gaṇhi (he seized).

Mahāvuttinā niggahītalopo, iñaāgamassa ettaṃ, aggahesi, paṭiggahesi, anuggahesi, aggaṇhiṃsu, gaṇhiṃsu. Aggahesuṃ, paṭiggahesuṃ, anuggahesuṃ.

According to the Mahāvutti, there is elision of the niggahīta, and the 'i' augment becomes 'e': aggahesi, paṭiggahesi, anuggahesi, aggaṇhiṃsu, gaṇhiṃsu, aggahesuṃ, paṭiggahesuṃ, anuggahesuṃ.

Ssatyādimhi-gaṇhissati, gahessati, gaṇhissanti, gahessanti iccādi.

In the future tense: gaṇhissati, gahessati, gaṇhissanti, gahessanti, etc.

Rudhādigaṇo niṭṭhito.

The Rudhādi group is concluded.

Divādigaṇa

The Divādi Group

Atha divādigaṇo vuccate.

Now the Divādi group is explained.

Idha dhātūnaṃ kamo antakkharavasena vattabbo sabbaso sadisarūpattā.

Here, the order of the roots should be stated according to their final letters, since they are entirely similar in form.

Muca, vica, yuja, luja, vija, gada, pada, mada, vida, idha, kudha, gidha, budha, yudha, vidha, sidha, sudha mana, hana, kupa, dīpa, lupa, vapa, supa, divu, sivu, tasa, tusa, disa, dusa, sisa, susa, daha, naha, muha.

muca, vica, yuja, luja, vija, gada, pada, mada, vida, idha, kudha, gidha, budha, yudha, vidha, sidha, sudha, mana, hana, kupa, dīpa, lupa, vapa, supa, divu, sivu, tasa, tusa, disa, dusa, sisa, susa, daha, naha, muha.

663. Divādīhi yaka ka. 447; rū. 510; nī. 928; caṃ. 1.1.87; pā. 3.1.69.

663. From the Divādi roots, the suffix ya.

Divādīhi kriyatthehi kattari kānubandho yapaccayo hoti.

From the Divādi roots, when expressing action, the suffix ya with the kā-anubandha is added in the agentive.

Dibbati.

Dibbati.

Muca-muttiyaṃ, yassa pubbarūpattaṃ, muccati, vimuccati. Akammakattā suddhakammarūpaṃ na labbhati.

For muca—in the sense of release; its forms are muccati, vimuccati. Because the agent is intransitive, a pure passive form is not obtained.

Kārite-moceti[M 0.0442], mocayati, mocāpeti, mocāpayati.

In the causative: moceti, mocayati, mocāpeti, mocāpayati.

Kamme-mocīyati, mocāpīyati, muccatu, dukkhā muccantu.

In the passive: mocīyati, mocāpīyati. Muccatu, dukkhā muccantu.

Ssatyādimhi dhātvantassa kkho, mokkhati, mokkhanti.

In the future tense, the final consonant of the root becomes kkh: mokkhati, mokkhanti.

Vica-viveke, viviccati, viviccanti.

For vica—in the sense of discernment: viviccati, viviccanti.

Kārite-viveceti, vivecayati, vivecāpeti, vivecāpayati.

In the causative: viveceti, vivecayati, vivecāpeti, vivecāpayati.

Kamme-vivecīyati, vivecāpīyati iccādi.

In the passive: vivecīyati, vivecāpīyati, etc.

Yuja-yuttiyaṃ, yujjati, yujjanti.

For yuja—in the sense of joining: yujjati, yujjanti.

Luja-vināse, lujjati, lujjanti.

For luja—in the sense of breaking, destruction: lujjati, lujjanti.

Vija-bhaya, calanesu, saṃvijjati, saṃvijjanti.

For vija—in the senses of fear and agitation: saṃvijjati, saṃvijjanti.

Kārite-saṃvejeti, saṃvejayati, saṃvejenti, saṃvejayanti iccādi.

In the causative: saṃvejeti, saṃvejayati, saṃvejenti, saṃvejayanti, etc.

Gada-gajjane, megho gajjati, gajjanti.

For gada—in the sense of roaring: megho gajjati, gajjanti.

Pada-gatimhi, uppajjati, uppajjanti, nipajjati, vipajjati, sampajjati, āpajjati, samāpajjati, paṭipajjati.

For pada—in the sense of going: uppajjati, uppajjanti, nipajjati, vipajjati, sampajjati, āpajjati, samāpajjati, paṭipajjati.

Kamme-tena āpatti āpajjati, jhānaṃ samāpajjati, maggo paṭipajjati.

In the passive: tena āpatti āpajjati, jhānaṃ samāpajjati, maggo paṭipajjati.

Kyamhi parepi yaka hoti, tena āpatti āpajjīyati. Jhānaṃ samāpajjīyati, maggo paṭipajjīyati.

When the passive suffix ya follows, the conjugational sign ya also occurs: tena āpatti āpajjīyati, jhānaṃ samāpajjīyati, maggo paṭipajjīyati.

Kārite-uppādeti, uppādayati, nipphādeti, nipphādayati. Sampādeti, sampādayati, āpādeti, āpādayati, paṭipādeti, paṭipādayati, paṭipajjāpeti, paṭipajjāpayati.

In the causative: uppādeti, uppādayati, nipphādeti, nipphādayati, sampādeti, sampādayati, āpādeti, āpādayati, paṭipādeti, paṭipādayati, paṭipajjāpeti, paṭipajjāpayati.

Kamme-uppādīyati, nipphādīyati, sampādīyati, āpādīyati, paṭipādīyati.

In the passive: uppādīyati, nipphādīyati, sampādīyati, āpādīyati, paṭipādīyati.

Uppajjatu[M 0.0443], uppajjantu, uppajjeyya, uppajjeyyuṃ, kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa patto uppajjiyetha, cīvaraṃ uppajjiyetha, parikkhāro uppajjiyethāti mahāva. 67 imāni pana kattu, kammarūpāni.

Uppajjatu, uppajjantu, uppajjeyya, uppajjeyyuṃ. “How then might a bowl arise for the pupil? Might robes arise? Might requisites arise?” These are indeed agentive and passive forms.

Īādimhi-uppajji, nipajji, vipajji, sampajji, āpajji, samāpajji, paṭipajji.

In the aorist: uppajji, nipajji, vipajji, sampajji, āpajji, samāpajji, paṭipajji.

664. Kvaci vikaraṇānaṃ ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

664. Sometimes, of the vikaraṇas.

Vikaraṇānaṃ kvaci lopo hoti.

Sometimes there is elision of the vikaraṇas.

Cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi saṃ. ni. 5.1081 iccādi, uppajjiṃsu, nipajjiṃsu.

Cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi, etc. Uppajjiṃsu, nipajjiṃsu.

Mada-ummāde, majjati, majjanti.

For mada—in the sense of intoxication and madness: majjati, majjanti.

Vida-sattāyaṃ, vijjati, saṃvijjati.

For vida—in the sense of existence: vijjati, saṃvijjati.

Idha-samiddhiyaṃ, ijjhati, samijjhati.

For idha—in the sense of prosperity: ijjhati, samijjhati.

Kudha-kope, kujjhati, kujjhanti.

For kudha—in the sense of anger: kujjhati, kujjhanti.

Budha-avagamane, bujjhati, sambujjhati.

For budha—in the sense of understanding: bujjhati, sambujjhati.

Paṭipubbo niddakkhaye vikasane ca, paṭibujjhati.

With the prefix paṭi—in the sense of discerning and unfolding: paṭibujjhati (he awakens/understands).

Kamme-tena dhammo bujjhati, dhammā bujjhanti, bujjhare, bujjhīyati, bujjhīyanti.

In the passive: tena dhammo bujjhati (by him the Dhamma is understood); dhammā bujjhanti (phenomena are understood); bujjhare (they are understood); bujjhīyati (it is understood); bujjhīyanti (they are understood).

Kārite-bodheti, bodhayati, bodhāpeti, bodhāpayati, bujjhāpeti, bujjhāpayati.

In the causative: bodheti, bodhayati, bodhāpeti, bodhāpayati (he causes to awaken/enlighten); bujjhāpeti, bujjhāpayati (he causes to understand).

Yudha-sampahāre, mallo mallena saddhiṃ yujjhati, dve senā yujjhanti, dve meṇḍā yujjhanti, dve usabhā yujjhanti, dve hatthino yujjhanti, dve kukkuṭā yujjhanti.

The root yudh in the sense of battle: mallo mallena saddhiṃ yujjhati (a wrestler fights with a wrestler); dve senā yujjhanti (two armies fight); dve meṇḍā yujjhanti (two rams fight); dve usabhā yujjhanti (two bulls fight); dve hatthino yujjhanti (two elephants fight); dve kukkuṭā yujjhanti (two roosters fight).

Kamme-yujjhīyati, yujjhīyanti.

In the passive: yujjhīyati (it is fought), yujjhīyanti (they are fought).

Kārite-yodheti[M 0.0444], yodhayati, yujjhāpeti, yujjhāpayati, “yodhetha māraṃ paññāvudhenā”ti dha. pa. 40 pāḷi.

In the causative: yodheti, yodhayati, yujjhāpeti, yujjhāpayati (he causes to fight). The Pāli text states: 'yodhetha māraṃ paññāvudhenā' ('Fight Māra with the weapon of wisdom').

Vidha-tāḷane, sarena migaṃ vijjhati, dhammaṃ paṭivijjhati, paṭivijjhanti.

The root vidh in the sense of striking/piercing: sarena migaṃ vijjhati (he pierces a deer with an arrow); dhammaṃ paṭivijjhati (he penetrates the Dhamma); paṭivijjhanti (they penetrate).

Kamme kattusadisampi rūpaṃ hoti, tena dhammo paṭivijjhati, dhammā paṭivijjhanti, paṭivijjhīyati, paṭivijjhīyanti.

In the passive, the form can also be similar to the active: tena dhammo paṭivijjhati (by him the Dhamma is penetrated); dhammā paṭivijjhanti (phenomena are penetrated); paṭivijjhīyati (it is penetrated); paṭivijjhīyanti (they are penetrated).

Kārite-vedheti, vedhayati, paṭivedheti, paṭivedhayati, iccādi.

In the causative: vedheti, vedhayati (he causes to pierce); paṭivedheti, paṭivedhayati (he causes to penetrate), etc.

Sidha-saṃsiddhiyaṃ, sijjhati, sijjhanti, sijjhare.

The root sidh in the sense of accomplishment: sijjhati (it succeeds), sijjhanti (they succeed), sijjhare (it prospers).

Kārite mahāvuttinā issa āttaṃ, sādheti, sādhayati, sādhenti, sādhayanti.

In the causative, according to the Mahāvutti, 'i' becomes 'ā': sādheti, sādhayati (he causes to accomplish); sādhenti, sādhayanti (they cause to accomplish).

Kamme-sādhīyati, sādhīyanti iccādi.

In the passive: sādhīyati (it is accomplished), sādhīyanti (they are accomplished), etc.

Sudha-suddhiyaṃ, sujjhati, sujjhanti, visujjhati, parisujjhati.

The root sudh in the sense of purity: sujjhati (it is purified), sujjhanti (they are purified), visujjhati (it is cleansed), parisujjhati (it is completely purified).

Kārite-sodheti, sodhayati.

In the causative: he causes to purify, he causes to purify.

Mana-maññanāyaṃ, maññati, avamaññati, atimaññati, maññanti, avamaññanti, atimaññanti iccādi.

The root man in the sense of conceiving: he conceives, he despises, he overestimates; they conceive, they despise, they overestimate, and so on.

Hana-vighāta, saṅghātesu, haññati, vihaññati, haññanti, vihaññanti iccādi.

The root han in the sense of striking and impact: it is struck, it is afflicted; they are struck, they are afflicted, and so on.

Kupa-kope, paro parassa kuppati, kucchivāto kuppati, rogo kuppati, paṭikuppati, tejodhātu pakuppati ma. ni. 1.305.

The root kup in the sense of anger: one is angry with another; the stomach wind is disturbed; a disease is aggravated; it is provoked; the fire element is deranged.

Kārite-kopeti, kopayati iccādi.

In the causative: he makes angry, he causes to be angry, and so on.

Dīpa-dittiyaṃ, dippati, dippanti, pure adhammo dippati cūḷava. 437.

The root dīp in the sense of radiance: it shines, they shine; formerly, unrighteousness shone.

Kamme-dīpīyati, dīpīyanti.

In the passive: it is illuminated, they are illuminated.

Kārite garupantattā na vuddhi, dīpeti, dīpayati, dīpenti, dīpayanti iccādi.

In the causative, because the final vowel is heavy, there is no strengthening: he causes to shine, he causes to shine; they cause to shine, they cause to shine, and so on.

Lupa-adassane[M 0.0445], luppati, luppanti.

The root lup in the sense of disappearance: it is elided, they are elided.

Kārite-lopeti, lopayati iccādi.

In the causative: he causes to cut off, he removes, and so on.

Vapa-bījanikkhepe, vappati, vappanti iccādi.

The root vap in the sense of sowing seeds: one sows, they sow, and so on.

Supa-suppane, suppati, suppanti.

The root sup in the sense of sleeping: he sleeps, they sleep.

Mahāvuttinā ādivuddhi, soppati, soppanti.

According to the Mahāvutti, there is initial strengthening: he sleeps, they sleep.

Samu-upasame nivāse ca, sammati, visammati, upasammati, vūpasammati, assame sammati, yattha sammati temiyo jā. 2.22.73, sammanti. Kārite na vuddhi, sameti, vūpasameti iccādi.

The root sam in the sense of calming and dwelling: he is calm, he becomes weary, he is appeased, he is completely appeased; he dwells in the hermitage; where Temiya dwells; they are calm. In the causative, there is no strengthening: he causes to be calm, he causes to be completely calm, and so on.

Divu-kīḷāyaṃ vijigīsāyaṃ byavahāre thuti, kanti, gati, sattīsu ca, ‘tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā’ti yamhi vassa battaṃ, ‘vaggalasehi te’ti yassa battaṃ, dibbati, dibbanti iccādi.

The root div in the sense of play, desire for victory, conduct, praise, beauty, movement, and power; according to the rule by which v becomes b: he plays or shines, they play or shine, and so on.

Sivu-saṃsibbane, sibbati, sibbanti, sibbeyya vā sibbāpeyya vā pāci. 176 iccādi.

The root siv in the sense of sewing: he sews, they sew; he might sew or cause to sew, and so on.

Tasa-santāse, tassati.

The root tas in the sense of trembling: he trembles.

Mahāvuttinā tassa trattaṃ, utrassati, ubbijjatīti attho. Tassati, paritassati, pipāsatīti attho.

According to the Mahāvutti, its meaning is `trattaṃ`, 'it is startled', and 'it is alarmed'. The meaning is also: it thirsts, it trembles greatly, and it is thirsty.

Kārite-tāseti, tāsayati iccādi.

In the causative voice: he frightens, he terrifies, etc.

Tusa-pītimhi, tussati, santussati.

The root `tus` is in the sense of joy: he is pleased, he is content.

Kammepi-tussati, santussati, tussīyati.

Also in the passive voice: he is pleased, he is content, one is pleased.

Kārite-toseti, tosayati iccādi.

In the causative voice: he causes to please, he satisfies, etc.

Disa-paññāyane, dissati, padissati, sandissati. Dissanti bālā abyattā mahāva. 76, nimittāni padissanti bu. vaṃ. 2.82, ime dhammā mayi sandissanti, ahañca imesu dhammesu sandissāmi ma. ni. 3.253 (thokaṃ visadisaṃ).

The root `dis` is in the sense of appearing: it appears, it becomes evident, it is seen. 'Ignorant fools appear'; 'signs become evident'; 'these qualities are seen in me, and I am seen in these qualities.'

Dusa-paṭighāte[M 0.0446], dussati. Dosaneyyesu dussati. Padussati, dussanti, padussanti.

The root `dus` is in the sense of harming: it is corrupted. It is corrupted in matters that provoke aversion. It is greatly corrupted, they are corrupted, they are greatly corrupted.

Kārite dīgho, dūseti, dūsayati.

In the causative voice, the vowel is lengthened: he defiles, he corrupts.

Kamme-dūsīyati iccādi.

In the passive voice: it is corrupted, etc.

Sisa-asabbayoge, sissati, avasissati. Sarīrāni avasissanti.

The root `sis` is in the sense of remaining: it remains, it is left over. 'The bodies are left over.'

Kārite-seseti, sesayati iccādi.

In the causative voice: he causes to remain, he leaves over, etc.

Susa-sussane, sussati. Aṭṭhi ca nhāru ca cammañca avasissatu, upasussatu me sarīre maṃsalohitaṃ ma. ni. 2.184 (thokaṃ visadisaṃ) iccādi.

The root `sus` is in the sense of drying up: it dries up. 'Let bone and sinew and skin remain; let the flesh and blood in my body dry up,' etc.

Daha-dāhe, ha, yānaṃ vipariyāyo, dayhati, dayhanti, ekacitakamhi dayhare.

The root `dah` is in the sense of burning. There is a metathesis of `h` and `y`: it burns, they burn; 'on a single pyre they are burned.'

Kārite-dāheti, dāhayati iccādi.

In the causative voice: he causes to burn (`dāheti`, `dāhayati`), etc.

Naha-bandhane, sannayhati, sannayhanti iccādi.

The root `nah` is in the sense of binding: he binds fast (`sannayhati`), they bind fast (`sannayhanti`), etc.

Muha-muyhane, muyhati, sammuyhati, sammuyhāmi, pamuyhāmi. Sabbā muyhanti me disā jā. 2.22.2185.

The root `muh` is in the sense of delusion: he is deluded (`muyhati`), he is utterly deluded (`sammuyhati`); I am utterly deluded (`sammuyhāmi`), I am deluded (`pamuyhāmi`). 'All directions are confused for me.'

Kārite-moheti, mohayati iccādi.

In the causative voice: he deludes (`moheti`, `mohayati`), etc.

Divādigaṇo niṭṭhito.

The Divādi Group is concluded.

Svādigaṇa

The Svādi Group

Atha svādigaṇo vuccate.

Now, the Svādi Group is explained.

Gi, ci, mi, vu, su, hi, āpa, saka.

gi, ci, mi, vu, su, hi, āpa, saka.

‘Kā’ti vattate.

`kā` is carried forward.

665. Svādito kṇo ka. 448; rū. 512; nī. 929; caṃ. 1.1.95; pā. 3.1.74; ‘svādīhi…’ (bahūsu).

665. After the Svādi roots, `kṇo`.

Svādīhi [M 0.0447] kriyatthehi paraṃ kānubandhā ṇā, ṇo iti dve paccayā honti.

After verbal roots of the Svādi class which signify action, the two suffixes `ṇā` and `ṇo` occur, having `ka` as an indicatory letter.

666. Na te kānubandhanāgamesu.

666. Not when followed by suffixes with a `ka`-anubandha or by augments.

Ivaṇṇu’vaṇṇānaṃ akārassa ca te e, o, ā na honti kānubandhanāgamesu paresūti vuddhipaṭisedho.

For the vowels `i`, `u`, and `a`, the vuddhi vowels `e`, `o`, and `ā` do not occur when followed by suffixes with a `ka`-anubandha or by augments—this is a prohibition of vuddhi.

Suṇāti, suṇoti.

`suṇāti`, `suṇoti` (he hears).

Gi-sadde, giṇāti, giṇoti, anugiṇāti, paṭigiṇāti.

The root `gi` is in the sense of 'sound': he sings (`giṇāti`, `giṇoti`), he recites after (`anugiṇāti`), he takes up a song (`paṭigiṇāti`).

Pubbassaralopo, anugiṇanti, paṭigiṇanti.

With elision of the preceding vowel: `anugiṇanti` (they recite after), `paṭigiṇanti` (they take up a song).

Ci-caye, mahāvuttinā ṇassa nattaṃ, vaḍḍhakī pākāraṃ cināti, cinoti, ācināti, ācinoti, apacināti, apacinoti, viddhaṃsetīti attho.

The root `ci` is in the sense of 'gathering' or 'heaping.' According to the Mahāvutti, `ṇ` becomes `n`. For example: a carpenter builds a wall (`vaḍḍhakī pākāraṃ cināti`, `cinoti`); he accumulates (`ācināti`, `ācinoti`); he removes (`apacināti`, `apacinoti`), the meaning of which is 'he destroys'.

Pubbassaralopo, cinanti, ācinanti, apacinanti.

With the elision of the preceding vowel: 'cinanti,' 'ācinanti,' 'apacinanti.'

Kamme-cīyati, ācīyati, apacīyati, cinīyati, ācinīyati, apacinīyati.

In the passive: 'cīyati,' 'ācīyati,' 'apacīyati,' 'cinīyati,' 'ācinīyati,' 'apacinīyati.'

Kārite-cayāpeti, cayāpayati, cināpeti, cināpayati iccādi.

In the causative: 'cayāpeti,' 'cayāpayati,' 'cināpeti,' 'cināpayati,' etc.

Mi-pakkhepe, miṇāti, miṇoti, mināti, minoti vā.

The root 'mi' in the sense of 'throwing' or 'casting': 'miṇāti,' 'miṇoti,' or 'mināti,' 'minoti.'

Vu-saṃvaraṇe, saṃvuṇāti, saṃvuṇoti, āvuṇāti, āvuṇoti.

The root 'vu' in the sense of 'covering' or 'restraining': 'saṃvuṇāti,' 'saṃvuṇoti,' 'āvuṇāti,' 'āvuṇoti.'

Su-savane, suṇāti, suṇoti, suṇanti, suṇāsi, suṇosi.

The root 'su' in the sense of 'hearing': 'suṇāti,' 'suṇoti,' 'suṇanti,' 'suṇāsi,' 'suṇosi.'

Rassatte-suṇasi [M 0.0448] nāga mahāva. 126. Suṇātha, suṇotha, suṇāmi, suṇomi, suṇāma, suṇoma.

When shortened: 'suṇasi nāga'. Further forms: 'suṇātha,' 'suṇotha,' 'suṇāmi,' 'suṇomi,' 'suṇāma,' 'suṇoma.'

Kamme ‘dīgho sarassā’ti kyamhi dīgho, sūyati, suyyati, sūyanti, suyyanti, suṇīyati, suṇīyanti.

In the passive, by the rule 'dīgho sarassā,' there is lengthening when 'kya' follows: 'sūyati,' 'suyyati,' 'sūyanti,' 'suyyanti,' 'suṇīyati,' 'suṇīyanti.'

Kārite-sāveti, anusāveti, sāvayati, anusāvayati, suṇāpeti, suṇāpayati.

In the causative: 'sāveti,' 'anusāveti,' 'sāvayati,' 'anusāvayati,' 'suṇāpeti,' 'suṇāpayati.'

Kamme-sāvīyati, anusāvīyati.

In the passive of the causative: 'sāvīyati,' 'anusāvīyati.'

Suṇātu, suṇantu, suyyatu, suyyantu, sāvetu, sāventu, suṇe, suṇeyya, suṇeyyuṃ, sūyeyya, suyyeyya, sūyeyyuṃ, suyyeyuṃ, sāveyya, sāveyyuṃ.

'suṇātu,' 'suṇantu,' 'suyyatu,' 'suyyantu,' 'sāvetu,' 'sāventu,' 'suṇe,' 'suṇeyya,' 'suṇeyyuṃ,' 'sūyeyya,' 'suyyeyya,' 'sūyeyyuṃ,' 'suyyeyuṃ,' 'sāveyya,' 'sāveyyuṃ.'

Īādimhi-asuṇi, suṇi.

In the aorist: 'asuṇi,' 'suṇi.'

667. Tesu suto kṇokṇānaṃ roṭa ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

667. After the root 'su', 'roṭa' is substituted for 'kṇo' and 'kṇānaṃ'.

Tesu īādīsu ssakāravantesu ca vacanesu sudhātuto paresaṃ kṇo, kṇānaṃ roṭa hoti, rānubandho sabbādesadīpanattho. ‘Rānubandhentasarādissā’ti suttena ādisarassa lopo, dvittaṃ.

In those verbal forms of the aorist (ī-ādi) and those containing 'ssa', for 'kṇo' and 'kṇānaṃ' following the root 'su', 'roṭa' is substituted. The anubandha 'ra' indicates a total substitution. By the rule 'rānubandhentasarādissā,' the initial vowel is elided, and there is gemination.

Assosi, assosuṃ, assosi, assosittha, assosiṃ, assosimhā, assosumhā, assosittha iccādi.

'assosi,' 'assosuṃ,' 'assosi,' 'assosittha,' 'assosiṃ,' 'assosimhā,' 'assosumhā,' 'assosittha,' etc.

Ssatyādimhi-suṇissati, sossati, suṇissanti, sossanti, suṇissasi, sossasi, suṇissatha, sossatha, suṇissāmi, sossāmi, suṇissāma, sossāma. Evaṃ parachakke.

In the future tense: 'suṇissati,' 'sossati,' 'suṇissanti,' 'sossanti,' 'suṇissasi,' 'sossasi,' 'suṇissatha,' 'sossatha,' 'suṇissāmi,' 'sossāmi,' 'suṇissāma,' 'sossāma.' Thus in the active voice.

Ssādimhi-asuṇissā, asossā, asuṇissaṃsu, sossaṃsu iccādi.

In the conditional: 'asuṇissā,' 'asossā,' 'asuṇissaṃsu,' 'sossaṃsu,' etc.

Papubbo [M 0.0449] hi-pesane, pahiṇāti, pahiṇoti, pahiṇanti.

The root 'hi' with the prefix 'pa' in the sense of 'sending forth': 'pahiṇāti,' 'pahiṇoti,' 'pahiṇanti.'

Īādimhi-dūtaṃ pahiṇi, pahiṇiṃsu, ‘kvaci vikaraṇāna’nti vikaraṇalopo, mahāvuttinā passa dīgho, dūtaṃ pāhesi pārā. 297; mahāva. 198, pāhesuṃ iccādi.

In the aorist: 'dūtaṃ pahiṇi,' 'pahiṇiṃsu.' By the rule 'kvaci vikaraṇāna,' there is elision of the vikaraṇa. According to the Mahāvutti, the 'pa' is lengthened: 'dūtaṃ pāhesi,' 'pāhesuṃ,' etc.

Āpa-pāpuṇane papubbo –

The root 'āpa' with the prefix 'pa' in the sense of 'reaching'—

668. Sakāpānaṃ kukku kṇe ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105; “…kukakū ṇe” (bahūsu).

668. For the roots 'saka' and 'āpa', there are the augments 'ku' and 'u' respectively, when 'kṇa' follows.

Saka, āpadhātūnaṃ kānubandhā kukāra, ukārā kamena āgamā honti kṇamhi paccaye.

For the roots 'saka' and 'āpa,' the letters 'ku' and 'u' with the anubandha 'k' become augments in sequence when the suffix 'kṇa' follows.

Pāpuṇoti, pāpuṇanti, sampāpuṇanti.

'pāpuṇoti,' 'pāpuṇanti,' 'sampāpuṇanti.'

Paripubbo pariyattiyaṃ, pariyāpuṇāti, pariyāpuṇanti.

Preceded by 'pari', in the sense of 'mastering': 'pariyāpuṇāti,' 'pariyāpuṇanti.'

Saṃpubbo-samāpuṇāti, parisamāpuṇāti, niṭṭhānaṃ gacchatīti attho.

Preceded by 'saṃ': 'samāpuṇāti,' 'parisamāpuṇāti,' the meaning of which is 'he goes to completion'.

Kṇeti kiṃ? Pappoti.

Why is 'when kṇa follows' specified? [The form is] 'pappoti'.

Kamme-pāpīyati, pāpīyanti.

In the passive: 'pāpīyati,' 'pāpīyanti.'

Kārite-pāpeti, pāpayati, pāpenti, pāpayanti.

In the causative: 'pāpeti,' 'pāpayati,' 'pāpenti,' 'pāpayanti.'

Kamme-pāpīyati, pāpīyanti.

In the passive of the causative: 'pāpīyati,' 'pāpīyanti.'

Īādimhi-pāpuṇi, pāpuṇiṃsu iccādi.

In the aorist: 'pāpuṇi,' 'pāpuṇiṃsu,' etc.

Saka-sattiyaṃ, sakkuṇoti, sakkuṇāti.

The root 'sak', in the sense of ability: he is able, he can.

Kṇeti kiṃ? Sakkoti, sakkuṇanti.

Why is 'kṇa' specified? He is able, they are able.

Īādimhi-asakkuṇi, sakkuṇi, asakkuṇiṃsu, sakkuṇiṃsu.

In the aorist: he was unable, he was able, they were unable, they were able.

669. Sakā kṇāssa kho īādo ‘…ṇāssa kha…” (bahūsu).

669. After 'sak', 'kṇā' becomes 'kh' when an aorist ending follows.

Sakamhā [M 0.0450] parassa kṇāssa kho hoti īādimhi.

After 'sak', 'kh' occurs in place of the subsequent 'kṇā' when an aorist ending follows.

Asakkhi, sakkhi, asakkhiṃsu, sakkhiṃsu iccādi.

He was unable, he was able, they were unable, they were able, and so on.

670. Sse vā ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

670. Optionally, when 'ssa' follows.

Sakamhā parassa kṇassa kho hoti vā sse pare.

After 'sak', 'kh' optionally occurs in place of the subsequent 'kṇā' when 'ssa' follows.

Sakkhissati, sakkuṇissati, sakkhissanti, sakkuṇissanti, sakkhissasi, sakkhissatha, sakkhissāmi, sakkhissāma, sakkuṇissāma.

He will be able, he will be able; they will be able, they will be able; you (singular) will be able, you (plural) will be able; I will be able, we will be able, we will be able.

‘Dakkha sakkha hehi hohīhi lopo’ti ssassa vikappena lopo, sakkhiti, sakkhissati, sakkhinti, sakkhissanti.

By the rule 'dakkha sakkha hehi hohīhi lopo,' there is optional elision of 'ssa', resulting in: sakkhiti, sakkhissati; sakkhinti, sakkhissanti.

Ssādimhi-asakkhissā, sakkhissā, asakkuṇissā, sakkuṇissā iccādi.

In the conditional: he would not be able, he would be able; he would not be able, he would be able, and so on.

Svādigaṇo niṭṭhito.

The Svādi group is concluded.

Kyādigaṇa

The Kyādi Group

Atha kyādigaṇo vuccate.

Now the Kyādi group is explained.

Kī, ji, ñā, dhū, pu, bhū, mā, mū, lū.

Kī, ji, ñā, dhū, pu, bhū, mā, mū, lū.

671. Kyādīhi kṇā ka. 449; rū. 513; nī. 930; caṃ. 1.1.101 …pe… 3.1.81.

671. After the Kyādi roots, 'kṇā' is the suffix.

Kīiccādīhi kriyatthehi paraṃ kattari kānubandho ṇāpaccayo hoti.

After the roots 'kī' and so on, which have the sense of action, the suffix 'ṇā', with 'k' as an indicatory letter, occurs in the active voice.

672. Kṇāknāsu rasso ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105; caṃ. 6.1.108; pā. 7.3.80.

672. When 'kṇā' and 'knā' follow, the root vowel is shortened.

Etesu [M 0.0451] dīghadhātūnaṃ rasso hoti.

When these follow, the long vowels of the roots are shortened.

Kī-dabbavinimaye, kiṇāti, kiṇanti, vikkiṇāti, vikkiṇanti.

The root 'kī', in the sense of exchange of goods: he buys, they buy; he sells, they sell.

Kamme-kīyati, kiyyati, vikkīyati, vikkiyyati, vikkiyyanti.

In the passive voice: it is bought, it is bought; it is sold, it is sold, they are sold.

Kārite-vikkāyeti, vikkāyayati, kīṇāpeti, kīṇāpayati iccādi.

In the causative: he causes to sell, he causes to sell; he causes to buy, he causes to buy, and so on.

673. Jyādīhi knā ka. 449; rū. 513; nī. 930.

673. After the roots beginning with 'ji', 'knā' is the suffix.

Jiiccādīhi kattari kānubandho nāpaccayo hoti.

After the roots 'ji' and so on, the suffix 'nā', with 'k' as an indicatory letter, occurs in the active voice.

Jināti, jinanti.

He conquers, they conquer.

Kamme-jīyati, jiyyati, jinīyati, jiniyyati.

In the passive voice: it is conquered, it is conquered, it is conquered, it is conquered.

Kārite-jayāpeti, jayāpayati, parājeti, parājayati, parājenti, parājayanti, jināpeti, jināpayati, ajini, jini, ajiniṃsu, jiniṃsu, jinissati, jinissanti iccādi.

In the causative: he causes to conquer, he causes to conquer; he defeats, he defeats; they defeat, they defeat; he causes to conquer, he causes to conquer. Aorist: he conquered, he conquered; they conquered, they conquered. Future: he will conquer, they will conquer, and so on.

Ñā-avabodhane.

The root 'ñā', in the sense of understanding.

674. Ñāssa ne jā ka. 470; rū. 514; nī. 950; caṃ. 6.1.107; pā. 7.3.70, 79.

674. Of 'ñā', there is 'jā' when 'nā' follows.

Nāpaccaye pare ñāssa jā hoti.

When the suffix 'nā' follows, 'ñā' becomes 'jā'.

Jānāti, pajānāti, ājānāti, sañjānāti, vijānāti, abhijānāti, parijānāti, paṭijānāti, jānanti.

He knows, he understands, he knows well, he cognizes, he discerns, he directly knows, he fully understands, he acknowledges, they know.

Kamme-ñāyati, paññāyati, aññāyati, saññāyati, viññāyati, abhiññāyati, pariññāyati, paṭiññāyati, ñāyanti.

In the passive: is known, is discerned, is understood, is perceived, is cognized, is directly known, is fully known, is acknowledged, they are known.

Kārite-ñāpeti[M 0.0452], ñāpayati, ñāpenti, ñāpayanti, jānāpeti, jānāpayati, jānāpenti, jānāpayanti.

In the causative: he causes to know, he causes to know, they cause to know, they cause to know, he causes to know, he causes to know, they cause to know, they cause to know.

Kamme-ñāpīyati, saññāpīyati, jānāpīyati.

In the passive: is made known, is signified, is made known.

675. Ñāssa sanāssa nāyo timhi ka. 509; rū. 516; nī. 1022.

675. For `ñā` with `nā`, `nā` is the substitute in the third person.

Nāsahitassa ñāssa nāyo hoti timhi, suttavibhattiyā anti, antesu ca.

For `ñā` accompanied by `nā`, `nā` is the substitute in the third person singular, and by the rule of the sutta, also in `anti` and `ante`.
