Nāyati. Viceyya viceyya atthe panāyatīti kho bhikkhave vipassīti vuccati dī. ni. 2.41-44. Nāyanti. “Animittā na nāyare”ti visuddhi 1.174 pāḷi.

He knows. 'Having discerned, having discerned the meanings, he understands'—thus, O monks, he is called 'Vipassī.' They know. 'The signless are not known' is the Pāli text.

Eyyādimhi-jāneyya, jāneyyuṃ, jāneyyāsi, jāneyyātha, jāneyyāmi, jāneyyāma.

In the optative: he would know, they would know, you would know, you all would know, I would know, we would know.

Utte-jāneyyāmu.

In the first person: we would know.

Eyyāmassa emutte “kathaṃ jānemu taṃ maya”nti jā. 2.22.7 pāḷi.

For the ending `eyyāma`, `emu` is the substitute in the first person: 'How should we know him?' is the Pāli text.

676. Eyyassiyāñā vā ka. 508; rū. 515; nī. 1021.

676. For `eyya`, `iyā` and `ñā` are optional substitutes.

Ñāto eyyassa iyā, ñā honti, vāsaddena eyyumādīnampi ñū, ñāsi, ñātha, ñāmi, ñāmādesā honti, eyyamiccassa ñañca.

It is known that `iyā` and `ñā` are substitutes for `eyya`. And optionally, `ñū, ñāsi, ñātha, ñāmi, ñāmā` are also substitutions for `eyyuṃ` and so on, and `ña` for `eyyāmi`.

Jāniyā.

He would know.

677. Ñāmhi jaṃ ka. 470; rū. 514; nī. 950.

677. When `ñā` follows, `jaṃ` is the substitute.

Ñādese pare sanāssa ñāssa jaṃ hoti.

When the substitute `ñā` follows, `jaṃ` occurs for the `nā` affix and the `ñā` root.

Jaññā, vijaññā.

He would know, he would understand.

Suttavibhattena [M 0.0453] ñūādīsupi jaṃ hoti. “Pāpaṃ katvā mā maṃ jaññūti icchati su. ni. 127; vibha. 894 ‘jaññā’ti, vivekadhammaṃ ahaṃ vijaññaṃ gavesitabbaṃ, jaññāmu ce sīlavantaṃ vadaññu”nti jā. 2.22.1301 pāḷī. ‘Jaññāsi, jaññātha, jaññāmi, jaññāmā’tipi yujjati.

By the rule of the sutta, `jaṃ` also occurs before `ñū` and so on. 'Having done evil, he wishes, "May they not know me." I would understand the quality of seclusion. If we should know the virtuous and generous one'—this is the Pāli text. 'You would know, you all would know, I would know, we would know'—these are also suitable.

678. Īssatyādīsu knālopo ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

678. In the aorist and future tenses, the `knā` affix is elided.

Knāssa lopo hoti vā īādimhi ssatyādimhi ca.

The elision of the `knā` affix occurs optionally when followed by the aorist marker `ī` and so on, and also when followed by the future marker `ssati` and so on.

Aññāsi, abbhaññāsi, ajāni, aññāsuṃ, aññaṃsu, abbhaññaṃsu, jāniṃsu, aññāsi, abbhaññāsi, ajāni, aññittha, jānittha, aññāsiṃ, abbhaññāsiṃ, ajāniṃ, jāniṃ, aññāsimhā, ajānimhā, jānimhā, ñāssati, jānissati, ñāssanti, jānissanti.

He knew, he directly knew, he knew; they knew, they knew, they directly knew, they knew; you (sg.) knew, you (sg.) directly knew, you (sg.) knew; you (pl.) knew, you (pl.) knew; I knew, I directly knew, I knew, I knew; we knew, we knew, we knew; he will know, he will know; they will know, they will know.

Kamme-viññāyissati, viññāyissanti.

In the passive: it will be cognized, they will be cognized.

679. Ssassa hi kamme ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

679. `Hi` is the substitute for `ssa` in the passive.

Ñāto ssassa hi hoti vā kamme.

It is known that `hi` is an optional substitute for `ssa` in the passive.

Paññāyihi. “Paññāyihinti etā, daharā”ti jā. 2.17.197 pāḷi. Paññāyissati, paññāyissanti iccādi.

It will be discerned. 'These young ones will be discerned' is the Pāli text. It will be discerned, they will be discerned, and so on.

Dhū-vidhunane, knāmhi rasso, dhunāti, dhunanti.

The root `dhū` in the sense of shaking. With the `knā` affix, the vowel is shortened: he shakes, they shake.

Kamme-dhunīyati, dhunīyanti.

In the passive: is shaken, they are shaken.

Kārite-dhunāpeti, dhunāpayati.

In the causative: he causes to shake, he causes to shake.

Pu-sodhane, punāti, punanti.

The root `pu` in the sense of purifying: he purifies, they purify.

Bhū-pattiyaṃ, rasso, abhisambhunāti, abhisambhunanti. Nāssa ṇatte-abhisambhuṇāti, abhisambhuṇanti.

The root `bhū` in the sense of attainment. The vowel is shortened: he fully attains, they fully attain. For the `nā` affix, with retroflexion: he fully attains, they fully attain.

Mā-parimāṇe[M 0.0454], mahāvuttinā dhātvantassa ittaṃ, mināti, nimmināti.

The root `mā` in the sense of measuring. By the great rule, `i` is substituted for the end of the root: he measures, he constructs.

Kamme-upamīyati, upamīyanti, nimmīyati, nimmīyanti.

In the passive voice: it is likened, they are likened; it is created, they are created.

Kārite-nagaraṃ māpeti, māpayati, māpīyati, māpīyanti, nimmini, nimminiṃsu, māpesi, māpayi, māpesuṃ, māpayuṃ, nimminissati, nimminissanti, māpessati, māpessanti iccādi.

In the causative voice: one causes a city to be built; it is caused to be built, they are caused to be built; one created, they created; one caused to build, one caused to build, they caused to build, they caused to build; one will create, they will create; one will cause to build, they will cause to build, and so on.

Mū-bandhane, munāti.

The root `mū` in the sense of binding: he binds.

Lū-chedane, rassattaṃ, lunāti, lunanti.

The root `lū` in the sense of cutting; the vowel is shortened: he cuts, they cut.

Kamme-lūyati, lūyanti.

In the passive voice: it is reaped, they are reaped.

Kārite-lāvayati, lāvayanti.

In the causative voice: he causes to reap, they cause to reap.

Kamme-lāvīyati iccādi.

In the passive voice: it is caused to be reaped, and so on.

Kyādigaṇo niṭṭhito.

The Kyādi group is concluded.

Tanādigaṇa

The Tanādi Group

Atha tanādigaṇo vuccate.

Now the Tanādi group is explained.

Āpa, kara, tana, saka.

Āpa, kara, tana, saka.

680. Tanāditvo ka. 451; rū. 520; nī. 932; caṃ. 1.1.97; pā. 3.1.79.

680. From the Tanādi group, o.

Tanādīhi paraṃ opaccayo hoti.

After the roots of the Tanādi group, the affix `o` occurs.

Tanoti.

He spreads.

Āpa-pāpuṇane papubbo. Dhātvantassa dvittaṃ rasso ca, pappoti, papponti.

The root `āp` in the sense of attaining, with the prefix `pa`. The final consonant of the root is doubled and the vowel is shortened: `pappoti`, `papponti`.

Kamme-pāpīyati, pāpīyanti.

In the passive voice: it is attained, they are attained.

Kārite-pāpeti, pāpayati.

In the causative voice: he causes to attain, he causes to attain.

Kamme-pāpīyati [M 0.0455] pāpīyanti iccādi.

In the passive voice: it is caused to be attained, they are caused to be attained, and so on.

Kara-karaṇe, karoti, karonti.

The root `kara` in the sense of doing: he does, they do.

Kamme-karīyati, karīyanti.

In the passive voice: it is done, they are done.

‘Tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā’ti yamhi dhātvantassa yattaṃ, kayyati, kayyanti, kayyare, kayyate, kayyante.

By the rule ‘Tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā,’ the final consonant of the root becomes `y`: `kayyati`, `kayyanti`, `kayyare`, `kayyate`, `kayyante`.

Kārite-kāreti, kārayati, kārenti, kārayanti, kārāpeti, kārāpayati, kārāpenti, kārāpayanti.

In the causative voice: he causes to make, he causes to make; they cause to make, they cause to make; he causes to have made, he causes to have made; they cause to have made, they cause to have made.

681. Karassa sossa kuṃ ka. 511; rū. 521; nī. 1124.

681. Of `kara`, `o` becomes `kuṃ`.

O-kārasahitassa karassa kuṃ hoti mi, mesu paresu.

For the root `kara` accompanied by the vowel `o`, it becomes `kuṃ` when `mi` and `ma` follow.

Kummi, kumma, “bhattu apacitiṃ kummi jā. 1.3.126, dhammassāpacitiṃ kummī”ti jā. 2.22.1752 pāḷī.

`Kummi`, `kumma`. The Pāli text is: ‘I pay respect to my husband; I pay respect to the Dhamma.’

682. Karotissa kho ka. 594; rū. 582; nī. 1198.

682. For `karoti`, `kho` is substituted.

Pādito parassa karadhātussa kvaci kho hoti.

Sometimes, for the root `kara` that follows a prefix, there is the substitution `kho`.

Saṅkharoti, saṅkharonti, abhisaṅkharoti, abhisaṅkharonti.

He conditions, they condition; he intentionally conditions, they intentionally condition.

Kamme-saṅkharīyati, saṅkharīyanti.

In the passive voice: it is conditioned, they are conditioned.

Kārite-saṅkhāreti, saṅkhārayati.

In the causative voice: he causes to condition, he causes to condition.

Ṇāpimhi na vuddhi, saṅkharāpeti, saṅkharāpayati.

With the suffix ṇāpi, there is no strengthening: he causes to prepare, he causes to prepare.

Kamme-saṅkhārīyati, saṅkharāpīyati.

In the passive: it is prepared, it is caused to be prepared.

683. Karassa sossa kubbakurukayirā ka. 511-2; rū. 521-2; nī. 1077-8-9-10; caṃ. 5.2.103; pā. 6.4.110.

683. Of the root kar with o, there are the substitutes kubba, kuru, and kayirā.

O-kārasahitassa karassa kubba, kuru, kayirā honti vā nta, māna, tyādīsu, mahāvuttinā vikappena kussa kruttaṃ.

For the root kar with the vowel o, the substitutes kubba, kuru, and kayirā occur optionally before endings such as nta, māna, ti, and so on. According to the Mahāvutti, ku optionally becomes kru.

Kubbati [M 0.0456] kubbanti, krubbati, krubbanti.

kubbati (he does), kubbanti (they do); krubbati (he does), krubbanti (they do).

Parachakke-kubbate, krubbate, kubbante, krubbante, kurute, kayirati, kayiranti, kayirasi, kayiratha, kayirāmi, kayirāma, kayirate, kayirante.

In the middle voice: kubbate (he does), krubbate (he does), kubbante (they do), krubbante (they do), kurute (he does); kayirati (it is done), kayiranti (they are done); kayirasi (you do), kayiratha (you do), kayirāmi (I do), kayirāma (we do); kayirate (it is done), kayirante (they are done).

Karotu, saṅkharotu, kubbatu, krubbatu, kurutu, agghaṃ kurutu no bhavaṃ dī. ni. 2.318, kayiratu.

karotu (let him do), saṅkharotu (let him prepare), kubbatu (let him do), krubbatu (let him do), kurutu (let him do); for example, ‘agghaṃ kurutu no bhavaṃ’ (may the venerable one set a price for us); kayiratu (let it be done).

Kareyya, saṅkhareyya, kubbeyya, krubbeyya, kayireyya.

kareyya (he should do), saṅkhareyya (he should prepare), kubbeyya (he should do), krubbeyya (he should do), kayireyya (it should be done).

684. Ṭā ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

684. The anubandha ṭā.

Kayirādesato parassa eyyavibhattissa ṭānubandho ā hoti vā.

Following the substitute kayirā, the ending eyya, which has the anubandha ṭ, optionally becomes ā.

So puññaṃ kayirā, puññaṃ ce puriso kayirā dha. pa. 118, kayirā naṃ punappunaṃ dha. pa. 118.

He should perform merit. If a person should perform merit, he should do it again and again.

685. Kayireyyasseyyumādīnaṃ ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1083-4-5-6-7.

685. Of kayireyya, eyyuṃ, and so on.

Kayirādesato parassa eyyuṃādīnaṃ eyyasaddassa lopo hoti.

Following the substitute kayirā, the eyya part of the endings eyyuṃ, and so on, is elided.

Kayiruṃ, kayireyyuṃ, kayirāsi, kayireyyāsi, kayirātha, kayireyyātha, kayirāmi, kayireyyāmi, kayirāma, kayireyyāma.

Kayiruṃ (they should do), kayireyyuṃ (they should do); kayirāsi (you should do), kayireyyāsi (you should do); kayirātha (you all should do), kayireyyātha (you all should do); kayirāmi (I should do), kayireyyāmi (I should do); kayirāma (we should do), kayireyyāma (we should do).

686. Ethassā ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1082.

686. Of `etha`, `ā`.

Kayirādesato parassa ethassa e-kārassa ā hoti vā.

After the substitute `kayirā`, the letter `e` of the ending `etha` optionally becomes `ā`.

So [M 0.0457] kayirātha, dīpaṃ kayirātha paṇḍito dha. pa. 28, kayirā ce kayirāthenaṃ dha. pa. 313; saṃ. ni. 1.89.

`So kayirātha` (he should do); `dīpaṃ kayirātha paṇḍito` (a wise person should make a refuge); `kayirā ce kayirāthenaṃ` (if one should do it, one should do it).

Īādimhi-akari, kari, saṅkhari, abhisaṅkhari, akubbi, kubbi, akrubbi, krubbi, akayiri, kayiri, akaruṃ, karuṃ, saṅkharuṃ, abhi, saṅkharuṃ, akariṃsu, kariṃsu, saṅkhariṃsu, abhisaṅkhariṃsu, akubbiṃsu, kubbiṃsu, akrubbiṃsu, krubbiṃsu, akayiriṃsu, kayiriṃsu, akayiruṃ, kayiruṃ.

In the aorist tense: `akari` (he did), `kari` (he did); `saṅkhari` (he prepared), `abhisaṅkhari` (he fully prepared); `akubbi` (he did), `kubbi` (he did), `akrubbi` (he did), `krubbi` (he did); `akayiri` (it was done), `kayiri` (it was done). Plural forms: `akaruṃ` (they did), `karuṃ` (they did); `saṅkharuṃ` (they prepared), `abhisaṅkharuṃ` (they fully prepared); `akariṃsu` (they did), `kariṃsu` (they did); `saṅkhariṃsu` (they prepared), `abhisaṅkhariṃsu` (they fully prepared); `akubbiṃsu` (they did), `kubbiṃsu` (they did), `akrubbiṃsu` (they did), `krubbiṃsu` (they did); `akayiriṃsu` (they were done), `kayiriṃsu` (they were done); `akayiruṃ` (they were done), `kayiruṃ` (they were done).

687. Kā īādīsu ka. 491; rū. 523; nī. 983.

687. The substitution `kā` in the aorist.

Īādīsu saokārassa karassa kā hoti vā.

In the aorist, the root `kar` with its vowel optionally becomes `kā`.

688. Dīghā īssa ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

688. Of `ī`, lengthening.

Ā, e, ūdīghehi parassa īvacanassa si hoti vā.

After the long vowels `ā`, `e`, and `ū`, the ending `ī` optionally becomes `si`.

Aṭṭhāsi, adāsi, vadesi, vajjesi, bhāvesi, kāresianubhosi, ahosi iccādi.

`Aṭṭhāsi` (he stood), `adāsi` (he gave), `vadesi` (he spoke), `vajjesi` (he avoided), `bhāvesi` (he developed), `kāresi` (he caused to be done), `anubhosi` (he experienced), `ahosi` (he was), and so forth.

So akāsi, te akaṃsu, gāthāyaṃ “akaṃsu satthuvacana”nti jā. 2.22.564 pāḷi. Akāsuṃ, tvaṃ akāsi. Mā tumhe evarūpaṃ akattha gavesitabbaṃ, mākattha pāpakaṃ kammaṃ, āvī vā yadi vā raho udā. 44. Akāsittha, ahaṃ akāsiṃ, mayaṃ akāsimhā, akamhā. Bhogesu vijjamānesu, dīpaṃ nākamha attano jā. 1.4.53. So akā. “Tato ekasataṃ khatye, anuyante bhavaṃ akā”ti jā. 2.20.94 pāḷi. Akāsittha vā, ahaṃ akaṃ, akaraṃ vā. “Tassāhaṃ vacanaṃ nākaṃ, pitu vuddhassa bhāsita”nti jā. 2.17.134 pāḷi.

`So akāsi` (he did), `te akaṃsu` (they did). In a verse, the Pāli is: “They followed the Teacher’s word.” `Akāsuṃ` (they did), `tvaṃ akāsi` (you did). `Mā tumhe evarūpaṃ akattha` (Do not you all do such a thing). `Mākattha pāpakaṃ kammaṃ, āvī vā yadi vā raho` (Do not do an evil deed, whether openly or in secret). `Akāsittha` (you all did), `ahaṃ akāsiṃ` (I did), `mayaṃ akāsimhā` (we did), `akamhā` (we did). `Bhogesu vijjamānesu, dīpaṃ nākamha attano` (Though wealth was present, we did not make a refuge for ourselves). `So akā` (he did). The Pāli is: “Then the Lord made one hundred khattiyas follow him.” `Akāsittha vā` (or you all did), `ahaṃ akaṃ` (I did), `akaraṃ vā` (or I did). The Pāli is: “I did not follow his word, the speech of my aged father.”

Kārite-so kāresi, kārayi, kārāpesi, kārāpayi, te kāresuṃ, kārayuṃ, kārāpesuṃ, kārāpayuṃ iccādi.

In the causative: `so kāresi, kārayi, kārāpesi, kārāpayi` (he caused to do); `te kāresuṃ, kārayuṃ, kārāpesuṃ, kārāpayuṃ` (they caused to do), and so forth.

Karissati [M 0.0458] saṅkharissati, kubbissati, krubbissati, kayirissati iccādi.

`Karissati` (he will do), `saṅkharissati` (he will prepare), `kubbissati` (he will do), `krubbissati` (he will do), `kayirissati` (it will be done), and so forth.

“Harassa cāhaṅa sse’ti ssena saha karassa rakārassa āhaṅa hoti, kāhati, kāhanti, kathaṃ kāhanti dārakā jā. 2.22.1849.

According to the rule ‘Harassa cāhaṅa sse,’ before `ssa`, the `ra` of `kara` becomes `āhaṅa`. For example: `kāhati` (he will do), `kāhanti` (they will do), as in `kathaṃ kāhanti dārakā` (how will the children fare?).

Iñāgame-kāhiti, kāhinti iccādi. Kāhasi, kāhatha. Kāhāmi kusalaṃ bahuṃ jā. 1.4.56, kāhāma puññasañcayaṃ apa. thera 1.1.401.

With the `i` augment: `kāhiti` (he will do), `kāhinti` (they will do), and so forth. `Kāhasi` (you will do), `kāhatha` (you all will do). `Kāhāmi kusalaṃ bahuṃ` (I will do much that is wholesome). `Kāhāma puññasañcayaṃ` (We will accumulate merit).

‘Āīādīsū’ti sutte yogavibhāgena ssatyādīsupi kā hoti, saṃyoge rassattaṃ, kassati, kassanti, kassasi, kassatha, kassāmi, kassāma, kassaṃ purisakāriyaṃ jā. 2.22.131.

By splitting the rule beginning ‘Āīādīsu,’ the substitution `kā` also occurs in the future tense (forms beginning with `ssa`). Before a consonant cluster, the vowel is shortened. For example: `kassati` (he will do), `kassanti` (they will do), `kassasi` (you will do), `kassatha` (you all will do), `kassāmi` (I will do), `kassāma` (we will do), as in `kassaṃ purisakāriyaṃ` (I will perform a man's duty).

Ssādimhi-akāhā, akarissā iccādi.

In the conditional tense: `akāhā` (he would have done), `akarissā` (he would have done), and so forth.

Tanu-vitthāre, tanoti.

The root tanu (is used) in the sense of extending: he extends.

Parassaralopo-tanonti.

Elision of the following vowel: tanonti (they extend).

689. Ovikaraṇassu parachakke ka. 511; rū. 521; nī. 1024.

689. The o-increment becomes u in the parachakka.

Parachakke pare ovikaraṇassa u hoti.

When the parachakka group follows, the o-increment becomes u.

Tanute, tanunte.

He spreads, they spread.

‘Yavā sare’ti ussa vatte-tanvante.

By the rule 'yavā sare,' the 'u' becomes 'v': tanvante (they extend).

690. Pubbachakke vā kvaci ka. 511; rū. 521; nī. 1024.

690. In the attanopada group, optionally in some cases.

Pubbachakke ovikaraṇassa kvaci u hoti vā.

In the attanopada group, the o-increment optionally becomes u in some cases.

Tanuti, kurutu.

He spreads, let him make.

Kvacīti kiṃ? Karoti.

Why the word 'sometimes'? [To form] karoti.

Vāti [M 0.0459] kiṃ? Tanoti.

Why the word 'optionally'? [To form] tanoti.

Kamme-tanīyati, taññati.

In the passive voice: it is extended, it is extended.

691. Tanassā vā ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

691. Of tanu, optionally ā.

Tanadhātussa na-kārassa ā hoti vā kyamhi.

Of the root tanu, the letter 'n' optionally becomes 'ā' when the passive suffix 'ya' follows.

Tāyati, tāyanti, patāyati, patāyanti. “Ito’dāni patāyanti, sūciyo balisāni cā”ti jā. 1.6.84 pāḷi. Tāyate, tāyante.

He is stretched, they are stretched; he is extended, they are extended. "From here now they extend, needles and hooks," this is a Pāli quotation. It is stretched, they are stretched.

Saka-sattiyaṃ, sakkoti, sakkonti, sakkosi, sakkotha, sakkomi, sakkoma.

The root sak (is used) in the sense of one's own power: he can, they can, you can, you (all) can, I can, we can.

Tanādigaṇo niṭṭhito.

The Tanādi group is concluded.

Curādigaṇa

The Curādi Group

Atha curādigaṇo vuccate.

Now the Curādi group is explained.

Āpa, kamu, gaṇa, ghaṭa, cinta, ceta, cura, dhara, pāla, pūja, manta, māna, vida.

Āp, kamu, gaṇa, ghaṭa, cinta, ceta, cura, dhara, pāla, pūja, manta, māna, vida.

692. Curādīhiṇi ka. 452; rū. 525; nī. 933; caṃ. 1.1.45; pā. 3.1.25; ‘curādito ṇi’ (bahūsu).

692. After the Curādi roots, ṇi.

Curādīhi kriyatthehi paraṃ sakatthe ṇipaccayo hoti.

After the Curādi roots, which have the meaning of action, the suffix ṇi occurs in its own sense.

Coreti, corayati.

He steals, he steals.

Vipubbo āpa-byāpane, byāpeti, byāpayati.

The root āp preceded by vi (is used) in the sense of pervading: he pervades, he pervades.

Kamu-icchāyaṃ, kāmeti, kāmayati, kāmenti, kāmayanti, nikāmeti, nikāmayati, nikāmenti, nikāmayanti.

The root kamu (is used) in the sense of desiring: he desires, he desires; they desire, they desire; he desires, he desires; they desire, they desire.

Kamme-kāmīyati, kāmīyanti.

In the passive voice: it is desired, they are desired.

Kārite ṇāpi eva, kāmāpeti, kāmāpayati.

In the causative, with the ṇāpe suffix, it is likewise: he causes to desire, he causes to desire.

Kamme-kāmāpīyati[M 0.0460], kāmāpayīyati.

In the passive voice: it is caused to be desired, it is caused to be desired.

Gaṇa-saṅkhyāne, gaṇa, ghaṭānaṃ tudādittā na vuddhi, gaṇeti, gaṇayati.

The root gaṇa (is used) in the sense of counting. For gaṇa and ghaṭ, because they belong to the Tudādi group, there is no vuddhi strengthening: he counts, he counts.

Ghaṭa-cetāyaṃ, ghaṭeti, ghaṭayati.

The root ghaṭa (is used) in the sense of striving: he strives, he strives.

Cinta-cintāyaṃ, garupantattā na vuddhi, cinteti, cintayati.

The root cint is in the sense of thinking. Due to its final syllable being heavy, there is no vowel lengthening: he thinks, he thinks.

Kamme-cintīyati, cintīyanti.

In the passive: it is contemplated; they are contemplated.

Kārite-cintāpeti, cintāpayati.

In the causative: he causes to think, he causes to think.

Kamme-cintāpīyati, cintāpayīyati.

In the passive causative: it is caused to be thought, it is caused to be thought.

Īādimhi-cintesi, cintayi, cinteyuṃ, cintayuṃ, cintesi, cintayi, cintayittha, cintesiṃ, cintayiṃ, cintesimhā, cintayimhā.

In the aorist: he thought, he thought; they thought, they thought; you (singular) thought; you (plural) thought; I thought, I thought; we thought, we thought.

Ceta-cetāyaṃ, ceteti, cetayati, cetenti, cetayanti.

The root cet is in the sense of intending: he intends, he intends; they intend, they intend.

Cura-theyye, coreti, corayati, corenti, corayanti.

The root cur is in the sense of stealing: he steals, he steals; they steal, they steal.

Dhara-dhāraṇe, dhāreti, dhārayati, dhārenti, dhārayanti.

The root dhar is in the sense of bearing: he bears, he bears; they bear, they bear.

Pāla-pālane, pāleti, pālayati, pālenti, pālayanti.

The root pāl is in the sense of protecting: he protects, he protects; they protect, they protect.

Pūja-pūjāyaṃ, garupantattā na vuddhi, pūjeti, pūjayati, pūjenti, pūjayanti.

The root pūj is in the sense of worship. Due to its final syllable being heavy, there is no vowel lengthening: he worships, he worships; they worship, they worship.

Manta-guttabhāsane, manteti, mantayati, mantenti, mantayanti.

The root mant is in the sense of secret speech: he consults, he consults; they consult, they consult.

Āpubbo kathane āmantane ca. Āmantayāmi vo bhikkhave dī. ni. 2.218, bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi dī. ni. 2.208.

With the prefix ā-, it is in the sense of speaking and addressing. 'I address you, monks.' The Blessed One addressed the monks.

Nipubbo-nimantane, nimanteti, nimantayati.

With the prefix ni-, it is in the sense of inviting: he invites, he invites.

Īādimhi-mantesi[M 0.0461], mantayi, āmantesi, āmantayi, nimantesi, nimantayi, mantesuṃ, mantayuṃ, mantayiṃsu rahogatā jā. 2.22.1918, mantessati, āmantessati, nimantessati, mantayissati, āmantayissati, nimantayissati iccādi.

In the aorist and future tenses: he consulted, he consulted; he addressed, he addressed; he invited, he invited; they consulted, they consulted, 'they consulted in private'; he will consult, he will address, he will invite; he will consult, he will address, he will invite, and so on.

Māna-pūjāyaṃ, māneti, mānayati, mānenti, mānayanti iccādi.

The root mān is in the sense of honoring: he honors, he honors; they honor, they honor, and so on.

Vida-anubhavane, vedeti, vedayati, paṭisaṃvedeti, paṭisaṃvedayati.

The root vid is in the sense of experiencing: he experiences, he experiences; he directly experiences, he directly experiences.

Paṭi, ni, papubbo ācikkhane, paṭivedeti, paṭivedayati, nivedeti, nivedayati, pavedeti, pavedayati iccādi.

With the prefixes paṭi-, ni-, and pa-, it is in the sense of declaring: he reports, he reports; he announces, he announces; he proclaims, he proclaims, and so on.

Curādigaṇo niṭṭhito.

The Curādi group is concluded.

Vikaraṇapaccayarāsi niṭṭhito.

The collection of conjugational sign suffixes is concluded.

Sāmañña kha, cha, sarāsi

General Section on kha, cha, and sa Suffixes

Atha dhātupaccayā vuccante.

Now the root-suffixes are explained.

Kriyāvācībhāvena dhāturūpā paccayā dhātupaccayā, kriyatthapaccayāti vuttaṃ hoti, tasmā tehipi sabbesaṃ tyādi, tabbādivibhatti, paccayānaṃ sambhavo.

Suffixes that have the form of a root are called root-suffixes because they express an action; it is said that they are suffixes that convey the meaning of an action. Therefore, from them also, the application of all suffixes, such as the verbal endings beginning with ti and the gerundive endings beginning with tabba, is possible.

Tija, māna, kita, gupa, badha.

Tij, mān, kit, gup, badh.

693. Tijamānehi khasā khamāvīmaṃsāsu ka. 433; rū. 528; nī. 906-9; caṃ. 1.1.17, 28; pā. 3.1.5.

693. From the roots tij and mān, the suffixes kha and sa occur in the senses of patience and investigation, respectively.

Khamāyaṃ vīmaṃsāyañca pavattehi tija, mānadhātūhi paraṃ kamena kha, sapaccayā honti.

After the roots tij and mān, when they are used in the sense of patience and investigation, the suffixes kha and sa occur respectively.

Tija-khamāyaṃ, iminā khapaccayo.

From the root tij in the sense of patience, by this rule the kha suffix is applied.

694. Khachasānamekassaraṃ dve ka. 458; rū. 461; nī. 939; caṃ. 5.1.1; pā. 6.1.1, 9; ‘…mekasarodi…’ (bahūsu).

694. Of a monosyllabic root before the suffixes kha, cha, and sa, it becomes two; that is, the root is reduplicated.

Kha[M 0.0462], cha, sapaccayantānaṃ dhāturūpānaṃ paṭhamaṃ saddarūpaṃ ekassaraṃ dverūpaṃ hotīti ‘tija, tija’iti dvirūpe kate ‘loponādibyañjanassā’ti anādibyañjanabhūtassa ja-kārassa lopo, ‘pararūpamayakāre byañjane’ti dhātvantajakārassa pararūpattaṃ. ‘Catutthadutiyesvesaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā’ti saṃyogādissa khassa kattaṃ, ‘titikkha’iti dhātupaccayantarūpaṃ, tato tyādyuppatti.

For root-forms ending in the suffixes kha, cha, and sa, the first, monosyllabic sound-form is reduplicated. Thus, when the reduplication 'tija, tija' is made, by the rule loponādibyañjanassa, there is elision of the non-initial consonant 'j'. By the rule pararūpamayakāre byañjane, the final 'j' of the root takes the form of the following consonant. By the rule Catutthadutiyesvesaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā, the 'kh' at the beginning of a conjunct becomes 'k'. Thus, 'titikkha' is the form ending in a root-suffix, and from that arise the verbal endings beginning with ti.

Titikkhati, titikkhanti.

He endures; they endure.

Kamme-titikkhīyati.

In the passive: it is endured.

Kārite-titikkheti, titikkhayati, titikkhāpeti, titikkhāpayati.

In the causative: he causes to endure, he causes to endure, he causes to cause to endure, he causes to cause to endure.

Kamme-titikkhāpīyati, titikkhāpīyanti.

In the passive of the causative: it is caused to be endured, they are caused to be endured.

Titikkhatu, titikkhantu, titikkheyya, titikkheyyuṃ iccādi.

Let him endure, let them endure, he should endure, they should endure, and so on.

Khamāyanti kiṃ? Tija-nisāne, tejeti, tejenti.

Why is 'in the sense of patience' specified? From the root `Tija`, in the sense of sharpening: he sharpens, they sharpen.

Kārite-tejeti. “Samuttejeti sampahaṃsetī”ti ma. ni. 3.276 pāḷi.

In the causative: he causes to sharpen. The Pāli text states: 'He arouses and gladdens.'

Māna-vīmaṃsāyaṃ, tato sapaccayo. ‘Khachasānamekassaraṃ dve’ti ‘māna, māna’iti dvirūpe kate –

From the root `Māna`, in the sense of investigation; from that, the `sa` suffix. By the rule '`Khachasānamekassaraṃ dve`', when the reduplicated form '`māna, māna`' is made—

695. Mānassa vī parassa ca maṃ ka. 463-7; rū. 532-3; nī. 944.

695. For `māna`, the preceding part becomes `vī`, and the following part becomes `maṃ`.

Dvitte pubbassa mānassa vī hoti, parassa ca sabbassa mānassa maṃ hoti.

In the reduplicated form, the preceding `māna` becomes `vī`, and the entire following `māna` becomes `maṃ`.

Vīmaṃsati, vīmaṃsanti.

He investigates, they investigate.

Kamme-vīmaṃsīyati[M 0.0463], vīmaṃsīyanti.

In the passive: it is investigated, they are investigated.

Kārite-vīmaṃseti, vīmaṃsayati, vīmaṃsāpeti, vīmaṃsāpayati.

In the causative: he causes to investigate, he causes to investigate, he causes to cause to investigate, he causes to cause to investigate.

Kamme-vīmaṃsāpīyati, vīmaṃsāpīyanti.

In the passive of the causative: it is caused to be investigated, they are caused to be investigated.

Vīmaṃsāyanti kiṃ? Māna-pūjāyaṃ, māneti, sammāneti, abhimāneti, pūjetīti attho.

Why is 'in the sense of investigation' specified? From the root `Māna` in the sense of honoring: he honors, he respects, he esteems; the meaning is 'he honors'.

Kita-rogāpanayane saṃsaye ca.

The root `kit` is used in the sense of removing disease and in doubt.

696. Kitā tikicchāsaṃsayesu cho ka. 433; rū. 528; nī. 906-9; caṃ. 1.1.18; pā. 3.1.5 kā.

696. After `kit`, in the senses of treatment and doubt, the suffix is `cha`.

Tikicchāyaṃ saṃsaye ca pavattakitadhātuto paraṃ cho hoti.

After the root `kit`, when it occurs in the sense of treatment and doubt, the suffix `cha` is applied.

‘Kita, kita’ iti dvirūpe kate –

When '`kita, kita`' is reduplicated—

697. Kitassāsaṃsayeti vā ka. 463; rū. 532; nī. 944.

697. For `kit` in the sense of non-doubt, `ti` (is substituted) optionally.

Saṃsayamhā aññasmiṃ tikicchatthe pavattassa kitadhātussa dvitte pubbassa kitassati hoti vā. ‘Pararūpamayakāre byañjane’ti pararūpattaṃ, saṃyogādissa cakārattaṃ.

For the root `kit`, when it occurs in the sense of treatment, which is other than doubt, the preceding `kit` of the reduplicated form optionally becomes `ti`. By the rule '`Pararūpamayakāre byañjane`', there is assimilation to the following form, and the initial of the conjunct consonant becomes `ca`.

Tikicchati, tikicchanti. Devāpi naṃ tikicchanti, mātāpettibharaṃ naraṃ jā. 2.22.408.

He treats, they treat. Even the gods treat him, the man who supports his mother and father.

Kamme-tikicchīyati, tikicchīyanti.

In the passive: it is treated, they are treated.

Kārite-tikiccheti, tikicchayati, tikicchāpeti, tikicchāpayati.

In the causative: he causes to treat, he causes to treat, he causes to cause to treat, he causes to cause to treat.

Vāsaddena tikārābhāve ‘kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā’ti dvitte pubbassa cavaggo, cikicchati, cikicchanti, cikicchīyati, cikicchīyanti.

By the word `vā` (optionally), in the absence of the `ti`-sound, by the rule 'for gutturals, palatals arise', the preceding part of the reduplicated form becomes a palatal: `cikicchati`, `cikicchanti`, `cikicchīyati`, `cikicchīyanti`.

Asaṃsayeti [M 0.0464] kiṃ? Vicikicchati, vicikicchanti.

Why is 'in non-doubt' specified? `vicikicchati` (he doubts), `vicikicchanti` (they doubt).

Tikicchattha, saṃsayatthato aññasmiṃ atthe –

In a meaning other than that of treatment and doubt—

Kita-ñāṇe nivāse ca, ketati, saṃketati, niketati.

The root `kit` is used in the sense of knowledge and dwelling: `ketati`, `saṃketati`, `niketati`.

Gupa-nindāyaṃ.

The root `gup` is used in the sense of blame.

698. Nindāyaṃ gupabadhā bassa bho ca ka. 433; rū. 528; caṃ. 1.1.19, 20; pā. 3.1.5, 6 kā.

698. In the sense of blame, after `gup` and `badh`, and `ba` becomes `bho`.

Nindāyaṃ pavattehi gupa, badhehi paraṃ chapaccayo hoti, bassa ca bho hoti. Dvirūpe kate anādibyañjanalopo.

After `gup` and `badh`, when they occur in the sense of blame, the suffix `cha` is applied, and `ba` becomes `bho`. When reduplication is made, there is elision of a non-initial consonant.

699. Gupissi ka. 465; rū. 463; nī. 946; ‘gupissussa’ (bahūsu).

699. For `gup`, there is `i`.

Gupissa dvitte pubbassa u-kārassa i hoti. Gassa cavaggattaṃ, dhātvantassa pararūpattaṃ, saṃyogādissa paṭhamattaṃ.

When the root `gup` is reduplicated, the vowel `u` of the first part becomes `i`. The `g` becomes a palatal, the final consonant of the root is assimilated to the following, and the first consonant of the cluster becomes the first of its class.

Jigucchati, jigucchanti.

`Jigucchati` (he loathes), `jigucchanti` (they loathe).

Kamme-jigucchīyati, jigucchīyanti.

In the passive voice: `jigucchīyati` (he is loathed), `jigucchīyanti` (they are loathed).

Kārite-jiguccheti, jigucchayati, jigucchāpeti, jigucchāpayati. Jigucchatu, jigucchantu iccādi.

In the causative: `jiguccheti`, `jigucchayati`, `jigucchāpeti`, `jigucchāpayati` (he causes to loathe). `Jigucchatu` (let him loathe), `jigucchantu` (let them loathe), and so forth.

Nindāyanti kiṃ? Gupa-saṃvaraṇe, gopeti, gopayati.

Why is it specified ‘in the sense of blame’? Because the root `gup` is otherwise used in the sense of protecting, as in `gopeti` (he protects), `gopayati` (he protects).

Badha-nindāyaṃ, dvirūpādimhi kate –

The root `badh` in the sense of blame; when reduplication and so forth are performed:

700. Khachasessi ka. 465; rū. 463; nī. 946; ‘khachasesvassi’ (bahūsu).

700. Regarding `kha`, `cha`, and the rest.

Dvitte pubbassa assa i hoti kha, cha, sesūti assa ittaṃ, parabakārassa ca bhattaṃ, dhātvantassa pararūpādi.

When the root is reduplicated, the `a` of the first part becomes `i`. The following `ba` becomes `bha`. The final consonant of the root undergoes assimilation, and so forth.

Bibhacchati, virūpo hotīti attho. Bibhacchanti.

`Bibhacchati` (he is disgusted); the meaning is, he becomes ugly. `Bibhacchanti` (they are disgusted).

Nindāyanti [M 0.0465] kiṃ? Badha-bandhana, hiṃsāsu, bādheti, bādhayati. Vātaṃ jālena bādhesi jā. 1.12.8.

Why is it specified ‘in the sense of blame’? Because the root `badh` is otherwise used in the senses of binding and harming, as in `bādheti` (he obstructs), `bādhayati` (he obstructs). For example: `Vātaṃ jālena bādhesi` (You obstruct the wind with a net).

Kamme-bādhīyati, bādhīyanti, bajjhati, bajjhanti.

In the passive voice: `bādhīyati` (he is obstructed), `bādhīyanti` (they are obstructed); `bajjhati` (he is bound), `bajjhanti` (they are bound).

Iti sāmañña kha, cha, sarāsi.

Thus, in general, regarding `kha`, `cha`, and `sa`.

Tumicchatthe khachasarāsi

In the desiderative sense, regarding `kha`, `cha`, and `sa`.

701. Tuṃsmā lopo cicchāyaṃ te ka. 434; rū. 534; nī. 910; caṃ. 1.1.22; pā. 3.1.7.

701. From `tuṃ`, there is elision in the desiderative, and those (suffixes are introduced).

Tumantehi icchatthe te kha, cha, sā honti, tuṃpaccayassa ca lopo hoti. Idañca suttaṃ tumicchatthasambhave sati sabbadhātupadehipi kha, cha, sānaṃ pavattidīpanatthaṃ. Tena tumicchatthe sa, chapaccaye katvā ‘ū byañjanassā’ti sa, chānaṃ ādimhi īāgamaṃ katvā “aputtaṃ puttamiva ācarituṃ icchati puttīyīsati, pabbato viya attānaṃ ācarituṃ icchati pabbatāyīsati, dātuṃ icchati dicchati” iccādīni sijjhanti.

For those ending in `tuṃ`, in the desiderative sense, those suffixes, `kha`, `cha`, and `sa`, occur, and the suffix `tuṃ` is elided. And this rule is for the purpose of indicating the application of `kha`, `cha`, and `sa` even to all verbal stems when the desiderative meaning arises from `tuṃ`. Therefore, in the desiderative, having applied the suffixes `sa` and `cha`, and having applied the initial `ī` augment to `sa` and `cha` by the rule ‘ū byañjanassā’, examples like “he desires to treat a non-son like a son—`puttīyīsati`, he desires to act like a mountain—`pabbatāyīsati`, he desires to give—`dicchati`,” and so on, are established.

Bhuja, ghasa, hana, ji, hara, pā, su.

`Bhuja`, `ghasa`, `hana`, `ji`, `hara`, `pā`, `su`.

Bhuñjituṃ icchatīti atthe-bhujato khapaccayo, tuṃpaccayalopo, dvittaṃ, pubbassa anādilopo, pararūpatte saṃyogādissa paṭhamattaṃ, pubbassa bhassa battaṃ, bubhukkhati, bubhukkhanti, bubhukkhīyati, bubhukkhīyanti, bubhukkheti, bubhukkhayati, bubhukkhāpeti, bubhukkhāpayati, bubhukkhāpīyati, bubhukkhāpīyanti, bubhukkhatu, bubhukkhantu, bubhukkheyya, bubhukkheyyuṃ, bubhukkhi, bubhukkhiṃsu, bubhukkhissati, bubhukkhissanti, bubhukkhissā, bubhukkhissaṃsu.

In the sense of ‘he desires to eat’: the suffix `kha` is applied to `bhuj`, there is elision of the suffix `tuṃ`, reduplication, elision of the non-initial (vowel) of the preceding part, in assimilation, the initial consonant of the conjunct becomes the first of its class, and the `bha` of the preceding part becomes `ba`. Thus we have: `bubhukkhati` (he hungers), `bubhukkhanti` (they hunger), `bubhukkhīyati` (he is hungered), `bubhukkhīyanti` (they are hungered), `bubhukkheti` (he causes to hunger), `bubhukkhayati` (he causes to hunger), `bubhukkhāpeti` (he causes to hunger), `bubhukkhāpayati` (he causes to hunger), `bubhukkhāpīyati` (he is caused to hunger), `bubhukkhāpīyanti` (they are caused to hunger), `bubhukkhatu` (let him hunger), `bubhukkantu` (let them hunger), `bubhukkheyya` (he should hunger), `bubhukkheyyuṃ` (they should hunger), `bubhukkhi` (he hungered), `bubhukkhiṃsu` (they hungered), `bubhukkhissati` (he will hunger), `bubhukkhissanti` (they will hunger), `bubhukkhissā` (he will hunger), `bubhukkhissaṃsu` (they will hunger).

Ghasa-adane, ghasituṃ icchatīti atthe – chapaccayo, dvittādi, pubbassa ghassa gattaṃ, gassa jattaṃ, assa ittaṃ, jighacchati, jighacchanti, jighacchīyati, jighacchīyanti, jighaccheti, jighacchāpeti iccādi.

The root `ghas` is used in the sense of eating. In the sense of ‘he desires to eat’: the suffix `cha` is applied, with reduplication and other operations; the `gh` of the preceding part becomes `g`; the `g` becomes `j`; the `a` becomes `i`. Thus we have: `jighacchati`, `jighacchanti`, `jighacchīyati`, `jighacchīyanti`, `jighaccheti`, `jighacchāpeti`, etc.

Hana-hiṃ [M 0.0466] sāyaṃ, hantuṃ icchatīti atthe – chapaccayo, dvittādi, ‘kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā’ti pubbassa hassa jo, assa ittaṃ.

The root `han` is used in the sense of harming. In the sense of ‘he desires to kill’: the suffix `cha` is applied, with reduplication and other operations; by the rule ‘for the `kavagga` and `h`, letters of the `cavagga` are produced’, the `h` of the preceding part becomes `j`; and the `a` becomes `i`.

702. Parassa ghaṃ se.

702. For the following (root), `ghaṃ` is substituted when `sa` follows.

Dvitte parassa hanassa ghaṃ hoti se pare.

In reduplication, `ghaṃ` is substituted for the following `han` when `sa` follows.

Jighaṃsati, jighaṃsanti.

He desires to kill, they desire to kill.

Ji-jaye, jetuṃ icchatīti atthe – sapaccayo, dvittaṃ.

The root `ji` is used in the sense of conquering; in the sense of ‘he desires to conquer’ – the suffix `sa` is applied, and there is reduplication.

703. Jiharānaṃ gī ka. 462, 474; rū. 467, 535; nī. 943-954.

703. `Gī` is substituted for `ji` and `hara`.

Ji, harānaṃ dvitte parassa jissa harassa ca gī hoti se pare.

When `ji` and `hara` are reduplicated, `gī` is substituted for the following `ji` and `hara` when `sa` follows.

Jigīsati, jigīsanti, vijigīsati, vijigīsanti.

He desires to conquer, they desire to conquer; he desires to vanquish, they desire to vanquish.

Hara-haraṇe, dvittādi, parassa gī, pubbassa hassa jo, assa ittaṃ, jigīsati, harituṃ icchatīti attho, jigīsanti.

The root `hara` is used in the sense of taking. With reduplication and other operations, `gī` is substituted for the following part, the `h` of the preceding part becomes `j`, and its `a` becomes `i`. Thus, `jigīsati`, the meaning of which is ‘he desires to take’; and `jigīsanti`.

Pā-pāne, pivituṃ icchatīti atthe – sapaccayo, dvittaṃ, ‘rasso pubbassā’ti rasso, assa ittaṃ, pipāsati, pipāsanti, pipāsīyati, pipāsīyanti.

The root `pā` is used in the sense of drinking; in the sense of ‘he desires to drink’ – the suffix `sa` is applied, and there is reduplication; by the rule `rasso pubbassā`, there is shortening; the `a` of the preceding part becomes `i`. Thus, `pipāsati`, `pipāsanti`, `pipāsīyati`, `pipāsīyanti`.

Su-savane, sotuṃ icchatīti atthe – dvitte parassa dvittaṃ, sussusati sussūsati (bahūsu), sussusanti, sussusīyati, sussusīyanti, sussuseti, sussusayati, sussusāpeti, sussusāpayati, sussusāpīyati, sussusāpīyanti, sussusatu, sussusantu iccādi.

The root `su` is used in the sense of hearing; in the sense of ‘he desires to hear’ – in reduplication, there is doubling of the following part. Thus, `sussusati`, `sussusanti`, `sussusīyati`, `sussusīyanti`, `sussuseti`, `sussusayati`, `sussusāpeti`, `sussusāpayati`, `sussusāpīyati`, `sussusāpīyanti`, `sussusatu`, `sussusantu`, and so on.

Titikkhituṃ icchatīti atthe – titikkhato sapaccayo, sapaccayaparattā puna dvittappasaṅge –

In the sense of ‘he desires to endure’: from `titikkha`, the suffix `sa` is applied; and because it is followed by the suffix `sa`, when the occasion for reduplication again arises –

704. Na puna caṃ. 5.1.6.

704. id

Sakiṃ [M 0.0467] dvitte kate puna dvittaṃ na āpajjatīti puna dvittābhāvo, ‘ū byañjanassā’ti ū āgamo.

id

Titikkhisati, titikkhisanti iccādi. Evaṃ tikicchituṃ icchatīti tikicchisati, tikicchisanti, cikicchisati, cikicchisanti iccādi.

id

Iti tumicchatthe kha, cha, sa rāsi.

id

Nāmadhāturāsi

id

Puttaṃ icchatīti atthe –

id

705. Īyo kammā ka. 437; rū. 538; nī. 912; caṃ. 1.1.23, 24; pā. 3.1.8, 9.

705. id

Kammatthā nāmapadamhā icchatthe īyo hotīti kammabhūtā puttasaddato icchāyaṃ īyo, ‘puttīya’iti dhātupaccayantarūpaṃ, tato tyādyuppatti.

id

Puttīyati, puttīyanti, puttīyeti, puttīyayati, puttīyāpeti, puttīyāpayati, puttīyāpīyati, puttīyāpīyanti. Evaṃ cīvarīyati, cīvarīyanti, pattīyati, pattīyanti, parikkhārīyati, parikkhārīyanti iccādi.

id

Aputtaṃ sissaṃ puttamiva ācaratīti atthe –

id

706. Upamāṇācāre ka. 436; rū. 537; nī. 912; caṃ. 1.1.25; pā. 3.1.10.

706. id

Upamīyati upametabbo attho etenāti upamānaṃ, upamānabhūtā kammapadato ācāratthe īyo hoti.

id

Puttīyati[M 0.0468], puttīyanti sissaṃ.

id

Kamme-aputtopi putto viya ācarīyati puttīyīyati, puttīyīyanti, puttīyeti, puttīyayati, puttīyāpeti, puttīyāpayati, puttīyāpīyati, puttīyāpīyanti. Evaṃ sissīyati, sissīyanti.

id

Kuṭiyaṃ viya pāsāde ācaratīti atthe –

id

707. Ādhārā ka. 436; rū. 537; nī. 912; caṃ. 1.1.26; pā. 3.1.10.

707. id

Upamānabhūtā ādhārabhūtā ca nāmamhā ācāratthe īyo hoti.

id

Kuṭīyati, kuṭīyanti pāsāde, nadiyaṃ viya samudde ācarati nadīyati, nadīyanti iccādi.

id

Araññe viya nagare ācarati araññīyati, araññīyanti nagare. Evaṃ gehīyati vihāre.

id

Lokadhammehi akampanīyaṭṭhena pabbato viya attānaṃ ācaratīti atthe –

id

708. Kattutāyo ka. 435; rū. 536; nī. 911; caṃ. 1.1.27; pā. 3.1.11.

708. id

Upamānabhūtā kattubhūtā ca nāmamhā ācāratthe āyo hotīti pabbatasaddato āyo. Tato tyādyuppatti.

id

Pabbatāyati saṅgho, pabbatāyanti, cicciṭo viya attānaṃ ācarati cicciṭāyati, saddo. Evaṃ paṭapaṭāyati, kaṭakaṭāyati, dhūmadhūmāyati, dhūpāyati, sandhūpāyati.

id

Abhusampi [M 0.0469] bhusaṃ bhavatīti atthe –

id

709. Jhatthe ka. 435; rū. 536; nī. 911; caṃ. 1.1.30; pā. 3.1.12, 13.

709. id

Cīpaccayassa attho abbhūtatabbhāvo jhattho nāma. Kattuto jhatthe āyo hoti.

id

Bhusāyati, bhusāyanti, apaṭopi paṭo bhavati paṭāyati, paṭāyanti, alohitampi lohitaṃ bhavati lohitāyati. Evaṃ nīlāyati, kamalāyati, candāyati, candanāyati, kañcanāyati, vajirāyati.

id

Kattutotveva? Bhusaṃ karoti.

id

Saddaṃ karotīti atthe –

id

710. Saddādīhi karoti ka. 435; rū. 536; nī. 911; caṃ. 1.1.36; pā. 3.1.17, 18; ‘saddādīni’ (bahūsu).

710. id

Saddādīhi dutiyantehi nāmehi karotyatthe āyo hoti.

From nouns such as `sadda` and so on, which are in the accusative case, the suffix `āyo` occurs in the sense of ‘he makes’.

Saddāyati, saddāyanti, veraṃ karoti verāyati, verāyanti, kalahaṃ karoti kalahāyati, kalahāyanti, mettaṃ karoti mettāyati, mettāyanti, karuṇaṃ karoti karuṇāyati, karuṇāyanti, muditaṃ karoti muditāyati, muditāyanti, upekkhaṃ karoti upekkhāyati, upekkhāyanti, kukkuccaṃ karoti kukkuccāyati, kukkuccāyanti, piyaṃ karoti piyāyati, piyāyanti, paccayaṃ saddahanaṃ karoti pattiyāyati, pattiyāyanti, taṇhaṃ karoti taṇhāyati, taṇhāyanti, taṇhīyati, taṇhīyanti vā, karotyatthe īyo. Mama idanti karoti mamāyati, mamāyanti.

`Saddāyati` (he makes a sound), `saddāyanti` (they make a sound); from `veraṃ karoti` (he makes enmity), `verāyati` (he acts with enmity), `verāyanti` (they act with enmity); from `kalahaṃ karoti` (he makes a quarrel), `kalahāyati` (he quarrels), `kalahāyanti` (they quarrel); from `mettaṃ karoti` (he makes loving-kindness), `mettāyati` (he practices loving-kindness), `mettāyanti` (they practice loving-kindness); from `karuṇaṃ karoti` (he makes compassion), `karuṇāyati` (he practices compassion), `karuṇāyanti` (they practice compassion); from `muditaṃ karoti` (he makes appreciative joy), `muditāyati` (he practices appreciative joy), `muditāyanti` (they practice appreciative joy); from `upekkhaṃ karoti` (he makes equanimity), `upekkhāyati` (he practices equanimity), `upekkhāyanti` (they practice equanimity); from `kukkuccaṃ karoti` (he makes remorse), `kukkuccāyati` (he feels remorse), `kukkuccāyanti` (they feel remorse); from `piyaṃ karoti` (he makes affection), `piyāyati` (he acts affectionately), `piyāyanti` (they act affectionately); from `paccayaṃ saddahanaṃ karoti` (he makes conviction in conditions), `pattiyāyati` (he has conviction), `pattiyāyanti` (they have conviction); from `taṇhaṃ karoti` (he makes craving), `taṇhāyati` (he craves), `taṇhāyanti` (they crave); or `taṇhīyati`, `taṇhīyanti`—the suffix `īyo` is in the sense of ‘he makes’. From `mama idaṃ ti karoti` (he makes ‘this is mine’), `mamāyati` (he is possessive), `mamāyanti` (they are possessive).

Namo [M 0.0470] karotīti atthe –

In the sense of ‘he pays homage’:

711. Namotvasso caṃ. 1.1.37; pā. 3.1.19.

711. From `namo`, the suffix `assa` (is applied).

Namosaddato karotyatthe asso hoti.

From the word `namo`, in the sense of ‘he makes’, `assa` occurs.

Namassati, namassanti.

He pays homage, they pay homage.

Samānaṃ sadisaṃ karotīti atthe –

In the sense of ‘he makes equal or similar’:

712. Dhātvatthe nāmasmi pā. 3.1.21, 25.

712. From a noun, in the sense of a verbal root.

Dhātvattho vuccati yā kāci kriyā. Nāmasmā dhātvatthe i hoti. ‘Yuvaṇṇānameo paccaye’ti issa ettaṃ.

‘The sense of a verbal root’ is said to be any action. From a noun, in the sense of a verbal root, `i` occurs. By the rule `Yuvaṇṇānameo paccaye`, `i` becomes `e`.

Samāneti, samānenti.

He makes equal, they make equal.

‘Eonamayāvā sare’ti essa ayādeso. ‘Ṇiṇāpyāpīhi vā’ti ettha vāsaddena lapaccayo, samānayati, samānayanti, piṇaṃ karoti piṇeti, piṇayati, kusalaṃ pucchati kusaleti, kusalayati, visuddhaṃ hoti visuddheti, visuddhayati, vīṇāya upagāyati upavīṇeti, upavīṇāyati, paññāya atikkamati atipaññeti, atipaññāyati, vaccaṃ karoti vacceti, vaccayati, muttaṃ karoti mutteti, muttayati, balena pīḷeti baleti, balayati.

By the rule `Eonamayāvā sare`, `e` is substituted by `aya`. By the rule `Ṇiṇāpyāpīhi vā`, here by the word `vā`, the suffix `la` is added; `samānayati` (he makes equal), `samānayanti` (they make equal); from `piṇaṃ karoti` (he makes a lump), `piṇeti`, `piṇayati`; from `kusalaṃ pucchati` (he asks about what is wholesome), `kusaleti`, `kusalayati`; from `visuddhaṃ hoti` (he becomes pure), `visuddheti`, `visuddhayati`; from `vīṇāya upagāyati` (he sings along with the lute), `upavīṇeti`, `upavīṇāyati`; from `paññāya atikkamati` (he surpasses with wisdom), `atipaññeti`, `atipaññāyati`; from `vaccaṃ karoti` (he defecates), `vacceti`, `vaccayati`; from `muttaṃ karoti` (he urinates), `mutteti`, `muttayati`; from `balena pīḷeti` (he oppresses with strength), `baleti`, `balayati`.

Assa itte-balīyati, balīyanti. “Abalānaṃ balīyantī”ti pāḷi.

When `a` becomes `ī`: `balīyati`, `balīyanti`. The Pāli text states: “They act mightily against the weak.”

Saccaṃ karotīti atthe –

In the sense of ‘he makes true’:

713. Saccādīhāpi saṃyuttanikāye; rū. 540; nī. 914; pā. 3.1.25.

713. Also from 'sacca' and so forth.

Saccādīhi nāmehi dhātvatthe āpi hoti.

From nouns such as 'sacca' and so on, in the sense of a verbal root, the suffix 'āpi' occurs.

Saccāpeti[M 0.0471], saccāpenti, atthavibhāgaṃ karoti atthāpeti, atthāpenti, bedasatthaṃ karoti bedāpeti, bedāpenti, sukkhaṃ karoti sukkhāpeti, sukkhāpenti, sukhaṃ karoti sukhāpeti, sukhāpenti, dukkhaṃ karoti dukkhāpeti, dukkhāpenti, uṇhaṃ karoti uṇhāpeti, uṇhāpenti iccādi.

He makes true, they make true; he makes a division of meaning, thus he expounds, they expound; he makes a distinction in the teaching, thus he causes to distinguish, they cause to distinguish; he makes dry, thus he causes to dry, they cause to dry; he makes happy, thus he causes to be happy, they cause to be happy; he causes suffering, thus he causes to suffer, they cause to suffer; he makes hot, thus he causes to be hot, they cause to be hot, and so on.

Aputtaṃ puttamiva ācarati puttīyati, puttīyituṃ icchatīti atthe ‘tuṃsmā lopo cicchāyaṃ te’ti sapaccayo.

He treats one who is not a son as a son: this is `puttīyati`. In the sense of 'he desires to act as a son,' by the rule 'tuṃsmā lopo cicchāyaṃ te,' the suffix 'sa' is added.

714. Yathiṭṭhaṃ syādino ka. 458; rū. 461; nī. 939; caṃ. 5.1.8; pā. 6.1.3.

714. As desired, from 'sya' and so on.

Icchīyatīti iṭṭhaṃ, yaṃ yaṃ iṭṭhaṃ yathiṭṭhaṃ. “Yamiṭṭha”ntipi pāṭho. Syādyantassa yathiṭṭhaṃ ekassaraṃ ādibhūta’maññaṃ vā dverūpaṃ hoti, na tyādissa viya ādibhūtamevāti attho. ‘Ū byañjanassā’ti ū āgamo.

'Iṭṭhaṃ' means 'what is desired'; 'yathiṭṭhaṃ' means 'whatever is desired.' The reading 'yamiṭṭhaṃ' is also found. For a word ending in 'sya' and so on, as desired, a single vowel, either the initial one or another, is reduplicated; the meaning is that it is not like in the case of 'tyādi' and so on, where it is only the initial one. By the rule 'Ū byañjanassā,' 'ū' is an augment.

Ādimhi dvitte-pupputtīyisati.

When the beginning is doubled: 'pupputtīyisati'.

Majjhe dvitte-puttittīyisati.

When the middle is doubled: 'puttittīyisati'.

Akamalaṃ kamalaṃ bhavati kamalāyati, kamalāyituṃ icchatīti kakamalāyisati, kamamalāyisati, kamalalāyisati iccādi.

What is not a lotus becomes a lotus; this is `kamalāyati`, to act like a lotus. From the meaning 'he desires to act like a lotus' come the forms `kakamalāyisati`, `kamamalāyisati`, `kamalalāyisati`, and so on.

Iti nāmadhāturāsi.

Thus ends the section on denominative verbs.

Iti niruttidīpaniyā nāma moggallānadīpaniyā

Thus in the Niruttidīpanī, also known as the Moggallāna-dīpanī,

Tyādikaṇḍo nāma ākhyātakaṇḍo

the section on 'ti' and so on, called the verb section,

Niṭṭhito.

is finished.

7. Kitakaṇḍa

7. The Section on Primary Suffixes (Kita)

Dhātvantavikārarāsi

The Section on Modifications at the End of Roots

Visaṃyogarūparāsi

The Section on Forms of Disjunction

Atha [M 0.0472] dhātupaccayasaṃsiddhaṃ kāla, kāraka, liṅga, saṅkhyā, kriyābhedadīpakaṃ dabbappadhānavācakaṃ kitakapadaṃ dīpiyate.

Now, the primary derivative (`kitaka`) words, formed from roots and suffixes, indicative of distinctions of time, agent, gender, number, and action, and expressing substance as primary, are explained.

Tattha atītādayo kālabhedo nāma.

Therein, past and so on are called distinctions of time.

Kattā ca kammañca karaṇañca sampadānañca apādānañca adhikaraṇañca bhāvo cāti satta sādhanāni kārakabhedo nāma.

Agent, object, instrument, dative, ablative, locative, and state—these seven means are called distinctions of case.

Itthiliṅgādīni liṅgabhedo nāma.

Feminine gender and so on are called distinctions of gender.

Ekatta, bahuttabhedo saṅkhyābhedo nāma.

The distinction between singular and plural is called the distinction of number.

Tassīlakriyā, taddhammakriyā, tassādhukārakriyā, attamānakriyā, abhikkhaññakriyā, arahakriyā, sakkakriyā, pesanakriyā, atisaggakriyā, pattakālārocanakriyā, avassambhāvīkriyādayo kriyābhedo nāma.

Action of that nature, action of that quality, action of doing well for that, action of self-esteem, frequent action, action of being worthy, action of being able, action of sending, action of excessive giving, action of informing at the proper time, inevitable action, and so on are called distinctions of action.

“Gamanaṃ bhavati, pacanaṃ jānāti” iccādīsu paccayatthabhūto bhāvo nāma sādhanarūpo hoti. Jāti viya saṅkhatadhammassa dhātvatthabhūtāya sādhyakriyāya sādhakattā liṅgattayayutto ca hoti, kriyā, kāro, karaṇanti siddhattā saṅkhyābhedayutto ca hoti-nānādhātvatthānañca kattu, kammānañca kālādīnañca bhedena sarūpabhedasabbhavato, tasmā sopi dabbe eva saṅgayhatīti katvā ‘dabbappadhānavācaka’nti vuttaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbaṃ tyādikaṇḍe bhāvasādhanavinicchaye vuttameva.

In expressions like 'going happens', 'cooking is known', the state (bhāva), which is the meaning of the suffix, is of the nature of a means. Like birth for conditioned phenomena, being the meaning of the verbal root, it serves as the means for the action to be accomplished, and is endowed with the three genders; and since it is established as action, agent, and instrument, it is also endowed with distinctions of number. Due to the existence of distinctions in form through the diversity of verbal root meanings, and of agents, objects, time, and so on, therefore, considering that it is also included in substance, it is called 'expressing substance as primary'. All the rest has been explained in the section on the determination of the state as a means in the tyādi chapter.

‘Bahula’nti [M 0.0473] ca ‘kriyatthā’ti ca vattante –

The terms 'bahula' (variously) and 'kriyatthā' (for the purpose of action) are in effect.

715. Kattari bhūte kta ktavantu ktāvī ka. 555; rū. 612; nī. 1142; caṃ. 1.2.66 …pe… 3.2.102.

715. In the agentive sense, in the past, the suffixes kta, ktavantu, and ktāvī occur.

Abhavīti bhūto, atīto, bhūte vattabbe kriyatthā kattari kānubandhā ta, tavantu, tāvīpaccayā honti, kānubandhā ‘na te kānubandhanāgamesū’ti sutte visesanatthā.

'Abhavī' means 'bhūta', that is, 'past'. When the past is to be expressed, for the purpose of action, in the agentive sense, the suffixes ta, tavantu, and tāvī, which have 'ka' as an anubandha, occur. The 'ka' anubandhas are for the purpose of specification in the rule 'na te kānubandhanāgamesu'.

716. Kto bhāvakammesu ka. 556; rū. 622; nī. 1143; caṃ. 1.2.67 …pe… 3.2.102; 3.4.70.

716. The suffix kta is used in the sense of state and object.

Bhūte vattabbe kriyatthā bhāva, kammesu kānubandho tapaccayo hoti.

When the past is to be expressed, for the purpose of action, in the sense of state and object, the suffix ta, which has 'ka' as an anubandha, occurs.

Abhavīti bhūto-puriso, bhūtā-itthī, bhūtaṃ-kulaṃ, kārite dhātuto ṇānubandhānaṃ paṭhamaṃ sampattattā ‘na te kānubandhanāgamesū’ti paṭisedho na pāpuṇāti, ‘yuvaṇṇānameo paccaye’ti ovuddhi, ‘āvāyā ṇānubandhe’ti ossa āvattaṃ, tato tapaccayo.

'Abhavīti' means 'bhūta': a man who has been, a woman who has been, a family that has been. In the case of a causative root, because the anubandha ṇa is first obtained, the prohibition 'na te kānubandhanāgamesu' does not apply. By 'yuvaṇṇānameo paccaye', there is vuddhi of 'o', and by 'āvāyā ṇānubandhe', there is the change of 'o' to 'āva'. Then comes the suffix ta.

717. Ñī byañjanassa ka. 605; rū. 547; nī. 1210.

717. The augment ī (with anubandha ñ) is for a suffix beginning with a consonant.

Byañjanādipaccayassa ādimhi ñānubandho īkāro āgacchati.

To the beginning of a suffix that starts with a consonant, the vowel ī, which has ñ as an anubandha, is added as an augment.

Kattari-abhāvayitthāti bhāvito-puriso, bhāvitāitthī, bhāvitaṃ-kulaṃ.

In the agentive sense: 'he developed', hence bhāvito-puriso, a man who has developed; bhāvitā-itthī, a woman who has developed; bhāvitaṃ-kulaṃ, a family that has developed.

Kamme-anubhūyitthāti anubhūto-bhogo, anubhūtāsampatti, anubhūtaṃ-sukhaṃ.

In the objective sense: 'it was experienced', hence anubhūto-bhogo, enjoyment that was experienced; anubhūtā-sampatti, prosperity that was experienced; anubhūtaṃ-sukhaṃ, happiness that was experienced.

Kārite-bhāvīyitthāti bhāvito-maggo, bhāvitāpaṭipadā, bhāvitaṃ-cittaṃ.

In the causative sense: 'it was cultivated', hence bhāvito-maggo, the path that was cultivated; bhāvitā-paṭipadā, the practice that was cultivated; bhāvitaṃ-cittaṃ, the mind that was cultivated.

Tavantu[M 0.0474], tāvīsu-abhavīti bhūtavā-puriso, bhūtavantī, bhūtavatī-itthī, bhūtavaṃ-kulaṃ, guṇavantusamaṃ. Bhūtāvī-puriso. Bhūtāvinī-itthī, bhūtāvi-cittaṃ, daṇḍī, daṇḍinīsamaṃ. Puriso bhogaṃ anubhūto, purisena bhogo anubhūto.

In the case of tavantu and tāvī: 'he was', hence bhūtavā-puriso, a man who has been; bhūtavantī or bhūtavatī-itthī, a woman who has been; bhūtavaṃ-kulaṃ, a family that has been; this is similar to guṇavantu. Bhūtāvī-puriso, a man who has been. Bhūtāvinī-itthī, a woman who has been; bhūtāvi-cittaṃ, a mind that has been; this is similar to daṇḍī and daṇḍinī. The man experienced enjoyment; enjoyment was experienced by the man.

Ettha ca kitapaccayānaṃ attho duvidho vāccattho, abhidheyyattho cāti sabbaṃ tyādikaṇḍe vuttanayena veditabbaṃ.

And here, the meaning of the kita suffixes is twofold: the expressed meaning and the signified meaning. All this should be understood according to the method explained in the tyādi chapter.

Purimesu pana chasu sādhanesu paccayānaṃ abhidheyyattho padantarena ācikkhīyati, bhāvasādhane pana attano dhātunā eva.

However, in the first six means, the signified meaning of the suffixes is indicated by another word, but in the case of the means of state, it is indicated by its own root alone.

Tattha ca kattusatti, kammasatti, karaṇasatti, sampadānasatti, apādānasatti, adhikaraṇasattisaṅkhātaṃ vāccatthaṃ ujuṃ vadantā kitapaccayā attano abhidheyyapadena samānaliṅga, vibhatti, saṅkhyāyuttā hutvā vadanti.

And in that regard, the kita suffixes, directly expressing the expressed meaning—designated as the agent's power, the object's power, the instrument's power, the recipient's power, the ablative's power, and the locative's power—do so by having the same gender, case, and number as their own signified word.

Taṃ yathā? –

How is that?

Kattari tāva-puriso bhogaṃ anubhūto, purisā bhogaṃ anubhūtā…pe… purisesu bhogaṃ anubhūtesu, itthī bhogaṃ anubhūtā, itthiyo bhogaṃ anubhūtāyo…pe… itthīsu bhogaṃ anubhūtāsu, kulaṃ bhogaṃ anubhūtaṃ, kulāni bhogaṃ anabhūtāni…pe… kulesu bhogaṃ anubhūtesu.

First, in the agentive sense: the man has experienced wealth, the men have experienced wealth… and so on up to… when the men have experienced wealth; the woman has experienced wealth, the women have experienced wealth… and so on up to… when the women have experienced wealth; the family has experienced wealth, the families have experienced wealth… and so on up to… when the families have experienced wealth.

Kamme-bhogo purisena anubhūto, bhogā purisena anubhūtā…pe… bhogesu purisena anubhūtesu, sampatti purisena anubhūtā, sampattiyo purisena anubhūtāyo…pe… sampattīsu purisena anubhūtāsu, sukhaṃ purisena anubhūtaṃ, sukhāni purisena anubhūtāni…pe… sukhesu purisena anubhūtesu. Esa nayo karaṇādīsupi.

In the objective sense: wealth was experienced by the man, riches were experienced by the man… and so on up to… when riches were experienced by the man; prosperity was experienced by the man, prosperities were experienced by the man… and so on up to… when prosperities were experienced by the man; happiness was experienced by the man, happinesses were experienced by the man… and so on up to… when happinesses were experienced by the man. This is the method for the instrumental and other cases as well.

Evaṃ kitavācakā attano abhidheyyapadena samānaliṅga, vibhatti, saṅkhyāyuttā hutvā taṃ taṃ sādhanaṃ vadanti.

Thus, words formed with kita suffixes, having the same gender, case, and number as their signified word, express that particular means.

‘Itthiyamaṇatikayakyā [M 0.0475] cā’ti itthiyaṃ tipaccayo, anubhavanaṃ, anubhūyate vā anubhūti. “Tissassa anubhūti, phussassa anubhūti” iccādikā bahū anubhūtiyopi sijjhanti, tasmā “anubhūti, anubhūtiyo, anubhūtiṃ, anubhūtiyo…pe… anubhūtīsū”ti yujjati.

By the rule 'Itthiyamaṇatikayakyā ca', the suffix ti occurs in the feminine. 'Anubhavanaṃ' (experiencing) or 'anubhūyate' (is experienced) is anubhūti (experience). Many instances of anubhūti are also formed, such as 'Tissassa anubhūti' (Tissa’s experience) and 'Phussassa anubhūti' (Phussa’s experience). Therefore, the forms 'anubhūti, anubhūtiyo, anubhūtiṃ, anubhūtiyo… and so on up to… anubhūtīsu' are correct.

503 718. Kattari ltuṇakā ka. 527, 530; rū. 568, 590; nī. 1109, 1114; caṃ. 1.1.139; pā. 3.1.133, 134.

503 718. In the agentive sense, ltu and ṇaka.

Kattukārake kriyatthā ltu, ṇakā honti, lānubandho tussa kattari nibandhanattho, ‘ltupitādīnamā’ti visesanattho ca.

In the agentive case, for the purpose of action, the suffixes ltu and ṇaka occur. The anubandha 'l' in 'ltu' is for the purpose of restricting it to the agent, and also for specification in the rule 'ltupitādīnamā'.

Anubhavatīti anubhūtā, anubhūtāro, satthusamaṃ.

'He experiences', hence anubhūtā (singular) and anubhūtāro (plural), similar to satthu (the Teacher).

Sāmaññavidhānattā arahatthe sattiatthe tassīla, taddhamma, tassādhukāra, attamānesu ca kālattaye ca bhavanti.

Because it is a general rule, they occur in the sense of worthiness, in the sense of ability, in the senses of having such a nature, such a quality, or such a good practice, in the sense of self-esteem, and in the three periods of time.

Arahatthe-brahmaṇo brahmaṇiyā pariggahitā.

In the sense of 'arahat': a brahmin is taken by a brahmin woman.

Sattiatthe-bhagavā anuppannassa maggassa uppādetā.

In the sense of being/existence: the Blessed One is the producer of the unarisen path.

Tassīlādīsu-pasayhapavattā.

In the sense of one's nature, etc.: proceeding by force.

Attamāne-attānaṃ paṇḍitaṃ maññatīti paṇḍitamānitā.

In self-conceit: thinking oneself wise is conceit of wisdom.

719. Pubbekakattukānaṃ ka. 564; rū. 640; nīti. 1150-6; caṃ. 1.3.131; pā. 3.4.21.

719. Concerning a Single Agent for a Prior Action.

Yāsaṃ visesana, visesyānaṃ dvinnaṃ pubbā’parakriyānaṃ kattā ekova hoti. Tāsu pubbakriyāyaṃ bhāvatthe tuna, tvāna, tvāpaccayā honti. ‘Eonamayavā sare’ti īkāre pare ovuddhiyā avattaṃ.

For sentences in which the agent of two prior and subsequent actions, whether qualifier or qualified, is one and the same, the suffixes 'tuna,' 'tvāna,' and 'tvā' occur in the sense of the verbal noun for the prior action. By the rule ‘Eonamayavā sare’, when 'ī' follows, 'o-vuddhi' becomes 'ava'.

Bhogaṃ anubhavituna, anubhutvāna, anubhutvā.

Having experienced wealth; having experienced; having experienced.

Ekakattukānanti [M 0.0476] kiṃ? Devadatto bhuñji, yaññadatto gacchati.

What is meant by 'having one agent'? Devadatta ate; Yaññadatta goes.

Pubbeti kiṃ? Pacchā bhuñjati, paṭhamaṃ pacati.

What is meant by 'prior'? He eats afterwards, he cooks first.

Bahulādhikārā samānā’parakriyāsupi nānākattukāsupi tunādayo bhavanti. Thakkacca daṇḍo patati, dvāraṃ saṃvaritvā nikkhamati, puriso sīhaṃ disvā bhayaṃ uppajjatīti.

Due to the rule of 'bahula' (frequent/various application), 'tuna' and so on occur even in similar subsequent actions and even with different agents. For example: The staff falls, having been struck; having closed the door, he goes out; having seen a lion, fear arises in the man.

Yasmiṃ vākye aparakriyāpadaṃ na dissati. Yathā? Pabbataṃ atikkamma nadī, atikkamma nadiṃ pabbato, ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe arūpāti, tatthapi sattākriyā viññāyateva sabbapadatthānaṃ sattānātivattanato. Aparakriyārahite asamānakattuke ca vākye paṭhamantayogassa diṭṭhattā kattaripi tunādīnaṃ sambhavo yutto.

In a sentence where a subsequent action verb is not seen. For example: 'Having crossed the mountain, there is the river; having crossed the river, there is the mountain; those peaceful liberations which, having transcended forms, are the formless attainments.' Even there, the action of being is understood, because the existence of all word-meanings does not go beyond existence. In a sentence lacking a subsequent action and having a non-identical agent, since a connection with a word in the nominative case is seen, the possibility of 'tuna' and so on occurring in the agentive sense is reasonable.

720. Paṭisedhālaṃkhalūnaṃ tuna tvāna tvā vā paṭisedhelaṃkhalūnaṃ tunattvāna ttvā vā’ (bahūsu).

720. With 'alaṃ' and 'khalu' in the sense of prohibition, the suffixes 'tuna', 'tvāna', and 'tvā' occur optionally.

Paṭisedhatthānaṃ alaṃ, khalūnaṃ yoge tunādayo honti vā.

In conjunction with 'alaṃ' and 'khalu' when they have the meaning of prohibition, the suffixes 'tuna' and so on occur optionally.

Alaṃ bhutvā, khalu bhutvā, alaṃ bhuttena, khalu bhuttena vā.

Enough of eating, stop eating; or, enough with what has been eaten, stop with what has been eaten.

721. Tuṃtāyetave bhāve bhavissatikriyāyaṃ tadatthāyaṃ ka. 561-2-3; rū. 636, 638-9; nī. 1148-9.

721. The suffixes 'tuṃ', 'tāye', and 'tave' occur in the sense of the action, for a future action, and for that purpose.

Tassā tassā kriyāya atthabhūtāya bhavissamānakriyāya gamyamānāya bhāvatthe tuṃ, tāye, tavepaccayā bhavanti. Suttapadavaḍḍhanena tuyepaccayopi.

For each action, being meaningful, when a future action is implied, the suffixes 'tuṃ', 'tāye', and 'tave' occur in the sense of the verbal noun. By the expansion of the sūtra-pada, the suffix 'tuye' also occurs.

Anubhavituṃ gacchati, anubhavitāye gacchati, anubhavitave gacchati, anubhavituṃ icchati, kāmeti, sakkoti, jānāti. Tathā kālo anubhavituṃ, samayo anubhavituṃ, velā anubhavituṃ[M 0.0477]. Tathā anubhavituṃ mano, anubhavituṃ soko, cakkhu daṭṭhuṃ, sotaṃ sotuṃ, mano viññātuṃ, hattho kātuṃ, pādo gantuṃ, dhanu yujjhituṃ, jaḷo vattuṃ, mando gantuṃ, alaso kattunti.

He goes to experience, he goes for experiencing, he goes for the sake of experiencing; he wishes to experience, desires to experience, is able to experience, knows how to experience. Likewise, time to experience, occasion to experience, moment to experience. Likewise, the mind to experience, sorrow to experience, the eye to see, the ear to hear, the mind to know, the hand to do, the foot to go, the bow to fight, the mute to speak, the slow to go, the lazy to act.

Ettha ca “kālo anubhavitu”ntiādīsu sattāvasena hetukriyā sijjhati, tasmā “anubhavituṃ kālo bhavatī”tiādinā attho veditabbo.

Here, too, in "time to experience," etc., the causal action is accomplished by means of being/existence. Therefore, the meaning should be understood as "it is time for experiencing," etc.

Ime panettha tāye, tuyepayogā – āgatāmha imaṃ dhammasamayaṃ, dakkhitāye aparājitasaṅghaṃ dī. ni. 2.332. Alañhi te jagghitāye, mamaṃ disvāna edisaṃ jā. 1.5.137. Ko tādisaṃ arahati khāditāye jā. 1.16.92, atthi hehiti so maggo, na so sakkā na hotuye bu. vaṃ. 2.9 ‘hetuye’, arahasi naṃ yācituye tuvampi, arahasi no jānituye katāni iccādi.

Here are these usages of 'tāye' and 'tuye': We have come to this Dhamma assembly to see the invincible Sangha. Indeed, it is enough for you to laugh, seeing me in such a state. Who is worthy to devour such as this? There is that path; it is not possible for it not to exist. You too are worthy to ask for it, and you are worthy to know the things done by us, and so on.

722. Bhāvakammesu tabbānīyā ka. 540; rū. 545; nī. 1125.

722. In the senses of verbal noun and passive: the suffixes 'tabba' and 'anīya'.

Bhāve kammani ca tabba, anīyā honti. Suttapadavaḍḍhanena tabya, tāya, teyyapaccayāpi honti.

In the senses of verbal noun and passive, the suffixes 'tabba' and 'anīya' occur. By the expansion of the sūtra-pada, the suffixes 'tabya', 'tāya', and 'teyya' also occur.

Anubhavitabbo-bhogo, anubhavitabbā-sampatti, anubhavitabbaṃ-sukhaṃ.

Wealth is to be enjoyed, success is to be enjoyed, happiness is to be enjoyed.

Bahulādhikārā kattādīsvapi bhavanti, tapantīti tapanīyāpāpadhammā, upaṭṭhātīti upaṭṭhānīyo-sisso. Pavuccati etenāti pavacanīyo-upajjhāyo, niyyanti etenāti niyyānīyo, so eva niyyāniko.

Due to the rule of 'bahula' (frequent/various application), they also occur in the agentive, etc., senses. Because they cause torment, evil states are called 'tapanīya'. Because he attends, a pupil is called 'upaṭṭhānīya'. Because one is instructed by him, a preceptor is called 'pavacanīya'. Because one is led out by this, it is called 'niyyānīya'; that itself is 'niyyānika'.

Sinā-soceyye, sināyanti etenāti sinānīyaṃcuṇṇaṃ, dīyate assāti dānīyo-brāhmaṇo. Sammā vattati etthāti sammāvattanīyo-guru.

In the sense of bathing and cleansing: because one bathes with it, it is 'sinānīyaṃ cuṇṇaṃ' (bathing powder); because something is given to him, a brahmin is 'dānīyo' (worthy of a gift); because one behaves rightly towards him, a teacher is 'sammāvattanīyo' (one to be treated rightly).

Idha [M 0.0478] gāthā vuccati –

Here a verse is spoken:

Arahatthe ca sakkatthe, pattakāle ca pesane;

Tabbādayo atisagge, avassādhamiṇesu ca.

In the sense of worthiness and capability, and at the proper time and in sending; the suffixes beginning with -tabba are used in the sense of permission, and also in the senses of necessity and debt.

Tattha “araha sakka visiṭṭhe kattarī”ti vuttiyaṃ vuttaṃ, tasmā bhavatīti bhabbo, bhavituṃ arahatīti attho, majjatīti majjaṃ, madanīyaṃ, majjituṃ sakkotīti attho, evampi yujjati.

Therein, it is stated in the commentary: 'In the agent, in the sense of worthy, capable, and excellent.' Therefore, 'bhabbo' (capable) is from 'he becomes,' meaning 'he is worthy to become.' 'Majjaṃ' (intoxicant) is from 'it intoxicates,' meaning 'madanīyaṃ' (intoxicating), that is, 'it is able to intoxicate.' This too is fitting.

Pattakāle-kattabbo bhavatā kaṭo, esa kālo kaṭakaraṇassāti dīpeti.

In the sense of 'the proper time': 'A mat is to be made by you.' This indicates: 'This is the time for making the mat'.

Pesane-gantabbo bhavatā gāmo, gacchatu bhavaṃ gāmanti dīpeti.

In the sense of 'sending': 'The village is to be gone to by you.' This indicates: 'Let the venerable one go to the village'.

Atisajjanaṃ sambodhanaṃ atisaggo, upadeso ceva vidhi ca. Tattha kattabbā’kattabbassa kammassa ācikkhaṇaṃ upadeso, dānaṃ dātabbaṃ, sīlaṃ rakkhitabbaṃ, pāṇo na hantabbo, adinnaṃ na ādātabbaṃ dī. ni. 3.85. Kattabbā’kattabbākāradassanaṃ vidhi, sakkaccaṃ dānaṃ dātabbaṃ, no asakkaccaṃ.

Atisagga means permission, exhortation, and also instruction and prescription. Therein, instruction is the declaration of an action that should be done and should not be done: 'A gift is to be given; virtue is to be protected; a living being is not to be killed; what is not given is not to be taken.' Prescription is the showing of the manner in which something should be done and should not be done: 'A gift is to be given respectfully, not disrespectfully.'

Avassake-gamanīyo abhisamparāyo, avassaṃ gantabboti attho.

In the sense of 'necessity': 'The future life is to be gone to.' The meaning is: 'It must certainly be gone to'.

Yaṃ iṇaṃ adentassa daṇḍo āgacchati, idaṃ adhamiṇaṃ nāma, sataṃ me dātabbaṃ bhavatāti.

When a penalty comes to one who does not pay a debt, this is called 'being a debtor.' For example: 'A hundred is to be given to me by you.'

Ime panettha tabya, tāya, teyyapayogā – na brāhmaṇe addhike tiṭṭhamāne, gantabyamāhu dvipadinda seṭṭha jā. 1.10.13 (gantabba). Bhūtagāmapātabyatā, kāmesu pātabyatā pāci. 90, alajjitāye lajjanti dha. pa. 316, lajjitāye na lajjare. Ghātetāyaṃ vā ghātetuṃ, pabbājetāyaṃ vā pabbājetuṃ ma. ni. 1.357, ñāteyyaṃ, diṭṭheyyaṃ, patteyyaṃ, viddheyyaṃ maṃ amaññatha jā. 2.22.297.

Here are some usages of the suffixes -tabya, -tāya, and -teyya: 'When a brahmin is standing on a journey, they say one must go, O best of bipeds.' 'Destruction of plants, destruction in regard to sensual pleasures.' 'They are ashamed of what is not to be ashamed of; they are not ashamed of what is to be ashamed of.' 'For killing or to kill, for banishing or to banish.' 'Do not think me knowable, seeable, attainable, or penetrable.'

Ta,ti[M 0.0479], tu, tavantu, tāvī, tvā, tvāna, tuna, tuṃ, tave, tāye, tuye, tabba. Ime takārapaccayā nāma.

Ta, ti, tu, tavantu, tāvī, tvā, tvāna, tuna, tuṃ, tave, tāye, tuye, tabba. These are called the suffixes containing the letter 't'.

Kara, khanu, gā, gamu, jana, ṭhā, tanu, thara, dhā, dhara, namu, pā, phara, bhara, mana, mara, ramu, sara, hara, hana.

Kara, khanu, gā, gamu, jana, ṭhā, tanu, thara, dhā, dhara, namu, pā, phara, bhara, mana, mara, ramu, sara, hara, hana.

723. Gamādirānaṃ lopontassa ka. 586-7; rū. 600, 632; nī. 1190, 1191.

723. Elision of the final letter of roots beginning with gamu.

Gamādīnaṃ makāra, nakārantānaṃ rakārantānañca dhātūnaṃ antassa lopo hoti kānubandhe tapaccaye pare tvādivajjite.

Of the roots beginning with gamu that end in the letters m, n, and r, the final letter is elided when the suffix -ta with the anubandha k follows, excluding the suffixes beginning with -tvā.

Kara-karaṇe, karīyitthāti kato-vihāro, katāgūhā, kataṃ-gehaṃ, sakkarīyitthāti sakkato, mahāvuttinā santassa so.

The root kara in the sense of 'doing': `karīyittha` (it was done) becomes kato. For example: vihāro kato (a monastery was made), gūhā katā (a cave was made), gehaṃ kataṃ (a house was made). `sakkarīyittha` (it was honored) becomes sakkato (honored). According to the Mahāvutti, the 's' is from santa.

‘Karotissa kho’ti pādito karassa kassa kho, saṅkharīyitthāti saṅkhato, abhisaṅkhato, visaṅkharittha vikirīyitthāti visaṅkhato, upakarīyittha sajjīyitthāti upakkhaṭo, ‘tathanarānaṃ ṭaṭhaṇalā’ti tassa ṭo. Evaṃ dukkaṭaṃ.

From the line beginning 'Karotissa kho,' 'kassa kho' is from 'karassa.' `saṅkharīyittha` becomes saṅkhato (prepared) and abhisaṅkhato (fully prepared). `visaṅkharittha` or `vikirīyittha` becomes visaṅkhato (dismantled). `upakarīyittha` or `sajjīyittha` becomes upakkhaṭo (prepared); by the rule 'tathanarānaṃ ṭaṭhaṇalā,' its 't' becomes 'ṭ'. Similarly, dukkaṭaṃ.

Parito karīyitthāti parikkhato, purato karīyitthāti purakkhato, purekkhato vā, mahāvuttinā purassa ettaṃ.

`Parito karīyittha` becomes parikkhato (surrounded). `Purato karīyittha` becomes purakkhato or, alternatively, purekkhato; according to the Mahāvutti, the vowel of pura becomes 'e'.

Khanu-avadāraṇe, khaññitthāti khato-āvāṭo.

The root khanu in the sense of 'digging up': `khaññittha` (it was dug) becomes khato. For example: āvāṭo khato (a pit was dug).

Gā-sadde.

The root gā in the sense of 'sound'.

724. Gāpānamī ka. 588; rū. 620; nī. 1192.

724. Of gā and pā, the vowel becomes ī.

Gā, pānaṃ anto īkāro hoti kānubandhe tapaccaye pare tvādivajjite.

Of the roots gā and pā, the final vowel becomes ī when the suffix -ta with the anubandha k follows, excluding the suffixes beginning with -tvā.

Gāyitthāti gītaṃ, samodhānetvā gāyitthāti saṅgītopariyattidhammo.

`Gāyittha` (it was sung) becomes gītaṃ (song). `Samodhānetvā gāyittha` (it was sung together) becomes saṅgīta, as in saṅgīto pariyattidhammo (the scriptural teaching that was chanted together).

Gamu-gatimhi [M 0.0480] agacchīti gato, agacchīyitthāti vā gato. Evaṃ āgato, uggato, duggato, niggato, vigato, sugato, saṅgato, anugato, apagato, avagato, upagato, adhigato.

The root gamu in the sense of 'going': `agacchi` (he went) becomes gato (gone), or `agacchīyittha` (it was gone to) becomes gato. Similarly: āgato (come), uggato (arisen), duggato (gone to a bad destination), niggato (gone out), vigato (departed), sugato (well-gone), saṅgato (met), anugato (followed), apagato (gone away), avagato (understood), upagato (approached), adhigato (attained).

Jana-jātiyaṃ.

The root jana in the sense of 'generation'.

725. Janissā ka. 585; rū. 619; nī. 1189.

725. Of jana, the result is ā.

Janissa nassa ā hoti kānubandhe tapaccaye pare tvādivajjite.

Of the root jana, the 'n' becomes 'ā' when the suffix -ta with the anubandha k follows, excluding the suffixes beginning with -tvā.

Ajāyitthāti jāto, dujjāto, sujāto, sañjāto, anujāto, avajāto, atijāto.

`Ajāyittha` (he was born) becomes jāto (born). Similarly: dujjāto (ill-born), sujāto (well-born), sañjāto (arisen), anujāto (born in conformity), avajāto (degenerate), atijāto (superior).

Suttavibhattena aññasmimpi vaṇṇe pare nassa ā hoti, puttaṃ vijāyitvā, vijāyituṃ, vijāyanaṃ, vijāyantī-itthī, vijāyamānā, puttaṃ janetīti jāyā iccādi, sabbattha mahāvuttinā sare pare yāgamo, mahāvuttinā vā sabbattha nassa yādeso ādidīgho ca.

By extension of the rule, even when another letter follows, the 'n' becomes 'ā'. For example: puttaṃ vijāyitvā (having given birth to a son), vijāyituṃ (to give birth), vijāyanaṃ (giving birth), vijāyantī-itthī (a woman giving birth), vijāyamānā (giving birth), puttaṃ janetīti jāyā (she who bears a son is a wife), etc. Universally, according to the Mahāvutti, when a vowel follows, there is the augment 'y'; or, according to the Mahāvutti, universally there is the substitution of 'y' for 'n' and lengthening of the initial vowel.

Ṭhā-gatinivattiyaṃ.

The root ṭhā in the sense of 'cessation of movement'.

726. Ṭhāssi ka. 588; rū. 620; nī. 1192.

726. Of ṭhā, the vowel becomes i.

Ṭhāssa i hoti kānubandhe takāre tvādivajjite.

Of the root ṭhā, the vowel becomes i when the suffix -ta with the anubandha k follows, excluding the suffixes beginning with -tvā.

Aṭṭhāsīti ṭhito, uṭṭhito, niṭṭhito, saṇṭhito, adhiṭṭhito.

`Aṭṭhāsi` (he stood) becomes ṭhito (stood). Similarly: uṭṭhito (arisen), niṭṭhito (completed), saṇṭhito (established), adhiṭṭhito (determined).

Tanu-vitthāre, ātaññitthāti ātataṃ, vitataṃ, ātatavitataṃ, tūriyabhedo.

The root tanu in the sense of 'stretching': `ātaññittha` (it was stretched) becomes ātataṃ (stretched), vitataṃ (spread out), and ātatavitataṃ (stretched and spread out), which is a type of musical instrument.

Thara-santharaṇe, santharīyitthāti santhato, vitthato.

The root thara in the sense of 'spreading': `santharīyittha` (it was spread) becomes santhato (spread) and vitthato (spread out).

Dhā-dhāraṇe.

The root dhā in the sense of 'holding'.

727. Dhāssa hi ka. 517; rū. 488; nī. 1105.

727. Of dhā, the result is hi.

Dhādhātussa [M 0.0481] dhassa hi hoti kānubandhe takāre tvādivajjite.

Of the root dhā, the 'dh' becomes 'hi' when the suffix -ta with the anubandha k follows, excluding the suffixes beginning with -tvā.

Ādhīyitthāti āhito, āgyāhito, vidhīyitthāti vihito, nidhīyitthāti nihito, sandhīyitthāti saṃhito, odhīyitthāti ohito, abhidhīyitthāti abhihito, pidhīyitthāti pihito, apihito. Dvitte pubbassa tatiyattaṃ, ‘dhāssa ho’ti suttena parassa hattaṃ, ādahito, vidahito, nidahito, saṃdahito, saddahito vā, sannidahito, odahito, pidahito, apidahito, paridahito.

`Ādhīyittha` (it was placed) becomes `āhito` (placed) or `āgyāhito` (placed upon); `vidhīyittha` becomes `vihito` (arranged); `nidhīyittha` becomes `nihito` (deposited); `sandhīyittha` becomes `saṃhito` (composed); `odhīyittha` becomes `ohito` (put down); `abhidhīyittha` becomes `abhihito` (addressed); `pidhīyittha` becomes `pihito` or `apihito` (covered). When doubled, the first becomes the third letter of its class, and by the sutta 'dhāssa ho,' the second becomes 'h'. Alternatively, there are the forms: `ādahito`, `vidahito`, `nidahito`, `saṃdahito`, or `saddahito` (believed), `sannidahito`, `odahito`, `pidahito`, `apidahito`, `paridahito`.

Dhara-dhāraṇe, uddharīyitthāti uddhaṭo, samuddhaṭo, niddhaṭo, tassa ṭattaṃ.

The root `Dhara` is in the sense of bearing. 'It was lifted up' (`uddharīyittha`) becomes `uddhaṭo` (drawn out), `samuddhaṭo` (completely drawn out), `niddhaṭo` (removed); its final consonant becomes `ṭa`.

Namu-namane, namitthāti nato, unnato, samunnato, onato, avanato.

The root `Namu` is in the sense of bending. 'He bent' (`namittha`) becomes `nato` (bowed), `unnato` (raised up), `samunnato` (fully raised up), `onato` (bent down), `avanato` (bent down).

Pā-pāne, ‘gāpānamī’ti īttaṃ, pīyitthāti pītaṃ.

The root `Pā` is in the sense of drinking. By the rule 'gāpānamī,' there is a change to `ī`. 'It was drunk' (`pīyittha`) becomes `pītaṃ` (drunk).

Phara-pharaṇe, pharittha, pharīyitthāti vā phuṭo, vipphuṭo, samphuṭo, ophuṭo, mahāvuttinā phassa uttaṃ, tassa ṭattaṃ.

The root `Phara` is in the sense of spreading. From 'he spread' (`pharittha`) or 'it was spread' (`pharīyittha`) come the forms `phuṭo` (spread), `vipphuṭo` (pervaded), `samphuṭo` (completely pervaded), `ophuṭo` (covered). By the Mahāvutti, the `a` of `pha` becomes `u`, and its `ra` becomes `ṭa`.

Bhara-dhāraṇe, bharīyitthāti bhato, ābhato, ābhaṭo vā. Udakātalamubbhato, ubbhataṃ saṅghena kathinaṃ mahāva. 317, sambhataṃ dhanaṃ.

The root `Bhara` is in the sense of bearing. 'It was borne' (`bharīyittha`) becomes `bhato` (carried), `ābhato` (brought), or `ābhaṭo` (brought). Examples: 'drawn up from the water's surface' (`udakātalamubbhato`); 'the kathina is withdrawn by the Sangha' (`ubbhataṃ saṅghena kathinaṃ`); 'wealth is accumulated' (`sambhataṃ dhanaṃ`).

Mana-ñāṇe, mato, mahājanena sammatoti mahāsammato, sammatā sīmā mahāva. 139, anumato, abhimato.

The root `Mana` is in the sense of knowing. Hence `mato` (thought, considered). 'Because he is agreed upon by the great populace' (`mahājanena sammato`), he is called `Mahāsammato` (the Great Elect). Other examples: `sammatā sīmā` (the boundary is agreed upon); `anumato` (approved); `abhimato` (esteemed).
