From the root `kant` in the sense of 'cutting': having cut (`kacca`), having hacked (`vikacca`), having sliced (`kantitvā`), having carved (`vikantitvā`).

Nikara-vañcane, nikacca kitavasseva saṃ. ni. 1.35.

From `ni` + `kar` in the sense of 'deceiving': '...having deceived, like a gambler.'

Pata-gatiyaṃ, pacca, nipacca, patitvā, nipatitvā.

From the root `pat` in the sense of falling: having fallen, having fallen down, having fallen, having fallen down.

Katha-kathane, sākaccha.

From the root `kath` in the sense of speaking: having discussed.

Pada-gatiyaṃ, pajja, āpajja, nipajja, vipajja, sampajja, upasampajja, paṭipajja.

From the root `pad` in the sense of motion: having gone, having come upon, having lain down, having perished, having become endowed with, having undertaken the higher life, having practiced.

‘Ū byañjanassā’ti īāgame ‘padādīnaṃ yuka’iti yāgamo, pubbarūpaṃ, pajjiya, pajjiyāna, āpajjiya, āpajjiyāna, nipajjiya, vipajjiya, sampajjiya, paṭipajjiya.

By the rule ‘Ū byañjanassā,’ there is the insertion of `ī`; by ‘padādīnaṃ yuka,’ there is the insertion of `ya` and assimilation to the preceding consonant, giving: pajjiya, pajjiyāna, āpajjiya, āpajjiyāna, nipajjiya, vipajjiya, sampajjiya, paṭipajjiya.

Āpubba sada-ghaṭṭane, āsajja naṃ tathāgataṃ itivu. 89, kākova selamāsajja. Chejja, chijja, chindiya, acchijja, acchindiya, vicchijja, vicchindiya, paricchijja, paricchindiya, bhejja, bhijja, sambhijja, paṭisambhijja, bhindiya, sambhindiya.

From the root `sad` preceded by `ā`, in the sense of assailing, as in: ‘having assailed that Tathāgata, like a crow assailing a rock.’ Also: having cut; having cut; having cut; having snatched away; having snatched away; having cut off; having cut off; having delimited; having delimited; having broken; having broken; having broken up; having analyzed; having broken; having broken up.

Budha-ñāṇe, bujjha, sambujjha, abhisambujjha, bujjhiya, bujjhiyāna, “marīcikūpamaṃ abhisambuddhāno”ti pāḷi, dādese assa ottaṃ katvā siddhā yathā ‘anupādiyāno’ti.

From the root `budh` in the sense of knowing: having awakened, having fully awakened, having completely awakened, having awakened, having awakened. The Pāḷi text is: ‘completely awakening to what is like a mirage.’ These forms are accomplished by changing `a` to `o` in the substitute `dā`, as in `anupādiyāno`.

Vadha-hiṃsāyaṃ[M 0.0509], vajjha, vajjhiya.

From the root `vadh` in the sense of harming: having killed, having killed.

Vidha-tāḷane, vijjha, vijjhiya.

From the root `vidh` in the sense of striking: having pierced, having pierced.

Khana-vilekhane, khañña, khaṇiya, nāssa ṇattaṃ.

From the root `khan` in the sense of digging: having dug, having dug. For this, there is no change of `n` to `ṇ`.

Pavagge –

In the P-Group:

Khippa, nikhippa, saṃkhippa, khipiya, saṃkhipiya.

Having thrown, having laid down, having summarized, having thrown, having summarized.

Labi-avasaṃsane, yalopo, ālamba, vilamba, avalamba.

From the root `lab` in the sense of hanging down, with elision of `ya`: having taken hold of, having delayed, having depended on.

Lubi-santhambhane, daṇḍamolumba tiṭṭhati, jhānamolumba vattati.

From the root `lub` in the sense of holding fast, as in: ‘He stands leaning on a staff’; ‘He continues leaning on jhāna.’

Upubbo uddharaṇe “ullumbatu maṃ bhante saṅgho”ti mahāva. 71 (ullumpatu) ādīsu viya, ullumba, ārabbha, samārabbha, labbhā, upalabbhā, dīgho.

Preceded by `u`, in the sense of lifting up, as in such cases as ‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha lift me up.’ Also: ullumba (having lifted up), ārabbha (having begun), samārabbha (having undertaken), labbhā (having obtained), upalabbhā (having acquired). The vowel is lengthened.

Pakkamma, akkamma, vikkamma, nikkhamma, okkamma, abhikkamma, atikkamma, paṭikkamma, āgamma, saṅgamma.

Having departed, having trodden upon, having strode forward, having gone out, having stepped down, having advanced, having transgressed, having stepped back, having come, having assembled.

Sama-upadhāraṇe. Nisamma rāja kayirā, nānisamma disampati jā. 1.4.128 (nisamma khattiyo).

From the root `sam` in the sense of careful examination, as in: ‘A king should act having carefully examined; a ruler of the land should not act without having carefully examined.’

Samu-santiyaṃ khede ca, upasamma, vūpasamma, vissamma.

From the root `sam` in the sense of peace and also fatigue: having become calm, having been allayed, having taken rest.

Kasa-kaḍḍhane, apakassa.

From the root `kas` in the sense of dragging: having dragged away.

Disa-pekkhane, ādissa, uddissa, odissa, apadissa.

From the root `dis` in the sense of pointing out: having pointed to, having aimed at, having specified, having referred to.

Phusa-samphasse. Phussa phussa byantīkaroti a. ni. 4.195.

From the root phus in the sense of contact, as in: ‘Having repeatedly touched, one brings to an end.’

Vasa-nivāse. Upavassaṃ kho pana kattikatemāsapuṇṇamaṃ pārā. 653 (kattikapuṇṇamaṃ), bindāgamo.

From the root vas in the sense of dwelling, as in: ‘having dwelt until the full moon of the three-month period ending in Kattika...’ There is an insertion of a nasal.

Visa-pavesane, pavissa, nivissa, abhinivissa iccādi.

From the root vis in the sense of entering: having entered, having settled down, having adhered to, and so on.

Iti tvādivikārarāsi.

Thus ends the section on the modifications of the suffixes tvā and so on.

Paccayavikārarāsi niṭṭhito.

The section on the modification of suffixes is finished.

Pakatirūparāsi

The Section on Unmodified Forms

Tādipaccayarāsi

The Section on the Suffixes ta and so on

Atha [M 0.0510] pakatirūparāsi vuccate.

Now the section on unmodified forms will be stated.

Ta,ti, tu, tavantu, tāvī, tvā, tvāna, tuna, tuṃ, tave, tāye, tabba.

The suffixes are: ta, ti, tu, tavantu, tāvī, tvā, tvāna, tuna, tuṃ, tave, tāye, tabba.

Dā, khyā, gā, ghā, ṭā, ṭhā, tā, thā, dā, dhā, pā, phā, bhā, mā, yā, lā, vā, sā, hā.

Dā, khyā, gā, ghā, ṭā, ṭhā, tā, thā, dā, dhā, pā, phā, bhā, mā, yā, lā, vā, sā, hā.

Akkhāto, svākkhāto, ākhyāto, vikhyāto.

Declared, well-declared, proclaimed, renowned.

‘Ū byañjanassā’ti kvaci īāgamo rasso ca, saṅgāyito, ghāyito, ñāto.

By the rule ‘Ū byañjanassā,’ there is sometimes the insertion of ī and also shortening, as in: recited, smelled, known.

‘Jyādīhi knā’ti nāpaccayo, jānito.

By the rule ‘Jyādīhi knā,’ the suffix is nā, as in: known.

Kārite-ñāpito, ñāpayito. Puttaṃ tāyati rakkhatīti tāto-pitā. Datto, dvittaṃ rassattañca. Devadatto, brahmadatto, yaññadatto, dāpito, dāpayito.

In the causative: made known, caused to be known. Because he protects and guards a son, he is a tāta—a father. Datto (given) is formed with doubling and shortening. For example: Devadatta, Brahmadatta, Yaññadatta. Also: caused to be given, caused to be given.

Mahāvuttinā passa pivo, pivito.

According to the Mahāvutti, see the forms pivo and pivito (drunk).

Phā-vuddhiyaṃ, phito pabhātā ratti.

From the root phā in the sense of increasing: phito (swollen, full), as in ‘The night has dawned.’

Mā-māne, mito, sammito, upamito, nimmito, yāto, lāto, vāto.

From the root mā in the sense of measuring: measured, equaled, compared, created. Also: gone, taken, blown.

Mahāvuttinā vāssuttaṃ, nibbuto, parinibbuto, nibbāpito, parinibbāpito, osito, pariyosito, osāpito, pariyosāpito, pahito, pajahito, hāpito.

According to the Mahāvutti, vā is changed to u. Examples: extinguished, completely extinguished, caused to be extinguished, caused to be completely extinguished, finished, completely finished, caused to be finished, caused to be completely finished, sent forth, abandoned, caused to be abandoned.

Timhi-ñatti, datti, pāti, phāti, nibbuti, parinibbuti.

With the suffix -ti: knowledge, giving, drinking, increase, extinction, complete extinction.

Tumhi-saṅkhātā sabbadhammānaṃ jā. 2.22.1451, akkhātāro tathāgatā dha. pa. 276 aññātāro bhavissanti dī. ni. 2.68, ñāpetā, ñāpayitā. Uṭṭhātā vindate dhanaṃ saṃ. ni. 1.246.

With the suffix -tu: a reckoner of all things; the Tathāgatas are proclaimers; they will be knowers; one who makes known; one who causes to know. ‘One who strives finds wealth.’

‘Ū lasse’ti [M 0.0511] kvaci īssa ettaṃ, uṭṭhāpetā, samuṭṭhāpetā, aghassa tātā, tāyitā, dātā, dāpetā, sandhātā, sandhāpetā, māpitā, māpayitā, nibbāpetā, nibbāpayitā, hāpetā, hāpayitā.

By the rule ‘Ū lasse,’ sometimes ī becomes e. Examples: one who causes to stand up, one who causes to arise; a protector from evil, a savior; a giver, one who causes to give; one who connects, one who causes to connect; one who causes to measure, one who causes to measure; one who causes to extinguish, one who causes to extinguish; one who causes to abandon, one who causes to abandon.

Tavantu, tāvīsu-akkhatā, akkhātāvī iccādi.

With the suffixes -tavantu and -tāvī: akkhātā (a proclaimer), akkhātāvī (one who has proclaimed), and so on.

Tvādīsu saṃyoge rassattaṃ, ñatvā, jānitvā, ñāpetvā, jānāpetvā, ṭhatvā.

With suffixes like -tvā, shortening occurs in a conjunct consonant: ñatvā (having known), jānitvā (having known), ñāpetvā (having made known), jānāpetvā (having caused to know), ṭhatvā (having stood).

Pādito ṭhāssa ṭhaho, saṇṭhahitvā, patiṭṭhahitvā.

After a prefix, ṭhaha is the substitute for the root ṭhā: saṇṭhahitvā (having established), patiṭṭhahitvā (having established).

Kārite kvaci rassattaṃ, ṭhapetvā, paṭṭhapetvā, patiṭṭhāpetvā, datvā, ādiyitvā, samādiyitvā, dajjitvā.

In the causative, shortening sometimes occurs: ṭhapetvā (having placed), paṭṭhapetvā (having set up), patiṭṭhāpetvā (having established), datvā (having given), ādiyitvā (having taken), samādiyitvā (having undertaken), dajjitvā (having given).

Dada-dāne, tvāssa pyo, yamhi dassa jo, yassa pubbarūpaṃ dīgho, dajjā, dāpetvā.

From the root dā (to give): tvā becomes pya; before ya, da becomes ja; the ya is assimilated to the preceding consonant, and there is lengthening. Examples: dajjā (one should give), dāpetvā (having caused to give).

Pādito rasso, samādapetvā.

After a prefix, shortening occurs: samādapetvā (having caused to undertake).

Dhā-dhāraṇe, dvittaṃ, pubbassa tatiyattaṃ rasso ca, parassa ‘dhāssa ho’ti ho, padahitvā, vidahitvā, nidahitvā, saddahitvā, odahitvā, pidahitvā, paridahitvā.

For the root dhā (to hold): there is reduplication; for the first part of the reduplication, the third consonant of the class and shortening occur; and for the second part, dhā becomes ha by the rule 'dhāssa ho.' Examples: padahitvā (having striven), vidahitvā (having arranged), nidahitvā (having deposited), saddahitvā (having believed), odahitvā (having applied), pidahitvā (having closed), paridahitvā (having put on).

Kārite-ādhapetvā, sannidhāpetvā, pivitvā, pitvā vā, pāyetvā, māpetvā, osāpetvā, pariyosāpetvā, hitvā, pajahitvā, hāpetvā, pajahāpetvā.

In the causative: ādhapetvā (having caused to place), sannidhāpetvā (having caused to deposit). Also: pivitvā or pitvā (having drunk), pāyetvā (having caused to drink), māpetvā (having caused to measure), osāpetvā (having caused to end), pariyosāpetvā (having caused to come to a complete end), hitvā (having abandoned), pajahitvā (having abandoned), hāpetvā (having caused to abandon), pajahāpetvā (having caused to abandon).

Tuṃ, tavesu-akkhātuṃ, akkhātave, saṅkhātuṃ, saṅkhātave, ñātuṃ, ñātave, jānituṃ, jānitave, ñāpetuṃ, ñāpetave, jānāpetuṃ, jānāpetave, ṭhātuṃ, ṭhātave, saṇṭhātuṃ, saṇṭhātave, saṇṭhahituṃ, saṇṭhahitave, ṭhapetuṃ, ṭhapetave, saṇṭhāpetuṃ, saṇṭhāpetave, dātuṃ, dātave, padātuṃ, padātave, ādātuṃ, ādātave, dajjituṃ, dajjitave, dāpetuṃ, dāpetave, samādapetuṃ, samādapetave, sandhātuṃ, sandhātave, saddahituṃ, saddahetuṃ, saddahetave, nidhetuṃ, nidhetave [M 0.0512] sandhāpetuṃ, nidhāpetuṃ, pātuṃ, pivituṃ, pātave, pivetave, mātuṃ, minituṃ, pametuṃ, upametuṃ, yātuṃ, yāyituṃ, yātave, osāyetuṃ, osāpetuṃ, pariyosāpetuṃ, hātuṃ, pahātuṃ, māradheyyaṃ pahātave dha. pa. 34, jahituṃ, pajahituṃ, hāpetuṃ, pahāpetuṃ, jahāpetuṃ.

With the suffixes -tuṃ and -tave: akkhātuṃ, akkhātave (to proclaim); saṅkhātuṃ, saṅkhātave (to reckon); ñātuṃ, ñātave (to know); jānituṃ, jānitave (to know); ñāpetuṃ, ñāpetave (to make known); jānāpetuṃ, jānāpetave (to cause to know); ṭhātuṃ, ṭhātave (to stand); saṇṭhātuṃ, saṇṭhātave (to be established); saṇṭhahituṃ, saṇṭhahitave (to be established); ṭhapetuṃ, ṭhapetave (to place); saṇṭhāpetuṃ, saṇṭhāpetave (to establish); dātuṃ, dātave (to give); padātuṃ, padātave (to bestow); ādātuṃ, ādātave (to take); dajjituṃ, dajjitave (to give); dāpetuṃ, dāpetave (to cause to give); samādapetuṃ, samādapetave (to cause to undertake); sandhātuṃ, sandhātave (to connect); saddahituṃ, saddahetuṃ, saddahetave (to believe); nidhetuṃ, nidhetave (to deposit); sandhāpetuṃ (to cause to connect); nidhāpetuṃ (to cause to deposit); pātuṃ, pivituṃ (to drink); pātave, pivetave (to drink); mātuṃ, minituṃ (to measure); pametuṃ, upametuṃ (to compare); yātuṃ, yāyituṃ, yātave (to go); osāyetuṃ, osāpetuṃ (to cause to end); pariyosāpetuṃ (to cause to come to a complete end); hātuṃ, pahātuṃ (to abandon); māradheyyaṃ pahātave (to abandon the realm of Māra); jahituṃ, pajahituṃ (to abandon); hāpetuṃ, pahāpetuṃ (to cause to abandon); jahāpetuṃ (to cause to abandon).

Tabbamhi-akkhātabbaṃ, saṅkhātabbaṃ, saṅkhyātabbaṃ, gāyitabbaṃ, ñātabbaṃ, jānitabbaṃ, ñāpetabbaṃ, jānāpetabbaṃ, ṭhātabbaṃ, ṭhapetabbaṃ, dātabbaṃ, ādātabbaṃ, samādātabbaṃ, dāpetabbaṃ, samādapetabbaṃ, vidhātabbaṃ, vidahitabbaṃ, pātabbaṃ, pivitabbaṃ, minitabbaṃ, minetabbaṃ, yātabbaṃ, lātabbaṃ, pahātabbaṃ.

With the suffix `-tabba`: to be proclaimed; to be reckoned; to be reckoned; to be sung; to be known; to be known; to be made known; to be caused to be known; to be stood upon; to be placed; to be given; to be taken; to be undertaken; to be caused to be given; to be caused to be undertaken; to be arranged; to be arranged; to be drunk; to be drunk; to be measured; to be measured; to be gone to; to be obtained; to be abandoned.

Ivaṇṇesu vipubbo i-gatyaṃ, vīto, vītadoso vītamoho saṃ. ni. 1.249, udito, samudito, dāgamo.

Among roots ending in `-i`: for the root `i` (to go) with the prefix `vi-`: `vīto` (devoid of), as in `vītadoso` (free from hatred), `vītamoho` (free from delusion). With the prefix `ud-`: `udito` (arisen), `samudito` (fully arisen), with the augment `d`.

Samito, sameto, samaveto, apeto, upeto, samupeto, abhito, kīto, kayito, kiṇito, cito, cinito, ācito, upacito, sañcito, jito, parājito, ḍito, oḍḍito, nīto, ānīto, vinīto, oṇīto, paṇīto, nassa ṇattaṃ.

`samito` (pacified); `sameto` (assembled); `samaveto` (combined); `apeto` (departed); `upeto` (endowed with); `samupeto` (fully endowed with); `abhito` (approached); `kīto`, `kayito`, `kiṇito` (bought); `cito`, `cinito` (piled up); `ācito`, `upacito`, `sañcito` (accumulated); `jito` (conquered); `parājito` (defeated); `ḍito`, `oḍḍito` (flown); `nīto` (led); `ānīto` (brought); `vinīto` (trained); `oṇīto` (removed); `paṇīto` (excellent), where `n` becomes `ṇ`.

Pīto, bhīto, mito, sito, nissito, pahito.

`pīto` (drunk); `bhīto` (frightened); `mito` (measured); `sito` (dependent); `nissito` (dependent on); `pahito` (sent).

Timhi-samiti, viciti, nīti, dvitte ādivuddhi, netti, saddhammanetti, bhīti.

With the suffix `-ti`: `samiti` (assembly), `viciti` (investigation), `nīti` (guidance). When a double consonant follows, there is `vuddhi` of the initial vowel, as in `netti` (guidance), `saddhammanetti` (the guide to the true Dhamma). Also, `bhīti` (fear).

Tumhi-sametā, abhisametā, vicetā, jetā, netā, vinetā, ninnetā.

With the suffix `-tu` (forming agent nouns): `sametā` (one who assembles), `abhisametā` (one who fully understands), `vicetā` (one who investigates), `jetā` (a conqueror), `netā` (a leader), `vinetā` (a trainer), `ninnetā` (one who leads out).

Tavantu, tāvīsu-sametavā, sametāvī, abhisametavā, abhisametāvī iccādi.

With the suffixes `-tavantu` and `-tāvī`: `sametavā`, `sametāvī` (one who has assembled); `abhisametavā`, `abhisametāvī` (one who has fully understood), and so on.

Tvādīsu-sametvā, upetvā, kiṇitvā, vicinitvā, jetvā, vijetvā, jinitvā, vijinitvā, parājetvā, netvā, ānetvā [M 0.0513] vinetvā, nayitvā, ānayitvā, vinayitvā, allīyitvā, paṭisallīyitvā, sayitvā.

With suffixes like `-tvā`: `sametvā` (having assembled), `upetvā` (having approached), `kiṇitvā` (having bought), `vicinitvā` (having investigated), `jetvā` (having conquered), `vijetvā` (having thoroughly conquered), `jinitvā` (having conquered), `vijinitvā` (having thoroughly conquered), `parājetvā` (having defeated), `netvā` (having led), `ānetvā` (having brought), `vinetvā` (having trained), `nayitvā` (having led), `ānayitvā` (having brought), `vinayitvā` (having trained), `allīyitvā` (having adhered), `paṭisallīyitvā` (having gone into seclusion), `sayitvā` (having lain down).

Tuṃ, tavesu-sametuṃ, upetuṃ, samupetuṃ, sametave, ketuṃ, kiṇituṃ, ketave, vicetuṃ, vicinituṃ, jetuṃ, vijetuṃ, nituṃ, ānituṃ, vinituṃ, netuṃ, ānetuṃ, vinetuṃ, nayituṃ, ānayituṃ, vinayituṃ, netave.

With the suffixes `-tuṃ` and `-tave`: `sametuṃ` (to assemble), `upetuṃ` (to approach), `samupetuṃ` (to approach together), `sametave` (to assemble); `ketuṃ` (to buy), `kiṇituṃ` (to buy), `ketave` (to buy); `vicetuṃ`, `vicinituṃ` (to investigate); `jetuṃ`, `vijetuṃ` (to conquer); `nituṃ` (to lead), `ānituṃ` (to bring), `vinituṃ` (to train); `netuṃ` (to lead), `ānetuṃ` (to bring), `vinetuṃ` (to train); `nayituṃ` (to lead), `ānayituṃ` (to bring), `vinayituṃ` (to train); `netave` (to lead).

Tabbamhi-sametabbaṃ, ketabbaṃ, kiṇitabbaṃ iccādi.

With the suffix `-tabba`: `sametabbaṃ` (to be assembled), `ketabbaṃ` (to be bought), `kiṇitabbaṃ` (to be bought), and so on.

Uvaṇṇesu-cuto, cavito.

Among roots ending in `-u`: `cuto`, `cavito` (fallen, departed).

Kārite-cāvito.

In the causative: `cāvito` (caused to fall away, removed).

Juto, javito, thuto, abhitthuto, abhitthavito,

`juto`, `javito` (impelled); `thuto` (praised); `abhitthuto`, `abhitthavito` (highly praised).

Saṃpubbo dhu-vallabhe, sandhuto-mitto. “Asaṇṭhutaṃ cirasaṇṭhutenā”tipi pāḷi.

The root `dhu` with the prefix `saṃ-` has the meaning 'intimate.' Thus, `sandhuta` means 'a friend.' There is also the Pāli phrase: 'the unacquainted with the long-acquainted.'

Du-gatiyaṃ hiṃsāyañca, duto, upadduto.

The root `du` means 'to go' and 'to harm.' Examples: `duto` (afflicted), `upadduto` (oppressed).

Dhū-kampane, dhuto, niddhuto.

The root `dhū` means 'to shake.' Examples: `dhuto` (shaken), `niddhuto` (shaken off).

Bhūto, sambhūto.

`bhūto` (become; a being), `sambhūto` (come into being).

Kārite-bhāvito, sambhāvito, vibhāvito, paribhāvito.

In the causative: `bhāvito` (developed), `sambhāvito` (esteemed), `vibhāvito` (made clear), `paribhāvito` (imbued with).

Yu-missane, saṃyuto.

The root `yu` means 'to mix.' Example: `saṃyuto` (joined).

Ru-sadde, ruto, luto, vuto, saṃvuto, susaṃvuto, suto, vissuto.

The root `ru` means 'to make a sound.' Examples: `ruto` (sounded); `luto` (cut); `vuto` (restrained); `saṃvuto` (restrained); `susaṃvuto` (well-restrained); `suto` (heard); `vissuto` (renowned).

Hu-pūjāyaṃ, huto.

The root `hu` means 'to sacrifice.' Example: `huto` (offered in sacrifice).

Timhi-cavanaṃ cuti, thavanaṃ thuti, bhūti, vibhūti, savanaṃ suti,

With the suffix `-ti`: `cuti` (death) is the act of passing away (`cavanaṃ`); `thuti` (praise) is the act of praising (`thavanaṃ`); `bhūti` (prosperity); `vibhūti` (power); `suti` (hearing) is the act of hearing (`savanaṃ`).

Tumhi-cavitā, cāvetā, javitā, thavitā, santhavitā, sotā, sāvetā.

With the suffix `-tu`: `cavitā` (one who passes away), `cāvetā` (one who causes to pass away), `javitā` (one who impels), `thavitā` (a praiser), `santhavitā` (an extoller), `sotā` (a hearer), `sāvetā` (one who causes to hear).

Tavantu [M 0.0514] tāvīsu-cutavā, cutāvī, cāvetavā, cāvetāvī iccādi.

With the suffixes `-tavantu` and `-tāvī`: `cutavā`, `cutāvī` (one who has passed away); `cāvetavā`, `cāvetāvī` (one who has caused to pass away), and so on.

Tvādīsu-cavitvā, cavitvāna, cavituna, javitvā, abhitthavitvā, bhutvā, anubhavitvā, bhāvetvā, bhāvayitvā, sutvā, suṇitvā, sāvetvā, sāvayitvā.

With suffixes like `-tvā`: `cavitvā`, `cavitvāna`, `cavituna` (having passed away); `javitvā` (having hastened); `abhitthavitvā` (having highly praised); `bhutvā` (having become); `anubhavitvā` (having experienced); `bhāvetvā`, `bhāvayitvā` (having developed); `sutvā`, `suṇitvā` (having heard); `sāvetvā`, `sāvayitvā` (having caused to hear).

Tuṃ, tavesu-cavituṃ, cāvetuṃ, bhotuṃ, bhavituṃ, anubhavituṃ, bhāvetuṃ, bhāvayituṃ, sotuṃ, sāvetuṃ.

With the suffixes `-tuṃ` and `-tave`: `cavituṃ` (to pass away), `cāvetuṃ` (to cause to pass away), `bhotuṃ` or `bhavituṃ` (to be, to become), `anubhavituṃ` (to experience), `bhāvetuṃ` or `bhāvayituṃ` (to develop), `sotuṃ` (to hear), `sāvetuṃ` (to cause to hear).

Hū-sattāyaṃ, hotuṃ. “Yā icche puriso hotuṃ jā. 2.22.1282. Na so sakkā na hotuye”ti bu. vaṃ. 2.9 ‘…hetuye’ pāḷī.

The root `hū` means 'to be.' Example: `hotuṃ` (to be). There is the Pāli phrase: 'Whatever a person might wish to be, it is not possible for him not to be.'

Tabbamhi-cavitabbaṃ, bhavitabbaṃ, anubhavitabbaṃ, bhāvetabbaṃ, sotabbaṃ. Dvitte-sottabbaṃ, sāvetabbaṃ.

With the suffix `-tabba`: `cavitabbaṃ` (should be passed away from), `bhavitabbaṃ` (what should be), `anubhavitabbaṃ` (to be experienced), `bhāvetabbaṃ` (to be developed), `sotabbaṃ` (to be heard). With a double consonant: `sottabbaṃ` (to be heard), `sāvetabbaṃ` (to be caused to be heard).

Edantesu mahāvuttinā kvaci ekārassa ittaṃ, gāyito, apacāyito, apacito vā, ujjhāyito, nijjhāyito, abhijjhāyito.

Among roots ending in `-e`, according to the Mahāvutti, the `e` sometimes becomes `i`. Examples: `gāyito` (sung); `apacāyito` or `apacito` (honored); `ujjhāyito` (grumbled at); `nijjhāyito` (reflected upon); `abhijjhāyito` (coveted).

Gāyanaṃ gīti, apacāyanaṃ apaciti.

`gīti` (a song) is the act of singing (`gāyanaṃ`); `apaciti` (respect) is the act of honoring (`apacāyanaṃ`).

Tumhi-gāyitā, apacāyitā, ujjhāyitā.

With the suffix `-tu`: `gāyitā` (a singer), `apacāyitā` (one who honors), `ujjhāyitā` (one who grumbles).

Tavantu, tāvīsu-gāyitavā, gāyitāvī iccādi.

With the suffixes `tavantu` and `tāvī`: `gāyitavā` (one who has sung), `gāyitāvī` (a singer), and so on.

Gāyitvā, jhāyitvā, abhijjhāyitvā.

Having sung, having meditated, having coveted.

Gāyituṃ, gāyitave, apacāyituṃ, apacāyitave, jhāyituṃ, jhāyitave, abhijjhāyituṃ, abhijjhāyitave.

To sing, for singing; to revere, for revering; to meditate, for meditating; to covet, for coveting.

Gāyitabbaṃ, apacāyitabbaṃ, ujjhāyitabbaṃ.

What should be sung, what should be revered, what should be grumbled at.

Iti ekabyañjanadhātūnaṃ pakatirūparāsi.

Thus is the collection of natural forms of roots with a single consonant.

Bhūvādigaṇa

The Bhū Group

Anekabyañjanadhātūnaṃ [M 0.0515] pakatirūpāni tyādikaṇḍe vibhāganayena bhūvādīhi sattahi dhātugaṇehi ca kāritapaccayehi ca dhātupaccayehi ca yathālābhaṃ vibhajitvā vitthāretabbāni.

The natural forms of roots with more than one consonant, in the section beginning with `ti`, should be elaborated by dividing them according to the method of division by the seven root groups beginning with `bhū`, by causative suffixes, and by root suffixes, as they are found.

Atridaṃ nayadassanaṃ –

Here is an illustration of the method:

Āsa, isa, gamu, disa.

Āsa, isa, gamu, disa.

Āsa-upavesane, cchādesasutte ‘nta māna tyādīsū’ti adhikatattā tapaccayesucchādeso natthi, garuṃ upāsito, payirupāsito.

The root `ās` is in the sense of 'to sit.' In the rule concerning the substitution of `ccha`, because of its inclusion in the list beginning with `nta`, `māna`, `ti`, etc., there is no substitution of `ccha` before the `ta`-suffixes. For example: `garuṃ upāsito` (he has attended upon a teacher), `payirupāsito` (he has served).

Tumhi-upāsitā, upāsetā vā, upāsitavā, upāsitāvī, upāsitvā, upāsitvāna, upāsituna. ‘Pyo vā tvāssa samāse’ti pyādese-upāsiya, payirupāsiya, upasiyāna, upāsituṃ, upāsitave, upāsitabbo.

With the `tu` suffix: `upāsitā` or `upāsetā` (one who serves); `upāsitavā` (one who has served); `upāsitāvī` (one who serves); `upāsitvā`, `upāsitvāna`, `upāsituna` (absolutives). With the substitution of `pya` by the rule '`pyo vā tvāssa samāse`': `upāsiya`, `payirupāsiya`, `upasiyāna`. Infinitives: `upāsituṃ`, `upāsitave`. Gerundive: `upāsitabbo`.

Isu-icchā, kantīsu, bahulādhikārā cchādeso, icchito, icchitā, icchitavā, icchitāvī, icchituṃ, icchitave, icchitabbaṃ.

The root `is` is in the senses of 'desire' and 'longing.' The substitution of `ccha` occurs frequently. Forms: `icchito` (desired), `icchitā` (one who desires), `icchitavā` (one who has desired), `icchitāvī` (one who desires), `icchituṃ` and `icchitave` (to desire), `icchitabbaṃ` (what should be desired).

Kārite-icchāpito, icchāpitā, icchāpitāvī, icchāpetvā, icchāpetuṃ, icchāpetave, icchāpetabbaṃ.

In the causative: `icchāpito` (caused to desire), `icchāpitā` (one who causes to desire), `icchāpitāvī` (one who causes to desire), `icchāpetvā` (having caused to desire), `icchāpetuṃ` and `icchāpetave` (to cause to desire), `icchāpetabbaṃ` (what should be caused to desire).

Esadhātumhi-esito, pariyesito, esitā, pariyesitā, esitavā, pariyesitavā, esitvā, pariyesitvā, esitvāna, pariyesitvāna, esituṃ, pariyesituṃ, esitave, pariyesitave, esitabbaṃ, pariyesitabbaṃ.

With the root `es`: `esito` (sought), `pariyesito` (searched for); `esitā` (one who seeks), `pariyesitā` (one who searches for); `esitavā` (one who has sought), `pariyesitavā` (one who has searched for); `esitvā` and `esitvāna` (having sought), `pariyesitvā` and `pariyesitvāna` (having searched for); `esituṃ` and `esitave` (to seek), `pariyesituṃ` and `pariyesitave` (to search for); `esitabbaṃ` (what should be sought), `pariyesitabbaṃ` (what should be searched for).

Gamu-gatimhi, gamito, gamitā, gamitavā, gamitāvī, gamitvā, gamitvāna, gamituna, gamituṃ, gamitave, gamitabbaṃ.

The root `gam` is in the sense of 'to go.' Causative forms: `gamito` (caused to go), `gamitā` (one who causes to go), `gamitavā` (one who has caused to go), `gamitāvī` (one who causes to go); `gamitvā`, `gamitvāna`, `gamituna` (having caused to go); `gamituṃ`, `gamitave` (to cause to go); `gamitabbaṃ` (what should be caused to go).

Kārite-gamāpito, gamāpetā iccādi.

In the double causative: `gamāpito` (caused to make go), `gamāpetā` (one who causes to make go), and so on.

Disa-pekkhane [M 0.0516] passito, passitā, passetā vā, passitvā, passitvāna, passituna, passituṃ, passitave, passitabbaṃ.

The root `dis` is in the sense of 'to see.' Forms from the stem `passa`: `passito` (seen), `passitā` or `passetā` (one who sees/will see), `passitvā`, `passitvāna`, `passituna` (having seen), `passituṃ`, `passitave` (to see), `passitabbaṃ` (what should be seen).

Kārite-dassito, dassayito, dassitā, dassetā, dassayitā, dassitavā, dassitāvī, dassetvā, dassayitvā, dassetvāna, dassayitvāna, dassetuṃ, dassayituṃ, dassetabbaṃ.

In the causative: `dassito`, `dassayito` (shown); `dassitā`, `dassetā`, `dassayitā` (one who shows); `dassitavā`, `dassitāvī` (one who has shown); `dassetvā`, `dassayitvā`, `dassetvāna`, `dassayitvāna` (having shown); `dassetuṃ`, `dassayituṃ` (to show); `dassetabbaṃ` (what should be shown).

Dakkhādese-dakkhito, dakkhitā, dakkhitavā, dakkhitāvī, dakkhitvā, dakkhituṃ, dakkhitave, “dakkhitāye aparājitasaṅgha”nti dī. ni. 2.332 pāḷi, dakkhitabbaṃ.

When `dakkha` is the substitute: `dakkhito` (seen), `dakkhitā` (one who sees), `dakkhitavā` (one who has seen), `dakkhitāvī` (one who sees), `dakkhitvā` (having seen), `dakkhituṃ` and `dakkhitave` (to see). The Pāli text gives the example: `dakkhitāye aparājitasaṅgha` ('for the unconquered Saṅgha to see'). Also: `dakkhitabbaṃ` (what should be seen).

Dusa-nāse, kārite ṇipaccaye –

The root `dus` is in the sense of 'to be corrupt.' In the causative, with the `ṇi` suffix:

764. Ṇimhi dīgho dusassa ka. 486; rū. 543; nī. 977.

764. The vowel of `dus` is lengthened before `ṇi`.

Ṇimhi pare dusassa dīgho hoti.

When `ṇi` follows, the vowel of `dus` is lengthened.

Dūsito, dūsitā, dūsetā, dūsitavā, dūsitāvī, dūsetvā, dūsetvāna, dūsituna, dūsetuṃ, dūsetave.

Forms: `dūsito` (corrupted), `dūsitā` (one who corrupts), `dūsetā` (one who will corrupt), `dūsitavā` (one who has corrupted), `dūsitāvī` (one who corrupts); `dūsetvā`, `dūsetvāna`, `dūsituna` (having corrupted); `dūsetuṃ`, `dūsetave` (to corrupt).

Ṇimhīti kiṃ? Duṭṭho.

Why specify 'before `ṇi`'? To exclude cases like `duṭṭho` (corrupted).

Iti bhūvādigaṇo.

Thus ends the Bhū Group.

Rudhādigaṇa

The Rudh Group

Bhuja, yuja, chida, bhida, rudha.

Bhuja, yuja, chida, bhida, rudha.

765. Maṃ vā rudhādīnaṃ ka. 446; rū. 509; nī. 926.

765. A nasal infix is optionally inserted in the roots of the Rudh group.

Rudhādīnaṃ pubbantasarā paraṃ mānubandho niggahītāgamo hoti vā.

For the roots of the Rudh group, a `niggahīta` is optionally inserted after the root vowel.

Bhuñjito, bhuñjitā, bhuñjitavā, bhuñjitāvī, bhuñjitvā, bhuñjitvāna, bhuñjituna, bhuñjituṃ, bhuñjitave, bhuñjitabbaṃ.

Bhuñjito (eaten); bhuñjitā (one who eats); bhuñjitavā (one who has eaten); bhuñjitāvī (one who eats); bhuñjitvā, bhuñjitvāna, bhuñjituna (having eaten); bhuñjituṃ, bhuñjitave (to eat); bhuñjitabbaṃ (to be eaten).

Kārite-bhojito[M 0.0517], bhojitā, bhojetā vā, bhojitavā, bhojitāvī, bhojetvā, bhojayitvā, bhojetuṃ, bhojetave, bhojetabbaṃ, yuñjito, anuyuñjito, bhujadhātusadisaṃ.

In the causative: bhojito (fed); bhojitā or bhojetā (one who feeds); bhojitavā (one who has fed); bhojitāvī (one who feeds); bhojetvā, bhojayitvā (having fed); bhojetuṃ, bhojetave (to feed); bhojetabbaṃ (to be fed). The forms yuñjito (yoked) and anuyuñjito (enjoined) are similar to those from the root `bhuj`.

Chindito, chinditā, chindetā vā, chinditavā, chinditāvī, chinditvā, chinditvāna, chindituna. Pyādese-lataṃ dantehi chindiya gavesitabbaṃ, chindiyāna, sañchindiya, sañchindiyāna, chinditabbaṃ.

Chindito (cut); chinditā or chindetā (one who cuts); chinditavā (one who has cut); chinditāvī (one who cuts); chinditvā, chinditvāna, chindituna (having cut). When `ya` is substituted: 'lataṃ dantehi chindiya' (having cut the creeper with the teeth), chindiyāna, sañchindiya, sañchindiyāna. The gerundive is chinditabbaṃ (to be cut).

Kārite-chindāpito, chindāpetā iccādi.

In the causative: chindāpito (caused to cut), chindāpetā (one who causes to cut), and so on.

Bhindito, bhinditā, bhindetā vā, chidadhātusadisaṃ.

Bhindito (broken), bhinditā or bhindetā (one who breaks); the forms are similar to those from the root `chid`.

Rundhito, rundhitā, rundhetā, rundhitavā, rundhitāvī, rundhitvā, rundhitvāna, rundhituṃ, rundhitave, rundhitabbaṃ.

Rundhito (obstructed); rundhitā, rundhetā (one who obstructs); rundhitavā (one who has obstructed); rundhitāvī (one who obstructs); rundhitvā, rundhitvāna (having obstructed); rundhituṃ, rundhitave (to obstruct); rundhitabbaṃ (to be obstructed).

Kārite-rundhāpito, rundhāpayito iccādi.

In the causative: rundhāpito, rundhāpayito (caused to obstruct), and so on.

Iti rudhādigaṇo.

Thus ends the Rudhādi group.

Divādigaṇa

The Divādi Group

Pada, budha, tusa, divu.

The roots `pad` (to go), `budh` (to know), `tus` (to be pleased), `div` (to play).

766. Padādīnaṃ kvaci.

766. For the roots `pad` and so on, in some cases.

Padādīnaṃ kvaci yuka hoti, yāgamo, ‘tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā’ti cavaggattaṃ, ‘vaggalasehi te’ti yassa pubbarūpattaṃ.

For roots such as `pad`, the suffix `ya` is sometimes used, with the augment `y`. By the rule 'tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā,' there is a change to a palatal consonant. By the rule 'vaggalasehi te,' the `y` is assimilated to the preceding consonant.

Pajjito, āpajjito, paṭipajjito, paṭipajjitā, paṭipajjitavā, paṭipajjitāvī, paṭipajjitvā, paṭipajjitvāna, paṭipajjituna, paṭipajjituṃ, paṭipajjitave, paṭipajjitabbaṃ.

Pajjito (entered upon); āpajjito (incurred); paṭipajjito (practiced); paṭipajjitā (one who practices); paṭipajjitavā (one who has practiced); paṭipajjitāvī (one who practices); paṭipajjitvā, paṭipajjitvāna, paṭipajjituna (having practiced); paṭipajjituṃ, paṭipajjitave (to practice); paṭipajjitabbaṃ (should be practiced).

Kārite-āpādito, uppādito, nipphādito, sampādito, paṭipādito, āpāditā, āpādetā, uppāditā, anuppannassa [M 0.0518] maggassa uppādetā apa. therī 2.3.135, nipphāditā, nipphādetā, sampāditā, sampādetā, paṭipāditā, paṭipādetā, āpādetvā, uppādetvā, nipphādetvā, sampādetvā, paṭipādetvā, āpādetuṃ, uppādetuṃ, nipphādetuṃ, sampādetuṃ, paṭipādetuṃ, āpādetabbaṃ, uppādetabbaṃ, nipphādetabbaṃ, sampādetabbaṃ, paṭipādetabbaṃ, bujjhito, bujjhitā saccānīti buddho mahāni. 192, bujjhitavā, bujjhitāvī, bujjhitvā, bujjhitvāna, bujjhituna, bujjhituṃ, bujjhitave, bujjhitabbaṃ.

In the causative: āpādito: produced; uppādito: brought forth; nipphādito: perfected; sampādito: accomplished; paṭipādito: provided; āpāditā: one who has produced; āpādetā: one who produces; uppāditā: one who has brought forth; anuppannassa maggassa uppādetā: one who brings forth the unarisen path; nipphāditā: one who has perfected; nipphādetā: one who perfects; sampāditā: one who has accomplished; sampādetā: one who accomplishes; paṭipāditā: one who has provided; paṭipādetā: one who provides; āpādetvā: having produced; uppādetvā: having brought forth; nipphādetvā: having perfected; sampādetvā: having accomplished; paṭipādetvā: having provided; āpādetuṃ: to produce; uppādetuṃ: to bring forth; nipphādetuṃ: to perfect; sampādetuṃ: to accomplish; paṭipādetuṃ: to provide; āpādetabbaṃ: should be produced; uppādetabbaṃ: should be brought forth; nipphādetabbaṃ: should be perfected; sampādetabbaṃ: should be accomplished; paṭipādetabbaṃ: should be provided. Bujjito: awakened, understood; bujjhitā saccānīti buddho: one who has understood the truths, hence ‘Buddha’; bujjhitavā: one who has awakened; bujjhitāvī: one who has awakened; bujjhitvā: having awakened; bujjhitvāna: having awakened; bujjhituna: to awaken; bujjhituṃ: to awaken; bujjhitave: to awaken; bujjhitabbaṃ: should be awakened or understood.

Kārite-bodhito, bodhetā pajāyāti buddho mahāni. 192, bodhetavā, bodhetāvī, bodhayitvā, bodhayitvāna, bodhetuṃ, bodhetave, bodhetabbaṃ, tussito, santussito, tussitā, tussitavā, tussitāvī, tussitvā, tussituṃ, tussitabbaṃ.

In the causative: bodhito: caused to awaken; bodhetā pajāyāti buddho: one who awakens beings, hence ‘Buddha’; bodhetavā: one who has caused to awaken; bodhetāvī: one who has caused to awaken; bodhayitvā: having caused to awaken; bodhayitvāna: having caused to awaken; bodhetuṃ: to cause to awaken; bodhetave: to cause to awaken; bodhetabbaṃ: should be caused to awaken. Tussito: pleased; santussito: contented; tussitā: one who is pleased; tussitavā: one who has been pleased; tussitāvī: one who has been pleased; tussitvā: having been pleased; tussituṃ: to be pleased; tussitabbaṃ: should be pleased.

Kārite-tosito, tositā, tosetā vā, tositavā, tositāvī, tosetvā, tosetuṃ, tosetabbaṃ, dibbito, dibbitā, dibbitavā, dibbitāvī, dibbitvā, dibbituṃ, dibbitabbaṃ.

In the causative: tosito: caused to be pleased; tositā: one who has been caused to be pleased; tosetā vā: or, one who causes pleasure; tositavā: one who has caused to be pleased; tositāvī: one who has caused to be pleased; tosetvā: having caused to be pleased; tosetuṃ: to cause to be pleased; tosetabbaṃ: should be caused to be pleased. Dibbito: played; dibbitā: one who plays; dibbitavā: one who has played; dibbitāvī: one who has played; dibbitvā: having played; dibbituṃ: to play; dibbitabbaṃ: should be played.

Iti divādigaṇo.

Thus ends the Divādi group.

Svādigaṇa

The Svādi Group

Su, vu, āpa.

Su, vu, āpa.

Suṇito, suṇitā, sotā vā, suṇitavā, suṇitāvī, suṇitvā, suṇituṃ, suṇitabbaṃ.

Suṇito: heard; suṇitā: one who hears; sotā vā: or, a hearer; suṇitavā: one who has heard; suṇitāvī: one who has heard; suṇitvā: having heard; suṇituṃ: to hear; suṇitabbaṃ: should be heard.

Kārite-sāvito, sāvetā, sāvetavā, sāvetāvī, sāvetvā, sāvetuṃ, sāvetabbaṃ, saṃvuṇito, āvuṇito, saṃvuṇitā, saṃvuṇitvā, saṃvuṇituṃ, saṃvuṇitabbaṃ, pāpuṇito, pariyāpuṇito, pāpuṇitā, pariyāpuṇitā, pāpuṇitavā, pariyāpuṇitavā, pāpuṇitāvī, pariyāpuṇitāvī, pāpuṇitvā [M 0.0519] pariyāpuṇitvā, pāpuṇituṃ, pariyāpuṇituṃ, pāpuṇitabbo, pariyāpuṇitabbo.

In the causative: sāvito: caused to hear, announced; sāvetā: one who causes to hear, an announcer; sāvetavā: one who has caused to hear; sāvetāvī: one who has caused to hear; sāvetvā: having caused to hear; sāvetuṃ: to cause to hear; sāvetabbaṃ: should be caused to hear. Saṃvuṇito: covered, restrained; āvuṇito: covered; saṃvuṇitā: one who has restrained; saṃvuṇitvā: having restrained; saṃvuṇituṃ: to restrain; saṃvuṇitabbaṃ: should be restrained. Pāpuṇito: attained; pariyāpuṇito: mastered; pāpuṇitā: one who has attained; pariyāpuṇitā: one who has mastered; pāpuṇitavā: one who has attained; pariyāpuṇitavā: one who has mastered; pāpuṇitāvī: one who has attained; pariyāpuṇitāvī: one who has mastered; pāpuṇitvā: having attained; pariyāpuṇitvā: having mastered; pāpuṇituṃ: to attain; pariyāpuṇituṃ: to master; pāpuṇitabbo: should be attained; pariyāpuṇitabbo: should be mastered.

Kārite-pāpito, pāpitā, pāpetā vā, pāpetvā, pāpetuṃ iccādi.

In the causative: pāpito: caused to attain; pāpitā: one who has caused to attain; pāpetā vā: or, one who causes to attain; pāpetvā: having caused to attain; pāpetuṃ: to cause to attain, and so on.

Iti svādigaṇo.

Thus ends the Svādi group.

Kiyādigaṇo ekabyañjanesu vutto eva.

The Kiyādi group has already been discussed in the section on single-consonant roots.

Tanādigaṇa

The Tanādi Group

Kara, tana.

Kara: to do; tana: to spread.

‘Karotissa kho’ti kassa kho, abhisaṅkharito, abhisaṅkharitā, abhisaṅkharitavā, abhisaṅkharitāvī, karitvā, karitvāna, abhisaṅkharitvā, abhisaṅkharitvāna, abhisaṅkharituṃ, abhisaṅkharitabbaṃ.

‘Karotissa kho’ti kassa kho: ‘whose doing is it indeed?’ Abhisaṅkharito: formed, prepared; abhisaṅkharitā: one who forms; abhisaṅkharitavā: one who has formed; abhisaṅkharitāvī: one who has formed; karitvā: having done; karitvāna: having done; abhisaṅkharitvā: having formed; abhisaṅkharitvāna: having formed; abhisaṅkharituṃ: to form; abhisaṅkharitabbaṃ: should be formed.

Kārite-kārito, kārāpito, kāritā, kāretā, kārāpitā, kārāpetā, kāritavā, kāritāvī, kāretvā, kārāpetvā, kāretuṃ, kārāpetuṃ, kāretabbaṃ, kārāpetabbaṃ.

In the causative: kārito: caused to be done; kārāpito: caused to be done; kāritā: one who has caused to do; kāretā: one who causes to do; kārāpitā: one who has caused to be done; kārāpetā: one who causes to be done; kāritavā: one who has caused to do; kāritāvī: one who has caused to do; kāretvā: having caused to do; kārāpetvā: having caused to be done; kāretuṃ: to cause to do; kārāpetuṃ: to cause to be done; kāretabbaṃ: should be caused to do; kārāpetabbaṃ: should be caused to be done.

Tanito, tanitvā, tanituṃ iccādi.

Tanito: stretched; tanitvā: having stretched; tanituṃ: to stretch, and so on.

Iti tanādigaṇo.

Thus ends the Tanādi group.

Curādigaṇa

The Curādi Group

Kappa, cinta, cura, vida.

Kappa: to arrange, to think; cinta: to think; cura: to steal; vida: to experience.

Kappa-saṅkappane, kappito, saṅkappito, kappayito, saṅkappetā, saṅkappayitā, kappetavā, kappetāvī, kappetvā, kappayitvā, kappetuṃ, kappayituṃ, kappetabbaṃ, kappayitabbaṃ.

The root `kappa` is in the sense of planning. Kappito: planned; saṅkappito: thought out; kappayito: planned; saṅkappetā: one who plans; saṅkappayitā: one who plans; kappetavā: one who has planned; kappetāvī: one who has planned; kappetvā: having planned; kappayitvā: having planned; kappetuṃ: to plan; kappayituṃ: to plan; kappetabbaṃ: should be planned; kappayitabbaṃ: should be planned.

Kārite-kappāpito [M 0.0520] iccādi.

In the causative: kappāpito: caused to be planned, and so on.

Cintito, cintayito, cintetā, cintayitā, cintitavā, cintitāvī, cintetvā, cintayitvā, cintituṃ, cintetuṃ, cintayituṃ, cintitabbaṃ, cintetabbaṃ.

Cintito: thought; cintayito: thought; cintetā: one who thinks; cintayitā: one who thinks; cintitavā: one who has thought; cintitāvī: one who has thought; cintetvā: having thought; cintayitvā: having thought; cintituṃ: to think; cintetuṃ: to think; cintayituṃ: to think; cintitabbaṃ: should be thought; cintetabbaṃ: should be thought.

Kārite-cintāpito iccādi.

In the causative: cintāpito: caused to be thought, and so on.

Corito, corayito, coretā, corayitā iccādi.

Corito: stolen; corayito: stolen; coretā: one who steals; corayitā: one who steals, and so on.

Vedito, vedayito, vedetā, vedayitā iccādi.

Vedito: felt; vedayito: felt; vedetā: one who feels; vedayitā: one who feels, and so on.

Iti curādigaṇo.

Thus ends the Curādi group.

Titikkha, vīmaṃsa, bubhukkha, pabbatāya.

Titikkha: to endure; vīmaṃsa: to investigate; bubhukkha: to be hungry; pabbatāya: to act like a mountain.

Titikkhito, titikkhitā, titikkhitavā, titikkhitāvī, titikkhitvā, titikkhituṃ, titikkhitabbo.

Titikkhito: endured; titikkhitā: one who endures; titikkhitavā: one who has endured; titikkhitāvī: one who has endured; titikkhitvā: having endured; titikkhituṃ: to endure; titikkhitabbo: should be endured.

Kārite-titikkhāpito iccādi.

In the causative: titikkhāpito: caused to endure, and so on.

Vīmaṃsito, vīmaṃsetā, vīmaṃsitavā, vīmaṃsitāvī, vīmaṃsitvā, vīmaṃsituṃ, vīmaṃsitabbaṃ.

Vīmaṃsito: investigated; vīmaṃsetā: one who investigates; vīmaṃsitavā: one who has investigated; vīmaṃsitāvī: one who has investigated; vīmaṃsitvā: having investigated; vīmaṃsituṃ: to investigate; vīmaṃsitabbaṃ: should be investigated.

Kārite-vīmaṃsāpito iccādi.

In the causative: vīmaṃsāpito: caused to be investigated, and so on.

Bubhukkhito, bubhukkhitā, bubhukkhitavā, bubhukkhitāvī, bubhukkhitvā, bubhukkhituṃ, bubhukkhitabbaṃ.

Bubhukkhito: hungry; bubhukkhitā: one who is hungry; bubhukkhitavā: one who has been hungry; bubhukkhitāvī: one who has been hungry; bubhukkhitvā: having been hungry; bubhukkhituṃ: to be hungry; bubhukkhitabbaṃ: should be hungry.

Kārite-bubhukkhāpito iccādi.

In the causative: bubhukkhāpito: caused to be hungry, and so on.

Pabbatāyito, pabbatāyitā, pabbatāyitavā, pabbatāyitāvī, pabbatāyitvā, pabbatāyituṃ, pabbatāyitabbo.

Pabbatāyito: acted like a mountain; pabbatāyitā: one who acts like a mountain; pabbatāyitavā: one who has acted like a mountain; pabbatāyitāvī: one who has acted like a mountain; pabbatāyitvā: having acted like a mountain; pabbatāyituṃ: to act like a mountain; pabbatāyitabbo: should act like a mountain.

Kārite-pabbatāyāpito iccādi.

In the causative: pabbatāyāpito: caused to act like a mountain, and so on.

Evaṃ kukkuccāyito, kukkuccāyitā, kukkuccāyitavā, kukkuccāyitāvī, kukkuccāyitvā, kukkuccāyituṃ, kukkuccāyitabbaṃ[M 0.0521], piyāyito, piyāyitvā, piyāyituṃ iccādīni ca yojetabbāni.

Similarly, kukkuccāyito: felt remorse; kukkuccāyitā: one who feels remorse; kukkuccāyitavā: one who has felt remorse; kukkuccāyitāvī: one who has felt remorse; kukkuccāyitvā: having felt remorse; kukkuccāyituṃ: to feel remorse; kukkuccāyitabbaṃ: should feel remorse. And piyāyito: acted lovingly; piyāyitvā: having acted lovingly; piyāyituṃ: to act lovingly. And other similar forms should be supplied.

Atha visesarāsi vuccate.

Now a collection of special rules is stated.

767. Kattari cārambhe ka. 556-7; rū. 606, 622; nī. 1143-4.

767. In the agent and at the beginning.

Ārambho nāma ādikriyā-paṭhamārambho. Kriyārambhe vattabbe kattari ca bhāva, kammesu ca kto hoti, etena paccuppannepi kriyāsantāne paṭhamārambhaṃ paṭicca atītavisayo tapaccayo vihito, yathā? Bhuttāvī pavāritoti pāci. 238.

`Beginning` means the initial action, the first commencement. When the beginning of an action is to be expressed, the suffix kta occurs in the sense of the agent and the state, and in the sense of the object. By this, even in a present continuous action, with reference to the initial commencement, the past tense suffix ta is prescribed, as in: `Having eaten, one is satisfied.`

Puriso kaṭaṃ pakato, purisena kaṭo pakato.

A man has made a mat; a mat has been made by a man.

768. Ṭhāsavasasilisasīruhajarajanīhi ka. 556; rū. 606, 622; nī. 1143-4.

768. With the roots ṭhā, āsa, vasa, silisa, sī, ruha, jara, and janī.

Ṭhādīhi kattari ca bhāva, kammesu ca kto hoti.

After the roots ṭhā and so on, the suffix kta occurs in the sense of the agent and the state, and in the sense of the object.

Ṭhāmhi-upaṭṭhito garuṃ sisso, upaṭṭhito garu sissena.

In the case of ṭhā: A pupil has attended upon the teacher; the teacher has been attended upon by the pupil.

Āsamhi-upāsito garuṃ sisso, upāsito garu sissena.

In the case of āsa: A pupil has served the teacher; the teacher has been served by the pupil.

Vasamhi-anuvusito garuṃ sisso, anuvusito garu sissena.

In the case of vasa: A pupil has dwelt near the teacher; the teacher has been dwelt near by the pupil.

Silisa-āliṅgane, āsiliṭṭho pitaraṃ putto, āsiliṭṭho pitā puttena.

Silisa, in the sense of embracing: A son has embraced his father; a father has been embraced by his son.

Sīmhi-adhisayito ukkhaliṃ jano, adhisayitā ukkhali janena, uddhanaṃ āropitāti attho.

In the case of sī: A person has placed a pot upon it; a pot has been placed upon it by a person. The meaning is 'placed on the stove'.

Ruhamhi-ārūḷho rukkhaṃ jano, ārūḷho rukkho janena.

In the case of the root ruh: A person has climbed a tree; a tree has been climbed by a person.

Jaramhi-anujiṇṇo vasaliṃ devadatto, anujiṇṇā vasalī devadattena, anujāto māṇavikaṃ māṇavo, anujātā māṇavikā māṇavena.

In the case of the roots jar and jan: Devadatta has followed an outcast woman; an outcast woman has been followed by Devadatta. A young man has taken after a young woman; a young woman has been taken after by a young man.

769. Gamanatthākammakādhāre ca ka. 556-7; rū. 606, 622; nī. 1143-4.

769. And after roots with the sense of motion and intransitive roots, and in the sense of the locative.

Gamanatthadhātūhi [M 0.0522] akammakadhātūhi ca paraṃ ādhāre ca kattari ca bhāva, kammesu ca kto hoti.

After roots with the sense of motion and intransitive roots, the suffix kta occurs in the sense of the locative, as well as in the sense of the agent, the state, and the object.

Yanti etthāti yātaṃ, idaṃ tesaṃ yātaṃ. Padaṃ akkamati etthāti padakkantaṃ, idaṃ tesaṃ padakkantaṃ. Iha te yātā, ayaṃ tehi yāto maggo, iha tehi yātaṃ.

`That wherein they go` is `a place gone to`; this is their place gone to. `That wherein one steps` is `a place stepped upon`; this is their place stepped upon. Here they have gone. This is the path gone along by them. Here it has been gone by them.

Akammakamhi-idaṃ tesaṃ āsitaṃ ṭhānaṃ, iha te āsitā, idaṃ tehi āsitaṃ ṭhānaṃ, idha tehi āsitaṃ.

In the case of an intransitive root: This is their sitting place. Here they have sat. This is the place sat in by them. Here it has been sat by them.

770. Āhāratthā ka. 556-7; rū. 606, 622; nī. 1143-4.

770. From roots with the sense of consuming.

Ajjhoharaṇatthadhātuto kattari ca bhāva, kammesu ca ādhāre ca kto hoti.

From a root with the sense of consuming, the suffix kta occurs in the sense of the agent, the state, the object, and the locative.

Iha te bhuttā, asitā, pītā, khāyitā, sāyitā. Imāni tehi bhuttāni, asitāni, pītāni, khāyitāni, sāyitāni. Iha tesaṃ bhuttaṃ, asitaṃ, pītaṃ, khāyitaṃ, sāyitaṃ. Idaṃ tesaṃ bhuttaṃ ṭhānaṃ, asitaṃ ṭhānaṃ, pītaṃ ṭhānaṃ, khāyitaṃ ṭhānaṃ, sāyitaṃ ṭhānaṃ.

Here they have eaten, consumed, drunk, chewed, and tasted. These things have been eaten, consumed, drunk, chewed, and tasted by them. Here there has been eating, consuming, drinking, chewing, and tasting by them. This is their place of eating, place of consuming, place of drinking, place of chewing, and place of tasting.

Iti tādipaccayarāsi.

Thus ends the section on the suffix ta.

Anīyapaccayarāsi

The Section on the Suffix anīya

‘Bhāvakammesu tabbānīyā’ti anīyo, anubhuyyatīti anubhavanīyo.

By the rule `In the sense of the state and the object, tabba and anīya are used,` the suffix anīya is prescribed. `What is to be experienced` is anubhavanīyo.

Ākārantesu parassaralopo, kvaci yāgamo, upaṭṭhānīyo, dānīyo, padahatīti padhānīyo-yogāvacaro, pātabbanti pānīyaṃ, sāyituṃ arahatīti sāyanīyaṃ, paṭisāyanīyaṃ, pahānīyaṃ, abhitthavanīyaṃ, sotabbanti savanīyaṃ, hutabbanti [M 0.0523] havanīyaṃ, upāsanīyo, abhikkamitabboti abhikkamanīyo, rañjetīti rajjanīyo, gantabboti gamanīyo, vuccatīti vacanīyo.

After roots ending in ā, there is elision of the following vowel, and sometimes the augment y is inserted: upaṭṭhānīyo (to be attended to); dānīyo (to be given). `One who strives` is padhānīyo—a meditator. `What is to be drunk` is pānīyaṃ. `What is fit to be tasted` is sāyanīyaṃ. Also: paṭisāyanīyaṃ (to be put away); pahānīyaṃ (to be abandoned); abhitthavanīyaṃ (to be praised). `What is to be heard` is savanīyaṃ. `What is to be offered` is havanīyaṃ. Also: upāsanīyo (to be served). `What is to be approached` is abhikkamanīyo. `That which is delightful` is rajjanīyo. `What is to be gone to` is gamanīyo. `What is to be said` is vacanīyo.

Kara, tara, thara, dhara, sara, hara.

The roots kara, tara, thara, dhara, sara, hara.

771. Rā nassa ṇo ka. 549; rū. 550; nī. 1135.

771. After r, n becomes ṇ.

Rakārantadhātumhā parassa paccayanakārassa ṇo hoti.

After a root ending in r, the n of a following suffix becomes ṇ.

Kattabbanti karaṇīyaṃ, taritabbanti taraṇīyaṃ, attharitabbanti attharaṇīyaṃ, dhāretabbanti dhāraṇīyaṃ, sāretabbanti sāraṇīyaṃ, haritabbanti haraṇīyaṃ iccādi.

`What is to be done` is karaṇīyaṃ; `what is to be crossed` is taraṇīyaṃ; `what is to be spread` is attharaṇīyaṃ; `what is to be borne` is dhāraṇīyaṃ; `what is to be remembered` is sāraṇīyaṃ; `what is to be carried` is haraṇīyaṃ, and so on.

Rundhitabbanti rundhanīyaṃ, bhuñjitabbanti bhuñjanīyaṃ, bhojanīyaṃ, paribhojanīyaṃ, yojetabbanti yojanīyaṃ, dibbitabbanti dibbanīyaṃ, bujjhitabbanti bujjhanīyaṃ, pāpuṇitabbanti pāpanīyaṃ, ñāpetabbanti ñāpanīyaṃ, cintetabbanti cintanīyaṃ, vajjetabbanti vajjanīyaṃ, titikkhitabbanti titikkhanīyaṃ, vīmaṃsitabbanti vīmaṃsanīyaṃ iccādi.

`What is to be obstructed` is rundhanīyaṃ; `what is to be eaten` is bhuñjanīyaṃ, bhojanīyaṃ, paribhojanīyaṃ; `what is to be yoked` is yojanīyaṃ; `what is to be played` is dibbanīyaṃ; `what is to be understood` is bujjhanīyaṃ; `what is to be attained` is pāpanīyaṃ; `what is to be made known` is ñāpanīyaṃ; `what is to be thought` is cintanīyaṃ; `what is to be avoided` is vajjanīyaṃ; `what is to be endured` is titikkhanīyaṃ; `what is to be investigated` is vīmaṃsanīyaṃ, and so on.

Iti anīyapaccayarāsi.

Thus ends the section on the suffix anīya.

Nta, mānapaccayarāsi

The Section on the Suffixes nta and māna

Atha nta, mānapaccayā vuccante.

Now the suffixes nta and māna are explained.

772. Nto kattari vattamāne ka. 565; rū. 646; nī. 1157.

772. The suffix nta occurs in the agentive sense in the present tense.

Vattamāno vuccati paccuppanno, vattamāne kāle kriyatthā paraṃ kattari nto hoti.

The present is called the current time. In the present time, the suffix nta occurs after a verbal root in the agentive sense.

Bhū-sattāyaṃ, ‘kattari lo’ti apaccayo, ‘yuvaṇṇānameopaccaye’ti ovuddhi, bhavatīti bhonto-puriso, bhontaṃkulaṃ, bhontī-itthī.

From the root bhū in the sense of 'to be': the suffix a is added for the active voice. By the rule `yuvaṇṇānam eo paccaye`, there is strengthening to o. From bhavati (he is) comes bhonto puriso (a man who is), bhontaṃ kulaṃ (a family that is), bhontī itthī (a woman who is).

Puna [M 0.0524] ‘eonamayavā sare’ti ossa avādeso, bhavaṃpuriso, bhavantaṃ-kulaṃ, bhavantī, bhavatī, bhotī vā-itthī.

Again, by the rule `e o nam ay avā sare`, o is substituted by av, giving: bhavaṃ puriso (a man who is), bhavantaṃ kulaṃ (a family that is), and bhavantī, bhavatī, or bhotī for a woman.

773. Māno ka. 565; rū. 646; nī. 1157.

773. The suffix māna.

Vattamāne kāle kriyatthā paraṃ kattari māno hoti.

In the present time, the suffix māna occurs after a verbal root in the agentive sense.

Bhavamāno-puriso, bhavamānaṃ-kulaṃ, bhavamānā-itthī.

Bhavamāno puriso: a man who is becoming. Bhavamānaṃ kulaṃ: a family that is becoming. Bhavamānā itthī: a woman who is becoming.

774. Bhāvakammesu ca ka. 565; rū. 646; nī. 1157.

774. And in the sense of the state and the object.

Vattamāne kāle kriyatthā paraṃ bhāva, kammesu ca māno hoti. ‘Kyo bhāvakammesū…’ti yapaccayo.

In the present time, the suffix māna also occurs after a verbal root in the sense of the state and the object. The suffix ya (of the passive) is added, according to the rule `kyo bhāvakammesu...`.

Anubhūyateti anubhūyamāno bhogo purisena, anubhūyamānā sampatti, anubhūyamānaṃ sukhaṃ.

It is being experienced, thus: `anubhūyamāno bhogo purisena`, enjoyment being experienced by a man; `anubhūyamānā sampatti`, prosperity being experienced; `anubhūyamānaṃ sukhaṃ`, happiness being experienced.

Yassa dvittaṃ, anubhuyyamāno.

Of which there is a doubling: `anubhuyyamāno` (being experienced).

775. Te ssapubbānāgate.

775. In the future tense, they are preceded by `ssa`.

Anāgate kāle vattabbe te nta, mānapaccayā ssapubbā honti.

In the future tense, when the suffixes `-nta` and `-māna` are to be used, they are preceded by `ssa`.

Bhavissatīti bhavissanto rū. 403-piṭṭhe rūpavidhi passitabbo -puriso, bhavissantaṃ-kulaṃ, bhavissantī-vibhatti, bhavissatī vā, bhavissamāno, bhavissamānaṃ, bhavissamānā.

From `bhavissati` (he will be) come the forms: `bhavissanto puriso`, a man who will be; `bhavissantaṃ kulaṃ`, a family that will be; `bhavissantī vibhatti`, a declension that will be, or `bhavissatī` (feminine); and `bhavissamāno` (masculine), `bhavissamānaṃ` (neuter), `bhavissamānā` (feminine).

Kamme-anubhūyissamāno.

In the passive voice: `anubhūyissamāno` (one who will be experienced).

776. Mānassa massa.

776. Of `māna`: `ma` and `ssa`.

Mānapaccayassa massa kvaci lopo hoti.

Of the `ma` of the suffix `-māna` and of `ssa`, there is sometimes elision.

Nisinno vā sayāno khu. pā. 9.9 vā, sato sampajāno dī. ni. 1.217, niccaṃ nalopo.

With `nisinno vā sayāno vā, sato sampajāno`, there is always no elision.

Paññāyanto[M 0.0525], paññāyamāno.

`Paññāyanto`, `paññāyamāno` (appearing, being apparent).

Kamme-viññāyamāno.

In the passive voice: `viññāyamāno` (being known).

Kārite-ñāpento, ñāpayanto, ñāpayamāno.

In the causative: `ñāpento`, `ñāpayanto`, `ñāpayamāno` (causing to know, making known).

Kamme-ñāpīyamāno.

In the passive voice: `ñāpīyamāno` (being made to know).

Kiyādigaṇe-jānanto, jānamāno.

In the `ki`-group of roots: `jānanto`, `jānamāno` (knowing).

Kārite-jānāpento, jānāpayamāno.

In the causative: `jānāpento`, `jānāpayamāno` (causing to know).

Kamme-jānāpīyamāno.

In the passive voice: `jānāpīyamāno` (being made to know).

Tiṭṭhaṃ, tiṭṭhanto, tiṭṭhamāno, saṇṭhahaṃ, saṇṭhahanto, saṇṭhahamāno.

`Tiṭṭhaṃ`, `tiṭṭhanto`, `tiṭṭhamāno` (standing); `saṇṭhahaṃ`, `saṇṭhahanto`, `saṇṭhahamāno` (remaining, standing firm).

Kamme-upaṭṭhīyamāno.

In the passive voice: `upaṭṭhīyamāno` (being attended to, being served).

Kārite-patiṭṭhāpento, patiṭṭhāpayanto, patiṭṭhāpayamāno.

In the causative: `patiṭṭhāpento`, `patiṭṭhāpayanto`, `patiṭṭhāpayamāno` (causing to establish, setting up).

Kamme-patiṭṭhāpīyamāno.

In the passive voice: `patiṭṭhāpīyamāno` (being established).

Dento, dadanto, dajjanto, samādiyanto, dadamāno, dajjamāno, samādīyamāno.

`Dento`, `dadanto`, `dadamāno`, `dajjanto`, `dajjamāno` (giving); `samādiyanto`, `samādīyamāno` (undertaking).

Kamme-dīyamāno, diyyamāno.

In the passive voice: `dīyamāno`, `diyyamāno` (being given).

Kārite-dāpento, dāpayanto, samādapayanto, rasso.

In the causative: `dāpento`, `dāpayanto` (causing to give); `samādapayanto` (causing to undertake); with shortening (`rasso`).

Kamme-dāpīyamāno, samādāpīyamāno.

In the passive voice: `dāpīyamāno` (being made to give); `samādāpīyamāno` (being made to undertake).

Nidhento, nidahanto, nidahamāno, nidhiyyamāno, nidhāpento, nidhāpayanto, nidhāpayamāno, nidhāpīyamāno, yāyanto. Yāyanta’manuyāyanti jā. 2.22.1753, yāyamāno mahārājā, addā sīdantare nage jā. 2.22.566. Vāyanto, vāyamāno, nibbāyanto, parinibbāyanto, nibbāyamāno, nibbāpento, nibbāpayamāno[M 0.0526], nibbāpīyamāno, osāyanto, osāpento, osāpayanto, pahāyanto, pahāyamāno, jahanto, jahamāno, pahīyamāno, pahiyyamāno, jahīyamāno, hāpento, hāpayanto, hāpayamāno, jahāpento, jahāpayanto, jahāpayamāno, hāpīyamāno, jahāpīyamāno.

From `nidahati`: `nidhento`, `nidahanto`, `nidahamāno` (hiding); passive `nidhiyyamāno` (being hidden); causative `nidhāpento`, `nidhāpayanto`, `nidhāpayamāno` (causing to hide); causative passive `nidhāpīyamāno` (being made to hide). From `yāti`: `yāyanto` (going). Example: `Yāyantaṃ anuyāyanti` (They follow one who is going); `Yāyamāno mahārājā, addā sīdantare nage` (The great king, while going, saw a mountain in the Sīdantara ocean). From `vāyati`: `Vāyanto`, `vāyamāno` (blowing, weaving, striving). From `nibbāyati`: `nibbāyanto`, `parinibbāyanto`, `nibbāyamāno` (being extinguished); causative `nibbāpento`, `nibbāpayamāno` (causing to extinguish); causative passive `nibbāpīyamāno` (being made to be extinguished). From `osāyati`: `osāyanto` (ending); causative `osāpento`, `osāpayanto` (causing to end). From `jahati`: `pahāyanto`, `pahāyamāno`, `jahanto`, `jahamāno` (abandoning); passive `pahīyamāno`, `pahiyyamāno`, `jahīyamāno` (being abandoned); causative `hāpento`, `hāpayanto`, `hāpayamāno`, `jahāpento`, `jahāpayanto`, `jahāpayamāno` (causing to abandon); causative passive `hāpīyamāno`, `jahāpīyamāno` (being made to abandon).

Ivaṇṇesu-vikkayanto, vikkiṇanto, vinicchayanto, vinicchinanto, nito cassa cho.

For roots ending in `i`: `vikkayanto`, `vikkiṇanto` (selling); `vinicchayanto`, `vinicchinanto` (deciding). And after `ni`, `ci` becomes `chi`.

Ācayanto, ācinanto, jayanto, jinanto, ḍento, ḍemāno, nento, vinento, nayanto, vinayanto, nayamāno, niyyamāno, nayāpento, nayāpayamāno, sento, sayanto, semāno, sayamāno, sayāno vā, pahiṇanto, pahiṇamāno.

`Ācayanto`, `ācinanto` (accumulating); `jayanto`, `jinanto` (conquering); `ḍento`, `ḍemāno` (flying); `nento`, `vinento`, `nayanto`, `vinayanto`, `nayamāno` (leading, training, removing); passive `niyyamāno` (being led); causative `nayāpento`, `nayāpayamāno` (causing to lead); `sento`, `sayanto`, `semāno`, `sayamāno`, or `sayāno` (lying down, sleeping); `pahiṇanto`, `pahiṇamāno` (sending).

Uvaṇṇesu-cavanto, cavamāno, ṭhānā cāvanto, cāvayanto, cāvayamāno, javanto, javamāno, abhitthavanto, abhitthavamāno, abhitthavīyamāno, sandhavanto, sandhavamāno, dhunanto, niddhunanto, dhunamāno, niddhunamāno, punanto, ravanto, lunanto, āvuṇanto, pasavanto, vissavanto.

For roots ending in `u`: `cavanto`, `cavamāno` (falling, passing away); causative `ṭhānā cāvanto`, `cāvayanto`, `cāvayamāno` (causing to fall from a position); `javanto`, `javamāno` (running); `abhitthavanto`, `abhitthavamāno` (praising); passive `abhitthavīyamāno` (being praised); `sandhavanto`, `sandhavamāno` (flowing); `dhunanto`, `niddhunanto`, `dhunamāno`, `niddhunamāno` (shaking, shaking off); `punanto` (purifying); `ravanto` (sounding); `lunanto` (reaping); `āvuṇanto` (stringing); `pasavanto` (bringing forth); `vissavanto` (flowing out).

Kamme-suyyamāno.

In the passive voice: `suyyamāno` (being heard).

Kārite-sāvento, sāvayanto.

In the causative: `sāvento`, `sāvayanto` (causing to hear, announcing).

Svādigaṇe-suṇanto, suṇamāno.

In the Svādi group: suṇanto, suṇamāno (listening).

Kārite-suṇāpento, suṇāpayanto.

In the causative: suṇāpento, suṇāpayanto (causing to hear).

Hu-pūjāyaṃ, juhonto.

The root hu in the sense of worship: juhonto (offering, sacrificing).

Papubbo pahutte, pahonto, sampahonto.

Preceded by pa, in the sense of abundance: pahonto (being sufficient), sampahonto (being completely sufficient).

Hū-sattāyaṃ, honto.

The root hū in the sense of being: honto (being, existing).

Edantesu-ento[M 0.0527]. Atthaṃ entamhi sūriye jā. 2.22.2187 (atthaṅgatamhi), samento, abhisamento, khāyanto, khāyamāno, gāyanto, gāyamāno, gāyīyamāno, gāyāpento, gāyāpayanto, apacāyanto, dhammaṃ apacāyamāno, jhāyanto, jhāyamāno, pajjhāyanto, ujjhāyanto, nijjhāyanto, abhijjhāyanto.

For roots ending in e: ento (going). Atthaṃ entamhi sūriye (when the sun is setting). samento, abhisamento (being calm, being thoroughly calm); khāyanto, khāyamāno (appearing); gāyanto, gāyamāno (singing); gāyīyamāno (being sung); gāyāpento, gāyāpayanto (causing to sing); apacāyanto, dhammaṃ apacāyamāno (respecting, respecting the Dhamma); jhāyanto, jhāyamāno (meditating); pajjhāyanto (burning); ujjhāyanto (complaining); nijjhāyanto (contemplating); abhijjhāyanto (coveting).

Kārite-jhāpento, ujjhāpento, yalopo.

In the causative: jhāpento (causing to burn); ujjhāpento (causing to complain); with elision of ya.

Bhāyanto, bhāyamāno, sāliṃ lāyanto, lāyamāno, cīvaraṃ vāyanto, vāyamāno.

Bhāyanto, bhāyamāno (fearing); sāliṃ lāyanto, lāyamāno (reaping rice); cīvaraṃ vāyanto, vāyamāno (weaving a robe).

Kile-kīḷāyaṃ pemane ca, kelāyanto, kelāyamāno, cālento piyāyantoti vā attho.

The root kil in the sense of play and affection: kelāyanto, kelāyamāno (sporting, caressing); or the meaning is cālento (agitating) or piyāyanto (loving).

Gile-gelaññe, gilāyanto.

The root gil in the sense of sickness: gilāyanto (being sick).

Cine-avamaññane, cināyanto.

The root ci in the sense of disrespect: cināyanto (despising).

Pale-gatiyaṃ, palāyanto.

The root pal in the sense of going: palāyanto (fleeing, running away).

Mile-hāniyaṃ, milāyanto.

The root mil in the sense of decay: milāyanto (fading, decaying).

Saṅkase-nivāse, saṅkasāyanto iccādi.

Regarding Saṅkassa, in the sense of dwelling: saṅkasāyanto (desiring to go to Saṅkassa), and so forth.

Anekabyañjanesu-asa-bhuvi, “ntamānāntantiyiyuṃsvādilopo”ti nta, mānesu ādilopo, santo, samāno, upāsanto, upāsamāno, upāsīyamāno, icchanto, icchamāno, icchīyamāno, gacchanto, gacchamāno, gacchīyamāno.

For multiconsonantal roots like as (to be) and bhū (to be), by the rule 'ntamānāntantiyiyuṃsvādilopo,' there is elision of the initial vowel of the suffixes nta and māna: santo, samāno (being); upāsanto, upāsamāno (attending upon); upāsīyamāno (being attended upon); icchanto, icchamāno (desiring); icchīyamāno (being desired); gacchanto, gacchamāno (going); gacchīyamāno (being gone to).

Yassa pubbarūpatte-gammamāno, adhigammamāno, anāgate ssapubbo- “labha vasa chida gama bhida rudānaṃ cchaṅa”iti ssena saha dhātvantassa ccho, gacchanto, gamissanto, gacchamāno, gamissamāno, jiranto, jiramāno, jiyyanto, jiyyamāno, dahanto, dahamāno.

When there is a preceding form in the passive: gammamāno (being gone to), adhigammamāno (being attained). In the future, preceded by ssa, by the rule 'labha vasa chida gama bhida rudānaṃ cchaṅa,' the end of the root together with ssa becomes ccha: gacchanto, gamissanto (going, who will go); gacchamāno, gamissamāno (going, who will go); jiranto, jiramāno (aging); jiyyanto, jiyyamāno (decaying); dahanto, dahamāno (burning).

Dahassa [M 0.0528] dassa ḍo, ḍahanto, ḍahamāno.

For the root dah, da becomes ḍa: ḍahanto, ḍahamāno (burning).

Kamme-ḍayhamāno.

In the passive: ḍayhamāno (being burned).

Disa-pekkhane, passanto, passamāno, passīyamāno.

The root dis in the sense of seeing: passanto, passamāno (seeing); passīyamāno (being seen).

Kārite-dassento, dassayanto, dassayamāno.

In the causative: dassento, dassayanto, dassayamāno (showing, causing to see).

Labhanto, labhamāno.

Labhanto, labhamāno (obtaining, getting).

Kamme pubbarūpaṃ, labbhamāno, upalabbhamāno.

In the passive, with a preceding form: labbhamāno (being obtained), upalabbhamāno (being found).

Anāgate-lacchanto, labhissanto, lacchamāno, labhissamāno.

In the future: lacchanto, labhissanto, lacchamāno, labhissamāno (who will obtain).

Maranto, maramāno, miyanto, miyamāno.

Maranto, maramāno, miyanto, miyamāno (dying, passing away).

Yamu-uparame, niyamanto, saññamanto, saññamamāno, niyacchanto.

The root yam in the sense of restraint: niyamanto (restraining), saññamanto, saññamamāno (controlling), niyacchanto (restraining).

Kārite-niyāmento.

In the causative: niyāmento (causing to restrain, appointing).

Rudanto, rodanto, rodamāno.

Rudanto, rodanto, rodamāno (weeping, wailing).

Anāgate-rucchanto, rodissanto, rucchamāno, rodissamāno.

In the future: rucchanto, rodissanto, rucchamāno, rodissamāno (who will weep, about to weep).

Vacanto, vacamāno.

Vacanto, vacamāno (speaking, saying).

Kamme ‘assū’ti uttaṃ, vuccamāno.

In the passive, by the rule 'assū'ti, the vowel a becomes u: vuccamāno (being said).

Kārite-vācento, vācayanto, vācayamāno.

In the causative: vācento, vācayanto, vācayamāno (causing to speak, making recite).

Kamme-vācīyamāno.

In the passive of the causative: vācīyamāno (being made to speak).

Anāgate-‘vaca bhuja muca visānaṃ kkhaṅa’iti ssena saha dhātvantassa kkhādeso, vakkhanto, vakkhamāno, vadanto, vadamāno, ovadanto, ovadamāno, vajjanto, vajjamāno.

In the future, by the rule ‘vaca bhuja muca visānaṃ kkhaṅa,’ the end of the root together with ‘ssa’ is substituted by ‘kkha’: vakkhanto, vakkhamāno (who will speak). Also: vadanto, vadamāno (speaking); ovadanto, ovadamāno (advising); vajjanto, vajjamāno (speaking).

Kamme-vadīyamāno, ovadīyamāno, ovajjamāno.

In the passive: vadīyamāno (being spoken to), ovadīyamāno (being advised), ovajjamāno (being admonished).

Kārite-bheriṃ vādento, vādayamāno.

In the causative: bheriṃ vādento, vādayamāno (causing a drum to sound, beating a drum).

Vasanto [M 0.0529] vasamāno.

Vasanto, vasamāno (dwelling, living).

Kamme pubbarūpattaṃ, upavassamāno.

In the passive, with a prefix: upavassamāno (being dwelt near).

Vāsento, vāsayanto.

Vāsento, vāsayanto (causing to dwell, causing to inhabit).

Anāgate-vacchanto, vasissanto, vacchamāno, vasissamāno.

In the future: vacchanto, vasissanto, vacchamāno, vasissamāno (who will dwell, about to dwell).

Pavisanto, pavisamāno.

Pavisanto, pavisamāno (entering).

Kamme-pavisīyamāno.

In the passive: pavisīyamāno (being entered).

Anāgate-pavekkhanto, pavisissanto, pavekkhamāno, pavisissamāno iccādi.

In the future: pavekkhanto, pavisissanto, pavekkhamāno, pavisissamāno (who will enter, about to enter), etc.

Rudhādimhi-rundhanto, rundhamāno.

In the Rudha group: rundhanto, rundhamāno (obstructing).

Kamme-rundhīyamāno.

In the passive: rundhīyamāno (being obstructed).

Pubbarūpatte-rujjhamāno.

In the assimilated passive form: rujjhamāno (being obstructed).

Rodhento, rodhamāno, rodhīyamāno.

Rodhento, rodhamāno (causing to obstruct, imprisoning); rodhīyamāno (being imprisoned).

Chindanto, chindamāno, chindīyamāno, chijjamāno, chindāpento, chindāpayanto.

Chindanto, chindamāno (cutting); chindīyamāno, chijjamāno (being cut); chindāpento, chindāpayanto (causing to cut).

Anāgate-checchanto, chindissanto, checchamāno, chindissamāno.

In the future: checchanto, chindissanto, checchamāno, chindissamāno (who will cut, about to cut).

Bhindanto, bhindamāno, bhindīyamāno, bhijjamāno, bhecchanto, bhindissanto, bhecchamāno, bhindissamāno.

Bhindanto, bhindamāno (breaking); bhindīyamāno, bhijjamāno (being broken); bhecchanto, bhindissanto, bhecchamāno, bhindissamāno (who will break, about to break).

Bhuñjanto, bhuñjamāno.

Bhuñjanto, bhuñjamāno (eating, enjoying).

Kamme-bhuñjīyamāno.

In the passive: bhuñjīyamāno (being eaten, being enjoyed).

Pubbarūpatte-bhujjamāno.

In the assimilated passive form: bhujjamāno (being consumed).

Bhojento, bhojayanto, bhojayamāno, bhojīyamāno.

Bhojento, bhojayanto, bhojayamāno (causing to eat, feeding); bhojīyamāno (being fed).

Anāgate-bhokkhanto[M 0.0530], bhuñjissanto, bhokkhamāno, bhuñjissamāno.

In the future: bhokkhanto, bhuñjissanto, bhokkhamāno, bhuñjissamāno (who will eat, about to eat).

Muñcanto, muñcamāno, muñcīyamāno, muccamāno.

Muñcanto, muñcamāno (releasing); muñcīyamāno, muccamāno (being released).

Anāgate-mokkhanto, muñcissanto, mokkhamāno, muñcissamāno iccādi.

In the future: mokkhanto, muñcissanto, mokkhamāno, muñcissamāno (who will release, about to release), etc.

Divādimhi suddhakatturūpaṃ suddhakammarūpañca pubbarūpe sadisameva, dibbanto, dibbamāno, dibbīyamāno.

In the Divādi group, the active and simple passive forms are like the preceding forms: dibbanto, dibbamāno (playing); dibbīyamāno (being played).

Pubbarūpatte-dibbamāno.

In the assimilated passive form: dibbamāno (being played).

Chijjanto, chijjamāno, chedāpento, chedāpayamāno.

Chijjanto, chijjamāno (being cut); chedāpento, chedāpayamāno (causing to cut).

Bujjhanto, bujjhamāno, bujjhīyamāno, bodhento, bodhayanto, bodhayamāno.

Bujjhanto, bujjhamāno (awakening, understanding); bujjhīyamāno (being awakened, being understood); bodhento, bodhayanto, bodhayamāno (causing to awaken, teaching).

Muccanto, muccamāno, mocento, mocayanto, mocayamāno, mocīyamāno.

Being freed, being freed; causing to free, causing to free, causing to free; being caused to be freed.

Yujjanto, yujjamāno iccādi.

Striving, striving, and so on.

Svādimhi-suṇanto, suṇamāno.

In the Svādi group: hearing, hearing.

Kamme-suyyamāno.

In the passive: being heard.

Kārite-sāvento, sāvayanto, sāvayamāno.

In the causative: causing to hear, causing to hear, causing to hear.

Pāpuṇanto, dhammaṃ pariyāpuṇanto, pariyāpuṇamāno, pāpuṇīyamāno, pāpīyamāno.

Attaining; mastering the Dhamma, mastering; being attained, being attained.

Kārite-pāpento, pāpayanto, pāpayamāno.

In the causative: causing to attain, causing to attain, causing to attain.

Pari, saṃpubbo-parisamāpento, parisamāpayanto, parisamāpayamāno, parisamāpīyamāno.

With the prefixes pari- and saṃ-: causing to complete, causing to complete, causing to complete; being caused to complete.

Sakkuṇanto, āvuṇanto iccādi.

Being able, stringing, and so on.

Kiyādimhi-kiṇanto, kiṇāpento, vikkayanto iccādi.

In the Kiyādi group: buying, causing to buy, selling, and so on.

Tanādimhi-tanonto[M 0.0531], karonto, kubbanto, kubbamāno, krubbanto, krubbamāno, kurumāno, kayiranto, kayiramāno.

In the Tanādi group: extending; doing, doing, doing, doing, doing, doing; being done, being done.

Kamme-karīyamāno, kayyamāno, ‘tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā’ti dhātvantassa yādeso.

In the passive: being done, being made; there is a substitution of 'y' for the final of the root according to the rule: 'tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā.'

Saṅkharonto, abhisaṅkharonto.

Forming, fabricating.

Kārite-kārento, kārayanto, kārayamāno, kārīyamāno.

In the causative: causing to do, causing to do, causing to do; being made to do.

Sakkonto iccādi.

Being able, and so on.

Curādimhi-corento, corayanto, corayamāno, thenento, thenayanto, thenayamāno, cintento, cintayanto, cintayamāno, cintīyamāno, cintāpento, cintāpayanto, cintāpayamāno, cintāpīyamāno iccādi.

In the Curādi group: stealing, stealing, stealing; stealing, stealing, stealing; thinking, thinking, thinking; being thought about; causing to think, causing to think, causing to think; being caused to think, and so on.

Titikkhanto, titikkhamāno, titikkhīyamāno, titikkhāpento, titikkhāpayanto, titikkhāpayamāno, vīmaṃsanto, tikicchanto, cikicchanto, vicikicchanto.

Enduring, enduring; being endured; causing to endure, causing to endure, causing to endure; investigating; treating, treating; doubting.

Bhuñjituṃ icchatīti bubhukkhanto, ghasituṃ icchatīti jighacchanto, pātuṃ paribhuñjituṃ icchatīti pipāsanto, gottuṃ saṃvarituṃ icchatīti jigucchanto, harituṃ pariyesituṃ icchatīti jigīsanto, vijetuṃ icchatīti vijigīsanto.

Wishing to eat, thus being hungry; wishing to devour, thus being ravenous; wishing to drink and enjoy, thus being thirsty; wishing to guard and restrain, thus being disgusted; wishing to take and seek, thus being acquisitive; wishing to conquer, thus wishing to conquer.

Pabbato viya attānaṃ caratīti pabbatāyanto, pabbatāyamāno, piyāyanto, mettāyantoiccādīni ca yojetabbāni.

Behaving like a mountain, thus acting like a mountain; acting friendly; acting with loving-kindness. And other similar forms should be supplied.

Iti nta, mānapaccayarāsi.

Here ends the section on the suffixes -nta and -māna.

Ṇyādipaccayarāsi

The Collection of Suffixes beginning with -ṇya

Atha [M 0.0532] ṇya, ya, yakapaccayantā vuccante.

Now, words ending in the suffixes -ṇya and -ya are discussed.

777. Ghyaṇa.

777. Ghyaṇa.

Bhāva, kammesu gha, ṇānubandho yapaccayo hoti. Ghānubandho ‘kagācajānaṃ ghānubandhe’tiādīsu visesanattho. Ṇānubandho vuddhidīpanattho. Evaṃ sabbattha.

In the senses of state (bhāva) and passive (kamma), the suffix -ya with the indicators `gh` and `ṇ` occurs. The indicator `gh` is for special purposes, as in rules like 'kagācajānaṃ ghānubandhe.' The indicator `ṇ` is for indicating vowel strengthening (vuddhi). Thus it is in all cases.

Anubhavitabboti anubhāviyo bhogo purisena, anubhāviyaṃ sukhaṃ, anubhāviyā sampatti.

That which is to be experienced: wealth to be experienced by a person, happiness to be experienced, prosperity to be experienced.

778. Āsse ca.

778. And e for ā.

Ādantadhātūnaṃ āssa e hoti ghyaṇamhi. Casaddena ivaṇṇadhātūnaṃ āgamaīkārassa ca ettaṃ.

For roots ending in ā, e replaces ā before the -ṇya suffix. By the word 'and' (ca), for roots ending in i, e also replaces the augment ī.

Akkhātabbaṃ kathetabbanti akkheyyaṃ.

Because it should be declared and spoken, it is declarable.

Yassa dvittaṃ, saṅkhātabbanti saṅkhyeyyaṃ, saṅkhātuṃ asakkuṇeyyanti asaṅkhyeyyaṃ, gāyitabbanti geyyaṃ-sagāthakaṃ suttaṃ, ghāyituṃ arahatīti gheyyaṃ, ghāyanīyaṃ, apacāyituṃ arahatīti apaceyyaṃ, ñātuṃ arahatīti ñeyyaṃ, ājānituṃ arahatīti aññeyyaṃ, viññeyyaṃ, abhiññeyyaṃ, pariññeyyaṃ.

Countable, because it is to be reckoned; innumerable, because it cannot be reckoned; singable, because it is to be sung—a discourse with verses; smellable (`gheyyaṃ`, `ghāyanīyaṃ`), because it is fit to be smelled; venerable, because it is fit to be revered; knowable, because it is fit to be known; to be understood, to be discerned, to be directly known, and to be fully understood, because it is fit to be understood.

Īāgame-jāniyaṃ, vijāniyaṃ, īssa rasso.

With the augment ī: to be known, to be distinguished; the ī is shortened.

Jāneyyaṃ, vijāneyyaṃ, adhiṭṭhātabbanti adhiṭṭheyyaṃ, adhiṭṭhaheyyaṃ, dātabbanti deyyaṃ, ādātabbanti ādeyyaṃ, saddahituṃ arahatīti saddaheyyaṃ, vidhātuṃ arahatīti vidheyyaṃ, na vidheyyaṃ avidheyyaṃ-anattalakkhaṇaṃ, mārassa āṇā dahati etthāti māradheyyaṃ, maccudheyyaṃ, sannihitabbanti sannidheyyaṃ, abhidhātabbaṃ kathetabbanti abhidheyyaṃ, pidahitabbanti pidheyyaṃ, alopo, apidheyyaṃ vā, pātabbanti peyyaṃ, minetabbanti meyyaṃ, pametabbanti [M 0.0533] pameyyaṃ, upecca minituṃ arahatīti upameyyaṃ, hātabbanti heyyaṃ, paheyyaṃ, pajaheyyaṃ.

To be known, to be understood; because it should be determined, it is determinable or resolvable; because it should be given, it is to be given; because it should be taken, it is to be taken; because it is fit to be believed, it is credible; because it is fit to be governed, it is governable; not governable is ungovernable—the characteristic of not-self; because 'the command of Māra is placed here,' it is the realm of Māra; the realm of Death; because it is placed near, it is a deposit; because it should be designated or spoken, it is a designation; because it should be covered, it is to be covered; with elision of 'a', or alternatively, not to be covered; because it should be drunk, it is drinkable; because it should be measured, it is measurable; because it should be estimated, it is estimable; because it is fit to be approached and measured, it is comparable; because it should be abandoned, it is to be abandoned, to be abandoned, to be abandoned.

Ivaṇṇesu-ajjhāyitabbanti ajjheyyaṃ, adhiyeyyaṃ, upetabbanti upeyyaṃ, vikkiṇitabbanti vikkeyyaṃ, vikkāyiyaṃ, vikkāyeyyaṃ, vikkiṇeyyaṃ vā, vicinitabbanti viceyyaṃ, vicineyyaṃ, jetabbanti jeyyaṃ, vijeyyaṃ, netabbanti neyyaṃ, vineyyaṃ, adhisayitabbanti adhiseyyaṃ, pahitabbanti pāheyyaṃ, pahiṇeyyaṃ vā.

In the case of 'i' vowels: because it should be studied, it is ajjheyyaṃ or adhiyeyyaṃ; because it should be approached, it is upeyyaṃ; because it should be sold, it is vikkeyyaṃ, vikkāyiyaṃ, vikkāyeyyaṃ, or vikkiṇeyyaṃ; because it should be examined, it is viceyyaṃ or vicineyyaṃ; because it should be conquered, it is jeyyaṃ or vijeyyaṃ; because it should be led, it is neyyaṃ or vineyyaṃ; because it should be lain upon, it is adhiseyyaṃ; because it should be sent, it is pāheyyaṃ or pahiṇeyyaṃ.

Uvaṇṇesu vuddhiāvādeso, ku-sadde, kuyyatīti kāveyyaṃ.

In the case of 'u' vowels, there is a vuddhi strengthening and an āva substitution. For the root ku, meaning 'to sound', because it is sounded (kuyyati), it becomes kāveyyaṃ.

Īssa abhāve vassa battaṃ rasso ca, kabyaṃ.

In the absence of ī, for v there is the substitution of b, and there is shortening; hence, kabyaṃ.

Pubbarūpatte kabbaṃ, cāvetabbanti cāveyyaṃ, javitabbanti javeyyaṃ, abhitthavitabbanti abhitthaveyyaṃ, bhavituṃ arahatīti bhabbaṃ. Juhotabbanti habyaṃ-sappi.

By assimilation to the preceding consonant, it becomes kabbaṃ; because it should be caused to move, it is cāveyyaṃ; because it should be hurried, it is javeyyaṃ; because it should be praised, it is abhitthaveyyaṃ; because it is fit to become, it is bhabbaṃ; because it should be offered as an oblation, it is habyaṃ—ghee.

Edantesu-apacāyitabbanti apaceyyaṃ, apacāyiyaṃ.

In the case of roots ending in 'e': because it should be respected, it is apaceyyaṃ or apacāyiyaṃ.

Ve-tantasantāne, vetabbanti veyyaṃ.

For the root ve, in the sense of weaving or continuity: because it should be woven, it is veyyaṃ.

Vaca, bhaja, bhuja, yujādīhi ghyaṇapaccayo.

From the roots vaca, bhaja, bhuja, yuj, and so forth, the suffix ghyaṇa is applied.

779. Kagā cajānaṃ ghānubandhe ka. 623; rū. 554; nī. 1229.

779. Ka and ga are substituted for ca and ja when gha is an anubandha.

Ca, jānaṃ dhātvantānaṃ ka, gā honti ghānubandhe paccaye pare.

The final ca and ja of roots become ka and ga respectively, when a suffix with gha as an anubandha follows.

Vattabbanti vākyaṃ, vākkaṃ, vāccaṃ, vāceyyaṃ vā.

Because it should be spoken, it is vākyaṃ, vākkaṃ, vāccaṃ, or vāceyyaṃ.

Bhaja-sevāyaṃ, bhajitabbanti bhāgyaṃ, bhaggaṃ, bhuñjitabbanti bhogyaṃ, bhoggaṃ, yuñjitabbanti yogyaṃ, yoggaṃ.

The root bhaj is in the sense of serving; because it should be served, it is bhāgyaṃ or bhaggaṃ. Because it should be eaten or enjoyed, it is bhogyaṃ or bhoggaṃ. Because it should be joined or applied, it is yogyaṃ or yoggaṃ.

780. Vadādīhi yo ka. 541; rū. 552; nī. 1126.

780. From vada and so forth, the suffix ya is applied.

Vadādīhi bhāva, kammesu bahulaṃ yo hoti.

From vada and so forth, the suffix ya frequently occurs in the sense of state or being and action or object.

Bhuñjibhabbanti [M 0.0534] bhojjaṃ, khāditabbanti khajjaṃ, vituditabbanti vitujjaṃ, panuditabbanti panujjaṃ, pajjitabbanti pajjaṃ, majjati etenāti majjaṃ.

Because it should be eaten, it is bhojjaṃ; because it should be chewed, it is khajjaṃ; because it should be pricked, it is vitujjaṃ; because it should be dispelled, it is panujjaṃ; because it should be gone to, it is pajjaṃ; that by which one becomes intoxicated is majjaṃ (an intoxicant).

Muda-hāse, pamodati etenāti pāmojjaṃ, vadīyatīti vajjaṃ.

The root mud is in the sense of gladness. That by which one delights is pāmojjaṃ (joy). That which is spoken is vajjaṃ (blame, fault).

Vadha-hiṃsāyaṃ, vadhitabbanti vajjhaṃ, vijjhitabbanti vijjhaṃ, punanti sujjhanti sattā etenāti puññaṃ, nāgamo.

The root vadh is in the sense of harming. Because it should be killed, it is vajjhaṃ. Because it should be pierced, it is vijjhaṃ. Because beings are purified and cleansed by this, it is puññaṃ (merit); there is no augmentation.

Vihaññate vihaññaṃ, vapiyateti vappaṃ, supanaṃ soppaṃ, labhitabbanti labbhaṃ, gantabbanti gammaṃ, damituṃ arahatīti dammaṃ, ramitabbanti rammaṃ, abhirammaṃ, nisāmīyate nisammaṃ, visamīyate visammaṃ, phusīyateti phasso, ussa attaṃ.
