Titikkhanaṃ titikkhā, vīmaṃsanaṃ vīmaṃsā, tikicchanaṃ tikicchā, vigatā tikicchā etissāti vicikicchā, bhottuṃ icchā bubhukkhā, bubhokkhā vā, ghasituṃ icchā jighacchā, pātuṃ paribhuñjituṃ icchā pipāsā, harituṃ icchā jigīsā, vijetuṃ icchā vijigīsā, hantuṃ icchā jighaṃsā iccādi.

Enduring is 'titikkhā' (endurance); investigating is 'vīmaṃsā' (investigation); treating is 'tikicchā' (treatment); that from which treatment has departed is 'vicikicchā' (doubt). The desire to eat is 'bubhukkhā' (hunger), or 'bubhokkhā'; the desire to devour is 'jighacchā'; the desire to drink and consume is 'pipāsā' (thirst); the desire to seize is 'jigīsā'; the desire to conquer is 'vijigīsā'; the desire to kill is 'jighaṃsā', and so on.

Ṇamhi-ara-gatiyaṃ, arati sīghaṃ vijjhamānā gacchatīti ārāvedhako, karonti nānākammakāraṇāyo etthāti kārā-addu[M 0.0557], jiyyanti etāyāti jārā, tarati sīghataraṃ gacchatīti tārā, bhāsanti etāyāti bhāsā, dhāreti sīghaṃ vahatīti dhārā, khaggadhārā, vuṭṭhidhārā, mayati vividhākāraṃ gacchati etāyāti māyā, likhīyate lekhā, vuccateti vācā, harati manoramaṃ pavattetīti hārā-muttāvali iccādi.

With the suffix Ṇa: from the root 'ar' in the sense of 'going'. It goes swiftly while piercing, hence ārāvedhako (one who pierces with an awl). They perform various actions here, therefore kārā (prison) or addu (bond). They decay by this, therefore jārā (old age, decay). It crosses, goes very swiftly, therefore tārā (star). They speak by this, therefore bhāsā (language). It bears, flows swiftly, therefore dhārā (stream, edge); the sword's edge (khaggadhārā), the rain's downpour (vuṭṭhidhārā). It goes in diverse ways by this, therefore māyā (illusion). It is written, therefore lekhā (writing). It is spoken, therefore vācā (speech). It carries, causes to proceed delightfully, therefore hārā (garland), muttāvali (pearl necklace), and so on.

Yakpaccaye-saha kathanaṃ sākacchā, tathanaṃ tacchā, nipajjanaṃ nipajjā, vidati jānātīti vijjā, vidanti jānanti etāyāti vā vijjā, vijjāpaṭipakkhā avijjā, nisajjanaṃ nisajjā.

With the ya-suffix: Speaking together is discussion (sākacchā). The state of being true is truth (tacchā). The act of lying down is lying down (nipajjā). One knows, understands, therefore it is knowledge (vijjā); or, they know, understand by this, therefore it is knowledge (vijjā). The opposite of knowledge is ignorance (avijjā). The act of sitting down is sitting (nisajjā).

Idha-ijjhane, samijjhanaṃ samijjhā.

From the root 'idh' in the sense of 'flourishing': The act of flourishing is success (samijjhā).

Sidha-nipphattiyaṃ, sijjhanaṃ sijjhā iccādi.

From the root 'sidh' in the sense of 'accomplishment': The act of accomplishing is accomplishment (sijjhā), and so on.

Yamhi-maja-saṃsuddhiyaṃ, sammajjanaṃ sammajjā, apecca vajanaṃ gamanaṃ pabbajjā, caraṇaṃ cariyā, paricaraṇaṃ pāricariyā, ‘ūbyañjanassā’ti īāgamo rasso ca.

With the suffix 'ya', from the root 'maj' in the sense of 'purification': The act of sweeping is sweeping (sammajjā). Going away, going forth, is going forth (pabbajjā). The act of conducting is conduct (cariyā). The act of attending is service (pāricariyā). According to the rule 'ūbyañjanassa', the augment 'ī' is added and it is shortened.

Jāgara-niddakkhaye, jāgaraṇaṃ jāgariyā, seti etthāti seyyā, dvittaṃ.

From the root 'jāgar' in the sense of 'cessation of sleep': The act of being awake is wakefulness (jāgariyā). One lies down here, therefore it is a bed or the act of lying down (seyyā); there is doubling.

Anamhi-saha gāyanti sajjhāyanti etthāti saṅgāyanā, ṭhāpīyate patiṭṭhīyate patiṭṭhānā, pāpīyate pāpanā, sampāpanā, parisamāpanā, upāsīyate upāsanā, payirūpāsanā, esīyate esanā, pariyesanā, kāmesanā, bhavesanā, brahmacariyesanā, chejjabhejjādikassa kammassa karaṇaṃ kammakāraṇā, ādivuddhi, dvattiṃsa kammakāraṇā.

With the ana-suffix: They sing together, recite here, therefore it is recitation (saṅgāyanā). It is established, fixed, therefore it is establishment (patiṭṭhānā). It is made to reach, therefore it is causing to reach (pāpanā); complete causing to reach (sampāpanā); complete finishing (parisamāpanā). It is attended to, therefore it is attendance (upāsanā); attending all around (payirūpāsanā). It is sought, therefore it is seeking (esanā); complete seeking (pariyesanā); seeking for sensual pleasures (kāmesanā); seeking for existence (bhavesanā); seeking for the holy life (brahmacariyesanā). The doing of actions such as cutting and piercing is the cause of action (kammakāraṇā); there is initial vowel strengthening. Thirty-two causes of action (dvattiṃsa kammakāraṇā).

Citi-cetāyaṃ, cetenti sampayuttā dhammā etāyāti cetanā, cintīyate cintanā, ṭhapīyate ṭhapanā, dīpīyate dīpanā, vipassanti etāyāti vipassanā, sandassīyate sandassanā, desīyate desanā, desīyati etāyāti vā desanā, patthīyate patthanā, pharīyate pharaṇā, phusīyate phusanā, bhāvīyate bhāvanā, vibhāvanā, sambhāvanā, mantīyate mantanā, nimantanā[M 0.0558], āmantanā, punappunaṃ modanti etāyāti anumodanā, yācīyate yācanā, ādarena yācanā āyācanā, yojīyate yojanā.

From the root 'ci' in the sense of 'thinking': Associated states intend by this, therefore it is volition (cetanā). It is thought, therefore it is thinking (cintanā). It is established, therefore it is establishment (ṭhapanā). It is illuminated, therefore it is illumination (dīpanā). They see clearly by this, therefore it is insight (vipassanā). It is shown, therefore it is showing (sandassanā). It is taught, therefore it is teaching (desanā); or, it is taught by this, therefore it is teaching (desanā). It is desired, therefore it is aspiration (patthanā). It is pervaded, therefore it is pervasion (pharaṇā). It is touched, therefore it is touching (phusanā). It is developed, therefore it is development (bhāvanā); special development (vibhāvanā); thorough development (sambhāvanā). It is deliberated, therefore it is deliberation (mantanā); invitation (nimantanā); addressing (āmantanā). They repeatedly rejoice by this, therefore it is rejoicing (anumodanā). It is begged, therefore it is begging (yācanā); begging with respect is entreaty (āyācanā). It is joined, therefore it is joining (yojanā).

Raca-vidhāne, racīyate racanā, āracanā, viracanā.

From the root 'rac' in the sense of 'arranging': It is arranged, therefore it is arrangement (racanā); also āracanā, viracanā.

Vaṭṭa-vaṭṭane, āvaṭṭanā, vivaṭṭanā, vedīyate vedanā.

From the root 'vaṭṭ' in the sense of 'revolving': Revolving towards (āvaṭṭanā), revolving away (vivaṭṭanā). It is felt, therefore it is feeling (vedanā).

Vara-icchāyaṃ, pavārīyate icchāpīyate pavāraṇā, vāsīyate vāsanā, āsīsīyate āsīsanā, hiṃsīyate hiṃsanā iccādi.

From the root 'var' in the sense of 'wishing': It is chosen, desired, therefore it is invitation (pavāraṇā). It is perfumed, therefore it is a latent impression (vāsanā). It is wished for, therefore it is wishing (āsīsanā). It is harmed, therefore it is harming (hiṃsanā), and so on.

Timhi-bahulādhikārā anitthiyampiti hoti, gāyanaṃ gīti, saha gāyanaṃ saṅgīti, duggīti, anugīti, ayaṃ amhākaṃ abbhantarimoti ñāyatīti ñāti, jānanaṃ ñatti, dvittaṃ, ṭhānaṃ ṭhiti.

With the ti-suffix: by the principle of varied application, it can also occur in the non-feminine gender. The act of singing is song (gīti). Singing together is communal chanting (saṅgīti); bad song (duggīti); following song (anugīti). 'This is our internal one,' thus he is known, therefore he is a kinsman (ñāti). The act of knowing is an intimation (ñatti); there is doubling. The act of standing is stability (ṭhiti).

Dā-avakhaṇḍane, dīyati etāyāti datti, dvittaṃ, dhāretīti dhāti, dahanaṃ akampanaṃ dhīti, samādahanaṃ samādhīti, mahāvuttinā āssaṃ īttaṃ, dvitte dhassa dattaṃ rasso ca, dīdhiti-raṃsi.

From the root 'dā' in the sense of 'cutting': It is given by this, therefore it is a gift (datti); there is doubling. She who holds or sustains is a nurse (dhāti). Burning, unshaken, is wisdom (dhīti). Composing is concentration (samādhīti). By the great commentary, 'ā' becomes 'ī'. In doubling, 'dh' becomes 'd', and there is shortening. Dīdhiti means a ray (raṃsi).

Nibbāyanaṃ nibbuti, āssa uttaṃ, saha ayanaṃ samiti, eti āgacchatīti īti-upaddavo, vicinanaṃ viciti, vijayanaṃ vijiti, nīyati ñāyati etāyāti nīti, lokanīti, dhammanīti, saddanīti, bhavaṃ netīti bhavanetti, vuddhi dvittañca, saddhammanetti, pinayatīti pīti, bhāyanaṃ bhīti, cavanaṃ cuti, javanaṃ juti, thavanaṃ thuti, abhitthuti, pavanaṃ pūti, bhavanaṃ bhūti, suṭṭhu bhavatīti subhūti, vibhavanaṃ vibhūti, suṭṭhu munanaṃ bandhanaṃ sammuti, savanaṃ suti, suyyateti vā suti, pasuti, upasuti, hūyateti huti, ānetvā hutabbāti āhuti, cāyanaṃ pūjanaṃ citi, dvitte-citti, apaciti, essa attaṃ, nijjhāyanaṃ nijjhatti.

Extinguishing is quenching (nibbuti); its 'ā' becomes 'u'. Going together is assembly (samiti). It comes, it approaches, therefore it is calamity (īti), a disaster (upaddavo). Examining is investigation (viciti). Conquering is victory (vijiti). By this one is led or known, therefore it is guidance (nīti); worldly guidance (lokanīti); guidance in the Dhamma (dhammanīti); grammar (saddanīti). It leads to existence, therefore it is the guide to existence (bhavanetti); with vowel gradation and doubling, there is guidance in the good Dhamma (saddhammanetti). It delights, therefore it is delight (pīti). Fearing is fear (bhīti). Passing away is decease (cuti). Swiftness is radiance (juti). Praising is praise (thuti); high praise (abhitthuti). Decaying is putridity (pūti). Being is prosperity (bhūti). It exists well, therefore it is well-being (subhūti). Manifestation is magnificence (vibhūti). Thinking well, binding, is consensus (sammuti). Hearing is hearing (suti); or, it is heard, therefore it is hearing (suti); birth (pasuti); listening closely (upasuti). It is sacrificed, therefore it is sacrifice (huti); having brought what is to be offered, it is an offering (āhuti). Piling up, worship, is a pyre or worship (citi); with doubling, it is mind (citti); reverence (apaciti). Its 'a' becomes 'at' (essa attaṃ). Contemplation is absorption (nijjhatti).

Mahāvuttinā takāre karassa kuttaṃ, kriyā kutti, sarakutti, itthikuttaṃ, purisakuttaṃ, janetīti janetti, īāgamassa ettaṃ[M 0.0559], bandhīyateti bandhati, pajjatīti patti, padāti vā, īāgamassa āttaṃ, vasanti etthāti vasati-gehaṃ, vasanaṃ vā vasati iccādi.

According to the Mahāvutti, when 'ta' follows, 'kar' becomes 'kut'. Examples are: action (kriyā), making (kutti), vowel-making (sarakutti), womanhood (itthikuttaṃ), manhood (purisakuttaṃ). It generates, therefore it is a mother (janetti). The augment 'ī' becomes 'e'. It is bound, therefore it is a binding (bandhati). It goes, therefore it is attainment (patti); or, it gives (padāti). The augment 'ī' becomes 'ā'. They dwell here, therefore it is a dwelling, a house (vasati-gehaṃ); or, dwelling (vasanaṃ), thus dwelling (vasati), and so on.

802. Jāhāhi ni.

802. After 'jā' and 'hā', 'ni'.

Etehi ni hoti.

After these, the suffix 'ni' occurs.

Jā-hāniyaṃ, jiyyate jāni, dhanajāni, bhogajāni, mahantī jāni assāti mahājāniyo, hiyyate hāni, vaṇṇahāni, balahāni, āyuhāni, avahāni, parihāni.

From the roots 'jā' and 'hā' in the sense of loss ('hāniyaṃ'): It decays, therefore it is loss (jāni); loss of wealth (dhanajāni); loss of possessions (bhogajāni). One who has great loss is 'mahājāniyo'. It diminishes, therefore it is loss (hāni); loss of complexion (vaṇṇahāni); loss of strength (balahāni); loss of life (āyuhāni); diminution (avahāni); decline (parihāni).

803. Karā ririyo ka. 554; rū. 601; nī. 1141.

803. After 'kar', 'ririyo'.

Karamhā itthiyaṃ ririyo hoti.

After the root 'kar', in the feminine gender, the suffix 'ririyo' occurs.

Karīyate kiriyā, nipātanena kriyāti sijjhati.

It is done, therefore it is action (kiriyā). The form 'kriyā' is accomplished by irregular formation.

Iti itthiliṅgarūparāsi.

Thus ends the section on feminine gender forms.

Rīrikkhādipaccayarāsi

The Section on Suffixes beginning with 'rī' and 'rikkha'

804. Samānaññabhavantayāditūpamānā disā kamme rīrikkhakā ka. 642; rū. 588; nī. 1269.

804. After 'samāna', 'añña', 'bhavanta', those beginning with 'ya', and 'dis' used as a standard of comparison, the suffixes 'rī', 'rikkha', and 'ka' occur in the sense of the object.

Samāno ca añño ca bhavanto ca yādi ca etehi upamānabhūtehi paraṃ disamhā kammerī ca rikkho ca ko cāti ete paccayā honti, rī, rikkhesu ‘rānubandhentasarādissā’ti suttena disassa antassarādīnaṃ lopo, kānubandho avuddhattho, ‘rīrikkhakesu’iccādīhi samāsasuttehi pubbapadānaṃ rūpaṃ sādhetabbaṃ.

After these—'samāna', 'añña', 'bhavanta', and those beginning with 'ya'—which serve as standards of comparison, and after 'dis', the suffixes 'rī', 'rikkha', and 'ka' occur in the sense of the object. When 'rī' and 'rikkha' follow, by the rule 'rānubandhentasarādissā', there is elision of the final vowel and initial part of 'dis'. The indicatory 'k' serves to prevent vowel gradation. The form of the preceding words should be derived according to the rules for compounds, such as in 'rīrikkhakesu'.

Ya, ta, eta, ima, kiṃ, tumha, amha, bhavanta, samāna, añña.

Ya, ta, eta, ima, kiṃ, tumha, amha, bhavanta, samāna, añña.

Yo viya dissatīti yādī, yādikkho, yādiso, yaṃ viya naṃ passantīti yādī, ye viya dissantīti yādino, itthiyaṃ-yā [M 0.0560] viya dissatīti yādinī, yādikkhā, yādikkhī, yādisā, yādisī, yā viya dissantīti yādiniyo, yādikkhāyo, yādikkhiyo, yādisāyo, yādisiyo. Evaṃ sesesupi.

‘Like which he appears’ ('yo viya dissati'): 'yādī', 'yādikkho', 'yādiso'. ‘Like which they see him’ ('yaṃ viya naṃ passanti'): 'yādī'. ‘Like which they (masc. pl.) appear’ ('ye viya dissanti'): 'yādino'. In the feminine: ‘Like which she appears’ ('yā viya dissati'): 'yādinī', 'yādikkhā', 'yādikkhī', 'yādisā', 'yādisī'. ‘Like which they (fem. pl.) appear’ ('yā viya dissanti'): 'yādiniyo', 'yādikkhāyo', 'yādikkhiyo', 'yādisāyo', 'yādisiyo'. Thus it is for the remaining words as well.

So viya dissatīti tādī, tādikkho, tādiso.

‘Like that he appears’ ('so viya dissati'): 'tādī', 'tādikkho', 'tādiso'.

Eso viya dissatīti edī, edikkho, ediso, etādī, etādikkho, etādiso vā.

‘Like this one he appears’ ('eso viya dissati'): 'edī', 'edikkho', 'ediso', or alternatively 'etādī', 'etādikkho', 'etādiso'.

Ayaṃ viya dissatīti īdī, īdikkho, īdiso.

‘Like this one he appears’ ('ayaṃ viya dissati'): 'īdī', 'īdikkho', 'īdiso'.

Ko viya dissatīti kīdī, kīdikkho, kīdiso.

‘Like whom does he appear?’ ('ko viya dissati'): 'kīdī', 'kīdikkho', 'kīdiso'.

Tvaṃ viya dissatīti tādī, tādikkho, tādiso.

‘Like you he appears’ ('tvaṃ viya dissati'): 'tādī', 'tādikkho', 'tādiso'.

Ahaṃ viya dissatīti mādī, mādikkho, mādiso.

‘Like me he appears’ ('ahaṃ viya dissati'): 'mādī', 'mādikkho', 'mādiso'.

Bahutte pana tumhe viya dissantīti tumhādī, tumhādikkho, tumhādiso.

In the plural, however: ‘Like you (pl.) they appear’ ('tumhe viya dissanti'): 'tumhādī', 'tumhādikkho', 'tumhādiso'.

Amhe viya dissantīti amhādī, amhādikkho, amhādiso.

‘Like us they appear’ ('amhe viya dissanti'): 'amhādī', 'amhādikkho', 'amhādiso'.

Bhavaṃ viya dissatīti bhavādī, bhavādikkho, bhavādiso.

‘Like the venerable one he appears’ ('bhavaṃ viya dissati'): 'bhavādī', 'bhavādikkho', 'bhavādiso'.

Samāno viya dissatīti sadī, sadikkho, sadiso.

‘Like an equal he appears’ ('samāno viya dissati'): 'sadī', 'sadikkho', 'sadiso'.

Añño viya dissatīti aññādī, aññādikkho, aññādiso.

‘Like another he appears’ ('añño viya dissati'): 'aññādī', 'aññādikkho', 'aññādiso'.

Itthiyaṃ-yā viya dissatīti yādisā-itthī, yādisī-itthī. Tādisā-itthī, tādisī-itthī iccādi.

In the feminine: ‘Like which (she) appears’ ('yā viya dissati') gives 'yādisā-itthī' (a woman of which kind), 'yādisī-itthī'. Similarly, 'tādisā-itthī', 'tādisī-itthī', and so on.

805. Vamādīhi thu ka. 644; rū. 661; nī. 1271-3; ‘vamādīhyathu’ (bahūsu).

805. After 'vam', etc., 'thu'.

Vamādīhi bhāvakārakesu thu hoti.

After the root 'vam' and others, the suffix 'thu' occurs in the sense of state or agent.

Vamīyateti vamathu, davīyateti davathu iccādi.

‘It is vomited’ ('vamīyati'), therefore 'vamathu' (vomiting). ‘It is burned’ ('davīyati'), therefore 'davathu' (burning), and so on.

806. Kvi ka. 530; rū. 584; nī. 1112.

806. The suffix 'kvi'.

Bhāvakārakesu [M 0.0561] kvi hoti.

The affix 'kvi' occurs in the sense of state/action and agent.

807. Kvissa ka. 639; rū. 585; nī. 1266.

807. Elision of 'kvi'.

Kvissa lopo hoti.

Elision of 'kvi' occurs.

Ivaṇṇesu tāva-bhuso cayati vaḍḍhatīti acci, dvittaṃ rassattañca, vividhena cayati vaḍḍhatīti vīci, pañca māre jinātīti māraji, bhaddaṃ jinātīti bhaddaji. Evaṃ puṇṇaji, gāmaṃ samūhaṃ netīti gāmaṇī, nassa ṇattaṃ. Senaṃ netīti senānī iccādi.

First, in the case of roots ending in 'i': 'bhuso cayati vaḍḍhatīti' (that which accumulates and grows greatly) is 'acci' (flame), with doubling and shortening; 'vividhena cayati vaḍḍhatīti' (that which accumulates and grows in various ways) is 'vīci' (wave); 'pañca māre jinātīti' (he who conquers the five Māras) is 'māraji' (conqueror of the Māras); 'bhaddaṃ jinātīti' (he who wins what is auspicious) is 'bhaddaji'. Similarly, 'puṇṇaji'; 'gāmaṃ samūhaṃ netīti' (he who leads a village or group) is 'gāmaṇī' (village headman), with 'n' becoming 'ṇ'. 'Senaṃ netīti' (he who leads an army) is 'senānī' (general), and so on.

Uvaṇṇesu-māreti cāveti cāti maccu, mahāvuttinā rassa pararūpattaṃ, vividhena javati sīghaṃ pharatīti vijju, bhavanti etthāti bhū-bhūmi, pabhavati issaraṃ karotīti pabhū, vibhavanaṃ vibhū, abhibhavatīti abhibhū, sayaṃ bhavatīti sayambhū, gottaṃ abhibhavatīti gottabhū, gotrabhū iccādi.

In the case of roots ending in 'u': 'māreti cāveti cāti' (that which kills and removes) is 'maccu' (death); by the great rule, shortening and assimilation to the following sound occur; 'vividhena javati sīghaṃ pharatīti' (that which moves swiftly and spreads quickly in various ways) is 'vijju' (lightning); 'bhavanti etthāti' (that in which things come to be) is 'bhū' (earth, ground); 'pabhavati issaraṃ karotīti' (he who is powerful and exercises lordship) is 'pabhū' (lord, master); 'vibhavanaṃ' (power) is 'vibhū'; 'abhibhavatīti' (he who overcomes) is 'abhibhū' (overcomer); 'sayaṃ bhavatīti' (he who comes to be by himself) is 'sayambhū' (self-existent); 'gottaṃ abhibhavatīti' (he who overcomes lineage) is 'gottabhū' or 'gotrabhū' (one who has transcended lineage), and so on.

Byañjanantesu –

In the case of roots ending in a consonant:

808. Kvimhi lopontabyañjanassa ka. 615; rū. 586; nī. 1220.

808. Elision of the final consonant when 'kvi' is present.

Dhātūnaṃ antabyañjanassa lopo hoti kvimhi.

The final consonant of roots is elided when 'kvi' is present.

Antaṃ karotīti antako, nandaṃ karotīti nandako, jīvaṃ karotīti jīvako, cittaṃ vicittaṃ karotīti cittako, sukhena khamitabbanti sukhaṃ, dukkhena khamitabbanti dukkhaṃ, parito khaññateti parikkhā, saṃ attānaṃ khanatīti saṅkho, na gacchatīti ago-nago, sīsaṃ upagacchatīti sīsūpago. Evaṃ gīvūpago, ninnaṭṭhānaṃ gacchatīti ninnagā-nadī, turaṃ sīghaṃ gacchatīti turaṅgo, majjhe bindāgamo.

'Antaṃ karotīti' (he who makes an end) is 'antako'; 'nandaṃ karotīti' (he who makes joy) is 'nandako'; 'jīvaṃ karotīti' (he who makes life) is 'jīvako'; 'cittaṃ vicittaṃ karotīti' (he who makes things varied) is 'cittako' (an artist); 'sukhena khamitabbanti' (that which is to be endured with ease) is 'sukhaṃ'; 'dukkhena khamitabbanti' (that which is to be endured with difficulty) is 'dukkhaṃ'; 'parito khaññateti' (that which is dug all around) is 'parikkhā' (a trench); 'saṃ attānaṃ khanatīti' (that which digs itself) is 'saṅkho' (a conch); 'na gacchatīti' (that which does not go) is 'ago' or 'nago' (mountain, tree); 'sīsaṃ upagacchatīti' (that which approaches the head) is 'sīsūpago'. Similarly, 'gīvūpago'; 'ninnaṭṭhānaṃ gacchatīti' (that which goes to a low place) is 'ninnagā' (a river); 'turaṃ sīghaṃ gacchatīti' (that which goes swiftly and quickly) is 'turaṅgo' (a horse), with a nasal inserted in the middle.

Bhujena [M 0.0562] kuṭilena gacchatīti bhujago, urena gacchatīti urago, khena ākāsena gacchatīti khago, vehāse gacchatīti vihago, mahāvuttinā vehāsassa vihādeso.

'Bhujena kuṭilena gacchatīti' (that which goes crookedly with its coils) is 'bhujago' (a snake); 'urena gacchatīti' (that which goes on its chest) is 'urago' (a snake); 'khena ākāsena gacchatīti' (that which goes through the sky) is 'khago' (a bird); 'vehāse gacchatīti' (that which goes in the sky) is 'vihago' (a bird); by the great rule, 'vehāsa' is substituted by 'vihā'.

“Go gacchati, gāvo gacchantī”tiādīsu pana “gocaro, godhano, gottaṃ, gotrabhū”tiādīsu ca kvimhi antabyañjanalope kvilope ca kate mahāvuttinā upantassa ottaṃ katvā goiti pakatirūpaṃ veditabbaṃ, balaṃ gaṇīyati etthāti balaggaṃ, bhattaṃ gaṇhanti etthāti bhattaggaṃ. Evaṃ salākaggaṃ, uposathaggaṃ.

However, in cases like 'go gacchati' (the ox goes), 'gāvo gacchantī' (the oxen go), etc., and in words like 'gocaro' (pasture), 'godhano' (wealth of cattle), 'gottaṃ' (lineage), 'gotrabhū' (one who has transcended lineage), etc., when the final consonant is elided due to 'kvi' and 'kvi' itself is elided, by the great rule, the penultimate vowel is changed to 'o', and the original form 'go' should be understood. 'Balaṃ gaṇīyati etthāti' (that in which the force is counted) is 'balaggaṃ' (the best of the force); 'bhattaṃ gaṇhanti etthāti' (that in which food is taken) is 'bhattaggaṃ' (a refectory). Similarly, 'salākaggaṃ' (a place for distributing lots), 'uposathaggaṃ' (an Uposatha hall).

Kammena jāyatīti kammajo. Evaṃ cittajo, utujo, attani jātoti atrajo, pubbe jāto pubbajo, pacchā jāto anujo, saha jāyatīti sahajo, thale jāyatīti thalajaṃ. Evaṃ dakajaṃ, vārijaṃ, ambujaṃ. Aṇḍe jāyatīti aṇḍajo, dvikkhattuṃ jāyatīti dvijo, saha bhāsanti etthāti sabhā, kuñje ramatīti kuñjaro iccādi.

'Kammena jāyatīti' (that which is born from action) is 'kammajo'. Similarly, 'cittajo' (mind-born), 'utujo' (season-born); 'attani jāto' (he who is born from oneself) is 'atrajo' (a son); 'pubbe jāto' (he who is born before) is 'pubbajo' (an elder); 'pacchā jāto' (he who is born after) is 'anujo' (a younger brother); 'saha jāyatīti' (that which is born together) is 'sahajo' (innate); 'thale jāyatīti' (that which is born on land) is 'thalajaṃ' (terrestrial). Similarly, 'dakajaṃ' (aquatic), 'vārijaṃ' (water-born), 'ambujaṃ' (a lotus). 'Aṇḍe jāyatīti' (that which is born from an egg) is 'aṇḍajo' (oviparous); 'dvikkhattuṃ jāyatīti' (that which is born twice) is 'dvijo' (twice-born); 'saha bhāsanti etthāti' (that in which they speak together) is 'sabhā' (an assembly); 'kuñje ramatīti' (that which delights in a thicket) is 'kuñjaro' (an elephant), and so on.

809. Kvimhi gho paripaccāsamohi ka. 538; rū. 595; nī. 1123; ‘…pacca…’ (bahūsu).

809. When 'kvi' follows, 'gha' is the substitute for 'han' after 'pari', 'pati', 'ā', 'saṃ', and 'o'.

Pari ca pati ca ā ca sañca o ca etehi parassa hanassa gho hoti kvimhi.

After 'pari', 'pati', 'ā', 'saṃ', and 'o', the root 'han' becomes 'gha' when 'kvi' is present.

Parihaññatīti paligho, rassa lattaṃ. Patihanatīti paṭigho, tassa ṭattaṃ. Bhuso hanati bādhatīti aghaṃ-dukkhaṃ pāpañca, visesena bhuso hanatīti byaggho, diṭṭhi, sīlasāmaññena saṃhatoti saṅgho-samūho, devasaṅgho, brahmasaṅgho, migasaṅgho, ohanati adhobhāgaṃ katvā māretīti ogho, kilesogho, saṃsārogho, udakogho.

'Parihaññatīti' (that which is struck all around) is 'paligho' (a crossbar), with 'r' becoming 'l'. 'Patihanatīti' (that which strikes against) is 'paṭigho' (aversion), with 't' becoming 'ṭ'. 'Bhuso hanati bādhatīti' (that which greatly harms and oppresses) is 'aghaṃ' (suffering and evil). 'Visesena bhuso hanatīti' (that which especially and greatly harms) is 'byaggho' (a tiger), and 'diṭṭhi' (wrong view). 'Sīlasāmaññena saṃhatoti' (that which is united by common virtue) is 'saṅgho' (an assembly), such as the assembly of devas, the assembly of brahmās, the assembly of deer. 'Ohanati adhobhāgaṃ katvā māretīti' (that which strikes down, causing to descend and killing) is 'ogho' (a flood), such as the flood of defilements, the flood of saṃsāra, the flood of water.

Suttavibhattiyā aññatopi gho hoti, mātaraṃ hanatīti mātugho. Evaṃ pitugho iccādi.

By the force of the rule, 'gha' also occurs elsewhere: 'mātaraṃ hanatīti' (he who kills his mother) is 'mātugho' (a matricide). Similarly, 'pitugho' (a patricide), and so on.

810. Ṇvādayo ka. 650; rū. 651; nī. 1288.

810. The affixes beginning with 'ṇu'.

Kriyatthā [M 0.0563] bhāvakārakesu ṇuādayo honti, upari vuccamāno sabbo ṇvādikaṇḍo imassa suttassa niddeso hoti, tasmā idha kiñcimattaṃ vuccate.

The affixes beginning with ṇu occur in the senses of action, state/action, and agent. The entire section on ṇvādi, which will be explained subsequently, serves as an exposition of this rule. Therefore, only a little is mentioned here.

Karotīti kāru-sippī, ayati vaḍḍhatīti āyu, ayanti vaḍḍhanti sattā etenāti vā āyu-jīvitaṃ, sobhāvisesaṃ rahanti jahanti canda, sūriyā etenāti rāhu-asurindo, hitasukhaṃ sādhetīti sādhu-sappuriso, vāyatīti vāyuvāto iccādi.

'Karotīti' (He who does or makes) is 'kāru,' an artisan. 'Ayati vaḍḍhatīti' (That which extends and grows) is 'āyu,' life. Or, 'ayanti vaḍḍhanti sattā etenāti' (That by which beings extend and grow) is 'āyu,' life-force. 'Sobhāvisesaṃ rahanti jahanti canda, sūriyā etenāti' (That by which the moon and sun abandon their special radiance) is 'rāhu,' the lord of the Asuras. 'Hitasukhaṃ sādhetīti' (He who accomplishes welfare and happiness) is 'sādhu,' a virtuous person. 'Vāyatīti' (That which blows) is 'vāyu,' the wind, and so on.

Iti rīrikkhādipaccayarāsi.

Thus concludes the collection of suffixes, etc., beginning with rīrikkha.

Pakatirūparāsi niṭṭhito.

The collection of natural forms is concluded.

Iti niruttidīpaniyā nāma moggallānadīpaniyā

Thus, in the Niruttidīpanī, also known as the Moggallānadīpanī,

Tabbādikaṇḍo nāma kitakaṇḍo niṭṭhito.

the Kitakaṇḍa, named the Tabbādikaṇḍa, is concluded.
